```go
// Package eventbus is the in-process pub/sub seam between modules
// (e.g. settlement executed → notifications module queues the SMS).
// It deliberately mirrors a message-broker API: when the platform splits
// into microservices, this interface is re-implemented over Kafka/NATS
// (blueprint §15) without touching module code.
package eventbus

import (
	"context"
	"log/slog"
	"sync"
	"time"
)

// Topics published across module seams.
const (
	TopicPourRecorded       = "pour.recorded"
	TopicInvoiceIssued      = "invoice.issued"
	TopicGateBlocked        = "qc.gate_blocked"
	TopicSettlementExecuted = "settlement.executed"
	TopicPayoutCredited     = "payout.credited"
	TopicMVUDispatched      = "mvu.dispatched"
)

// Handler consumes a published event. Payload types are documented per topic
// by the publishing module.
type Handler func(ctx context.Context, topic string, payload any)

// Bus is a minimal async pub/sub.
type Bus struct {
	log *slog.Logger

	mu   sync.RWMutex
	subs map[string][]Handler
}

// New builds an empty bus.
func New(log *slog.Logger) *Bus {
	return &Bus{log: log, subs: make(map[string][]Handler)}
}

// Subscribe registers a handler for a topic. Call during module wiring only
// (not concurrently with Publish traffic).
func (b *Bus) Subscribe(topic string, h Handler) {
	b.mu.Lock()
	defer b.mu.Unlock()
	b.subs[topic] = append(b.subs[topic], h)
}

// Publish dispatches asynchronously: each handler runs on its own goroutine
// with a bounded context and panic isolation, so a slow or broken subscriber
// can never stall the request path.
func (b *Bus) Publish(topic string, payload any) {
	b.mu.RLock()
	handlers := b.subs[topic]
	b.mu.RUnlock()

	for _, h := range handlers {
		h := h
		go func() {
			ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 15*time.Second)
			defer cancel()
			defer func() {
				if rec := recover(); rec != nil {
					b.log.Error("eventbus handler panic",
						slog.String("topic", topic), slog.Any("panic", rec))
				}
			}()
			h(ctx, topic, payload)
		}()
	}
}
```

```go
// Package middleware carries the cross-cutting HTTP concerns: token
// authentication, role enforcement, audit capture, per-IP rate limiting,
// Prometheus metrics.
package middleware

import (
	"net/http"
	"strings"

	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/auth"
	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/httpx"
)

// Authenticate verifies the Bearer token and installs the Actor on the
// request context. Requests without a valid token are rejected — public
// routes simply don't mount this middleware.
func Authenticate(jwtm *auth.JWTManager) func(http.Handler) http.Handler {
	return func(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
		return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
			header := r.Header.Get("Authorization")
			token, ok := strings.CutPrefix(header, "Bearer ")
			if !ok || token == "" {
				httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Unauthorized("missing bearer token"))
				return
			}
			claims, err := jwtm.Parse(token)
			if err != nil {
				httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Unauthorized("invalid or expired token"))
				return
			}
			actor := auth.Actor{
				PartyID:          claims.PartyID,
				Phone:            claims.Phone,
				KYCTier:          claims.KYCTier,
				Kind:             claims.Kind,
				RoleAssignmentID: claims.RoleAssignmentID,
				RoleCode:         claims.RoleCode,
				OrgUnitID:        claims.OrgUnitID,
				OrgType:          claims.OrgType,
			}
			next.ServeHTTP(w, r.WithContext(auth.WithActor(r.Context(), actor)))
		})
	}
}
```

```go
package middleware

import (
	"net/http"

	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/domain"
	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/auth"
	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/httpx"
)

// RequireRoles allows only ROLE-kind tokens whose role is in the allow-list.
// SUPER_ADMIN passes every gate (break-glass admin — all its calls are
// audited by the audit middleware).
func RequireRoles(roles ...string) func(http.Handler) http.Handler {
	allowed := make(map[string]struct{}, len(roles))
	for _, r := range roles {
		allowed[r] = struct{}{}
	}
	return func(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
		return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
			actor, ok := auth.ActorFrom(r.Context())
			if !ok {
				httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Unauthorized("authentication required"))
				return
			}
			if actor.Kind != auth.TokenKindRole {
				httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Forbidden("a role token is required — select a role first (POST /api/v1/auth/role/select)"))
				return
			}
			if actor.RoleCode == domain.RoleSuperAdmin {
				next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
				return
			}
			if _, ok := allowed[actor.RoleCode]; !ok {
				httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Forbidden("role "+actor.RoleCode+" is not permitted for this action"))
				return
			}
			next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
		})
	}
}

// RequireSession allows any authenticated party (session or role token) —
// used for identity endpoints like "list my roles".
func RequireSession(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
	return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		if _, ok := auth.ActorFrom(r.Context()); !ok {
			httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Unauthorized("authentication required"))
			return
		}
		next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
	})
}
```

```go
package middleware

import (
	"net/http"

	chimw "github.com/go-chi/chi/v5/middleware"

	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/audit"
)

// AuditMutations records every state-changing request (non-GET/HEAD/OPTIONS)
// into the immutable audit trail: actor, action, status, IP, request ID.
// Runs after the handler so the final status code is captured; the write
// itself is async and adds no request latency.
func AuditMutations(rec *audit.Recorder) func(http.Handler) http.Handler {
	return func(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
		return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
			if r.Method == http.MethodGet || r.Method == http.MethodHead || r.Method == http.MethodOptions {
				next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
				return
			}
			ww := chimw.NewWrapResponseWriter(w, r.ProtoMajor)
			next.ServeHTTP(ww, r)

			rec.Record(r.Context(), audit.Entry{
				Action:    "http." + r.Method + " " + r.URL.Path,
				Status:    ww.Status(),
				IP:        r.RemoteAddr,
				RequestID: chimw.GetReqID(r.Context()),
			})
		})
	}
}
```

```go
package middleware

import (
	"net"
	"net/http"
	"sync"
	"time"

	"golang.org/x/time/rate"

	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/httpx"
)

// PerIPRateLimit applies a token-bucket limit per client IP. In-memory by
// design: each API replica defends itself; global fairness belongs to the
// gateway/WAF tier in production (blueprint §6).
func PerIPRateLimit(rps float64, burst int) func(http.Handler) http.Handler {
	type bucket struct {
		lim  *rate.Limiter
		seen time.Time
	}
	var (
		mu      sync.Mutex
		buckets = make(map[string]*bucket)
	)

	// Janitor: drop buckets idle >10 min so the map can't grow unbounded.
	go func() {
		for range time.Tick(5 * time.Minute) {
			mu.Lock()
			for ip, b := range buckets {
				if time.Since(b.seen) > 10*time.Minute {
					delete(buckets, ip)
				}
			}
			mu.Unlock()
		}
	}()

	return func(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
		return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
			ip, _, err := net.SplitHostPort(r.RemoteAddr)
			if err != nil {
				ip = r.RemoteAddr
			}
			mu.Lock()
			b, ok := buckets[ip]
			if !ok {
				b = &bucket{lim: rate.NewLimiter(rate.Limit(rps), burst)}
				buckets[ip] = b
			}
			b.seen = time.Now()
			mu.Unlock()

			if !b.lim.Allow() {
				httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.TooManyRequests("too many requests — slow down"))
				return
			}
			next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
		})
	}
}
```

```go
package middleware

import (
	"net/http"
	"strconv"
	"time"

	"github.com/go-chi/chi/v5"
	chimw "github.com/go-chi/chi/v5/middleware"
	"github.com/prometheus/client_golang/prometheus"
	"github.com/prometheus/client_golang/prometheus/promauto"
)

var (
	httpRequestsTotal = promauto.NewCounterVec(prometheus.CounterOpts{
		Name: "saathi_http_requests_total",
		Help: "HTTP requests by method, route pattern and status.",
	}, []string{"method", "route", "status"})

	httpRequestDuration = promauto.NewHistogramVec(prometheus.HistogramOpts{
		Name:    "saathi_http_request_duration_seconds",
		Help:    "HTTP request latency by method and route pattern.",
		Buckets: []float64{.005, .01, .025, .05, .1, .25, .5, 1, 2.5, 5},
	}, []string{"method", "route"})
)

// Metrics records request count + latency labelled by the chi route PATTERN
// (e.g. /api/v1/collection/pours/{id}), not the raw path — bounded label
// cardinality, dashboard-friendly.
func Metrics(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
	return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		start := time.Now()
		ww := chimw.NewWrapResponseWriter(w, r.ProtoMajor)
		next.ServeHTTP(ww, r)

		route := "unmatched"
		if rc := chi.RouteContext(r.Context()); rc != nil {
			if p := rc.RoutePattern(); p != "" {
				route = p
			}
		}
		httpRequestsTotal.WithLabelValues(r.Method, route, strconv.Itoa(ww.Status())).Inc()
		httpRequestDuration.WithLabelValues(r.Method, route).Observe(time.Since(start).Seconds())
	})
}
```

```go
// Package httpapi assembles the HTTP surface: global middleware, operational
// endpoints (health/readiness/metrics/version), and the /api/v1 tree where
// every domain module mounts its routes.
package httpapi

import (
	"context"
	"net/http"
	"time"

	"github.com/go-chi/chi/v5"
	chimw "github.com/go-chi/chi/v5/middleware"
	"github.com/prometheus/client_golang/prometheus/promhttp"

	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/deps"
	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/httpx"
	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/middleware"
)

// Version is stamped via -ldflags at release build time.
var Version = "0.1.0-dev"

// New builds the fully wired HTTP handler.
func New(d *deps.Deps) http.Handler {
	r := chi.NewRouter()

	// Order matters: recover innermost-last so panics in anything above are caught.
	r.Use(chimw.RequestID)
	r.Use(chimw.RealIP)
	r.Use(middleware.Metrics)
	r.Use(middleware.PerIPRateLimit(d.Cfg.RateLimitRPS, d.Cfg.RateLimitBurst))
	r.Use(chimw.Recoverer)
	r.Use(chimw.Timeout(30 * time.Second))

	// Operational endpoints — outside /api/v1, never authenticated.
	r.Get("/healthz", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		httpx.JSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]string{"status": "ok"})
	})
	r.Get("/readyz", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(r.Context(), 2*time.Second)
		defer cancel()
		if err := d.DB.Client().Ping(ctx, nil); err != nil {
			httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Internal(err))
			return
		}
		httpx.JSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]string{"status": "ready"})
	})
	r.Handle("/metrics", promhttp.Handler())
	r.Get("/version", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		httpx.JSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]string{"version": Version, "service": "saathi-backend"})
	})

	r.Route("/api/v1", func(api chi.Router) {
		api.Use(middleware.AuditMutations(d.Audit))
		RegisterModules(api, d)
	})

	return r
}
```

```go
// Command server boots the Saathi backend API: config → logger → MongoDB
// (env-only URI) → indexes → platform services → HTTP router, with graceful
// shutdown on SIGINT/SIGTERM.
package main

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"log/slog"
	"net/http"
	"os"
	"os/signal"
	"syscall"
	"time"

	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/config"
	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/httpapi"
	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/audit"
	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/auth"
	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/deps"
	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/eventbus"
	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/flags"
	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/logger"
	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/mongodb"
	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/orgscope"
	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/provenance"
)

func main() {
	if err := run(); err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "fatal:", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}

func run() error {
	cfg, err := config.Load()
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	log := logger.New(cfg.LogLevel, cfg.Env)

	bootCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 30*time.Second)
	defer cancel()

	client, db, err := mongodb.Connect(bootCtx, cfg.MongoURI, cfg.MongoDB)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer func() {
		shutdownCtx, c := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
		defer c()
		_ = client.Disconnect(shutdownCtx)
	}()
	log.Info("mongodb connected", slog.String("db", cfg.MongoDB))

	if err := mongodb.EnsureIndexes(bootCtx, db); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	log.Info("indexes ensured")

	flagSvc := flags.NewService(db)
	if err := flagSvc.EnsureDefaults(bootCtx, map[string]flags.Flag{
		flags.FlagCollarTelemetry:  {Enabled: false, Description: "Dormant collar/wearable telemetry ingestion (§9) — flip when a scheme lands"},
		flags.FlagPhotoOCR:         {Enabled: true, Description: "Photo-OCR bridge for legacy analyzers (§8.2)"},
		flags.FlagONDC:             {Enabled: false, Description: "ONDC commerce compatibility (§11, Phase 3)"},
		flags.FlagConsumerCommerce: {Enabled: true, Description: "Consumer browse/order endpoints (§11)"},
	}); err != nil {
		return err
	}

	d := &deps.Deps{
		Cfg:    cfg,
		Log:    log,
		DB:     db,
		JWT:    auth.NewJWTManager(cfg.JWTSecret, cfg.AccessTokenTTL),
		Ledger: provenance.NewLedger(db),
		Audit:  audit.NewRecorder(db, log),
		Flags:  flagSvc,
		Orgs:   orgscope.NewResolver(db),
		Bus:    eventbus.New(log),
	}

	srv := &http.Server{
		Addr:              fmt.Sprintf(":%d", cfg.Port),
		Handler:           httpapi.New(d),
		ReadHeaderTimeout: 10 * time.Second,
		ReadTimeout:       30 * time.Second,
		WriteTimeout:      60 * time.Second,
		IdleTimeout:       2 * time.Minute,
	}

	errCh := make(chan error, 1)
	go func() {
		log.Info("saathi backend listening",
			slog.Int("port", cfg.Port), slog.String("env", cfg.Env), slog.String("version", httpapi.Version))
		if err := srv.ListenAndServe(); err != nil && !errors.Is(err, http.ErrServerClosed) {
			errCh <- err
		}
	}()

	stop := make(chan os.Signal, 1)
	signal.Notify(stop, syscall.SIGINT, syscall.SIGTERM)

	select {
	case err := <-errCh:
		return err
	case sig := <-stop:
		log.Info("shutting down", slog.String("signal", sig.String()))
	}

	shutdownCtx, cancelShutdown := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 15*time.Second)
	defer cancelShutdown()
	return srv.Shutdown(shutdownCtx)
}
```

```go
	fmt.Printf("  super admin phone: %s (OTP_DEV_MODE returns the OTP in the login response)\n", cfg.SeedAdminPhone)
	fmt.Println("  demo phones: sacheev 9000000001 · adhyaksh 9000000002 · farmer 9000000011 · rider 9000000021")
	fmt.Println("               bmc-op 9000000031 · plant-op 9000000041 · lab 9000000042 · consumer 9000000051")
	return nil
}

// upsert replaces the document with _id=id (insert if missing).
func upsert(ctx context.Context, coll *mongo.Collection, id string, doc any) error {
	_, err := coll.ReplaceOne(ctx,
		bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: id}},
		doc,
		options.Replace().SetUpsert(true),
	)
	return err
}
```

- POST /cattle/animals/{id}/bp-sync (RequireRoles VETERINARIAN, PCDF_ADMIN) → MOCK Bharat Pashudhan push: mark this animal's PENDING events SYNCED with bp_sync_ref "BP-MOCK-"+uuid[0:8]; return count.

POST /cattle/mvu-cases/{id}/close (RequireRoles VETERINARIAN) {visit_notes, health_event_ids?} → CLOSED. GET /cattle/mvu-cases?dcs_id=&status= (vet/driver/sacheev/mission) paged.

READINGS (RequireRoles SAMITI_SACHEEV, MILK_TESTER):
- POST /collection/readings {dcs_id, mode(ANALYZER_DIRECT|PHOTO_OCR|MANUAL), fat_pct, snf_pct, clr?, water_pct?, quantity_litres?, device_id?, photo_object_key?, ocr_confidence?, geo_lat?, geo_lng?, device_timestamp?} → RequireInScope(dcs_id); PHOTO_OCR requires d.Flags.Enabled(FlagPhotoOCR) else 403 FEATURE_DISABLED, and requires photo_object_key (evidence retention §8.2) + flag LOW_OCR_CONFIDENCE when ocr_confidence<0.75; MANUAL always gets IntegrityFlagManualEntry; missing geotag → IntegrityFlagMissingGeotag; |server-device time|>10min → IntegrityFlagClockSkew; domain.CheckPlausibility flags → PlausibilityOK=false (still stored — flagged, not rejected); provenance EventReadingRecorded entity EntityAnalyzerReading.

- POST /collection/pours/batch-sync {pours:[…max 500]} → per-item same logic, never abort the batch; response [{client_event_id, status created|duplicate|error, pour_id?, error?}]. THE offline reconnect path (§3.1).
- POST /collection/pours/{id}/supersede {reason, corrected:{quantity_litres?, fat_pct?, snf_pct?}} → append-only correction (§3.4): old pour status SUPERSEDED (doc stays); new pour (new uuid, client_event_id old+"::corr::"+uuid[0:8], supersedes_pour_id=old, repriced); provenance EventPourSuperseded on NEW pour refs old ("supersedes") payload {reason}; 409 if already superseded/cancelled or invoiced (invoice exists containing pour id and not HOLD).
- GET /collection/pours?dcs_id=&date=&shift=&farmer_party_id= → sacheev/tester/supervisor scope-checked; FARMER allowed but forced farmer_party_id=actor.PartyID; paged.
INVOICES:

- GET /collection/invoices?dcs_id=&date=&farmer_party_id=&status= → FARMER forced own; others scoped; paged. GET /collection/invoices/{id} → farmer-own or scoped role.

=== YOUR MODULE SPEC ===
Module "orgs" — the cooperative hierarchy (FEDERATION→MILK_UNION→{PLANT,BMC,DCS}). Route prefix: /orgs. All routes authenticated.
- POST /orgs (RequireRoles SUPER_ADMIN, PCDF_ADMIN) {type,name,code,parent_id?,district?,state?,geo_lat?,geo_lng?} → validate domain.IsValidOrgType; parent's type must be allowed by domain.ValidOrgParent[type] (FEDERATION needs no parent, must be unique root — reject a second FEDERATION); build Path = parent.Path + parent.ID; code unique (rely on index, map dup-key → Conflict ORG_CODE_EXISTS); d.Orgs.Invalidate on writes.
- PATCH /orgs/{id} (same roles) {name?,district?,active?,geo…} → no type/parent moves in v1 (reject with Unprocessable ORG_MOVE_UNSUPPORTED); Invalidate cache.
- GET /orgs/{id} (RequireSession) → org unit.
- GET /orgs/{id}/children (RequireSession) → paged children (parent_id index).
- GET /orgs/{id}/tree (RequireRoles SUPER_ADMIN, PCDF_ADMIN, MISSION_OFFICIAL, UNION_PRESIDENT, STATE_AUDITOR) → subtree via path array-containment query (path contains id), capped 500 nodes, returned as flat list with parent_id (client assembles).
- GET /orgs?type=DCS&district=… (RequireSession) → paged filtered list.
- GET /orgs/{id}/members (RequireRoles SAMITI_SACHEEV, SAMITI_ADHYAKSH, UNION_FIELD_SUPERVISOR, UNION_PRESIDENT, PCDF_ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN) → RequireInScope; join role_assignments (ACTIVE @ this org) with parties (phone, full_name, kyc_tier) — two queries + in-memory join, no $lookup needed; paged.
No provenance events. Unit test: parent-type validation matrix.

=== YOUR MODULE SPEC ===
Module "identity" — auth, parties, role assignments, KYC. Route prefixes: /auth, /parties, /roles, /kyc.
PUBLIC (no auth):
- POST /auth/otp/request {phone} → validate 10-digit Indian mobile; create otp_challenges doc {_id, phone, code_hash, expires_at(now+cfg.OTPTTL), attempts:0}; code via auth.GenerateNumericOTP(6), hash via auth.HMACHash(cfg.OTPHashSecret, phone, code). Also insert a notifications doc (mongodb.CollNotifications, domain.Notification, TemplateOTP, QUEUED) — the platformops worker "sends" it. If cfg.OTPDevMode: include dev_otp in the response.
- POST /auth/otp/verify {phone, otp} → load latest unexpired challenge; attempts>=5 → 429-style Forbidden; constant-time compare (auth.ConstantTimeEqual) else $inc attempts and 401. On success: delete challenges for phone; find-or-create Party (KYCTierMinimal, ACTIVE); return {access_token (session kind), refresh_token, party}. Refresh token: auth.RandomToken(32), store HMACHash(cfg.OTPHashSecret,"refresh",token) in refresh_tokens {token_hash, party_id, expires_at now+cfg.RefreshTokenTTL}.
- POST /auth/refresh {refresh_token} → lookup by hash; expired/missing → 401; ROTATE: delete old, issue new refresh + session access token.
AUTH (session or role) via RequireSession:
- POST /auth/logout {refresh_token} → delete token doc.
- GET /auth/roles → actor's role_assignments (status ACTIVE, usable now via ra.UsableAt) enriched with org unit name/type/code via d.Orgs.Get.
- POST /auth/role/select {role_assignment_id} → assignment must belong to actor + UsableAt(now); party KYC must satisfy domain.RequiredKYCTier[role] via domain.KYCTierSatisfies else 403 code KYC_TIER_INSUFFICIENT; return {access_token (role kind via d.JWT.IssueRoleToken, org type from d.Orgs)}.
- GET /parties/me → party + active assignments + latest kyc_records summary.
- PATCH /parties/me {full_name?, preferred_language?} → update own party.
KYC (RequireSession; mock DPI adapters clearly named as mocks in comments, real integration later):
- POST /kyc/aadhaar {aadhaar_number, consent:true, requested_tier "FARMER"|"STANDARD"} → NEVER store the number: keep last4 + vault ref uuid (Aadhaar Data Vault mock, §18-A); require consent=true → create consents doc (purpose AADHAAR_EKYC); create kyc_records VERIFIED (mock always succeeds); upgrade party.kyc_tier to requested tier (only upward, use domain.KYCTierSatisfies to avoid downgrade).
- POST /kyc/bank {account_number, ifsc} → mock penny-drop: bank_verified true, name match 0.92, store ONLY masked ****last4 + IFSC on latest kyc record (or create one).
- GET /kyc/me → own kyc records (masked fields only).
ROLE ADMIN via RequireRoles(SUPER_ADMIN, PCDF_ADMIN, UNION_PRESIDENT, SAMITI_ADHYAKSH):
- POST /roles/assignments {party_id|phone, role_code, org_unit_id, valid_from?, valid_to?} → role must be domain.IsValidRole; d.Orgs.RequireInScope(actor, org_unit_id); non-admin granters restricted: UNION_PRESIDENT may grant village/logistics/union-tier roles, SAMITI_ADHYAKSH may grant only FARMER/MILK_TESTER/LRP within own DCS; create ACTIVE assignment (granted_by=actor).
- DELETE /roles/assignments/{id} → status REVOKED + revoked_at/by (never delete the doc).
- GET /roles/assignments?org_unit_id=&role_code= → paged list, RequireInScope on org_unit_id.
No provenance events in this module. Unit test: role-grant permission matrix or KYC tier upgrade logic.

```text
27	// RateChart prices milk from fat/SNF, scoped to an org unit (union or
28	// federation). rate/L = BaseRatePerLitre + Fat%*FatRatePerPoint + SNF%*SNFRatePerPoint.
29	type RateChart struct {
30		ID               string    `bson:"_id"         json:"id"`
31		OrgUnitID        string    `bson:"org_unit_id" json:"org_unit_id"`
32		Name             string    `bson:"name"        json:"name"`
33		BaseRatePerLitre float64   `bson:"base_rate_per_litre" json:"base_rate_per_litre"`
34		FatRatePerPoint  float64   `bson:"fat_rate_per_point"  json:"fat_rate_per_point"`
35		SNFRatePerPoint  float64   `bson:"snf_rate_per_point"  json:"snf_rate_per_point"`
36		EffectiveFrom    time.Time `bson:"effective_from"      json:"effective_from"`
37		Active           bool      `bson:"active"      json:"active"`

39		CreatedAt        time.Time `bson:"created_at"  json:"created_at"`
40	}

42	// PricePour computes (ratePerLitre, amount) for a pour, rounded to paise.
43	func (rc RateChart) PricePour(fatPct, snfPct, qtyLitres float64) (rate, amount float64) {
44		rate = rc.BaseRatePerLitre + fatPct*rc.FatRatePerPoint + snfPct*rc.SNFRatePerPoint
45		rate = math.Round(rate*100) / 100
46		amount = math.Round(rate*qtyLitres*100) / 100
47		return rate, amount
48	}

92	// CheckPlausibility validates fat/SNF/qty against physical bounds and returns
93	// the violated flags (empty slice = plausible).
94	func CheckPlausibility(fatPct, snfPct, qtyLitres float64) []string {
95		var flags []string
96		if fatPct < PlausibleFatMin || fatPct > PlausibleFatMax ||
97			snfPct < PlausibleSNFMin || snfPct > PlausibleSNFMax {
98			flags = append(flags, IntegrityFlagImplausibleValue)
99		}
100		if qtyLitres != 0 && (qtyLitres < PlausibleQtyMin || qtyLitres > PlausibleQtyMax) {
101			flags = append(flags, IntegrityFlagImplausibleValue)
102		}
103		return flags
104	}

170	// DateKeyIST formats t as the YYYY-MM-DD settlement-day key in IST.
171	func DateKeyIST(t time.Time) string {
172		ist := time.FixedZone("IST", 5*3600+1800)
173		return t.In(ist).Format("2006-01-02")
174	}
```

```text
2	// invariants shared by every module. It has no behaviour beyond validation
3	// and no dependencies outside the standard library. This is the contract
4	// layer: modules depend on domain, never the other way around.
5	package domain
6	
7	// Role codes — the 23-role catalog from blueprint §5.2.

11		RoleFarmer         = "FARMER"
12		RoleSamitiSacheev  = "SAMITI_SACHEEV"  // DCS secretary — runs the collection console
13		RoleSamitiAdhyaksh = "SAMITI_ADHYAKSH" // DCS chairman — approvals & governance co-sign
14		RoleMilkTester     = "MILK_TESTER"
15		RoleLRP            = "LRP" // Local Resource Person (NDDB village extension)

21	
22		// Union tier

24		RoleUnionFieldSupervisor = "UNION_FIELD_SUPERVISOR"
25		RoleUnionPresident       = "UNION_PRESIDENT"
26	
27		// Plant tier
28		RolePlantOperator   = "PLANT_OPERATOR"
29		RolePlantLabAnalyst = "PLANT_LAB_ANALYST"
30	
31		// State / district tier
32		RolePCDFAdmin        = "PCDF_ADMIN"
33		RoleMissionOfficial  = "MISSION_OFFICIAL"
34		RoleDistrictVerifier = "DISTRICT_VERIFIER"
35	
36		// Health tier
37		RoleVeterinarian = "VETERINARIAN"
38		RoleMVUDriver    = "MVU_DRIVER"
39	
40		// Consumer tier
41		RoleConsumer = "CONSUMER"
42	
43		// Platform tier
44		RoleSupportAgent = "SUPPORT_AGENT"
45		RoleStateAuditor = "STATE_AUDITOR"
46		RoleSuperAdmin   = "SUPER_ADMIN"

52	// AllRoles is the closed set of grantable role codes.
53	var AllRoles = []string{
```

```text
29	// OrgUnit is a node in the cooperative hierarchy. Path holds the IDs of all
30	// ancestors from the root down to (and excluding) this node — kept denormalised
31	// so "is X inside Y's scope" is a single indexed array-containment check, with
32	// no recursive queries on the hot path.

39		Path      []string  `bson:"path"       json:"path"`
40		District  string    `bson:"district,omitempty"   json:"district,omitempty"`
41		State     string    `bson:"state,omitempty"      json:"state,omitempty"`
42		GeoLat    float64   `bson:"geo_lat,omitempty"    json:"geo_lat,omitempty"`
43		GeoLng    float64   `bson:"geo_lng,omitempty"    json:"geo_lng,omitempty"`
44		Active    bool      `bson:"active"     json:"active"`
45		CreatedAt time.Time `bson:"created_at" json:"created_at"`
46		UpdatedAt time.Time `bson:"updated_at" json:"updated_at"`
47	}
48	
49	// IsValidOrgType reports whether t is a known org-unit type.
50	func IsValidOrgType(t string) bool {
51		for _, v := range AllOrgTypes {
52			if v == t {
53				return true
54			}
55		}
56		return false
57	}
```

```text
130	// Parallel tier-1 proofs (FARMER vs STANDARD) satisfy each other.
131	func KYCTierSatisfies(have, need string) bool {
132		h, okH := kycRank[have]
133		n, okN := kycRank[need]

135			return false
136		}
137		return h >= n
138	}
```

```text
27	// RateChart prices milk from fat/SNF, scoped to an org unit (union or
28	// federation). rate/L = BaseRatePerLitre + Fat%*FatRatePerPoint + SNF%*SNFRatePerPoint.
29	type RateChart struct {
30		ID               string    `bson:"_id"         json:"id"`
31		OrgUnitID        string    `bson:"org_unit_id" json:"org_unit_id"`
32		Name             string    `bson:"name"        json:"name"`

35		SNFRatePerPoint  float64   `bson:"snf_rate_per_point"  json:"snf_rate_per_point"`

42	// PricePour computes (ratePerLitre, amount) for a pour, rounded to paise.
43	func (rc RateChart) PricePour(fatPct, snfPct, qtyLitres float64) (rate, amount float64) {
44		rate = rc.BaseRatePerLitre + fatPct*rc.FatRatePerPoint + snfPct*rc.SNFRatePerPoint
45		rate = math.Round(rate*100) / 100
46		amount = math.Round(rate*qtyLitres*100) / 100
47		return rate, amount
48	}

92	// CheckPlausibility validates fat/SNF/qty against physical bounds and returns
93	// the violated flags (empty slice = plausible).
94	func CheckPlausibility(fatPct, snfPct, qtyLitres float64) []string {
95		var flags []string
96		if fatPct < PlausibleFatMin || fatPct > PlausibleFatMax ||
97			snfPct < PlausibleSNFMin || snfPct > PlausibleSNFMax {
98			flags = append(flags, IntegrityFlagImplausibleValue)
99		}
100		if qtyLitres != 0 && (qtyLitres < PlausibleQtyMin || qtyLitres > PlausibleQtyMax) {
101			flags = append(flags, IntegrityFlagImplausibleValue)
102		}
103		return flags
104	}

170	// DateKeyIST formats t as the YYYY-MM-DD settlement-day key in IST.
171	func DateKeyIST(t time.Time) string {
172		ist := time.FixedZone("IST", 5*3600+1800)
173		return t.In(ist).Format("2006-01-02")
174	}
```

```text
1	package domain
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"time"
6	)
7	
8	// FSSAI limits for liquid milk (blueprint §8.3). Aflatoxin M1 is heat-stable
9	// and survives pasteurisation, so it MUST be gated upstream (BMC + plant),
10	// never only at the finished product.
11	const (
12		FSSAIAflatoxinM1MaxMicrogramPerKg = 0.5  // AFM1 ≤ 0.5 µg/kg
13		FSSAIColiformMaxCFUPerMl          = 10.0 // coliform ≤ 10 CFU/ml
14		FSSAITetracyclineMaxMgPerKg       = 0.1  // antibiotic MRL example
15	)
16	
17	// QC test names.
18	const (
19		TestAflatoxinM1  = "AFLATOXIN_M1"           // µg/kg
20		TestColiform     = "COLIFORM"               // CFU/ml
21		TestTPC          = "TPC"                    // CFU/ml, graded — recorded, not hard-gated here
22		TestAntibiotic   = "ANTIBIOTIC_TETRACYCLINE" // mg/kg
23		TestPhosphatase  = "PHOSPHATASE"            // 0 = negative (pass post-pasteurisation), 1 = positive
24		TestFat          = "FAT"                    // %
25		TestSNF          = "SNF"                    // %
26	)
27	
28	// QC stages.
29	const (
30		QCStageBMCRapid = "BMC_RAPID" // strip/rapid tests at the chilling centre
31		QCStagePlantLab = "PLANT_LAB" // full lab: ELISA/HPLC, culture, LC-MS/MS
32	)
33	
34	// QC subject types.
35	const (
36		QCSubjectDCSConsignment  = "DCS_CONSIGNMENT"
37		QCSubjectBMCLot          = "BMC_LOT"
38		QCSubjectProcessingBatch = "PROCESSING_BATCH"
39	)
40	
41	// QCTest is a single measurement inside a QC result.
42	type QCTest struct {
43		Name  string  `bson:"name"  json:"name"`
44		Value float64 `bson:"value" json:"value"`
45		Unit  string  `bson:"unit"  json:"unit"`
46		Pass  bool    `bson:"pass"  json:"pass"`
47	}
48	
49	// QCResult is the recorded outcome of testing one subject at one stage.
50	// OverallPass drives the safety gate; a certificate is attached to provenance
51	// on pass, a block + quarantine on fail.
52	type QCResult struct {
53		ID                string    `bson:"_id"          json:"id"`
54		SubjectType       string    `bson:"subject_type" json:"subject_type"`
55		SubjectID         string    `bson:"subject_id"   json:"subject_id"`
56		Stage             string    `bson:"stage"        json:"stage"`
57		Tests             []QCTest  `bson:"tests"        json:"tests"`
58		OverallPass       bool      `bson:"overall_pass" json:"overall_pass"`
59		FailureReasons    []string  `bson:"failure_reasons,omitempty" json:"failure_reasons,omitempty"`
60		AnalystPartyID    string    `bson:"analyst_party_id" json:"analyst_party_id"`
61		LabRef            string    `bson:"lab_ref,omitempty"            json:"lab_ref,omitempty"`
62		CertificateNumber string    `bson:"certificate_number,omitempty" json:"certificate_number,omitempty"`
63		RecordedAt        time.Time `bson:"recorded_at"  json:"recorded_at"`
64		ProvenanceSeq     int64     `bson:"provenance_seq,omitempty" json:"provenance_seq,omitempty"`
65	}
66	
67	// EvaluateQCTests applies the FSSAI gate to a set of tests: it fills each
68	// test's Pass verdict and returns the overall verdict plus human-readable
69	// failure reasons. Unknown test names are recorded but do not gate.
70	func EvaluateQCTests(tests []QCTest) (overallPass bool, failures []string, evaluated []QCTest) {
71		overallPass = true
72		evaluated = make([]QCTest, 0, len(tests))
73		for _, t := range tests {
74			pass := true
75			switch t.Name {
76			case TestAflatoxinM1:
77				if t.Value > FSSAIAflatoxinM1MaxMicrogramPerKg {
78					pass = false
79					failures = append(failures, fmt.Sprintf(
80						"AFLATOXIN_M1 %.3f µg/kg exceeds FSSAI limit %.1f µg/kg", t.Value, FSSAIAflatoxinM1MaxMicrogramPerKg))
81				}
82			case TestColiform:
83				if t.Value > FSSAIColiformMaxCFUPerMl {
84					pass = false
85					failures = append(failures, fmt.Sprintf(
86						"COLIFORM %.1f CFU/ml exceeds FSSAI limit %.0f CFU/ml", t.Value, FSSAIColiformMaxCFUPerMl))
87				}
88			case TestAntibiotic:
89				if t.Value > FSSAITetracyclineMaxMgPerKg {
90					pass = false
91					failures = append(failures, fmt.Sprintf(
92						"ANTIBIOTIC_TETRACYCLINE %.3f mg/kg exceeds MRL %.1f mg/kg", t.Value, FSSAITetracyclineMaxMgPerKg))
93				}
94			case TestPhosphatase:
95				if t.Value != 0 {
96					pass = false
97					failures = append(failures, "PHOSPHATASE positive — pasteurisation check failed (must be negative)")
98				}
99			}
100			t.Pass = pass
101			if !pass {
102				overallPass = false
103			}
104			evaluated = append(evaluated, t)
105		}
106		return overallPass, failures, evaluated
107	}
108
```

```text
24		OrgTypeProcessingPlant: {OrgTypeMilkUnion, OrgTypeFederation},

29	// OrgUnit is a node in the cooperative hierarchy. Path holds the IDs of all

31	// so "is X inside Y's scope" is a single indexed array-containment check, with
32	// no recursive queries on the hot path.

41		State     string    `bson:"state,omitempty"      json:"state,omitempty"`
```

```text
123		KYCTierRider:    2,

129	// KYCTierSatisfies reports whether a party at tier `have` meets `need`.
130	// Parallel tier-1 proofs (FARMER vs STANDARD) satisfy each other.
131	func KYCTierSatisfies(have, need string) bool {
132		h, okH := kycRank[have]
133		n, okN := kycRank[need]
134		if !okH || !okN {
135			return false
136		}
137		return h >= n
138	}
```

```text
24		PlausibleQtyMax = 200.0 // litres per pour
25	)
26	
27	// RateChart prices milk from fat/SNF, scoped to an org unit (union or
28	// federation). rate/L = BaseRatePerLitre + Fat%*FatRatePerPoint + SNF%*SNFRatePerPoint.
29	type RateChart struct {
30		ID               string    `bson:"_id"         json:"id"`
31		OrgUnitID        string    `bson:"org_unit_id" json:"org_unit_id"`
32		Name             string    `bson:"name"        json:"name"`

34		FatRatePerPoint  float64   `bson:"fat_rate_per_point"  json:"fat_rate_per_point"`
35		SNFRatePerPoint  float64   `bson:"snf_rate_per_point"  json:"snf_rate_per_point"`

42	// PricePour computes (ratePerLitre, amount) for a pour, rounded to paise.
43	func (rc RateChart) PricePour(fatPct, snfPct, qtyLitres float64) (rate, amount float64) {
44		rate = rc.BaseRatePerLitre + fatPct*rc.FatRatePerPoint + snfPct*rc.SNFRatePerPoint
45		rate = math.Round(rate*100) / 100
46		amount = math.Round(rate*qtyLitres*100) / 100
47		return rate, amount
48	}
49	
50	// Analyzer reading ingestion modes (blueprint §8.2): direct device integration
51	// is the tamper-resistant end-state; photo-OCR is the legacy bridge.

92	// CheckPlausibility validates fat/SNF/qty against physical bounds and returns
93	// the violated flags (empty slice = plausible).
94	func CheckPlausibility(fatPct, snfPct, qtyLitres float64) []string {
95		var flags []string
96		if fatPct < PlausibleFatMin || fatPct > PlausibleFatMax ||
97			snfPct < PlausibleSNFMin || snfPct > PlausibleSNFMax {
98			flags = append(flags, IntegrityFlagImplausibleValue)
99		}
100		if qtyLitres != 0 && (qtyLitres < PlausibleQtyMin || qtyLitres > PlausibleQtyMax) {
101			flags = append(flags, IntegrityFlagImplausibleValue)
102		}
103		return flags
104	}
```

```text
43	func (rc RateChart) PricePour(fatPct, snfPct, qtyLitres float64) (rate, amount float64) {
44		rate = rc.BaseRatePerLitre + fatPct*rc.FatRatePerPoint + snfPct*rc.SNFRatePerPoint

92	// CheckPlausibility validates fat/SNF/qty against physical bounds and returns
93	// the violated flags (empty slice = plausible).
94	func CheckPlausibility(fatPct, snfPct, qtyLitres float64) []string {
95		var flags []string
96		if fatPct < PlausibleFatMin || fatPct > PlausibleFatMax ||
97			snfPct < PlausibleSNFMin || snfPct > PlausibleSNFMax {
98			flags = append(flags, IntegrityFlagImplausibleValue)
99		}
100		if qtyLitres != 0 && (qtyLitres < PlausibleQtyMin || qtyLitres > PlausibleQtyMax) {
101			flags = append(flags, IntegrityFlagImplausibleValue)
102		}
103		return flags
104	}
```

```text
1	// Package domain holds the pure entity model of Saathi — structs, enums and
2	// invariants shared by every module. It has no behaviour beyond validation
3	// and no dependencies outside the standard library. This is the contract
4	// layer: modules depend on domain, never the other way around.
5	package domain
6	
7	// Role codes — the 23-role catalog from blueprint §5.2.
8	// A Party may hold many time-bounded, org-scoped RoleAssignments.
9	const (
10		// Village tier
11		RoleFarmer         = "FARMER"
12		RoleSamitiSacheev  = "SAMITI_SACHEEV"  // DCS secretary — runs the collection console
13		RoleSamitiAdhyaksh = "SAMITI_ADHYAKSH" // DCS chairman — approvals & governance co-sign
14		RoleMilkTester     = "MILK_TESTER"
15		RoleLRP            = "LRP" // Local Resource Person (NDDB village extension)
16		RoleAITech         = "AI_TECH"
17	
18		// Logistics tier
19		RoleVanRider      = "VAN_RIDER"
20		RoleDeliveryRider = "DELIVERY_RIDER"
21	
22		// Union tier
23		RoleBMCOperator          = "BMC_OPERATOR"
24		RoleUnionFieldSupervisor = "UNION_FIELD_SUPERVISOR"
25		RoleUnionPresident       = "UNION_PRESIDENT"
26	
27		// Plant tier
28		RolePlantOperator   = "PLANT_OPERATOR"
29		RolePlantLabAnalyst = "PLANT_LAB_ANALYST"
30	
31		// State / district tier
32		RolePCDFAdmin        = "PCDF_ADMIN"
33		RoleMissionOfficial  = "MISSION_OFFICIAL"
34		RoleDistrictVerifier = "DISTRICT_VERIFIER"
35	
36		// Health tier
37		RoleVeterinarian = "VETERINARIAN"
38		RoleMVUDriver    = "MVU_DRIVER"
39	
40		// Consumer tier
41		RoleConsumer = "CONSUMER"
42	
43		// Platform tier
44		RoleSupportAgent = "SUPPORT_AGENT"
45		RoleStateAuditor = "STATE_AUDITOR"
46		RoleSuperAdmin   = "SUPER_ADMIN"
47	
48		// System tier
49		RoleServiceAccount = "SERVICE_ACCOUNT"
50	)
51	
52	// AllRoles is the closed set of grantable role codes.
53	var AllRoles = []string{
54		RoleFarmer, RoleSamitiSacheev, RoleSamitiAdhyaksh, RoleMilkTester, RoleLRP, RoleAITech,
55		RoleVanRider, RoleDeliveryRider,
56		RoleBMCOperator, RoleUnionFieldSupervisor, RoleUnionPresident,
57		RolePlantOperator, RolePlantLabAnalyst,
58		RolePCDFAdmin, RoleMissionOfficial, RoleDistrictVerifier,
59		RoleVeterinarian, RoleMVUDriver,
60		RoleConsumer,
61		RoleSupportAgent, RoleStateAuditor, RoleSuperAdmin,
62		RoleServiceAccount,
63	}
64	
65	var roleSet = func() map[string]struct{} {
66		s := make(map[string]struct{}, len(AllRoles))
67		for _, r := range AllRoles {
68			s[r] = struct{}{}
69		}
70		return s
71	}()
72	
73	// IsValidRole reports whether code is one of the 23 catalog roles.
74	func IsValidRole(code string) bool {
75		_, ok := roleSet[code]
76		return ok
77	}
78	
79	// KYC assurance tiers (blueprint §4.2). Higher tiers unlock higher-trust roles.
80	const (
81		KYCTierMinimal  = "MINIMAL"  // mobile OTP only (consumer)
82		KYCTierFarmer   = "FARMER"   // Aadhaar OTP eKYC or offline XML + penny-drop
83		KYCTierStandard = "STANDARD" // Aadhaar eKYC
84		KYCTierRider    = "RIDER"    // Aadhaar eKYC + DL/RC
85		KYCTierHigh     = "HIGH"     // eKYC + org record / V-CIP for officials
86		KYCTierHighest  = "HIGHEST"  // platform admin: MFA + dual-control
87		KYCTierService  = "SERVICE"  // machine accounts: mTLS / scoped keys
88	)
89	
90	// RequiredKYCTier maps each role to the minimum KYC tier demanded before the
91	// role assignment becomes usable (blueprint §5.2 "KYC tier" column).
92	var RequiredKYCTier = map[string]string{
93		RoleFarmer:               KYCTierFarmer,
94		RoleSamitiSacheev:        KYCTierHigh,
95		RoleSamitiAdhyaksh:       KYCTierHigh,
96		RoleMilkTester:           KYCTierStandard,
97		RoleLRP:                  KYCTierStandard,
98		RoleAITech:               KYCTierStandard,
99		RoleVanRider:             KYCTierRider,
100		RoleDeliveryRider:        KYCTierRider,
101		RoleBMCOperator:          KYCTierStandard,
102		RoleUnionFieldSupervisor: KYCTierHigh,
103		RoleUnionPresident:       KYCTierHigh,
104		RolePlantOperator:        KYCTierHigh,
105		RolePlantLabAnalyst:      KYCTierHigh,
106		RolePCDFAdmin:            KYCTierHigh,
107		RoleMissionOfficial:      KYCTierHigh,
108		RoleDistrictVerifier:     KYCTierHigh,
109		RoleVeterinarian:         KYCTierHigh,
110		RoleMVUDriver:            KYCTierStandard,
111		RoleConsumer:             KYCTierMinimal,
112		RoleSupportAgent:         KYCTierHigh,
113		RoleStateAuditor:         KYCTierHigh,
114		RoleSuperAdmin:           KYCTierHighest,
115		RoleServiceAccount:       KYCTierService,
116	}

118	// kycRank orders tiers so "tier X satisfies requirement Y" is a comparison.
119	var kycRank = map[string]int{
120		KYCTierMinimal:  0,
121		KYCTierFarmer:   1,
122		KYCTierStandard: 1, // Farmer and Standard are parallel tier-1 proofs
123		KYCTierRider:    2,
124		KYCTierHigh:     3,
125		KYCTierHighest:  4,
126		KYCTierService:  4,
127	}
128	
129	// KYCTierSatisfies reports whether a party at tier `have` meets `need`.
130	// Parallel tier-1 proofs (FARMER vs STANDARD) satisfy each other.
131	func KYCTierSatisfies(have, need string) bool {
132		h, okH := kycRank[have]
133		n, okN := kycRank[need]
134		if !okH || !okN {
135			return false
136		}
137		return h >= n
138	}
```

```text
47	// UsableAt reports whether the assignment is active and inside its validity
48	// window at instant t.
49	func (ra RoleAssignment) UsableAt(t time.Time) bool {
50		if ra.Status != RoleAssignmentActive {
51			return false
52		}
53		if t.Before(ra.ValidFrom) {
54			return false
55		}
56		if ra.ValidTo != nil && t.After(*ra.ValidTo) {
57			return false
58		}
59		return true
60	}
```

```text
1	// Package httpx is the HTTP toolkit shared by every module: typed errors,
2	// uniform JSON envelopes, strict request decoding, pagination.
3	package httpx
4	
5	import (
6		"fmt"
7		"net/http"
8	)
9	
10	// AppError is the single error type handlers return. It carries the HTTP
11	// status plus a stable machine-readable code the frontend can switch on.
12	type AppError struct {
13		Status  int    `json:"-"`
14		Code    string `json:"code"`
15		Message string `json:"message"`
16		Details any    `json:"details,omitempty"`
17	
18		cause error // wrapped internal error — logged server-side, never serialised
19	}
20	
21	func (e *AppError) Error() string {
22		return fmt.Sprintf("%d %s: %s", e.Status, e.Code, e.Message)
23	}
24	
25	// WithDetails returns a copy carrying extra structured context.
26	func (e *AppError) WithDetails(d any) *AppError {
27		cp := *e
28		cp.Details = d
29		return &cp
30	}
31	
32	func newErr(status int, code, msg string) *AppError {
33		return &AppError{Status: status, Code: code, Message: msg}
34	}
35	
36	// Constructors — use these instead of raw errors in handlers/services.
37	
38	func BadRequest(code, msg string) *AppError { return newErr(http.StatusBadRequest, code, msg) }
39	
40	func Unauthorized(msg string) *AppError { return newErr(http.StatusUnauthorized, "UNAUTHORIZED", msg) }
41	
42	func Forbidden(msg string) *AppError { return newErr(http.StatusForbidden, "FORBIDDEN", msg) }
43	
44	func NotFound(resource string) *AppError {
45		return newErr(http.StatusNotFound, "NOT_FOUND", resource+" not found")
46	}
47	
48	func Conflict(code, msg string) *AppError { return newErr(http.StatusConflict, code, msg) }
49	
50	func Unprocessable(code, msg string) *AppError {
51		return newErr(http.StatusUnprocessableEntity, code, msg)
52	}
53	
54	func TooManyRequests(msg string) *AppError {
55		return newErr(http.StatusTooManyRequests, "RATE_LIMITED", msg)
56	}
57	
58	// Internal wraps an unexpected error. The cause is logged server-side but
59	// never leaked to the client.
60	func Internal(err error) *AppError {
61		e := newErr(http.StatusInternalServerError, "INTERNAL", "internal server error")
62		e.cause = err
63		return e
64	}
65	
66	func (e *AppError) Unwrap() error { return e.cause }
67
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
10	// envelope is the uniform success shape: {"data": ..., "meta": {...}?}.
11	type envelope struct {
12		Data any `json:"data"`
13		Meta any `json:"meta,omitempty"`
14	}
15	
16	type errEnvelope struct {
17		Error *AppError `json:"error"`
18	}
19	
20	// JSON writes a success response wrapped in the standard envelope.
21	func JSON(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, data any) {
22		writeJSON(w, status, envelope{Data: data})
23	}
24	
25	// JSONMeta writes a success response with list metadata (pagination etc.).
26	func JSONMeta(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, data, meta any) {
27		writeJSON(w, status, envelope{Data: data, Meta: meta})
28	}
29	
30	// Error writes the standard error envelope. Unexpected (non-AppError) errors
31	// become an opaque 500 and the cause is logged with the request context.
32	func Error(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, err error) {
33		var ae *AppError
34		if !errors.As(err, &ae) {
35			ae = Internal(err)
36		}
37		if ae.Status >= 500 {
38			slog.ErrorContext(r.Context(), "request failed",
39				slog.String("method", r.Method),
40				slog.String("path", r.URL.Path),
41				slog.String("code", ae.Code),
42				slog.Any("cause", ae.CauseOrSelf()),
43			)
44		}
45		writeJSON(w, ae.Status, errEnvelope{Error: ae})
46	}
47	
48	// CauseOrSelf returns the wrapped cause if present, else the error itself.
49	func (e *AppError) CauseOrSelf() error {
50		if e.cause != nil {
51			return e.cause
52		}
53		return e
54	}
55	
56	func writeJSON(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, v any) {
57		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json; charset=utf-8")
58		w.WriteHeader(status)
59		_ = json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(v)
60	}
61
```

```text
1	package httpx
2	
3	import (
4		"encoding/json"
5		"errors"
6		"fmt"
7		"io"
8		"net/http"
9		"strconv"
10	)
11	
12	// maxBodyBytes caps request bodies at 1 MiB — pours, readings and admin
13	// payloads are all tiny; photo evidence goes to the object store, not the API.
14	const maxBodyBytes = 1 << 20
15	
16	// DecodeJSON strictly decodes the request body into dst. It enforces the
17	// size cap and exactly one JSON value.
18	func DecodeJSON(r *http.Request, dst any) error {
19		r.Body = http.MaxBytesReader(nil, r.Body, maxBodyBytes)
20		dec := json.NewDecoder(r.Body)
21		if err := dec.Decode(dst); err != nil {
22			var maxErr *http.MaxBytesError
23			switch {
24			case errors.As(err, &maxErr):
25				return BadRequest("BODY_TOO_LARGE", fmt.Sprintf("request body exceeds %d bytes", maxBodyBytes))
26			case errors.Is(err, io.EOF):
27				return BadRequest("EMPTY_BODY", "request body is required")
28			default:
29				return BadRequest("MALFORMED_JSON", "request body is not valid JSON: "+err.Error())
30			}
31		}
32		if dec.More() {
33			return BadRequest("MALFORMED_JSON", "request body must contain a single JSON value")
34		}
35		return nil
36	}
37	
38	// Page holds validated pagination parameters.
39	type Page struct {
40		Limit  int64 `json:"limit"`
41		Offset int64 `json:"offset"`
42	}
43	
44	// ParsePage reads ?limit= and ?offset= with sane bounds (default 50, max 200).
45	func ParsePage(r *http.Request) Page {
46		p := Page{Limit: 50, Offset: 0}
47		if v := r.URL.Query().Get("limit"); v != "" {
48			if n, err := strconv.ParseInt(v, 10, 64); err == nil && n > 0 {
49				p.Limit = min(n, 200)
50			}
51		}
52		if v := r.URL.Query().Get("offset"); v != "" {
53			if n, err := strconv.ParseInt(v, 10, 64); err == nil && n >= 0 {
54				p.Offset = n
55			}
56		}
57		return p
58	}
59
```

```text
1	// Package httpx is the HTTP toolkit shared by every module: typed errors,
2	// uniform JSON envelopes, strict request decoding, pagination.
3	package httpx
4	
5	import (
6		"fmt"
7		"net/http"
8	)
9	
10	// AppError is the single error type handlers return. It carries the HTTP
11	// status plus a stable machine-readable code the frontend can switch on.
12	type AppError struct {
13		Status  int    `json:"-"`
14		Code    string `json:"code"`
15		Message string `json:"message"`
16		Details any    `json:"details,omitempty"`
17	
18		cause error // wrapped internal error — logged server-side, never serialised
19	}
20	
21	func (e *AppError) Error() string {
22		return fmt.Sprintf("%d %s: %s", e.Status, e.Code, e.Message)
23	}
24	
25	// WithDetails returns a copy carrying extra structured context.
26	func (e *AppError) WithDetails(d any) *AppError {
27		cp := *e
28		cp.Details = d
29		return &cp
30	}
31	
32	func newErr(status int, code, msg string) *AppError {
33		return &AppError{Status: status, Code: code, Message: msg}
34	}
35	
36	// Constructors — use these instead of raw errors in handlers/services.
37	
38	func BadRequest(code, msg string) *AppError { return newErr(http.StatusBadRequest, code, msg) }
39	
40	func Unauthorized(msg string) *AppError { return newErr(http.StatusUnauthorized, "UNAUTHORIZED", msg) }
41	
42	func Forbidden(msg string) *AppError { return newErr(http.StatusForbidden, "FORBIDDEN", msg) }
43	
44	func NotFound(resource string) *AppError {
45		return newErr(http.StatusNotFound, "NOT_FOUND", resource+" not found")
46	}
47	
48	func Conflict(code, msg string) *AppError { return newErr(http.StatusConflict, code, msg) }
49	
50	func Unprocessable(code, msg string) *AppError {
51		return newErr(http.StatusUnprocessableEntity, code, msg)
52	}
53	
54	func TooManyRequests(msg string) *AppError {
55		return newErr(http.StatusTooManyRequests, "RATE_LIMITED", msg)
56	}
57	
58	// Internal wraps an unexpected error. The cause is logged server-side but
59	// never leaked to the client.
60	func Internal(err error) *AppError {
61		e := newErr(http.StatusInternalServerError, "INTERNAL", "internal server error")
62		e.cause = err
63		return e
64	}
65	
66	func (e *AppError) Unwrap() error { return e.cause }
67
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
36	// Constructors — use these instead of raw errors in handlers/services.
37	
38	func BadRequest(code, msg string) *AppError { return newErr(http.StatusBadRequest, code, msg) }
39	
40	func Unauthorized(msg string) *AppError { return newErr(http.StatusUnauthorized, "UNAUTHORIZED", msg) }
41	
42	func Forbidden(msg string) *AppError { return newErr(http.StatusForbidden, "FORBIDDEN", msg) }
43	
44	func NotFound(resource string) *AppError {
45		return newErr(http.StatusNotFound, "NOT_FOUND", resource+" not found")
46	}
47	
48	func Conflict(code, msg string) *AppError { return newErr(http.StatusConflict, code, msg) }
49	
50	func Unprocessable(code, msg string) *AppError {
51		return newErr(http.StatusUnprocessableEntity, code, msg)
52	}
53	
54	func TooManyRequests(msg string) *AppError {
55		return newErr(http.StatusTooManyRequests, "RATE_LIMITED", msg)
56	}
57	
58	// Internal wraps an unexpected error. The cause is logged server-side but
59	// never leaked to the client.
60	func Internal(err error) *AppError {
61		e := newErr(http.StatusInternalServerError, "INTERNAL", "internal server error")
62		e.cause = err
63		return e
64	}
65	
66	func (e *AppError) Unwrap() error { return e.cause }
67
```

```text
32	// update — never an account deletion (blueprint §4.1).

39		ValidFrom time.Time  `bson:"valid_from"  json:"valid_from"`
40		ValidTo   *time.Time `bson:"valid_to,omitempty"   json:"valid_to,omitempty"` // nil = open-ended
41		Status    string     `bson:"status"      json:"status"`
42		RevokedAt *time.Time `bson:"revoked_at,omitempty" json:"revoked_at,omitempty"`
43		RevokedBy string     `bson:"revoked_by,omitempty" json:"revoked_by,omitempty"`
44		CreatedAt time.Time  `bson:"created_at"  json:"created_at"`
45	}

47	// UsableAt reports whether the assignment is active and inside its validity
48	// window at instant t.
49	func (ra RoleAssignment) UsableAt(t time.Time) bool {
50		if ra.Status != RoleAssignmentActive {
51			return false
52		}

54			return false
```

 `./internal/platform/httpx/decode.go`

```text
1	package httpx
2	
3	import (
4		"encoding/json"
5		"errors"
6		"fmt"
7		"io"
8		"net/http"
9		"strconv"
10	)
11	
12	// maxBodyBytes caps request bodies at 1 MiB — pours, readings and admin
13	// payloads are all tiny; photo evidence goes to the object store, not the API.
14	const maxBodyBytes = 1 << 20
15	
16	// DecodeJSON strictly decodes the request body into dst. It enforces the
17	// size cap and exactly one JSON value.
18	func DecodeJSON(r *http.Request, dst any) error {
19		r.Body = http.MaxBytesReader(nil, r.Body, maxBodyBytes)
20		dec := json.NewDecoder(r.Body)
21		if err := dec.Decode(dst); err != nil {
22			var maxErr *http.MaxBytesError
23			switch {
24			case errors.As(err, &maxErr):
25				return BadRequest("BODY_TOO_LARGE", fmt.Sprintf("request body exceeds %d bytes", maxBodyBytes))
26			case errors.Is(err, io.EOF):
27				return BadRequest("EMPTY_BODY", "request body is required")
28			default:
29				return BadRequest("MALFORMED_JSON", "request body is not valid JSON: "+err.Error())
30			}
31		}
32		if dec.More() {
33			return BadRequest("MALFORMED_JSON", "request body must contain a single JSON value")
34		}
35		return nil
36	}
37	
38	// Page holds validated pagination parameters.
39	type Page struct {
40		Limit  int64 `json:"limit"`
41		Offset int64 `json:"offset"`
42	}
43	
44	// ParsePage reads ?limit= and ?offset= with sane bounds (default 50, max 200).
45	func ParsePage(r *http.Request) Page {
46		p := Page{Limit: 50, Offset: 0}
47		if v := r.URL.Query().Get("limit"); v != "" {
48			if n, err := strconv.ParseInt(v, 10, 64); err == nil && n > 0 {
49				p.Limit = min(n, 200)
50			}
51		}
52		if v := r.URL.Query().Get("offset"); v != "" {
53			if n, err := strconv.ParseInt(v, 10, 64); err == nil && n >= 0 {
54				p.Offset = n
55			}
56		}
57		return p
58	}
59
```

```text
1	// Package httpx is the HTTP toolkit shared by every module: typed errors,
2	// uniform JSON envelopes, strict request decoding, pagination.
3	package httpx
4	
5	import (
6		"fmt"
7		"net/http"
8	)
9	
10	// AppError is the single error type handlers return. It carries the HTTP
11	// status plus a stable machine-readable code the frontend can switch on.
12	type AppError struct {
13		Status  int    `json:"-"`
14		Code    string `json:"code"`
15		Message string `json:"message"`
16		Details any    `json:"details,omitempty"`
17	
18		cause error // wrapped internal error — logged server-side, never serialised
19	}
20	
21	func (e *AppError) Error() string {
22		return fmt.Sprintf("%d %s: %s", e.Status, e.Code, e.Message)
23	}
24	
25	// WithDetails returns a copy carrying extra structured context.
26	func (e *AppError) WithDetails(d any) *AppError {
27		cp := *e
28		cp.Details = d
29		return &cp
30	}
31	
32	func newErr(status int, code, msg string) *AppError {
33		return &AppError{Status: status, Code: code, Message: msg}
34	}
35	
36	// Constructors — use these instead of raw errors in handlers/services.
37	
38	func BadRequest(code, msg string) *AppError { return newErr(http.StatusBadRequest, code, msg) }
39	
40	func Unauthorized(msg string) *AppError { return newErr(http.StatusUnauthorized, "UNAUTHORIZED", msg) }
41	
42	func Forbidden(msg string) *AppError { return newErr(http.StatusForbidden, "FORBIDDEN", msg) }
43	
44	func NotFound(resource string) *AppError {
45		return newErr(http.StatusNotFound, "NOT_FOUND", resource+" not found")
46	}
47	
48	func Conflict(code, msg string) *AppError { return newErr(http.StatusConflict, code, msg) }
49	
50	func Unprocessable(code, msg string) *AppError {
51		return newErr(http.StatusUnprocessableEntity, code, msg)
52	}
53	
54	func TooManyRequests(msg string) *AppError {
55		return newErr(http.StatusTooManyRequests, "RATE_LIMITED", msg)
56	}
57	
58	// Internal wraps an unexpected error. The cause is logged server-side but
59	// never leaked to the client.
60	func Internal(err error) *AppError {
```

```text
1	package httpx
2	
3	import (
4		"encoding/json"
5		"errors"
6		"fmt"
7		"io"
8		"net/http"
9		"strconv"
10	)
11	
12	// maxBodyBytes caps request bodies at 1 MiB — pours, readings and admin
13	// payloads are all tiny; photo evidence goes to the object store, not the API.
14	const maxBodyBytes = 1 << 20
15	
16	// DecodeJSON strictly decodes the request body into dst. It enforces the
17	// size cap and exactly one JSON value.
18	func DecodeJSON(r *http.Request, dst any) error {
19		r.Body = http.MaxBytesReader(nil, r.Body, maxBodyBytes)
20		dec := json.NewDecoder(r.Body)
21		if err := dec.Decode(dst); err != nil {
22			var maxErr *http.MaxBytesError
23			switch {
24			case errors.As(err, &maxErr):
25				return BadRequest("BODY_TOO_LARGE", fmt.Sprintf("request body exceeds %d bytes", maxBodyBytes))
26			case errors.Is(err, io.EOF):
27				return BadRequest("EMPTY_BODY", "request body is required")
28			default:
29				return BadRequest("MALFORMED_JSON", "request body is not valid JSON: "+err.Error())
30			}
31		}
32		if dec.More() {
33			return BadRequest("MALFORMED_JSON", "request body must contain a single JSON value")
34		}
35		return nil
36	}
37	
38	// Page holds validated pagination parameters.
39	type Page struct {
40		Limit  int64 `json:"limit"`
41		Offset int64 `json:"offset"`
42	}
43	
44	// ParsePage reads ?limit= and ?offset= with sane bounds (default 50, max 200).
45	func ParsePage(r *http.Request) Page {
46		p := Page{Limit: 50, Offset: 0}
47		if v := r.URL.Query().Get("limit"); v != "" {
48			if n, err := strconv.ParseInt(v, 10, 64); err == nil && n > 0 {
49				p.Limit = min(n, 200)
50			}
51		}
52		if v := r.URL.Query().Get("offset"); v != "" {
53			if n, err := strconv.ParseInt(v, 10, 64); err == nil && n >= 0 {
54				p.Offset = n
55			}
56		}
57		return p
58	}
59
```

```text
1	package httpx
2	
3	import (
4		"encoding/json"
5		"errors"
6		"log/slog"
7		"net/http"
8	)
9	
10	// envelope is the uniform success shape: {"data": ..., "meta": {...}?}.
11	type envelope struct {
12		Data any `json:"data"`
13		Meta any `json:"meta,omitempty"`
14	}
15	
16	type errEnvelope struct {
17		Error *AppError `json:"error"`
18	}
19	
20	// JSON writes a success response wrapped in the standard envelope.
21	func JSON(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, data any) {
22		writeJSON(w, status, envelope{Data: data})
23	}
24	
25	// JSONMeta writes a success response with list metadata (pagination etc.).
26	func JSONMeta(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, data, meta any) {
27		writeJSON(w, status, envelope{Data: data, Meta: meta})
28	}
29	
30	// Error writes the standard error envelope. Unexpected (non-AppError) errors
31	// become an opaque 500 and the cause is logged with the request context.
32	func Error(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, err error) {
33		var ae *AppError
34		if !errors.As(err, &ae) {
35			ae = Internal(err)
36		}
37		if ae.Status >= 500 {
38			slog.ErrorContext(r.Context(), "request failed",
39				slog.String("method", r.Method),
40				slog.String("path", r.URL.Path),
41				slog.String("code", ae.Code),
42				slog.Any("cause", ae.CauseOrSelf()),
43			)
44		}
45		writeJSON(w, ae.Status, errEnvelope{Error: ae})
46	}
47	
48	// CauseOrSelf returns the wrapped cause if present, else the error itself.
49	func (e *AppError) CauseOrSelf() error {
50		if e.cause != nil {
51			return e.cause
52		}
53		return e
54	}
55	
56	func writeJSON(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, v any) {
57		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json; charset=utf-8")
58		w.WriteHeader(status)
59		_ = json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(v)
60	}
61
```

```text
91	// role assignment becomes usable (blueprint §5.2 "KYC tier" column).

118	// kycRank orders tiers so "tier X satisfies requirement Y" is a comparison.
119	var kycRank = map[string]int{

122		KYCTierStandard: 1, // Farmer and Standard are parallel tier-1 proofs
123		KYCTierRider:    2,

129	// KYCTierSatisfies reports whether a party at tier `have` meets `need`.
130	// Parallel tier-1 proofs (FARMER vs STANDARD) satisfy each other.
131	func KYCTierSatisfies(have, need string) bool {
132		h, okH := kycRank[have]
133		n, okN := kycRank[need]
134		if !okH || !okN {
135			return false
136		}
137		return h >= n
138	}
```

```text
1	// Package middleware carries the cross-cutting HTTP concerns: token
2	// authentication, role enforcement, audit capture, per-IP rate limiting,
3	// Prometheus metrics.
4	package middleware
5	
6	import (
7		"net/http"
8		"strings"
9	
10		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/auth"
11		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/httpx"
12	)
13	
14	// Authenticate verifies the Bearer token and installs the Actor on the
15	// request context. Requests without a valid token are rejected — public
16	// routes simply don't mount this middleware.
17	func Authenticate(jwtm *auth.JWTManager) func(http.Handler) http.Handler {
18		return func(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
19			return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
20				header := r.Header.Get("Authorization")
21				token, ok := strings.CutPrefix(header, "Bearer ")
22				if !ok || token == "" {
23					httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Unauthorized("missing bearer token"))
24					return
25				}
26				claims, err := jwtm.Parse(token)
27				if err != nil {
28					httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Unauthorized("invalid or expired token"))
29					return
30				}
31				actor := auth.Actor{
32					PartyID:          claims.PartyID,
33					Phone:            claims.Phone,
34					KYCTier:          claims.KYCTier,
35					Kind:             claims.Kind,
36					RoleAssignmentID: claims.RoleAssignmentID,
37					RoleCode:         claims.RoleCode,
38					OrgUnitID:        claims.OrgUnitID,
39					OrgType:          claims.OrgType,
40				}
41				next.ServeHTTP(w, r.WithContext(auth.WithActor(r.Context(), actor)))
42			})
43		}
44	}
45
```

```text
1	// Package provenance implements the append-only, hash-chained event ledger —
2	// the source of truth for milk traceability (blueprint §7). Every link in the
3	// pour→QR chain is an immutable Event whose SHA-256 hash covers the previous
4	// event's hash, so history cannot be quietly rewritten (tamper-evidence,
5	// FSSAI recall-grade audit).
6	//
7	// Corrections are NEW events referencing the superseded entity — nothing is
8	// ever updated or deleted in this collection.
9	package provenance
10	
11	import (
12		"context"
13		"crypto/sha256"
14		"encoding/hex"
15		"encoding/json"
16		"errors"
17		"fmt"
18		"strconv"
19		"strings"
20		"time"
21	
22		"github.com/google/uuid"
23		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson"
24		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo"
25		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo/options"
26	)
27	
28	const collection = "provenance_events"
29	
30	// Ref is a directed edge to another entity in the trace graph
31	// (e.g. a consignment event referencing the pours it aggregates).
32	type Ref struct {
33		EntityType string `bson:"entity_type" json:"entity_type"`
34		EntityID   string `bson:"entity_id"   json:"entity_id"`
35		Relation   string `bson:"relation"    json:"relation"` // aggregates | supersedes | tested | yields | labels ...
36	}
37	
38	// ActorRef records who caused the event.
39	type ActorRef struct {
40		PartyID  string `bson:"party_id"  json:"party_id"`
41		RoleCode string `bson:"role_code" json:"role_code"`
42	}
43	
44	// Event is one immutable link in the ledger.
45	type Event struct {
46		ID         string         `bson:"_id"         json:"id"`
47		Seq        int64          `bson:"seq"         json:"seq"`
48		Type       string         `bson:"type"        json:"type"`
49		EntityType string         `bson:"entity_type" json:"entity_type"`
50		EntityID   string         `bson:"entity_id"   json:"entity_id"`
51		Refs       []Ref          `bson:"refs,omitempty"    json:"refs,omitempty"`
52		Actor      ActorRef       `bson:"actor"       json:"actor"`
53		OrgUnitID  string         `bson:"org_unit_id,omitempty" json:"org_unit_id,omitempty"`
54		Payload    map[string]any `bson:"payload,omitempty"     json:"payload,omitempty"`
55		TS         time.Time      `bson:"ts"          json:"ts"`
56		PrevHash   string         `bson:"prev_hash"   json:"prev_hash"`
57		Hash       string         `bson:"hash"        json:"hash"`
58	}
59	
60	// AppendInput describes a new event to chain.
61	type AppendInput struct {
62		Type       string
63		EntityType string
64		EntityID   string
65		Refs       []Ref
66		Actor      ActorRef
67		OrgUnitID  string
68		Payload    map[string]any
69	}
70	
71	// Ledger appends to and reads the hash chain.
72	type Ledger struct {
73		coll *mongo.Collection
74	}
75	
76	// NewLedger binds the ledger to the database.
77	func NewLedger(db *mongo.Database) *Ledger {
78		return &Ledger{coll: db.Collection(collection)}
79	}
80	
81	// genesisHash anchors the chain before the first event.
82	const genesisHash = "GENESIS"
83	
84	// Append chains a new event. Concurrency-safe without transactions: it reads
85	// the current head, computes seq+hash optimistically, and relies on the
86	// unique index on `seq` — a duplicate-key collision means another writer won
87	// the slot, so we re-read and retry.
88	func (l *Ledger) Append(ctx context.Context, in AppendInput) (*Event, error) {
89		const maxRetries = 12
90		for attempt := 0; attempt < maxRetries; attempt++ {
91			seq, prevHash, err := l.head(ctx)
92			if err != nil {
93				return nil, err
94			}
95			ev := &Event{
96				ID:         uuid.NewString(),
97				Seq:        seq + 1,
98				Type:       in.Type,
99				EntityType: in.EntityType,
100				EntityID:   in.EntityID,
101				Refs:       in.Refs,
102				Actor:      in.Actor,
103				OrgUnitID:  in.OrgUnitID,
104				Payload:    in.Payload,
105				TS:         time.Now().UTC(),
106				PrevHash:   prevHash,
107			}
108			ev.Hash = computeHash(ev)
109	
110			if _, err := l.coll.InsertOne(ctx, ev); err != nil {
111				if mongo.IsDuplicateKeyError(err) {
112					continue // lost the seq race — retry against the new head
113				}
114				return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance append: %w", err)
115			}
116			return ev, nil
117		}
118		return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance append: gave up after %d seq collisions", 12)
119	}
120	
121	// head returns the latest (seq, hash), or (0, GENESIS) for an empty chain.
122	func (l *Ledger) head(ctx context.Context) (int64, string, error) {
123		var last Event
124		err := l.coll.FindOne(ctx, bson.D{},
125			options.FindOne().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: -1}}),
126		).Decode(&last)
127		if errors.Is(err, mongo.ErrNoDocuments) {
128			return 0, genesisHash, nil
129		}
130		if err != nil {
131			return 0, "", fmt.Errorf("provenance head: %w", err)
132		}
133		return last.Seq, last.Hash, nil
134	}
135	
136	// computeHash covers everything that matters: position, linkage, content.
137	// Payload is canonicalised via encoding/json (map keys are sorted), so the
138	// digest is deterministic.
139	func computeHash(ev *Event) string {
140		payloadJSON, _ := json.Marshal(ev.Payload)
141		refParts := make([]string, 0, len(ev.Refs))
142		for _, r := range ev.Refs {
143			refParts = append(refParts, r.EntityType+":"+r.EntityID+":"+r.Relation)
144		}
145		material := strings.Join([]string{
146			ev.PrevHash,
147			strconv.FormatInt(ev.Seq, 10),
148			ev.Type,
149			ev.EntityType,
150			ev.EntityID,
151			strings.Join(refParts, ","),
152			ev.Actor.PartyID,
153			ev.Actor.RoleCode,
154			ev.OrgUnitID,
155			string(payloadJSON),
156			ev.TS.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339Nano),
157		}, "|")
158		sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(material))
159		return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
160	}
161	
162	// EventsForEntity returns an entity's own timeline in chain order.
163	func (l *Ledger) EventsForEntity(ctx context.Context, entityType, entityID string) ([]Event, error) {
164		cur, err := l.coll.Find(ctx,
165			bson.D{{Key: "entity_type", Value: entityType}, {Key: "entity_id", Value: entityID}},
166			options.Find().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: 1}}),
167		)
168		if err != nil {
169			return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance events for %s/%s: %w", entityType, entityID, err)
170		}
171		var out []Event
172		if err := cur.All(ctx, &out); err != nil {
173			return nil, err
174		}
175		return out, nil
176	}
177	
178	// Trace walks the provenance graph UPSTREAM from an entity: its events, plus
179	// (recursively) the events of everything those events reference. This is how
180	// a consumer QR resolves back to the contributing samiti set, and how a failed
181	// aflatoxin test walks back to source DCSes (blueprint §8.3).
182	func (l *Ledger) Trace(ctx context.Context, entityType, entityID string, maxDepth int) ([]Event, error) {
183		if maxDepth <= 0 {
184			maxDepth = 10
185		}
186		const hardEventCap = 2000
187	
188		type node struct{ etype, eid string }
189		visited := map[node]bool{}
190		frontier := []node{{entityType, entityID}}
191		var all []Event
192	
193		for depth := 0; depth < maxDepth && len(frontier) > 0; depth++ {
194			var next []node
195			for _, n := range frontier {
196				if visited[n] {
197					continue
198				}
199				visited[n] = true
200				evs, err := l.EventsForEntity(ctx, n.etype, n.eid)
201				if err != nil {
202					return nil, err
203				}
204				for _, ev := range evs {
205					all = append(all, ev)
206					if len(all) >= hardEventCap {
207						return all, nil
208					}
209					for _, ref := range ev.Refs {
210						nn := node{ref.EntityType, ref.EntityID}
211						if !visited[nn] {
212							next = append(next, nn)
213						}
214					}
215				}
216			}
217			frontier = next
218		}
219		return all, nil
220	}
221	
222	// DownstreamRefs finds events that reference the given entity — used to walk
223	// FORWARD (e.g. "which batches consumed this blocked BMC lot?").
224	func (l *Ledger) DownstreamRefs(ctx context.Context, entityID string) ([]Event, error) {
225		cur, err := l.coll.Find(ctx,
226			bson.D{{Key: "refs.entity_id", Value: entityID}},
227			options.Find().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: 1}}),
228		)
229		if err != nil {
230			return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance downstream of %s: %w", entityID, err)
231		}
232		var out []Event
233		if err := cur.All(ctx, &out); err != nil {
234			return nil, err
235		}
236		return out, nil
237	}
238	
239	// VerifyChain re-derives every hash in [fromSeq, toSeq] and checks linkage.
240	// Returns (true, 0) when intact, or (false, seq) of the first broken link.
241	func (l *Ledger) VerifyChain(ctx context.Context, fromSeq, toSeq int64) (bool, int64, error) {
242		filter := bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$gte", Value: fromSeq}, {Key: "$lte", Value: toSeq}}}}
243		cur, err := l.coll.Find(ctx, filter, options.Find().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: 1}}))
244		if err != nil {
245			return false, 0, fmt.Errorf("provenance verify: %w", err)
246		}
247		defer cur.Close(ctx)
248	
249		prevHash := ""
250		prevSeq := int64(0)
251		first := true
252		for cur.Next(ctx) {
253			var ev Event
254			if err := cur.Decode(&ev); err != nil {
255				return false, 0, err
256			}
257			if computeHash(&ev) != ev.Hash {
258				return false, ev.Seq, nil // content tampered
259			}
260			if !first {
261				if ev.Seq != prevSeq+1 || ev.PrevHash != prevHash {
262					return false, ev.Seq, nil // linkage broken
263				}
264			}
265			prevHash, prevSeq, first = ev.Hash, ev.Seq, false
266		}
267		return true, 0, cur.Err()
268	}
269	
270	// LatestSeq returns the current chain head sequence (0 = empty).
271	func (l *Ledger) LatestSeq(ctx context.Context) (int64, error) {
272		seq, _, err := l.head(ctx)
273		return seq, err
274	}
```

```text
11	// RequireRoles allows only ROLE-kind tokens whose role is in the allow-list.
12	// SUPER_ADMIN passes every gate (break-glass admin — all its calls are
13	// audited by the audit middleware).
14	func RequireRoles(roles ...string) func(http.Handler) http.Handler {
15		allowed := make(map[string]struct{}, len(roles))
16		for _, r := range roles {
17			allowed[r] = struct{}{}
18		}
19		return func(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
20			return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
21				actor, ok := auth.ActorFrom(r.Context())
22				if !ok {
23					httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Unauthorized("authentication required"))
24					return
25				}
26				if actor.Kind != auth.TokenKindRole {
27					httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Forbidden("a role token is required — select a role first (POST /api/v1/auth/role/select)"))
28					return
29				}
30				if actor.RoleCode == domain.RoleSuperAdmin {
31					next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
32					return
33				}
34				if _, ok := allowed[actor.RoleCode]; !ok {
35					httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Forbidden("role "+actor.RoleCode+" is not permitted for this action"))
36					return
37				}
38				next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
39			})
40		}
41	}
42	
43	// RequireSession allows any authenticated party (session or role token) —
44	// used for identity endpoints like "list my roles".
45	func RequireSession(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
46		return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
47			if _, ok := auth.ActorFrom(r.Context()); !ok {
48				httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Unauthorized("authentication required"))
49				return
50			}
51			next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
52		})
53	}
```
