11	import (
12		"context"
13		"crypto/sha256"
14		"encoding/hex"
15		"encoding/json"
16		"errors"
17		"fmt"
18		"strconv"
19		"strings"
20		"time"
21	
22		"github.com/google/uuid"
23		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson"
24		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo"
25		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo/options"
26	)
27	
28	const collection = "provenance_events"
29	
30	// Ref is a directed edge to another entity in the trace graph
31	// (e.g. a consignment event referencing the pours it aggregates).
32	type Ref struct {
33		EntityType string `bson:"entity_type" json:"entity_type"`
34		EntityID   string `bson:"entity_id"   json:"entity_id"`
35		Relation   string `bson:"relation"    json:"relation"` // aggregates | supersedes | tested | yields | labels ...
36	}
37	
38	// ActorRef records who caused the event.
39	type ActorRef struct {
40		PartyID  string `bson:"party_id"  json:"party_id"`
41		RoleCode string `bson:"role_code" json:"role_code"`
42	}
43	
44	// Event is one immutable link in the ledger.
45	type Event struct {
46		ID         string         `bson:"_id"         json:"id"`
47		Seq        int64          `bson:"seq"         json:"seq"`
48		Type       string         `bson:"type"        json:"type"`
49		EntityType string         `bson:"entity_type" json:"entity_type"`
50		EntityID   string         `bson:"entity_id"   json:"entity_id"`
51		Refs       []Ref          `bson:"refs,omitempty"    json:"refs,omitempty"`
52		Actor      ActorRef       `bson:"actor"       json:"actor"`
53		OrgUnitID  string         `bson:"org_unit_id,omitempty" json:"org_unit_id,omitempty"`
54		Payload    map[string]any `bson:"payload,omitempty"     json:"payload,omitempty"`
55		TS         time.Time      `bson:"ts"          json:"ts"`
56		PrevHash   string         `bson:"prev_hash"   json:"prev_hash"`
57		Hash       string         `bson:"hash"        json:"hash"`
58	}
59	
60	// AppendInput describes a new event to chain.
61	type AppendInput struct {
62		Type       string
63		EntityType string
64		EntityID   string
65		Refs       []Ref
66		Actor      ActorRef
67		OrgUnitID  string
68		Payload    map[string]any
69	}
70	
71	// Ledger appends to and reads the hash chain.
72	type Ledger struct {
73		coll *mongo.Collection
74	}
75	
76	// NewLedger binds the ledger to the database.
77	func NewLedger(db *mongo.Database) *Ledger {
78		return &Ledger{coll: db.Collection(collection)}
79	}
80	
81	// genesisHash anchors the chain before the first event.
82	const genesisHash = "GENESIS"
83	
84	// Append chains a new event. Concurrency-safe without transactions: it reads
85	// the current head, computes seq+hash optimistically, and relies on the
86	// unique index on `seq` — a duplicate-key collision means another writer won
87	// the slot, so we re-read and retry.
88	func (l *Ledger) Append(ctx context.Context, in AppendInput) (*Event, error) {
89		const maxRetries = 12
90		for attempt := 0; attempt < maxRetries; attempt++ {
91			seq, prevHash, err := l.head(ctx)
92			if err != nil {
93				return nil, err
94			}
95			ev := &Event{
96				ID:         uuid.NewString(),
97				Seq:        seq + 1,
98				Type:       in.Type,
99				EntityType: in.EntityType,
100				EntityID:   in.EntityID,
101				Refs:       in.Refs,
102				Actor:      in.Actor,
103				OrgUnitID:  in.OrgUnitID,
104				Payload:    in.Payload,
105				TS:         time.Now().UTC(),
106				PrevHash:   prevHash,
107			}
108			ev.Hash = computeHash(ev)
109	
110			if _, err := l.coll.InsertOne(ctx, ev); err != nil {
111				if mongo.IsDuplicateKeyError(err) {
112					continue // lost the seq race — retry against the new head
113				}
114				return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance append: %w", err)
115			}
116			return ev, nil
117		}
118		return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance append: gave up after %d seq collisions", 12)
119	}
120	
121	// head returns the latest (seq, hash), or (0, GENESIS) for an empty chain.
122	func (l *Ledger) head(ctx context.Context) (int64, string, error) {
123		var last Event
124		err := l.coll.FindOne(ctx, bson.D{},
125			options.FindOne().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: -1}}),
126		).Decode(&last)
127		if errors.Is(err, mongo.ErrNoDocuments) {
128			return 0, genesisHash, nil
129		}
130		if err != nil {
131			return 0, "", fmt.Errorf("provenance head: %w", err)
132		}
133		return last.Seq, last.Hash, nil
134	}
135	
136	// computeHash covers everything that matters: position, linkage, content.
137	// Payload is canonicalised via encoding/json (map keys are sorted), so the
138	// digest is deterministic.
139	func computeHash(ev *Event) string {
140		payloadJSON, _ := json.Marshal(ev.Payload)
141		refParts := make([]string, 0, len(ev.Refs))
142		for _, r := range ev.Refs {
143			refParts = append(refParts, r.EntityType+":"+r.EntityID+":"+r.Relation)
144		}
145		material := strings.Join([]string{
146			ev.PrevHash,
147			strconv.FormatInt(ev.Seq, 10),
148			ev.Type,
149			ev.EntityType,
150			ev.EntityID,
151			strings.Join(refParts, ","),
152			ev.Actor.PartyID,
153			ev.Actor.RoleCode,
154			ev.OrgUnitID,
155			string(payloadJSON),
156			ev.TS.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339Nano),
157		}, "|")
158		sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(material))
159		return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
160	}
161	
162	// EventsForEntity returns an entity's own timeline in chain order.
163	func (l *Ledger) EventsForEntity(ctx context.Context, entityType, entityID string) ([]Event, error) {
164		cur, err := l.coll.Find(ctx,
165			bson.D{{Key: "entity_type", Value: entityType}, {Key: "entity_id", Value: entityID}},
166			options.Find().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: 1}}),
167		)
168		if err != nil {
169			return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance events for %s/%s: %w", entityType, entityID, err)
170		}
171		var out []Event
172		if err := cur.All(ctx, &out); err != nil {
173			return nil, err
174		}
175		return out, nil
176	}
177	
178	// Trace walks the provenance graph UPSTREAM from an entity: its events, plus
179	// (recursively) the events of everything those events reference. This is how
180	// a consumer QR resolves back to the contributing samiti set, and how a failed
181	// aflatoxin test walks back to source DCSes (blueprint §8.3).
182	func (l *Ledger) Trace(ctx context.Context, entityType, entityID string, maxDepth int) ([]Event, error) {
183		if maxDepth <= 0 {
184			maxDepth = 10
185		}
186		const hardEventCap = 2000
187	
188		type node struct{ etype, eid string }
189		visited := map[node]bool{}
190		frontier := []node{{entityType, entityID}}
191		var all []Event
192	
193		for depth := 0; depth < maxDepth && len(frontier) > 0; depth++ {
194			var next []node
195			for _, n := range frontier {
196				if visited[n] {
197					continue
198				}
199				visited[n] = true
200				evs, err := l.EventsForEntity(ctx, n.etype, n.eid)
201				if err != nil {
202					return nil, err
203				}
204				for _, ev := range evs {
205					all = append(all, ev)
206					if len(all) >= hardEventCap {
207						return all, nil
208					}
209					for _, ref := range ev.Refs {
210						nn := node{ref.EntityType, ref.EntityID}
211						if !visited[nn] {
212							next = append(next, nn)
213						}
214					}
215				}
216			}
217			frontier = next
218		}
219		return all, nil
220	}
221	
222	// DownstreamRefs finds events that reference the given entity — used to walk
223	// FORWARD (e.g. "which batches consumed this blocked BMC lot?").
224	func (l *Ledger) DownstreamRefs(ctx context.Context, entityID string) ([]Event, error) {
225		cur, err := l.coll.Find(ctx,
226			bson.D{{Key: "refs.entity_id", Value: entityID}},
227			options.Find().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: 1}}),
228		)
229		if err != nil {
230			return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance downstream of %s: %w", entityID, err)
231		}
232		var out []Event
233		if err := cur.All(ctx, &out); err != nil {
234			return nil, err
235		}
236		return out, nil
237	}
238	
239	// VerifyChain re-derives every hash in [fromSeq, toSeq] and checks linkage.
240	// Returns (true, 0) when intact, or (false, seq) of the first broken link.
241	func (l *Ledger) VerifyChain(ctx context.Context, fromSeq, toSeq int64) (bool, int64, error) {
242		filter := bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$gte", Value: fromSeq}, {Key: "$lte", Value: toSeq}}}}
243		cur, err := l.coll.Find(ctx, filter, options.Find().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: 1}}))
244		if err != nil {
245			return false, 0, fmt.Errorf("provenance verify: %w", err)
246		}
247		defer cur.Close(ctx)
248	
249		prevHash := ""
250		prevSeq := int64(0)
251		first := true
252		for cur.Next(ctx) {
253			var ev Event
254			if err := cur.Decode(&ev); err != nil {
255				return false, 0, err
256			}
257			if computeHash(&ev) != ev.Hash {
258				return false, ev.Seq, nil // content tampered
259			}
260			if !first {
261				if ev.Seq != prevSeq+1 || ev.PrevHash != prevHash {
262					return false, ev.Seq, nil // linkage broken
263				}
264			}
265			prevHash, prevSeq, first = ev.Hash, ev.Seq, false
266		}
267		return true, 0, cur.Err()
268	}
269	
270	// LatestSeq returns the current chain head sequence (0 = empty).
271	func (l *Ledger) LatestSeq(ctx context.Context) (int64, error) {
272		seq, _, err := l.head(ctx)
273		return seq, err
274	}

1	// Package middleware carries the cross-cutting HTTP concerns: token
2	// authentication, role enforcement, audit capture, per-IP rate limiting,
3	// Prometheus metrics.
4	package middleware
5	
6	import (
7		"net/http"
8		"strings"
9	
10		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/auth"
11		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/httpx"
12	)
13	
14	// Authenticate verifies the Bearer token and installs the Actor on the
15	// request context. Requests without a valid token are rejected — public
16	// routes simply don't mount this middleware.
17	func Authenticate(jwtm *auth.JWTManager) func(http.Handler) http.Handler {
18		return func(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
19			return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
20				header := r.Header.Get("Authorization")
21				token, ok := strings.CutPrefix(header, "Bearer ")
22				if !ok || token == "" {
23					httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Unauthorized("missing bearer token"))
24					return
25				}
26				claims, err := jwtm.Parse(token)
27				if err != nil {
28					httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Unauthorized("invalid or expired token"))
29					return
30				}
31				actor := auth.Actor{
32					PartyID:          claims.PartyID,
33					Phone:            claims.Phone,
34					KYCTier:          claims.KYCTier,
35					Kind:             claims.Kind,
36					RoleAssignmentID: claims.RoleAssignmentID,
37					RoleCode:         claims.RoleCode,
38					OrgUnitID:        claims.OrgUnitID,
39					OrgType:          claims.OrgType,
40				}
41				next.ServeHTTP(w, r.WithContext(auth.WithActor(r.Context(), actor)))
42			})
43		}
44	}
45

1	package middleware
2	
3	import (
4		"net/http"
5	
6		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/domain"

9	)
10	
11	// RequireRoles allows only ROLE-kind tokens whose role is in the allow-list.
12	// SUPER_ADMIN passes every gate (break-glass admin — all its calls are
13	// audited by the audit middleware).
14	func RequireRoles(roles ...string) func(http.Handler) http.Handler {
15		allowed := make(map[string]struct{}, len(roles))
16		for _, r := range roles {
17			allowed[r] = struct{}{}
18		}
19		return func(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
20			return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
21				actor, ok := auth.ActorFrom(r.Context())
22				if !ok {
23					httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Unauthorized("authentication required"))
24					return
25				}
26				if actor.Kind != auth.TokenKindRole {
27					httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Forbidden("a role token is required — select a role first (POST /api/v1/auth/role/select)"))
28					return
29				}
30				if actor.RoleCode == domain.RoleSuperAdmin {
31					next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
32					return
33				}
34				if _, ok := allowed[actor.RoleCode]; !ok {
35					httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Forbidden("role "+actor.RoleCode+" is not permitted for this action"))
36					return
37				}
38				next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
39			})
40		}
41	}
42	
43	// RequireSession allows any authenticated party (session or role token) —
44	// used for identity endpoints like "list my roles".
45	func RequireSession(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
46		return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
47			if _, ok := auth.ActorFrom(r.Context()); !ok {
48				httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Unauthorized("authentication required"))
49				return
50			}
51			next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
52		})
53	}
54

1	// Package provenance implements the append-only, hash-chained event ledger —
2	// the source of truth for milk traceability (blueprint §7). Every link in the
3	// pour→QR chain is an immutable Event whose SHA-256 hash covers the previous
4	// event's hash, so history cannot be quietly rewritten (tamper-evidence,
5	// FSSAI recall-grade audit).
6	//
7	// Corrections are NEW events referencing the superseded entity — nothing is
8	// ever updated or deleted in this collection.
9	package provenance
10	
11	import (
12		"context"
13		"crypto/sha256"
14		"encoding/hex"
15		"encoding/json"
16		"errors"
17		"fmt"
18		"strconv"
19		"strings"
20		"time"
21	
22		"github.com/google/uuid"
23		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson"
24		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo"
25		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo/options"
26	)
27	
28	const collection = "provenance_events"
29	
30	// Ref is a directed edge to another entity in the trace graph
31	// (e.g. a consignment event referencing the pours it aggregates).
32	type Ref struct {
33		EntityType string `bson:"entity_type" json:"entity_type"`
34		EntityID   string `bson:"entity_id"   json:"entity_id"`
35		Relation   string `bson:"relation"    json:"relation"` // aggregates | supersedes | tested | yields | labels ...
36	}
37	
38	// ActorRef records who caused the event.
39	type ActorRef struct {
40		PartyID  string `bson:"party_id"  json:"party_id"`
41		RoleCode string `bson:"role_code" json:"role_code"`
42	}
43	
44	// Event is one immutable link in the ledger.
45	type Event struct {
46		ID         string         `bson:"_id"         json:"id"`
47		Seq        int64          `bson:"seq"         json:"seq"`
48		Type       string         `bson:"type"        json:"type"`
49		EntityType string         `bson:"entity_type" json:"entity_type"`
50		EntityID   string         `bson:"entity_id"   json:"entity_id"`
51		Refs       []Ref          `bson:"refs,omitempty"    json:"refs,omitempty"`
52		Actor      ActorRef       `bson:"actor"       json:"actor"`
53		OrgUnitID  string         `bson:"org_unit_id,omitempty" json:"org_unit_id,omitempty"`
54		Payload    map[string]any `bson:"payload,omitempty"     json:"payload,omitempty"`
55		TS         time.Time      `bson:"ts"          json:"ts"`
56		PrevHash   string         `bson:"prev_hash"   json:"prev_hash"`
57		Hash       string         `bson:"hash"        json:"hash"`
58	}
59	
60	// AppendInput describes a new event to chain.
61	type AppendInput struct {
62		Type       string
63		EntityType string
64		EntityID   string
65		Refs       []Ref
66		Actor      ActorRef
67		OrgUnitID  string
68		Payload    map[string]any
69	}
70	
71	// Ledger appends to and reads the hash chain.
72	type Ledger struct {
73		coll *mongo.Collection
74	}
75	
76	// NewLedger binds the ledger to the database.
77	func NewLedger(db *mongo.Database) *Ledger {
78		return &Ledger{coll: db.Collection(collection)}
79	}
80	
81	// genesisHash anchors the chain before the first event.
82	const genesisHash = "GENESIS"
83	
84	// Append chains a new event. Concurrency-safe without transactions: it reads
85	// the current head, computes seq+hash optimistically, and relies on the
86	// unique index on `seq` — a duplicate-key collision means another writer won
87	// the slot, so we re-read and retry.
88	func (l *Ledger) Append(ctx context.Context, in AppendInput) (*Event, error) {
89		const maxRetries = 12
90		for attempt := 0; attempt < maxRetries; attempt++ {
91			seq, prevHash, err := l.head(ctx)
92			if err != nil {
93				return nil, err
94			}
95			ev := &Event{
96				ID:         uuid.NewString(),
97				Seq:        seq + 1,
98				Type:       in.Type,
99				EntityType: in.EntityType,
100				EntityID:   in.EntityID,
101				Refs:       in.Refs,
102				Actor:      in.Actor,
103				OrgUnitID:  in.OrgUnitID,
104				Payload:    in.Payload,
105				TS:         time.Now().UTC(),
106				PrevHash:   prevHash,
107			}
108			ev.Hash = computeHash(ev)
109	
110			if _, err := l.coll.InsertOne(ctx, ev); err != nil {
111				if mongo.IsDuplicateKeyError(err) {
112					continue // lost the seq race — retry against the new head
113				}
114				return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance append: %w", err)
115			}
116			return ev, nil
117		}
118		return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance append: gave up after %d seq collisions", 12)
119	}
120	
121	// head returns the latest (seq, hash), or (0, GENESIS) for an empty chain.
122	func (l *Ledger) head(ctx context.Context) (int64, string, error) {
123		var last Event
124		err := l.coll.FindOne(ctx, bson.D{},
125			options.FindOne().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: -1}}),
126		).Decode(&last)
127		if errors.Is(err, mongo.ErrNoDocuments) {
128			return 0, genesisHash, nil
129		}
130		if err != nil {
131			return 0, "", fmt.Errorf("provenance head: %w", err)
132		}
133		return last.Seq, last.Hash, nil
134	}
135	
136	// computeHash covers everything that matters: position, linkage, content.
137	// Payload is canonicalised via encoding/json (map keys are sorted), so the
138	// digest is deterministic.
139	func computeHash(ev *Event) string {
140		payloadJSON, _ := json.Marshal(ev.Payload)
141		refParts := make([]string, 0, len(ev.Refs))
142		for _, r := range ev.Refs {
143			refParts = append(refParts, r.EntityType+":"+r.EntityID+":"+r.Relation)
144		}
145		material := strings.Join([]string{
146			ev.PrevHash,
147			strconv.FormatInt(ev.Seq, 10),
148			ev.Type,
149			ev.EntityType,
150			ev.EntityID,
151			strings.Join(refParts, ","),
152			ev.Actor.PartyID,
153			ev.Actor.RoleCode,
154			ev.OrgUnitID,
155			string(payloadJSON),
156			ev.TS.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339Nano),
157		}, "|")
158		sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(material))
159		return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
160	}
161	
162	// EventsForEntity returns an entity's own timeline in chain order.
163	func (l *Ledger) EventsForEntity(ctx context.Context, entityType, entityID string) ([]Event, error) {
164		cur, err := l.coll.Find(ctx,
165			bson.D{{Key: "entity_type", Value: entityType}, {Key: "entity_id", Value: entityID}},
166			options.Find().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: 1}}),
167		)
168		if err != nil {
169			return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance events for %s/%s: %w", entityType, entityID, err)
170		}
171		var out []Event
172		if err := cur.All(ctx, &out); err != nil {
173			return nil, err
174		}
175		return out, nil
176	}
177	
178	// Trace walks the provenance graph UPSTREAM from an entity: its events, plus
179	// (recursively) the events of everything those events reference. This is how
180	// a consumer QR resolves back to the contributing samiti set, and how a failed
181	// aflatoxin test walks back to source DCSes (blueprint §8.3).
182	func (l *Ledger) Trace(ctx context.Context, entityType, entityID string, maxDepth int) ([]Event, error) {
183		if maxDepth <= 0 {
184			maxDepth = 10
185		}
186		const hardEventCap = 2000
187	
188		type node struct{ etype, eid string }
189		visited := map[node]bool{}
190		frontier := []node{{entityType, entityID}}
191		var all []Event
192	
193		for depth := 0; depth < maxDepth && len(frontier) > 0; depth++ {
194			var next []node
195			for _, n := range frontier {
196				if visited[n] {
197					continue
198				}
199				visited[n] = true
200				evs, err := l.EventsForEntity(ctx, n.etype, n.eid)
201				if err != nil {
202					return nil, err
203				}
204				for _, ev := range evs {
205					all = append(all, ev)
206					if len(all) >= hardEventCap {
207						return all, nil
208					}
209					for _, ref := range ev.Refs {
210						nn := node{ref.EntityType, ref.EntityID}
211						if !visited[nn] {
212							next = append(next, nn)
213						}
214					}
215				}
216			}
217			frontier = next
218		}
219		return all, nil
220	}
221	
222	// DownstreamRefs finds events that reference the given entity — used to walk
223	// FORWARD (e.g. "which batches consumed this blocked BMC lot?").
224	func (l *Ledger) DownstreamRefs(ctx context.Context, entityID string) ([]Event, error) {
225		cur, err := l.coll.Find(ctx,
226			bson.D{{Key: "refs.entity_id", Value: entityID}},
227			options.Find().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: 1}}),
228		)
229		if err != nil {
230			return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance downstream of %s: %w", entityID, err)
231		}
232		var out []Event
233		if err := cur.All(ctx, &out); err != nil {
234			return nil, err
235		}
236		return out, nil
237	}
238	
239	// VerifyChain re-derives every hash in [fromSeq, toSeq] and checks linkage.
240	// Returns (true, 0) when intact, or (false, seq) of the first broken link.
241	func (l *Ledger) VerifyChain(ctx context.Context, fromSeq, toSeq int64) (bool, int64, error) {
242		filter := bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$gte", Value: fromSeq}, {Key: "$lte", Value: toSeq}}}}
243		cur, err := l.coll.Find(ctx, filter, options.Find().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: 1}}))
244		if err != nil {
245			return false, 0, fmt.Errorf("provenance verify: %w", err)
246		}
247		defer cur.Close(ctx)
248	
249		prevHash := ""
250		prevSeq := int64(0)
251		first := true
252		for cur.Next(ctx) {
253			var ev Event
254			if err := cur.Decode(&ev); err != nil {
255				return false, 0, err
256			}
257			if computeHash(&ev) != ev.Hash {
258				return false, ev.Seq, nil // content tampered
259			}
260			if !first {
261				if ev.Seq != prevSeq+1 || ev.PrevHash != prevHash {
262					return false, ev.Seq, nil // linkage broken
263				}
264			}
265			prevHash, prevSeq, first = ev.Hash, ev.Seq, false
266		}
267		return true, 0, cur.Err()
268	}
269	
270	// LatestSeq returns the current chain head sequence (0 = empty).
271	func (l *Ledger) LatestSeq(ctx context.Context) (int64, error) {
272		seq, _, err := l.head(ctx)
273		return seq, err
274	}
275

1	// Package auth owns tokens and credentials: JWT issue/verify, OTP generation
2	// and HMAC hashing, opaque refresh tokens. Nothing secret is ever stored in
3	// plaintext — OTPs and refresh tokens live in the DB only as HMAC-SHA256
4	// digests.
5	package auth
6	
7	import (
8		"fmt"
9		"time"
10	
11		"github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v5"
12		"github.com/google/uuid"
13	
14		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/domain"
15	)
16	
17	// Token kinds. A SESSION token proves "this phone logged in"; a ROLE token
18	// additionally pins one active role assignment + org scope (the role switcher
19	// simply issues a fresh ROLE token).
20	const (
21		TokenKindSession = "session"
22		TokenKindRole    = "role"
23	)
24	
25	// Claims is the JWT payload.
26	type Claims struct {
27		PartyID          string `json:"pid"`
28		Phone            string `json:"phn"`
29		KYCTier          string `json:"kyc"`
30		Kind             string `json:"knd"`
31		RoleAssignmentID string `json:"rid,omitempty"`
32		RoleCode         string `json:"rol,omitempty"`
33		OrgUnitID        string `json:"org,omitempty"`
34		OrgType          string `json:"ogt,omitempty"`
35		jwt.RegisteredClaims
36	}
37	
38	// JWTManager issues and parses access tokens.
39	type JWTManager struct {
40		secret []byte
41		ttl    time.Duration
42	}
43	
44	// NewJWTManager builds a manager with the shared HS256 secret and access TTL.
45	func NewJWTManager(secret string, ttl time.Duration) *JWTManager {
46		return &JWTManager{secret: []byte(secret), ttl: ttl}
47	}
48	
49	// IssueSessionToken returns a SESSION-kind access token for a logged-in party.
50	func (m *JWTManager) IssueSessionToken(p domain.Party) (string, error) {
51		return m.sign(Claims{
52			PartyID: p.ID,
53			Phone:   p.Phone,
54			KYCTier: p.KYCTier,
55			Kind:    TokenKindSession,
56		})
57	}
58	
59	// IssueRoleToken returns a ROLE-kind access token pinned to one assignment.
60	func (m *JWTManager) IssueRoleToken(p domain.Party, ra domain.RoleAssignment, orgType string) (string, error) {
61		return m.sign(Claims{
62			PartyID:          p.ID,
63			Phone:            p.Phone,
64			KYCTier:          p.KYCTier,
65			Kind:             TokenKindRole,
66			RoleAssignmentID: ra.ID,
67			RoleCode:         ra.RoleCode,
68			OrgUnitID:        ra.OrgUnitID,
69			OrgType:          orgType,
70		})
71	}
72	
73	func (m *JWTManager) sign(c Claims) (string, error) {
74		now := time.Now()
75		c.RegisteredClaims = jwt.RegisteredClaims{
76			Issuer:    "saathi-backend",
77			Subject:   c.PartyID,
78			IssuedAt:  jwt.NewNumericDate(now),
79			ExpiresAt: jwt.NewNumericDate(now.Add(m.ttl)),
80			ID:        uuid.NewString(),
81		}
82		return jwt.NewWithClaims(jwt.SigningMethodHS256, c).SignedString(m.secret)
83	}
84	
85	// Parse validates signature+expiry and returns the claims.
86	func (m *JWTManager) Parse(token string) (*Claims, error) {
87		parsed, err := jwt.ParseWithClaims(token, &Claims{},
88			func(t *jwt.Token) (any, error) { return m.secret, nil },
89			jwt.WithValidMethods([]string{jwt.SigningMethodHS256.Alg()}),
90			jwt.WithIssuer("saathi-backend"),
91		)
92		if err != nil {
93			return nil, fmt.Errorf("parse token: %w", err)
94		}
95		claims, ok := parsed.Claims.(*Claims)
96		if !ok || !parsed.Valid {
97			return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid token claims")
98		}
99		return claims, nil
100	}
101

1	// Package middleware carries the cross-cutting HTTP concerns: token
2	// authentication, role enforcement, audit capture, per-IP rate limiting,
3	// Prometheus metrics.
4	package middleware
5	
6	import (
7		"net/http"
8		"strings"
9	
10		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/auth"
11		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/httpx"
12	)
13	
14	// Authenticate verifies the Bearer token and installs the Actor on the
15	// request context. Requests without a valid token are rejected — public
16	// routes simply don't mount this middleware.
17	func Authenticate(jwtm *auth.JWTManager) func(http.Handler) http.Handler {
18		return func(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
19			return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
20				header := r.Header.Get("Authorization")
21				token, ok := strings.CutPrefix(header, "Bearer ")
22				if !ok || token == "" {
23					httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Unauthorized("missing bearer token"))
24					return
25				}
26				claims, err := jwtm.Parse(token)
27				if err != nil {
28					httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Unauthorized("invalid or expired token"))
29					return
30				}
31				actor := auth.Actor{
32					PartyID:          claims.PartyID,
33					Phone:            claims.Phone,
34					KYCTier:          claims.KYCTier,
35					Kind:             claims.Kind,
36					RoleAssignmentID: claims.RoleAssignmentID,
37					RoleCode:         claims.RoleCode,
38					OrgUnitID:        claims.OrgUnitID,
39					OrgType:          claims.OrgType,
40				}
41				next.ServeHTTP(w, r.WithContext(auth.WithActor(r.Context(), actor)))
42			})
43		}
44	}
45

1	// Package orgscope answers the RBAC question "is this resource inside the
2	// caller's organisational scope?" in O(1) DB reads. Org units denormalise
3	// their ancestor chain into Path, so scope checking is a set-membership test
4	// — no recursive tree walks on the hot path.
5	package orgscope
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"errors"
10		"sync"
11		"time"
12	
13		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson"
14		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo"
15	
16		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/domain"
17		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/auth"
18		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/httpx"
19	)
20	
21	const collection = "org_units"
22	
23	type cachedOrg struct {
24		org domain.OrgUnit
25		at  time.Time
26	}
27	
28	// Resolver caches org units briefly (the tree changes rarely, reads are hot).
29	type Resolver struct {
30		coll *mongo.Collection
31		ttl  time.Duration
32	
33		mu    sync.RWMutex
34		cache map[string]cachedOrg
35	}
36	
37	// NewResolver binds the resolver to the database.
38	func NewResolver(db *mongo.Database) *Resolver {
39		return &Resolver{
40			coll:  db.Collection(collection),
41			ttl:   60 * time.Second,
42			cache: make(map[string]cachedOrg),
43		}
44	}
45	
46	// Get returns an org unit by ID (cached).
47	func (r *Resolver) Get(ctx context.Context, id string) (*domain.OrgUnit, error) {
48		r.mu.RLock()
49		c, ok := r.cache[id]
50		r.mu.RUnlock()
51		if ok && time.Since(c.at) < r.ttl {
52			org := c.org
53			return &org, nil
54		}
55	
56		var org domain.OrgUnit
57		err := r.coll.FindOne(ctx, bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: id}}).Decode(&org)
58		if errors.Is(err, mongo.ErrNoDocuments) {
59			return nil, httpx.NotFound("org unit " + id)
60		}
61		if err != nil {
62			return nil, httpx.Internal(err)
63		}
64	
65		r.mu.Lock()
66		r.cache[id] = cachedOrg{org: org, at: time.Now()}
67		r.mu.Unlock()
68		return &org, nil
69	}
70	
71	// Invalidate drops a cached entry (call after updates).
72	func (r *Resolver) Invalidate(id string) {
73		r.mu.Lock()
74		delete(r.cache, id)
75		r.mu.Unlock()
76	}
77	
78	// InScope reports whether target sits at-or-below scope in the hierarchy:
79	// true when scope == target, or scope appears in target's ancestor Path.
80	func (r *Resolver) InScope(ctx context.Context, scopeOrgID, targetOrgID string) (bool, error) {
81		if scopeOrgID == targetOrgID {
82			return true, nil
83		}
84		target, err := r.Get(ctx, targetOrgID)
85		if err != nil {
86			return false, err
87		}
88		for _, ancestor := range target.Path {
89			if ancestor == scopeOrgID {
90				return true, nil
91			}
92		}
93		return false, nil
94	}
95	
96	// RequireInScope enforces the actor's org scope over a target org unit.
97	// SUPER_ADMIN and STATE_AUDITOR (read-wide roles rooted at the federation)
98	// pass automatically; everyone else needs ancestry.
99	func (r *Resolver) RequireInScope(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, targetOrgID string) error {
100		if actor.RoleCode == domain.RoleSuperAdmin || actor.RoleCode == domain.RoleStateAuditor {
101			return nil
102		}
103		if actor.OrgUnitID == "" {
104			return httpx.Forbidden("role token with org scope required")
105		}
106		ok, err := r.InScope(ctx, actor.OrgUnitID, targetOrgID)
107		if err != nil {
108			return err
109		}
110		if !ok {
111			return httpx.Forbidden("resource is outside your organisational scope")
112		}
113		return nil
114	}
115

11	// RequireRoles allows only ROLE-kind tokens whose role is in the allow-list.
12	// SUPER_ADMIN passes every gate (break-glass admin — all its calls are
13	// audited by the audit middleware).
14	func RequireRoles(roles ...string) func(http.Handler) http.Handler {
15		allowed := make(map[string]struct{}, len(roles))
16		for _, r := range roles {
17			allowed[r] = struct{}{}
18		}
19		return func(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
20			return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
21				actor, ok := auth.ActorFrom(r.Context())
22				if !ok {
23					httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Unauthorized("authentication required"))
24					return
25				}
26				if actor.Kind != auth.TokenKindRole {
27					httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Forbidden("a role token is required — select a role first (POST /api/v1/auth/role/select)"))
28					return
29				}
30				if actor.RoleCode == domain.RoleSuperAdmin {
31					next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
32					return
33				}
34				if _, ok := allowed[actor.RoleCode]; !ok {
35					httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Forbidden("role "+actor.RoleCode+" is not permitted for this action"))
36					return
37				}
38				next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
39			})
40		}
41	}
42	
43	// RequireSession allows any authenticated party (session or role token) —
44	// used for identity endpoints like "list my roles".
45	func RequireSession(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
46		return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {

48				httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Unauthorized("authentication required"))

1	// Package orgscope answers the RBAC question "is this resource inside the
2	// caller's organisational scope?" in O(1) DB reads. Org units denormalise
3	// their ancestor chain into Path, so scope checking is a set-membership test
4	// — no recursive tree walks on the hot path.
5	package orgscope
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"errors"
10		"sync"
11		"time"
12	
13		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson"
14		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo"
15	
16		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/domain"
17		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/auth"
18		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/httpx"
19	)
20	
21	const collection = "org_units"
22	
23	type cachedOrg struct {
24		org domain.OrgUnit
25		at  time.Time
26	}
27	
28	// Resolver caches org units briefly (the tree changes rarely, reads are hot).
29	type Resolver struct {
30		coll *mongo.Collection
31		ttl  time.Duration
32	
33		mu    sync.RWMutex
34		cache map[string]cachedOrg
35	}
36	
37	// NewResolver binds the resolver to the database.
38	func NewResolver(db *mongo.Database) *Resolver {
39		return &Resolver{
40			coll:  db.Collection(collection),
41			ttl:   60 * time.Second,
42			cache: make(map[string]cachedOrg),
43		}
44	}
45	
46	// Get returns an org unit by ID (cached).
47	func (r *Resolver) Get(ctx context.Context, id string) (*domain.OrgUnit, error) {
48		r.mu.RLock()
49		c, ok := r.cache[id]
50		r.mu.RUnlock()
51		if ok && time.Since(c.at) < r.ttl {
52			org := c.org
53			return &org, nil
54		}
55	
56		var org domain.OrgUnit
57		err := r.coll.FindOne(ctx, bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: id}}).Decode(&org)
58		if errors.Is(err, mongo.ErrNoDocuments) {
59			return nil, httpx.NotFound("org unit " + id)
60		}
61		if err != nil {
62			return nil, httpx.Internal(err)
63		}
64	
65		r.mu.Lock()
66		r.cache[id] = cachedOrg{org: org, at: time.Now()}
67		r.mu.Unlock()
68		return &org, nil
69	}
70	
71	// Invalidate drops a cached entry (call after updates).
72	func (r *Resolver) Invalidate(id string) {
73		r.mu.Lock()
74		delete(r.cache, id)
75		r.mu.Unlock()
76	}
77	
78	// InScope reports whether target sits at-or-below scope in the hierarchy:
79	// true when scope == target, or scope appears in target's ancestor Path.
80	func (r *Resolver) InScope(ctx context.Context, scopeOrgID, targetOrgID string) (bool, error) {
81		if scopeOrgID == targetOrgID {
82			return true, nil
83		}
84		target, err := r.Get(ctx, targetOrgID)
85		if err != nil {
86			return false, err
87		}
88		for _, ancestor := range target.Path {
89			if ancestor == scopeOrgID {
90				return true, nil
91			}
92		}
93		return false, nil
94	}
95	
96	// RequireInScope enforces the actor's org scope over a target org unit.
97	// SUPER_ADMIN and STATE_AUDITOR (read-wide roles rooted at the federation)
98	// pass automatically; everyone else needs ancestry.
99	func (r *Resolver) RequireInScope(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, targetOrgID string) error {
100		if actor.RoleCode == domain.RoleSuperAdmin || actor.RoleCode == domain.RoleStateAuditor {
101			return nil
102		}
103		if actor.OrgUnitID == "" {
104			return httpx.Forbidden("role token with org scope required")
105		}
106		ok, err := r.InScope(ctx, actor.OrgUnitID, targetOrgID)
107		if err != nil {
108			return err
109		}
110		if !ok {
111			return httpx.Forbidden("resource is outside your organisational scope")
112		}
113		return nil
114	}
115

1	// Package provenance implements the append-only, hash-chained event ledger —
2	// the source of truth for milk traceability (blueprint §7). Every link in the
3	// pour→QR chain is an immutable Event whose SHA-256 hash covers the previous
4	// event's hash, so history cannot be quietly rewritten (tamper-evidence,
5	// FSSAI recall-grade audit).
6	//
7	// Corrections are NEW events referencing the superseded entity — nothing is
8	// ever updated or deleted in this collection.
9	package provenance
10	
11	import (
12		"context"
13		"crypto/sha256"
14		"encoding/hex"
15		"encoding/json"
16		"errors"
17		"fmt"
18		"strconv"
19		"strings"
20		"time"
21	
22		"github.com/google/uuid"
23		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson"
24		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo"
25		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo/options"
26	)
27	
28	const collection = "provenance_events"
29	
30	// Ref is a directed edge to another entity in the trace graph
31	// (e.g. a consignment event referencing the pours it aggregates).
32	type Ref struct {
33		EntityType string `bson:"entity_type" json:"entity_type"`
34		EntityID   string `bson:"entity_id"   json:"entity_id"`
35		Relation   string `bson:"relation"    json:"relation"` // aggregates | supersedes | tested | yields | labels ...
36	}
37	
38	// ActorRef records who caused the event.
39	type ActorRef struct {
40		PartyID  string `bson:"party_id"  json:"party_id"`
41		RoleCode string `bson:"role_code" json:"role_code"`
42	}
43	
44	// Event is one immutable link in the ledger.
45	type Event struct {
46		ID         string         `bson:"_id"         json:"id"`
47		Seq        int64          `bson:"seq"         json:"seq"`
48		Type       string         `bson:"type"        json:"type"`
49		EntityType string         `bson:"entity_type" json:"entity_type"`
50		EntityID   string         `bson:"entity_id"   json:"entity_id"`
51		Refs       []Ref          `bson:"refs,omitempty"    json:"refs,omitempty"`
52		Actor      ActorRef       `bson:"actor"       json:"actor"`
53		OrgUnitID  string         `bson:"org_unit_id,omitempty" json:"org_unit_id,omitempty"`
54		Payload    map[string]any `bson:"payload,omitempty"     json:"payload,omitempty"`
55		TS         time.Time      `bson:"ts"          json:"ts"`
56		PrevHash   string         `bson:"prev_hash"   json:"prev_hash"`
57		Hash       string         `bson:"hash"        json:"hash"`
58	}
59	
60	// AppendInput describes a new event to chain.
61	type AppendInput struct {
62		Type       string
63		EntityType string
64		EntityID   string
65		Refs       []Ref
66		Actor      ActorRef
67		OrgUnitID  string
68		Payload    map[string]any
69	}
70	
71	// Ledger appends to and reads the hash chain.
72	type Ledger struct {
73		coll *mongo.Collection
74	}
75	
76	// NewLedger binds the ledger to the database.
77	func NewLedger(db *mongo.Database) *Ledger {
78		return &Ledger{coll: db.Collection(collection)}
79	}
80	
81	// genesisHash anchors the chain before the first event.
82	const genesisHash = "GENESIS"
83	
84	// Append chains a new event. Concurrency-safe without transactions: it reads
85	// the current head, computes seq+hash optimistically, and relies on the
86	// unique index on `seq` — a duplicate-key collision means another writer won
87	// the slot, so we re-read and retry.
88	func (l *Ledger) Append(ctx context.Context, in AppendInput) (*Event, error) {
89		const maxRetries = 12
90		for attempt := 0; attempt < maxRetries; attempt++ {
91			seq, prevHash, err := l.head(ctx)
92			if err != nil {
93				return nil, err
94			}
95			ev := &Event{
96				ID:         uuid.NewString(),
97				Seq:        seq + 1,
98				Type:       in.Type,
99				EntityType: in.EntityType,
100				EntityID:   in.EntityID,
101				Refs:       in.Refs,
102				Actor:      in.Actor,
103				OrgUnitID:  in.OrgUnitID,
104				Payload:    in.Payload,
105				TS:         time.Now().UTC(),
106				PrevHash:   prevHash,
107			}
108			ev.Hash = computeHash(ev)
109	
110			if _, err := l.coll.InsertOne(ctx, ev); err != nil {
111				if mongo.IsDuplicateKeyError(err) {
112					continue // lost the seq race — retry against the new head
113				}
114				return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance append: %w", err)
115			}
116			return ev, nil
117		}
118		return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance append: gave up after %d seq collisions", 12)
119	}
120	
121	// head returns the latest (seq, hash), or (0, GENESIS) for an empty chain.
122	func (l *Ledger) head(ctx context.Context) (int64, string, error) {
123		var last Event
124		err := l.coll.FindOne(ctx, bson.D{},
125			options.FindOne().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: -1}}),
126		).Decode(&last)
127		if errors.Is(err, mongo.ErrNoDocuments) {
128			return 0, genesisHash, nil
129		}
130		if err != nil {
131			return 0, "", fmt.Errorf("provenance head: %w", err)
132		}
133		return last.Seq, last.Hash, nil
134	}
135	
136	// computeHash covers everything that matters: position, linkage, content.
137	// Payload is canonicalised via encoding/json (map keys are sorted), so the
138	// digest is deterministic.
139	func computeHash(ev *Event) string {
140		payloadJSON, _ := json.Marshal(ev.Payload)
141		refParts := make([]string, 0, len(ev.Refs))
142		for _, r := range ev.Refs {
143			refParts = append(refParts, r.EntityType+":"+r.EntityID+":"+r.Relation)
144		}
145		material := strings.Join([]string{
146			ev.PrevHash,
147			strconv.FormatInt(ev.Seq, 10),
148			ev.Type,
149			ev.EntityType,
150			ev.EntityID,
151			strings.Join(refParts, ","),
152			ev.Actor.PartyID,
153			ev.Actor.RoleCode,
154			ev.OrgUnitID,
155			string(payloadJSON),
156			ev.TS.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339Nano),
157		}, "|")
158		sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(material))
159		return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
160	}
161	
162	// EventsForEntity returns an entity's own timeline in chain order.
163	func (l *Ledger) EventsForEntity(ctx context.Context, entityType, entityID string) ([]Event, error) {
164		cur, err := l.coll.Find(ctx,
165			bson.D{{Key: "entity_type", Value: entityType}, {Key: "entity_id", Value: entityID}},
166			options.Find().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: 1}}),
167		)
168		if err != nil {
169			return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance events for %s/%s: %w", entityType, entityID, err)
170		}
171		var out []Event
172		if err := cur.All(ctx, &out); err != nil {
173			return nil, err
174		}
175		return out, nil
176	}
177	
178	// Trace walks the provenance graph UPSTREAM from an entity: its events, plus
179	// (recursively) the events of everything those events reference. This is how
180	// a consumer QR resolves back to the contributing samiti set, and how a failed
181	// aflatoxin test walks back to source DCSes (blueprint §8.3).
182	func (l *Ledger) Trace(ctx context.Context, entityType, entityID string, maxDepth int) ([]Event, error) {
183		if maxDepth <= 0 {
184			maxDepth = 10
185		}
186		const hardEventCap = 2000
187	
188		type node struct{ etype, eid string }
189		visited := map[node]bool{}
190		frontier := []node{{entityType, entityID}}
191		var all []Event
192	
193		for depth := 0; depth < maxDepth && len(frontier) > 0; depth++ {
194			var next []node
195			for _, n := range frontier {
196				if visited[n] {
197					continue
198				}
199				visited[n] = true
200				evs, err := l.EventsForEntity(ctx, n.etype, n.eid)
201				if err != nil {
202					return nil, err
203				}
204				for _, ev := range evs {
205					all = append(all, ev)
206					if len(all) >= hardEventCap {
207						return all, nil
208					}
209					for _, ref := range ev.Refs {
210						nn := node{ref.EntityType, ref.EntityID}
211						if !visited[nn] {
212							next = append(next, nn)
213						}
214					}
215				}
216			}
217			frontier = next
218		}
219		return all, nil
220	}
221	
222	// DownstreamRefs finds events that reference the given entity — used to walk
223	// FORWARD (e.g. "which batches consumed this blocked BMC lot?").
224	func (l *Ledger) DownstreamRefs(ctx context.Context, entityID string) ([]Event, error) {
225		cur, err := l.coll.Find(ctx,
226			bson.D{{Key: "refs.entity_id", Value: entityID}},
227			options.Find().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: 1}}),
228		)
229		if err != nil {
230			return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance downstream of %s: %w", entityID, err)
231		}
232		var out []Event
233		if err := cur.All(ctx, &out); err != nil {
234			return nil, err
235		}
236		return out, nil
237	}
238	
239	// VerifyChain re-derives every hash in [fromSeq, toSeq] and checks linkage.
240	// Returns (true, 0) when intact, or (false, seq) of the first broken link.
241	func (l *Ledger) VerifyChain(ctx context.Context, fromSeq, toSeq int64) (bool, int64, error) {
242		filter := bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$gte", Value: fromSeq}, {Key: "$lte", Value: toSeq}}}}
243		cur, err := l.coll.Find(ctx, filter, options.Find().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: 1}}))
244		if err != nil {
245			return false, 0, fmt.Errorf("provenance verify: %w", err)
246		}
247		defer cur.Close(ctx)
248	
249		prevHash := ""
250		prevSeq := int64(0)
251		first := true
252		for cur.Next(ctx) {
253			var ev Event
254			if err := cur.Decode(&ev); err != nil {
255				return false, 0, err
256			}
257			if computeHash(&ev) != ev.Hash {
258				return false, ev.Seq, nil // content tampered
259			}
260			if !first {
261				if ev.Seq != prevSeq+1 || ev.PrevHash != prevHash {
262					return false, ev.Seq, nil // linkage broken
263				}
264			}
265			prevHash, prevSeq, first = ev.Hash, ev.Seq, false
266		}
267		return true, 0, cur.Err()
268	}
269	
270	// LatestSeq returns the current chain head sequence (0 = empty).
271	func (l *Ledger) LatestSeq(ctx context.Context) (int64, error) {
272		seq, _, err := l.head(ctx)
273		return seq, err
274	}
275

1	// Package httpx is the HTTP toolkit shared by every module: typed errors,
2	// uniform JSON envelopes, strict request decoding, pagination.
3	package httpx
4	
5	import (
6		"fmt"
7		"net/http"
8	)
9	
10	// AppError is the single error type handlers return. It carries the HTTP
11	// status plus a stable machine-readable code the frontend can switch on.
12	type AppError struct {
13		Status  int    `json:"-"`
14		Code    string `json:"code"`
15		Message string `json:"message"`
16		Details any    `json:"details,omitempty"`
17	
18		cause error // wrapped internal error — logged server-side, never serialised
19	}
20	
21	func (e *AppError) Error() string {
22		return fmt.Sprintf("%d %s: %s", e.Status, e.Code, e.Message)
23	}
24	
25	// WithDetails returns a copy carrying extra structured context.
26	func (e *AppError) WithDetails(d any) *AppError {
27		cp := *e
28		cp.Details = d
29		return &cp
30	}
31	
32	func newErr(status int, code, msg string) *AppError {
33		return &AppError{Status: status, Code: code, Message: msg}
34	}
35	
36	// Constructors — use these instead of raw errors in handlers/services.
37	
38	func BadRequest(code, msg string) *AppError { return newErr(http.StatusBadRequest, code, msg) }
39	
40	func Unauthorized(msg string) *AppError { return newErr(http.StatusUnauthorized, "UNAUTHORIZED", msg) }
41	
42	func Forbidden(msg string) *AppError { return newErr(http.StatusForbidden, "FORBIDDEN", msg) }
43	
44	func NotFound(resource string) *AppError {
45		return newErr(http.StatusNotFound, "NOT_FOUND", resource+" not found")
46	}
47	
48	func Conflict(code, msg string) *AppError { return newErr(http.StatusConflict, code, msg) }
49	
50	func Unprocessable(code, msg string) *AppError {
51		return newErr(http.StatusUnprocessableEntity, code, msg)
52	}
53	
54	func TooManyRequests(msg string) *AppError {
55		return newErr(http.StatusTooManyRequests, "RATE_LIMITED", msg)
56	}
57	
58	// Internal wraps an unexpected error. The cause is logged server-side but
59	// never leaked to the client.
60	func Internal(err error) *AppError {
61		e := newErr(http.StatusInternalServerError, "INTERNAL", "internal server error")
62		e.cause = err
63		return e
64	}
65	
66	func (e *AppError) Unwrap() error { return e.cause }
67

9	
10	// envelope is the uniform success shape: {"data": ..., "meta": {...}?}.
11	type envelope struct {
12		Data any `json:"data"`
13		Meta any `json:"meta,omitempty"`
14	}
15	
16	type errEnvelope struct {
17		Error *AppError `json:"error"`
18	}
19	
20	// JSON writes a success response wrapped in the standard envelope.
21	func JSON(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, data any) {
22		writeJSON(w, status, envelope{Data: data})
23	}
24	
25	// JSONMeta writes a success response with list metadata (pagination etc.).
26	func JSONMeta(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, data, meta any) {
27		writeJSON(w, status, envelope{Data: data, Meta: meta})
28	}
29	
30	// Error writes the standard error envelope. Unexpected (non-AppError) errors
31	// become an opaque 500 and the cause is logged with the request context.
32	func Error(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, err error) {
33		var ae *AppError
34		if !errors.As(err, &ae) {
35			ae = Internal(err)
36		}
37		if ae.Status >= 500 {
38			slog.ErrorContext(r.Context(), "request failed",
39				slog.String("method", r.Method),
40				slog.String("path", r.URL.Path),
41				slog.String("code", ae.Code),
42				slog.Any("cause", ae.CauseOrSelf()),
43			)
44		}
45		writeJSON(w, ae.Status, errEnvelope{Error: ae})
46	}
47	
48	// CauseOrSelf returns the wrapped cause if present, else the error itself.
49	func (e *AppError) CauseOrSelf() error {
50		if e.cause != nil {
51			return e.cause
52		}
53		return e
54	}
55	
56	func writeJSON(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, v any) {
57		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json; charset=utf-8")
58		w.WriteHeader(status)
59		_ = json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(v)
60	}

18	// HasRole reports whether the actor operates under one of the given roles.
19	func (a Actor) HasRole(roles ...string) bool {
20		for _, r := range roles {
21			if a.RoleCode == r {
22				return true
23			}
24		}
25		return false
26	}

28	type actorCtxKey struct{}
29	
30	// WithActor stores the actor on the context.
31	func WithActor(ctx context.Context, a Actor) context.Context {
32		return context.WithValue(ctx, actorCtxKey{}, a)

36	func ActorFrom(ctx context.Context) (Actor, bool) {

1	package httpx
2	
3	import (
4		"encoding/json"
5		"errors"
6		"fmt"
7		"io"
8		"net/http"
9		"strconv"
10	)
11	
12	// maxBodyBytes caps request bodies at 1 MiB — pours, readings and admin
13	// payloads are all tiny; photo evidence goes to the object store, not the API.
14	const maxBodyBytes = 1 << 20
15	
16	// DecodeJSON strictly decodes the request body into dst. It enforces the
17	// size cap and exactly one JSON value.
18	func DecodeJSON(r *http.Request, dst any) error {
19		r.Body = http.MaxBytesReader(nil, r.Body, maxBodyBytes)
20		dec := json.NewDecoder(r.Body)
21		if err := dec.Decode(dst); err != nil {
22			var maxErr *http.MaxBytesError
23			switch {
24			case errors.As(err, &maxErr):
25				return BadRequest("BODY_TOO_LARGE", fmt.Sprintf("request body exceeds %d bytes", maxBodyBytes))
26			case errors.Is(err, io.EOF):
27				return BadRequest("EMPTY_BODY", "request body is required")
28			default:
29				return BadRequest("MALFORMED_JSON", "request body is not valid JSON: "+err.Error())
30			}
31		}
32		if dec.More() {
33			return BadRequest("MALFORMED_JSON", "request body must contain a single JSON value")
34		}
35		return nil
36	}
37	
38	// Page holds validated pagination parameters.
39	type Page struct {
40		Limit  int64 `json:"limit"`
41		Offset int64 `json:"offset"`
42	}
43	
44	// ParsePage reads ?limit= and ?offset= with sane bounds (default 50, max 200).
45	func ParsePage(r *http.Request) Page {
46		p := Page{Limit: 50, Offset: 0}
47		if v := r.URL.Query().Get("limit"); v != "" {
48			if n, err := strconv.ParseInt(v, 10, 64); err == nil && n > 0 {
49				p.Limit = min(n, 200)
50			}
51		}
52		if v := r.URL.Query().Get("offset"); v != "" {
53			if n, err := strconv.ParseInt(v, 10, 64); err == nil && n >= 0 {
54				p.Offset = n
55			}
56		}
57		return p
58	}

1	// Package middleware carries the cross-cutting HTTP concerns: token
2	// authentication, role enforcement, audit capture, per-IP rate limiting,
3	// Prometheus metrics.
4	package middleware
5	
6	import (
7		"net/http"
8		"strings"
9	
10		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/auth"
11		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/httpx"
12	)
13	
14	// Authenticate verifies the Bearer token and installs the Actor on the
15	// request context. Requests without a valid token are rejected — public
16	// routes simply don't mount this middleware.
17	func Authenticate(jwtm *auth.JWTManager) func(http.Handler) http.Handler {
18		return func(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
19			return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
20				header := r.Header.Get("Authorization")
21				token, ok := strings.CutPrefix(header, "Bearer ")
22				if !ok || token == "" {
23					httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Unauthorized("missing bearer token"))
24					return
25				}
26				claims, err := jwtm.Parse(token)
27				if err != nil {
28					httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Unauthorized("invalid or expired token"))
29					return
30				}
31				actor := auth.Actor{
32					PartyID:          claims.PartyID,
33					Phone:            claims.Phone,
34					KYCTier:          claims.KYCTier,
35					Kind:             claims.Kind,
36					RoleAssignmentID: claims.RoleAssignmentID,
37					RoleCode:         claims.RoleCode,
38					OrgUnitID:        claims.OrgUnitID,
39					OrgType:          claims.OrgType,
40				}
41				next.ServeHTTP(w, r.WithContext(auth.WithActor(r.Context(), actor)))
42			})
43		}
44	}
45

1	package middleware
2	
3	import (
4		"net/http"
5	
6		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/domain"
7		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/auth"
8		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/httpx"
9	)
10	
11	// RequireRoles allows only ROLE-kind tokens whose role is in the allow-list.
12	// SUPER_ADMIN passes every gate (break-glass admin — all its calls are
13	// audited by the audit middleware).
14	func RequireRoles(roles ...string) func(http.Handler) http.Handler {
15		allowed := make(map[string]struct{}, len(roles))
16		for _, r := range roles {
17			allowed[r] = struct{}{}
18		}
19		return func(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
20			return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
21				actor, ok := auth.ActorFrom(r.Context())
22				if !ok {
23					httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Unauthorized("authentication required"))
24					return
25				}
26				if actor.Kind != auth.TokenKindRole {
27					httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Forbidden("a role token is required — select a role first (POST /api/v1/auth/role/select)"))
28					return
29				}
30				if actor.RoleCode == domain.RoleSuperAdmin {
31					next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
32					return
33				}
34				if _, ok := allowed[actor.RoleCode]; !ok {
35					httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Forbidden("role "+actor.RoleCode+" is not permitted for this action"))
36					return
37				}
38				next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
39			})
40		}
41	}
42	
43	// RequireSession allows any authenticated party (session or role token) —
44	// used for identity endpoints like "list my roles".
45	func RequireSession(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
46		return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
47			if _, ok := auth.ActorFrom(r.Context()); !ok {
48				httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Unauthorized("authentication required"))
49				return
50			}
51			next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
52		})
53	}
54

1	// Package provenance implements the append-only, hash-chained event ledger —
2	// the source of truth for milk traceability (blueprint §7). Every link in the
3	// pour→QR chain is an immutable Event whose SHA-256 hash covers the previous
4	// event's hash, so history cannot be quietly rewritten (tamper-evidence,
5	// FSSAI recall-grade audit).
6	//
7	// Corrections are NEW events referencing the superseded entity — nothing is
8	// ever updated or deleted in this collection.
9	package provenance
10	
11	import (
12		"context"
13		"crypto/sha256"
14		"encoding/hex"
15		"encoding/json"
16		"errors"
17		"fmt"
18		"strconv"
19		"strings"
20		"time"
21	
22		"github.com/google/uuid"
23		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson"
24		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo"
25		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo/options"
26	)
27	
28	const collection = "provenance_events"
29	
30	// Ref is a directed edge to another entity in the trace graph
31	// (e.g. a consignment event referencing the pours it aggregates).
32	type Ref struct {
33		EntityType string `bson:"entity_type" json:"entity_type"`
34		EntityID   string `bson:"entity_id"   json:"entity_id"`
35		Relation   string `bson:"relation"    json:"relation"` // aggregates | supersedes | tested | yields | labels ...
36	}
37	
38	// ActorRef records who caused the event.
39	type ActorRef struct {
40		PartyID  string `bson:"party_id"  json:"party_id"`
41		RoleCode string `bson:"role_code" json:"role_code"`
42	}
43	
44	// Event is one immutable link in the ledger.
45	type Event struct {
46		ID         string         `bson:"_id"         json:"id"`
47		Seq        int64          `bson:"seq"         json:"seq"`
48		Type       string         `bson:"type"        json:"type"`
49		EntityType string         `bson:"entity_type" json:"entity_type"`
50		EntityID   string         `bson:"entity_id"   json:"entity_id"`
51		Refs       []Ref          `bson:"refs,omitempty"    json:"refs,omitempty"`
52		Actor      ActorRef       `bson:"actor"       json:"actor"`
53		OrgUnitID  string         `bson:"org_unit_id,omitempty" json:"org_unit_id,omitempty"`
54		Payload    map[string]any `bson:"payload,omitempty"     json:"payload,omitempty"`
55		TS         time.Time      `bson:"ts"          json:"ts"`
56		PrevHash   string         `bson:"prev_hash"   json:"prev_hash"`
57		Hash       string         `bson:"hash"        json:"hash"`
58	}
59	
60	// AppendInput describes a new event to chain.
61	type AppendInput struct {
62		Type       string
63		EntityType string
64		EntityID   string
65		Refs       []Ref
66		Actor      ActorRef
67		OrgUnitID  string
68		Payload    map[string]any
69	}
70	
71	// Ledger appends to and reads the hash chain.
72	type Ledger struct {
73		coll *mongo.Collection
74	}
75	
76	// NewLedger binds the ledger to the database.
77	func NewLedger(db *mongo.Database) *Ledger {
78		return &Ledger{coll: db.Collection(collection)}
79	}
80	
81	// genesisHash anchors the chain before the first event.
82	const genesisHash = "GENESIS"
83	
84	// Append chains a new event. Concurrency-safe without transactions: it reads
85	// the current head, computes seq+hash optimistically, and relies on the
86	// unique index on `seq` — a duplicate-key collision means another writer won
87	// the slot, so we re-read and retry.
88	func (l *Ledger) Append(ctx context.Context, in AppendInput) (*Event, error) {
89		const maxRetries = 12
90		for attempt := 0; attempt < maxRetries; attempt++ {
91			seq, prevHash, err := l.head(ctx)
92			if err != nil {
93				return nil, err
94			}
95			ev := &Event{
96				ID:         uuid.NewString(),
97				Seq:        seq + 1,
98				Type:       in.Type,
99				EntityType: in.EntityType,
100				EntityID:   in.EntityID,
101				Refs:       in.Refs,
102				Actor:      in.Actor,
103				OrgUnitID:  in.OrgUnitID,
104				Payload:    in.Payload,
105				TS:         time.Now().UTC(),
106				PrevHash:   prevHash,
107			}
108			ev.Hash = computeHash(ev)
109	
110			if _, err := l.coll.InsertOne(ctx, ev); err != nil {
111				if mongo.IsDuplicateKeyError(err) {
112					continue // lost the seq race — retry against the new head
113				}
114				return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance append: %w", err)
115			}
116			return ev, nil
117		}
118		return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance append: gave up after %d seq collisions", 12)
119	}
120	
121	// head returns the latest (seq, hash), or (0, GENESIS) for an empty chain.
122	func (l *Ledger) head(ctx context.Context) (int64, string, error) {
123		var last Event
124		err := l.coll.FindOne(ctx, bson.D{},
125			options.FindOne().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: -1}}),
126		).Decode(&last)
127		if errors.Is(err, mongo.ErrNoDocuments) {
128			return 0, genesisHash, nil
129		}
130		if err != nil {
131			return 0, "", fmt.Errorf("provenance head: %w", err)
132		}
133		return last.Seq, last.Hash, nil
134	}
135	
136	// computeHash covers everything that matters: position, linkage, content.
137	// Payload is canonicalised via encoding/json (map keys are sorted), so the
138	// digest is deterministic.
139	func computeHash(ev *Event) string {
140		payloadJSON, _ := json.Marshal(ev.Payload)
141		refParts := make([]string, 0, len(ev.Refs))
142		for _, r := range ev.Refs {
143			refParts = append(refParts, r.EntityType+":"+r.EntityID+":"+r.Relation)
144		}
145		material := strings.Join([]string{
146			ev.PrevHash,
147			strconv.FormatInt(ev.Seq, 10),
148			ev.Type,
149			ev.EntityType,
150			ev.EntityID,
151			strings.Join(refParts, ","),
152			ev.Actor.PartyID,
153			ev.Actor.RoleCode,
154			ev.OrgUnitID,
155			string(payloadJSON),
156			ev.TS.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339Nano),
157		}, "|")
158		sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(material))
159		return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
160	}
161	
162	// EventsForEntity returns an entity's own timeline in chain order.
163	func (l *Ledger) EventsForEntity(ctx context.Context, entityType, entityID string) ([]Event, error) {
164		cur, err := l.coll.Find(ctx,
165			bson.D{{Key: "entity_type", Value: entityType}, {Key: "entity_id", Value: entityID}},
166			options.Find().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: 1}}),
167		)
168		if err != nil {
169			return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance events for %s/%s: %w", entityType, entityID, err)
170		}
171		var out []Event
172		if err := cur.All(ctx, &out); err != nil {
173			return nil, err
174		}
175		return out, nil
176	}
177	
178	// Trace walks the provenance graph UPSTREAM from an entity: its events, plus
179	// (recursively) the events of everything those events reference. This is how
180	// a consumer QR resolves back to the contributing samiti set, and how a failed
181	// aflatoxin test walks back to source DCSes (blueprint §8.3).
182	func (l *Ledger) Trace(ctx context.Context, entityType, entityID string, maxDepth int) ([]Event, error) {
183		if maxDepth <= 0 {
184			maxDepth = 10
185		}
186		const hardEventCap = 2000
187	
188		type node struct{ etype, eid string }
189		visited := map[node]bool{}
190		frontier := []node{{entityType, entityID}}
191		var all []Event
192	
193		for depth := 0; depth < maxDepth && len(frontier) > 0; depth++ {
194			var next []node
195			for _, n := range frontier {
196				if visited[n] {
197					continue
198				}
199				visited[n] = true
200				evs, err := l.EventsForEntity(ctx, n.etype, n.eid)
201				if err != nil {
202					return nil, err
203				}
204				for _, ev := range evs {
205					all = append(all, ev)
206					if len(all) >= hardEventCap {
207						return all, nil
208					}
209					for _, ref := range ev.Refs {
210						nn := node{ref.EntityType, ref.EntityID}
211						if !visited[nn] {
212							next = append(next, nn)
213						}
214					}
215				}
216			}
217			frontier = next
218		}
219		return all, nil
220	}
221	
222	// DownstreamRefs finds events that reference the given entity — used to walk
223	// FORWARD (e.g. "which batches consumed this blocked BMC lot?").
224	func (l *Ledger) DownstreamRefs(ctx context.Context, entityID string) ([]Event, error) {
225		cur, err := l.coll.Find(ctx,
226			bson.D{{Key: "refs.entity_id", Value: entityID}},
227			options.Find().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: 1}}),
228		)
229		if err != nil {
230			return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance downstream of %s: %w", entityID, err)
231		}
232		var out []Event
233		if err := cur.All(ctx, &out); err != nil {
234			return nil, err
235		}
236		return out, nil
237	}
238	
239	// VerifyChain re-derives every hash in [fromSeq, toSeq] and checks linkage.
240	// Returns (true, 0) when intact, or (false, seq) of the first broken link.
241	func (l *Ledger) VerifyChain(ctx context.Context, fromSeq, toSeq int64) (bool, int64, error) {
242		filter := bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$gte", Value: fromSeq}, {Key: "$lte", Value: toSeq}}}}
243		cur, err := l.coll.Find(ctx, filter, options.Find().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: 1}}))
244		if err != nil {
245			return false, 0, fmt.Errorf("provenance verify: %w", err)
246		}
247		defer cur.Close(ctx)
248	
249		prevHash := ""
250		prevSeq := int64(0)
251		first := true
252		for cur.Next(ctx) {
253			var ev Event
254			if err := cur.Decode(&ev); err != nil {
255				return false, 0, err
256			}
257			if computeHash(&ev) != ev.Hash {
258				return false, ev.Seq, nil // content tampered
259			}
260			if !first {
261				if ev.Seq != prevSeq+1 || ev.PrevHash != prevHash {
262					return false, ev.Seq, nil // linkage broken
263				}
264			}
265			prevHash, prevSeq, first = ev.Hash, ev.Seq, false
266		}
267		return true, 0, cur.Err()
268	}
269	
270	// LatestSeq returns the current chain head sequence (0 = empty).
271	func (l *Ledger) LatestSeq(ctx context.Context) (int64, error) {
272		seq, _, err := l.head(ctx)
273		return seq, err
274	}
275

1	// Package orgscope answers the RBAC question "is this resource inside the
2	// caller's organisational scope?" in O(1) DB reads. Org units denormalise
3	// their ancestor chain into Path, so scope checking is a set-membership test
4	// — no recursive tree walks on the hot path.
5	package orgscope
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"errors"
10		"sync"
11		"time"
12	
13		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson"
14		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo"
15	
16		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/domain"
17		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/auth"
18		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/httpx"
19	)
20	
21	const collection = "org_units"
22	
23	type cachedOrg struct {
24		org domain.OrgUnit
25		at  time.Time
26	}
27	
28	// Resolver caches org units briefly (the tree changes rarely, reads are hot).
29	type Resolver struct {
30		coll *mongo.Collection
31		ttl  time.Duration
32	
33		mu    sync.RWMutex
34		cache map[string]cachedOrg
35	}
36	
37	// NewResolver binds the resolver to the database.
38	func NewResolver(db *mongo.Database) *Resolver {
39		return &Resolver{
40			coll:  db.Collection(collection),
41			ttl:   60 * time.Second,
42			cache: make(map[string]cachedOrg),
43		}
44	}
45	
46	// Get returns an org unit by ID (cached).
47	func (r *Resolver) Get(ctx context.Context, id string) (*domain.OrgUnit, error) {
48		r.mu.RLock()
49		c, ok := r.cache[id]
50		r.mu.RUnlock()
51		if ok && time.Since(c.at) < r.ttl {
52			org := c.org
53			return &org, nil
54		}
55	
56		var org domain.OrgUnit
57		err := r.coll.FindOne(ctx, bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: id}}).Decode(&org)
58		if errors.Is(err, mongo.ErrNoDocuments) {
59			return nil, httpx.NotFound("org unit " + id)
60		}
61		if err != nil {
62			return nil, httpx.Internal(err)
63		}
64	
65		r.mu.Lock()
66		r.cache[id] = cachedOrg{org: org, at: time.Now()}
67		r.mu.Unlock()
68		return &org, nil
69	}
70	
71	// Invalidate drops a cached entry (call after updates).
72	func (r *Resolver) Invalidate(id string) {
73		r.mu.Lock()
74		delete(r.cache, id)
75		r.mu.Unlock()
76	}
77	
78	// InScope reports whether target sits at-or-below scope in the hierarchy:
79	// true when scope == target, or scope appears in target's ancestor Path.
80	func (r *Resolver) InScope(ctx context.Context, scopeOrgID, targetOrgID string) (bool, error) {
81		if scopeOrgID == targetOrgID {
82			return true, nil
83		}
84		target, err := r.Get(ctx, targetOrgID)
85		if err != nil {
86			return false, err
87		}
88		for _, ancestor := range target.Path {
89			if ancestor == scopeOrgID {
90				return true, nil
91			}
92		}
93		return false, nil
94	}
95	
96	// RequireInScope enforces the actor's org scope over a target org unit.
97	// SUPER_ADMIN and STATE_AUDITOR (read-wide roles rooted at the federation)
98	// pass automatically; everyone else needs ancestry.
99	func (r *Resolver) RequireInScope(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, targetOrgID string) error {
100		if actor.RoleCode == domain.RoleSuperAdmin || actor.RoleCode == domain.RoleStateAuditor {
101			return nil
102		}
103		if actor.OrgUnitID == "" {
104			return httpx.Forbidden("role token with org scope required")
105		}
106		ok, err := r.InScope(ctx, actor.OrgUnitID, targetOrgID)
107		if err != nil {
108			return err
109		}
110		if !ok {
111			return httpx.Forbidden("resource is outside your organisational scope")
112		}
113		return nil
114	}
115

1	// Package eventbus is the in-process pub/sub seam between modules
2	// (e.g. settlement executed → notifications module queues the SMS).
3	// It deliberately mirrors a message-broker API: when the platform splits
4	// into microservices, this interface is re-implemented over Kafka/NATS
5	// (blueprint §15) without touching module code.
6	package eventbus
7	
8	import (
9		"context"
10		"log/slog"
11		"sync"
12		"time"
13	)
14	
15	// Topics published across module seams.
16	const (
17		TopicPourRecorded       = "pour.recorded"
18		TopicInvoiceIssued      = "invoice.issued"
19		TopicGateBlocked        = "qc.gate_blocked"
20		TopicSettlementExecuted = "settlement.executed"
21		TopicPayoutCredited     = "payout.credited"
22		TopicMVUDispatched      = "mvu.dispatched"
23	)
24	
25	// Handler consumes a published event. Payload types are documented per topic
26	// by the publishing module.
27	type Handler func(ctx context.Context, topic string, payload any)
28	
29	// Bus is a minimal async pub/sub.
30	type Bus struct {
31		log *slog.Logger
32	
33		mu   sync.RWMutex
34		subs map[string][]Handler
35	}
36	
37	// New builds an empty bus.
38	func New(log *slog.Logger) *Bus {
39		return &Bus{log: log, subs: make(map[string][]Handler)}
40	}
41	
42	// Subscribe registers a handler for a topic. Call during module wiring only
43	// (not concurrently with Publish traffic).
44	func (b *Bus) Subscribe(topic string, h Handler) {
45		b.mu.Lock()
46		defer b.mu.Unlock()
47		b.subs[topic] = append(b.subs[topic], h)
48	}
49	
50	// Publish dispatches asynchronously: each handler runs on its own goroutine
51	// with a bounded context and panic isolation, so a slow or broken subscriber
52	// can never stall the request path.
53	func (b *Bus) Publish(topic string, payload any) {
54		b.mu.RLock()
55		handlers := b.subs[topic]
56		b.mu.RUnlock()
57	
58		for _, h := range handlers {
59			h := h
60			go func() {
61				ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 15*time.Second)
62				defer cancel()
63				defer func() {
64					if rec := recover(); rec != nil {
65						b.log.Error("eventbus handler panic",
66							slog.String("topic", topic), slog.Any("panic", rec))
67					}
68				}()
69				h(ctx, topic, payload)
70			}()
71		}
72	}
73

191		var all []Event
192	
193		for depth := 0; depth < maxDepth && len(frontier) > 0; depth++ {
194			var next []node
195			for _, n := range frontier {
196				if visited[n] {
197					continue
198				}
199				visited[n] = true
200				evs, err := l.EventsForEntity(ctx, n.etype, n.eid)
201				if err != nil {
202					return nil, err
203				}
204				for _, ev := range evs {
205					all = append(all, ev)
206					if len(all) >= hardEventCap {
207						return all, nil
208					}
209					for _, ref := range ev.Refs {
210						nn := node{ref.EntityType, ref.EntityID}
211						if !visited[nn] {
212							next = append(next, nn)
213						}
214					}
215				}
216			}
217			frontier = next
218		}
219		return all, nil
220	}
221	
222	// DownstreamRefs finds events that reference the given entity — used to walk
223	// FORWARD (e.g. "which batches consumed this blocked BMC lot?").
224	func (l *Ledger) DownstreamRefs(ctx context.Context, entityID string) ([]Event, error) {
225		cur, err := l.coll.Find(ctx,
226			bson.D{{Key: "refs.entity_id", Value: entityID}},
227			options.Find().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: 1}}),
228		)
229		if err != nil {
230			return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance downstream of %s: %w", entityID, err)
231		}
232		var out []Event
233		if err := cur.All(ctx, &out); err != nil {
234			return nil, err
235		}
236		return out, nil
237	}
238	
239	// VerifyChain re-derives every hash in [fromSeq, toSeq] and checks linkage.
240	// Returns (true, 0) when intact, or (false, seq) of the first broken link.
241	func (l *Ledger) VerifyChain(ctx context.Context, fromSeq, toSeq int64) (bool, int64, error) {
242		filter := bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$gte", Value: fromSeq}, {Key: "$lte", Value: toSeq}}}}
243		cur, err := l.coll.Find(ctx, filter, options.Find().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: 1}}))
244		if err != nil {
245			return false, 0, fmt.Errorf("provenance verify: %w", err)
246		}
247		defer cur.Close(ctx)
248	
249		prevHash := ""
250		prevSeq := int64(0)
251		first := true
252		for cur.Next(ctx) {
253			var ev Event
254			if err := cur.Decode(&ev); err != nil {
255				return false, 0, err
256			}
257			if computeHash(&ev) != ev.Hash {
258				return false, ev.Seq, nil // content tampered
259			}
260			if !first {
261				if ev.Seq != prevSeq+1 || ev.PrevHash != prevHash {
262					return false, ev.Seq, nil // linkage broken
263				}
264			}
265			prevHash, prevSeq, first = ev.Hash, ev.Seq, false
266		}
267		return true, 0, cur.Err()
268	}
269	
270	// LatestSeq returns the current chain head sequence (0 = empty).
271	func (l *Ledger) LatestSeq(ctx context.Context) (int64, error) {
272		seq, _, err := l.head(ctx)
273		return seq, err
274	}
275

1	// Package orgscope answers the RBAC question "is this resource inside the
2	// caller's organisational scope?" in O(1) DB reads. Org units denormalise
3	// their ancestor chain into Path, so scope checking is a set-membership test

6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"errors"
10		"sync"
11		"time"
12	
13		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson"

18		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/httpx"
19	)
20	
21	const collection = "org_units"
22	
23	type cachedOrg struct {
24		org domain.OrgUnit
25		at  time.Time
26	}
27	
28	// Resolver caches org units briefly (the tree changes rarely, reads are hot).
29	type Resolver struct {
30		coll *mongo.Collection
31		ttl  time.Duration
32	
33		mu    sync.RWMutex
34		cache map[string]cachedOrg
35	}
36	
37	// NewResolver binds the resolver to the database.
38	func NewResolver(db *mongo.Database) *Resolver {
39		return &Resolver{
40			coll:  db.Collection(collection),
41			ttl:   60 * time.Second,
42			cache: make(map[string]cachedOrg),
43		}
44	}
45	
46	// Get returns an org unit by ID (cached).
47	func (r *Resolver) Get(ctx context.Context, id string) (*domain.OrgUnit, error) {
48		r.mu.RLock()
49		c, ok := r.cache[id]
50		r.mu.RUnlock()
51		if ok && time.Since(c.at) < r.ttl {
52			org := c.org
53			return &org, nil
54		}
55	
56		var org domain.OrgUnit
57		err := r.coll.FindOne(ctx, bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: id}}).Decode(&org)
58		if errors.Is(err, mongo.ErrNoDocuments) {
59			return nil, httpx.NotFound("org unit " + id)
60		}
61		if err != nil {
62			return nil, httpx.Internal(err)
63		}
64	
65		r.mu.Lock()
66		r.cache[id] = cachedOrg{org: org, at: time.Now()}
67		r.mu.Unlock()
68		return &org, nil
69	}
70	
71	// Invalidate drops a cached entry (call after updates).
72	func (r *Resolver) Invalidate(id string) {
73		r.mu.Lock()
74		delete(r.cache, id)
75		r.mu.Unlock()
76	}
77	
78	// InScope reports whether target sits at-or-below scope in the hierarchy:
79	// true when scope == target, or scope appears in target's ancestor Path.
80	func (r *Resolver) InScope(ctx context.Context, scopeOrgID, targetOrgID string) (bool, error) {
81		if scopeOrgID == targetOrgID {
82			return true, nil
83		}
84		target, err := r.Get(ctx, targetOrgID)
85		if err != nil {
86			return false, err
87		}
88		for _, ancestor := range target.Path {
89			if ancestor == scopeOrgID {
90				return true, nil
91			}
92		}
93		return false, nil
94	}
95	
96	// RequireInScope enforces the actor's org scope over a target org unit.
97	// SUPER_ADMIN and STATE_AUDITOR (read-wide roles rooted at the federation)
98	// pass automatically; everyone else needs ancestry.
99	func (r *Resolver) RequireInScope(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, targetOrgID string) error {
100		if actor.RoleCode == domain.RoleSuperAdmin || actor.RoleCode == domain.RoleStateAuditor {
101			return nil
102		}
103		if actor.OrgUnitID == "" {
104			return httpx.Forbidden("role token with org scope required")
105		}
106		ok, err := r.InScope(ctx, actor.OrgUnitID, targetOrgID)
107		if err != nil {
108			return err
109		}
110		if !ok {
111			return httpx.Forbidden("resource is outside your organisational scope")
112		}
113		return nil
114	}

1	package auth

3	import (
4		"crypto/hmac"

13	
14	// GenerateNumericOTP returns a cryptographically random n-digit code.
15	func GenerateNumericOTP(n int) (string, error) {
16		if n <= 0 || n > 10 {
17			return "", fmt.Errorf("otp length out of range: %d", n)
18		}
19		max := big.NewInt(1)
20		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
21			max.Mul(max, big.NewInt(10))
22		}
23		v, err := rand.Int(rand.Reader, max)
24		if err != nil {
25			return "", fmt.Errorf("otp entropy: %w", err)
26		}
27		return fmt.Sprintf("%0*d", n, v), nil
28	}
29	
30	// HMACHash returns hex(HMAC-SHA256(secret, parts joined by '|')). Used for
31	// OTP codes (keyed to the phone) and refresh tokens, so a DB leak alone
32	// reveals no usable credentials.
33	func HMACHash(secret string, parts ...string) string {
34		mac := hmac.New(sha256.New, []byte(secret))
35		for i, p := range parts {
36			if i > 0 {
37				mac.Write([]byte{'|'})
38			}
39			mac.Write([]byte(p))
40		}
41		return hex.EncodeToString(mac.Sum(nil))
42	}
43	
44	// ConstantTimeEqual compares two hex digests without timing leaks.
45	func ConstantTimeEqual(a, b string) bool {
46		return subtle.ConstantTimeCompare([]byte(a), []byte(b)) == 1
47	}
48	
49	// RandomToken returns a URL-safe random token with nBytes of entropy —
50	// used for opaque refresh tokens.
51	func RandomToken(nBytes int) (string, error) {
52		buf := make([]byte, nBytes)
53		if _, err := rand.Read(buf); err != nil {
54			return "", fmt.Errorf("token entropy: %w", err)
55		}
56		return base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString(buf), nil
57	}

1	// Package httpx is the HTTP toolkit shared by every module: typed errors,
2	// uniform JSON envelopes, strict request decoding, pagination.
3	package httpx
4	
5	import (
6		"fmt"
7		"net/http"
8	)
9	
10	// AppError is the single error type handlers return. It carries the HTTP
11	// status plus a stable machine-readable code the frontend can switch on.
12	type AppError struct {
13		Status  int    `json:"-"`
14		Code    string `json:"code"`
15		Message string `json:"message"`
16		Details any    `json:"details,omitempty"`
17	
18		cause error // wrapped internal error — logged server-side, never serialised
19	}
20	
21	func (e *AppError) Error() string {
22		return fmt.Sprintf("%d %s: %s", e.Status, e.Code, e.Message)
23	}
24	
25	// WithDetails returns a copy carrying extra structured context.
26	func (e *AppError) WithDetails(d any) *AppError {
27		cp := *e
28		cp.Details = d
29		return &cp
30	}
31	
32	func newErr(status int, code, msg string) *AppError {
33		return &AppError{Status: status, Code: code, Message: msg}
34	}
35	
36	// Constructors — use these instead of raw errors in handlers/services.
37	
38	func BadRequest(code, msg string) *AppError { return newErr(http.StatusBadRequest, code, msg) }
39	
40	func Unauthorized(msg string) *AppError { return newErr(http.StatusUnauthorized, "UNAUTHORIZED", msg) }
41	
42	func Forbidden(msg string) *AppError { return newErr(http.StatusForbidden, "FORBIDDEN", msg) }
43	
44	func NotFound(resource string) *AppError {
45		return newErr(http.StatusNotFound, "NOT_FOUND", resource+" not found")
46	}
47	
48	func Conflict(code, msg string) *AppError { return newErr(http.StatusConflict, code, msg) }
49	
50	func Unprocessable(code, msg string) *AppError {
51		return newErr(http.StatusUnprocessableEntity, code, msg)
52	}
53	
54	func TooManyRequests(msg string) *AppError {
55		return newErr(http.StatusTooManyRequests, "RATE_LIMITED", msg)
56	}
57	
58	// Internal wraps an unexpected error. The cause is logged server-side but
59	// never leaked to the client.
60	func Internal(err error) *AppError {
61		e := newErr(http.StatusInternalServerError, "INTERNAL", "internal server error")
62		e.cause = err
63		return e
64	}
65	
66	func (e *AppError) Unwrap() error { return e.cause }
