1	// Package provenance implements the append-only, hash-chained event ledger —
2	// the source of truth for milk traceability (blueprint §7). Every link in the
3	// pour→QR chain is an immutable Event whose SHA-256 hash covers the previous
4	// event's hash, so history cannot be quietly rewritten (tamper-evidence,
5	// FSSAI recall-grade audit).
6	//
7	// Corrections are NEW events referencing the superseded entity — nothing is
8	// ever updated or deleted in this collection.
9	package provenance
10	
11	import (
12		"context"
13		"crypto/sha256"
14		"encoding/hex"
15		"encoding/json"
16		"errors"
17		"fmt"
18		"strconv"
19		"strings"
20		"time"
21	
22		"github.com/google/uuid"
23		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson"
24		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo"
25		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo/options"
26	)
27	
28	const collection = "provenance_events"
29	
30	// Ref is a directed edge to another entity in the trace graph
31	// (e.g. a consignment event referencing the pours it aggregates).
32	type Ref struct {
33		EntityType string `bson:"entity_type" json:"entity_type"`
34		EntityID   string `bson:"entity_id"   json:"entity_id"`
35		Relation   string `bson:"relation"    json:"relation"` // aggregates | supersedes | tested | yields | labels ...
36	}
37	
38	// ActorRef records who caused the event.
39	type ActorRef struct {
40		PartyID  string `bson:"party_id"  json:"party_id"`
41		RoleCode string `bson:"role_code" json:"role_code"`
42	}
43	
44	// Event is one immutable link in the ledger.
45	type Event struct {
46		ID         string         `bson:"_id"         json:"id"`
47		Seq        int64          `bson:"seq"         json:"seq"`
48		Type       string         `bson:"type"        json:"type"`
49		EntityType string         `bson:"entity_type" json:"entity_type"`
50		EntityID   string         `bson:"entity_id"   json:"entity_id"`
51		Refs       []Ref          `bson:"refs,omitempty"    json:"refs,omitempty"`
52		Actor      ActorRef       `bson:"actor"       json:"actor"`
53		OrgUnitID  string         `bson:"org_unit_id,omitempty" json:"org_unit_id,omitempty"`
54		Payload    map[string]any `bson:"payload,omitempty"     json:"payload,omitempty"`
55		TS         time.Time      `bson:"ts"          json:"ts"`
56		PrevHash   string         `bson:"prev_hash"   json:"prev_hash"`
57		Hash       string         `bson:"hash"        json:"hash"`
58	}
59	
60	// AppendInput describes a new event to chain.
61	type AppendInput struct {
62		Type       string
63		EntityType string
64		EntityID   string
65		Refs       []Ref
66		Actor      ActorRef
67		OrgUnitID  string
68		Payload    map[string]any
69	}
70	
71	// Ledger appends to and reads the hash chain.
72	type Ledger struct {
73		coll *mongo.Collection
74	}
75	
76	// NewLedger binds the ledger to the database.
77	func NewLedger(db *mongo.Database) *Ledger {
78		return &Ledger{coll: db.Collection(collection)}
79	}
80	
81	// genesisHash anchors the chain before the first event.
82	const genesisHash = "GENESIS"
83	
84	// Append chains a new event. Concurrency-safe without transactions: it reads
85	// the current head, computes seq+hash optimistically, and relies on the
86	// unique index on `seq` — a duplicate-key collision means another writer won
87	// the slot, so we re-read and retry.
88	func (l *Ledger) Append(ctx context.Context, in AppendInput) (*Event, error) {
89		const maxRetries = 12
90		for attempt := 0; attempt < maxRetries; attempt++ {
91			seq, prevHash, err := l.head(ctx)
92			if err != nil {
93				return nil, err
94			}
95			ev := &Event{
96				ID:         uuid.NewString(),
97				Seq:        seq + 1,
98				Type:       in.Type,
99				EntityType: in.EntityType,
100				EntityID:   in.EntityID,
101				Refs:       in.Refs,
102				Actor:      in.Actor,
103				OrgUnitID:  in.OrgUnitID,
104				Payload:    in.Payload,
105				// Millisecond precision: BSON datetimes store ms, so the persisted
106				// TS must equal the hashed TS or re-verification would break.
107				TS:       time.Now().UTC().Truncate(time.Millisecond),
108				PrevHash: prevHash,
109			}
110			ev.Hash = computeHash(ev)
111	
112			if _, err := l.coll.InsertOne(ctx, ev); err != nil {
113				if mongo.IsDuplicateKeyError(err) {
114					continue // lost the seq race — retry against the new head
115				}
116				return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance append: %w", err)
117			}
118			return ev, nil
119		}
120		return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance append: gave up after %d seq collisions", 12)
121	}
122	
123	// head returns the latest (seq, hash), or (0, GENESIS) for an empty chain.
124	func (l *Ledger) head(ctx context.Context) (int64, string, error) {
125		var last Event
126		err := l.coll.FindOne(ctx, bson.D{},
127			options.FindOne().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: -1}}),
128		).Decode(&last)
129		if errors.Is(err, mongo.ErrNoDocuments) {
130			return 0, genesisHash, nil
131		}
132		if err != nil {
133			return 0, "", fmt.Errorf("provenance head: %w", err)
134		}
135		return last.Seq, last.Hash, nil
136	}
137	
138	// computeHash covers everything that matters: position, linkage, content.
139	// Payload is canonicalised via encoding/json (map keys are sorted) and the
140	// timestamp to millisecond precision (BSON datetime resolution), so the
141	// digest is deterministic across a MongoDB round trip.
142	func computeHash(ev *Event) string {
143		payloadJSON, _ := json.Marshal(ev.Payload)
144		refParts := make([]string, 0, len(ev.Refs))
145		for _, r := range ev.Refs {
146			refParts = append(refParts, r.EntityType+":"+r.EntityID+":"+r.Relation)
147		}
148		material := strings.Join([]string{
149			ev.PrevHash,
150			strconv.FormatInt(ev.Seq, 10),
151			ev.Type,
152			ev.EntityType,
153			ev.EntityID,
154			strings.Join(refParts, ","),
155			ev.Actor.PartyID,
156			ev.Actor.RoleCode,
157			ev.OrgUnitID,
158			string(payloadJSON),
159			ev.TS.UTC().Truncate(time.Millisecond).Format(time.RFC3339Nano),
160		}, "|")
161		sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(material))
162		return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
163	}
164	
165	// EventsForEntity returns an entity's own timeline in chain order.
166	func (l *Ledger) EventsForEntity(ctx context.Context, entityType, entityID string) ([]Event, error) {
167		cur, err := l.coll.Find(ctx,
168			bson.D{{Key: "entity_type", Value: entityType}, {Key: "entity_id", Value: entityID}},
169			options.Find().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: 1}}),
170		)
171		if err != nil {
172			return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance events for %s/%s: %w", entityType, entityID, err)
173		}
174		var out []Event
175		if err := cur.All(ctx, &out); err != nil {
176			return nil, err
177		}
178		return out, nil
179	}
180	
181	// Trace walks the provenance graph UPSTREAM from an entity: its events, plus
182	// (recursively) the events of everything those events reference. This is how
183	// a consumer QR resolves back to the contributing samiti set, and how a failed
184	// aflatoxin test walks back to source DCSes (blueprint §8.3).
185	func (l *Ledger) Trace(ctx context.Context, entityType, entityID string, maxDepth int) ([]Event, error) {
186		if maxDepth <= 0 {
187			maxDepth = 10
188		}
189		const hardEventCap = 2000
190	
191		type node struct{ etype, eid string }
192		visited := map[node]bool{}
193		frontier := []node{{entityType, entityID}}
194		var all []Event
195	
196		for depth := 0; depth < maxDepth && len(frontier) > 0; depth++ {
197			var next []node
198			for _, n := range frontier {
199				if visited[n] {
200					continue
201				}
202				visited[n] = true
203				evs, err := l.EventsForEntity(ctx, n.etype, n.eid)
204				if err != nil {
205					return nil, err
206				}
207				for _, ev := range evs {
208					all = append(all, ev)
209					if len(all) >= hardEventCap {
210						return all, nil
211					}
212					for _, ref := range ev.Refs {
213						nn := node{ref.EntityType, ref.EntityID}
214						if !visited[nn] {
215							next = append(next, nn)
216						}
217					}
218				}
219			}
220			frontier = next
221		}
222		return all, nil
223	}
224	
225	// DownstreamRefs finds events that reference the given entity — used to walk
226	// FORWARD (e.g. "which batches consumed this blocked BMC lot?").
227	func (l *Ledger) DownstreamRefs(ctx context.Context, entityID string) ([]Event, error) {
228		cur, err := l.coll.Find(ctx,
229			bson.D{{Key: "refs.entity_id", Value: entityID}},
230			options.Find().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: 1}}),
231		)
232		if err != nil {
233			return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance downstream of %s: %w", entityID, err)
234		}
235		var out []Event
236		if err := cur.All(ctx, &out); err != nil {
237			return nil, err
238		}
239		return out, nil
240	}
241	
242	// VerifyChain re-derives every hash in [fromSeq, toSeq] and checks linkage.
243	// Returns (true, 0) when intact, or (false, seq) of the first broken link.
244	func (l *Ledger) VerifyChain(ctx context.Context, fromSeq, toSeq int64) (bool, int64, error) {
245		filter := bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$gte", Value: fromSeq}, {Key: "$lte", Value: toSeq}}}}
246		cur, err := l.coll.Find(ctx, filter, options.Find().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: 1}}))
247		if err != nil {
248			return false, 0, fmt.Errorf("provenance verify: %w", err)
249		}
250		defer cur.Close(ctx)
251	
252		prevHash := ""
253		prevSeq := int64(0)
254		first := true
255		for cur.Next(ctx) {
256			var ev Event
257			if err := cur.Decode(&ev); err != nil {
258				return false, 0, err
259			}
260			if computeHash(&ev) != ev.Hash {
261				return false, ev.Seq, nil // content tampered
262			}
263			if !first {
264				if ev.Seq != prevSeq+1 || ev.PrevHash != prevHash {
265					return false, ev.Seq, nil // linkage broken
266				}
267			}
268			prevHash, prevSeq, first = ev.Hash, ev.Seq, false
269		}
270		return true, 0, cur.Err()
271	}
272	
273	// LatestSeq returns the current chain head sequence (0 = empty).
274	func (l *Ledger) LatestSeq(ctx context.Context) (int64, error) {
275		seq, _, err := l.head(ctx)
276		return seq, err
277	}

Confirmed the defect by reading the actual code. My verification:

**Route gate** (module.go:34): `r.With(middleware.RequireSession).Get("/active", h.getActiveRateChart)`. The parent route only adds `middleware.Authenticate(d.JWT)` (line 27). `RequireSession` (rbac.go:45-53) passes *any* authenticated actor — session-kind or role-kind, any role including CONSUMER, no org scope required.

**Handler** (handler.go:41-53): reads `dcs_id` straight from the query string and passes it to `svc.ResolveActiveChart(r.Context(), dcsID)`. The actor is never even fetched here — `requestActor(r)` is not called, so the service has no actor to scope-check against.

**Service** (service.go:101-138): `ResolveActiveChart(ctx, dcsID string)` — no `auth.Actor` parameter at all. It only verifies the org exists (`Orgs.Get`) and is of type DCS, then resolves the nearest active chart up the org path. No `RequireInScope`, no membership check.

**Payload** (domain/collection.go): `RateChart` serializes `base_rate_per_litre`, `fat_rate_per_point`, `snf_rate_per_point` as plain JSON fields — the full pricing policy is returned via `httpx.JSON`.

**Contrast confirms the outlier**: every sibling read/write path fetches the actor and calls `RequireInScope` on the target DCS — `CreateReading` (182), `ListReadings` (254), `CreatePour` (288), `SupersedePour` (466), `ListPours` (578), `GenerateInvoices` (617), `ListInvoices` (724), `GetInvoice` (757). `ResolveActiveChart` is the only DCS-scoped read that doesn't.

**Refutation attempts failed**: (a) The repo call `activeChartsForOrgs` uses org IDs derived from the requested DCS's own path — not the actor's scope — so there is no downstream scope filter. (b) `RequireSession` does not restrict to role tokens; even a bare session with no role selected passes. (c) There is no `RequireInScope` anywhere in the call chain.

**Concrete exploit**: A CONSUMER (or a SamitiSacheev scoped to DCS in state A) authenticates, obtains any valid token, then issues `GET /api/v1/collection/rate-charts/active?dcs_id=<any-DCS-id-in-state-B>`. The response is HTTP 200 with the full confidential pricing chart for that out-of-scope DCS. Iterating `dcs_id` enumerates every DCS's procurement pricing nationwide.

11	// AuditMutations records every state-changing request (non-GET/HEAD/OPTIONS)
12	// into the immutable audit trail: actor, action, status, IP, request ID.
13	// Runs after the handler so the final status code is captured; the write
14	// itself is async and adds no request latency.
15	func AuditMutations(rec *audit.Recorder) func(http.Handler) http.Handler {
16		return func(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
17			return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
18				if r.Method == http.MethodGet || r.Method == http.MethodHead || r.Method == http.MethodOptions {
19					next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
20					return
21				}
22				ww := chimw.NewWrapResponseWriter(w, r.ProtoMajor)
23				next.ServeHTTP(ww, r)
24	
25				rec.Record(r.Context(), audit.Entry{
26					Action:    "http." + r.Method + " " + r.URL.Path,
27					Status:    ww.Status(),
28					IP:        r.RemoteAddr,
29					RequestID: chimw.GetReqID(r.Context()),
30				})
31			})
32		}
33	}

50		if a, ok := auth.ActorFrom(ctx); ok {
51			if e.ActorPartyID == "" {
52				e.ActorPartyID = a.PartyID
53			}
54			if e.ActorRole == "" {
55				e.ActorRole = a.RoleCode
56			}
57		}
58		e.ID = uuid.NewString()
59		e.TS = time.Now().UTC()
60	
61		go func() {
62			writeCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
63			defer cancel()
64			if _, err := r.coll.InsertOne(writeCtx, e); err != nil {
65				r.log.Error("audit write failed", slog.String("action", e.Action), slog.Any("err", err))
66			}
67		}()
68	}

Adversarially VERIFY this claimed defect in /Users/divyanshmangla/parag-saathi-be (export PATH="/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH"). Read the actual code; try to REFUTE it. It is real only if you can name concrete inputs/state that misbehave. Claim: [medium] Unknown routes and disallowed methods return chi's plain-text defaults, breaking the uniform JSON error envelope @ internal/httpapi/router.go:25 — The router never sets r.NotFound(...) or r.MethodNotAllowed(...), so any unmatched path under /api/v1 (e.g. GET /api/v1/collection/invoice — a typo of /invoices) returns chi's default '404 page not found' as text/plain, and a wrong method (e.g. GET /api/v1/settlements/{id}/approve) returns a bare text 405 — neither carries the {"error":{code,message}} envelope every other response uses. Clients that parse the standard error envelope get a JSON parse failure instead of a machine-readable code. Same class of issue: chimw.Timeout(30s) (line 33) writes a bare, body-less 504 when a handler returns after deadline. Fix: register NotFound/MethodNotAllowed handlers that call httpx.Error with proper AppErrors (404 NOT_FOUND / 405 METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED).

1	// Package httpapi assembles the HTTP surface: global middleware, operational
2	// endpoints (health/readiness/metrics/version), and the /api/v1 tree where
3	// every domain module mounts its routes.
4	package httpapi
5	
6	import (
7		"context"
8		"net/http"
9		"time"
10	
11		"github.com/go-chi/chi/v5"
12		chimw "github.com/go-chi/chi/v5/middleware"
13		"github.com/prometheus/client_golang/prometheus/promhttp"
14	
15		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/deps"
16		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/httpx"
17		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/middleware"
18	)
19	
20	// Version is stamped via -ldflags at release build time.
21	var Version = "0.1.0-dev"
22	
23	// New builds the fully wired HTTP handler.
24	func New(d *deps.Deps) http.Handler {
25		r := chi.NewRouter()
26	
27		// Order matters: recover innermost-last so panics in anything above are caught.
28		r.Use(chimw.RequestID)
29		r.Use(chimw.RealIP)
30		r.Use(middleware.Metrics)
31		r.Use(middleware.PerIPRateLimit(d.Cfg.RateLimitRPS, d.Cfg.RateLimitBurst))
32		r.Use(chimw.Recoverer)
33		r.Use(chimw.Timeout(30 * time.Second))
34	
35		// Operational endpoints — outside /api/v1, never authenticated.
36		r.Get("/healthz", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
37			httpx.JSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]string{"status": "ok"})
38		})
39		r.Get("/readyz", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
40			ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(r.Context(), 2*time.Second)
41			defer cancel()
42			if err := d.DB.Client().Ping(ctx, nil); err != nil {
43				httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Internal(err))
44				return
45			}
46			httpx.JSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]string{"status": "ready"})
47		})
48		r.Handle("/metrics", promhttp.Handler())
49		r.Get("/version", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
50			httpx.JSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]string{"version": Version, "service": "saathi-backend"})
51		})
52	
53		r.Route("/api/v1", func(api chi.Router) {
54			api.Use(middleware.AuditMutations(d.Audit))
55			RegisterModules(api, d)
56		})
57	
58		return r
59	}
60

// MVU (1962 Mobile Veterinary Unit) dispatch statuses (blueprint §10).
const (
	MVUCaseRequested  = "REQUESTED"
	MVUCaseDispatched = "DISPATCHED"
	MVUCaseArrived    = "ARRIVED"
	MVUCaseClosed     = "CLOSED"
	MVUCaseCancelled  = "CANCELLED"
)

// MVUCase tracks an in-app "call 1962 MVU" request through to the visit log.
type MVUCase struct {
	ID             string     `bson:"_id"        json:"id"`
	AnimalID       string     `bson:"animal_id,omitempty" json:"animal_id,omitempty"`
	FarmerPartyID  string     `bson:"farmer_party_id"     json:"farmer_party_id"`
	DCSID          string     `bson:"dcs_id"     json:"dcs_id"`
	Symptoms       string     `bson:"symptoms,omitempty"  json:"symptoms,omitempty"`
	Status         string     `bson:"status"     json:"status"`
	VetPartyID     string     `bson:"vet_party_id,omitempty"    json:"vet_party_id,omitempty"`
	DriverPartyID  string     `bson:"driver_party_id,omitempty" json:"driver_party_id,omitempty"`
	VisitNotes     string     `bson:"visit_notes,omitempty"     json:"visit_notes,omitempty"`
	HealthEventIDs []string   `bson:"health_event_ids,omitempty" json:"health_event_ids,omitempty"`
	RequestedAt    time.Time  `bson:"requested_at" json:"requested_at"`
	ClosedAt       *time.Time `bson:"closed_at,omitempty" json:"closed_at,omitempty"`
}

// EducationContent is a vernacular audio/video/infographic item for the
// education hub (blueprint §10) — icon-navigable, pre-cacheable offline.
type EducationContent struct {
	ID          string    `bson:"_id"      json:"id"`
	Topic       string    `bson:"topic"    json:"topic"` // CLEAN_MILKING, FEED_RATION, BREED_CARE...
	Title       string    `bson:"title"    json:"title"`
	Language    string    `bson:"language" json:"language"`
	MediaType   string    `bson:"media_type" json:"media_type"` // AUDIO, VIDEO, INFOGRAPHIC
	MediaURL    string    `bson:"media_url"  json:"media_url"`
	DurationSec int       `bson:"duration_sec,omitempty" json:"duration_sec,omitempty"`
	Published   bool      `bson:"published"  json:"published"`
	CreatedAt   time.Time `bson:"created_at" json:"created_at"`
}

Adversarially VERIFY this claimed defect in /Users/divyanshmangla/parag-saathi-be (export PATH="/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH"). Read the actual code; try to REFUTE it. It is real only if you can name concrete inputs/state that misbehave. Claim: [medium] orgs list meta uses "count" (items on page) where every other module returns "total" @ internal/modules/orgs/models.go:47 — Eight modules (identity, cattle, plant, quality, logistics, platformops, settlement, publictrace) return list meta as {limit, offset, total} where total is the full matching count. orgs alone returns {limit, offset, count} where Count = len(page items) (handler.go:80,107,123). A shared frontend paginator reading meta.total gets undefined on GET /orgs, GET /orgs/{id}/children and GET /orgs/{id}/members, and cannot compute page count; conversely meta.count is not the collection size (a directory of 500 DCS units with limit=50 reports count:50 and no way to know 500 exist). Fix: return the collection total under the platform-wide "total" key (add a repo count query), keeping count only if additionally needed.

// Package eventbus is the in-process pub/sub seam between modules
// (e.g. settlement executed → notifications module queues the SMS).
// It deliberately mirrors a message-broker API: when the platform splits
// into microservices, this interface is re-implemented over Kafka/NATS
// (blueprint §15) without touching module code.
package eventbus

import (
	"context"
	"log/slog"
	"sync"
	"time"
)

// Topics published across module seams.
const (
	TopicPourRecorded       = "pour.recorded"
	TopicInvoiceIssued      = "invoice.issued"
	TopicGateBlocked        = "qc.gate_blocked"
	TopicSettlementExecuted = "settlement.executed"
	TopicPayoutCredited     = "payout.credited"
	TopicMVUDispatched      = "mvu.dispatched"
)

// Handler consumes a published event. Payload types are documented per topic
// by the publishing module.
type Handler func(ctx context.Context, topic string, payload any)

// Bus is a minimal async pub/sub.
type Bus struct {
	log *slog.Logger

	mu   sync.RWMutex
	subs map[string][]Handler
}

// New builds an empty bus.
func New(log *slog.Logger) *Bus {
	return &Bus{log: log, subs: make(map[string][]Handler)}
}

// Subscribe registers a handler for a topic. Call during module wiring only
// (not concurrently with Publish traffic).
func (b *Bus) Subscribe(topic string, h Handler) {
	b.mu.Lock()
	defer b.mu.Unlock()
	b.subs[topic] = append(b.subs[topic], h)
}

// Publish dispatches asynchronously: each handler runs on its own goroutine
// with a bounded context and panic isolation, so a slow or broken subscriber
// can never stall the request path.
func (b *Bus) Publish(topic string, payload any) {
	b.mu.RLock()
	handlers := b.subs[topic]
	b.mu.RUnlock()

	for _, h := range handlers {
		h := h
		go func() {
			ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 15*time.Second)
			defer cancel()
			defer func() {
				if rec := recover(); rec != nil {
					b.log.Error("eventbus handler panic",
						slog.String("topic", topic), slog.Any("panic", rec))
				}
			}()
			h(ctx, topic, payload)
		}()
	}
}

1	// Package middleware carries the cross-cutting HTTP concerns: token
2	// authentication, role enforcement, audit capture, per-IP rate limiting,
3	// Prometheus metrics.
4	package middleware
5	
6	import (
7		"net/http"
8		"strings"
9	
10		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/auth"
11		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/httpx"
12	)
13	
14	// Authenticate verifies the Bearer token and installs the Actor on the
15	// request context. Requests without a valid token are rejected — public
16	// routes simply don't mount this middleware.
17	func Authenticate(jwtm *auth.JWTManager) func(http.Handler) http.Handler {
18		return func(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
19			return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
20				header := r.Header.Get("Authorization")
21				token, ok := strings.CutPrefix(header, "Bearer ")
22				if !ok || token == "" {
23					httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Unauthorized("missing bearer token"))
24					return
25				}
26				claims, err := jwtm.Parse(token)
27				if err != nil {
28					httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Unauthorized("invalid or expired token"))
29					return
30				}
31				actor := auth.Actor{
32					PartyID:          claims.PartyID,
33					Phone:            claims.Phone,
34					KYCTier:          claims.KYCTier,
35					Kind:             claims.Kind,
36					RoleAssignmentID: claims.RoleAssignmentID,
37					RoleCode:         claims.RoleCode,
38					OrgUnitID:        claims.OrgUnitID,
39					OrgType:          claims.OrgType,
40				}
41				next.ServeHTTP(w, r.WithContext(auth.WithActor(r.Context(), actor)))
42			})
43		}
44	}

10	// envelope is the uniform success shape: {"data": ..., "meta": {...}?}.
11	type envelope struct {
12		Data any `json:"data"`
13		Meta any `json:"meta,omitempty"`
14	}
15	
16	type errEnvelope struct {
17		Error *AppError `json:"error"`
18	}

30	// Error writes the standard error envelope. Unexpected (non-AppError) errors
31	// become an opaque 500 and the cause is logged with the request context.
32	func Error(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, err error) {
33		var ae *AppError
34		if !errors.As(err, &ae) {
35			ae = Internal(err)
36		}
37		if ae.Status >= 500 {
38			slog.ErrorContext(r.Context(), "request failed",
39				slog.String("method", r.Method),
40				slog.String("path", r.URL.Path),
41				slog.String("code", ae.Code),
42				slog.Any("cause", ae.CauseOrSelf()),
43			)
44		}
45		writeJSON(w, ae.Status, errEnvelope{Error: ae})
46	}

48	// CauseOrSelf returns the wrapped cause if present, else the error itself.
49	func (e *AppError) CauseOrSelf() error {
50		if e.cause != nil {
51			return e.cause
52		}
53		return e
54	}

56	func writeJSON(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, v any) {
57		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json; charset=utf-8")
58		w.WriteHeader(status)
59		_ = json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(v)

```text
1	// Package eventbus is the in-process pub/sub seam between modules
2	// (e.g. settlement executed → notifications module queues the SMS).
3	// It deliberately mirrors a message-broker API: when the platform splits
4	// into microservices, this interface is re-implemented over Kafka/NATS
5	// (blueprint §15) without touching module code.
6	package eventbus
7	
8	import (
9		"context"
10		"log/slog"
11		"sync"
12		"time"
13	)
14	
15	// Topics published across module seams.
16	const (
17		TopicPourRecorded       = "pour.recorded"
18		TopicInvoiceIssued      = "invoice.issued"
19		TopicGateBlocked        = "qc.gate_blocked"
20		TopicSettlementExecuted = "settlement.executed"
21		TopicPayoutCredited     = "payout.credited"
22		TopicMVUDispatched      = "mvu.dispatched"
23	)
24	
25	// Handler consumes a published event. Payload types are documented per topic
26	// by the publishing module.
27	type Handler func(ctx context.Context, topic string, payload any)
28	
29	// Bus is a minimal async pub/sub.
30	type Bus struct {
31		log *slog.Logger
32	
33		mu   sync.RWMutex
34		subs map[string][]Handler
35	}
36	
37	// New builds an empty bus.
38	func New(log *slog.Logger) *Bus {
39		return &Bus{log: log, subs: make(map[string][]Handler)}
40	}
41	
42	// Subscribe registers a handler for a topic. Call during module wiring only
43	// (not concurrently with Publish traffic).
44	func (b *Bus) Subscribe(topic string, h Handler) {
45		b.mu.Lock()
46		defer b.mu.Unlock()
47		b.subs[topic] = append(b.subs[topic], h)
48	}
49	
50	// Publish dispatches asynchronously: each handler runs on its own goroutine
51	// with a bounded context and panic isolation, so a slow or broken subscriber
52	// can never stall the request path.
53	func (b *Bus) Publish(topic string, payload any) {
54		b.mu.RLock()
55		handlers := b.subs[topic]
56		b.mu.RUnlock()
57	
58		for _, h := range handlers {
59			h := h
60			go func() {
61				ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 15*time.Second)
62				defer cancel()
63				defer func() {
64					if rec := recover(); rec != nil {
65						b.log.Error("eventbus handler panic",
66							slog.String("topic", topic), slog.Any("panic", rec))
67					}
68				}()
69				h(ctx, topic, payload)
70			}()
71		}
72	}
73

232	// decodeBusPayload structurally re-decodes a bus payload into this module's
233	// mirror struct — modules never import each other's types (module contract).
234	func decodeBusPayload(payload any, dst any) error {
235		raw, err := json.Marshal(payload)
236		if err != nil {
237			return fmt.Errorf("marshal bus payload: %w", err)
238		}
239		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, dst); err != nil {

241		}
242		return nil
243	}

273		orgUnitID, err := s.repo.subjectOrgUnit(ctx, event.SubjectType, event.SubjectID)

277		}
278		union, err := s.unionAncestor(ctx, orgUnitID)

281				slog.String("org_unit_id", orgUnitID), slog.Any("err", err))
282			return
283		}
284		if union == nil {
285			s.deps.Log.Error("platformops: gate_blocked org has no union ancestor",
286				slog.String("org_unit_id", orgUnitID))
287			return
288		}
289	
290		supervisors, err := s.repo.listActiveRoleHolders(ctx, union.ID, domain.RoleUnionFieldSupervisor)
291		if err != nil {

293			return
294		}

296		params := map[string]string{

302		now := time.Now().UTC()

304		for _, assignment := range supervisors {

package middleware_test

import (

// Mirrors the exact mounting in internal/httpapi/router.go: an outer
// middleware at the /api/v1 level (like AuditMutations) reading
// r.Context() after next.ServeHTTP, with Authenticate-style context
// injection happening inside the module subtree.
func TestOuterMiddlewareSeesNoActor(t *testing.T) {
	r := chi.NewRouter()

	var outerSawActor, innerSawActor bool
	var outerActor auth.Actor

		// Stand-in for AuditMutations: reads r.Context() after handler runs,

32	func Error(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, err error) {
33		var ae *AppError
34		if !errors.As(err, &ae) {
35			ae = Internal(err)
36		}
37		if ae.Status >= 500 {

41				slog.String("code", ae.Code),
42				slog.Any("cause", ae.CauseOrSelf()),
43			)
44		}
45		writeJSON(w, ae.Status, errEnvelope{Error: ae})
46	}
47	
48	// CauseOrSelf returns the wrapped cause if present, else the error itself.
49	func (e *AppError) CauseOrSelf() error {
50		if e.cause != nil {

// pour (such pours are frozen — corrections must go through settlement).
func (r *repo) pourIsInvoiced(ctx context.Context, pourID string) (bool, error) {
	n, err := r.invoices.CountDocuments(ctx, bson.D{
		{Key: "pour_ids", Value: pourID},
		{Key: "status", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$ne", Value: domain.InvoiceStatusHold}}},
	})

		return false, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("count invoices for pour: %w", err))

import (

type MVUCase struct {
	ID             string     `json:"id"`
	AnimalID       string     `json:"animal_id,omitempty"`
	FarmerPartyID  string     `json:"farmer_party_id"`
	DCSID          string     `json:"dcs_id"`
	Symptoms       string     `json:"symptoms,omitempty"`
	Status         string     `json:"status"`
	VetPartyID     string     `json:"vet_party_id,omitempty"`
	DriverPartyID  string     `json:"driver_party_id,omitempty"`
	VisitNotes     string     `json:"visit_notes,omitempty"`
	HealthEventIDs []string   `json:"health_event_ids,omitempty"`
	RequestedAt    time.Time  `json:"requested_at"`

}

// Exact copy of platformops mvuDispatchedEvent (models.go:105-113).
type mvuDispatchedEvent struct {
	CaseID        string `json:"case_id"`
	MVUCaseID     string `json:"mvu_case_id"`
	FarmerPartyID string `json:"farmer_party_id"`
	Phone         string `json:"phone"`
	AnimalID      string `json:"animal_id"`
	DCSID         string `json:"dcs_id"`
	ETA           string `json:"eta"`
}

func main() {
	payload := &MVUCase{
		ID:            "mvu-case-42",
		AnimalID:      "animal-7",
		FarmerPartyID: "farmer-9",
		DCSID:         "dcs-1",
		Status:        "DISPATCHED",
		RequestedAt:   time.Now().UTC(),
	}
	// decodeBusPayload logic (platformops/service.go:234-243)
	raw, _ := json.Marshal(payload)
	var event mvuDispatchedEvent
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &event); err != nil {
		fmt.Println("decode error:", err)
		return
	}
	caseID := event.CaseID
	if caseID == "" {
		caseID = event.MVUCaseID
	}
	fmt.Printf("addressee check passes: %v (FarmerPartyID=%q)\n",
		!(event.FarmerPartyID == "" && event.Phone == ""), event.FarmerPartyID)
	fmt.Printf("resolved case_id param: %q\n", caseID)
	fmt.Printf("rendered SMS: %q\n",
		fmt.Sprintf("MVU 1962 van dispatched for your animal (case %s). Please stay reachable. - Saathi", caseID))
}

func TestUnmatchedRouteBodies(t *testing.T) {
	// Disconnected client: never dialed for these requests.
	client, err := mongo.Connect(context.Background(), options.Client().ApplyURI("mongodb://127.0.0.1:1/?connectTimeoutMS=100&serverSelectionTimeoutMS=100"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	db := client.Database("verify")
	log := slog.Default()

	d := &deps.Deps{
		Cfg:    &config.Config{RateLimitRPS: 50, RateLimitBurst: 100},
		Log:    log,
		DB:     db,
		JWT:    auth.NewJWTManager("secret", time.Hour),
		Ledger: provenance.NewLedger(db),
		Audit:  audit.NewRecorder(db, log),
		Flags:  flags.NewService(db),
		Orgs:   orgscope.NewResolver(db),
		Bus:    eventbus.New(log),
	}
	h := New(d)

	cases := []struct {
		method, path string
	}{
		{"GET", "/api/v1/collection/invoice"},          // typo of /invoices -> 404
		{"GET", "/api/v1/settlements/abc123/approve"},  // POST-only route -> 405
		{"GET", "/api/v1/nope"},                        // unknown -> 404
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		req := httptest.NewRequest(c.method, c.path, nil)
		rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
		h.ServeHTTP(rec, req)
		t.Logf("%s %s -> status=%d content-type=%q body=%q",
			c.method, c.path, rec.Code, rec.Header().Get("Content-Type"), rec.Body.String())
		_ = http.StatusOK
	}
}

```

Repo /Users/divyanshmangla/parag-saathi-be. export PATH="/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH". Apply fixes for these CONFIRMED review findings (dedupe overlapping ones; keep domain/platform contracts canonical; no new deps):
1. [critical/correctness] GenerateInvoices silently drops pours recorded after a farmer's first daily invoice — farmers never get paid for them @ internal/modules/collection/service.go:668
   Invoices are unique per (farmer, DCS, invoice_date) (unique index in internal/platform/mongodb/indexes.go:113), but pours arrive in two shifts per day. If GenerateInvoices runs after the MORNING shift and again after EVENING (or any pour lands after the first run), the second run builds a new invoice for the farmer's not-yet-invoiced pours, hits the unique-index duplicate on insert, and treats it as a benign race: `resp.Existing++; continue` (lines 668-675). The evening pours are never added to the existing invoice and can never be invoiced by any later run — the money silently disappears from the same-day payment loop with a success response. Failure scenario: farmer pours 5L MORNING, staff runs generate (invoice issued for 5L), farmer pours 6L EVENING, staff runs generate again → response says Created=0/Existing=1, the 6L pour stays un-invoiced and unpaid forever.
   Suggested: In GenerateInvoices, stop treating a duplicate insert as fully benign. On duplicate=true, load the existing invoice for (farmerID, req.DCSID, dateKey) and merge the new pours into it instead of dropping them: if the existing invoice is still ISSUED (not PAID/settled/claimed by a settlement batch), atomically $push the new pour IDs and $inc total_quantity_litres/total_amount (rounding after), append a provenance event (e.g. EventInvoiceAmended with aggregates refs to the new pours), republish/notify, and count it as updated in the response. If the existing invoice is already PAID or claimed by a settlement batch, do not mutate it — either fail loudly (surface the un-invoiceable pours in the response so staff can act) or support supplemental invoices by widening the unique key (e.g. add a per-day sequence to the (farmer, dcs, invoice_date) index) so late pours get their own invoice. Alternatively/simply: replace insert-then-ignore with a findOneAndUpdate upsert keyed on (farmer_party_id, dcs_id, invoice_date) that $push-es pour_ids and $inc-s totals, guarded by status=ISSUED. Also add a regression test: pour morning, generate, pour evening, generate again, assert the evening pour ends up on an invoice.
2. [high/correctness] CreateBatch never claims BMC lots — the same DISPATCHED lot can be pooled into unlimited processing batches @ internal/modules/plant/service.go:319
   CreateBMCLot atomically claims its consignments (ClaimConsignments flips DELIVERED→ACCEPTED with the lot ID), but CreateBatch only reads each BMC lot and checks `canPoolBMCLot(lot.Status)` (status == DISPATCHED) without any status flip, batch stamp, or uniqueness guard. A BMC lot stays DISPATCHED forever after being pooled, so a second (or hundredth) CreateBatch call listing the same lot succeeds. Failure scenario: plant operator submits CreateBatch twice with the same bmc_lot_ids (double-click, retry after timeout) → two batches each counting the full InputLitres of the same physical milk, both with 'pools' provenance refs to the same lot — double-counted volume and a corrupted trace graph (one lot's milk 'became' two independent product lines). Also a race: two concurrent CreateBatch calls both pass the read-time check.
   Suggested: Mirror the ClaimConsignments pattern: add a terminal BMCLotStatusPooled (or stamp pooled_batch_id) and a repo method ClaimBMCLots(ctx, ids, batchID) that runs UpdateMany with filter {_id: {$in: ids}, status: DISPATCHED} and $set {status: POOLED, batch_id: batchID}, returning ModifiedCount. In CreateBatch, call it before InsertBatch and fail with a Conflict (rolling back / not inserting) if ModifiedCount != len(ids) — this atomically closes both the double-submit and the concurrent race. Optionally also add a client-supplied idempotency key on CreateBatchRequest with a unique index for safe retries.
3. [high/correctness] Settlement batch stuck permanently in EXECUTING on any mid-execution failure — farmers unpaid with no recovery path @ internal/modules/settlement/service.go:284
   Execute claims the batch via APPROVED→EXECUTING (line 284), then performs per-invoice work (latestBankMasked, insertPayout, markInvoicesPaid, transition to EXECUTED). Any error or process crash in that window (e.g. a Mongo error from latestBankMasked at line 302 returns immediately) leaves the batch in EXECUTING. A retry of POST /execute reloads the batch, and validateExecution (line 54) rejects anything not APPROVED with 409 'settlement batch is EXECUTING' — forever. Invoices stay SETTLEMENT_PENDING, payouts partially inserted, and no API can move the batch out of EXECUTING (Approve/Reject require PENDING_APPROVAL). The insertPayout duplicate-tolerant 'retry of an interrupted run' logic (repo.go:208) is unreachable because the state machine forbids re-entering Execute — confirming the retry path was intended but is impossible.
   Suggested: Make Execute re-entrant so the already-idempotent per-invoice logic is reachable. In validateExecution, accept both APPROVED and EXECUTING. In Execute, attempt the APPROVED->EXECUTING transition; if it does not match (ok == false), re-read the batch and proceed only if its status is EXECUTING (resume of an interrupted run), otherwise return the 409. The existing insertPayout duplicate-key tolerance plus payoutByInvoice reuse makes the payout loop safe to replay, and markInvoicesPaid/final transition are already idempotent-guarded. To prevent two concurrent executors resuming the same batch, stamp an executing_at (or lease token) on the APPROVED->EXECUTING claim and only allow resume when the lease is stale (e.g. older than a few minutes). Alternatively/additionally, on mid-execution error do a best-effort EXECUTING->FAILED transition using the already-defined domain.SettlementStatusFailed, and permit FAILED->EXECUTING re-execution.
4. [medium/correctness] CreatePour re-validates business state before the idempotency check, so offline replays of already-stored pours fail instead of returning the stored pour @ internal/modules/collection/service.go:293
   The client_event_id duplicate is only detected at insertPour (line 346), after farmerIsActiveMember (line 293), the plausibility gate, and resolveChartForPricing (line 309) have all re-run against *current* state. A replay of a pour that is already persisted therefore errors out whenever context changed since first sync: the farmer's role assignment was revoked or its valid_to lapsed → 422 FARMER_NOT_MEMBER; no chart currently covers the DCS → 422 NO_ACTIVE_RATE_CHART. In BatchSyncPours (line 422) the item is reported as ERROR even though the pour exists server-side, so the offline device keeps the record dirty and retries forever / surfaces a false sync failure. Idempotent replay should short-circuit on the stored client_event_id before state-dependent checks.
   Suggested: In CreatePour, after the cheap field validation (and optionally the RequireInScope check), short-circuit on the idempotency key before any state-dependent business checks: call s.repo.pourByClientEventID(ctx, req.ClientEventID); if found, return (existing, true, nil); if the error is a 404, proceed. Keep the existing insertPour duplicate handling as-is to cover the race where two concurrent requests both miss the lookup — the unique index remains the atomic backstop. This makes replays return the stored pour regardless of subsequent membership/rate-chart changes, so BatchSyncPours correctly reports DUPLICATE and offline devices can mark the record clean.
5. [medium/correctness] Pour insert + ledger append is not atomic: a provenance failure returns 500, and the retry reports success while the pour permanently lacks its ledger event @ internal/modules/collection/service.go:358
   CreatePour inserts the pour (line 346), then appends EventPourRecorded (recordPourProvenance, line 358). If the append fails (seq-collision retries exhausted, transient Mongo error), the client gets 500 with the pour already persisted. The natural retry hits the client_event_id duplicate path and returns the stored pour with idempotentReplay=true — a success — but the provenance append, eventbus publish, and farmer receipt SMS are never re-attempted. Result: a RECORDED, invoiceable pour with provenance_seq=0 and no EventPourRecorded in the hash-chained ledger, silently breaking the pour→QR trace and audit guarantees for that pour. There is no reconciliation job; contrast with the cattle module which deliberately makes ledger appends best-effort-with-logging.
   Suggested: Two complementary changes. (1) Heal on replay: in CreatePour's duplicate branch (internal/modules/collection/service.go:350-356), after fetching the existing pour, if existing.Status == domain.PourStatusRecorded && existing.ProvenanceSeq == 0, call s.recordPourProvenance(ctx, actor, existing) and, on success, s.d.Bus.Publish(eventbus.TopicPourRecorded, *existing) and queueFarmerSMS before returning (existing, true, nil); if the append fails again, return the 500 rather than a fake success, so the client keeps retrying until the saga completes. Idempotency of the append itself can be guarded by first checking Ledger.EventsForEntity(EntityMilkPour, existing.ID) for an EventPourRecorded, or by making recordPourProvenance skip the append when one exists. (2) Backstop reconciliation: add a small periodic job (or startup sweep) that finds pours with status=RECORDED and provenance_seq missing/0 older than a few minutes, appends the missing EventPourRecorded, and stamps the seq — covering clients that never retry. Apply the same replay-heal pattern to the identical windows in CreateReading, SupersedePour, and GenerateInvoices, or, if the team prefers the cattle module's stance, make the trade-off explicit and log loudly with a metric instead of returning 500.
6. [medium/correctness] Pours recorded after consignment creation are permanently excluded from every consignment — milk on the van missing from totals and traceability @ internal/modules/logistics/service.go:82
   createConsignment snapshots the shift's RECORDED pours (findRecordedPours, line 82) into PourIDs/TotalQuantityLitres at creation time, yet the OPEN status is documented as 'still accepting pours' (domain/logistics.go:7) and CreatePour has no guard against recording into a shift whose consignment already exists. The unique dcs+date+shift index means a second createConsignment returns 409 CONSIGNMENT_EXISTS, and there is no API to add pours to an OPEN consignment. Failure scenario: Sacheev creates the consignment at 09:50, a farmer pours at 09:55 (CreatePour succeeds normally) → that milk is physically loaded but absent from the consignment's pour_ids, litres, weighted fat/SNF and can_count; downstream BMC-lot litres understate reality and the pour's provenance chain dead-ends before the pooling boundary while it still gets invoiced.
   Suggested: Move the pour aggregation from the OPEN boundary to the seal boundary: in dispatchConsignment, re-run findRecordedPours/aggregatePours for the consignment's dcs+date+shift and update PourIDs, TotalQuantityLitres, CanCount, AvgFatPct, AvgSNFPct (and emit the pour refs on the dispatch provenance event or a supplemental event) before marking DISPATCHED — making the createConsignment snapshot provisional. Alternatively (or additionally, belt-and-braces), have CreatePour reject with a 409 (e.g. SHIFT_CONSIGNED) when a consignment already exists for that dcs_id+pour_date+shift, so milk can never be recorded into an already-pooled shift. Either approach must also cover SupersedePour, which can mutate the RECORDED pour set of an already-created consignment the same way.
7. [medium/correctness] Pour-receipt SMS renders an empty quantity: producer sends param "qty" but the renderer reads "quantity" @ internal/modules/platformops/service.go:164
   collection/service.go:363 queues TemplatePourReceipt with params {"qty", "rate", "amount"}, but renderSMS formats the message with p("quantity") (platformops/service.go:164-165). The nil-safe param lookup hides the mismatch, so every farmer pour-receipt SMS renders as 'L @ Rs 42.30 = Rs 444.15 credited to today's bill' with the litres missing (and the same in the Hindi line) — the primary anti-cheating receipt for low-literacy farmers omits the one number they need to verify. Invoice-issued SMS is also affected differently: collection sends "qty" (line 705) which the INVOICE_ISSUED template never uses (harmless), but the POUR_RECEIPT case is a live data loss in the rendered message.
   Suggested: Align the param key across producer and renderer. Simplest: in internal/modules/collection/service.go:363 change the map key "qty" to "quantity" (matching renderSMS). Alternatively change p("quantity") to p("qty") in internal/modules/platformops/service.go:164-165. Optionally also rename the unused "qty" at collection/service.go:705 or drop it. Add a unit test asserting renderSMS(TemplatePourReceipt, ...) with the exact params produced by RecordPour includes the litres value, to prevent key drift recurring.
8. [medium/correctness] MVU-dispatched SMS always shows an empty case reference: publisher emits MVUCase with json key "id" but the subscriber expects "case_id"/"mvu_case_id" @ internal/modules/platformops/models.go:106
   cattle/service.go:353 publishes the full *domain.MVUCase on TopicMVUDispatched; its ID marshals as json "id" (domain/cattle.go:78). platformops' mirror struct mvuDispatchedEvent only maps "case_id" and "mvu_case_id" (models.go:106-107), so CaseID and MVUCaseID are always empty after the structural re-decode, and onMVUDispatched (service.go:324-328) queues the SMS with params["case_id"]="". The farmer receives 'MVU 1962 van dispatched for your animal (case ).' with no case number to quote on the 1962 helpline. The ETA param is likewise never populated since MVUCase has no eta field.
   Suggested: Make the subscriber's mirror struct also accept the publisher's actual key: add `ID string `json:"id"`` to mvuDispatchedEvent in internal/modules/platformops/models.go and extend the fallback chain in onMVUDispatched (internal/modules/platformops/service.go:324-327) to `caseID := event.CaseID; if caseID == "" { caseID = event.MVUCaseID }; if caseID == "" { caseID = event.ID }`. Alternatively (cleaner contract), have cattle/service.go:353 publish a purpose-built event payload with explicit `case_id`, `farmer_party_id`, `animal_id`, `dcs_id` keys instead of the raw domain document, and add a test asserting the queued notification's params["case_id"] is non-empty after a dispatch. The eta param can be dropped from the template/mirror or left as-is until MVUCase actually carries an ETA.
9. [critical/authz] Plaintext login OTP exposed via GET /notifications → full account takeover by SUPPORT_AGENT @ internal/modules/platformops/service.go:107
   The login OTP is queued into the notifications outbox in cleartext: identity/service.go:136 sets Params: map[string]string{"otp": code} on a domain.Notification, and domain.Notification.Params is JSON-serialized (domain/notification.go, `json:"params,omitempty"`). listNotifications returns StoredNotification (which inlines domain.Notification, including Params) with no redaction, and the route GET /api/v1/notifications?phone=&status= (platformops/module.go:54-55) is open to RoleSupportAgent and takes an attacker-controlled `phone` filter. Attack: a SUPPORT_AGENT (a low-trust help-desk role) calls the PUBLIC, unauthenticated POST /api/v1/auth/otp/request for any victim phone (including SUPER_ADMIN / SAMITI_ADHYAKSH / farmer), then GET /notifications?phone=<victim>&status=QUEUED, reads Params.otp, and completes POST /auth/otp/verify to mint the victim's session token — impersonating any user in the system. The mock SMS worker also copies the OTP into meta.rendered_en/hi (service.go renderSMS TemplateOTP), so even SENT notifications keep leaking it. This defeats authentication for every account and breaks settlement dual-control (a support agent can take over an approver's account).
   Suggested: Stop exposing the cleartext OTP to the notifications read surface. Concrete options, ideally combined: (1) In platformops listNotifications (service.go/repo.go), project out or redact sensitive params for the OTP template — never return params.otp or meta.rendered_* for TemplateKey==domain.TemplateOTP; e.g. strip the "otp" key and blank the rendered lines before responding. (2) Restrict GET /api/v1/notifications to RoleSuperAdmin only (drop RoleSupportAgent from module.go:54), since a help-desk role has no need to read outbox message bodies. (3) Do not persist the raw OTP in the outbox at all: render the OTP SMS only at send time inside the worker/provider adapter, storing a non-reversible reference in the document rather than the plaintext code; the delivery worker can hold the code transiently without writing it to a readable collection. Also avoid writing the rendered OTP text into meta.rendered_en/hi for the OTP template.
10. [high/authz] Settlement payout-history IDOR: any DCS/union staff role can read any farmer's financials nationwide @ internal/modules/settlement/service.go:456
   PayoutHistory pins only FARMER tokens to their own party; for every other allowed role it uses the caller-supplied farmer_party_id verbatim with NO org-scope / DCS binding (no RequireInScope, no membership check) before calling repo.payoutsByFarmer. The route GET /api/v1/settlements/payouts (settlement/module.go:60-66) admits SAMITI_SACHEEV, SAMITI_ADHYAKSH, UNION_FIELD_SUPERVISOR, UNION_PRESIDENT and STATE_AUDITOR. Attack: a village SAMITI_SACHEEV enumerates or guesses farmer_party_id values and reads any farmer's full payout history — amount, UTR bank-transaction reference, masked bank account, credited timestamps — for farmers in other DCSes, unions and states, entirely outside their scope. Contrast collection.ListInvoices, which for staff requires a dcs_id and enforces RequireInScope; the payouts endpoint omits that control.
   Suggested: In PayoutHistory, for non-FARMER staff roles resolve the target farmer's DCS (via party/KYC lookup) and call s.orgs.RequireInScope(ctx, actor, farmerDCSID) before repo.payoutsByFarmer, mirroring Detail and collection.ListInvoices. Optionally require an explicit dcs_id param for staff and enforce that the farmer belongs to it.
11. [medium/authz] Cattle animal + health-history reads lack RequireInScope: cross-tenant read of animal health PII @ internal/modules/cattle/service.go:91
   canViewAnimal only blocks a FARMER from viewing animals they do not own; for the other route-allowed roles (VETERINARIAN, AI_TECH, MISSION_OFFICIAL) it applies no organisational scope check at all. GetAnimal (line 183) and ListHealthEvents therefore let a VETERINARIAN or AI_TECH — roles that are org-scoped to a single DCS/union — read ANY animal record and its full health/treatment/disease history (owner party id, Pashu Aadhaar, clinical details) anywhere in the federation, with no RequireInScope on animal.DCSID (unlike LogHealthEvent/SyncBharatPashudhan, which do call RequireInScope). Additionally, ListAnimals (line 176) only pins FARMER tokens and session-kind tokens to their own herd; any other role token (e.g. a CONSUMER who selected their role) is left unpinned and can enumerate the entire animal registry by owner/DCS. The in-code TODO only mentions future DPDP consent; the missing org-scope control is a separate, unaddressed authorization gap.
   Suggested: In GetAnimal and ListHealthEvents, after FindAnimalByID, add an org-scope check for non-owner roles, e.g. for callers that are not the owning FARMER call s.d.Orgs.RequireInScope(ctx, actor, animal.DCSID) (mirroring LogHealthEvent/SyncBharatPashudhan). Fold this into canViewAnimal by passing the resolver, or gate it in the service methods. In ListAnimals, stop leaving arbitrary role tokens unpinned: for any role that is not a wide-scope admin/auditor, constrain the query to the caller's org scope (RequireInScope on the requested dcs_id, and reject or scope-limit owner_party_id) instead of pinning only FARMER/session tokens — so a CONSUMER (or any narrowly-scoped role) cannot enumerate the whole registry.
12. [medium/authz] Active rate chart readable across scope by any authenticated user @ internal/modules/collection/module.go:34
   GET /api/v1/collection/rate-charts/active?dcs_id= is gated only by RequireSession (any authenticated party — including a CONSUMER or a farmer from another state), and the service ResolveActiveChart (collection/service.go:101) performs no RequireInScope check on the supplied dcs_id nor any membership check. Any logged-in user can therefore iterate dcs_id values and read the confidential procurement pricing policy (base rate per litre, fat/SNF component rates) of every DCS in the country, outside their organisational scope. Every other collection read path (readings, pours, invoices for staff) enforces RequireInScope on the target DCS; this one does not.

The same pattern (unindexed created_at sort) also affects logistics listConsignments/listTrips. Require a selective filter or extend the index catalog to cover these sort keys.
   Suggested: Extend the index catalog in internal/platform/mongodb/indexes.go to cover the sort keys: for CollBatchQRs add idx({product_lot_id:1, issued_at:-1}) (replacing the bare product_lot_id index) and idx({issued_at:-1}); for CollBMCLots add idx({date:-1, created_at:-1}) and idx({status:1, date:-1, created_at:-1}); for CollConsignments and CollRouteTrips add idx({created_at:-1}) plus status/filter-prefixed variants matching the actual filter combinations (e.g. {status:1, created_at:-1}, {dcs_id:1, created_at:-1}, {union_id:1, created_at:-1}, {van_rider_party_id:1, created_at:-1}). Alternatively (or additionally) require a selective filter — e.g. make product_lot_id mandatory in ListQRs and bmc_id or date mandatory in ListBMCLots — and use EstimatedDocumentCount instead of CountDocuments when the filter is empty.
29. [critical/contract] Audit middleware runs outside auth, so every HTTP mutation audit entry records an empty actor @ internal/platform/middleware/audit.go:25
   AuditMutations is mounted once at the /api/v1 level (internal/httpapi/router.go:54), but Authenticate is mounted per-module inside each subtree. Authenticate installs the Actor via next.ServeHTTP(w, r.WithContext(...)), which never propagates back to the outer middleware's request. AuditMutations then calls rec.Record(r.Context(), ...) on the ORIGINAL request context, so auth.ActorFrom(ctx) in Recorder.Record (internal/platform/audit/recorder.go:50) always misses and every 'http.POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE ...' audit entry persists with empty actor_party_id and actor_role. Concrete failure: a SUPER_ADMIN flips a feature flag via PUT /api/v1/admin/flags/x — the audit log shows the action, status and IP but no actor, and a STATE_AUDITOR query GET /audit/logs?actor_party_id=... can never match any HTTP mutation. This silently defeats the who-did-what audit contract (rbac.go:12 explicitly relies on it for break-glass SUPER_ADMIN accountability) and is unrecoverable retroactively. Fix: capture the actor after the handler runs by having Authenticate stash a mutable holder on the context before the module chain, or record from a response-writer wrapper that observes the inner request, or mount audit inside each module after Authenticate.
   Suggested: Any of the three proposed approaches works; the least invasive given this codebase: have AuditMutations install a mutable actor holder before running the chain, and have Authenticate fill it. Concretely: (1) in internal/platform/auth/actor.go add a holder type (e.g. `type actorHolder struct { a *Actor }` with ctx key + `WithActorHolder(ctx)` / `setHolder(ctx, Actor)` helpers); (2) in AuditMutations (audit.go), before next.ServeHTTP do `r = r.WithContext(auth.WithActorHolder(r.Context()))`, and after the handler read the holder to populate Entry.ActorPartyID/ActorRole explicitly; (3) in Authenticate (auth.go:41), in addition to WithActor, call the holder setter so the identity flows outward. Alternative equally valid fix: move AuditMutations out of router.go and mount it inside each module immediately after Authenticate (but that risks a module forgetting it — a router-level test asserting audit coverage would then be needed). Also add a regression test asserting that a mutation through an authenticated module route produces an audit Entry with a non-empty actor_party_id (inject a fake Recorder or extract the actor-resolution logic so it is testable without Mongo).
30. [high/contract] MVU-dispatched bus payload key mismatch: farmer SMS renders an empty case ID @ internal/modules/cattle/service.go:353
   cattle publishes the raw *domain.MVUCase on eventbus.TopicMVUDispatched; its JSON shape has the case ID under "id" (internal/domain/cattle.go:78). The platformops subscriber structurally decodes into mvuDispatchedEvent, which only accepts "case_id" or "mvu_case_id" (internal/modules/platformops/models.go:105-113) — the publisher matches neither, so event.CaseID and event.MVUCaseID are both empty. onMVUDispatched then queues the MVU_DISPATCHED SMS with params{case_id: ""}, and renderSMS produces 'MVU 1962 van dispatched for your animal (case ). Please stay reachable.' (internal/modules/platformops/service.go:161). Every dispatched 1962 MVU case sends the farmer a notification with a blank case reference. Fix: publish an explicit event struct with a case_id JSON tag (matching the tolerant subscriber), e.g. {case_id, farmer_party_id, animal_id, dcs_id}.
   Suggested: In internal/modules/cattle/service.go DispatchMVUCase, stop publishing the raw *domain.MVUCase and publish an explicit event payload whose JSON keys match the tolerant subscriber, e.g.:

	s.d.Bus.Publish(eventbus.TopicMVUDispatched, map[string]any{
		"case_id":         updated.ID,
		"farmer_party_id": updated.FarmerPartyID,
		"animal_id":       updated.AnimalID,
		"dcs_id":          updated.DCSID,
	})

(or a small named struct with `json:"case_id"` etc. tags, and update the doc comment at lines 320-321 accordingly). Alternatively/additionally, make platformops' mvuDispatchedEvent also accept the "id" key as a fallback — but publishing an explicit contract struct is the cleaner fix and matches how other topics (e.g. payout.credited) document their shapes. A regression test that round-trips the published payload through decodeBusPayload into mvuDispatchedEvent and asserts a non-empty case_id would lock the cross-module contract in place.
31. [medium/contract] Unknown routes and disallowed methods return chi's plain-text defaults, breaking the uniform JSON error envelope @ internal/httpapi/router.go:25
   The router never sets r.NotFound(...) or r.MethodNotAllowed(...), so any unmatched path under /api/v1 (e.g. GET /api/v1/collection/invoice — a typo of /invoices) returns chi's default '404 page not found' as text/plain, and a wrong method (e.g. GET /api/v1/settlements/{id}/approve) returns a bare text 405 — neither carries the {"error":{code,message}} envelope every other response uses. Clients that parse the standard error envelope get a JSON parse failure instead of a machine-readable code. Same class of issue: chimw.Timeout(30s) (line 33) writes a bare, body-less 504 when a handler returns after deadline. Fix: register NotFound/MethodNotAllowed handlers that call httpx.Error with proper AppErrors (404 NOT_FOUND / 405 METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED).
   Suggested: In internal/httpapi/router.go New(), after r := chi.NewRouter() (or right after the middleware stack), register:

r.NotFound(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.NewErr(http.StatusNotFound, "NOT_FOUND", "route not found"))
})
r.MethodNotAllowed(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.NewErr(http.StatusMethodNotAllowed, "METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED", "method not allowed for this route"))
})

using whatever constructor internal/platform/httpx/errors.go exposes (it has an unexported newErr(status, code, message); either export a generic constructor or add httpx.RouteNotFound()/httpx.MethodNotAllowed() helpers alongside the existing httpx.NotFound(resource)). Note chi propagates the router-level NotFound/MethodNotAllowed handlers into subrouters created via Route(), so registering them once on the top-level router covers /api/v1 subtrees — but verify with a quick httptest covering an inner path (e.g. authenticated GET /api/v1/collection/invoice) since inner Route() calls create fresh Mux instances; if inner subtrees don't inherit, register the same handlers inside the /api/v1 Route closure as well. For the 504 case, either wrap chimw.Timeout with a small custom middleware that writes the JSON envelope on deadline, or accept it and document it.
32. [medium/contract] orgs list meta uses "count" (items on page) where every other module returns "total" @ internal/modules/orgs/models.go:47
   Eight modules (identity, cattle, plant, quality, logistics, platformops, settlement, publictrace) return list meta as {limit, offset, total} where total is the full matching count. orgs alone returns {limit, offset, count} where Count = len(page items) (handler.go:80,107,123). A shared frontend paginator reading meta.total gets undefined on GET /orgs, GET /orgs/{id}/children and GET /orgs/{id}/members, and cannot compute page count; conversely meta.count is not the collection size (a directory of 500 DCS units with limit=50 reports count:50 and no way to know 500 exist). Fix: return the collection total under the platform-wide "total" key (add a repo count query), keeping count only if additionally needed.
   Suggested: In internal/modules/orgs: add CountDocuments queries to the repo alongside the List, ListChildren, and ListMembers reads (same filter, without limit/offset), thread the total through service.List/Children/Members as an extra (int64) return, and change ListMeta to `Total int64 `json:"total"`` (drop Count, or keep it additionally if any client already depends on it). Update handler.go:80,107,123 to populate Total from the repo count instead of len(items). For members (which joins role assignments with parties in memory), count the matching ACTIVE role-assignment documents for the org as the total. Leave TreeMeta's count/truncated alone — the tree endpoint is not paginated and its count is genuinely the node count.
33. [medium/contract] collection list endpoints return pagination meta with no total (raw httpx.Page passed as meta) @ internal/modules/collection/handler.go:79
   listReadings (line 79), listPours (line 145) and listInvoices (line 177) call httpx.JSONMeta(w, 200, items, page), serialising httpx.Page directly, so meta is only {"limit":N,"offset":N} with no total — unlike every other module's list endpoints which include total. The collection services/repos never compute a count either. Concrete failure: the core procurement screens (pours, readings, invoices — the highest-traffic lists in the product) cannot render 'page X of Y' or know when to stop paging except by fetching until an empty page, while the identical UI against /cattle, /plant, /settlements etc. works off meta.total. Fix: add count queries in the collection repo and return the shared {limit, offset, total} meta shape.
   Suggested: In internal/modules/collection/repo.go add count queries mirroring the list filters (e.g. countReadings/countPours/countInvoices using CountDocuments with the same bson filter the list queries build). Change the service methods ListReadings/ListPours/ListInvoices to return ([]T, int64, error), running the count alongside the find. In handler.go replace `httpx.JSONMeta(w, http.StatusOK, items, page)` at lines 79, 145 and 177 with the shared meta shape used elsewhere, e.g. a module-local `listMeta{Limit: page.Limit, Offset: page.Offset, Total: total}` matching cattle/plant/logistics.
After fixing: go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./... -count=1, then rerun bash scripts/smoke.sh — everything must be green. If a finding is wrong-in-context, skip it and say why.

97	// ResolveActiveChart finds the rate chart pricing a DCS's pours: among active
98	// charts already effective on the DCS itself or any of its ancestors, the
99	// nearest org wins; ties break to the latest effective_from. Returns
100	// httpx.NotFound when no chart covers the DCS.
101	func (s *service) ResolveActiveChart(ctx context.Context, dcsID string) (*domain.RateChart, error) {
102		dcs, err := s.d.Orgs.Get(ctx, dcsID)
103		if err != nil {
104			return nil, err
105		}
106		if dcs.Type != domain.OrgTypeDCS {
107			return nil, httpx.BadRequest("NOT_A_DCS", "org unit "+dcsID+" is not a DCS")
108		}
109	
110		// Distance 0 = the DCS itself; Path is root→parent, so walk it backwards.
111		distance := map[string]int{dcs.ID: 0}
112		orgIDs := []string{dcs.ID}
113		for i := len(dcs.Path) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
114			distance[dcs.Path[i]] = len(dcs.Path) - i
115			orgIDs = append(orgIDs, dcs.Path[i])
116		}
117	
118		charts, err := s.repo.activeChartsForOrgs(ctx, orgIDs, time.Now().UTC())
119		if err != nil {
120			return nil, err
121		}
122		var best *domain.RateChart
123		for i := range charts {
124			c := &charts[i]
125			if best == nil {
126				best = c
127				continue
128			}
129			dc, db := distance[c.OrgUnitID], distance[best.OrgUnitID]
130			if dc < db || (dc == db && c.EffectiveFrom.After(best.EffectiveFrom)) {
131				best = c
132			}
133		}
134		if best == nil {
135			return nil, httpx.NotFound("active rate chart for DCS " + dcsID)
136		}
137		return best, nil
138	}

160			}
161			if skew > maxClockSkew {
162				out = append(out, domain.IntegrityFlagClockSkew)
163			}
164		}
165		return out
166	}
167	
168	// CreateReading stores one analyzer measurement. Suspicious readings are
169	// flagged, never rejected — the anomaly trail is the deterrent (§8.2).
170	func (s *service) CreateReading(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, req CreateReadingRequest) (*domain.AnalyzerReading, error) {
171		if req.DCSID == "" {
172			return nil, httpx.BadRequest("VALIDATION", "dcs_id is required")
173		}
174		switch req.Mode {
175		case domain.ReadingModeDirect, domain.ReadingModePhotoOCR, domain.ReadingModeManual:
176		default:
177			return nil, httpx.BadRequest("VALIDATION", "mode must be ANALYZER_DIRECT, PHOTO_OCR or MANUAL")
178		}
179		if req.FatPct <= 0 || req.SNFPct <= 0 {
180			return nil, httpx.BadRequest("VALIDATION", "fat_pct and snf_pct are required")
181		}
182		if err := s.d.Orgs.RequireInScope(ctx, actor, req.DCSID); err != nil {
183			return nil, err
184		}
185		if req.Mode == domain.ReadingModePhotoOCR {
186			if !s.d.Flags.Enabled(ctx, flags.FlagPhotoOCR) {
187				featureErr := httpx.Forbidden("photo-OCR ingestion is disabled on this deployment")
188				featureErr.Code = "FEATURE_DISABLED"
189				return nil, featureErr
190			}
191			if req.PhotoObjectKey == "" {
192				return nil, httpx.BadRequest("VALIDATION", "photo_object_key is required for PHOTO_OCR (evidence retention, §8.2)")
193			}
194		}
195	
196		now := time.Now().UTC()
197		var deviceTS time.Time
198		if req.DeviceTimestamp != nil {
199			deviceTS = req.DeviceTimestamp.UTC()
200		}
201		hasGeo := req.GeoLat != nil && req.GeoLng != nil
202		integrityFlags := deriveIntegrityFlags(req.Mode, req.OCRConfidence, hasGeo, deviceTS, now)
203		plausibilityFlags := domain.CheckPlausibility(req.FatPct, req.SNFPct, req.QuantityLitres)
204		integrityFlags = append(integrityFlags, plausibilityFlags...)
205	
206		reading := &domain.AnalyzerReading{
207			ID:               uuid.NewString(),
208			DCSID:            req.DCSID,
209			DeviceID:         req.DeviceID,
210			Mode:             req.Mode,
211			FatPct:           req.FatPct,
212			SNFPct:           req.SNFPct,
213			CLR:              req.CLR,
214			WaterPct:         req.WaterPct,
215			QuantityLitres:   req.QuantityLitres,
216			PhotoObjectKey:   req.PhotoObjectKey,
217			OCRConfidence:    req.OCRConfidence,
218			DeviceTimestamp:  deviceTS,
219			ServerReceivedAt: now,
220			IntegrityFlags:   integrityFlags,
221			PlausibilityOK:   len(plausibilityFlags) == 0,
222			RecordedBy:       actor.PartyID,
223			CreatedAt:        now,
224		}
225		if hasGeo {
226			reading.GeoLat, reading.GeoLng = *req.GeoLat, *req.GeoLng
227		}
228		if err := s.repo.insertReading(ctx, reading); err != nil {
229			return nil, err
230		}
231	
232		if _, err := s.d.Ledger.Append(ctx, provenance.AppendInput{
233			Type:       domain.EventReadingRecorded,
234			EntityType: domain.EntityAnalyzerReading,
235			EntityID:   reading.ID,
236			Actor:      provenance.ActorRef{PartyID: actor.PartyID, RoleCode: actor.RoleCode},
237			OrgUnitID:  reading.DCSID,
238			Payload: map[string]any{
239				"mode":            reading.Mode,
240				"integrity_flags": reading.IntegrityFlags,
241			},
242		}); err != nil {
243			return nil, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("append reading provenance: %w", err))
244		}
245		return reading, nil
246	}

248	// ListReadings pages a DCS's readings for anomaly review, optionally
249	// restricted to one IST day.
250	func (s *service) ListReadings(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, dcsID, date string, page httpx.Page) ([]domain.AnalyzerReading, error) {
251		if dcsID == "" {
252			return nil, httpx.BadRequest("VALIDATION", "dcs_id is required")
253		}

255			return nil, err
256		}
257		var dayStart, dayEnd *time.Time
258		if date != "" {

260			if err != nil {
261				return nil, err
262			}

265		return s.repo.listReadings(ctx, dcsID, dayStart, dayEnd, page)

268	// --- pours ---
269	
270	// CreatePour records one farmer's pour with same-day pricing. Replays of the
271	// same client_event_id return the stored pour with idempotentReplay=true —
272	// offline sync retries are harmless (§3.1).
273	func (s *service) CreatePour(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, req CreatePourRequest) (pour *domain.MilkPour, idempotentReplay bool, err error) {
274		if req.ClientEventID == "" || req.FarmerPartyID == "" || req.DCSID == "" {
275			return nil, false, httpx.BadRequest("VALIDATION", "client_event_id, farmer_party_id and dcs_id are required")
276		}
277		if req.Shift != domain.ShiftMorning && req.Shift != domain.ShiftEvening {
278			return nil, false, httpx.BadRequest("VALIDATION", "shift must be MORNING or EVENING")
279		}
280		if req.QuantityLitres <= 0 {
281			return nil, false, httpx.BadRequest("VALIDATION", "quantity_litres must be positive")
282		}
283		switch req.Source {
284		case domain.ReadingModeDirect, domain.ReadingModePhotoOCR, domain.ReadingModeManual:
285		default:
286			return nil, false, httpx.BadRequest("VALIDATION", "source must be ANALYZER_DIRECT, PHOTO_OCR or MANUAL")
287		}
288		if err := s.d.Orgs.RequireInScope(ctx, actor, req.DCSID); err != nil {
289			return nil, false, err
290		}
291	
292		now := time.Now().UTC()
293		member, err := s.repo.farmerIsActiveMember(ctx, req.FarmerPartyID, req.DCSID, now)
294		if err != nil {
295			return nil, false, err
296		}
297		if !member {
298			return nil, false, httpx.Unprocessable("FARMER_NOT_MEMBER",
299				"farmer does not hold an active FARMER assignment at this DCS")
300		}
301	
302		// HARD plausibility gate: receipts must be trustworthy, so implausible
303		// values are rejected here (unlike readings, which are merely flagged).
304		if violations := domain.CheckPlausibility(req.FatPct, req.SNFPct, req.QuantityLitres); len(violations) > 0 {
305			return nil, false, httpx.Unprocessable("IMPLAUSIBLE_VALUES",
306				"fat/SNF/quantity outside physically plausible bounds")
307		}
308	
309		chart, err := s.resolveChartForPricing(ctx, req.DCSID)
310		if err != nil {
311			return nil, false, err
312		}
313		rate, amount := chart.PricePour(req.FatPct, req.SNFPct, req.QuantityLitres)
314	
315		pouredAt := now
316		if req.PouredAt != nil {
317			pouredAt = req.PouredAt.UTC()
318		}
319		p := &domain.MilkPour{
320			ID:                uuid.NewString(),
321			ClientEventID:     req.ClientEventID,
322			FarmerPartyID:     req.FarmerPartyID,
323			AnimalID:          req.AnimalID,
324			DCSID:             req.DCSID,
325			Shift:             req.Shift,
326			PourDate:          domain.DateKeyIST(pouredAt),
327			QuantityLitres:    req.QuantityLitres,
328			FatPct:            req.FatPct,
329			SNFPct:            req.SNFPct,
330			CLR:               req.CLR,
331			RatePerLitre:      rate,
332			Amount:            amount,
333			RateChartID:       chart.ID,
334			AnalyzerReadingID: req.AnalyzerReadingID,
335			Source:            req.Source,
336			Status:            domain.PourStatusRecorded,
337			PouredAt:          pouredAt,
338			RecordedBy:        actor.PartyID,
339			DeviceID:          req.DeviceID,
340			CreatedAt:         now,
341		}
342		if req.GeoLat != nil && req.GeoLng != nil {
343			p.GeoLat, p.GeoLng = *req.GeoLat, *req.GeoLng
344		}
345	
346		duplicate, err := s.repo.insertPour(ctx, p)
347		if err != nil {
348			return nil, false, err
349		}
350		if duplicate {
351			existing, err := s.repo.pourByClientEventID(ctx, req.ClientEventID)
352			if err != nil {
353				return nil, false, err
354			}
355			return existing, true, nil
356		}
357	
358		if err := s.recordPourProvenance(ctx, actor, p); err != nil {
359			return nil, false, err
360		}
361		s.d.Bus.Publish(eventbus.TopicPourRecorded, *p)
362		s.queueFarmerSMS(ctx, p.FarmerPartyID, domain.TemplatePourReceipt, map[string]string{
363			"qty":    fmt.Sprintf("%.2f", p.QuantityLitres),
364			"rate":   fmt.Sprintf("%.2f", p.RatePerLitre),
365			"amount": fmt.Sprintf("%.2f", p.Amount),
366		})
367		return p, false, nil
368	}
369	
370	// recordPourProvenance appends EventPourRecorded and stamps the ledger seq
371	// onto the pour.
372	func (s *service) recordPourProvenance(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, p *domain.MilkPour) error {
373		refs := []provenance.Ref{
374			{EntityType: domain.EntityParty, EntityID: p.FarmerPartyID, Relation: "produced_by"},
375		}
376		if p.AnimalID != "" {
377			refs = append(refs, provenance.Ref{EntityType: domain.EntityAnimal, EntityID: p.AnimalID, Relation: "from_animal"})
378		}
379		if p.AnalyzerReadingID != "" {
380			refs = append(refs, provenance.Ref{EntityType: domain.EntityAnalyzerReading, EntityID: p.AnalyzerReadingID, Relation: "measured_by"})
381		}
382		ev, err := s.d.Ledger.Append(ctx, provenance.AppendInput{
383			Type:       domain.EventPourRecorded,
384			EntityType: domain.EntityMilkPour,
385			EntityID:   p.ID,
386			Refs:       refs,
387			Actor:      provenance.ActorRef{PartyID: actor.PartyID, RoleCode: actor.RoleCode},
388			OrgUnitID:  p.DCSID,
389			Payload: map[string]any{
390				"quantity_litres": p.QuantityLitres,
391				"rate_per_litre":  p.RatePerLitre,
392				"amount":          p.Amount,
393			},
394		})
395		if err != nil {
396			return httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("append pour provenance: %w", err))
397		}
398		if err := s.repo.setPourProvenanceSeq(ctx, p.ID, ev.Seq); err != nil {
399			return err
400		}
401		p.ProvenanceSeq = ev.Seq
402		return nil
403	}
