```text
9	// Org-unit types — the cooperative backbone RBAC is scoped to (blueprint §5.1,
10	// PCDF constitution: Samiti/DCS → Sangh/Union → PCDF apex).
11	const (
12		OrgTypeFederation      = "FEDERATION"       // PCDF / Parag (state apex)
13		OrgTypeMilkUnion       = "MILK_UNION"       // district Sangh
14		OrgTypeProcessingPlant = "PROCESSING_PLANT" // PCDF plant
15		OrgTypeBMC             = "BMC"              // bulk milk cooler / chilling centre
16		OrgTypeDCS             = "DCS"              // village samiti
17	)
18	
19	// AllOrgTypes is the closed set of org-unit types.
20	var AllOrgTypes = []string{
21		OrgTypeFederation, OrgTypeMilkUnion, OrgTypeProcessingPlant, OrgTypeBMC, OrgTypeDCS,
22	}
23	
24	// ValidOrgParent encodes the allowed hierarchy edges.
25	var ValidOrgParent = map[string][]string{
26		OrgTypeFederation:      {}, // root
27		OrgTypeMilkUnion:       {OrgTypeFederation},
28		OrgTypeProcessingPlant: {OrgTypeMilkUnion, OrgTypeFederation},
29		OrgTypeBMC:             {OrgTypeMilkUnion},
30		OrgTypeDCS:             {OrgTypeMilkUnion, OrgTypeBMC},
31	}
32	
33	// OrgUnit is a node in the cooperative hierarchy.
34	//
35	// ID scheme: `_id` is a generated ObjectID (relations always reference it);
36	// Code is the human-readable unique business key (e.g. "DCS-01842") used for
37	// display, lookups and seed idempotency — never for joins.
38	//
39	// Path holds the ObjectIDs of all ancestors from the root down to (and
40	// excluding) this node — denormalised so "is X inside Y's scope" is a single
41	// indexed array-containment check with no recursive queries on the hot path.
42	type OrgUnit struct {
43		ID        primitive.ObjectID   `bson:"_id,omitempty" json:"id"`
44		Type      string               `bson:"type"          json:"type"`
45		Name      string               `bson:"name"          json:"name"`
46		Code      string               `bson:"code"          json:"code"` // unique business key, e.g. "DCS-01842"
47		ParentID  *primitive.ObjectID  `bson:"parent_id,omitempty" json:"parent_id,omitempty"`
48		Path      []primitive.ObjectID `bson:"path"          json:"path"`
49		District  string               `bson:"district,omitempty" json:"district,omitempty"`
50		State     string               `bson:"state,omitempty"    json:"state,omitempty"`
51		GeoLat    float64              `bson:"geo_lat,omitempty"  json:"geo_lat,omitempty"`
52		GeoLng    float64              `bson:"geo_lng,omitempty"  json:"geo_lng,omitempty"`
53		Active    bool                 `bson:"active"        json:"active"`
54		CreatedAt time.Time            `bson:"created_at"    json:"created_at"`
55		UpdatedAt time.Time            `bson:"updated_at"    json:"updated_at"`
56	}
57	
58	// IsValidOrgType reports whether t is a known org-unit type.
59	func IsValidOrgType(t string) bool {
60		for _, v := range AllOrgTypes {
61			if v == t {
62				return true
63			}
64		}
65		return false
66	}
```

```text
1	// Package identity owns authentication (OTP login, refresh-token rotation,
2	// role selection), the Party registry, org-scoped role assignments and KYC
3	// verification — blueprint §4 (identity) and §5 (roles & RBAC).
4	//
5	// Route prefixes (mounted under /api/v1): /auth, /parties, /roles, /kyc.
6	// This module emits no provenance events; identity changes are covered by
7	// the audit middleware.
8	package identity
9	
10	import (
11		"github.com/go-chi/chi/v5"
12	
13		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/domain"
14		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/deps"
15		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/middleware"
16	)
17	
18	// Register wires repo → service → handler and mounts the identity routes.
19	func Register(r chi.Router, d *deps.Deps) {
20		repo := newRepository(d.DB)
21		svc := newService(d, repo)
22		h := newHandler(svc)
23	
24		r.Route("/auth", func(r chi.Router) {
25			// Public login flow — no token yet.
26			r.Post("/otp/request", h.requestOTP)
27			r.Post("/otp/verify", h.verifyOTP)
28			r.Post("/refresh", h.refresh)
29	
30			// Any logged-in party (session or role token).
31			r.Group(func(r chi.Router) {
32				r.Use(middleware.Authenticate(d.JWT), middleware.RequireSession)
33				r.Post("/logout", h.logout)
34				r.Get("/roles", h.listMyRoles)
35				r.Post("/role/select", h.selectRole)
36			})
37		})
38	
39		r.Route("/parties", func(r chi.Router) {
40			r.Use(middleware.Authenticate(d.JWT), middleware.RequireSession)
41			r.Get("/me", h.getMe)
42			r.Patch("/me", h.patchMe)
43		})
44	
45		r.Route("/kyc", func(r chi.Router) {
46			r.Use(middleware.Authenticate(d.JWT), middleware.RequireSession)
47			r.Post("/aadhaar", h.verifyAadhaar)
48			r.Post("/bank", h.verifyBank)
49			r.Get("/me", h.listMyKYC)
50		})
51	
52		r.Route("/roles", func(r chi.Router) {
53			r.Use(middleware.Authenticate(d.JWT))
54			// SUPER_ADMIN passes RequireRoles automatically; the fine-grained
55			// granter matrix (§5.2) is enforced in the service.
56			r.Use(middleware.RequireRoles(
57				domain.RolePCDFAdmin,
58				domain.RoleUnionPresident,
59				domain.RoleSamitiAdhyaksh,
60			))
61			r.Post("/assignments", h.createAssignment)
62			r.Delete("/assignments/{id}", h.revokeAssignment)
63			r.Get("/assignments", h.listAssignments)
64		})
65	}
66
```

```text
9	// TestGranterMayGrant pins the role-grant permission matrix (blueprint §5.2):
10	// admins are unrestricted, UNION_PRESIDENT covers village/logistics/union
11	// tiers, SAMITI_ADHYAKSH covers only village workers, everyone else nothing.
12	func TestGranterMayGrant(t *testing.T) {
13		cases := []struct {
14			name        string
15			granterRole string
16			roleCode    string
17			want        bool
18		}{
19			// Admin granters: unrestricted.
20			{"super admin grants farmer", domain.RoleSuperAdmin, domain.RoleFarmer, true},
21			{"super admin grants super admin", domain.RoleSuperAdmin, domain.RoleSuperAdmin, true},
22			{"pcdf admin grants plant operator", domain.RolePCDFAdmin, domain.RolePlantOperator, true},
23			{"pcdf admin grants union president", domain.RolePCDFAdmin, domain.RoleUnionPresident, true},
24	
25			// UNION_PRESIDENT: village + logistics + union tiers.
26			{"union president grants farmer", domain.RoleUnionPresident, domain.RoleFarmer, true},
27			{"union president grants sacheev", domain.RoleUnionPresident, domain.RoleSamitiSacheev, true},
28			{"union president grants adhyaksh", domain.RoleUnionPresident, domain.RoleSamitiAdhyaksh, true},
29			{"union president grants milk tester", domain.RoleUnionPresident, domain.RoleMilkTester, true},
30			{"union president grants lrp", domain.RoleUnionPresident, domain.RoleLRP, true},
31			{"union president grants ai tech", domain.RoleUnionPresident, domain.RoleAITech, true},
32			{"union president grants van rider", domain.RoleUnionPresident, domain.RoleVanRider, true},
33			{"union president grants delivery rider", domain.RoleUnionPresident, domain.RoleDeliveryRider, true},
34			{"union president grants bmc operator", domain.RoleUnionPresident, domain.RoleBMCOperator, true},
35			{"union president grants field supervisor", domain.RoleUnionPresident, domain.RoleUnionFieldSupervisor, true},
36			{"union president grants union president", domain.RoleUnionPresident, domain.RoleUnionPresident, true},
37			{"union president cannot grant plant operator", domain.RoleUnionPresident, domain.RolePlantOperator, false},
38			{"union president cannot grant pcdf admin", domain.RoleUnionPresident, domain.RolePCDFAdmin, false},
39			{"union president cannot grant super admin", domain.RoleUnionPresident, domain.RoleSuperAdmin, false},
40			{"union president cannot grant veterinarian", domain.RoleUnionPresident, domain.RoleVeterinarian, false},
41	
42			// SAMITI_ADHYAKSH: only FARMER / MILK_TESTER / LRP.
43			{"adhyaksh grants farmer", domain.RoleSamitiAdhyaksh, domain.RoleFarmer, true},
44			{"adhyaksh grants milk tester", domain.RoleSamitiAdhyaksh, domain.RoleMilkTester, true},
45			{"adhyaksh grants lrp", domain.RoleSamitiAdhyaksh, domain.RoleLRP, true},

49			{"adhyaksh cannot grant union president", domain.RoleSamitiAdhyaksh, domain.RoleUnionPresident, false},

52			// blocks them anyway — the matrix must still deny defensively).

54			{"sacheev cannot grant farmer", domain.RoleSamitiSacheev, domain.RoleFarmer, false},
55		}

60				}
61			})
```

```text
1	package auth
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"sync"
6	)
7	
8	// Actor is the authenticated caller extracted from a verified token and
9	// stored on the request context by the auth middleware.
10	type Actor struct {
11		PartyID          string
12		Phone            string
13		KYCTier          string
14		Kind             string // session | role
15		RoleAssignmentID string
16		RoleCode         string
17		OrgUnitID        string
18		OrgType          string
19	}
20	
21	// HasRole reports whether the actor operates under one of the given roles.
22	func (a Actor) HasRole(roles ...string) bool {
23		for _, r := range roles {
24			if a.RoleCode == r {
25				return true
26			}
27		}
28		return false
29	}
30	
31	type actorCtxKey struct{}
32	
33	// actorHolder is a mutable cell installed by OUTER middleware (audit) so
34	// identity established by INNER middleware (Authenticate) can flow back out.
35	// Context values only propagate inward; the shared pointer bridges the gap.
36	type actorHolder struct {
37		mu sync.Mutex
38		a  *Actor
39	}
40	
41	type actorHolderCtxKey struct{}
42	
43	// WithActorHolder installs an empty actor holder on the context. Middleware
44	// mounted before authentication uses it to observe the actor after the
45	// handler chain ran.
46	func WithActorHolder(ctx context.Context) context.Context {
47		return context.WithValue(ctx, actorHolderCtxKey{}, &actorHolder{})
48	}
49	
50	// HeldActor returns the actor captured by an inner WithActor call, if a
51	// holder was installed and authentication happened.
52	func HeldActor(ctx context.Context) (Actor, bool) {
53		h, ok := ctx.Value(actorHolderCtxKey{}).(*actorHolder)
54		if !ok {
55			return Actor{}, false
56		}
57		h.mu.Lock()
58		defer h.mu.Unlock()
59		if h.a == nil {
60			return Actor{}, false
61		}
62		return *h.a, true
63	}
64	
65	// WithActor stores the actor on the context, and also fills the outward
66	// actor holder when one was installed upstream (see WithActorHolder).
67	func WithActor(ctx context.Context, a Actor) context.Context {
68		if h, ok := ctx.Value(actorHolderCtxKey{}).(*actorHolder); ok {
69			h.mu.Lock()
70			cp := a
71			h.a = &cp
72			h.mu.Unlock()
73		}
74		return context.WithValue(ctx, actorCtxKey{}, a)
75	}
76	
77	// ActorFrom retrieves the actor, if any.
78	func ActorFrom(ctx context.Context) (Actor, bool) {
79		a, ok := ctx.Value(actorCtxKey{}).(Actor)
80		return a, ok
81	}
```

 `./internal/platform/orgscope/resolver.go`

```text
1	// Package orgscope answers the RBAC question "is this resource inside the
2	// caller's organisational scope?" in O(1) DB reads. Org units denormalise
3	// their ancestor chain into Path ([]ObjectID), so scope checking is a
4	// set-membership test — no recursive tree walks on the hot path.
5	package orgscope
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"errors"
10		"sync"
11		"time"
12	
13		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson"
14		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson/primitive"
15		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo"
16	
17		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/domain"
18		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/auth"
19		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/httpx"
20	)
21	
22	const collection = "org_units"
23	
24	type cachedOrg struct {
25		org domain.OrgUnit
26		at  time.Time
27	}
28	
29	// Resolver caches org units briefly (the tree changes rarely, reads are hot).
30	type Resolver struct {
31		coll *mongo.Collection
32		ttl  time.Duration
33	
34		mu    sync.RWMutex
35		cache map[string]cachedOrg // keyed by ObjectID hex
36	}
37	
38	// NewResolver binds the resolver to the database.
39	func NewResolver(db *mongo.Database) *Resolver {
40		return &Resolver{
41			coll:  db.Collection(collection),
42			ttl:   60 * time.Second,
43			cache: make(map[string]cachedOrg),
44		}
45	}
46	
47	// Get returns an org unit by ObjectID (cached).
48	func (r *Resolver) Get(ctx context.Context, id primitive.ObjectID) (*domain.OrgUnit, error) {
49		key := id.Hex()
50		r.mu.RLock()
51		c, ok := r.cache[key]
52		r.mu.RUnlock()
53		if ok && time.Since(c.at) < r.ttl {
54			org := c.org
55			return &org, nil
56		}
57	
58		var org domain.OrgUnit
59		err := r.coll.FindOne(ctx, bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: id}}).Decode(&org)
60		if errors.Is(err, mongo.ErrNoDocuments) {
61			return nil, httpx.NotFound("org unit " + key)
62		}
63		if err != nil {
64			return nil, httpx.Internal(err)
65		}
66	
67		r.mu.Lock()
68		r.cache[key] = cachedOrg{org: org, at: time.Now()}
69		r.mu.Unlock()
70		return &org, nil
71	}
72	
73	// GetByCode returns an org unit by its unique human-readable business code
74	// (e.g. "DCS-01842") — display/lookup use only, never for joins.
75	func (r *Resolver) GetByCode(ctx context.Context, code string) (*domain.OrgUnit, error) {
76		var org domain.OrgUnit
77		err := r.coll.FindOne(ctx, bson.D{{Key: "code", Value: code}}).Decode(&org)
78		if errors.Is(err, mongo.ErrNoDocuments) {
79			return nil, httpx.NotFound("org unit with code " + code)
80		}
81		if err != nil {
82			return nil, httpx.Internal(err)
83		}
84		return &org, nil
85	}
86	
87	// Invalidate drops a cached entry (call after updates).
88	func (r *Resolver) Invalidate(id primitive.ObjectID) {
89		r.mu.Lock()
90		delete(r.cache, id.Hex())
91		r.mu.Unlock()
92	}
93	
94	// InScope reports whether target sits at-or-below scope in the hierarchy:
95	// true when scope == target, or scope appears in target's ancestor Path.
96	func (r *Resolver) InScope(ctx context.Context, scopeOrgID, targetOrgID primitive.ObjectID) (bool, error) {
97		if scopeOrgID == targetOrgID {
98			return true, nil
99		}
100		target, err := r.Get(ctx, targetOrgID)
101		if err != nil {
102			return false, err
103		}
104		for _, ancestor := range target.Path {
105			if ancestor == scopeOrgID {
106				return true, nil
107			}
108		}
109		return false, nil
110	}
111	
112	// RequireInScope enforces the actor's org scope over a target org unit.
113	// SUPER_ADMIN and STATE_AUDITOR (read-wide roles rooted at the federation)
114	// pass automatically; everyone else needs ancestry. The actor carries its
115	// org unit as an ObjectID hex string (JWT claims are JSON); it is parsed here.
116	func (r *Resolver) RequireInScope(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, targetOrgID primitive.ObjectID) error {
117		if actor.RoleCode == domain.RoleSuperAdmin || actor.RoleCode == domain.RoleStateAuditor {
118			return nil
119		}
120		if actor.OrgUnitID == "" {
121			return httpx.Forbidden("role token with org scope required")
122		}
123		scopeID, err := primitive.ObjectIDFromHex(actor.OrgUnitID)
124		if err != nil {
125			return httpx.Forbidden("role token carries an invalid org scope")
126		}
127		ok, err := r.InScope(ctx, scopeID, targetOrgID)
128		if err != nil {
129			return err
130		}
131		if !ok {
132			return httpx.Forbidden("resource is outside your organisational scope")
133		}
134		return nil
135	}
136
```

```text
1	// Package provenance implements the append-only, hash-chained event ledger —
2	// the source of truth for milk traceability (blueprint §7). Every link in the
3	// pour→QR chain is an immutable Event whose SHA-256 hash covers the previous
4	// event's hash, so history cannot be quietly rewritten (tamper-evidence,
5	// FSSAI recall-grade audit).
6	//
7	// Corrections are NEW events referencing the superseded entity — nothing is
8	// ever updated or deleted in this collection.
9	package provenance
10	
11	import (
12		"context"
13		"crypto/sha256"
14		"encoding/hex"
15		"encoding/json"
16		"errors"

32	// (e.g. a consignment event referencing the pours it aggregates).
33	type Ref struct {
34		EntityType string `bson:"entity_type" json:"entity_type"`
35		EntityID   string `bson:"entity_id"   json:"entity_id"`
36		Relation   string `bson:"relation"    json:"relation"` // aggregates | supersedes | tested | yields | labels ...
37	}

43	}
44	
45	// Event is one immutable link in the ledger. `_id` is a generated ObjectID;
46	// EntityID and Refs carry the referenced documents' ObjectIDs as hex strings
47	// (the ledger is a generic event log spanning every entity type, and hex
48	// strings keep the hash material canonical and human-inspectable).
49	type Event struct {
50		ID         primitive.ObjectID `bson:"_id,omitempty" json:"id"`
51		Seq        int64          `bson:"seq"         json:"seq"`
52		Type       string         `bson:"type"        json:"type"`
53		EntityType string         `bson:"entity_type" json:"entity_type"`
54		EntityID   string         `bson:"entity_id"   json:"entity_id"`
55		Refs       []Ref          `bson:"refs,omitempty"    json:"refs,omitempty"`
56		Actor      ActorRef       `bson:"actor"       json:"actor"`
57		OrgUnitID  string         `bson:"org_unit_id,omitempty" json:"org_unit_id,omitempty"`
58		Payload    map[string]any `bson:"payload,omitempty"     json:"payload,omitempty"`
59		TS         time.Time      `bson:"ts"          json:"ts"`
60		PrevHash   string         `bson:"prev_hash"   json:"prev_hash"`
61		Hash       string         `bson:"hash"        json:"hash"`
62	}
63	
64	// AppendInput describes a new event to chain.
65	type AppendInput struct {
66		Type       string
67		EntityType string
68		EntityID   string
69		Refs       []Ref
70		Actor      ActorRef
71		OrgUnitID  string
72		Payload    map[string]any
73	}
74	
75	// Ledger appends to and reads the hash chain.
76	type Ledger struct {
77		coll *mongo.Collection
78	
79		// appendMu serialises the head-read+insert of Append within this process:
80		// every ledger write system-wide shares one global seq, so without local
81		// serialisation concurrent handlers (e.g. a morning pour rush plus a
82		// GenerateInvoices loop) burn duplicate-key retries against each other.
83		// The unique seq index remains the atomic backstop across processes.
84		appendMu sync.Mutex
85	}
86	
87	// NewLedger binds the ledger to the database.
88	func NewLedger(db *mongo.Database) *Ledger {
89		return &Ledger{coll: db.Collection(collection)}
90	}
91	
92	// genesisHash anchors the chain before the first event.
93	const genesisHash = "GENESIS"
94	
95	// Append chains a new event. Concurrency-safe without transactions: it reads
96	// the current head, computes seq+hash optimistically, and relies on the
97	// unique index on `seq` — a duplicate-key collision means another writer won
98	// the slot, so we re-read and retry.
99	func (l *Ledger) Append(ctx context.Context, in AppendInput) (*Event, error) {
100		// Serialise appends within this process (see appendMu): local writers no
101		// longer race each other for the seq slot, so under single-instance
102		// deployment the retry loop only ever fires against external writers.
103		l.appendMu.Lock()
104		defer l.appendMu.Unlock()
105	
106		const maxRetries = 12
107		for attempt := 0; attempt < maxRetries; attempt++ {
108			seq, prevHash, err := l.head(ctx)
109			if err != nil {
110				return nil, err
111			}
112			ev := &Event{
113				ID:         primitive.NewObjectID(),
114				Seq:        seq + 1,
115				Type:       in.Type,
116				EntityType: in.EntityType,
117				EntityID:   in.EntityID,
118				Refs:       in.Refs,
119				Actor:      in.Actor,
120				OrgUnitID:  in.OrgUnitID,
121				Payload:    in.Payload,
122				// Millisecond precision: BSON datetimes store ms, so the persisted
123				// TS must equal the hashed TS or re-verification would break.
124				TS:       time.Now().UTC().Truncate(time.Millisecond),
125				PrevHash: prevHash,
126			}
127			ev.Hash = computeHash(ev)
128	
129			if _, err := l.coll.InsertOne(ctx, ev); err != nil {
130				if mongo.IsDuplicateKeyError(err) {
131					continue // lost the seq race — retry against the new head
132				}
133				return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance append: %w", err)
134			}
135			return ev, nil
136		}
137		return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance append: gave up after %d seq collisions", 12)
138	}
139	
140	// head returns the latest (seq, hash), or (0, GENESIS) for an empty chain.
141	func (l *Ledger) head(ctx context.Context) (int64, string, error) {
142		var last Event
143		err := l.coll.FindOne(ctx, bson.D{},
144			options.FindOne().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: -1}}),
145		).Decode(&last)
146		if errors.Is(err, mongo.ErrNoDocuments) {
147			return 0, genesisHash, nil
148		}
149		if err != nil {
150			return 0, "", fmt.Errorf("provenance head: %w", err)
151		}
152		return last.Seq, last.Hash, nil
153	}
154	
155	// computeHash covers everything that matters: position, linkage, content.
156	// Payload is canonicalised via encoding/json (map keys are sorted) and the
157	// timestamp to millisecond precision (BSON datetime resolution), so the
158	// digest is deterministic across a MongoDB round trip.
159	func computeHash(ev *Event) string {
160		payloadJSON, _ := json.Marshal(ev.Payload)
161		refParts := make([]string, 0, len(ev.Refs))
162		for _, r := range ev.Refs {
163			refParts = append(refParts, r.EntityType+":"+r.EntityID+":"+r.Relation)
164		}
165		material := strings.Join([]string{
166			ev.PrevHash,
167			strconv.FormatInt(ev.Seq, 10),
168			ev.Type,
169			ev.EntityType,
170			ev.EntityID,
171			strings.Join(refParts, ","),
172			ev.Actor.PartyID,
173			ev.Actor.RoleCode,
174			ev.OrgUnitID,
175			string(payloadJSON),
176			ev.TS.UTC().Truncate(time.Millisecond).Format(time.RFC3339Nano),
177		}, "|")
178		sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(material))
179		return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
180	}
181	
182	// EventsForEntity returns an entity's own timeline in chain order.
183	func (l *Ledger) EventsForEntity(ctx context.Context, entityType, entityID string) ([]Event, error) {
184		cur, err := l.coll.Find(ctx,
185			bson.D{{Key: "entity_type", Value: entityType}, {Key: "entity_id", Value: entityID}},
186			options.Find().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: 1}}),
187		)
188		if err != nil {
189			return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance events for %s/%s: %w", entityType, entityID, err)
190		}
191		var out []Event
192		if err := cur.All(ctx, &out); err != nil {
193			return nil, err
194		}
195		return out, nil
196	}
197	
198	// Trace walks the provenance graph UPSTREAM from an entity: its events, plus
199	// (recursively) the events of everything those events reference. This is how
200	// a consumer QR resolves back to the contributing samiti set, and how a failed
201	// aflatoxin test walks back to source DCSes (blueprint §8.3).
202	func (l *Ledger) Trace(ctx context.Context, entityType, entityID string, maxDepth int) ([]Event, error) {
203		return l.TraceStopAt(ctx, entityType, entityID, maxDepth, nil)
204	}
205	
206	// TraceStopAt is Trace with a stop set: entity types in stopExpand are still
207	// fetched (their events appear in the result) but their refs are never
208	// followed. The consumer QR scan stops at the consignment/pooling boundary so
209	// hundreds of per-pour nodes (and cross-route trip fan-out) are never walked.
210	//
211	// Each BFS level is batched into a bounded number of $or queries instead of
212	// one Find per node, so a walk costs O(depth) round trips, not O(nodes).
213	func (l *Ledger) TraceStopAt(ctx context.Context, entityType, entityID string, maxDepth int, stopExpand map[string]bool) ([]Event, error) {
214		if maxDepth <= 0 {
215			maxDepth = 10
216		}
217		const hardEventCap = 2000
218	
219		type node struct{ etype, eid string }
220		visited := map[node]bool{}
221		frontier := []node{{entityType, entityID}}
222		var all []Event
223	
224		for depth := 0; depth < maxDepth && len(frontier) > 0; depth++ {
225			// Deduplicate this level against everything already visited.
226			level := make([]node, 0, len(frontier))
227			for _, n := range frontier {
228				if visited[n] {
229					continue
230				}
231				visited[n] = true
232				level = append(level, n)
233			}
234			if len(level) == 0 {
235				break
236			}
237	
238			var next []node
239			// One indexed query per chunk of the level (not per node).
240			const orChunk = 200
241			for start := 0; start < len(level); start += orChunk {
242				end := min(start+orChunk, len(level))
243				clauses := make(bson.A, 0, end-start)
244				for _, n := range level[start:end] {
245					clauses = append(clauses, bson.D{
246						{Key: "entity_type", Value: n.etype},
247						{Key: "entity_id", Value: n.eid},
248					})
249				}
250				cur, err := l.coll.Find(ctx,
251					bson.D{{Key: "$or", Value: clauses}},
252					options.Find().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: 1}}).SetLimit(hardEventCap),
253				)
254				if err != nil {
255					return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance trace level: %w", err)
256				}
257				var evs []Event
258				if err := cur.All(ctx, &evs); err != nil {
259					return nil, err
260				}
261				for _, ev := range evs {
262					all = append(all, ev)
263					if len(all) >= hardEventCap {
264						return all, nil
265					}
266					if stopExpand != nil && stopExpand[ev.EntityType] {
267						continue // include the node's events, never follow its refs
268					}
269					for _, ref := range ev.Refs {
270						nn := node{ref.EntityType, ref.EntityID}
271						if !visited[nn] {
272							next = append(next, nn)
273						}
274					}
275				}
276			}
277			frontier = next
278		}
279		return all, nil
280	}
281	
282	// DownstreamRefs finds events that reference the given entity — used to walk
283	// FORWARD (e.g. "which batches consumed this blocked BMC lot?"). The limit is
284	// pushed into the query: only the LAST limit referencing events are fetched
285	// (ascending chain order preserved). limit <= 0 falls back to 2000.
286	func (l *Ledger) DownstreamRefs(ctx context.Context, entityID string, limit int64) ([]Event, error) {
287		if limit <= 0 {
288			limit = 2000
289		}
290		cur, err := l.coll.Find(ctx,
291			bson.D{{Key: "refs.entity_id", Value: entityID}},
292			options.Find().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: -1}}).SetLimit(limit),
293		)
294		if err != nil {
295			return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance downstream of %s: %w", entityID, err)
296		}
297		var out []Event
298		if err := cur.All(ctx, &out); err != nil {
299			return nil, err
300		}
301		// Restore ascending chain order.
302		for i, j := 0, len(out)-1; i < j; i, j = i+1, j-1 {
303			out[i], out[j] = out[j], out[i]
304		}
305		return out, nil
306	}
307	
308	// EventsForEntityPage returns one page of an entity's own timeline in chain
309	// order, with skip/limit pushed into the query.
310	func (l *Ledger) EventsForEntityPage(ctx context.Context, entityType, entityID string, offset, limit int64) ([]Event, error) {
311		cur, err := l.coll.Find(ctx,
312			bson.D{{Key: "entity_type", Value: entityType}, {Key: "entity_id", Value: entityID}},
313			options.Find().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: 1}}).SetSkip(offset).SetLimit(limit),
314		)
315		if err != nil {
316			return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance events page for %s/%s: %w", entityType, entityID, err)
317		}
318		var out []Event
319		if err := cur.All(ctx, &out); err != nil {
320			return nil, err
321		}
322		return out, nil
323	}
324	
325	// CountEventsForEntity returns the total number of events on an entity's
326	// timeline (pagination meta companion of EventsForEntityPage).
327	func (l *Ledger) CountEventsForEntity(ctx context.Context, entityType, entityID string) (int64, error) {
328		n, err := l.coll.CountDocuments(ctx,
329			bson.D{{Key: "entity_type", Value: entityType}, {Key: "entity_id", Value: entityID}})
330		if err != nil {
331			return 0, fmt.Errorf("provenance count for %s/%s: %w", entityType, entityID, err)
332		}
333		return n, nil
334	}
335	
336	// VerifyChain re-derives every hash in [fromSeq, toSeq] and checks linkage.
337	// Returns (true, 0) when intact, or (false, seq) of the first broken link.
338	func (l *Ledger) VerifyChain(ctx context.Context, fromSeq, toSeq int64) (bool, int64, error) {
339		filter := bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$gte", Value: fromSeq}, {Key: "$lte", Value: toSeq}}}}
340		cur, err := l.coll.Find(ctx, filter, options.Find().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: 1}}))
341		if err != nil {
342			return false, 0, fmt.Errorf("provenance verify: %w", err)
343		}
344		defer cur.Close(ctx)
345	
346		prevHash := ""
347		prevSeq := int64(0)
348		first := true
349		for cur.Next(ctx) {
350			var ev Event
351			if err := cur.Decode(&ev); err != nil {
352				return false, 0, err
353			}
354			if computeHash(&ev) != ev.Hash {
355				return false, ev.Seq, nil // content tampered
356			}
357			if !first {
358				if ev.Seq != prevSeq+1 || ev.PrevHash != prevHash {
359					return false, ev.Seq, nil // linkage broken
360				}
361			}
362			prevHash, prevSeq, first = ev.Hash, ev.Seq, false
363		}
364		return true, 0, cur.Err()
365	}
366	
367	// LatestSeq returns the current chain head sequence (0 = empty).
368	func (l *Ledger) LatestSeq(ctx context.Context) (int64, error) {
369		seq, _, err := l.head(ctx)
370		return seq, err
371	}
```

```text
package auth

import (
	"context"
	"sync"

// Actor is the authenticated caller extracted from a verified token and
// stored on the request context by the auth middleware.
type Actor struct {
	PartyID          string
	Phone            string
	KYCTier          string
	Kind             string // session | role
	RoleAssignmentID string
	RoleCode         string
	OrgUnitID        string
	OrgType          string
}

// HasRole reports whether the actor operates under one of the given roles.
func (a Actor) HasRole(roles ...string) bool {
	for _, r := range roles {
		if a.RoleCode == r {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

type actorCtxKey struct{}

// actorHolder is a mutable cell installed by OUTER middleware (audit) so
// identity established by INNER middleware (Authenticate) can flow back out.
// Context values only propagate inward; the shared pointer bridges the gap.
type actorHolder struct {
	mu sync.Mutex
	a  *Actor
}

type actorHolderCtxKey struct{}

// WithActorHolder installs an empty actor holder on the context. Middleware
// mounted before authentication uses it to observe the actor after the
// handler chain ran.
func WithActorHolder(ctx context.Context) context.Context {
	return context.WithValue(ctx, actorHolderCtxKey{}, &actorHolder{})
}

// HeldActor returns the actor captured by an inner WithActor call, if a
// holder was installed and authentication happened.
func HeldActor(ctx context.Context) (Actor, bool) {
	h, ok := ctx.Value(actorHolderCtxKey{}).(*actorHolder)
	if !ok {
		return Actor{}, false
	}
	h.mu.Lock()
	defer h.mu.Unlock()
	if h.a == nil {
		return Actor{}, false
	}
	return *h.a, true
}

// WithActor stores the actor on the context, and also fills the outward
// actor holder when one was installed upstream (see WithActorHolder).
func WithActor(ctx context.Context, a Actor) context.Context {
	if h, ok := ctx.Value(actorHolderCtxKey{}).(*actorHolder); ok {
		h.mu.Lock()
		cp := a
		h.a = &cp
		h.mu.Unlock()
	}
	return context.WithValue(ctx, actorCtxKey{}, a)
}

// ActorFrom retrieves the actor, if any.
func ActorFrom(ctx context.Context) (Actor, bool) {
	a, ok := ctx.Value(actorCtxKey{}).(Actor)
	return a, ok
}
package auth

import (
	"context"
	"testing"
)

// TestActorHolderPropagatesOutward pins the mechanism the audit middleware
// relies on: identity installed by INNER middleware (WithActor) must be
// observable from the OUTER frame that installed the holder — otherwise
// every HTTP mutation audit entry records an empty actor.
func TestActorHolderPropagatesOutward(t *testing.T) {
	outer := WithActorHolder(context.Background())

	// Before authentication runs, the holder is empty.
	if _, ok := HeldActor(outer); ok {
		t.Fatal("HeldActor must be empty before WithActor runs")
	}

	// Inner middleware derives a child context — the holder pointer is shared.
	actor := Actor{PartyID: "party-1", RoleCode: "SUPER_ADMIN"}
	inner := WithActor(outer, actor)

	got, ok := HeldActor(outer)
	if !ok {
		t.Fatal("HeldActor(outer) must observe the actor set on the inner context")
	}
	if got.PartyID != "party-1" || got.RoleCode != "SUPER_ADMIN" {
		t.Fatalf("held actor = %+v, want party-1/SUPER_ADMIN", got)
	}

	// The regular inward lookup still works on the inner context.
	if a, ok := ActorFrom(inner); !ok || a.PartyID != "party-1" {
		t.Fatalf("ActorFrom(inner) = %+v, %v", a, ok)
	}

	// Without a holder installed, WithActor is a no-op for HeldActor.
	plain := WithActor(context.Background(), actor)
	if _, ok := HeldActor(plain); ok {
		t.Fatal("HeldActor must report false when no holder was installed")
	}
}
```

```text
7	
8	// Role codes — the role catalog from blueprint §5.2, grounded in the PCDF
9	// cooperative constitution (Farmer → Samiti/DCS → Sangh/Union → PCDF).
10	// A Party may hold many time-bounded, org-scoped RoleAssignments.
11	//
12	// The catalog is deliberately open for extension: adding a future role is a
13	// new constant + AllRoles entry + RequiredKYCTier entry — nothing else.
14	const (
15		// Village tier
16		RoleFarmer         = "FARMER"
17		RoleSamitiSacheev  = "SAMITI_SACHEEV"  // DCS paid Secretary (UPCS Act §31) — runs the collection console
18		RoleSamitiAdhyaksh = "SAMITI_ADHYAKSH" // DCS Chairman/Sabhapati (elected, honorary, §30)
19		RoleMilkTester     = "MILK_TESTER"
20		RoleLRP            = "LRP" // Local Resource Person (NDDB village extension)
21		RoleAITech         = "AI_TECH"
22	
23		// Field / organisation tier
24		// ORGANISING_MANAGER is the ground-level field worker (Dairy Development
25		// Department pattern: "promotes and organises new samitis") who performs
26		// doorstep KYC capture and first-level verification.
27		RoleOrganisingManager = "ORGANISING_MANAGER"
28	
29		// Logistics tier
30		RoleVanRider      = "VAN_RIDER"
31		RoleDeliveryRider = "DELIVERY_RIDER"
32	
33		// Union tier
34		RoleBMCOperator          = "BMC_OPERATOR"
35		RoleUnionFieldSupervisor = "UNION_FIELD_SUPERVISOR"
36		RoleUnionPresident       = "UNION_PRESIDENT"
37	
38		// Plant tier
39		RolePlantOperator   = "PLANT_OPERATOR"
40		RolePlantLabAnalyst = "PLANT_LAB_ANALYST"
41	
42		// State / district tier
43		RolePCDFAdmin        = "PCDF_ADMIN"
44		RoleMissionOfficial  = "MISSION_OFFICIAL"
45		RoleDistrictVerifier = "DISTRICT_VERIFIER"
46	
47		// Health tier
48		RoleVeterinarian = "VETERINARIAN"
49		RoleMVUDriver    = "MVU_DRIVER"
50	
51		// Consumer tier
52		RoleConsumer = "CONSUMER"
53	
54		// Platform tier
55		RoleSupportAgent = "SUPPORT_AGENT"
56		RoleStateAuditor = "STATE_AUDITOR"
57		RoleSuperAdmin   = "SUPER_ADMIN"
58	
59		// System tier
60		RoleServiceAccount = "SERVICE_ACCOUNT"
61	)
62	
63	// AllRoles is the closed set of grantable role codes (extend here).
64	var AllRoles = []string{
65		RoleFarmer, RoleSamitiSacheev, RoleSamitiAdhyaksh, RoleMilkTester, RoleLRP, RoleAITech,
66		RoleOrganisingManager,
67		RoleVanRider, RoleDeliveryRider,
68		RoleBMCOperator, RoleUnionFieldSupervisor, RoleUnionPresident,
69		RolePlantOperator, RolePlantLabAnalyst,
70		RolePCDFAdmin, RoleMissionOfficial, RoleDistrictVerifier,
71		RoleVeterinarian, RoleMVUDriver,
72		RoleConsumer,
73		RoleSupportAgent, RoleStateAuditor, RoleSuperAdmin,
74		RoleServiceAccount,
75	}
76	
77	var roleSet = func() map[string]struct{} {
78		s := make(map[string]struct{}, len(AllRoles))
79		for _, r := range AllRoles {
80			s[r] = struct{}{}
81		}
82		return s
83	}()
84	
85	// IsValidRole reports whether code is one of the catalog roles.
86	func IsValidRole(code string) bool {
87		_, ok := roleSet[code]
88		return ok
89	}
90	
91	// KYC assurance tiers (blueprint §4.2). Higher tiers unlock higher-trust roles.
92	const (
93		KYCTierMinimal  = "MINIMAL"  // mobile OTP only (consumer)
94		KYCTierFarmer   = "FARMER"   // Aadhaar OTP eKYC or offline XML + penny-drop
95		KYCTierStandard = "STANDARD" // Aadhaar eKYC
96		KYCTierRider    = "RIDER"    // Aadhaar eKYC + DL/RC
97		KYCTierHigh     = "HIGH"     // eKYC + org record / V-CIP for officials
98		KYCTierHighest  = "HIGHEST"  // platform admin: MFA + dual-control
99		KYCTierService  = "SERVICE"  // machine accounts: mTLS / scoped keys
100	)
101	
102	// RequiredKYCTier maps each role to the minimum KYC tier a party must hold
103	// before a role token for it can be issued (blueprint §5.2 "KYC tier").
104	// Tier upgrades happen ONLY through the KYC approval workflow: submit →
105	// PENDING → reviewed by an authorised approver → VERIFIED. There is no
106	// self-service tier upgrade.
107	var RequiredKYCTier = map[string]string{
108		RoleFarmer:               KYCTierFarmer,
109		RoleSamitiSacheev:        KYCTierHigh,
110		RoleSamitiAdhyaksh:       KYCTierHigh,
111		RoleMilkTester:           KYCTierStandard,
112		RoleLRP:                  KYCTierStandard,
113		RoleAITech:               KYCTierStandard,
114		RoleOrganisingManager:    KYCTierHigh,
115		RoleVanRider:             KYCTierRider,
116		RoleDeliveryRider:        KYCTierRider,
117		RoleBMCOperator:          KYCTierStandard,
118		RoleUnionFieldSupervisor: KYCTierHigh,
119		RoleUnionPresident:       KYCTierHigh,
120		RolePlantOperator:        KYCTierHigh,
121		RolePlantLabAnalyst:      KYCTierHigh,
122		RolePCDFAdmin:            KYCTierHigh,
123		RoleMissionOfficial:      KYCTierHigh,
124		RoleDistrictVerifier:     KYCTierHigh,
125		RoleVeterinarian:         KYCTierHigh,
126		RoleMVUDriver:            KYCTierStandard,
127		RoleConsumer:             KYCTierMinimal,
128		RoleSupportAgent:         KYCTierHigh,
129		RoleStateAuditor:         KYCTierHigh,
130		RoleSuperAdmin:           KYCTierHighest,
131		RoleServiceAccount:       KYCTierService,
132	}
133	
134	// kycRank orders tiers so "tier X satisfies requirement Y" is a comparison.
135	var kycRank = map[string]int{
136		KYCTierMinimal:  0,
137		KYCTierFarmer:   1,
138		KYCTierStandard: 1, // Farmer and Standard are parallel tier-1 proofs
139		KYCTierRider:    2,
140		KYCTierHigh:     3,
141		KYCTierHighest:  4,
142		KYCTierService:  4,
143	}
144	
145	// KYCTierSatisfies reports whether a party at tier `have` meets `need`.
146	// Parallel tier-1 proofs (FARMER vs STANDARD) satisfy each other.
147	func KYCTierSatisfies(have, need string) bool {
148		h, okH := kycRank[have]
149		n, okN := kycRank[need]
150		if !okH || !okN {
151			return false
152		}
153		return h >= n
154	}
155	
156	// KYCApprovableTiers maps an approver ROLE to the KYC tiers it may approve.
157	// Ground staff clear the field tiers; only federation admins clear HIGH;
158	// only SUPER_ADMIN clears HIGHEST. Extend when new approver roles arrive.
159	var KYCApprovableTiers = map[string][]string{
160		RoleOrganisingManager: {KYCTierMinimal, KYCTierFarmer, KYCTierStandard, KYCTierRider},
161		RoleDistrictVerifier:  {KYCTierMinimal, KYCTierFarmer, KYCTierStandard, KYCTierRider},
162		RolePCDFAdmin:         {KYCTierMinimal, KYCTierFarmer, KYCTierStandard, KYCTierRider, KYCTierHigh},
163		RoleSuperAdmin:        {KYCTierMinimal, KYCTierFarmer, KYCTierStandard, KYCTierRider, KYCTierHigh, KYCTierHighest, KYCTierService},
164	}
165	
166	// CanApproveKYCTier reports whether approverRole may approve a KYC record
167	// requesting the given tier.
168	func CanApproveKYCTier(approverRole, tier string) bool {
169		for _, t := range KYCApprovableTiers[approverRole] {
170			if t == tier {
171				return true
172			}
173		}
174		return false
175	}
176
```

```text
3	import (

8	
9	// Party statuses.

11		PartyStatusActive    = "ACTIVE"
12		PartyStatusSuspended = "SUSPENDED"
13	)
14	
15	// Party is the single identity record per human (blueprint §4.1):
16	// one phone number = one Party = many org-scoped RoleAssignments.
17	// `_id` is a generated ObjectID; `phone` is the unique natural key used for
18	// login — relations always reference the ObjectID, never the phone.
19	type Party struct {
20		ID                primitive.ObjectID `bson:"_id,omitempty" json:"id"`
21		Phone             string             `bson:"phone"         json:"phone"`
22		FullName          string             `bson:"full_name,omitempty"          json:"full_name,omitempty"`
23		PreferredLanguage string             `bson:"preferred_language,omitempty" json:"preferred_language,omitempty"` // "hi", "en", ...
24		KYCTier           string             `bson:"kyc_tier"      json:"kyc_tier"`
25		Status            string             `bson:"status"        json:"status"`
26		CreatedAt         time.Time          `bson:"created_at"    json:"created_at"`
27		UpdatedAt         time.Time          `bson:"updated_at"    json:"updated_at"`
28	}
29	
30	// RoleAssignment statuses.
31	const (
32		RoleAssignmentActive  = "ACTIVE"
33		RoleAssignmentRevoked = "REVOKED"
34	)
35	
36	// RoleAssignment grants one role to one party inside one org unit for a
37	// validity window. Revoking a Sacheev after an election is a single record
38	// update — never an account deletion (blueprint §4.1).
39	type RoleAssignment struct {
40		ID        primitive.ObjectID  `bson:"_id,omitempty" json:"id"`
41		PartyID   primitive.ObjectID  `bson:"party_id"      json:"party_id"`
42		RoleCode  string              `bson:"role_code"     json:"role_code"`
43		OrgUnitID primitive.ObjectID  `bson:"org_unit_id"   json:"org_unit_id"`
44		GrantedBy *primitive.ObjectID `bson:"granted_by,omitempty" json:"granted_by,omitempty"`
45		ValidFrom time.Time           `bson:"valid_from"    json:"valid_from"`
46		ValidTo   *time.Time          `bson:"valid_to,omitempty"   json:"valid_to,omitempty"` // nil = open-ended
47		Status    string              `bson:"status"        json:"status"`
48		RevokedAt *time.Time          `bson:"revoked_at,omitempty" json:"revoked_at,omitempty"`
49		RevokedBy *primitive.ObjectID `bson:"revoked_by,omitempty" json:"revoked_by,omitempty"`
50		CreatedAt time.Time           `bson:"created_at"    json:"created_at"`
51	}
52	
53	// UsableAt reports whether the assignment is active and inside its validity
54	// window at instant t.
55	func (ra RoleAssignment) UsableAt(t time.Time) bool {
56		if ra.Status != RoleAssignmentActive {
57			return false
58		}
59		if t.Before(ra.ValidFrom) {
60			return false
61		}
62		if ra.ValidTo != nil && t.After(*ra.ValidTo) {
63			return false
64		}
65		return true
66	}
67	
68	// KYC record statuses — the approval workflow:
69	// submit → PENDING → (Organising Manager / District Verifier / PCDF Admin /
70	// Super Admin reviews) → VERIFIED (tier upgraded) or REJECTED (with reason).
71	// A role token is only issuable once the party's tier satisfies the role's
72	// RequiredKYCTier, so "login as rider" is impossible before approval.
73	const (
74		KYCStatusPending  = "PENDING"
75		KYCStatusVerified = "VERIFIED"
76		KYCStatusRejected = "REJECTED"
77	)
78	
79	// KYCRecord stores verification evidence for a party at a requested tier.
80	// Aadhaar compliance (blueprint §18-A): only the LAST 4 digits and an opaque
81	// vault reference are ever stored — never the full number, never biometrics.
82	type KYCRecord struct {
83		ID                primitive.ObjectID   `bson:"_id,omitempty" json:"id"`
84		PartyID           primitive.ObjectID   `bson:"party_id"      json:"party_id"`
85		RequestedTier     string               `bson:"requested_tier" json:"requested_tier"`
86		AadhaarLast4      string               `bson:"aadhaar_last4,omitempty"       json:"aadhaar_last4,omitempty"`
87		AadhaarVaultRef   string               `bson:"aadhaar_vault_ref,omitempty"   json:"aadhaar_vault_ref,omitempty"` // opaque token from the Aadhaar Data Vault
88		BankAccountMasked string               `bson:"bank_account_masked,omitempty" json:"bank_account_masked,omitempty"`
89		BankIFSC          string               `bson:"bank_ifsc,omitempty"           json:"bank_ifsc,omitempty"`
90		BankVerified      bool                 `bson:"bank_verified"                 json:"bank_verified"`
91		BankNameMatch     float64              `bson:"bank_name_match,omitempty"     json:"bank_name_match,omitempty"` // penny-drop name-match score 0..1
92		DigiLockerDocs    []DocRef             `bson:"digilocker_docs,omitempty"     json:"digilocker_docs,omitempty"`
93		VideoKYCRef       string               `bson:"video_kyc_ref,omitempty"       json:"video_kyc_ref,omitempty"`
94		ConsentID         *primitive.ObjectID  `bson:"consent_id,omitempty"          json:"consent_id,omitempty"`
95		Status            string               `bson:"status"        json:"status"`
96		RejectionReason   string               `bson:"rejection_reason,omitempty" json:"rejection_reason,omitempty"`
97		ReviewedBy        *primitive.ObjectID  `bson:"reviewed_by,omitempty"      json:"reviewed_by,omitempty"` // approver party
98		ReviewedByRole    string               `bson:"reviewed_by_role,omitempty" json:"reviewed_by_role,omitempty"`
99		ReviewedAt        *time.Time           `bson:"reviewed_at,omitempty"      json:"reviewed_at,omitempty"`
100		VerifiedAt        *time.Time           `bson:"verified_at,omitempty"      json:"verified_at,omitempty"`
101		CreatedAt         time.Time            `bson:"created_at"    json:"created_at"`
102		UpdatedAt         time.Time            `bson:"updated_at"    json:"updated_at"`
103	}
104	
105	// DocRef points at an externally fetched document (DigiLocker etc.).
106	type DocRef struct {
107		DocType   string    `bson:"doc_type"  json:"doc_type"` // LAND_RECORD, CASTE_CERT, DL, RC ...
108		Issuer    string    `bson:"issuer"    json:"issuer"`
109		RefID     string    `bson:"ref_id"    json:"ref_id"`
110		FetchedAt time.Time `bson:"fetched_at" json:"fetched_at"`

121		GrantedAt   time.Time          `bson:"granted_at"    json:"granted_at"`
122		WithdrawnAt *time.Time         `bson:"withdrawn_at,omitempty" json:"withdrawn_at,omitempty"`
```

```text
11	func TestQRTokenRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
12		const secret = "test-qr-secret"
13		issuedAt := time.Date(2026, 7, 6, 9, 30, 0, 0, time.UTC)
14	
15		token := signQRToken(secret, "[REDACTED:generic-api-key]", "lot-123", issuedAt)
16	
17		code, lotID, ts, err := parseQRToken(secret, token)
18		if err != nil {
19			t.Fatalf("parseQRToken: unexpected error: %v", err)
20		}
21		if code != "[REDACTED:generic-api-key]" {
22			t.Errorf("qr code: got %q, want %q", code, "[REDACTED:generic-api-key]")
23		}
24		if lotID != "lot-123" {
25			t.Errorf("product lot id: got %q, want %q", lotID, "lot-123")
26		}
27		if !ts.Equal(issuedAt) {
28			t.Errorf("issued at: got %v, want %v", ts, issuedAt)
29		}
30	}

32	func TestQRTokenRejectsForgery(t *testing.T) {
33		const secret = "test-qr-secret"
34		issuedAt := time.Now().UTC()
35		token := signQRToken(secret, "PRG-AAAA2222", "lot-legit", issuedAt)
36	
37		cases := []struct {
38			name   string
39			secret string
40			token  string
41		}{
42			{"wrong secret", "attacker-secret", token},
43			{"tampered payload", secret, "X" + token[1:]},
44			{"tampered signature", secret, token[:len(token)-1] + flipHexChar(token[len(token)-1])},
45			{"missing separator", secret, strings.ReplaceAll(token, ".", "")},
46			{"garbage", secret, "not-a-token"},
47			{"empty", secret, ""},
48		}
49		for _, tc := range cases {
50			t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
51				if _, _, _, err := parseQRToken(tc.secret, tc.token); err == nil {
52					t.Errorf("parseQRToken accepted a forged/malformed token")
53				}
54			})
55		}
56	}
57	
58	// flipHexChar returns a different valid hex digit so signature length stays
59	// intact while its value changes.
60	func flipHexChar(c byte) string {
61		if c == '0' {
62			return "1"
63		}
64		return "0"
65	}

77			if len(body) != qrCodeLength {

86				}
```

```text
9	// Notification channels — SMS/IVR are essential, not optional, for low-literacy
```

```text
44	// PricePour computes (ratePerLitre, amount) for a pour, rounded to paise.
45	func (rc RateChart) PricePour(fatPct, snfPct, qtyLitres float64) (rate, amount float64) {
46		rate = rc.BaseRatePerLitre + fatPct*rc.FatRatePerPoint + snfPct*rc.SNFRatePerPoint
47		rate = math.Round(rate*100) / 100
48		amount = math.Round(rate*qtyLitres*100) / 100
49		return rate, amount
50	}

94	// CheckPlausibility validates fat/SNF/qty against physical bounds and returns
95	// the violated flags (empty slice = plausible).
96	func CheckPlausibility(fatPct, snfPct, qtyLitres float64) []string {
97		var flags []string
98		if fatPct < PlausibleFatMin || fatPct > PlausibleFatMax ||
99			snfPct < PlausibleSNFMin || snfPct > PlausibleSNFMax {
100			flags = append(flags, IntegrityFlagImplausibleValue)
101		}
102		if qtyLitres != 0 && (qtyLitres < PlausibleQtyMin || qtyLitres > PlausibleQtyMax) {
103			flags = append(flags, IntegrityFlagImplausibleValue)
104		}
105		return flags
106	}
```

```text
	code := make([]byte, qrCodeLength)
	for i, b := range buf {
		code[i] = qrAlphabet[int(b)%len(qrAlphabet)]
	}
	return "PRG-" + string(code), nil
}

// signQRToken builds the forgery-proof token printed inside the QR:
// base64url(qr_code|product_lot_id|issued_unix) + "." + hex(HMAC-SHA256).
// The consumer app resolves the payload; the signature proves it was minted
// by this server, so IDs cannot be guessed onto counterfeit packs.
func signQRToken(secret, qrCode, productLotID string, issuedAt time.Time) string {
	payload := qrCode + "|" + productLotID + "|" + strconv.FormatInt(issuedAt.Unix(), 10)
	mac := hmac.New(sha256.New, []byte(secret))
	mac.Write([]byte(payload))
	return base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString([]byte(payload)) + "." + hex.EncodeToString(mac.Sum(nil))
}

// parseQRToken verifies and unpacks a signed QR token.
func parseQRToken(secret, token string) (qrCode, productLotID string, issuedAt time.Time, err error) {
	payloadB64, sigHex, found := strings.Cut(token, ".")
	if !found {
		return "", "", time.Time{}, errors.New("qr token: missing signature separator")
	}
	payloadBytes, err := base64.RawURLEncoding.DecodeString(payloadB64)
	if err != nil {
		return "", "", time.Time{}, fmt.Errorf("qr token: bad payload encoding: %w", err)
	}
	sig, err := hex.DecodeString(sigHex)
	if err != nil {
		return "", "", time.Time{}, fmt.Errorf("qr token: bad signature encoding: %w", err)
```

```text
8	// Actor is the authenticated caller extracted from a verified token and
9	// stored on the request context by the auth middleware.
10	type Actor struct {
11		PartyID          string
12		Phone            string
13		KYCTier          string

15		RoleAssignmentID string
16		RoleCode         string

18		OrgType          string
19	}

21	// HasRole reports whether the actor operates under one of the given roles.
22	func (a Actor) HasRole(roles ...string) bool {
23		for _, r := range roles {
24			if a.RoleCode == r {
25				return true
26			}
27		}
28		return false
29	}

31	type actorCtxKey struct{}
32	
33	// actorHolder is a mutable cell installed by OUTER middleware (audit) so
34	// identity established by INNER middleware (Authenticate) can flow back out.
35	// Context values only propagate inward; the shared pointer bridges the gap.
36	type actorHolder struct {
37		mu sync.Mutex
38		a  *Actor
39	}
40	
41	type actorHolderCtxKey struct{}
42	
43	// WithActorHolder installs an empty actor holder on the context. Middleware
44	// mounted before authentication uses it to observe the actor after the
45	// handler chain ran.
46	func WithActorHolder(ctx context.Context) context.Context {
47		return context.WithValue(ctx, actorHolderCtxKey{}, &actorHolder{})
48	}
49	
50	// HeldActor returns the actor captured by an inner WithActor call, if a
51	// holder was installed and authentication happened.
52	func HeldActor(ctx context.Context) (Actor, bool) {
53		h, ok := ctx.Value(actorHolderCtxKey{}).(*actorHolder)
54		if !ok {
55			return Actor{}, false
56		}
57		h.mu.Lock()
58		defer h.mu.Unlock()
59		if h.a == nil {
60			return Actor{}, false
61		}
62		return *h.a, true
63	}
64	
65	// WithActor stores the actor on the context, and also fills the outward
66	// actor holder when one was installed upstream (see WithActorHolder).
67	func WithActor(ctx context.Context, a Actor) context.Context {
68		if h, ok := ctx.Value(actorHolderCtxKey{}).(*actorHolder); ok {
69			h.mu.Lock()
70			cp := a
71			h.a = &cp
72			h.mu.Unlock()
73		}
74		return context.WithValue(ctx, actorCtxKey{}, a)
75	}
76	
77	// ActorFrom retrieves the actor, if any.
78	func ActorFrom(ctx context.Context) (Actor, bool) {
79		a, ok := ctx.Value(actorCtxKey{}).(Actor)
80		return a, ok
81	}
```

```text
1	// Package eventbus is the in-process pub/sub seam between modules
2	// (e.g. settlement executed → notifications module queues the SMS).
3	// It deliberately mirrors a message-broker API: when the platform splits
4	// into microservices, this interface is re-implemented over Kafka/NATS
5	// (blueprint §15) without touching module code.
6	package eventbus
7	
8	import (
9		"context"
10		"log/slog"
11		"sync"
12		"time"
13	)
14	
15	// Topics published across module seams.
16	const (
17		TopicPourRecorded       = "pour.recorded"
18		TopicInvoiceIssued      = "invoice.issued"
19		TopicGateBlocked        = "qc.gate_blocked"
20		TopicSettlementExecuted = "settlement.executed"
21		TopicPayoutCredited     = "payout.credited"
22		TopicMVUDispatched      = "mvu.dispatched"
23	)
24	
25	// Handler consumes a published event. Payload types are documented per topic
26	// by the publishing module.
27	type Handler func(ctx context.Context, topic string, payload any)
28	
29	// Bus is a minimal async pub/sub.
30	type Bus struct {
31		log *slog.Logger
32	
33		mu   sync.RWMutex
34		subs map[string][]Handler
35	}
36	
37	// New builds an empty bus.
38	func New(log *slog.Logger) *Bus {
39		return &Bus{log: log, subs: make(map[string][]Handler)}
40	}
41	
42	// Subscribe registers a handler for a topic. Call during module wiring only
43	// (not concurrently with Publish traffic).
44	func (b *Bus) Subscribe(topic string, h Handler) {
45		b.mu.Lock()
46		defer b.mu.Unlock()
47		b.subs[topic] = append(b.subs[topic], h)
48	}
49	
50	// Publish dispatches asynchronously: each handler runs on its own goroutine
51	// with a bounded context and panic isolation, so a slow or broken subscriber
52	// can never stall the request path.
53	func (b *Bus) Publish(topic string, payload any) {
54		b.mu.RLock()
55		handlers := b.subs[topic]
56		b.mu.RUnlock()
57	
58		for _, h := range handlers {
59			h := h
60			go func() {
61				ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 15*time.Second)
62				defer cancel()
63				defer func() {
64					if rec := recover(); rec != nil {
65						b.log.Error("eventbus handler panic",
66							slog.String("topic", topic), slog.Any("panic", rec))
67					}
68				}()
69				h(ctx, topic, payload)
70			}()
71		}
72	}
73
```

```text
20	// Entry is one audit record. `_id` is a generated ObjectID; actor identifiers
21	// arrive from JWT claims as ObjectID hex strings.

25		ActorRole    string         `bson:"actor_role,omitempty" json:"actor_role,omitempty"`
26		Action       string         `bson:"action"         json:"action"` // e.g. "http.POST /api/v1/collection/pours" or "support.pii_lookup"
27		TargetType   string         `bson:"target_type,omitempty" json:"target_type,omitempty"`
28		TargetID     string         `bson:"target_id,omitempty"   json:"target_id,omitempty"`
29		Status       int            `bson:"status,omitempty"      json:"status,omitempty"`
30		IP           string         `bson:"ip,omitempty"          json:"ip,omitempty"`
31		RequestID    string         `bson:"request_id,omitempty"  json:"request_id,omitempty"`
32		Meta         map[string]any `bson:"meta,omitempty"        json:"meta,omitempty"`
33		TS           time.Time      `bson:"ts"             json:"ts"`
34	}
35	
36	// Recorder persists audit entries asynchronously so auditing never adds
37	// latency to the request path.
38	type Recorder struct {
39		coll *mongo.Collection
40		log  *slog.Logger
41	}

45		return &Recorder{coll: db.Collection(collection), log: log}
46	}

48	// Record fills identity fields from the request context and persists the
49	// entry in the background (fire-and-forget with its own timeout).
50	func (r *Recorder) Record(ctx context.Context, e Entry) {
51		if a, ok := auth.ActorFrom(ctx); ok {

53				e.ActorPartyID = a.PartyID

57			}

60		e.TS = time.Now().UTC()
61	
62		go func() {

64			defer cancel()
65			if _, err := r.coll.InsertOne(writeCtx, e); err != nil {
66				r.log.Error("audit write failed", slog.String("action", e.Action), slog.Any("err", err))
```

```text
1	// Package orgscope answers the RBAC question "is this resource inside the
2	// caller's organisational scope?" in O(1) DB reads. Org units denormalise
3	// their ancestor chain into Path ([]ObjectID), so scope checking is a
4	// set-membership test — no recursive tree walks on the hot path.
5	package orgscope
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"errors"
10		"sync"
11		"time"
12	
13		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson"
14		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson/primitive"
15		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo"
16	
17		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/domain"
18		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/auth"
19		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/httpx"
20	)
21	
22	const collection = "org_units"
23	
24	type cachedOrg struct {
25		org domain.OrgUnit
26		at  time.Time
27	}
28	
29	// Resolver caches org units briefly (the tree changes rarely, reads are hot).
30	type Resolver struct {
31		coll *mongo.Collection
32		ttl  time.Duration
33	
34		mu    sync.RWMutex
35		cache map[string]cachedOrg // keyed by ObjectID hex
36	}
37	
38	// NewResolver binds the resolver to the database.
39	func NewResolver(db *mongo.Database) *Resolver {
40		return &Resolver{
41			coll:  db.Collection(collection),
42			ttl:   60 * time.Second,
43			cache: make(map[string]cachedOrg),
44		}
45	}
46	
47	// Get returns an org unit by ObjectID (cached).
48	func (r *Resolver) Get(ctx context.Context, id primitive.ObjectID) (*domain.OrgUnit, error) {
49		key := id.Hex()
50		r.mu.RLock()
51		c, ok := r.cache[key]
52		r.mu.RUnlock()
53		if ok && time.Since(c.at) < r.ttl {
54			org := c.org
55			return &org, nil
56		}
57	
58		var org domain.OrgUnit
59		err := r.coll.FindOne(ctx, bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: id}}).Decode(&org)
60		if errors.Is(err, mongo.ErrNoDocuments) {
61			return nil, httpx.NotFound("org unit " + key)
62		}
63		if err != nil {
64			return nil, httpx.Internal(err)
65		}
66	
67		r.mu.Lock()
68		r.cache[key] = cachedOrg{org: org, at: time.Now()}
69		r.mu.Unlock()
70		return &org, nil
71	}
72	
73	// GetByCode returns an org unit by its unique human-readable business code
74	// (e.g. "DCS-01842") — display/lookup use only, never for joins.
75	func (r *Resolver) GetByCode(ctx context.Context, code string) (*domain.OrgUnit, error) {
76		var org domain.OrgUnit
77		err := r.coll.FindOne(ctx, bson.D{{Key: "code", Value: code}}).Decode(&org)
78		if errors.Is(err, mongo.ErrNoDocuments) {
79			return nil, httpx.NotFound("org unit with code " + code)
80		}
81		if err != nil {
82			return nil, httpx.Internal(err)
83		}
84		return &org, nil
85	}
86	
87	// Invalidate drops a cached entry (call after updates).
88	func (r *Resolver) Invalidate(id primitive.ObjectID) {
89		r.mu.Lock()
90		delete(r.cache, id.Hex())
91		r.mu.Unlock()
92	}
93	
94	// InScope reports whether target sits at-or-below scope in the hierarchy:
95	// true when scope == target, or scope appears in target's ancestor Path.
96	func (r *Resolver) InScope(ctx context.Context, scopeOrgID, targetOrgID primitive.ObjectID) (bool, error) {
97		if scopeOrgID == targetOrgID {
98			return true, nil
99		}
100		target, err := r.Get(ctx, targetOrgID)
101		if err != nil {
102			return false, err
103		}
104		for _, ancestor := range target.Path {
105			if ancestor == scopeOrgID {
106				return true, nil
107			}
108		}
109		return false, nil
110	}
111	
112	// RequireInScope enforces the actor's org scope over a target org unit.
113	// SUPER_ADMIN and STATE_AUDITOR (read-wide roles rooted at the federation)
114	// pass automatically; everyone else needs ancestry. The actor carries its
115	// org unit as an ObjectID hex string (JWT claims are JSON); it is parsed here.
116	func (r *Resolver) RequireInScope(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, targetOrgID primitive.ObjectID) error {
117		if actor.RoleCode == domain.RoleSuperAdmin || actor.RoleCode == domain.RoleStateAuditor {
118			return nil
119		}
120		if actor.OrgUnitID == "" {
121			return httpx.Forbidden("role token with org scope required")
122		}
123		scopeID, err := primitive.ObjectIDFromHex(actor.OrgUnitID)
124		if err != nil {
125			return httpx.Forbidden("role token carries an invalid org scope")
126		}
127		ok, err := r.InScope(ctx, scopeID, targetOrgID)
128		if err != nil {
129			return err
130		}
131		if !ok {
132			return httpx.Forbidden("resource is outside your organisational scope")
133		}
134		return nil
135	}
136
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	// Package auth owns tokens and credentials: JWT issue/verify, OTP generation
2	// and HMAC hashing, opaque refresh tokens. Nothing secret is ever stored in
3	// plaintext — OTPs and refresh tokens live in the DB only as HMAC-SHA256
4	// digests.
5	package auth
6	
7	import (
8		"fmt"
9		"time"
10	
11		"github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v5"
12		"github.com/google/uuid"
13	
14		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/domain"
15	)
16	
17	// Token kinds. A SESSION token proves "this phone logged in"; a ROLE token
18	// additionally pins one active role assignment + org scope (the role switcher
19	// simply issues a fresh ROLE token).
20	const (
21		TokenKindSession = "session"
22		TokenKindRole    = "role"
23	)
24	
25	// Claims is the JWT payload.
26	type Claims struct {
27		PartyID          string `json:"pid"`
28		Phone            string `json:"phn"`
29		KYCTier          string `json:"kyc"`
30		Kind             string `json:"knd"`
31		RoleAssignmentID string `json:"rid,omitempty"`
32		RoleCode         string `json:"rol,omitempty"`
33		OrgUnitID        string `json:"org,omitempty"`
34		OrgType          string `json:"ogt,omitempty"`
35		jwt.RegisteredClaims
36	}
37	
38	// JWTManager issues and parses access tokens.
39	type JWTManager struct {
40		secret []byte
41		ttl    time.Duration
42	}
43	
44	// NewJWTManager builds a manager with the shared HS256 secret and access TTL.
45	func NewJWTManager(secret string, ttl time.Duration) *JWTManager {
46		return &JWTManager{secret: []byte(secret), ttl: ttl}
47	}
48	
49	// IssueSessionToken returns a SESSION-kind access token for a logged-in party.
50	// ObjectIDs travel in claims as hex strings (JWTs are JSON).
51	func (m *JWTManager) IssueSessionToken(p domain.Party) (string, error) {
52		return m.sign(Claims{
53			PartyID: p.ID.Hex(),
54			Phone:   p.Phone,
55			KYCTier: p.KYCTier,
56			Kind:    TokenKindSession,
57		})
58	}
59	
60	// IssueRoleToken returns a ROLE-kind access token pinned to one assignment.
61	func (m *JWTManager) IssueRoleToken(p domain.Party, ra domain.RoleAssignment, orgType string) (string, error) {
62		return m.sign(Claims{
63			PartyID:          p.ID.Hex(),
64			Phone:            p.Phone,
65			KYCTier:          p.KYCTier,
66			Kind:             TokenKindRole,
67			RoleAssignmentID: ra.ID.Hex(),
68			RoleCode:         ra.RoleCode,
69			OrgUnitID:        ra.OrgUnitID.Hex(),
70			OrgType:          orgType,
71		})
72	}
73	
74	func (m *JWTManager) sign(c Claims) (string, error) {
75		now := time.Now()
76		c.RegisteredClaims = jwt.RegisteredClaims{
77			Issuer:    "saathi-backend",
78			Subject:   c.PartyID,
79			IssuedAt:  jwt.NewNumericDate(now),
80			ExpiresAt: jwt.NewNumericDate(now.Add(m.ttl)),
81			ID:        uuid.NewString(),
82		}
83		return jwt.NewWithClaims(jwt.SigningMethodHS256, c).SignedString(m.secret)
84	}
85	
86	// Parse validates signature+expiry and returns the claims.
87	func (m *JWTManager) Parse(token string) (*Claims, error) {
88		parsed, err := jwt.ParseWithClaims(token, &Claims{},
89			func(t *jwt.Token) (any, error) { return m.secret, nil },
90			jwt.WithValidMethods([]string{jwt.SigningMethodHS256.Alg()}),
91			jwt.WithIssuer("saathi-backend"),
92		)
93		if err != nil {
94			return nil, fmt.Errorf("parse token: %w", err)
95		}
96		claims, ok := parsed.Claims.(*Claims)
97		if !ok || !parsed.Valid {
98			return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid token claims")
99		}
100		return claims, nil
101	}
102
```

```text
1	// Package eventbus is the in-process pub/sub seam between modules
2	// (e.g. settlement executed → notifications module queues the SMS).
3	// It deliberately mirrors a message-broker API: when the platform splits
4	// into microservices, this interface is re-implemented over Kafka/NATS
5	// (blueprint §15) without touching module code.
6	package eventbus
7	
8	import (
9		"context"
10		"log/slog"
11		"sync"
12		"time"
13	)
14	
15	// Topics published across module seams.
16	const (
17		TopicPourRecorded       = "pour.recorded"
18		TopicInvoiceIssued      = "invoice.issued"
19		TopicGateBlocked        = "qc.gate_blocked"
20		TopicSettlementExecuted = "settlement.executed"
21		TopicPayoutCredited     = "payout.credited"
22		TopicMVUDispatched      = "mvu.dispatched"
23	)
24	
25	// Handler consumes a published event. Payload types are documented per topic
26	// by the publishing module.
27	type Handler func(ctx context.Context, topic string, payload any)
28	
29	// Bus is a minimal async pub/sub.
30	type Bus struct {
31		log *slog.Logger
32	
33		mu   sync.RWMutex
34		subs map[string][]Handler
35	}
36	
37	// New builds an empty bus.
38	func New(log *slog.Logger) *Bus {
39		return &Bus{log: log, subs: make(map[string][]Handler)}
40	}
41	
42	// Subscribe registers a handler for a topic. Call during module wiring only
43	// (not concurrently with Publish traffic).
44	func (b *Bus) Subscribe(topic string, h Handler) {
45		b.mu.Lock()
46		defer b.mu.Unlock()
47		b.subs[topic] = append(b.subs[topic], h)
48	}
49	
50	// Publish dispatches asynchronously: each handler runs on its own goroutine
51	// with a bounded context and panic isolation, so a slow or broken subscriber
52	// can never stall the request path.
53	func (b *Bus) Publish(topic string, payload any) {
54		b.mu.RLock()
55		handlers := b.subs[topic]
56		b.mu.RUnlock()
57	
58		for _, h := range handlers {
59			h := h
60			go func() {
61				ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 15*time.Second)
62				defer cancel()
63				defer func() {
64					if rec := recover(); rec != nil {
65						b.log.Error("eventbus handler panic",
66							slog.String("topic", topic), slog.Any("panic", rec))
67					}
68				}()
69				h(ctx, topic, payload)
70			}()
71		}
72	}
73
```

```text
33	// OrgUnit is a node in the cooperative hierarchy.
34	//
35	// ID scheme: `_id` is a generated ObjectID (relations always reference it);
36	// Code is the human-readable unique business key (e.g. "DCS-01842") used for
37	// display, lookups and seed idempotency — never for joins.
38	//
39	// Path holds the ObjectIDs of all ancestors from the root down to (and
40	// excluding) this node — denormalised so "is X inside Y's scope" is a single
41	// indexed array-containment check with no recursive queries on the hot path.
42	type OrgUnit struct {
43		ID        primitive.ObjectID   `bson:"_id,omitempty" json:"id"`
44		Type      string               `bson:"type"          json:"type"`
45		Name      string               `bson:"name"          json:"name"`
46		Code      string               `bson:"code"          json:"code"` // unique business key, e.g. "DCS-01842"
47		ParentID  *primitive.ObjectID  `bson:"parent_id,omitempty" json:"parent_id,omitempty"`
48		Path      []primitive.ObjectID `bson:"path"          json:"path"`
49		District  string               `bson:"district,omitempty" json:"district,omitempty"`
50		State     string               `bson:"state,omitempty"    json:"state,omitempty"`
51		GeoLat    float64              `bson:"geo_lat,omitempty"  json:"geo_lat,omitempty"`
52		GeoLng    float64              `bson:"geo_lng,omitempty"  json:"geo_lng,omitempty"`
53		Active    bool                 `bson:"active"        json:"active"`
54		CreatedAt time.Time            `bson:"created_at"    json:"created_at"`
55		UpdatedAt time.Time            `bson:"updated_at"    json:"updated_at"`
56	}
57	
58	// IsValidOrgType reports whether t is a known org-unit type.
59	func IsValidOrgType(t string) bool {
60		for _, v := range AllOrgTypes {
61			if v == t {
62				return true
63			}
64		}
65		return false
66	}
```

```text
	RevokedBy *primitive.ObjectID `bson:"revoked_by,omitempty" json:"revoked_by,omitempty"`
	CreatedAt time.Time           `bson:"created_at"    json:"created_at"`
}
```

```text
1	// Package httpx is the HTTP toolkit shared by every module: typed errors,
2	// uniform JSON envelopes, strict request decoding, pagination.
3	package httpx
4	
5	import (
6		"fmt"
7		"net/http"
8	)
9	
10	// AppError is the single error type handlers return. It carries the HTTP
11	// status plus a stable machine-readable code the frontend can switch on.
12	type AppError struct {
13		Status  int    `json:"-"`
14		Code    string `json:"code"`
15		Message string `json:"message"`
16		Details any    `json:"details,omitempty"`
17	
18		cause error // wrapped internal error — logged server-side, never serialised
19	}
20	
21	func (e *AppError) Error() string {
22		return fmt.Sprintf("%d %s: %s", e.Status, e.Code, e.Message)
23	}
24	
25	// WithDetails returns a copy carrying extra structured context.
26	func (e *AppError) WithDetails(d any) *AppError {
27		cp := *e
28		cp.Details = d
29		return &cp
30	}
31	
32	func newErr(status int, code, msg string) *AppError {
33		return &AppError{Status: status, Code: code, Message: msg}
34	}
35	
36	// Constructors — use these instead of raw errors in handlers/services.
37	
38	func BadRequest(code, msg string) *AppError { return newErr(http.StatusBadRequest, code, msg) }
39	
40	func Unauthorized(msg string) *AppError { return newErr(http.StatusUnauthorized, "UNAUTHORIZED", msg) }
41	
42	func Forbidden(msg string) *AppError { return newErr(http.StatusForbidden, "FORBIDDEN", msg) }
43	
44	func NotFound(resource string) *AppError {
45		return newErr(http.StatusNotFound, "NOT_FOUND", resource+" not found")
46	}
47	
48	// RouteNotFound is the router-level 404 for unmatched paths, keeping the
49	// uniform JSON error envelope on typo'd routes.
50	func RouteNotFound() *AppError {
51		return newErr(http.StatusNotFound, "NOT_FOUND", "route not found")
52	}
53	
54	// MethodNotAllowed is the router-level 405 for wrong-method requests.
55	func MethodNotAllowed() *AppError {
56		return newErr(http.StatusMethodNotAllowed, "METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED", "method not allowed for this route")
57	}
58	
59	func Conflict(code, msg string) *AppError { return newErr(http.StatusConflict, code, msg) }
60	
61	func Unprocessable(code, msg string) *AppError {
62		return newErr(http.StatusUnprocessableEntity, code, msg)
63	}
64	
65	func TooManyRequests(msg string) *AppError {
66		return newErr(http.StatusTooManyRequests, "RATE_LIMITED", msg)
67	}
68	
69	// Internal wraps an unexpected error. The cause is logged server-side but
70	// never leaked to the client.
71	func Internal(err error) *AppError {
72		e := newErr(http.StatusInternalServerError, "INTERNAL", "internal server error")
73		e.cause = err
74		return e
75	}
76	
77	func (e *AppError) Unwrap() error { return e.cause }
78
```

```text
1	// Package mongodb owns the MongoDB connection and the index catalog.
2	// The connection string comes exclusively from configuration (env) — never
3	// from code.
4	package mongodb
5	
6	import (
7		"context"
8		"fmt"
9		"time"
10	
11		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo"
12		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo/options"
13		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo/readpref"
14	)
15	
16	// Connect dials MongoDB, verifies the connection with a ping, and returns the
17	// client plus the application database handle. Pool sizing targets peak
18	// pour-time write bursts (twice-daily shift spikes, blueprint §16).
19	func Connect(ctx context.Context, uri, dbName string) (*mongo.Client, *mongo.Database, error) {
20		opts := options.Client().
21			ApplyURI(uri).
22			SetMaxPoolSize(200).
23			SetMinPoolSize(8).
24			SetMaxConnIdleTime(5 * time.Minute).
25			SetServerSelectionTimeout(5 * time.Second).
26			SetTimeout(15 * time.Second)
27	
28		client, err := mongo.Connect(ctx, opts)
29		if err != nil {
30			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("mongo connect: %w", err)
31		}
32	
33		pingCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 5*time.Second)
34		defer cancel()
35		if err := client.Ping(pingCtx, readpref.Primary()); err != nil {
36			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("mongo ping (%s): %w", uri, err)
37		}
38	
39		return client, client.Database(dbName), nil
40	}
41
```

```text
// Package collection implements the core procurement loop of Saathi
// (blueprint §8.1, §8.2): org-scoped rate charts, anti-tamper analyzer
// readings, offline-first idempotent milk pours with same-day pricing, and
// per-farmer daily invoices behind the same-day payment promise.
//
// Bus topics published by this module:
//   - eventbus.TopicPourRecorded  — payload domain.MilkPour (the newly recorded pour)
//   - eventbus.TopicInvoiceIssued — payload domain.Invoice (the newly issued invoice)
package collection

import (
	"github.com/go-chi/chi/v5"

	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/domain"
	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/deps"
	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/middleware"
)

// Register mounts the collection module under /collection and wires the
// handler → service → repo stack onto the shared platform dependencies.
func Register(r chi.Router, d *deps.Deps) {
	repo := newRepo(d)
	svc := newService(d, repo)
	h := &handler{svc: svc}

	r.Route("/collection", func(r chi.Router) {
		r.Use(middleware.Authenticate(d.JWT))

		// Rate charts: pricing policy is set at union/federation level and
		// resolved downward to each DCS (nearest ancestor wins).
		r.Route("/rate-charts", func(r chi.Router) {
			r.With(middleware.RequireRoles(domain.RolePCDFAdmin, domain.RoleUnionPresident)).
				Post("/", h.createRateChart)
			r.With(middleware.RequireSession).Get("/active", h.getActiveRateChart)
		})

		// Analyzer readings: flagged, never rejected (anti-tamper envelope §8.2).
		r.Route("/readings", func(r chi.Router) {
			r.With(middleware.RequireRoles(domain.RoleSamitiSacheev, domain.RoleMilkTester)).
				Post("/", h.createReading)
			r.With(middleware.RequireRoles(
				domain.RoleSamitiSacheev, domain.RoleMilkTester, domain.RoleUnionFieldSupervisor,
			)).Get("/", h.listReadings)
		})

		// Pours: THE core loop — offline-first idempotent, hard plausibility gate.
		r.Route("/pours", func(r chi.Router) {
			r.Group(func(r chi.Router) {
				r.Use(middleware.RequireRoles(domain.RoleSamitiSacheev, domain.RoleMilkTester))
				r.Post("/", h.createPour)
				r.Post("/batch-sync", h.batchSyncPours)
				r.Post("/{id}/supersede", h.supersedePour)
			})
			r.With(middleware.RequireRoles(
				domain.RoleSamitiSacheev, domain.RoleMilkTester,
				domain.RoleUnionFieldSupervisor, domain.RoleFarmer,
			)).Get("/", h.listPours)
		})

		// Invoices: the same-day settlement artefact (§8.1).
```

```text
// payoutCreditedEvent mirrors the settlement module's payload on
```

```text
1	// Package httpx is the HTTP toolkit shared by every module: typed errors,
2	// uniform JSON envelopes, strict request decoding, pagination.
3	package httpx
4	
5	import (
6		"fmt"
7		"net/http"
8	)
9	
10	// AppError is the single error type handlers return. It carries the HTTP
11	// status plus a stable machine-readable code the frontend can switch on.
12	type AppError struct {
13		Status  int    `json:"-"`
14		Code    string `json:"code"`
15		Message string `json:"message"`
16		Details any    `json:"details,omitempty"`
17	
18		cause error // wrapped internal error — logged server-side, never serialised
19	}
20	
21	func (e *AppError) Error() string {
22		return fmt.Sprintf("%d %s: %s", e.Status, e.Code, e.Message)
23	}
24	
25	// WithDetails returns a copy carrying extra structured context.
26	func (e *AppError) WithDetails(d any) *AppError {
27		cp := *e
28		cp.Details = d
29		return &cp
30	}
31	
32	func newErr(status int, code, msg string) *AppError {
33		return &AppError{Status: status, Code: code, Message: msg}
34	}
35	
36	// Constructors — use these instead of raw errors in handlers/services.
37	
38	func BadRequest(code, msg string) *AppError { return newErr(http.StatusBadRequest, code, msg) }
39	
40	func Unauthorized(msg string) *AppError { return newErr(http.StatusUnauthorized, "UNAUTHORIZED", msg) }
41	
42	func Forbidden(msg string) *AppError { return newErr(http.StatusForbidden, "FORBIDDEN", msg) }
43	
44	func NotFound(resource string) *AppError {
45		return newErr(http.StatusNotFound, "NOT_FOUND", resource+" not found")
46	}
47	
48	// RouteNotFound is the router-level 404 for unmatched paths, keeping the
49	// uniform JSON error envelope on typo'd routes.
50	func RouteNotFound() *AppError {
51		return newErr(http.StatusNotFound, "NOT_FOUND", "route not found")
52	}
53	
54	// MethodNotAllowed is the router-level 405 for wrong-method requests.
55	func MethodNotAllowed() *AppError {
56		return newErr(http.StatusMethodNotAllowed, "METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED", "method not allowed for this route")
57	}
58	
59	func Conflict(code, msg string) *AppError { return newErr(http.StatusConflict, code, msg) }
60	
61	func Unprocessable(code, msg string) *AppError {
62		return newErr(http.StatusUnprocessableEntity, code, msg)
63	}
64	
65	func TooManyRequests(msg string) *AppError {
66		return newErr(http.StatusTooManyRequests, "RATE_LIMITED", msg)
67	}
68	
69	// Internal wraps an unexpected error. The cause is logged server-side but
70	// never leaked to the client.
71	func Internal(err error) *AppError {
72		e := newErr(http.StatusInternalServerError, "INTERNAL", "internal server error")
73		e.cause = err
74		return e
75	}
76	
77	func (e *AppError) Unwrap() error { return e.cause }
78
```

```text
1	package middleware

11	// RequireRoles allows only ROLE-kind tokens whose role is in the allow-list.
12	// SUPER_ADMIN passes every gate (break-glass admin — all its calls are
13	// audited by the audit middleware).
14	func RequireRoles(roles ...string) func(http.Handler) http.Handler {
15		allowed := make(map[string]struct{}, len(roles))
16		for _, r := range roles {
17			allowed[r] = struct{}{}
18		}
19		return func(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
20			return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
21				actor, ok := auth.ActorFrom(r.Context())
22				if !ok {
23					httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Unauthorized("authentication required"))
24					return
25				}
26				if actor.Kind != auth.TokenKindRole {
27					httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Forbidden("a role token is required — select a role first (POST /api/v1/auth/role/select)"))
28					return
29				}
30				if actor.RoleCode == domain.RoleSuperAdmin {
31					next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
32					return
33				}
34				if _, ok := allowed[actor.RoleCode]; !ok {
35					httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Forbidden("role "+actor.RoleCode+" is not permitted for this action"))
36					return
37				}
38				next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
39			})
40		}
41	}
42	
43	// RequireSession allows any authenticated party (session or role token) —
44	// used for identity endpoints like "list my roles".
45	func RequireSession(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
46		return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
47			if _, ok := auth.ActorFrom(r.Context()); !ok {
48				httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Unauthorized("authentication required"))
49				return
50			}
51			next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
52		})
53	}
```
