```go
package logistics

import (
	"net/http"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson/primitive"

	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/domain"
	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/httpx"
)

// Fixed ObjectIDs shared across the state-machine test tables.
var (
	testRider      = primitive.NewObjectID()
	testOtherRider = primitive.NewObjectID()
	testTrip       = primitive.NewObjectID()
	testUnion      = primitive.NewObjectID()
	testDCS1       = primitive.NewObjectID()
	testDCS2       = primitive.NewObjectID()
	testCon1       = primitive.NewObjectID()
	testCon2       = primitive.NewObjectID()
	testUnknownCon = primitive.NewObjectID()
)

// tripFixture builds a two-stop trip; picked marks which consignment IDs are
// already picked up.
func tripFixture(status string, picked ...primitive.ObjectID) *domain.RouteTrip {
	pickedSet := map[primitive.ObjectID]bool{}
	for _, id := range picked {
		pickedSet[id] = true
	}
	now := time.Now().UTC()
	stops := []domain.RouteStop{
		{DCSID: testDCS1, ConsignmentID: testCon1},
		{DCSID: testDCS2, ConsignmentID: testCon2},
	}
	for i := range stops {
		if pickedSet[stops[i].ConsignmentID] {
			stops[i].PickedUpAt = &now
		}
	}
	return &domain.RouteTrip{
		ID:              testTrip,
		UnionID:         testUnion,
		VanRiderPartyID: testRider,
		Status:          status,
		Stops:           stops,
	}
}

func assertAppError(t *testing.T, err *httpx.AppError, wantStatus int, wantCode string) {
	t.Helper()
	if wantStatus == 0 {
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("expected no error, got %v", err)
		}
		return
	}
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("expected %d %s, got nil", wantStatus, wantCode)
	}
	if err.Status != wantStatus {
		t.Fatalf("status = %d, want %d (err: %v)", err.Status, wantStatus, err)
	}
	if wantCode != "" && err.Code != wantCode {
		t.Fatalf("code = %q, want %q (err: %v)", err.Code, wantCode, err)
	}
}

func TestValidatePickup(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name          string
		trip          *domain.RouteTrip
		rider         primitive.ObjectID
		consignmentID primitive.ObjectID
		wantStatus    int
		wantCode      string
	}{
		{
			name: "wrong rider is forbidden",
			trip: tripFixture(domain.TripStatusPlanned), rider: testOtherRider, consignmentID: testCon1,
			wantStatus: http.StatusForbidden, wantCode: "FORBIDDEN",
		},
		{
			name: "pickup on delivered trip conflicts",
			trip: tripFixture(domain.TripStatusDelivered, testCon1, testCon2), rider: testRider, consignmentID: testCon1,
			wantStatus: http.StatusConflict, wantCode: "TRIP_ALREADY_DELIVERED",
		},
		{
			name: "consignment not planned on this trip is not found",
			trip: tripFixture(domain.TripStatusPlanned), rider: testRider, consignmentID: testUnknownCon,
			wantStatus: http.StatusNotFound, wantCode: "NOT_FOUND",
		},
		{
			name: "double pickup of the same stop conflicts",
			trip: tripFixture(domain.TripStatusInProgress, testCon1), rider: testRider, consignmentID: testCon1,
			wantStatus: http.StatusConflict, wantCode: "STOP_ALREADY_PICKED",
		},
		{
			name: "first pickup on planned trip is allowed",
			trip: tripFixture(domain.TripStatusPlanned), rider: testRider, consignmentID: testCon1,
		},
		{
			name: "second pickup on in-progress trip is allowed",
			trip: tripFixture(domain.TripStatusInProgress, testCon1), rider: testRider, consignmentID: testCon2,
		},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			assertAppError(t, validatePickup(tc.trip, tc.rider, tc.consignmentID), tc.wantStatus, tc.wantCode)
		})
	}
}

func TestValidateDeliver(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name       string
		trip       *domain.RouteTrip
		rider      primitive.ObjectID
		wantStatus int
		wantCode   string
	}{
		{
			name: "wrong rider is forbidden",
			trip: tripFixture(domain.TripStatusInProgress, testCon1, testCon2), rider: testOtherRider,
			wantStatus: http.StatusForbidden, wantCode: "FORBIDDEN",
		},
		{
			name: "delivering twice conflicts",
			trip: tripFixture(domain.TripStatusDelivered, testCon1, testCon2), rider: testRider,
			wantStatus: http.StatusConflict, wantCode: "TRIP_ALREADY_DELIVERED",
		},
		{
			name: "deliver before any pickup is unprocessable",
			trip: tripFixture(domain.TripStatusPlanned), rider: testRider,
			wantStatus: http.StatusUnprocessableEntity, wantCode: "STOPS_NOT_PICKED",
		},
		{
			name: "deliver with one unpicked stop is unprocessable",
			trip: tripFixture(domain.TripStatusInProgress, testCon1), rider: testRider,
			wantStatus: http.StatusUnprocessableEntity, wantCode: "STOPS_NOT_PICKED",
		},
		{
			name: "deliver with all stops picked is allowed",
			trip: tripFixture(domain.TripStatusInProgress, testCon1, testCon2), rider: testRider,
		},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			assertAppError(t, validateDeliver(tc.trip, tc.rider), tc.wantStatus, tc.wantCode)
		})
	}
}

func TestValidateColdChain(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name       string
		trip       *domain.RouteTrip
		rider      primitive.ObjectID
		wantStatus int
		wantCode   string
	}{
		{
			name: "wrong rider is forbidden",
			trip: tripFixture(domain.TripStatusInProgress), rider: testOtherRider,
			wantStatus: http.StatusForbidden, wantCode: "FORBIDDEN",
		},
		{
			name: "logging after delivery conflicts",
			trip: tripFixture(domain.TripStatusDelivered, testCon1, testCon2), rider: testRider,
			wantStatus: http.StatusConflict, wantCode: "TRIP_ALREADY_DELIVERED",
		},
		{
			name: "logging while planned is allowed",
			trip: tripFixture(domain.TripStatusPlanned), rider: testRider,
		},
		{
			name: "logging while in progress is allowed",
			trip: tripFixture(domain.TripStatusInProgress, testCon1), rider: testRider,
		},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			assertAppError(t, validateColdChain(tc.trip, tc.rider), tc.wantStatus, tc.wantCode)
		})
	}
}

func TestValidateStopConsignment(t *testing.T) {
	consignment := func(status string, dcsID primitive.ObjectID) *domain.DCSConsignment {
		return &domain.DCSConsignment{ID: testCon1, DCSID: dcsID, Status: status}
	}
	tests := []struct {
		name        string
		consignment *domain.DCSConsignment
		stopDCSID   primitive.ObjectID
		wantStatus  int
		wantCode    string
	}{
		{
			name:        "planning an OPEN consignment conflicts (pickup before dispatch)",
			consignment: consignment(domain.ConsignmentStatusOpen, testDCS1), stopDCSID: testDCS1,
			wantStatus: http.StatusConflict, wantCode: "CONSIGNMENT_NOT_DISPATCHED",
		},
		{
			name:        "planning an already picked-up consignment conflicts",
			consignment: consignment(domain.ConsignmentStatusPickedUp, testDCS1), stopDCSID: testDCS1,
			wantStatus: http.StatusConflict, wantCode: "CONSIGNMENT_NOT_DISPATCHED",
		},
		{
			name:        "consignment from another DCS is unprocessable",
			consignment: consignment(domain.ConsignmentStatusDispatch, testDCS1), stopDCSID: testDCS2,
			wantStatus: http.StatusUnprocessableEntity, wantCode: "CONSIGNMENT_DCS_MISMATCH",
		},
		{
			name:        "dispatched consignment at its own DCS is allowed",
			consignment: consignment(domain.ConsignmentStatusDispatch, testDCS1), stopDCSID: testDCS1,
		},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			assertAppError(t, validateStopConsignment(tc.consignment, tc.stopDCSID), tc.wantStatus, tc.wantCode)
		})
	}
}

func TestAggregatePours(t *testing.T) {
	p1 := primitive.NewObjectID()
	p2 := primitive.NewObjectID()
	rows := []pourRow{
		{ID: p1, QuantityLitres: 10, FatPct: 4.0, SNFPct: 8.0},
		{ID: p2, QuantityLitres: 30, FatPct: 6.0, SNFPct: 9.0},
	}
	ids, total, fat, snf := aggregatePours(rows)
	if len(ids) != 2 || ids[0] != p1 || ids[1] != p2 {
		t.Fatalf("ids = %v", ids)
	}
	if total != 40 {
		t.Fatalf("total = %v, want 40", total)
	}
	if fat != 5.5 { // (4*10 + 6*30) / 40
		t.Fatalf("weighted fat = %v, want 5.5", fat)
	}
	if snf != 8.75 { // (8*10 + 9*30) / 40
		t.Fatalf("weighted snf = %v, want 8.75", snf)
	}
}
```

```go
package collection

import (
	"net/http"

	"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson/primitive"

	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/auth"
	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/httpx"
)

// handler is the HTTP edge of the collection module: decode, call service,
// respond. No business logic, no MongoDB.
type handler struct {
	svc *service
}

// requestActor returns the authenticated actor (guaranteed present by the
// Authenticate middleware on every route of this module).
func requestActor(r *http.Request) auth.Actor {
	actor, _ := auth.ActorFrom(r.Context())
	return actor
}

// optionalQueryID parses an optional ObjectID query parameter: absent means
// the zero ObjectID (no filter), present-but-malformed is a 400.
func optionalQueryID(r *http.Request, param string) (primitive.ObjectID, error) {
	raw := r.URL.Query().Get(param)
	if raw == "" {
		return primitive.NilObjectID, nil
	}
	return httpx.ParseID(raw, param)
}

// createRateChart handles POST /collection/rate-charts.
func (h *handler) createRateChart(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	var req CreateRateChartRequest
	if err := httpx.DecodeJSON(r, &req); err != nil {
		httpx.Error(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	chart, err := h.svc.CreateRateChart(r.Context(), requestActor(r), req)
	if err != nil {
		httpx.Error(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	httpx.JSON(w, http.StatusCreated, chart)
}

// getActiveRateChart handles GET /collection/rate-charts/active?dcs_id=.
func (h *handler) getActiveRateChart(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	if r.URL.Query().Get("dcs_id") == "" {
		httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.BadRequest("VALIDATION", "dcs_id query parameter is required"))
		return
	}
	dcsID, err := httpx.ParseID(r.URL.Query().Get("dcs_id"), "dcs_id")
	if err != nil {
		httpx.Error(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	chart, err := h.svc.ResolveActiveChart(r.Context(), requestActor(r), dcsID)
	if err != nil {
		httpx.Error(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	httpx.JSON(w, http.StatusOK, chart)
}

// createReading handles POST /collection/readings.
func (h *handler) createReading(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	var req CreateReadingRequest
	if err := httpx.DecodeJSON(r, &req); err != nil {
		httpx.Error(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	reading, err := h.svc.CreateReading(r.Context(), requestActor(r), req)
	if err != nil {
		httpx.Error(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	httpx.JSON(w, http.StatusCreated, reading)
}

// listReadings handles GET /collection/readings?dcs_id=&date=.
func (h *handler) listReadings(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	page := httpx.ParsePage(r)
	dcsID, err := optionalQueryID(r, "dcs_id") // absent → service's "required" validation
	if err != nil {
		httpx.Error(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	readings, total, err := h.svc.ListReadings(r.Context(), requestActor(r),
		dcsID, r.URL.Query().Get("date"), page)
	if err != nil {
		httpx.Error(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	httpx.JSONMeta(w, http.StatusOK, readings, listMeta{Limit: page.Limit, Offset: page.Offset, Total: total})
}

// createPour handles POST /collection/pours.
func (h *handler) createPour(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	var req CreatePourRequest
	if err := httpx.DecodeJSON(r, &req); err != nil {
		httpx.Error(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	pour, replay, err := h.svc.CreatePour(r.Context(), requestActor(r), req)
	if err != nil {
		httpx.Error(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	if replay {
		httpx.JSON(w, http.StatusOK, PourResponse{Pour: *pour, IdempotentReplay: true})
		return
	}
	httpx.JSON(w, http.StatusCreated, PourResponse{Pour: *pour})
}

// batchSyncPours handles POST /collection/pours/batch-sync.
func (h *handler) batchSyncPours(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	var req BatchSyncRequest
	if err := httpx.DecodeJSON(r, &req); err != nil {
		httpx.Error(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	results, err := h.svc.BatchSyncPours(r.Context(), requestActor(r), req)
	if err != nil {
		httpx.Error(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	httpx.JSON(w, http.StatusOK, results)
}

// supersedePour handles POST /collection/pours/{id}/supersede.
func (h *handler) supersedePour(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	id, err := httpx.PathID(r, "id")
	if err != nil {
		httpx.Error(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	var req SupersedePourRequest
	if err := httpx.DecodeJSON(r, &req); err != nil {
		httpx.Error(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	pour, err := h.svc.SupersedePour(r.Context(), requestActor(r), id, req)
	if err != nil {
		httpx.Error(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	httpx.JSON(w, http.StatusCreated, PourResponse{Pour: *pour})
}

// listPours handles GET /collection/pours?dcs_id=&date=&shift=&farmer_party_id=.
func (h *handler) listPours(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	page := httpx.ParsePage(r)
	q := r.URL.Query()
	dcsID, err := optionalQueryID(r, "dcs_id")
	if err != nil {
		httpx.Error(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	farmerID, err := optionalQueryID(r, "farmer_party_id")
	if err != nil {
		httpx.Error(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	pours, total, err := h.svc.ListPours(r.Context(), requestActor(r), pourListFilter{
		DCSID:         dcsID,
		Date:          q.Get("date"),
		Shift:         q.Get("shift"),
		FarmerPartyID: farmerID,
	}, page)
	if err != nil {
		httpx.Error(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	httpx.JSONMeta(w, http.StatusOK, pours, listMeta{Limit: page.Limit, Offset: page.Offset, Total: total})
}

// generateInvoices handles POST /collection/invoices/generate.
func (h *handler) generateInvoices(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	var req GenerateInvoicesRequest
	if err := httpx.DecodeJSON(r, &req); err != nil {
		httpx.Error(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	resp, err := h.svc.GenerateInvoices(r.Context(), requestActor(r), req)
	if err != nil {
		httpx.Error(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	httpx.JSON(w, http.StatusOK, resp)
}

// listInvoices handles GET /collection/invoices?dcs_id=&date=&farmer_party_id=&status=.
func (h *handler) listInvoices(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	page := httpx.ParsePage(r)
	q := r.URL.Query()
	dcsID, err := optionalQueryID(r, "dcs_id")
	if err != nil {
		httpx.Error(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	farmerID, err := optionalQueryID(r, "farmer_party_id")
	if err != nil {
		httpx.Error(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	invoices, total, err := h.svc.ListInvoices(r.Context(), requestActor(r), invoiceListFilter{
		DCSID:         dcsID,
		Date:          q.Get("date"),
		FarmerPartyID: farmerID,
		Status:        q.Get("status"),
	}, page)
	if err != nil {
		httpx.Error(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	httpx.JSONMeta(w, http.StatusOK, invoices, listMeta{Limit: page.Limit, Offset: page.Offset, Total: total})
}

// getInvoice handles GET /collection/invoices/{id}.
func (h *handler) getInvoice(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	id, err := httpx.PathID(r, "id")
	if err != nil {
		httpx.Error(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	invoice, err := h.svc.GetInvoice(r.Context(), requestActor(r), id)
	if err != nil {
		httpx.Error(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	httpx.JSON(w, http.StatusOK, invoice)
}
```

```go
package cattle

import (
	"net/http"
	"testing"

	"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson/primitive"

	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/domain"
	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/auth"
)

func TestValidatePashuAadhaar(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name    string
		input   string
		wantErr bool
	}{
		{name: "valid 12 digits", input: "123456789012", wantErr: false},
		{name: "valid all zeros", input: "000000000000", wantErr: false},
		{name: "empty", input: "", wantErr: true},
		{name: "too short", input: "12345678901", wantErr: true},
		{name: "too long", input: "1234567890123", wantErr: true},
		{name: "contains letter", input: "12345678901A", wantErr: true},
		{name: "contains space", input: "123456 89012", wantErr: true},
		{name: "contains hyphen", input: "1234-5678901", wantErr: true},
		{name: "unicode digits rejected", input: "١٢٣٤٥٦٧٨٩٠١٢", wantErr: true},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			err := validatePashuAadhaar(tt.input)
			if (err != nil) != tt.wantErr {
				t.Fatalf("validatePashuAadhaar(%q) error = %v, wantErr %v", tt.input, err, tt.wantErr)
			}
			if err != nil {
				if err.Status != http.StatusBadRequest {
					t.Fatalf("validatePashuAadhaar(%q) status = %d, want %d", tt.input, err.Status, http.StatusBadRequest)
				}
				if err.Code != "INVALID_PASHU_AADHAAR" {
					t.Fatalf("validatePashuAadhaar(%q) code = %q, want INVALID_PASHU_AADHAAR", tt.input, err.Code)
				}
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestResolveAnimalOwner(t *testing.T) {
	farmerID := primitive.NewObjectID()
	sacheevID := primitive.NewObjectID()
	vetID := primitive.NewObjectID()
	otherFarmerID := primitive.NewObjectID()
	behalfFarmerID := primitive.NewObjectID()

	farmer := auth.Actor{PartyID: farmerID.Hex(), RoleCode: domain.RoleFarmer}
	sacheev := auth.Actor{PartyID: sacheevID.Hex(), RoleCode: domain.RoleSamitiSacheev}
	vet := auth.Actor{PartyID: vetID.Hex(), RoleCode: domain.RoleVeterinarian}

	tests := []struct {
		name           string
		actor          auth.Actor
		actorID        primitive.ObjectID
		requestedOwner *primitive.ObjectID
		wantOwner      primitive.ObjectID
		wantStatus     int    // 0 = no error expected
		wantCode       string // checked only when wantStatus != 0
	}{
		{
			name:           "farmer omitting owner registers self",
			actor:          farmer,
			actorID:        farmerID,
			requestedOwner: nil,
			wantOwner:      farmerID,
		},
		{
			name:           "farmer naming own party id registers self",
			actor:          farmer,
			actorID:        farmerID,
			requestedOwner: &farmerID,
			wantOwner:      farmerID,
		},
		{
			name:           "farmer naming another party is forbidden",
			actor:          farmer,
			actorID:        farmerID,
			requestedOwner: &otherFarmerID,
			wantStatus:     http.StatusForbidden,
			wantCode:       "FORBIDDEN",
		},
		{
			name:           "sacheev must name the owner",
			actor:          sacheev,
			actorID:        sacheevID,
			requestedOwner: nil,
			wantStatus:     http.StatusBadRequest,
			wantCode:       "OWNER_REQUIRED",
		},
		{
			name:           "sacheev naming an owner registers on their behalf",
			actor:          sacheev,
			actorID:        sacheevID,
			requestedOwner: &behalfFarmerID,
			wantOwner:      behalfFarmerID,
		},
		{
			name:           "veterinarian naming an owner registers on their behalf",
			actor:          vet,
			actorID:        vetID,
			requestedOwner: &behalfFarmerID,
			wantOwner:      behalfFarmerID,
		},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			owner, err := resolveAnimalOwner(tt.actor, tt.actorID, tt.requestedOwner)
			if tt.wantStatus == 0 {
				if err != nil {
					t.Fatalf("resolveAnimalOwner() unexpected error: %v", err)
				}
				if owner != tt.wantOwner {
					t.Fatalf("resolveAnimalOwner() owner = %q, want %q", owner.Hex(), tt.wantOwner.Hex())
				}
				return
			}
			if err == nil {
				t.Fatalf("resolveAnimalOwner() expected error, got owner %q", owner.Hex())
			}
			if err.Status != tt.wantStatus {
				t.Fatalf("resolveAnimalOwner() status = %d, want %d", err.Status, tt.wantStatus)
			}
			if err.Code != tt.wantCode {
				t.Fatalf("resolveAnimalOwner() code = %q, want %q", err.Code, tt.wantCode)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestCanViewAnimal(t *testing.T) {
	ownerID := primitive.NewObjectID()
	otherFarmerID := primitive.NewObjectID()
	vetID := primitive.NewObjectID()
	moID := primitive.NewObjectID()
	animal := &domain.Animal{ID: primitive.NewObjectID(), OwnerPartyID: ownerID}

	tests := []struct {
		name      string
		actor     auth.Actor
		actorID   primitive.ObjectID
		wantAllow bool
	}{
		{
			name:      "owner farmer may view",
			actor:     auth.Actor{PartyID: ownerID.Hex(), RoleCode: domain.RoleFarmer},
			actorID:   ownerID,
			wantAllow: true,
		},
		{
			name:      "non-owner farmer is forbidden",
			actor:     auth.Actor{PartyID: otherFarmerID.Hex(), RoleCode: domain.RoleFarmer},
			actorID:   otherFarmerID,
			wantAllow: false,
		},
		{
			name:      "veterinarian may view (v1 role check; consent TODO)",
			actor:     auth.Actor{PartyID: vetID.Hex(), RoleCode: domain.RoleVeterinarian},
			actorID:   vetID,
			wantAllow: true,
		},
		{
			name:      "mission official may view (v1 role check; consent TODO)",
			actor:     auth.Actor{PartyID: moID.Hex(), RoleCode: domain.RoleMissionOfficial},
			actorID:   moID,
			wantAllow: true,
		},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			err := canViewAnimal(tt.actor, tt.actorID, animal)
			if tt.wantAllow && err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("canViewAnimal() unexpected error: %v", err)
			}
			if !tt.wantAllow {
				if err == nil {
					t.Fatal("canViewAnimal() expected forbidden, got nil")
				}
				if err.Status != http.StatusForbidden {
					t.Fatalf("canViewAnimal() status = %d, want %d", err.Status, http.StatusForbidden)
				}
			}
		})
	}
}
```

Behaviour changes:
A. POST /kyc/aadhaar {aadhaar_number, consent, requested_tier} — requested_tier ∈ {FARMER, STANDARD, RIDER, HIGH}; creates KYCRecord with RequestedTier + status=PENDING. NO auto-verify, NO tier change (delete the mock auto-approve). Masking rules unchanged (last4 + vault ref only). If the party already has a PENDING record for the same requested_tier, return that one (200) instead of duplicating. Response includes status PENDING and a human message "awaiting verification".
B. POST /kyc/bank — unchanged mock penny-drop, attaches bank fields to the party's latest KYC record (any status) or creates a PENDING one carrying just bank evidence.
C. NEW GET /kyc/pending?limit&offset — RequireRoles(ORGANISING_MANAGER, DISTRICT_VERIFIER, PCDF_ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN); newest-first PENDING records enriched with party {id, phone, full_name, current kyc_tier}; meta carries total. Audit-record the access (action "kyc.pending_list").
D. NEW POST /kyc/{id}/approve — same roles; record must be PENDING (else 409 KYC_NOT_PENDING); service checks domain.CanApproveKYCTier(actor.RoleCode, record.RequestedTier) — even SUPER_ADMIN goes through the map (it allows everything) — else 403 KYC_TIER_NOT_APPROVABLE; set VERIFIED + reviewed_by/reviewed_by_role/reviewed_at/verified_at; upgrade party.kyc_tier ONLY upward (if !domain.KYCTierSatisfies(current, requested) → set requested); insert notifications doc TemplateKYCApproved {tier} to the party's phone; d.Audit.Record "kyc.approve" target the record; INFO log.
E. NEW POST /kyc/{id}/reject {reason} — same roles + same approvable-tier check; PENDING→REJECTED + rejection_reason + reviewed_by; TemplateKYCRejected notification; audit "kyc.reject"; WARN log.
F. Role-grant matrix: additionally allow ORGANISING_MANAGER to grant FARMER and CONSUMER within their org scope (RequireInScope). Role select logic unchanged — with auto-verify gone it now genuinely blocks un-approved users (403 KYC_TIER_INSUFFICIENT).
G. Migration: all party/assignment/kyc/consent/refresh-token lookups by ObjectID; refresh_tokens.party_id becomes ObjectID; otp_challenges keyed by phone (string, unchanged).
Tests: update existing; ADD table-driven tests for CanApproveKYCTier enforcement and the PENDING→VERIFIED party-tier upgrade (upward only).

```text
1	// Package orgscope answers the RBAC question "is this resource inside the
2	// caller's organisational scope?" in O(1) DB reads. Org units denormalise
3	// their ancestor chain into Path ([]ObjectID), so scope checking is a
4	// set-membership test — no recursive tree walks on the hot path.
5	package orgscope
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"errors"
10		"sync"
11		"time"
12	
13		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson"
14		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson/primitive"
15		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo"
16	
17		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/domain"
18		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/auth"
19		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/httpx"
20	)
21	
22	const collection = "org_units"
23	
24	type cachedOrg struct {
25		org domain.OrgUnit
26		at  time.Time
27	}
28	
29	// Resolver caches org units briefly (the tree changes rarely, reads are hot).
30	type Resolver struct {
31		coll *mongo.Collection
32		ttl  time.Duration
33	
34		mu    sync.RWMutex
35		cache map[string]cachedOrg // keyed by ObjectID hex
36	}
37	
38	// NewResolver binds the resolver to the database.
39	func NewResolver(db *mongo.Database) *Resolver {
40		return &Resolver{
41			coll:  db.Collection(collection),
42			ttl:   60 * time.Second,
43			cache: make(map[string]cachedOrg),
44		}
45	}
46	
47	// Get returns an org unit by ObjectID (cached).
48	func (r *Resolver) Get(ctx context.Context, id primitive.ObjectID) (*domain.OrgUnit, error) {
49		key := id.Hex()
50		r.mu.RLock()
51		c, ok := r.cache[key]
52		r.mu.RUnlock()
53		if ok && time.Since(c.at) < r.ttl {
54			org := c.org
55			return &org, nil
56		}
57	
58		var org domain.OrgUnit
59		err := r.coll.FindOne(ctx, bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: id}}).Decode(&org)
60		if errors.Is(err, mongo.ErrNoDocuments) {
61			return nil, httpx.NotFound("org unit " + key)
62		}
63		if err != nil {
64			return nil, httpx.Internal(err)
65		}
66	
67		r.mu.Lock()
68		r.cache[key] = cachedOrg{org: org, at: time.Now()}
69		r.mu.Unlock()
70		return &org, nil
71	}
72	
73	// GetByCode returns an org unit by its unique human-readable business code
74	// (e.g. "DCS-01842") — display/lookup use only, never for joins.
75	func (r *Resolver) GetByCode(ctx context.Context, code string) (*domain.OrgUnit, error) {
76		var org domain.OrgUnit
77		err := r.coll.FindOne(ctx, bson.D{{Key: "code", Value: code}}).Decode(&org)
78		if errors.Is(err, mongo.ErrNoDocuments) {
79			return nil, httpx.NotFound("org unit with code " + code)
80		}
81		if err != nil {
82			return nil, httpx.Internal(err)
83		}
84		return &org, nil
85	}
86	
87	// Invalidate drops a cached entry (call after updates).
88	func (r *Resolver) Invalidate(id primitive.ObjectID) {
89		r.mu.Lock()
90		delete(r.cache, id.Hex())
91		r.mu.Unlock()
92	}
93	
94	// InScope reports whether target sits at-or-below scope in the hierarchy:
95	// true when scope == target, or scope appears in target's ancestor Path.
96	func (r *Resolver) InScope(ctx context.Context, scopeOrgID, targetOrgID primitive.ObjectID) (bool, error) {
97		if scopeOrgID == targetOrgID {
98			return true, nil
99		}
100		target, err := r.Get(ctx, targetOrgID)
101		if err != nil {
102			return false, err
103		}
104		for _, ancestor := range target.Path {
105			if ancestor == scopeOrgID {
106				return true, nil
107			}
108		}
109		return false, nil
110	}
111	
112	// RequireInScope enforces the actor's org scope over a target org unit.
113	// SUPER_ADMIN and STATE_AUDITOR (read-wide roles rooted at the federation)
114	// pass automatically; everyone else needs ancestry. The actor carries its
115	// org unit as an ObjectID hex string (JWT claims are JSON); it is parsed here.
116	func (r *Resolver) RequireInScope(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, targetOrgID primitive.ObjectID) error {
117		if actor.RoleCode == domain.RoleSuperAdmin || actor.RoleCode == domain.RoleStateAuditor {
118			return nil
119		}
120		if actor.OrgUnitID == "" {
121			return httpx.Forbidden("role token with org scope required")
122		}
123		scopeID, err := primitive.ObjectIDFromHex(actor.OrgUnitID)
124		if err != nil {
125			return httpx.Forbidden("role token carries an invalid org scope")
126		}
127		ok, err := r.InScope(ctx, scopeID, targetOrgID)
128		if err != nil {
129			return err
130		}
131		if !ok {
132			return httpx.Forbidden("resource is outside your organisational scope")
133		}
134		return nil
135	}
136
```

```text
2	// the source of truth for milk traceability (blueprint §7). Every link in the

4	// event's hash, so history cannot be quietly rewritten (tamper-evidence,

24		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson/primitive"
25		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo"
26		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo/options"
27	)
28	
29	const collection = "provenance_events"
30	
31	// Ref is a directed edge to another entity in the trace graph
32	// (e.g. a consignment event referencing the pours it aggregates).
33	type Ref struct {
34		EntityType string `bson:"entity_type" json:"entity_type"`
35		EntityID   string `bson:"entity_id"   json:"entity_id"`
36		Relation   string `bson:"relation"    json:"relation"` // aggregates | supersedes | tested | yields | labels ...
37	}
38	
39	// ActorRef records who caused the event.
40	type ActorRef struct {
41		PartyID  string `bson:"party_id"  json:"party_id"`
42		RoleCode string `bson:"role_code" json:"role_code"`
43	}
44	
45	// Event is one immutable link in the ledger. `_id` is a generated ObjectID;
46	// EntityID and Refs carry the referenced documents' ObjectIDs as hex strings
47	// (the ledger is a generic event log spanning every entity type, and hex
48	// strings keep the hash material canonical and human-inspectable).
49	type Event struct {
50		ID         primitive.ObjectID `bson:"_id,omitempty" json:"id"`
51		Seq        int64          `bson:"seq"         json:"seq"`
52		Type       string         `bson:"type"        json:"type"`
53		EntityType string         `bson:"entity_type" json:"entity_type"`
54		EntityID   string         `bson:"entity_id"   json:"entity_id"`
55		Refs       []Ref          `bson:"refs,omitempty"    json:"refs,omitempty"`
56		Actor      ActorRef       `bson:"actor"       json:"actor"`
57		OrgUnitID  string         `bson:"org_unit_id,omitempty" json:"org_unit_id,omitempty"`
58		Payload    map[string]any `bson:"payload,omitempty"     json:"payload,omitempty"`
59		TS         time.Time      `bson:"ts"          json:"ts"`
60		PrevHash   string         `bson:"prev_hash"   json:"prev_hash"`
61		Hash       string         `bson:"hash"        json:"hash"`
62	}
63	
64	// AppendInput describes a new event to chain.
65	type AppendInput struct {
66		Type       string
67		EntityType string
68		EntityID   string
69		Refs       []Ref
70		Actor      ActorRef
71		OrgUnitID  string
72		Payload    map[string]any
73	}
74	
75	// Ledger appends to and reads the hash chain.
76	type Ledger struct {
77		coll *mongo.Collection
78	
79		// appendMu serialises the head-read+insert of Append within this process:
80		// every ledger write system-wide shares one global seq, so without local
81		// serialisation concurrent handlers (e.g. a morning pour rush plus a
82		// GenerateInvoices loop) burn duplicate-key retries against each other.
83		// The unique seq index remains the atomic backstop across processes.
84		appendMu sync.Mutex
85	}
86	
87	// NewLedger binds the ledger to the database.
88	func NewLedger(db *mongo.Database) *Ledger {
89		return &Ledger{coll: db.Collection(collection)}
90	}
91	
92	// genesisHash anchors the chain before the first event.
93	const genesisHash = "GENESIS"
94	
95	// Append chains a new event. Concurrency-safe without transactions: it reads
96	// the current head, computes seq+hash optimistically, and relies on the
97	// unique index on `seq` — a duplicate-key collision means another writer won
98	// the slot, so we re-read and retry.
99	func (l *Ledger) Append(ctx context.Context, in AppendInput) (*Event, error) {
100		// Serialise appends within this process (see appendMu): local writers no
101		// longer race each other for the seq slot, so under single-instance
102		// deployment the retry loop only ever fires against external writers.
103		l.appendMu.Lock()
104		defer l.appendMu.Unlock()
105	
106		const maxRetries = 12
107		for attempt := 0; attempt < maxRetries; attempt++ {
108			seq, prevHash, err := l.head(ctx)
109			if err != nil {
110				return nil, err
111			}
112			ev := &Event{
113				ID:         primitive.NewObjectID(),
114				Seq:        seq + 1,
115				Type:       in.Type,
116				EntityType: in.EntityType,
117				EntityID:   in.EntityID,
118				Refs:       in.Refs,
119				Actor:      in.Actor,
120				OrgUnitID:  in.OrgUnitID,
121				Payload:    in.Payload,
122				// Millisecond precision: BSON datetimes store ms, so the persisted
123				// TS must equal the hashed TS or re-verification would break.
124				TS:       time.Now().UTC().Truncate(time.Millisecond),
125				PrevHash: prevHash,
126			}
127			ev.Hash = computeHash(ev)
128	
129			if _, err := l.coll.InsertOne(ctx, ev); err != nil {
130				if mongo.IsDuplicateKeyError(err) {
131					continue // lost the seq race — retry against the new head
132				}
133				return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance append: %w", err)
134			}
135			return ev, nil
136		}
137		return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance append: gave up after %d seq collisions", 12)
138	}
139	
140	// head returns the latest (seq, hash), or (0, GENESIS) for an empty chain.
141	func (l *Ledger) head(ctx context.Context) (int64, string, error) {
142		var last Event
143		err := l.coll.FindOne(ctx, bson.D{},
144			options.FindOne().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: -1}}),
145		).Decode(&last)
146		if errors.Is(err, mongo.ErrNoDocuments) {
147			return 0, genesisHash, nil
148		}
149		if err != nil {
150			return 0, "", fmt.Errorf("provenance head: %w", err)
151		}
152		return last.Seq, last.Hash, nil
153	}
154	
155	// computeHash covers everything that matters: position, linkage, content.
156	// Payload is canonicalised via encoding/json (map keys are sorted) and the
157	// timestamp to millisecond precision (BSON datetime resolution), so the
158	// digest is deterministic across a MongoDB round trip.
159	func computeHash(ev *Event) string {
160		payloadJSON, _ := json.Marshal(ev.Payload)
161		refParts := make([]string, 0, len(ev.Refs))
162		for _, r := range ev.Refs {
163			refParts = append(refParts, r.EntityType+":"+r.EntityID+":"+r.Relation)
164		}
165		material := strings.Join([]string{
166			ev.PrevHash,
167			strconv.FormatInt(ev.Seq, 10),
168			ev.Type,
169			ev.EntityType,
170			ev.EntityID,
171			strings.Join(refParts, ","),
172			ev.Actor.PartyID,
173			ev.Actor.RoleCode,
174			ev.OrgUnitID,
175			string(payloadJSON),
176			ev.TS.UTC().Truncate(time.Millisecond).Format(time.RFC3339Nano),
177		}, "|")
178		sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(material))
179		return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
180	}
181	
182	// EventsForEntity returns an entity's own timeline in chain order.
183	func (l *Ledger) EventsForEntity(ctx context.Context, entityType, entityID string) ([]Event, error) {
184		cur, err := l.coll.Find(ctx,
185			bson.D{{Key: "entity_type", Value: entityType}, {Key: "entity_id", Value: entityID}},
186			options.Find().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: 1}}),
187		)
188		if err != nil {
189			return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance events for %s/%s: %w", entityType, entityID, err)
190		}
191		var out []Event
192		if err := cur.All(ctx, &out); err != nil {
193			return nil, err
194		}
195		return out, nil
196	}
197	
198	// Trace walks the provenance graph UPSTREAM from an entity: its events, plus
199	// (recursively) the events of everything those events reference. This is how
200	// a consumer QR resolves back to the contributing samiti set, and how a failed
201	// aflatoxin test walks back to source DCSes (blueprint §8.3).
202	func (l *Ledger) Trace(ctx context.Context, entityType, entityID string, maxDepth int) ([]Event, error) {
203		return l.TraceStopAt(ctx, entityType, entityID, maxDepth, nil)
204	}
205	
206	// TraceStopAt is Trace with a stop set: entity types in stopExpand are still
207	// fetched (their events appear in the result) but their refs are never
208	// followed. The consumer QR scan stops at the consignment/pooling boundary so
209	// hundreds of per-pour nodes (and cross-route trip fan-out) are never walked.
210	//
211	// Each BFS level is batched into a bounded number of $or queries instead of
212	// one Find per node, so a walk costs O(depth) round trips, not O(nodes).
213	func (l *Ledger) TraceStopAt(ctx context.Context, entityType, entityID string, maxDepth int, stopExpand map[string]bool) ([]Event, error) {
214		if maxDepth <= 0 {
215			maxDepth = 10
216		}
217		const hardEventCap = 2000
218	
219		type node struct{ etype, eid string }
220		visited := map[node]bool{}
221		frontier := []node{{entityType, entityID}}
222		var all []Event
223	
224		for depth := 0; depth < maxDepth && len(frontier) > 0; depth++ {
225			// Deduplicate this level against everything already visited.
226			level := make([]node, 0, len(frontier))
227			for _, n := range frontier {
228				if visited[n] {
229					continue
230				}
231				visited[n] = true
232				level = append(level, n)
233			}
234			if len(level) == 0 {
235				break
236			}
237	
238			var next []node
239			// One indexed query per chunk of the level (not per node).
240			const orChunk = 200
241			for start := 0; start < len(level); start += orChunk {
242				end := min(start+orChunk, len(level))
243				clauses := make(bson.A, 0, end-start)
244				for _, n := range level[start:end] {
245					clauses = append(clauses, bson.D{
246						{Key: "entity_type", Value: n.etype},
247						{Key: "entity_id", Value: n.eid},
248					})
249				}
250				cur, err := l.coll.Find(ctx,
251					bson.D{{Key: "$or", Value: clauses}},
252					options.Find().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: 1}}).SetLimit(hardEventCap),
253				)
254				if err != nil {
255					return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance trace level: %w", err)
256				}
257				var evs []Event
258				if err := cur.All(ctx, &evs); err != nil {
259					return nil, err
260				}
261				for _, ev := range evs {
262					all = append(all, ev)
263					if len(all) >= hardEventCap {
264						return all, nil
265					}
266					if stopExpand != nil && stopExpand[ev.EntityType] {
267						continue // include the node's events, never follow its refs
268					}
269					for _, ref := range ev.Refs {
270						nn := node{ref.EntityType, ref.EntityID}
271						if !visited[nn] {
272							next = append(next, nn)
273						}
274					}
275				}
276			}
277			frontier = next
278		}
279		return all, nil
280	}
281	
282	// DownstreamRefs finds events that reference the given entity — used to walk
283	// FORWARD (e.g. "which batches consumed this blocked BMC lot?"). The limit is
284	// pushed into the query: only the LAST limit referencing events are fetched
285	// (ascending chain order preserved). limit <= 0 falls back to 2000.
286	func (l *Ledger) DownstreamRefs(ctx context.Context, entityID string, limit int64) ([]Event, error) {
287		if limit <= 0 {
288			limit = 2000
289		}
290		cur, err := l.coll.Find(ctx,
291			bson.D{{Key: "refs.entity_id", Value: entityID}},
292			options.Find().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: -1}}).SetLimit(limit),
293		)
294		if err != nil {
295			return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance downstream of %s: %w", entityID, err)
296		}
297		var out []Event
298		if err := cur.All(ctx, &out); err != nil {
299			return nil, err
300		}
301		// Restore ascending chain order.
302		for i, j := 0, len(out)-1; i < j; i, j = i+1, j-1 {
303			out[i], out[j] = out[j], out[i]
304		}
305		return out, nil
306	}
307	
308	// EventsForEntityPage returns one page of an entity's own timeline in chain
309	// order, with skip/limit pushed into the query.
310	func (l *Ledger) EventsForEntityPage(ctx context.Context, entityType, entityID string, offset, limit int64) ([]Event, error) {
311		cur, err := l.coll.Find(ctx,
312			bson.D{{Key: "entity_type", Value: entityType}, {Key: "entity_id", Value: entityID}},
313			options.Find().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: 1}}).SetSkip(offset).SetLimit(limit),
314		)
315		if err != nil {
316			return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance events page for %s/%s: %w", entityType, entityID, err)
317		}
318		var out []Event
319		if err := cur.All(ctx, &out); err != nil {
320			return nil, err
321		}
322		return out, nil
323	}
324	
325	// CountEventsForEntity returns the total number of events on an entity's
326	// timeline (pagination meta companion of EventsForEntityPage).
327	func (l *Ledger) CountEventsForEntity(ctx context.Context, entityType, entityID string) (int64, error) {
328		n, err := l.coll.CountDocuments(ctx,
329			bson.D{{Key: "entity_type", Value: entityType}, {Key: "entity_id", Value: entityID}})
330		if err != nil {
331			return 0, fmt.Errorf("provenance count for %s/%s: %w", entityType, entityID, err)
332		}
333		return n, nil
334	}
335	
336	// VerifyChain re-derives every hash in [fromSeq, toSeq] and checks linkage.
337	// Returns (true, 0) when intact, or (false, seq) of the first broken link.
338	func (l *Ledger) VerifyChain(ctx context.Context, fromSeq, toSeq int64) (bool, int64, error) {
339		filter := bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$gte", Value: fromSeq}, {Key: "$lte", Value: toSeq}}}}
340		cur, err := l.coll.Find(ctx, filter, options.Find().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: 1}}))
341		if err != nil {
342			return false, 0, fmt.Errorf("provenance verify: %w", err)
343		}
344		defer cur.Close(ctx)
345	
346		prevHash := ""
347		prevSeq := int64(0)
348		first := true
349		for cur.Next(ctx) {
350			var ev Event
351			if err := cur.Decode(&ev); err != nil {
352				return false, 0, err
353			}
354			if computeHash(&ev) != ev.Hash {
355				return false, ev.Seq, nil // content tampered
356			}
357			if !first {
358				if ev.Seq != prevSeq+1 || ev.PrevHash != prevHash {
359					return false, ev.Seq, nil // linkage broken
360				}
361			}
362			prevHash, prevSeq, first = ev.Hash, ev.Seq, false
363		}
364		return true, 0, cur.Err()
365	}
366	
367	// LatestSeq returns the current chain head sequence (0 = empty).
368	func (l *Ledger) LatestSeq(ctx context.Context) (int64, error) {
369		seq, _, err := l.head(ctx)
370		return seq, err
371	}
```

```text
10	// ParseID converts an ObjectID hex string (from JSON bodies, query params or
11	// JWT claims) into a primitive.ObjectID, or returns a 400 with the offending
12	// field name.
13	func ParseID(hex, field string) (primitive.ObjectID, error) {
14		id, err := primitive.ObjectIDFromHex(hex)
15		if err != nil {
16			return primitive.NilObjectID, BadRequest("INVALID_ID", field+" must be a valid object id")
17		}
18		return id, nil
19	}
20	
21	// PathID extracts a chi URL parameter and parses it as an ObjectID.
22	func PathID(r *http.Request, param string) (primitive.ObjectID, error) {
23		return ParseID(chi.URLParam(r, param), param)
24	}
```

```text
1	// Package orgscope answers the RBAC question "is this resource inside the
2	// caller's organisational scope?" in O(1) DB reads. Org units denormalise
3	// their ancestor chain into Path ([]ObjectID), so scope checking is a
4	// set-membership test — no recursive tree walks on the hot path.
5	package orgscope
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"errors"
10		"sync"
11		"time"
12	
13		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson"
14		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson/primitive"
15		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo"

17		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/domain"

20	)
21	
22	const collection = "org_units"
23	
24	type cachedOrg struct {
25		org domain.OrgUnit
26		at  time.Time
27	}
28	
29	// Resolver caches org units briefly (the tree changes rarely, reads are hot).
30	type Resolver struct {
31		coll *mongo.Collection
32		ttl  time.Duration
33	
34		mu    sync.RWMutex
35		cache map[string]cachedOrg // keyed by ObjectID hex
36	}
37	
38	// NewResolver binds the resolver to the database.
39	func NewResolver(db *mongo.Database) *Resolver {
40		return &Resolver{
41			coll:  db.Collection(collection),
42			ttl:   60 * time.Second,
43			cache: make(map[string]cachedOrg),
44		}
45	}
46	
47	// Get returns an org unit by ObjectID (cached).
48	func (r *Resolver) Get(ctx context.Context, id primitive.ObjectID) (*domain.OrgUnit, error) {
49		key := id.Hex()
50		r.mu.RLock()
51		c, ok := r.cache[key]
52		r.mu.RUnlock()
53		if ok && time.Since(c.at) < r.ttl {
54			org := c.org
55			return &org, nil
56		}
57	
58		var org domain.OrgUnit
59		err := r.coll.FindOne(ctx, bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: id}}).Decode(&org)
60		if errors.Is(err, mongo.ErrNoDocuments) {
61			return nil, httpx.NotFound("org unit " + key)
62		}
63		if err != nil {
64			return nil, httpx.Internal(err)
65		}
66	
67		r.mu.Lock()
68		r.cache[key] = cachedOrg{org: org, at: time.Now()}
69		r.mu.Unlock()
70		return &org, nil
71	}
72	
73	// GetByCode returns an org unit by its unique human-readable business code
74	// (e.g. "DCS-01842") — display/lookup use only, never for joins.
75	func (r *Resolver) GetByCode(ctx context.Context, code string) (*domain.OrgUnit, error) {
76		var org domain.OrgUnit
77		err := r.coll.FindOne(ctx, bson.D{{Key: "code", Value: code}}).Decode(&org)
78		if errors.Is(err, mongo.ErrNoDocuments) {
79			return nil, httpx.NotFound("org unit with code " + code)
80		}
81		if err != nil {
82			return nil, httpx.Internal(err)
83		}
84		return &org, nil
85	}
86	
87	// Invalidate drops a cached entry (call after updates).
88	func (r *Resolver) Invalidate(id primitive.ObjectID) {
89		r.mu.Lock()
90		delete(r.cache, id.Hex())
91		r.mu.Unlock()
92	}
93	
94	// InScope reports whether target sits at-or-below scope in the hierarchy:
95	// true when scope == target, or scope appears in target's ancestor Path.
96	func (r *Resolver) InScope(ctx context.Context, scopeOrgID, targetOrgID primitive.ObjectID) (bool, error) {
97		if scopeOrgID == targetOrgID {
98			return true, nil
99		}
100		target, err := r.Get(ctx, targetOrgID)
101		if err != nil {
102			return false, err
103		}
104		for _, ancestor := range target.Path {
105			if ancestor == scopeOrgID {
106				return true, nil
107			}
108		}
109		return false, nil
110	}
111	
112	// RequireInScope enforces the actor's org scope over a target org unit.
113	// SUPER_ADMIN and STATE_AUDITOR (read-wide roles rooted at the federation)
114	// pass automatically; everyone else needs ancestry. The actor carries its
115	// org unit as an ObjectID hex string (JWT claims are JSON); it is parsed here.
116	func (r *Resolver) RequireInScope(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, targetOrgID primitive.ObjectID) error {
117		if actor.RoleCode == domain.RoleSuperAdmin || actor.RoleCode == domain.RoleStateAuditor {
118			return nil
119		}
120		if actor.OrgUnitID == "" {
121			return httpx.Forbidden("role token with org scope required")
122		}
123		scopeID, err := primitive.ObjectIDFromHex(actor.OrgUnitID)
124		if err != nil {
125			return httpx.Forbidden("role token carries an invalid org scope")
126		}
127		ok, err := r.InScope(ctx, scopeID, targetOrgID)
128		if err != nil {
129			return err
130		}
131		if !ok {
132			return httpx.Forbidden("resource is outside your organisational scope")
133		}
134		return nil
135	}
136
```

```text
1	// Package provenance implements the append-only, hash-chained event ledger —
2	// the source of truth for milk traceability (blueprint §7). Every link in the
3	// pour→QR chain is an immutable Event whose SHA-256 hash covers the previous
4	// event's hash, so history cannot be quietly rewritten (tamper-evidence,
5	// FSSAI recall-grade audit).
6	//
7	// Corrections are NEW events referencing the superseded entity — nothing is
8	// ever updated or deleted in this collection.
9	package provenance
10	
11	import (
12		"context"
13		"crypto/sha256"
14		"encoding/hex"

31	// Ref is a directed edge to another entity in the trace graph
32	// (e.g. a consignment event referencing the pours it aggregates).
33	type Ref struct {
34		EntityType string `bson:"entity_type" json:"entity_type"`
35		EntityID   string `bson:"entity_id"   json:"entity_id"`
36		Relation   string `bson:"relation"    json:"relation"` // aggregates | supersedes | tested | yields | labels ...
37	}

42		RoleCode string `bson:"role_code" json:"role_code"`
43	}

45	// Event is one immutable link in the ledger. `_id` is a generated ObjectID;
46	// EntityID and Refs carry the referenced documents' ObjectIDs as hex strings
47	// (the ledger is a generic event log spanning every entity type, and hex
48	// strings keep the hash material canonical and human-inspectable).
49	type Event struct {
50		ID         primitive.ObjectID `bson:"_id,omitempty" json:"id"`
51		Seq        int64          `bson:"seq"         json:"seq"`
52		Type       string         `bson:"type"        json:"type"`
53		EntityType string         `bson:"entity_type" json:"entity_type"`
54		EntityID   string         `bson:"entity_id"   json:"entity_id"`
55		Refs       []Ref          `bson:"refs,omitempty"    json:"refs,omitempty"`
56		Actor      ActorRef       `bson:"actor"       json:"actor"`
57		OrgUnitID  string         `bson:"org_unit_id,omitempty" json:"org_unit_id,omitempty"`
58		Payload    map[string]any `bson:"payload,omitempty"     json:"payload,omitempty"`
59		TS         time.Time      `bson:"ts"          json:"ts"`
60		PrevHash   string         `bson:"prev_hash"   json:"prev_hash"`
61		Hash       string         `bson:"hash"        json:"hash"`
62	}
63	
64	// AppendInput describes a new event to chain.
65	type AppendInput struct {
66		Type       string
67		EntityType string
68		EntityID   string
69		Refs       []Ref
70		Actor      ActorRef
71		OrgUnitID  string
72		Payload    map[string]any
73	}
74	
75	// Ledger appends to and reads the hash chain.
76	type Ledger struct {
77		coll *mongo.Collection
78	
79		// appendMu serialises the head-read+insert of Append within this process:
80		// every ledger write system-wide shares one global seq, so without local
81		// serialisation concurrent handlers (e.g. a morning pour rush plus a
82		// GenerateInvoices loop) burn duplicate-key retries against each other.
83		// The unique seq index remains the atomic backstop across processes.
84		appendMu sync.Mutex
85	}
86	
87	// NewLedger binds the ledger to the database.
88	func NewLedger(db *mongo.Database) *Ledger {
89		return &Ledger{coll: db.Collection(collection)}
90	}
91	
92	// genesisHash anchors the chain before the first event.
93	const genesisHash = "GENESIS"
94	
95	// Append chains a new event. Concurrency-safe without transactions: it reads
96	// the current head, computes seq+hash optimistically, and relies on the
97	// unique index on `seq` — a duplicate-key collision means another writer won
98	// the slot, so we re-read and retry.
99	func (l *Ledger) Append(ctx context.Context, in AppendInput) (*Event, error) {
100		// Serialise appends within this process (see appendMu): local writers no
101		// longer race each other for the seq slot, so under single-instance
102		// deployment the retry loop only ever fires against external writers.
103		l.appendMu.Lock()
104		defer l.appendMu.Unlock()
105	
106		const maxRetries = 12
107		for attempt := 0; attempt < maxRetries; attempt++ {
108			seq, prevHash, err := l.head(ctx)
109			if err != nil {
110				return nil, err
111			}
112			ev := &Event{
113				ID:         primitive.NewObjectID(),
114				Seq:        seq + 1,
115				Type:       in.Type,
116				EntityType: in.EntityType,
117				EntityID:   in.EntityID,
118				Refs:       in.Refs,
119				Actor:      in.Actor,
120				OrgUnitID:  in.OrgUnitID,
121				Payload:    in.Payload,
122				// Millisecond precision: BSON datetimes store ms, so the persisted
123				// TS must equal the hashed TS or re-verification would break.
124				TS:       time.Now().UTC().Truncate(time.Millisecond),
125				PrevHash: prevHash,
126			}
127			ev.Hash = computeHash(ev)
128	
129			if _, err := l.coll.InsertOne(ctx, ev); err != nil {
130				if mongo.IsDuplicateKeyError(err) {
131					continue // lost the seq race — retry against the new head
132				}
133				return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance append: %w", err)
134			}
135			return ev, nil
136		}
137		return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance append: gave up after %d seq collisions", 12)
138	}
139	
140	// head returns the latest (seq, hash), or (0, GENESIS) for an empty chain.
141	func (l *Ledger) head(ctx context.Context) (int64, string, error) {
142		var last Event
143		err := l.coll.FindOne(ctx, bson.D{},
144			options.FindOne().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: -1}}),
145		).Decode(&last)
146		if errors.Is(err, mongo.ErrNoDocuments) {
147			return 0, genesisHash, nil
148		}
149		if err != nil {
150			return 0, "", fmt.Errorf("provenance head: %w", err)
151		}
152		return last.Seq, last.Hash, nil
153	}
154	
155	// computeHash covers everything that matters: position, linkage, content.
156	// Payload is canonicalised via encoding/json (map keys are sorted) and the
157	// timestamp to millisecond precision (BSON datetime resolution), so the
158	// digest is deterministic across a MongoDB round trip.
159	func computeHash(ev *Event) string {
160		payloadJSON, _ := json.Marshal(ev.Payload)
161		refParts := make([]string, 0, len(ev.Refs))
162		for _, r := range ev.Refs {
163			refParts = append(refParts, r.EntityType+":"+r.EntityID+":"+r.Relation)
164		}
165		material := strings.Join([]string{
166			ev.PrevHash,
167			strconv.FormatInt(ev.Seq, 10),
168			ev.Type,
169			ev.EntityType,
170			ev.EntityID,
171			strings.Join(refParts, ","),
172			ev.Actor.PartyID,
173			ev.Actor.RoleCode,
174			ev.OrgUnitID,
175			string(payloadJSON),
176			ev.TS.UTC().Truncate(time.Millisecond).Format(time.RFC3339Nano),
177		}, "|")
178		sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(material))
179		return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
180	}
181	
182	// EventsForEntity returns an entity's own timeline in chain order.
183	func (l *Ledger) EventsForEntity(ctx context.Context, entityType, entityID string) ([]Event, error) {
184		cur, err := l.coll.Find(ctx,
185			bson.D{{Key: "entity_type", Value: entityType}, {Key: "entity_id", Value: entityID}},
186			options.Find().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: 1}}),
187		)
188		if err != nil {
189			return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance events for %s/%s: %w", entityType, entityID, err)
190		}
191		var out []Event
192		if err := cur.All(ctx, &out); err != nil {
193			return nil, err
194		}
195		return out, nil
196	}
197	
198	// Trace walks the provenance graph UPSTREAM from an entity: its events, plus
199	// (recursively) the events of everything those events reference. This is how
200	// a consumer QR resolves back to the contributing samiti set, and how a failed
201	// aflatoxin test walks back to source DCSes (blueprint §8.3).
202	func (l *Ledger) Trace(ctx context.Context, entityType, entityID string, maxDepth int) ([]Event, error) {
203		return l.TraceStopAt(ctx, entityType, entityID, maxDepth, nil)
204	}
205	
206	// TraceStopAt is Trace with a stop set: entity types in stopExpand are still
207	// fetched (their events appear in the result) but their refs are never
208	// followed. The consumer QR scan stops at the consignment/pooling boundary so
209	// hundreds of per-pour nodes (and cross-route trip fan-out) are never walked.
210	//
211	// Each BFS level is batched into a bounded number of $or queries instead of
212	// one Find per node, so a walk costs O(depth) round trips, not O(nodes).
213	func (l *Ledger) TraceStopAt(ctx context.Context, entityType, entityID string, maxDepth int, stopExpand map[string]bool) ([]Event, error) {
214		if maxDepth <= 0 {
215			maxDepth = 10
216		}
217		const hardEventCap = 2000
218	
219		type node struct{ etype, eid string }
220		visited := map[node]bool{}
221		frontier := []node{{entityType, entityID}}
222		var all []Event
223	
224		for depth := 0; depth < maxDepth && len(frontier) > 0; depth++ {
225			// Deduplicate this level against everything already visited.
226			level := make([]node, 0, len(frontier))
227			for _, n := range frontier {
228				if visited[n] {
229					continue
230				}
231				visited[n] = true
232				level = append(level, n)
233			}
234			if len(level) == 0 {
235				break
236			}
237	
238			var next []node
239			// One indexed query per chunk of the level (not per node).
240			const orChunk = 200
241			for start := 0; start < len(level); start += orChunk {
242				end := min(start+orChunk, len(level))
243				clauses := make(bson.A, 0, end-start)
244				for _, n := range level[start:end] {
245					clauses = append(clauses, bson.D{
246						{Key: "entity_type", Value: n.etype},
247						{Key: "entity_id", Value: n.eid},
248					})
249				}
250				cur, err := l.coll.Find(ctx,
251					bson.D{{Key: "$or", Value: clauses}},
252					options.Find().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: 1}}).SetLimit(hardEventCap),
253				)
254				if err != nil {
255					return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance trace level: %w", err)
256				}
257				var evs []Event
258				if err := cur.All(ctx, &evs); err != nil {
259					return nil, err
260				}
261				for _, ev := range evs {
262					all = append(all, ev)
263					if len(all) >= hardEventCap {
264						return all, nil
265					}
266					if stopExpand != nil && stopExpand[ev.EntityType] {
267						continue // include the node's events, never follow its refs
268					}
269					for _, ref := range ev.Refs {
270						nn := node{ref.EntityType, ref.EntityID}
271						if !visited[nn] {
272							next = append(next, nn)
273						}
274					}
275				}
276			}
277			frontier = next
278		}
279		return all, nil
280	}
281	
282	// DownstreamRefs finds events that reference the given entity — used to walk
283	// FORWARD (e.g. "which batches consumed this blocked BMC lot?"). The limit is
284	// pushed into the query: only the LAST limit referencing events are fetched
285	// (ascending chain order preserved). limit <= 0 falls back to 2000.
286	func (l *Ledger) DownstreamRefs(ctx context.Context, entityID string, limit int64) ([]Event, error) {
287		if limit <= 0 {
288			limit = 2000
289		}
290		cur, err := l.coll.Find(ctx,
291			bson.D{{Key: "refs.entity_id", Value: entityID}},
292			options.Find().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: -1}}).SetLimit(limit),
293		)
294		if err != nil {
295			return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance downstream of %s: %w", entityID, err)
296		}
297		var out []Event
298		if err := cur.All(ctx, &out); err != nil {
299			return nil, err
300		}
301		// Restore ascending chain order.
302		for i, j := 0, len(out)-1; i < j; i, j = i+1, j-1 {
303			out[i], out[j] = out[j], out[i]
304		}
305		return out, nil
306	}
307	
308	// EventsForEntityPage returns one page of an entity's own timeline in chain
309	// order, with skip/limit pushed into the query.
310	func (l *Ledger) EventsForEntityPage(ctx context.Context, entityType, entityID string, offset, limit int64) ([]Event, error) {
311		cur, err := l.coll.Find(ctx,
312			bson.D{{Key: "entity_type", Value: entityType}, {Key: "entity_id", Value: entityID}},
313			options.Find().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: 1}}).SetSkip(offset).SetLimit(limit),
314		)
315		if err != nil {
316			return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance events page for %s/%s: %w", entityType, entityID, err)
317		}
318		var out []Event
319		if err := cur.All(ctx, &out); err != nil {
320			return nil, err
321		}
322		return out, nil
323	}
324	
325	// CountEventsForEntity returns the total number of events on an entity's
326	// timeline (pagination meta companion of EventsForEntityPage).
327	func (l *Ledger) CountEventsForEntity(ctx context.Context, entityType, entityID string) (int64, error) {
328		n, err := l.coll.CountDocuments(ctx,
329			bson.D{{Key: "entity_type", Value: entityType}, {Key: "entity_id", Value: entityID}})
330		if err != nil {
331			return 0, fmt.Errorf("provenance count for %s/%s: %w", entityType, entityID, err)
332		}
333		return n, nil
334	}
335	
336	// VerifyChain re-derives every hash in [fromSeq, toSeq] and checks linkage.
337	// Returns (true, 0) when intact, or (false, seq) of the first broken link.
338	func (l *Ledger) VerifyChain(ctx context.Context, fromSeq, toSeq int64) (bool, int64, error) {
339		filter := bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$gte", Value: fromSeq}, {Key: "$lte", Value: toSeq}}}}
340		cur, err := l.coll.Find(ctx, filter, options.Find().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: 1}}))
341		if err != nil {
342			return false, 0, fmt.Errorf("provenance verify: %w", err)
343		}
344		defer cur.Close(ctx)
345	
346		prevHash := ""
347		prevSeq := int64(0)
348		first := true
349		for cur.Next(ctx) {
350			var ev Event
351			if err := cur.Decode(&ev); err != nil {
352				return false, 0, err
353			}
354			if computeHash(&ev) != ev.Hash {
355				return false, ev.Seq, nil // content tampered
356			}
357			if !first {
358				if ev.Seq != prevSeq+1 || ev.PrevHash != prevHash {
359					return false, ev.Seq, nil // linkage broken
360				}
361			}
362			prevHash, prevSeq, first = ev.Hash, ev.Seq, false
363		}
364		return true, 0, cur.Err()
365	}
366	
367	// LatestSeq returns the current chain head sequence (0 = empty).
368	func (l *Ledger) LatestSeq(ctx context.Context) (int64, error) {
369		seq, _, err := l.head(ctx)
370		return seq, err
371	}
```

```text
9		"errors"

29	// Resolver caches org units briefly (the tree changes rarely, reads are hot).
30	type Resolver struct {

32		ttl  time.Duration

34		mu    sync.RWMutex
35		cache map[string]cachedOrg // keyed by ObjectID hex

38	// NewResolver binds the resolver to the database.
39	func NewResolver(db *mongo.Database) *Resolver {

41			coll:  db.Collection(collection),
42			ttl:   60 * time.Second,
43			cache: make(map[string]cachedOrg),
```

```text
1	// Package provenance implements the append-only, hash-chained event ledger —
2	// the source of truth for milk traceability (blueprint §7). Every link in the
3	// pour→QR chain is an immutable Event whose SHA-256 hash covers the previous
4	// event's hash, so history cannot be quietly rewritten (tamper-evidence,
5	// FSSAI recall-grade audit).
6	//
7	// Corrections are NEW events referencing the superseded entity — nothing is
8	// ever updated or deleted in this collection.
9	package provenance
10	
11	import (
12		"context"
13		"crypto/sha256"
14		"encoding/hex"
15		"encoding/json"
16		"errors"
17		"fmt"
18		"strconv"
19		"strings"
20		"sync"
21		"time"
22	
23		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson"
24		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson/primitive"
25		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo"
26		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo/options"
27	)
28	
29	const collection = "provenance_events"
30	
31	// Ref is a directed edge to another entity in the trace graph
32	// (e.g. a consignment event referencing the pours it aggregates).
33	type Ref struct {
34		EntityType string `bson:"entity_type" json:"entity_type"`
35		EntityID   string `bson:"entity_id"   json:"entity_id"`
36		Relation   string `bson:"relation"    json:"relation"` // aggregates | supersedes | tested | yields | labels ...
37	}
38	
39	// ActorRef records who caused the event.
40	type ActorRef struct {
41		PartyID  string `bson:"party_id"  json:"party_id"`
42		RoleCode string `bson:"role_code" json:"role_code"`
43	}
44	
45	// Event is one immutable link in the ledger. `_id` is a generated ObjectID;
46	// EntityID and Refs carry the referenced documents' ObjectIDs as hex strings
47	// (the ledger is a generic event log spanning every entity type, and hex
48	// strings keep the hash material canonical and human-inspectable).
49	type Event struct {
50		ID         primitive.ObjectID `bson:"_id,omitempty" json:"id"`
51		Seq        int64          `bson:"seq"         json:"seq"`
52		Type       string         `bson:"type"        json:"type"`
53		EntityType string         `bson:"entity_type" json:"entity_type"`
54		EntityID   string         `bson:"entity_id"   json:"entity_id"`
55		Refs       []Ref          `bson:"refs,omitempty"    json:"refs,omitempty"`
56		Actor      ActorRef       `bson:"actor"       json:"actor"`
57		OrgUnitID  string         `bson:"org_unit_id,omitempty" json:"org_unit_id,omitempty"`
58		Payload    map[string]any `bson:"payload,omitempty"     json:"payload,omitempty"`
59		TS         time.Time      `bson:"ts"          json:"ts"`
60		PrevHash   string         `bson:"prev_hash"   json:"prev_hash"`
61		Hash       string         `bson:"hash"        json:"hash"`
62	}
63	
64	// AppendInput describes a new event to chain.
65	type AppendInput struct {
66		Type       string
67		EntityType string
68		EntityID   string
69		Refs       []Ref
70		Actor      ActorRef
71		OrgUnitID  string
72		Payload    map[string]any
73	}
74	
75	// Ledger appends to and reads the hash chain.
76	type Ledger struct {
77		coll *mongo.Collection
78	
79		// appendMu serialises the head-read+insert of Append within this process:
80		// every ledger write system-wide shares one global seq, so without local
81		// serialisation concurrent handlers (e.g. a morning pour rush plus a
82		// GenerateInvoices loop) burn duplicate-key retries against each other.
83		// The unique seq index remains the atomic backstop across processes.
84		appendMu sync.Mutex
85	}
86	
87	// NewLedger binds the ledger to the database.
88	func NewLedger(db *mongo.Database) *Ledger {
89		return &Ledger{coll: db.Collection(collection)}
90	}
91	
92	// genesisHash anchors the chain before the first event.
93	const genesisHash = "GENESIS"
94	
95	// Append chains a new event. Concurrency-safe without transactions: it reads
96	// the current head, computes seq+hash optimistically, and relies on the
97	// unique index on `seq` — a duplicate-key collision means another writer won
98	// the slot, so we re-read and retry.
99	func (l *Ledger) Append(ctx context.Context, in AppendInput) (*Event, error) {
100		// Serialise appends within this process (see appendMu): local writers no
101		// longer race each other for the seq slot, so under single-instance
102		// deployment the retry loop only ever fires against external writers.
103		l.appendMu.Lock()
104		defer l.appendMu.Unlock()
105	
106		const maxRetries = 12
107		for attempt := 0; attempt < maxRetries; attempt++ {
108			seq, prevHash, err := l.head(ctx)
109			if err != nil {
110				return nil, err
111			}
112			ev := &Event{
113				ID:         primitive.NewObjectID(),
114				Seq:        seq + 1,
115				Type:       in.Type,
116				EntityType: in.EntityType,
117				EntityID:   in.EntityID,
118				Refs:       in.Refs,
119				Actor:      in.Actor,
120				OrgUnitID:  in.OrgUnitID,
121				Payload:    in.Payload,
122				// Millisecond precision: BSON datetimes store ms, so the persisted
123				// TS must equal the hashed TS or re-verification would break.
124				TS:       time.Now().UTC().Truncate(time.Millisecond),
125				PrevHash: prevHash,
126			}
127			ev.Hash = computeHash(ev)
128	
129			if _, err := l.coll.InsertOne(ctx, ev); err != nil {
130				if mongo.IsDuplicateKeyError(err) {
131					continue // lost the seq race — retry against the new head
132				}
133				return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance append: %w", err)
134			}
135			return ev, nil
136		}
137		return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance append: gave up after %d seq collisions", 12)
138	}
139	
140	// head returns the latest (seq, hash), or (0, GENESIS) for an empty chain.
141	func (l *Ledger) head(ctx context.Context) (int64, string, error) {
142		var last Event
143		err := l.coll.FindOne(ctx, bson.D{},
144			options.FindOne().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: -1}}),
145		).Decode(&last)
146		if errors.Is(err, mongo.ErrNoDocuments) {
147			return 0, genesisHash, nil
148		}
149		if err != nil {
150			return 0, "", fmt.Errorf("provenance head: %w", err)
151		}
152		return last.Seq, last.Hash, nil
153	}
154	
155	// computeHash covers everything that matters: position, linkage, content.
156	// Payload is canonicalised via encoding/json (map keys are sorted) and the
157	// timestamp to millisecond precision (BSON datetime resolution), so the
158	// digest is deterministic across a MongoDB round trip.
159	func computeHash(ev *Event) string {
160		payloadJSON, _ := json.Marshal(ev.Payload)
161		refParts := make([]string, 0, len(ev.Refs))
162		for _, r := range ev.Refs {
163			refParts = append(refParts, r.EntityType+":"+r.EntityID+":"+r.Relation)
164		}
165		material := strings.Join([]string{
166			ev.PrevHash,
167			strconv.FormatInt(ev.Seq, 10),
168			ev.Type,
169			ev.EntityType,
170			ev.EntityID,
171			strings.Join(refParts, ","),
172			ev.Actor.PartyID,
173			ev.Actor.RoleCode,
174			ev.OrgUnitID,
175			string(payloadJSON),
176			ev.TS.UTC().Truncate(time.Millisecond).Format(time.RFC3339Nano),
177		}, "|")
178		sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(material))
179		return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
180	}
181	
182	// EventsForEntity returns an entity's own timeline in chain order.
183	func (l *Ledger) EventsForEntity(ctx context.Context, entityType, entityID string) ([]Event, error) {
184		cur, err := l.coll.Find(ctx,
185			bson.D{{Key: "entity_type", Value: entityType}, {Key: "entity_id", Value: entityID}},
186			options.Find().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: 1}}),
187		)
188		if err != nil {
189			return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance events for %s/%s: %w", entityType, entityID, err)
190		}
191		var out []Event
192		if err := cur.All(ctx, &out); err != nil {
193			return nil, err
194		}
195		return out, nil
196	}
197	
198	// Trace walks the provenance graph UPSTREAM from an entity: its events, plus
199	// (recursively) the events of everything those events reference. This is how
200	// a consumer QR resolves back to the contributing samiti set, and how a failed
201	// aflatoxin test walks back to source DCSes (blueprint §8.3).
202	func (l *Ledger) Trace(ctx context.Context, entityType, entityID string, maxDepth int) ([]Event, error) {
203		return l.TraceStopAt(ctx, entityType, entityID, maxDepth, nil)
204	}
205	
206	// TraceStopAt is Trace with a stop set: entity types in stopExpand are still
207	// fetched (their events appear in the result) but their refs are never
208	// followed. The consumer QR scan stops at the consignment/pooling boundary so
209	// hundreds of per-pour nodes (and cross-route trip fan-out) are never walked.
210	//
211	// Each BFS level is batched into a bounded number of $or queries instead of
212	// one Find per node, so a walk costs O(depth) round trips, not O(nodes).
213	func (l *Ledger) TraceStopAt(ctx context.Context, entityType, entityID string, maxDepth int, stopExpand map[string]bool) ([]Event, error) {
214		if maxDepth <= 0 {
215			maxDepth = 10
216		}
217		const hardEventCap = 2000
218	
219		type node struct{ etype, eid string }
220		visited := map[node]bool{}
221		frontier := []node{{entityType, entityID}}
222		var all []Event
223	
224		for depth := 0; depth < maxDepth && len(frontier) > 0; depth++ {
225			// Deduplicate this level against everything already visited.
226			level := make([]node, 0, len(frontier))
227			for _, n := range frontier {
228				if visited[n] {
229					continue
230				}
231				visited[n] = true
232				level = append(level, n)
233			}
234			if len(level) == 0 {
235				break
236			}
237	
238			var next []node
239			// One indexed query per chunk of the level (not per node).
240			const orChunk = 200
241			for start := 0; start < len(level); start += orChunk {
242				end := min(start+orChunk, len(level))
243				clauses := make(bson.A, 0, end-start)
244				for _, n := range level[start:end] {
245					clauses = append(clauses, bson.D{
246						{Key: "entity_type", Value: n.etype},
247						{Key: "entity_id", Value: n.eid},
248					})
249				}
250				cur, err := l.coll.Find(ctx,
251					bson.D{{Key: "$or", Value: clauses}},
252					options.Find().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: 1}}).SetLimit(hardEventCap),
253				)
254				if err != nil {
255					return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance trace level: %w", err)
256				}
257				var evs []Event
258				if err := cur.All(ctx, &evs); err != nil {
259					return nil, err
260				}
261				for _, ev := range evs {
262					all = append(all, ev)
263					if len(all) >= hardEventCap {
264						return all, nil
265					}
266					if stopExpand != nil && stopExpand[ev.EntityType] {
267						continue // include the node's events, never follow its refs
268					}
269					for _, ref := range ev.Refs {
270						nn := node{ref.EntityType, ref.EntityID}
271						if !visited[nn] {
272							next = append(next, nn)
273						}
274					}
275				}
276			}
277			frontier = next
278		}
279		return all, nil
280	}
281	
282	// DownstreamRefs finds events that reference the given entity — used to walk
283	// FORWARD (e.g. "which batches consumed this blocked BMC lot?"). The limit is
284	// pushed into the query: only the LAST limit referencing events are fetched
285	// (ascending chain order preserved). limit <= 0 falls back to 2000.
286	func (l *Ledger) DownstreamRefs(ctx context.Context, entityID string, limit int64) ([]Event, error) {
287		if limit <= 0 {
288			limit = 2000
289		}
290		cur, err := l.coll.Find(ctx,
291			bson.D{{Key: "refs.entity_id", Value: entityID}},
292			options.Find().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: -1}}).SetLimit(limit),
293		)
294		if err != nil {
295			return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance downstream of %s: %w", entityID, err)
296		}
297		var out []Event
298		if err := cur.All(ctx, &out); err != nil {
299			return nil, err
300		}
301		// Restore ascending chain order.
302		for i, j := 0, len(out)-1; i < j; i, j = i+1, j-1 {
303			out[i], out[j] = out[j], out[i]
304		}
305		return out, nil
306	}
307	
308	// EventsForEntityPage returns one page of an entity's own timeline in chain
309	// order, with skip/limit pushed into the query.
310	func (l *Ledger) EventsForEntityPage(ctx context.Context, entityType, entityID string, offset, limit int64) ([]Event, error) {
311		cur, err := l.coll.Find(ctx,
312			bson.D{{Key: "entity_type", Value: entityType}, {Key: "entity_id", Value: entityID}},
313			options.Find().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: 1}}).SetSkip(offset).SetLimit(limit),
314		)
315		if err != nil {
316			return nil, fmt.Errorf("provenance events page for %s/%s: %w", entityType, entityID, err)
317		}
318		var out []Event
319		if err := cur.All(ctx, &out); err != nil {
320			return nil, err
321		}
322		return out, nil
323	}
324	
325	// CountEventsForEntity returns the total number of events on an entity's
326	// timeline (pagination meta companion of EventsForEntityPage).
327	func (l *Ledger) CountEventsForEntity(ctx context.Context, entityType, entityID string) (int64, error) {
328		n, err := l.coll.CountDocuments(ctx,
329			bson.D{{Key: "entity_type", Value: entityType}, {Key: "entity_id", Value: entityID}})
330		if err != nil {
331			return 0, fmt.Errorf("provenance count for %s/%s: %w", entityType, entityID, err)
332		}
333		return n, nil
334	}
335	
336	// VerifyChain re-derives every hash in [fromSeq, toSeq] and checks linkage.
337	// Returns (true, 0) when intact, or (false, seq) of the first broken link.
338	func (l *Ledger) VerifyChain(ctx context.Context, fromSeq, toSeq int64) (bool, int64, error) {
339		filter := bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$gte", Value: fromSeq}, {Key: "$lte", Value: toSeq}}}}
340		cur, err := l.coll.Find(ctx, filter, options.Find().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: 1}}))
341		if err != nil {
342			return false, 0, fmt.Errorf("provenance verify: %w", err)
343		}
344		defer cur.Close(ctx)
345	
346		prevHash := ""
347		prevSeq := int64(0)
348		first := true
349		for cur.Next(ctx) {
350			var ev Event
351			if err := cur.Decode(&ev); err != nil {
352				return false, 0, err
353			}
354			if computeHash(&ev) != ev.Hash {
355				return false, ev.Seq, nil // content tampered
356			}
357			if !first {
358				if ev.Seq != prevSeq+1 || ev.PrevHash != prevHash {
359					return false, ev.Seq, nil // linkage broken
360				}
361			}
362			prevHash, prevSeq, first = ev.Hash, ev.Seq, false
363		}
364		return true, 0, cur.Err()
365	}
366	
367	// LatestSeq returns the current chain head sequence (0 = empty).
368	func (l *Ledger) LatestSeq(ctx context.Context) (int64, error) {
369		seq, _, err := l.head(ctx)
370		return seq, err
371	}
372
```

```text
10	// ParseID converts an ObjectID hex string (from JSON bodies, query params or
11	// JWT claims) into a primitive.ObjectID, or returns a 400 with the offending
12	// field name.
13	func ParseID(hex, field string) (primitive.ObjectID, error) {
14		id, err := primitive.ObjectIDFromHex(hex)
15		if err != nil {
16			return primitive.NilObjectID, BadRequest("INVALID_ID", field+" must be a valid object id")
17		}
18		return id, nil
19	}
20	
21	// PathID extracts a chi URL parameter and parses it as an ObjectID.
22	func PathID(r *http.Request, param string) (primitive.ObjectID, error) {
23		return ParseID(chi.URLParam(r, param), param)
24	}
```

```text
44	// PricePour computes (ratePerLitre, amount) for a pour, rounded to paise.

46		rate = rc.BaseRatePerLitre + fatPct*rc.FatRatePerPoint + snfPct*rc.SNFRatePerPoint

94	// CheckPlausibility validates fat/SNF/qty against physical bounds and returns
95	// the violated flags (empty slice = plausible).
96	func CheckPlausibility(fatPct, snfPct, qtyLitres float64) []string {
97		var flags []string
98		if fatPct < PlausibleFatMin || fatPct > PlausibleFatMax ||
99			snfPct < PlausibleSNFMin || snfPct > PlausibleSNFMax {
100			flags = append(flags, IntegrityFlagImplausibleValue)
101		}
102		if qtyLitres != 0 && (qtyLitres < PlausibleQtyMin || qtyLitres > PlausibleQtyMax) {
103			flags = append(flags, IntegrityFlagImplausibleValue)
104		}
105		return flags
106	}
```
