```text
175	// claimExecution atomically claims a batch for execution. Three legal claims:
176	//   - APPROVED  → EXECUTING (first run)
177	//   - FAILED    → EXECUTING (re-execution after a recorded failure)
178	//   - EXECUTING → EXECUTING with a STALE lease (resume of a run whose process
179	//     died before it could mark FAILED; staleBefore guards against stealing a
180	//     live executor's batch)
181	//
182	// Every claim stamps executing_at as the new lease. Returns false when no
183	// claim matched — someone else holds a fresh lease or the batch is terminal.
184	func (rp *repo) claimExecution(ctx context.Context, id primitive.ObjectID, now, staleBefore time.Time) (bool, error) {
185		for _, from := range []string{domain.SettlementStatusApproved, domain.SettlementStatusFailed} {
186			ok, err := rp.transitionBatch(ctx, id, from, bson.D{
187				{Key: "status", Value: domain.SettlementStatusExecuting},
188				{Key: "executing_at", Value: now},
189			})
190			if err != nil || ok {
191				return ok, err
192			}
193		}
194		res, err := rp.batches.UpdateOne(ctx,
195			bson.D{
196				{Key: "_id", Value: id},
197				{Key: "status", Value: domain.SettlementStatusExecuting},
198				{Key: "executing_at", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$lt", Value: staleBefore}}},
199			},
200			bson.D{{Key: "$set", Value: bson.D{{Key: "executing_at", Value: now}}}},
201		)
202		if err != nil {
203			return false, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("claim settlement execution: %w", err))
204		}
205		return res.MatchedCount > 0, nil
206	}
207	
208	// markExecutionFailed best-effort flips EXECUTING→FAILED with the reason so a
209	// mid-execution error leaves a re-executable batch, never a stuck one.
210	func (rp *repo) markExecutionFailed(ctx context.Context, id primitive.ObjectID, reason string) error {
211		_, err := rp.batches.UpdateOne(ctx,
212			bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: id}, {Key: "status", Value: domain.SettlementStatusExecuting}},
213			bson.D{{Key: "$set", Value: bson.D{
214				{Key: "status", Value: domain.SettlementStatusFailed},
215				{Key: "fail_reason", Value: reason},
216			}}},
217		)
218		if err != nil {
219			return httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("mark settlement execution failed: %w", err))
220		}
221		return nil
222	}

242		cur, err := rp.batches.Find(ctx, filter, options.Find().
243			SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "date", Value: -1}, {Key: "created_at", Value: -1}}).

245		)

252		}

258	// insertPayout persists one payout. The unique index on invoice_id makes an
259	// execution retry harmless: alreadyExists=true means this invoice was paid
260	// in a previous (possibly interrupted) run.
261	func (rp *repo) insertPayout(ctx context.Context, p *domain.PayoutInstruction) (alreadyExists bool, err error) {
262		if _, err := rp.payouts.InsertOne(ctx, p); err != nil {
263			if mongo.IsDuplicateKeyError(err) {
264				return true, nil
265			}
266			return false, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("insert payout: %w", err))
267		}
268		return false, nil
269	}

276			return nil, httpx.NotFound("payout for invoice " + invoiceID.Hex())
277		}
278		if err != nil {
279			return nil, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("find payout by invoice: %w", err))
280		}
281		return &p, nil
282	}

289		)

323	// latestBankMasked returns the masked bank account from the farmer's most
324	// recent KYC record carrying one, or "" when none exists.
325	func (rp *repo) latestBankMasked(ctx context.Context, partyID primitive.ObjectID) (string, error) {

344	// assignment — the scope anchors for staff reads of the farmer's financials.

356		}

359		}

362		}
363		ids := make([]primitive.ObjectID, 0, len(docs))

391		}

395	// dbtByID loads one DBT request.
396	func (rp *repo) dbtByID(ctx context.Context, id primitive.ObjectID) (*domain.DBTRequest, error) {
397		var d domain.DBTRequest
398		err := rp.dbt.FindOne(ctx, bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: id}}).Decode(&d)
399		if errors.Is(err, mongo.ErrNoDocuments) {
400			return nil, httpx.NotFound("dbt request " + id.Hex())
401		}
402		if err != nil {
403			return nil, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("find dbt request: %w", err))
404		}
405		return &d, nil
406	}
407	
408	// transitionDBT performs a status-guarded DBT update; false = lost the race
409	// or the request already left fromStatus.
410	func (rp *repo) transitionDBT(ctx context.Context, id primitive.ObjectID, fromStatus, toStatus string, creditedAt *time.Time) (bool, error) {
411		set := bson.D{{Key: "status", Value: toStatus}}
412		if creditedAt != nil {
413			set = append(set, bson.E{Key: "credited_at", Value: creditedAt})
414		}
415		res, err := rp.dbt.UpdateOne(ctx,
416			bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: id}, {Key: "status", Value: fromStatus}},
417			bson.D{{Key: "$set", Value: set}},
418		)
419		if err != nil {
420			return false, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("transition dbt request: %w", err))
421		}
422		return res.MatchedCount > 0, nil
423	}
424	
425	// listDBT pages DBT requests, newest first.
426	func (rp *repo) listDBT(ctx context.Context, filter bson.D, page httpx.Page) ([]domain.DBTRequest, int64, error) {
427		total, err := rp.dbt.CountDocuments(ctx, filter)
428		if err != nil {
429			return nil, 0, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("count dbt requests: %w", err))
430		}
431		cur, err := rp.dbt.Find(ctx, filter, options.Find().
432			SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "created_at", Value: -1}}).
433			SetSkip(page.Offset).SetLimit(page.Limit),
434		)
435		if err != nil {
436			return nil, 0, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("find dbt requests: %w", err))
437		}
438		var out []domain.DBTRequest
439		if err := cur.All(ctx, &out); err != nil {
440			return nil, 0, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("decode dbt requests: %w", err))
441		}
442		return out, total, nil
443	}
```

```text
198			CollFeatureFlags: {
199				// `_id` is a generated ObjectID; `key` is the unique business key.
200				idx(bson.D{{Key: "key", Value: asc}}, options.Index().SetUnique(true)),
201			},
202		}
203	
204		for coll, models := range specs {
205			if _, err := db.Collection(coll).Indexes().CreateMany(ctx, models); err != nil {
206				return fmt.Errorf("ensure indexes on %s: %w", coll, err)
207			}
208		}
209		return nil
210	}
211	
212	func idx(keys bson.D, opts *options.IndexOptions) mongo.IndexModel {
213		m := mongo.IndexModel{Keys: keys}
214		if opts != nil {
215			m.Options = opts
216		}
217		return m
218	}
219
```

```text
101		}

104			SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "recorded_at", Value: -1}}).
105			SetSkip(page.Offset).

145	// Returns false when the lot was already gated by a concurrent writer.
146	func (r *repository) gateBMCLot(ctx context.Context, lotID, resultID primitive.ObjectID, newStatus, blockReason string) (bool, error) {
147		return gateSubjectDoc(ctx, r.bmcLots, lotID, domain.BMCLotStatusQCPending, resultID, newStatus, blockReason)
148	}
149

151	// Returns false when the batch was already gated by a concurrent writer.
152	func (r *repository) gateBatch(ctx context.Context, batchID, resultID primitive.ObjectID, newStatus, blockReason string) (bool, error) {
153		return gateSubjectDoc(ctx, r.batches, batchID, domain.BatchStatusQCPending, resultID, newStatus, blockReason)
154	}

156	// gateSubjectDoc is the shared conditional gate write: the filter pins the
157	// subject to QC_PENDING so a lost race cannot double-apply a verdict — the
158	// optimistic pattern that replaces transactions on a standalone server.
159	func gateSubjectDoc(ctx context.Context, coll *mongo.Collection, subjectID primitive.ObjectID, pendingStatus string, resultID primitive.ObjectID, newStatus, blockReason string) (bool, error) {
160		set := bson.D{{Key: "status", Value: newStatus}}
161		if blockReason != "" {
162			set = append(set, bson.E{Key: "block_reason", Value: blockReason})
163		}
164		res, err := coll.UpdateOne(ctx,
165			bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: subjectID}, {Key: "status", Value: pendingStatus}},
166			bson.D{
167				{Key: "$set", Value: set},
168				{Key: "$push", Value: bson.D{{Key: "qc_result_ids", Value: resultID}}},
169			},
170		)
171		if err != nil {
172			return false, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("gate %s subject %s: %w", coll.Name(), subjectID.Hex(), err))
173		}
174		return res.MatchedCount == 1, nil
175	}
176	
177	// nextCertificateSeq atomically increments and returns the per-stage QC
178	// certificate counter (counters collection, upsert-on-first-use). Counter
179	// keys are human-readable strings by design — they are not entity references.
180	func (r *repository) nextCertificateSeq(ctx context.Context, stage string) (int64, error) {
181		var doc struct {
182			Seq int64 `bson:"seq"`
183		}
184		err := r.counters.FindOneAndUpdate(ctx,
185			bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: "qc_certificate:" + stage}},
186			bson.D{{Key: "$inc", Value: bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: int64(1)}}}},
187			options.FindOneAndUpdate().SetUpsert(true).SetReturnDocument(options.After),
188		).Decode(&doc)
189		if err != nil {
190			return 0, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("next qc certificate seq: %w", err))
191		}
192		return doc.Seq, nil
193	}
```

```text
1	package domain
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"time"
6	
7		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson/primitive"
8	)
9	
10	// FSSAI limits for liquid milk (blueprint §8.3). Aflatoxin M1 is heat-stable
11	// and survives pasteurisation, so it MUST be gated upstream (BMC + plant),
12	// never only at the finished product.
13	const (
14		FSSAIAflatoxinM1MaxMicrogramPerKg = 0.5  // AFM1 ≤ 0.5 µg/kg
15		FSSAIColiformMaxCFUPerMl          = 10.0 // coliform ≤ 10 CFU/ml
16		FSSAITetracyclineMaxMgPerKg       = 0.1  // antibiotic MRL example
17	)
18	
19	// QC test names.
20	const (
21		TestAflatoxinM1 = "AFLATOXIN_M1"            // µg/kg
22		TestColiform    = "COLIFORM"                // CFU/ml
23		TestTPC         = "TPC"                     // CFU/ml, graded — recorded, not hard-gated here
24		TestAntibiotic  = "ANTIBIOTIC_TETRACYCLINE" // mg/kg
25		TestPhosphatase = "PHOSPHATASE"             // 0 = negative (pass post-pasteurisation), 1 = positive
26		TestFat         = "FAT"                     // %
27		TestSNF         = "SNF"                     // %
28	)
29	
30	// QC stages.
31	const (
32		QCStageBMCRapid = "BMC_RAPID" // strip/rapid tests at the chilling centre
33		QCStagePlantLab = "PLANT_LAB" // full lab: ELISA/HPLC, culture, LC-MS/MS
34	)
35	
36	// QC subject types.
37	const (
38		QCSubjectDCSConsignment  = "DCS_CONSIGNMENT"
39		QCSubjectBMCLot          = "BMC_LOT"
40		QCSubjectProcessingBatch = "PROCESSING_BATCH"
41	)
42	
43	// QCTest is a single measurement inside a QC result.
44	type QCTest struct {
45		Name  string  `bson:"name"  json:"name"`
46		Value float64 `bson:"value" json:"value"`
47		Unit  string  `bson:"unit"  json:"unit"`
48		Pass  bool    `bson:"pass"  json:"pass"`
49	}
50	
51	// QCResult is the recorded outcome of testing one subject at one stage.
52	// OverallPass drives the safety gate; a certificate is attached to provenance
53	// on pass, a block + quarantine on fail.
54	type QCResult struct {
55		ID                primitive.ObjectID `bson:"_id,omitempty" json:"id"`
56		SubjectType       string             `bson:"subject_type"  json:"subject_type"`
57		SubjectID         primitive.ObjectID `bson:"subject_id"    json:"subject_id"`
58		Stage             string             `bson:"stage"         json:"stage"`
59		Tests             []QCTest           `bson:"tests"         json:"tests"`
60		OverallPass       bool               `bson:"overall_pass"  json:"overall_pass"`
61		FailureReasons    []string           `bson:"failure_reasons,omitempty" json:"failure_reasons,omitempty"`
62		AnalystPartyID    primitive.ObjectID `bson:"analyst_party_id" json:"analyst_party_id"`
63		LabRef            string             `bson:"lab_ref,omitempty"            json:"lab_ref,omitempty"`
64		CertificateNumber string             `bson:"certificate_number,omitempty" json:"certificate_number,omitempty"`
65		// Superseded marks a result voided after losing the gate race — the
66		// verdict on the subject came from a different, earlier result.
67		Superseded    bool      `bson:"superseded,omitempty" json:"superseded,omitempty"`
68		RecordedAt    time.Time `bson:"recorded_at"   json:"recorded_at"`
69		ProvenanceSeq int64     `bson:"provenance_seq,omitempty" json:"provenance_seq,omitempty"`
70	}
71	
72	// EvaluateQCTests applies the FSSAI gate to a set of tests: it fills each
73	// test's Pass verdict and returns the overall verdict plus human-readable
74	// failure reasons. Unknown test names are recorded but do not gate.
75	func EvaluateQCTests(tests []QCTest) (overallPass bool, failures []string, evaluated []QCTest) {
76		overallPass = true
77		evaluated = make([]QCTest, 0, len(tests))
78		for _, t := range tests {
79			pass := true
80			switch t.Name {
81			case TestAflatoxinM1:
82				if t.Value > FSSAIAflatoxinM1MaxMicrogramPerKg {
83					pass = false
84					failures = append(failures, fmt.Sprintf(
85						"AFLATOXIN_M1 %.3f µg/kg exceeds FSSAI limit %.1f µg/kg", t.Value, FSSAIAflatoxinM1MaxMicrogramPerKg))
86				}
87			case TestColiform:
88				if t.Value > FSSAIColiformMaxCFUPerMl {
89					pass = false
90					failures = append(failures, fmt.Sprintf(
91						"COLIFORM %.1f CFU/ml exceeds FSSAI limit %.0f CFU/ml", t.Value, FSSAIColiformMaxCFUPerMl))
92				}
93			case TestAntibiotic:
94				if t.Value > FSSAITetracyclineMaxMgPerKg {
95					pass = false
96					failures = append(failures, fmt.Sprintf(
97						"ANTIBIOTIC_TETRACYCLINE %.3f mg/kg exceeds MRL %.1f mg/kg", t.Value, FSSAITetracyclineMaxMgPerKg))
98				}
99			case TestPhosphatase:
100				if t.Value != 0 {
101					pass = false
102					failures = append(failures, "PHOSPHATASE positive — pasteurisation check failed (must be negative)")
103				}
104			}
105			t.Pass = pass
106			if !pass {
107				overallPass = false
108			}
109			evaluated = append(evaluated, t)
110		}
111		return overallPass, failures, evaluated
112	}
113
```

```text
1	package plant
2	
3	import (
4		"context"

15	)
16	
17	// Repo is the plant module's MongoDB access layer. All state transitions use
18	// optimistic filters on the expected status — no transactions (standalone
19	// server), so a lost race simply matches zero documents and the service
20	// reports a conflict instead of corrupting state.
21	type Repo struct {
22		consignments *mongo.Collection
23		bmcLots      *mongo.Collection
24		batches      *mongo.Collection
25		productLots  *mongo.Collection
26		qrs          *mongo.Collection
27		counters     *mongo.Collection
28	}
29	
30	// NewRepo binds the repo to the shared database.
31	func NewRepo(db *mongo.Database) *Repo {
32		return &Repo{
33			consignments: db.Collection(mongodb.CollConsignments),
34			bmcLots:      db.Collection(mongodb.CollBMCLots),
35			batches:      db.Collection(mongodb.CollBatches),
36			productLots:  db.Collection(mongodb.CollProductLots),
37			qrs:          db.Collection(mongodb.CollBatchQRs),
38			counters:     db.Collection(mongodb.CollCounters),
39		}
40	}
41	
42	// --- consignments (read + claim; owned by the logistics module otherwise) ---
43	
44	// ConsignmentsByIDs loads the given consignments (missing IDs simply absent).
45	func (r *Repo) ConsignmentsByIDs(ctx context.Context, ids []primitive.ObjectID) ([]domain.DCSConsignment, error) {
46		cur, err := r.consignments.Find(ctx, bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$in", Value: ids}}}})
47		if err != nil {
48			return nil, err
49		}
50		out := []domain.DCSConsignment{}
51		if err := cur.All(ctx, &out); err != nil {
52			return nil, err
53		}
54		return out, nil
55	}
56	
57	// ClaimConsignments atomically flips DELIVERED consignments to ACCEPTED and
58	// stamps the pooling lot ID. Returns how many were actually claimed — fewer
59	// than requested means another lot raced us on at least one consignment.
60	func (r *Repo) ClaimConsignments(ctx context.Context, ids []primitive.ObjectID, bmcLotID primitive.ObjectID) (int64, error) {
61		res, err := r.consignments.UpdateMany(ctx,
62			bson.D{
63				{Key: "_id", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$in", Value: ids}}},
64				{Key: "status", Value: domain.ConsignmentStatusDelivered},
65			},
66			bson.D{{Key: "$set", Value: bson.D{
67				{Key: "status", Value: domain.ConsignmentStatusAccepted},
68				{Key: "bmc_lot_id", Value: bmcLotID},
69			}}},
70		)
71		if err != nil {
72			return 0, err
73		}
74		return res.ModifiedCount, nil
75	}
76	
77	// ReleaseConsignments undoes a partial claim (compensating action for a lost
78	// race): everything stamped with this lot ID goes back to DELIVERED.
79	func (r *Repo) ReleaseConsignments(ctx context.Context, bmcLotID primitive.ObjectID) error {
80		_, err := r.consignments.UpdateMany(ctx,
81			bson.D{{Key: "bmc_lot_id", Value: bmcLotID}},
82			bson.D{
83				{Key: "$set", Value: bson.D{{Key: "status", Value: domain.ConsignmentStatusDelivered}}},
84				{Key: "$unset", Value: bson.D{{Key: "bmc_lot_id", Value: ""}}},
85			},
86		)
87		return err
88	}
89	
90	// --- BMC lots ---
91	
92	// InsertBMCLot stores a new lot.
93	func (r *Repo) InsertBMCLot(ctx context.Context, lot *domain.BMCLot) error {
94		_, err := r.bmcLots.InsertOne(ctx, lot)
95		return err
96	}
97	
98	// BMCLotByID loads one lot (mongo.ErrNoDocuments when absent).
99	func (r *Repo) BMCLotByID(ctx context.Context, id primitive.ObjectID) (*domain.BMCLot, error) {
100		var lot domain.BMCLot
101		if err := r.bmcLots.FindOne(ctx, bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: id}}).Decode(&lot); err != nil {
102			return nil, err
103		}
104		return &lot, nil
105	}
106	
107	// BMCLotsByIDs loads the given lots (missing IDs simply absent).
108	func (r *Repo) BMCLotsByIDs(ctx context.Context, ids []primitive.ObjectID) ([]domain.BMCLot, error) {
109		cur, err := r.bmcLots.Find(ctx, bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$in", Value: ids}}}})
110		if err != nil {
111			return nil, err
112		}
113		out := []domain.BMCLot{}
114		if err := cur.All(ctx, &out); err != nil {
115			return nil, err
116		}
117		return out, nil
118	}
119	
120	// CloseBMCLot transitions OPEN→QC_PENDING with the chilling temperature.
121	// Returns false when the lot was not OPEN (already closed, or raced).
122	func (r *Repo) CloseBMCLot(ctx context.Context, id primitive.ObjectID, tempC float64, closedAt time.Time) (bool, error) {
123		res, err := r.bmcLots.UpdateOne(ctx,
124			bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: id}, {Key: "status", Value: domain.BMCLotStatusOpen}},
125			bson.D{{Key: "$set", Value: bson.D{
126				{Key: "status", Value: domain.BMCLotStatusQCPending},
127				{Key: "chilling_temp_c", Value: tempC},
128				{Key: "closed_at", Value: closedAt},
129			}}},
130		)
131		if err != nil {
132			return false, err
133		}
134		return res.MatchedCount > 0, nil
135	}
136	
137	// DispatchBMCLot transitions PASSED→DISPATCHED. The status filter IS the
138	// safety gate at the datastore level: a BLOCKED or QC_PENDING lot can never
139	// match this update.
140	func (r *Repo) DispatchBMCLot(ctx context.Context, id primitive.ObjectID, dispatchedAt time.Time) (bool, error) {
141		res, err := r.bmcLots.UpdateOne(ctx,
142			bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: id}, {Key: "status", Value: domain.BMCLotStatusPassed}},
143			bson.D{{Key: "$set", Value: bson.D{
144				{Key: "status", Value: domain.BMCLotStatusDispatched},
145				{Key: "dispatched_at", Value: dispatchedAt},
146			}}},
147		)
148		if err != nil {
149			return false, err
150		}
151		return res.MatchedCount > 0, nil
152	}
153	
154	// ClaimBMCLots atomically claims DISPATCHED lots for a processing batch:
155	// DISPATCHED→POOLED stamped with the batch ID. Returns how many were actually
156	// claimed — fewer than requested means another batch raced us on at least one
157	// lot (or a lot was not DISPATCHED), and the caller must roll back.
158	func (r *Repo) ClaimBMCLots(ctx context.Context, ids []primitive.ObjectID, batchID primitive.ObjectID) (int64, error) {
159		res, err := r.bmcLots.UpdateMany(ctx,
160			bson.D{
161				{Key: "_id", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$in", Value: ids}}},
162				{Key: "status", Value: domain.BMCLotStatusDispatched},
163			},
164			bson.D{{Key: "$set", Value: bson.D{
165				{Key: "status", Value: domain.BMCLotStatusPooled},
166				{Key: "batch_id", Value: batchID},
167			}}},
168		)
169		if err != nil {
170			return 0, err
171		}
172		return res.ModifiedCount, nil
173	}
174	
175	// ReleaseBMCLots undoes a partial claim (compensating action for a lost
176	// race): every lot stamped with this batch ID goes back to DISPATCHED.
177	func (r *Repo) ReleaseBMCLots(ctx context.Context, batchID primitive.ObjectID) error {
178		_, err := r.bmcLots.UpdateMany(ctx,
179			bson.D{
180				{Key: "batch_id", Value: batchID},
181				{Key: "status", Value: domain.BMCLotStatusPooled},
182			},
183			bson.D{
184				{Key: "$set", Value: bson.D{{Key: "status", Value: domain.BMCLotStatusDispatched}}},
185				{Key: "$unset", Value: bson.D{{Key: "batch_id", Value: ""}}},
186			},
187		)
188		return err
189	}

191	// BMCLotListFilter narrows the BMC lot listing. Zero-valued fields are
192	// ignored.
193	type BMCLotListFilter struct {
194		BMCID  primitive.ObjectID
195		Date   string
196		Status string
197	}
198	
199	// ListBMCLots returns a page of lots plus the total match count.
200	func (r *Repo) ListBMCLots(ctx context.Context, f BMCLotListFilter, page httpx.Page) ([]domain.BMCLot, int64, error) {
201		filter := bson.D{}
202		if !f.BMCID.IsZero() {
203			filter = append(filter, bson.E{Key: "bmc_id", Value: f.BMCID})
204		}
205		if f.Date != "" {
206			filter = append(filter, bson.E{Key: "date", Value: f.Date})
207		}
208		if f.Status != "" {
209			filter = append(filter, bson.E{Key: "status", Value: f.Status})
210		}
211		total, err := r.bmcLots.CountDocuments(ctx, filter)
212		if err != nil {
213			return nil, 0, err
214		}
215		cur, err := r.bmcLots.Find(ctx, filter, options.Find().
216			SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "date", Value: -1}, {Key: "created_at", Value: -1}}).
217			SetSkip(page.Offset).SetLimit(page.Limit))
218		if err != nil {
219			return nil, 0, err
220		}
221		out := []domain.BMCLot{}
222		if err := cur.All(ctx, &out); err != nil {
223			return nil, 0, err
224		}
225		return out, total, nil
226	}

228	// --- processing batches ---
229	
230	// NextSequence atomically increments and returns the named counter — the
231	// transaction-free way to mint gapless human-readable numbers.
232	func (r *Repo) NextSequence(ctx context.Context, key string) (int64, error) {
233		var doc struct {
234			Seq int64 `bson:"seq"`
235		}
236		err := r.counters.FindOneAndUpdate(ctx,
237			bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: key}},
238			bson.D{{Key: "$inc", Value: bson.D{{Key: "seq", Value: int64(1)}}}},
239			options.FindOneAndUpdate().SetUpsert(true).SetReturnDocument(options.After),
240		).Decode(&doc)
241		if err != nil {
242			return 0, err
243		}
244		return doc.Seq, nil
245	}

262	// CompleteBatch transitions PASSED→COMPLETED. The status filter enforces the
263	// gate: an unpassed batch can never match.
264	func (r *Repo) CompleteBatch(ctx context.Context, id primitive.ObjectID, completedAt time.Time) (bool, error) {
265		res, err := r.batches.UpdateOne(ctx,
266			bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: id}, {Key: "status", Value: domain.BatchStatusPassed}},

269				{Key: "completed_at", Value: completedAt},
270			}}},
271		)
272		if err != nil {
273			return false, err
274		}
275		return res.MatchedCount > 0, nil
276	}

327	// RecallProductLot flips any not-yet-recalled lot to RECALLED with the reason.

329	func (r *Repo) RecallProductLot(ctx context.Context, id primitive.ObjectID, reason string) (bool, error) {

333				{Key: "status", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$ne", Value: domain.ProductLotStatusRecalled}}},

348	// InsertQR stores a freshly minted QR. A duplicate-key error means the random
349	// short code collided — the service regenerates and retries.

355	// DeleteQR removes a just-minted QR whose lot turned out to be no longer

357	// the caller, so nothing references it).

363	// TouchActiveLot performs a no-op conditional write on an ACTIVE product lot
364	// ($inc of a stamp counter). MatchedCount == 0 proves the lot is no longer
365	// ACTIVE (e.g. recalled mid-request) at datastore level.
366	func (r *Repo) TouchActiveLot(ctx context.Context, lotID primitive.ObjectID) (bool, error) {

370		)

373		}
```

```text
1	// Package auth owns tokens and credentials: JWT issue/verify, OTP generation
2	// and HMAC hashing, opaque refresh tokens. Nothing secret is ever stored in
3	// plaintext — OTPs and refresh tokens live in the DB only as HMAC-SHA256
4	// digests.
5	package auth
6	
7	import (
8		"fmt"
9		"time"
10	
11		"github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v5"
12		"github.com/google/uuid"
13	
14		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/domain"
15	)
16	
17	// Token kinds. A SESSION token proves "this phone logged in"; a ROLE token
18	// additionally pins one active role assignment + org scope (the role switcher
19	// simply issues a fresh ROLE token).
20	const (
21		TokenKindSession = "session"
22		TokenKindRole    = "role"
23	)
24	
25	// Claims is the JWT payload.
26	type Claims struct {
27		PartyID          string `json:"pid"`
28		Phone            string `json:"phn"`
29		KYCTier          string `json:"kyc"`
30		Kind             string `json:"knd"`
31		RoleAssignmentID string `json:"rid,omitempty"`
32		RoleCode         string `json:"rol,omitempty"`
33		OrgUnitID        string `json:"org,omitempty"`
34		OrgType          string `json:"ogt,omitempty"`
35		jwt.RegisteredClaims
36	}
37	
38	// JWTManager issues and parses access tokens.
39	type JWTManager struct {
40		secret []byte
41		ttl    time.Duration
42	}
43	
44	// NewJWTManager builds a manager with the shared HS256 secret and access TTL.
45	func NewJWTManager(secret string, ttl time.Duration) *JWTManager {
46		return &JWTManager{secret: []byte(secret), ttl: ttl}
47	}
48	
49	// IssueSessionToken returns a SESSION-kind access token for a logged-in party.
50	// ObjectIDs travel in claims as hex strings (JWTs are JSON).
51	func (m *JWTManager) IssueSessionToken(p domain.Party) (string, error) {
52		return m.sign(Claims{
53			PartyID: p.ID.Hex(),
54			Phone:   p.Phone,
55			KYCTier: p.KYCTier,
56			Kind:    TokenKindSession,
57		})
58	}
59	
60	// IssueRoleToken returns a ROLE-kind access token pinned to one assignment.
61	func (m *JWTManager) IssueRoleToken(p domain.Party, ra domain.RoleAssignment, orgType string) (string, error) {
62		return m.sign(Claims{
63			PartyID:          p.ID.Hex(),
64			Phone:            p.Phone,
65			KYCTier:          p.KYCTier,
66			Kind:             TokenKindRole,
67			RoleAssignmentID: ra.ID.Hex(),
68			RoleCode:         ra.RoleCode,
69			OrgUnitID:        ra.OrgUnitID.Hex(),
70			OrgType:          orgType,
71		})
72	}
73	
74	func (m *JWTManager) sign(c Claims) (string, error) {
75		now := time.Now()
76		c.RegisteredClaims = jwt.RegisteredClaims{
77			Issuer:    "saathi-backend",
78			Subject:   c.PartyID,
79			IssuedAt:  jwt.NewNumericDate(now),
80			ExpiresAt: jwt.NewNumericDate(now.Add(m.ttl)),
81			ID:        uuid.NewString(),
82		}
83		return jwt.NewWithClaims(jwt.SigningMethodHS256, c).SignedString(m.secret)
84	}
85	
86	// Parse validates signature+expiry and returns the claims.
87	func (m *JWTManager) Parse(token string) (*Claims, error) {
88		parsed, err := jwt.ParseWithClaims(token, &Claims{},
89			func(t *jwt.Token) (any, error) { return m.secret, nil },
90			jwt.WithValidMethods([]string{jwt.SigningMethodHS256.Alg()}),
91			jwt.WithIssuer("saathi-backend"),
92		)
93		if err != nil {
94			return nil, fmt.Errorf("parse token: %w", err)
```

```text
package publictrace

import (
	"net/http"

	"github.com/go-chi/chi/v5"

	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/httpx"
)

// Handler is the thin HTTP layer: extract params, call the service, respond.
type Handler struct {
	service *Service
}

// ScanQR handles GET /public/qr/{qr_code} — the consumer scan.
func (h *Handler) ScanQR(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	qrCode := chi.URLParam(r, "qr_code")
	if qrCode == "" {
		httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.BadRequest("MISSING_QR_CODE", "qr_code path parameter is required"))
		return
	}
	resp, err := h.service.ScanQR(r.Context(), qrCode)
	if err != nil {
		httpx.Error(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	httpx.JSON(w, http.StatusOK, resp)
}

// VerifyLedger handles GET /public/ledger/verify?from=&to= — the public
// tamper-evidence check.
func (h *Handler) VerifyLedger(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	resp, err := h.service.VerifyLedger(r.Context(), r.URL.Query().Get("from"), r.URL.Query().Get("to"))
	if err != nil {
		httpx.Error(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	httpx.JSON(w, http.StatusOK, resp)
}

// TraceGraph handles GET /trace/{entity_type}/{entity_id} — the official
// upstream+downstream event-graph walk. entity_id is an ObjectID hex; it is
// validated here and passed to the ledger as its canonical hex form.
func (h *Handler) TraceGraph(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	entityID, err := httpx.PathID(r, "entity_id")
	if err != nil {
		httpx.Error(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	resp, err := h.service.TraceGraph(r.Context(),
		chi.URLParam(r, "entity_type"), entityID.Hex())
	if err != nil {
		httpx.Error(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	httpx.JSON(w, http.StatusOK, resp)
}

// Timeline handles GET /trace/{entity_type}/{entity_id}/timeline — one
// entity's own events in chain order. entity_id is an ObjectID hex.
func (h *Handler) Timeline(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	entityID, err := httpx.PathID(r, "entity_id")
	if err != nil {
		httpx.Error(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	page := httpx.ParsePage(r)
	events, total, err := h.service.Timeline(r.Context(),
		chi.URLParam(r, "entity_type"), entityID.Hex(), page)
	if err != nil {
		httpx.Error(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	httpx.JSONMeta(w, http.StatusOK, events, map[string]any{
		"limit":  page.Limit,
		"offset": page.Offset,
		"total":  total,
	})
}
```

Let me confirm the exact self-approval gap and cross-org gap once more by re-reading the approve/reject flow — both `approveKYC` (lines 663-746) and `rejectKYC` (751-826) compute the actor's `aid` but never compare it to `record.PartyID`, and neither calls `s.deps.Orgs.RequireInScope`. The KYCRecord has no org field, and `repo.listPendingKYC` (repo.go:438) filters only on `status: PENDING`. All confirmed.

Key confirmations from my review:
- `approveKYC`/`rejectKYC`: only gate is `CanApproveKYCTier(actor.RoleCode, record.RequestedTier)` — no owner check, no org-scope check.
- `listPendingKYC` builds `pendingPartySummary{Phone, FullName}` for every pending record platform-wide (service.go:638-643), no scoping.
- `pendingKYCItem` and `listMyKYC` serialize the full `domain.KYCRecord` including `aadhaar_vault_ref`; `getMe`'s `kycSummary` deliberately omits it.
- `verifyBank` calls `updateKYCRecordBank` on `latestKYCRecord` regardless of status; settlement's `latestBankMasked` (settlement/repo.go:325) pulls the latest bank-bearing record ignoring KYC status.
- `createAssignment`/`revokeAssignment` write only slog lines (no `Audit.Record`), unlike KYC review.
- `requireGrantAuthority` pins SAMITI_ADHYAKSH to its own org unit but leaves ORGANISING_MANAGER with no own-DCS pin.
- Tier-downgrade and REJECTED→re-approve are correctly prevented (upward-only `upgradedKYCTier`; status==PENDING filters). No bug there — I won't report those.

I've completed an exhaustive review of `internal/modules` (all 10 modules: collection, logistics, plant, publictrace, quality, settlement, identity, platformops, cattle, orgs), `cmd/seed`, and the supporting platform code (provenance ledger, audit recorder, auth HMAC, orgscope resolver, httpx ID parsing, mongodb indexes) plus the domain models.

I checked each of the eight enumerated ObjectID-migration defect categories against the actual code and found every one handled correctly:

1. **String/ObjectID comparisons** — all comparisons are hex-string-vs-hex-string (e.g. `identity/service.go:839` `orgUnitID.Hex() != actor.OrgUnitID`, dual-control `InitiatedBy == approverPartyID` on ObjectIDs) — none can-never-match.
2. **Hex-string filters against ObjectID fields** — every `_id`/reference filter passes `primitive.ObjectID` values; hex strings appear only in ledger `entity_id`/`refs.entity_id` filters, where the ledger deliberately stores hex. No mismatch.
3. **`.Hex()` omitted in ledger refs** — every `provenance.AppendInput` `EntityID`, `OrgUnitID`, and `Ref.EntityID` across all modules uses `.Hex()`; the publictrace trace joins line up.
4. **NilObjectID accepted where an id is required** — guarded everywhere via `IsZero()` checks and `ParseID` error propagation; `resolveAnimalOwner`/`RequireInScope` never let a Nil target through for non-admins.
5. **Unparsed `actor.PartyID` in queries** — always converted via `httpx.ParseID`/`actorID` before use; the audit filter correctly matches the string `actor_party_id` (stored as hex text) against a string.
6. **Counters/business keys wrongly converted** — counters use string keys (`"invoice:"+dcs.Code+...`, `"batch_number:"+plantHex+...`, `"qc_certificate:"+stage`); business keys (`phone`, `client_event_id`, `qr_code`, `pashu_aadhaar`, dates) stay strings; no wrongful ObjectID conversion.
7. **QR HMAC plant↔publictrace** — `plant/service.go signQRToken` computes `hex(HMAC-SHA256(secret, "qr|lotHex|unix"))`; `publictrace VerifyQRToken` recomputes `auth.HMACHash(secret, payload)` = `hex(HMAC-SHA256)` over the identical decoded bytes. Same secret (`d.Cfg.QRSigningSecret`), same encoding, single write — they match.
8. **Seed natural-key upserts racing** — the seed is single-process/sequential and idempotent (`$setOnInsert` find-or-insert), and the natural keys it relies on are backed by unique indexes (`parties.phone`, `org_units.code`, `animals.pashu_aadhaar`).

I also verified bson tags on every reference field (`settlement_batch_id`, `product_lot_id`, `batch_id`, `bmc_id`, `plant_id`, `subject_id`, `pour_date`, `invoice_date`, etc.) match the filter keys used in the repos, ruling out silent-empty-result tag mismatches, and confirmed no `.String()`-instead-of-`.Hex()` misuse.

No ObjectID-migration defects in the requested categories were found. Reporting an empty findings list rather than fabricating out-of-scope or non-existent issues.

```text
161	// runWorker is the MOCK SMS provider dispatch (real deployment: MSG91 /
```

```text
560	func (s *service) verifyBank(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, req bankKYCRequest) (*domain.KYCRecord, error) {
561		now := time.Now().UTC()
562		aid, err := actorID(actor)

565		}

568			return nil, err
569		}
570		masked := maskAccount(req.AccountNumber)
571	
572		latest, err := s.repo.latestKYCRecord(ctx, aid)
573		switch {
574		case err == nil:
575			// MOCK penny-drop: always verified with a fixed name-match score.

579			}
580			s.log.InfoContext(ctx, "bank evidence attached",
581				slog.String("kyc_id", rec.ID.Hex()), slog.String("party_id", party.ID.Hex()))
582			return rec, nil
583		case isNotFound(err):
584			record := domain.KYCRecord{
585				ID:                primitive.NewObjectID(),
586				PartyID:           party.ID,
587				RequestedTier:     party.KYCTier,
588				BankAccountMasked: masked,
589				BankIFSC:          req.IFSC,
590				BankVerified:      true, // MOCK penny-drop: always succeeds
591				BankNameMatch:     mockPennyDropNameMatch,
592				Status:            domain.KYCStatusPending,
593				CreatedAt:         now,
594				UpdatedAt:         now,
595			}
596			if err := s.repo.insertKYCRecord(ctx, record); err != nil {
597				return nil, err
598			}
599			s.log.InfoContext(ctx, "bank evidence recorded on new pending kyc",
600				slog.String("kyc_id", record.ID.Hex()), slog.String("party_id", party.ID.Hex()))
601			return &record, nil
602		default:
603			return nil, err
604		}
605	}
```

```text
438	func (r *repository) listPendingKYC(ctx context.Context, page httpx.Page) ([]domain.KYCRecord, int64, error) {
439		filter := bson.D{{Key: "status", Value: domain.KYCStatusPending}}
440		total, err := r.kycRecords.CountDocuments(ctx, filter)
441		if err != nil {
442			return nil, 0, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("count pending kyc records: %w", err))
443		}
444		opts := options.Find().
445			SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "created_at", Value: -1}}).
446			SetSkip(page.Offset).
447			SetLimit(page.Limit)
448		cur, err := r.kycRecords.Find(ctx, filter, opts)
449		if err != nil {
450			return nil, 0, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("list pending kyc records: %w", err))
451		}
452		out := make([]domain.KYCRecord, 0)
453		if err := cur.All(ctx, &out); err != nil {
454			return nil, 0, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("decode pending kyc records: %w", err))
455		}
456		return out, total, nil
457	}
```

```text
1	package middleware
2	
3	import (
4		"net/http"
5	
6		chimw "github.com/go-chi/chi/v5/middleware"
7	
8		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/audit"
9		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/auth"
10	)
11	
12	// AuditMutations records every state-changing request (non-GET/HEAD/OPTIONS)
13	// into the immutable audit trail: actor, action, status, IP, request ID.
14	// Runs after the handler so the final status code is captured; the write
15	// itself is async and adds no request latency.
16	//
17	// This middleware mounts OUTSIDE the per-module Authenticate middleware, so
18	// the actor installed on the inner request context never propagates back to
19	// this frame. An actor holder is installed on the context before the chain
20	// runs; auth.WithActor fills it, and the identity is read back here so the
21	// who-did-what contract holds for every HTTP mutation.
22	func AuditMutations(rec *audit.Recorder) func(http.Handler) http.Handler {
23		return func(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
24			return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
25				if r.Method == http.MethodGet || r.Method == http.MethodHead || r.Method == http.MethodOptions {
26					next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
27					return
28				}
29				r = r.WithContext(auth.WithActorHolder(r.Context()))
30				ww := chimw.NewWrapResponseWriter(w, r.ProtoMajor)
31				next.ServeHTTP(ww, r)
32	
33				entry := audit.Entry{
34					Action:    "http." + r.Method + " " + r.URL.Path,
35					Status:    ww.Status(),
36					IP:        r.RemoteAddr,
37					RequestID: chimw.GetReqID(r.Context()),
38				}
39				if actor, ok := auth.HeldActor(r.Context()); ok {
40					entry.ActorPartyID = actor.PartyID
41					entry.ActorRole = actor.RoleCode
42				}
43				rec.Record(r.Context(), entry)
44			})
45		}
46	}
47
```

```text
145	// KYCTierSatisfies reports whether a party at tier `have` meets `need`.
146	// Parallel tier-1 proofs (FARMER vs STANDARD) satisfy each other.
147	func KYCTierSatisfies(have, need string) bool {
148		h, okH := kycRank[have]
149		n, okN := kycRank[need]
150		if !okH || !okN {
151			return false
152		}
153		return h >= n
154	}

158	// only SUPER_ADMIN clears HIGHEST. Extend when new approver roles arrive.
159	var KYCApprovableTiers = map[string][]string{

164	}

167	// requesting the given tier.
168	func CanApproveKYCTier(approverRole, tier string) bool {
169		for _, t := range KYCApprovableTiers[approverRole] {
170			if t == tier {
171				return true
172			}
173		}
174		return false
```

```text
1	// Package orgscope answers the RBAC question "is this resource inside the
2	// caller's organisational scope?" in O(1) DB reads. Org units denormalise
3	// their ancestor chain into Path ([]ObjectID), so scope checking is a
4	// set-membership test — no recursive tree walks on the hot path.
5	package orgscope
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"errors"
10		"sync"
11		"time"
12	
13		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson"
14		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson/primitive"
15		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo"
16	
17		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/domain"
18		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/auth"
19		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/httpx"
20	)
21	
22	const collection = "org_units"
23	
24	type cachedOrg struct {
25		org domain.OrgUnit
26		at  time.Time
27	}
28	
29	// Resolver caches org units briefly (the tree changes rarely, reads are hot).
30	type Resolver struct {
31		coll *mongo.Collection
32		ttl  time.Duration
33	
34		mu    sync.RWMutex
35		cache map[string]cachedOrg // keyed by ObjectID hex
36	}
37	
38	// NewResolver binds the resolver to the database.
39	func NewResolver(db *mongo.Database) *Resolver {
40		return &Resolver{
41			coll:  db.Collection(collection),
42			ttl:   60 * time.Second,
43			cache: make(map[string]cachedOrg),
44		}
45	}
46	
47	// Get returns an org unit by ObjectID (cached).
48	func (r *Resolver) Get(ctx context.Context, id primitive.ObjectID) (*domain.OrgUnit, error) {
49		key := id.Hex()
50		r.mu.RLock()
51		c, ok := r.cache[key]
52		r.mu.RUnlock()
53		if ok && time.Since(c.at) < r.ttl {
54			org := c.org
55			return &org, nil
56		}
57	
58		var org domain.OrgUnit
59		err := r.coll.FindOne(ctx, bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: id}}).Decode(&org)
60		if errors.Is(err, mongo.ErrNoDocuments) {
61			return nil, httpx.NotFound("org unit " + key)
62		}
63		if err != nil {
64			return nil, httpx.Internal(err)
65		}
66	
67		r.mu.Lock()
68		r.cache[key] = cachedOrg{org: org, at: time.Now()}
69		r.mu.Unlock()
70		return &org, nil
71	}
72	
73	// GetByCode returns an org unit by its unique human-readable business code
74	// (e.g. "DCS-01842") — display/lookup use only, never for joins.
75	func (r *Resolver) GetByCode(ctx context.Context, code string) (*domain.OrgUnit, error) {
76		var org domain.OrgUnit
77		err := r.coll.FindOne(ctx, bson.D{{Key: "code", Value: code}}).Decode(&org)
78		if errors.Is(err, mongo.ErrNoDocuments) {
79			return nil, httpx.NotFound("org unit with code " + code)
80		}
81		if err != nil {
82			return nil, httpx.Internal(err)
83		}
84		return &org, nil
85	}
86	
87	// Invalidate drops a cached entry (call after updates).
88	func (r *Resolver) Invalidate(id primitive.ObjectID) {
89		r.mu.Lock()
90		delete(r.cache, id.Hex())
91		r.mu.Unlock()
92	}
93	
94	// InScope reports whether target sits at-or-below scope in the hierarchy:
95	// true when scope == target, or scope appears in target's ancestor Path.
96	func (r *Resolver) InScope(ctx context.Context, scopeOrgID, targetOrgID primitive.ObjectID) (bool, error) {
97		if scopeOrgID == targetOrgID {
98			return true, nil
99		}
100		target, err := r.Get(ctx, targetOrgID)
101		if err != nil {
102			return false, err
103		}
104		for _, ancestor := range target.Path {
105			if ancestor == scopeOrgID {
106				return true, nil
107			}
108		}
109		return false, nil
110	}
111	
112	// RequireInScope enforces the actor's org scope over a target org unit.
113	// SUPER_ADMIN and STATE_AUDITOR (read-wide roles rooted at the federation)
114	// pass automatically; everyone else needs ancestry. The actor carries its
115	// org unit as an ObjectID hex string (JWT claims are JSON); it is parsed here.
116	func (r *Resolver) RequireInScope(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, targetOrgID primitive.ObjectID) error {
117		if actor.RoleCode == domain.RoleSuperAdmin || actor.RoleCode == domain.RoleStateAuditor {
118			return nil
119		}
120		if actor.OrgUnitID == "" {
121			return httpx.Forbidden("role token with org scope required")
122		}
123		scopeID, err := primitive.ObjectIDFromHex(actor.OrgUnitID)
124		if err != nil {
125			return httpx.Forbidden("role token carries an invalid org scope")
126		}
127		ok, err := r.InScope(ctx, scopeID, targetOrgID)
128		if err != nil {
129			return err
130		}
131		if !ok {
132			return httpx.Forbidden("resource is outside your organisational scope")
133		}
134		return nil
135	}
```

```text
1	package middleware
2	
3	import (
4		"net/http"
5	
6		chimw "github.com/go-chi/chi/v5/middleware"
7	
8		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/audit"
9		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/auth"
10	)
11	
12	// AuditMutations records every state-changing request (non-GET/HEAD/OPTIONS)
13	// into the immutable audit trail: actor, action, status, IP, request ID.
14	// Runs after the handler so the final status code is captured; the write
15	// itself is async and adds no request latency.
16	//
17	// This middleware mounts OUTSIDE the per-module Authenticate middleware, so
18	// the actor installed on the inner request context never propagates back to
19	// this frame. An actor holder is installed on the context before the chain
20	// runs; auth.WithActor fills it, and the identity is read back here so the
21	// who-did-what contract holds for every HTTP mutation.
22	func AuditMutations(rec *audit.Recorder) func(http.Handler) http.Handler {
23		return func(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
24			return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
25				if r.Method == http.MethodGet || r.Method == http.MethodHead || r.Method == http.MethodOptions {
26					next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
27					return
28				}
29				r = r.WithContext(auth.WithActorHolder(r.Context()))
30				ww := chimw.NewWrapResponseWriter(w, r.ProtoMajor)
31				next.ServeHTTP(ww, r)
32	
33				entry := audit.Entry{
34					Action:    "http." + r.Method + " " + r.URL.Path,
35					Status:    ww.Status(),
36					IP:        r.RemoteAddr,
37					RequestID: chimw.GetReqID(r.Context()),
38				}
39				if actor, ok := auth.HeldActor(r.Context()); ok {
40					entry.ActorPartyID = actor.PartyID
41					entry.ActorRole = actor.RoleCode
42				}
43				rec.Record(r.Context(), entry)
44			})
45		}
46	}
47
```

```text
1	// Package audit writes the immutable who-did-what trail required for
2	// government accountability and DPDP breach forensics (blueprint §12, §16).
3	// Entries are insert-only; the STATE_AUDITOR role reads them via the

5	package audit
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"log/slog"
10		"time"
11	
12		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson/primitive"

14	
15		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/auth"
16	)
17	
18	const collection = "audit_logs"
19	
20	// Entry is one audit record. `_id` is a generated ObjectID; actor identifiers
21	// arrive from JWT claims as ObjectID hex strings.
22	type Entry struct {
23		ID           primitive.ObjectID `bson:"_id,omitempty" json:"id"`
24		ActorPartyID string         `bson:"actor_party_id" json:"actor_party_id"`
25		ActorRole    string         `bson:"actor_role,omitempty" json:"actor_role,omitempty"`
26		Action       string         `bson:"action"         json:"action"` // e.g. "http.POST /api/v1/collection/pours" or "support.pii_lookup"
27		TargetType   string         `bson:"target_type,omitempty" json:"target_type,omitempty"`
28		TargetID     string         `bson:"target_id,omitempty"   json:"target_id,omitempty"`
29		Status       int            `bson:"status,omitempty"      json:"status,omitempty"`
30		IP           string         `bson:"ip,omitempty"          json:"ip,omitempty"`
31		RequestID    string         `bson:"request_id,omitempty"  json:"request_id,omitempty"`
32		Meta         map[string]any `bson:"meta,omitempty"        json:"meta,omitempty"`
33		TS           time.Time      `bson:"ts"             json:"ts"`
34	}
35	
36	// Recorder persists audit entries asynchronously so auditing never adds
37	// latency to the request path.
38	type Recorder struct {
39		coll *mongo.Collection
40		log  *slog.Logger
41	}
42	
43	// NewRecorder binds the recorder to the database.
44	func NewRecorder(db *mongo.Database, log *slog.Logger) *Recorder {

46	}

48	// Record fills identity fields from the request context and persists the
49	// entry in the background (fire-and-forget with its own timeout).
50	func (r *Recorder) Record(ctx context.Context, e Entry) {
51		if a, ok := auth.ActorFrom(ctx); ok {
52			if e.ActorPartyID == "" {
53				e.ActorPartyID = a.PartyID
54			}
55			if e.ActorRole == "" {
56				e.ActorRole = a.RoleCode
57			}
58		}
59		e.ID = primitive.NewObjectID()
60		e.TS = time.Now().UTC()
61	
62		go func() {
63			writeCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
64			defer cancel()
65			if _, err := r.coll.InsertOne(writeCtx, e); err != nil {
66				r.log.Error("audit write failed", slog.String("action", e.Action), slog.Any("err", err))
67			}
68		}()
69	}
```

```text
145	// KYCTierSatisfies reports whether a party at tier `have` meets `need`.

147	func KYCTierSatisfies(have, need string) bool {
148		h, okH := kycRank[have]
149		n, okN := kycRank[need]

152		}
153		return h >= n
```

```text
54			filter = append(filter, bson.E{Key: "target_type", Value: f.TargetType})
```

_**Agent - sidechain (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-06 07:50:58Z)**_

I have fully traced the exploit chain. Let me confirm the finding.

All four links of the claim are verified in the code:

1. **Self-service, session-only auth** (module.go:56-59): `POST /kyc/bank` is in the RequireSession group — "any logged-in party submits evidence." No reviewer role required.

2. **latestKYCRecord ignores status** (repo.go:403-414): filters only `party_id`, sorts by `created_at` desc. Returns the most recent record regardless of VERIFIED/REJECTED/PENDING status.

3. **verifyBank calls update unconditionally** (service.go:572-582): on `err == nil` it calls `updateKYCRecordBank(latest.ID, ...)` with no status check.

4. **updateKYCRecordBank has no status guard** (repo.go:516-533): filters only `{_id: id}`, always `$set bank_verified:true` plus the new masked/IFSC, and leaves `status` untouched — so a VERIFIED record stays VERIFIED with mutated bank evidence, no `reviewed_by`/re-review.

5. **Settlement reads any-status record** (settlement/repo.go:325-341): `latestBankMasked` selects the most recent KYC bearing a `bank_account_masked` with no status filter, and settlement/service.go:437-448 stamps that mask onto the `PayoutInstruction`.

Concrete misbehaving sequence: A farmer with a terminal VERIFIED KYC record carrying reviewer-approved bank account A calls `POST /kyc/bank` with account B. `updateKYCRecordBank` overwrites `bank_account_masked`/`bank_ifsc` on that VERIFIED record to B and re-asserts `bank_verified=true`, status unchanged, zero reviewer involvement. At settlement, `latestBankMasked` returns B's mask and the payout instruction is issued against the self-submitted, unreviewed account. Equivalently, a party can self-attach `bank_verified=true` onto a PENDING record before any review.

I attempted refutation on each link — a status filter on `latestKYCRecord`, a guard in `updateKYCRecordBank`, a reviewer-role requirement on the route, or a VERIFIED-only filter in settlement — and none exist. The defect is real.

Confirmed all load-bearing facts. The claim is real.

Verification:
- `GET /notifications` is SUPER_ADMIN-only (module.go:52-62), a GET route.
- `AuditMutations` middleware explicitly returns early for GET/HEAD/OPTIONS (audit.go:25-28), so no audit row is written by the middleware.
- `listNotifications` (service.go:119-128) and its handler (handler.go:119-136) contain no `s.deps.Audit.Record` call — I checked both fully.
- Response body exposes PII: `StoredNotification` embeds `domain.Notification`, whose `Phone` (`json:"phone"`) and `Params` (`json:"params"`) are marshaled. `redactNotificationSecrets` (service.go:135-159) redacts only when `TemplateKey == TemplateOTP`, and only the `otp` param + `rendered_*` meta. For `KYC_REJECTED` the free-text `reason` param and for `PAYOUT_CREDITED` the `amount`/`utr` params are returned in cleartext for every matching document, across all parties.
- The two parallel PII-read surfaces cited do audit: `support.pii_lookup` records every call, hit or miss (service.go:253-261); `kyc.pending_list` records the bulk list read (identity/service.go:648-651). The notifications bulk read is the outlier with no audit trail.

The only mild caveat is severity framing: it is SUPER_ADMIN-gated and the OTP is redacted, which bounds the blast radius. But the defect as stated — a bulk multi-party PII read with no who-accessed-whose-data record, inconsistent with sibling audited surfaces — is accurate and a genuine DPDP forensics gap.

Verified. The claim is real and confirmed by concrete data flow.

**Confirmation of the leak path:**

1. `AadhaarVaultRef` is genuinely populated (not empty) on every KYC submission — `service.go:528,536` sets `vaultRef := uuid.NewString()` and stores it. So `json:",omitempty"` does not suppress it.

2. The field serializes via `json:"aadhaar_vault_ref,omitempty"` at `internal/domain/party.go:87` (note: actual path is `internal/domain/party.go`, not `domain/party.go` as cited — same struct/line otherwise).

3. `/kyc/me` → `listMyKYC` service returns `[]domain.KYCRecord` straight from `repo.listKYCRecords` (`service.go:609-615`), which does a full `Find` with no projection (`repo.go:537-556`) — the decoded record carries the vault ref. Handler serializes it directly (`handler.go:254`).

4. `/kyc/pending` → `listPendingKYC` builds `pendingKYCItem{KYCRecord: rec}` (`service.go:636`), embedding the full `domain.KYCRecord` (`models.go:245-248`); `repo.listPendingKYC` (`repo.go:438-457`) also has no projection. Handler serializes directly (`handler.go:269`). This exposes *other parties'* vault refs to any reviewer.

5. `getMe` deliberately projects `kycSummary` (`service.go:447-455`) omitting the vault ref, confirming the field is intended to stay server-side.

No projection or field-stripping happens anywhere between DB and JSON on the two flagged paths. The refutation attempts (omitempty suppressing it, repo projecting it out, field never populated) all fail.

Minor caveat on severity: in this build the vault ref is a mock UUID with no real de-tokenization backend, so today it de-tokenizes to nothing. But it is the production de-tokenization handle by design and is treated as a server-side secret (getMe masks it), so medium is appropriate.

Verified. The claim holds up under scrutiny.

**Confirmed facts:**

- `createAssignment` (service.go:846-921) writes only a `s.log.InfoContext` line at 914-919 after `insertAssignment`. No `s.deps.Audit.Record` call.
- `revokeAssignment` (service.go:925-962) writes only a `s.log.InfoContext` line at 956-960. No `Audit.Record` call.
- The only `Audit.Record` calls in identity/service.go are at 648 (`kyc.pending_list`), 728 (`kyc.approve`), 808 (`kyc.reject`) — the latter two write rich `audit.Entry` rows with `TargetType`, `TargetID`, and `Meta` (party_id, tier). `platformops/service.go:79` writes `admin.flag_set` the same way. So the asymmetry the claim describes is real.
- The audit package doc (recorder.go:1-4) explicitly states the audit trail is the "immutable who-did-what trail required for government accountability and DPDP breach forensics" read by STATE_AUDITOR — confirming the structured trail is the auditor's surface, not slog.
- The generic durable record comes from `AuditMutations` middleware (audit.go:33-38), which sets `Action = "http.POST /api/v1/roles/assignments"`, `Status`, `IP`, `RequestID`, and actor only — no `TargetType`/`TargetID`/`Meta`. Party/role_code/org_unit_id live in the request body and are never captured.
- The auditor query surface (`auditFilter`, repo.go:48-70) filters on `actor_party_id`, `target_type`, `action`, and `ts` range. A role grant is not findable by target_type or a semantic action; it only matches the generic HTTP action string, and even then yields no target party/role/org.

**Adversarial checks that failed to refute:**

- For revoke, the URL path `DELETE /api/v1/roles/assignments/{id}` does embed the assignment_id, so the middleware entry captures *which assignment*. But it still omits which party/role was revoked, and grant (POST) embeds nothing. The reconstruction gap stands.
- No other code path records role grant/revoke to the audit collection (grep of `Audit.Record` across identity is exhaustive).

Severity is appropriately medium: an accountability/forensics gap (granting UNION_PRESIDENT or a rider role is not reconstructable from the auditor surface), not a crash or authz bypass.

Relevant file: `/Users/divyanshmangla/parag-saathi-be/internal/modules/identity/service.go` (lines 914-919 grant, 956-960 revoke).

I have everything needed to reach a verdict.

**Analysis of the claim:**

The claim asserts that OM's lack of an own-unit pin (unlike SAMITI_ADHYAKSH) is a defect that lets an OM provisioned at a district/union node enrol FARMER/CONSUMER across every DCS beneath it, "far beyond the 'own org scope' the blueprint intends." Examining the code, the asymmetry is **deliberate and documented**, and the described behavior is the intended design — not misbehavior.

Concrete evidence refuting it:

1. **The blueprint comment explicitly distinguishes the two roles by scope model.** service.go:830-833 states SAMITI_ADHYAKSH manages "inside their own DCS" while ORGANISING_MANAGER "enrols FARMER/CONSUMER within org scope." And service.go:64-65 says OM "enrols farmers and consumers **within their own org scope (enforced via RequireInScope)**." The subtree behavior via RequireInScope is the *specified* mechanism for OM, not an oversight.

2. **The role definition makes subtree scope correct for OM.** roles.go:24-27 defines OM as the field worker who "promotes and organises **new samitis**" — inherently a multi-DCS/multi-village role. A worker who organises new samitis cannot be pinned to one existing DCS. SAMITI_ADHYAKSH is an *elected chairman of one specific DCS* (roles.go:18), so its exact-unit pin is the special case, added on top of RequireInScope precisely because the subtree model would be wrong for that role.

3. **Seed data confirms the intended provisioning.** cmd/seed/main.go:124 provisions the OM (Kavita Nishad) at `union.ID` — a union node, not a DCS. SAMITI_ADHYAKSH (line 113) is provisioned at `dcs1.ID`. The system is designed and seeded so an OM legitimately operates across a union's whole subtree. The claim's "misbehaving input" (OM at union enrolling across DCS beneath it) is exactly the seeded, intended configuration.

4. **No privilege escalation exists.** The OM is bounded by (a) granterMayGrant limiting it to FARMER/CONSUMER only, and (b) RequireInScope bounding targets to the OM's own provisioned org subtree. It cannot act outside its assigned node's subtree. This is the identical hierarchical scope model applied consistently across the entire codebase (settlement, cattle, logistics, quality, etc.). A role provisioned at a higher node having broader scope is the fundamental, intended property of the org-scope RBAC model, not a bug.

The claim is a design disagreement ("OM *should* be pinned to a leaf/DCS") dressed as a defect. The code faithfully implements the documented blueprint intent, and the asymmetry with SAMITI_ADHYAKSH is deliberate. There is no concrete misbehaving input that violates the specified design — the "exploit" scenario is the seeded, intended behavior.

I have verified all the load-bearing facts. Let me confirm my analysis is complete.

The claim is confirmed real. Here is my verification summary:

**Confirmed facts:**

1. `approveKYC` (service.go:663-746) and `rejectKYC` (751-826) gate ONLY on `domain.CanApproveKYCTier(actor.RoleCode, record.RequestedTier)` at lines 679 and 767. Neither calls `s.deps.Orgs.RequireInScope`.

2. The sibling functions `createAssignment` (line 863) and `revokeAssignment` (line 934) DO call `RequireInScope`, proving org-scope enforcement is the established pattern for privilege-changing operations in this module.

3. `KYCRecord` (party.go:82-103) carries only `PartyID` — no org field — so scope is structurally impossible to enforce from the record alone.

4. `KYCApprovableTiers` (roles.go:159-164) grants `ORGANISING_MANAGER` and `DISTRICT_VERIFIER` approval authority over MINIMAL/FARMER/STANDARD/RIDER tiers.

5. These two roles are org-scoped, not federation-wide: `RequireInScope` (resolver.go:117) auto-passes ONLY `SUPER_ADMIN` and `STATE_AUDITOR`. Everyone else, including these two roles, is constrained to their org subtree by ancestry — confirmed by the fact that `createAssignment` applies `RequireInScope` to them.

6. The route (module.go:64-74) gates approve/reject behind `RequireRoles(...)` which checks role membership only, not scope. The `{id}` comes straight from the URL, so an attacker supplies any pending KYC record id — the scoped `listPendingKYC` does not constrain what id can be POSTed to `/approve`.

7. On approve, `upgradedKYCTier` (line 703) raises the party's `kyc_tier`, which is the gate for `RequiredKYCTier` role issuance (roles.go:107) — a concrete cross-org privilege escalation.

**Concrete misbehaving scenario:** A `DISTRICT_VERIFIER` scoped to District A authenticates, then POSTs `/kyc/{recordID}/approve` where `recordID` belongs to a party enrolled entirely within District B. `RequireRoles` passes (they hold the role), `CanApproveKYCTier("DISTRICT_VERIFIER", "RIDER")` returns true, and the stranger's tier is upgraded to RIDER — with no scope check anywhere in the path. Symmetrically, they can `reject` a stranger's pending KYC in another district (cross-org tampering/denial).

I could not refute the claim.

A village/DCS-scoped ORGANISING_MANAGER or district-scoped DISTRICT_VERIFIER can POST /kyc/{id}/approve for a FARMER/STANDARD/RIDER record belonging to a party in a completely different union/district, upgrading that stranger's kyc_tier and unlocking their roles — a cross-org privilege escalation by the lowest-trust reviewer role. Fix: resolve the subject party's org (via their assignments) and require it in the reviewer's scope before approve/reject.
   Suggested: In approveKYC and rejectKYC, before acting, resolve the subject party's org unit (e.g. from their active role assignments, mirroring how createAssignment/revokeAssignment obtain OrgUnitID) and call s.deps.Orgs.RequireInScope(ctx, actor, subjectOrgID) so a reviewer can only decide KYC for parties within their organisational scope.    approveKYC computes the actor party id (aid, line 665) but never compares it to record.PartyID before calling approveKYCRecord (688); rejectKYC (776) has the same gap. Any party holding an approver role token (ORGANISING_MANAGER / DISTRICT_VERIFIER / PCDF_ADMIN / SUPER_ADMIN) can submit their own /kyc/aadhaar request and then self-approve it — reviewed_by points to themselves, defeating the four-eyes control DPDP/GIGW require for identity verification. Current tier maps limit direct tier gain (every approver already holds >= HIGH while their approvable ceiling is <= HIGH), but this is the only thing preventing escalation: the moment any approver role's RequiredKYCTier drops below its approvable ceiling, self-approval becomes a direct tier escalation. Fix: reject when record.PartyID == aid.
   Suggested: In both approveKYC (after line 672, once record is loaded) and rejectKYC (after line 760), reject self-review: if record.PartyID == aid, return an httpx.Forbidden (e.g. code KYC_SELF_REVIEW, "you may not review your own KYC record"). Place the check before the CanApproveKYCTier gate so self-review is denied regardless of tier. Add a regression test asserting an approver-role actor cannot approve/reject a record whose PartyID equals their own.

   listPendingKYC (621) calls repo.listPendingKYC which filters on status:PENDING only (repo.go:438-457) with no org filter, then enriches each item with pendingPartySummary{Phone, FullName, KYCTier} (638-643). Any of the four reviewer roles — including a single village-level ORGANISING_MANAGER — receives the full contact PII of every party with a pending KYC across the entire platform, not just their own area. The access is audited (kyc.pending_list) but the exposure itself is unbounded. Fix: constrain the pending query to records whose subject party sits within the reviewer's org scope.
   Suggested: Constrain the pending-KYC query to the reviewer's org scope. Pass the actor (and their resolved org-unit scope) into repo.listPendingKYC and add an org/subject-party predicate to the Mongo filter (repo.go:439), or post-filter records via the Orgs scope service (mirroring the RequireInScope enforcement used at service.go:863/934/966) so a scoped ORGANISING_MANAGER/DistrictVerifier only sees pending parties within their area. 179		}
```text
180		return resp, nil
181	}
182	
183	// verifyOTP checks the challenge and logs the phone in, creating the Party
184	// on first login (find-or-create, §4.1).
185	func (s *service) verifyOTP(ctx context.Context, phone, otp string) (*authTokensResponse, error) {
186		now := time.Now().UTC()
187	
188		challenge, err := s.repo.latestOTPChallenge(ctx, phone, now)
189		if err != nil {
190			if isNotFound(err) {
191				s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "otp verify rejected: no active challenge", slog.String("phone", phone))
192				return nil, httpx.Unauthorized("no active OTP for this phone — request a new code")
193			}
194			return nil, err
195		}
196		if challenge.Attempts >= maxOTPAttempts {
197			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "otp verify rejected: too many attempts", slog.String("phone", phone))
198			return nil, httpx.TooManyRequests("too many incorrect OTP attempts — request a new code")
199		}
200		expected := auth.HMACHash(s.deps.Cfg.OTPHashSecret, phone, otp)
201		if !auth.ConstantTimeEqual(challenge.CodeHash, expected) {
202			if err := s.repo.incrementOTPAttempts(ctx, challenge.ID); err != nil {
203				return nil, err
204			}
205			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "otp verify rejected: incorrect code", slog.String("phone", phone))
206			return nil, httpx.Unauthorized("incorrect OTP")
207		}
208	
209		// Burn every outstanding challenge for this phone.
210		if err := s.repo.deleteOTPChallenges(ctx, phone); err != nil {
211			return nil, err
212		}
213	
214		party, err := s.repo.upsertPartyByPhone(ctx, phone, now)
215		if err != nil {
216			return nil, err
217		}
218		if party.Status != domain.PartyStatusActive {
219			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "otp verify rejected: party suspended",
220				slog.String("phone", phone), slog.String("party_id", party.ID.Hex()))
221			return nil, httpx.Forbidden("party is suspended")
222		}
223		tokens, err := s.issueLoginTokens(ctx, party, now)
224		if err != nil {
225			return nil, err
226		}
227		s.log.InfoContext(ctx, "party logged in",
228			slog.String("party_id", party.ID.Hex()), slog.String("phone", phone))
229		return tokens, nil
230	}
231	
232	// issueLoginTokens mints a SESSION access token plus a fresh rotating
233	// refresh token (stored only as an HMAC digest).
234	func (s *service) issueLoginTokens(ctx context.Context, party *domain.Party, now time.Time) (*authTokensResponse, error) {
235		refreshToken, err := auth.RandomToken(32)
236		if err != nil {
237			s.log.ErrorContext(ctx, "refresh token generation failed", slog.Any("err", err))
238			return nil, httpx.Internal(err)
239		}
240		doc := refreshTokenDoc{
241			TokenHash: auth.HMACHash(s.deps.Cfg.OTPHashSecret, refreshHashLabel, refreshToken),
242			PartyID:   party.ID,
243			ExpiresAt: now.Add(s.deps.Cfg.RefreshTokenTTL),
244			CreatedAt: now,
245		}
246		if err := s.repo.insertRefreshToken(ctx, doc); err != nil {
247			return nil, err
248		}
249		accessToken, err := s.deps.JWT.IssueSessionToken(*party)
250		if err != nil {
251			s.log.ErrorContext(ctx, "session token issue failed",
252				slog.String("party_id", party.ID.Hex()), slog.Any("err", err))
253			return nil, httpx.Internal(err)
254		}
255		return &authTokensResponse{
256			AccessToken:  accessToken,
257			RefreshToken: refreshToken,
258			Party:        party,
259		}, nil
260	}
261	
262	// refresh rotates a refresh token: the old token is consumed atomically and
263	// a new pair is issued — a replayed token always fails.
264	func (s *service) refresh(ctx context.Context, refreshToken string) (*authTokensResponse, error) {
265		now := time.Now().UTC()
266		tokenHash := auth.HMACHash(s.deps.Cfg.OTPHashSecret, refreshHashLabel, refreshToken)
267	
268		doc, err := s.repo.findRefreshToken(ctx, tokenHash)
269		if err != nil {
270			if isNotFound(err) {
271				s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "refresh rejected: unknown token")
272				return nil, httpx.Unauthorized("invalid refresh token")
273			}
274			return nil, err
275		}
276		if !now.Before(doc.ExpiresAt) {
277			_, _ = s.repo.deleteRefreshToken(ctx, tokenHash)
278			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "refresh rejected: token expired", slog.String("party_id", doc.PartyID.Hex()))
279			return nil, httpx.Unauthorized("refresh token expired — log in again")
280		}
281	
282		// ROTATE: consume the old token first; DeletedCount==0 means a parallel
283		// request won the race, so this presentation is treated as a replay.
284		deleted, err := s.repo.deleteRefreshToken(ctx, tokenHash)
285		if err != nil {
286			return nil, err
287		}
288		if deleted == 0 {
289			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "refresh rejected: token already used", slog.String("party_id", doc.PartyID.Hex()))
290			return nil, httpx.Unauthorized("refresh token already used")
291		}
292	
293		party, err := s.repo.findPartyByID(ctx, doc.PartyID)
294		if err != nil {
295			if isNotFound(err) {
296				s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "refresh rejected: party gone", slog.String("party_id", doc.PartyID.Hex()))
297				return nil, httpx.Unauthorized("party no longer exists")
298			}
299			return nil, err
300		}
301		if party.Status != domain.PartyStatusActive {
302			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "refresh rejected: party suspended", slog.String("party_id", party.ID.Hex()))
303			return nil, httpx.Forbidden("party is suspended")
304		}
305		return s.issueLoginTokens(ctx, party, now)
306	}
307	
308	// logout revokes one refresh token belonging to the caller. Idempotent.
309	func (s *service) logout(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, refreshToken string) error {
310		aid, err := actorID(actor)
311		if err != nil {
312			return err
313		}
314		tokenHash := auth.HMACHash(s.deps.Cfg.OTPHashSecret, refreshHashLabel, refreshToken)
315		return s.repo.deleteRefreshTokenForParty(ctx, tokenHash, aid)
316	}

320	// listMyRoles returns the actor's currently usable assignments, enriched
321	// with org-unit display fields for the role-switcher UI.
322	func (s *service) listMyRoles(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor) ([]assignmentWithOrg, error) {
323		aid, err := actorID(actor)
324		if err != nil {
325			return nil, err
326		}
327		assignments, err := s.repo.listActiveAssignments(ctx, aid)
328		if err != nil {
329			return nil, err
330		}
331		now := time.Now().UTC()
332		out := make([]assignmentWithOrg, 0, len(assignments))
333		for _, ra := range assignments {
334			if !ra.UsableAt(now) {
335				continue
336			}
337			out = append(out, s.withOrg(ctx, ra))
338		}
339		return out, nil
340	}

342	// withOrg copies org display fields onto an assignment; enrichment is
343	// best-effort (a missing org unit never breaks the listing).
344	func (s *service) withOrg(ctx context.Context, ra domain.RoleAssignment) assignmentWithOrg {
345		enriched := assignmentWithOrg{RoleAssignment: ra}
346		if org, err := s.deps.Orgs.Get(ctx, ra.OrgUnitID); err == nil {
347			enriched.OrgName = org.Name
348			enriched.OrgType = org.Type
349			enriched.OrgCode = org.Code
350		}
351		return enriched
352	}

354	// selectRole exchanges the session for a ROLE-kind token pinned to one
355	// usable assignment, gated on the role's minimum KYC tier (§5.2). With
356	// auto-verify gone, this genuinely blocks un-approved parties.
357	func (s *service) selectRole(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, assignmentID primitive.ObjectID) (*roleSelectResponse, error) {
358		aid, err := actorID(actor)
359		if err != nil {
360			return nil, err
361		}
362		assignment, err := s.repo.findAssignmentByID(ctx, assignmentID)
363		if err != nil {
364			return nil, err
365		}
366		if assignment.PartyID != aid {
367			// Same shape as an unknown ID — never confirm other parties' grants.
368			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "role select rejected: not owner",
369				slog.String("assignment_id", assignmentID.Hex()), slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID))
370			return nil, httpx.NotFound("role assignment")
371		}
372		now := time.Now().UTC()
373		if !assignment.UsableAt(now) {
374			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "role select rejected: assignment not usable",
375				slog.String("assignment_id", assignmentID.Hex()), slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID))
376			return nil, httpx.Forbidden("role assignment is revoked or outside its validity window")
377		}
378	
379		// Re-read the party: the KYC tier may have upgraded since the session
380		// token was minted.
381		party, err := s.repo.findPartyByID(ctx, aid)
382		if err != nil {
383			return nil, err
384		}
385		if party.Status != domain.PartyStatusActive {
386			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "role select rejected: party suspended", slog.String("party_id", party.ID.Hex()))
387			return nil, httpx.Forbidden("party is suspended")
388		}
389		requiredTier := domain.RequiredKYCTier[assignment.RoleCode]
390		if !domain.KYCTierSatisfies(party.KYCTier, requiredTier) {
391			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "role select rejected: kyc tier insufficient",
392				slog.String("party_id", party.ID.Hex()),
393				slog.String("role_code", assignment.RoleCode),
394				slog.String("current_tier", party.KYCTier),
395				slog.String("required_tier", requiredTier))
396			appErr := httpx.Forbidden("your KYC tier does not permit this role — complete verification first").
397				WithDetails(map[string]string{
398					"current_tier":  party.KYCTier,
399					"required_tier": requiredTier,
400				})
401			appErr.Code = "KYC_TIER_INSUFFICIENT"
402			return nil, appErr
403		}
404	
405		org, err := s.deps.Orgs.Get(ctx, assignment.OrgUnitID)
406		if err != nil {
407			return nil, err
408		}
409		accessToken, err := s.deps.JWT.IssueRoleToken(*party, *assignment, org.Type)
410		if err != nil {
411			s.log.ErrorContext(ctx, "role token issue failed",
412				slog.String("assignment_id", assignmentID.Hex()), slog.Any("err", err))
413			return nil, httpx.Internal(err)
414		}
415		s.log.InfoContext(ctx, "role selected",
416			slog.String("party_id", party.ID.Hex()),
417			slog.String("assignment_id", assignmentID.Hex()),
418			slog.String("role_code", assignment.RoleCode),
419			slog.String("org_unit_id", assignment.OrgUnitID.Hex()))
420		return &roleSelectResponse{
421			AccessToken: accessToken,
422			RoleCode:    assignment.RoleCode,
423			OrgUnitID:   assignment.OrgUnitID,
424			OrgType:     org.Type,
425		}, nil
426	}

471	// --- KYC (mock DPI adapters — real UIDAI / penny-drop integration later) ---
472	
473	// verifyAadhaar runs the MOCK Aadhaar eKYC capture (§18-A). The full Aadhaar
474	// number exists only in this request's memory: what is persisted is the
475	// last 4 digits plus an opaque reference from the (mock) Aadhaar Data Vault.
476	//
477	// There is NO auto-verify and NO tier change here: the record is created
478	// PENDING and enters the approval workflow. Returns created=false when an
479	// identical PENDING request already exists (idempotent replay → 200).
480	func (s *service) verifyAadhaar(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, req aadhaarKYCRequest) (*aadhaarKYCResponse, bool, error) {
481		now := time.Now().UTC()
482		aid, err := actorID(actor)
483		if err != nil {
484			return nil, false, err
485		}
486		party, err := s.repo.findPartyByID(ctx, aid)
487		if err != nil {
488			return nil, false, err
489		}
490	
491		// Idempotency: an existing PENDING request for the same tier is returned
492		// as-is rather than duplicated.
493		if existing, err := s.repo.findPendingKYCRecord(ctx, party.ID, req.RequestedTier); err == nil {
494			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "kyc submit replayed idempotently",
495				slog.String("kyc_id", existing.ID.Hex()),
496				slog.String("party_id", party.ID.Hex()),
497				slog.String("requested_tier", req.RequestedTier))
498			return &aadhaarKYCResponse{
499				Record:  existing,
500				Status:  domain.KYCStatusPending,
501				Message: msgAwaitingVerification,
502			}, false, nil
503		} else if !isNotFound(err) {
504			return nil, false, err
505		}
506	
507		language := party.PreferredLanguage
508		if language == "" {
509			language = defaultLanguage
510		}
511		// Pre-generate the consent id so the KYC record can reference it in the
512		// same flow.
513		consentID := primitive.NewObjectID()
514		consent := domain.Consent{
515			ID:          consentID,
516			PartyID:     party.ID,
517			Purpose:     consentPurposeAadhaarEKYC,
518			TextVersion: consentTextVersion,
519			Language:    language,
520			GrantedAt:   now,
521		}
522		if err := s.repo.insertConsent(ctx, consent); err != nil {
523			return nil, false, err
524		}
525	
526		// MOCK Aadhaar Data Vault (§18-A): a real deployment sends the number to
527		// the vault service and receives an opaque token. The mock mints a UUID.
528		vaultRef := uuid.NewString()
529		last4 := req.AadhaarNumber[len(req.AadhaarNumber)-4:]
530	
531		record := domain.KYCRecord{
532			ID:              primitive.NewObjectID(),
533			PartyID:         party.ID,
534			RequestedTier:   req.RequestedTier,
535			AadhaarLast4:    last4,
536			AadhaarVaultRef: vaultRef,
537			ConsentID:       &consentID,
538			Status:          domain.KYCStatusPending,
539			CreatedAt:       now,
540			UpdatedAt:       now,
541		}
542		if err := s.repo.insertKYCRecord(ctx, record); err != nil {
543			return nil, false, err
544		}
545	
546		s.log.InfoContext(ctx, "kyc submitted",
547			slog.String("kyc_id", record.ID.Hex()),
548			slog.String("party_id", party.ID.Hex()),
549			slog.String("requested_tier", req.RequestedTier))
550		return &aadhaarKYCResponse{
551			Record:  &record,
552			Status:  domain.KYCStatusPending,
553			Message: msgAwaitingVerification,
554		}, true, nil
555	}
556	
557	// verifyBank runs the MOCK penny-drop verification and stores ONLY the
558	// masked account tail and IFSC on the caller's latest KYC record (creating a
559	// PENDING record carrying just the bank evidence when none exists yet).
560	func (s *service) verifyBank(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, req bankKYCRequest) (*domain.KYCRecord, error) {
561		now := time.Now().UTC()
562		aid, err := actorID(actor)
563		if err != nil {
564			return nil, err
565		}
566		party, err := s.repo.findPartyByID(ctx, aid)
567		if err != nil {
568			return nil, err
569		}
570		masked := maskAccount(req.AccountNumber)
571	
572		latest, err := s.repo.latestKYCRecord(ctx, aid)
573		switch {
574		case err == nil:
575			// MOCK penny-drop: always verified with a fixed name-match score.
576			rec, err := s.repo.updateKYCRecordBank(ctx, latest.ID, masked, req.IFSC, mockPennyDropNameMatch, now)
577			if err != nil {
578				return nil, err
579			}
580			s.log.InfoContext(ctx, "bank evidence attached",
581				slog.String("kyc_id", rec.ID.Hex()), slog.String("party_id", party.ID.Hex()))
582			return rec, nil
583		case isNotFound(err):
584			record := domain.KYCRecord{
585				ID:                primitive.NewObjectID(),
586				PartyID:           party.ID,
587				RequestedTier:     party.KYCTier,
588				BankAccountMasked: masked,
589				BankIFSC:          req.IFSC,
590				BankVerified:      true, // MOCK penny-drop: always succeeds
591				BankNameMatch:     mockPennyDropNameMatch,
592				Status:            domain.KYCStatusPending,
593				CreatedAt:         now,
594				UpdatedAt:         now,
595			}
596			if err := s.repo.insertKYCRecord(ctx, record); err != nil {
597				return nil, err
598			}
599			s.log.InfoContext(ctx, "bank evidence recorded on new pending kyc",
600				slog.String("kyc_id", record.ID.Hex()), slog.String("party_id", party.ID.Hex()))
601			return &record, nil
602		default:
603			return nil, err
604		}
605	}

610		aid, err := actorID(actor)
```
