38	let refreshToken: string | null = null;
39	
40	export function getAuthToken(): string | null {
41	  return accessToken;
42	}
43	export function getRefreshToken(): string | null {
44	  return refreshToken;
45	}
46	
47	/** Store both tokens (login / refresh rotation). */
48	export function setTokens(t: { access: string | null; refresh: string | null }): void {
49	  accessToken = t.access;
50	  refreshToken = t.refresh;
51	  if (t.access) void AsyncStorage.setItem(ACCESS_KEY, t.access);
52	  else void AsyncStorage.removeItem(ACCESS_KEY);
53	  if (t.refresh) void AsyncStorage.setItem(REFRESH_KEY, t.refresh);
54	  else void AsyncStorage.removeItem(REFRESH_KEY);
55	}
56	
57	/** Swap only the access token (role-select issues a ROLE-kind token). */
58	export function setAccessToken(token: string): void {
59	  accessToken = token;
60	  void AsyncStorage.setItem(ACCESS_KEY, token);
61	}
62	
63	export function clearTokens(): void {
64	  setTokens({ access: null, refresh: null });
65	}
66	
67	/** Call once at startup (root layout) before authenticated requests. */
68	export async function hydrateAuthToken(): Promise<void> {
69	  const [a, r] = await Promise.all([
70	    AsyncStorage.getItem(ACCESS_KEY),
71	    AsyncStorage.getItem(REFRESH_KEY),
72	  ]);
73	  accessToken = a;
74	  refreshToken = r;
75	}
76	
77	/** Registered by the root layout: fired when auth is irrecoverably lost. */
78	let onUnauthorized: (() => void) | null = null;
79	export function setOnUnauthorized(cb: (() => void) | null): void {
80	  onUnauthorized = cb;
81	}
82	
83	export class ApiError extends Error {
84	  constructor(
85	    public status: number,
86	    public code: string,
87	    message: string,
88	    public details?: unknown,
89	  ) {
90	    super(message);
91	    this.name = 'ApiError';
92	  }
93	}
94	
95	type HttpMethod = 'GET' | 'POST' | 'PUT' | 'PATCH' | 'DELETE';
96	
97	export interface EndpointSpec<TIn, TOut> {
98	  method: HttpMethod;
99	  /** REST path for http mode; also documents the backend contract */
100	  path: (input: TIn) => string;
101	  /** camelCase input → snake_case wire body (http mode only) */
102	  mapRequest?: (input: TIn) => unknown;
103	  /** snake_case wire data → domain shape (http mode only) */
104	  mapResponse?: (raw: unknown) => TOut;
105	  /** In-app implementation for mock mode */
106	  mock: (input: TIn, db: MockDb) => TOut | Promise<TOut>;
107	}
108	
109	function sleep(ms: number): Promise<void> {
110	  return new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));
111	}
112	
113	/** JSON-safe deep clone (results are plain data; keeps Hermes compatibility). */
114	function deepClone<T>(value: T): T {
115	  return value === undefined ? value : (JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value)) as T);
116	}
117	
118	/** Raw http call: bearer header, envelope unwrap, AppError mapping. */
119	async function httpCall(method: HttpMethod, path: string, body: unknown): Promise<unknown> {
120	  const hasBody = method !== 'GET' && method !== 'DELETE' && body !== undefined;
121	  const res = await fetch(BASE + path, {
122	    method,
123	    headers: {
124	      Accept: 'application/json',
125	      ...(hasBody ? { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } : {}),
126	      ...(accessToken ? { Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}` } : {}),
127	    },
128	    body: hasBody ? JSON.stringify(body) : undefined,
129	  });
130	  const text = await res.text().catch(() => '');
131	  let json: unknown;
132	  try {
133	    json = text ? JSON.parse(text) : undefined;
134	  } catch {
135	    json = undefined;
136	  }
137	  if (!res.ok) {
138	    const err = (json as { error?: { code?: string; message?: string; details?: unknown } })
139	      ?.error;
140	    throw new ApiError(
141	      res.status,
142	      err?.code ?? `HTTP_${res.status}`,
143	      err?.message ?? res.statusText,
144	      err?.details,
145	    );
146	  }
147	  // Success envelope: { data, meta? } - unwrap data; tolerate bare payloads.
148	  if (json && typeof json === 'object' && 'data' in (json as Record<string, unknown>)) {
149	    return (json as { data: unknown }).data;
150	  }
151	  return json;
152	}
153	
154	/** Single-flight refresh: rotate the token pair via POST /auth/refresh. */
155	let refreshInFlight: Promise<boolean> | null = null;
156	async function tryRefresh(): Promise<boolean> {
157	  if (!refreshToken) return false;
158	  refreshInFlight ??= (async () => {
159	    try {
160	      const data = (await httpCall('POST', '/auth/refresh', {
161	        refresh_token: refreshToken,
162	      })) as { access_token: string; refresh_token: string };
163	      setTokens({ access: data.access_token, refresh: data.refresh_token });
164	      return true;
165	    } catch {
166	      return false;
167	    } finally {
168	      refreshInFlight = null;
169	    }
170	  })();
171	  return refreshInFlight;
172	}
173	
174	/** Declare a typed API endpoint. Returns the callable used by feature code. */
175	export function endpoint<TIn = void, TOut = unknown>(
176	  spec: EndpointSpec<TIn, TOut>,
177	): (input: TIn) => Promise<TOut> {
178	  return async (input: TIn): Promise<TOut> => {
179	    if (MODE === 'mock') {
180	      const { db } = await import('@/core/mocks/db');
181	      // Simulated network latency so loading states are honest
182	      await sleep(120 + Math.random() * 230);
183	      const result = await spec.mock(input, db);
184	      // Deep-clone so callers can never mutate the mock store through results
185	      return deepClone(result);
186	    }
187	
188	    const path = spec.path(input);
189	    const body = spec.mapRequest ? spec.mapRequest(input) : (input as unknown);
190	    try {
191	      const raw = await httpCall(spec.method, path, body);
192	      return spec.mapResponse ? spec.mapResponse(raw) : (raw as TOut);
193	    } catch (e) {
194	      // One refresh + retry on expired access tokens (never for /auth/* itself)
195	      if (e instanceof ApiError && e.status === 401 && !path.startsWith('/auth/')) {
196	        if (await tryRefresh()) {
197	          const raw = await httpCall(spec.method, path, body);
198	          return spec.mapResponse ? spec.mapResponse(raw) : (raw as TOut);
199	        }
200	        clearTokens();
201	        onUnauthorized?.();
202	      }
203	      throw e;
204	    }
205	  };
206	}

1	# Saathi API contract (frontend ↔ backend)
2	
3	The mobile app ships with an in-app mock backend; flipping
4	`EXPO_PUBLIC_API_MODE=http` + `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` points the same typed
5	calls at the real API. **This file is the request-for-implementation for the
6	backend team.** The authoritative, always-current definitions (exact TS
7	request/response types + reference semantics in the `mock` bodies) live in
8	[`src/core/api/endpoints/`](../src/core/api/endpoints/) with the shared domain
9	model in [`src/core/types/domain.ts`](../src/core/types/domain.ts).
10	
11	Conventions (matching the implemented backend): success envelope
12	`{"data": ..., "meta"?}`; error envelope `{"error": {"code", "message", "details"?}}`;
13	snake_case wire fields (the app maps them to its camelCase domain in
14	`mapRequest`/`mapResponse` per endpoint); `Authorization: Bearer <access token>`;
15	rotating refresh tokens via `POST /auth/refresh` (the client auto-refreshes
16	once on 401 and retries); IDs opaque strings; timestamps ISO-8601.
17	
18	## Auth / identity (`auth.ts`) - ✅ aligned with `parag-saathi-be` `internal/modules/identity`
19	| Method & path | Purpose |
20	| --- | --- |
21	| `POST /auth/otp/request` | `{phone}` → `{phone, expires_at, dev_otp?}` (dev_otp only in dev mode) |
22	| `POST /auth/otp/verify` | `{phone, otp}` → `{access_token (SESSION), refresh_token, party}`; find-or-creates the Party on first login (§4.1) |
23	| `GET /parties/me` | → `{party, assignments (+org_name/org_type/org_code), kyc?}` - feeds the role switcher |
24	| `POST /auth/role/select` | `{role_assignment_id}` → `{access_token (ROLE-scoped), role_code, org_unit_id}` |
25	| `POST /auth/refresh` | `{refresh_token}` → rotated token pair (single-flight in the client) |
26	| `POST /auth/logout` | `{refresh_token}` - revoke (called fire-and-forget on sign-out) |
27	| `PATCH /parties/me` | `{full_name?, preferred_language?}` |
28	| `POST /kyc/aadhaar` | `{aadhaar_number, consent, requested_tier}` - number transient, never stored (§18-A) |
29	| `POST /kyc/bank` | `{account_number, ifsc}` - penny-drop; only masked tail persisted |
30	
31	## Real-time & live badges (`events.ts` + `sse.ts`) - ✅ PR #2

33	| --- | --- |
34	| `GET /events/stream` | Server-Sent Events (bearer-auth). The app streams it via XHR (`core/api/sse.ts`); `useLiveSync` invalidates query caches on `kyc.queue_changed`, `settlement.changed`, `quality.changed`, `pour.recorded`. Heartbeats every ~25s |
35	| `GET /kyc/pending/count` | `{count, capped}` - scoped pending-KYC badge for reviewer dashboards |
36	
37	## Org (`org.ts`)

39	| `GET /org-units/:id` | One org unit |
40	
41	## Collections - DCS console (`collections.ts`)
42	| `GET /dcs/:dcsId/members` | Farmer roster + pouredToday |
43	| `GET /pours?dcsId&farmerPartyId&date&shift` | Pour list |
44	| `POST /pours` | Record a pour; server computes rate from the two-axis chart, enforces §8.2 plausibility bounds (`422 IMPLAUSIBLE_READING`), and upserts the same-day DRAFT invoice (§8.1) |
45	| `POST /pours/ocr-extract` | Photo-OCR bridge: analyzer-screen photo → `{fatPct, snfPct, confidence}` (§8.2) |
46	| `GET /lots?dcsId&date&status` · `GET /lots/:id` | Consignment lots |
47	| `POST /lots` | Pool the shift's RECORDED pours into an OPEN lot |
48	| `POST /lots/:id/dispatch` | OPEN → DISPATCHED; attaches to today's route stop |

50	## Payments (`payments.ts`) - §8.1 / §18-B

97	| `GET /admin/feature-flags` · `PUT /admin/feature-flags/:key` | Capability gating (collar dormant path, §3.6/§9) |
98	| `GET /admin/audit-events?limit` | Append-only audit trail |

```text
I now have the complete picture across both codebases. Here is the detailed structured report.

---

# Saathi Auth + Multi-Role Login Flow — FE ⇄ BE Alignment Report

Scope: `parag-saathi-fe` (React Native/Expo, `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_MODE` defaults to `http` → real backend at `…/api/v1`) vs `parag-saathi-be` `internal/modules/identity`. All wire shapes are the snake_case JSON the Go backend serialises, wrapped in the standard envelope.

## Envelope (both confirmed to match)
- Success: `{ "data": <payload>, "meta"?: {...} }` — `httpx.JSON`/`JSONMeta` (`respond.go:21`). FE unwraps `.data` in `client.ts:148`.
- Error: `{ "error": { "code": "...", "message": "...", "details"?: {...} } }` — `errEnvelope` + `AppError` json tags `code`/`message`/`details` (`errors.go:12`). FE maps to `ApiError(status, code, message, details)` (`client.ts:137`).
- Auth: `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`. A 401 on a non-`/auth/*` path triggers one single-flight `POST /auth/refresh` + retry (`client.ts:195`).

---

## 1. THE LOGIN FLOW

It is a **two-call** flow. `verify` does NOT return assignments; the app then calls `GET /parties/me`.

**Step A — `POST /auth/otp/request`**
Request `{ "phone": "9876543210" }` → Response (`otpRequestResponse`, models.go:47):
```json
{ "data": { "phone": "9876543210", "expires_at": "2026-07-09T12:05:00Z", "dev_otp": "483920" } }
```
`dev_otp` present ONLY when `cfg.OTPDevMode` on. FE maps to `{ otpSent, expiresAt, devHint }` (`auth.ts:115`).

**Step B — `POST /auth/otp/verify`**
Request `{ "phone": "9876543210", "otp": "483920" }` → Response (`authTokensResponse`, models.go:71):
```json
{ "data": {
  "access_token": "<JWT kind=session>",
  "refresh_token": "<opaque>",
  "party": { "id":"...", "phone":"9876543210", "full_name":"Ramesh Yadav",
             "preferred_language":"hi", "kyc_tier":"HIGH", "status":"ACTIVE",
             "created_at":"...", "updated_at":"..." }
} }
```
Returns tokens + party only — **no assignments, no role picker data**. The SESSION JWT claims (`jwt.go:26`) carry `pid/phn/kyc/knd=session` but NOT role/org.

**Step C — `GET /parties/me`** (with the SESSION token; `RequireSession` allows session or role tokens, rbac.go:45). Returns party + usable assignments + KYC (see §3).

**Decision logic** (`app/login.tsx:69-77`): the mutation chains `verifyOtp → setTokens → fetchMe`, and on the resulting `Session`:
- `session.assignments.length === 1` → `activateRole(assignments[0].id)` (calls `/auth/role/select`) then `router.replace(roleHomePath(...))` → straight to dashboard.
- otherwise (`>1` **or `0`**) → `router.replace('/select-role')`.

So the picker is shown whenever there is **not exactly one** assignment. `RoleGate`/`app/index.tsx` enforce the same: no session → `/login`; session but no active role → `/select-role`. The backend `listMyRoles` filters assignments to `UsableAt(now)` (ACTIVE + inside validity window) — but does NOT filter by KYC tier, so the count driving the picker is the count of active assignments.

---

## 2. ROLE SELECT — `POST /auth/role/select`

Requires an authenticated session/role token (mounted under `/auth` group with `RequireSession`).

Request (`roleSelectRequest`, models.go:112) — FE `mapRequest` at `auth.ts:210` sends:
```json
{ "role_assignment_id": "<ObjectID hex>" }
```
Response (`roleSelectResponse`, models.go:124):
```json
{ "data": { "access_token":"<JWT kind=role>", "role_code":"SAMITI_SACHEEV",
            "org_unit_id":"<hex>", "org_type":"DCS" } }
```
FE reads `access_token`, `role_code`, `org_unit_id` (ignores `org_type`) and calls `setAccessToken(...)` — swaps ONLY the access token to the ROLE-kind JWT (`store.ts:45-49`). The ROLE JWT adds claims `rid/rol/org/ogt`.

Service gates before issuing (`service.go:358`): ownership (assignment.PartyID == actor) else `404 NOT_FOUND`; `UsableAt` else `403 FORBIDDEN`; party active; and **KYC tier** — `403` with `code:"KYC_TIER_INSUFFICIENT"` + `details:{current_tier, required_tier}` if `party.KYCTier` doesn't satisfy `RequiredKYCTier[role]`.

**Org fields the app needs per assignment**: the picker needs `org_name` (rendered as the tile subtitle). It also consumes `org_type` and `org_code` to build the `OrgUnit` (`orgFromAssignment`, auth.ts:84) but only `name` is displayed. These come from `/parties/me` assignment enrichment (§3), not from role/select.

---

## 3. `GET /parties/me` WIRE SHAPE

`meResponse` (models.go:144), enriched. Example for Ramesh (multi-role):
```json
{ "data": {
  "party": { "id":"...", "phone":"9876543210", "full_name":"Ramesh Yadav",
             "preferred_language":"hi", "kyc_tier":"HIGH", "status":"ACTIVE",
             "created_at":"...", "updated_at":"..." },
  "assignments": [
    { "id":"<hex A>", "party_id":"...", "role_code":"FARMER",
      "org_unit_id":"<semari hex>", "valid_from":"...", "valid_to":null,
      "status":"ACTIVE", "granted_by":"...", "created_at":"...",
      "org_name":"Semari Dairy Cooperative Society", "org_type":"DCS", "org_code":"DCS-BBK-0142" },
    { "id":"<hex B>", "party_id":"...", "role_code":"SAMITI_SACHEEV",
      "org_unit_id":"<semari hex>", "valid_from":"...", "valid_to":null,
      "status":"ACTIVE", "granted_by":"...", "created_at":"...",
      "org_name":"Semari Dairy Cooperative Society", "org_type":"DCS", "org_code":"DCS-BBK-0142" }
  ],
  "kyc": { "requested_tier":"HIGH", "status":"VERIFIED", "aadhaar_last4":"3210",
           "bank_account_masked":"****3210", "bank_ifsc":"SBIN0001234",
           "bank_verified":true, "verified_at":"..." }
} }
```
- **Party fields**: `id, phone, full_name?, preferred_language?, kyc_tier, status, created_at, updated_at`. FE `mapParty` (auth.ts:60) reads `full_name, phone, kyc_tier, created_at` + derives `aadhaarMasked`/`bankVerified` from `kyc`.
- **assignments[]** — each is `assignmentWithOrg` = full `domain.RoleAssignment` (`id, party_id, role_code, org_unit_id, granted_by?, valid_from, valid_to?, status, revoked_at?, revoked_by?, created_at`) + enrichment `org_name?, org_type?, org_code?` (models.go:101, `withOrg` service.go:345, best-effort — omitted if org lookup fails). FE `mapAssignment` maps `role_code→role`, `status==='ACTIVE'→active` (auth.ts:72). FE dedupes `orgUnits[]` from the enrichment.
- **kyc summary** (`kycSummary`, models.go:131): `requested_tier, status, aadhaar_last4?, bank_account_masked?, bank_ifsc?, bank_verified, verified_at?`. Omitted entirely if no KYC record.

---

## 4. MULTI-ROLE (farmer + sachiv)

**FE representation**: `Session = { party, assignments: RoleAssignment[], orgUnits: OrgUnit[] }` (domain.ts:67). A party with 2 roles = 2 entries in `assignments`, each a distinct `{ id, role, orgUnitId, active }`. Seed proof: Ramesh `9876543210` = `p_ramesh`, HIGH tier, with `mkAsg('p_ramesh','FARMER','org_dcs_semari')` + `mkAsg('p_ramesh','SAMITI_SACHEEV','org_dcs_semari')` (db.ts:517-518) — both ACTIVE, same DCS.

**Picker render** (`app/select-role.tsx:45-87`): maps `session.assignments`, and per assignment:
- `const meta = ROLES[a.role]` → tile icon + `meta.label`/`meta.labelHi`.
- `session.orgUnits.find(o => o.id === a.orgUnitId)` → subtitle `org.name`/`org.nameHi`.
- Two tiles ("Farmer" and "Sachiv"), both subtitled "Semari…", keyed by `a.id`.

**Switching**: tap → `activateRole(a.id)` → `POST /auth/role/select {role_assignment_id: a.id}` → new ROLE token via `setAccessToken`, `activeAssignmentId` persisted to AsyncStorage → `router.replace(roleHomePath(a))`. To re-switch, the user returns to `/select-role` and picks the other assignment; a fresh role/select mints a new ROLE token that overwrites the previous one. `useActiveRole`/`useActiveOrgUnit` (store.ts:74-86) resolve the active assignment/org from `activeAssignmentId`.

**What the backend MUST return for this to work**:
1. `/parties/me` returns **all** usable assignments (it does — `listMyRoles`), each with a **stable distinct `id`** (used as `role_assignment_id`) and **distinct `role_code`**.
2. Each assignment carries **org enrichment** (`org_name` at minimum) so the picker subtitle renders without a second call.
3. `/auth/role/select` accepts any of those `id`s and returns a role-scoped `access_token`.
4. **`role_code` values must be in the FE `ROLES` map** — see §6 (crash risk).

---

## 5. KYC WIRE SHAPES

**`POST /kyc/aadhaar`** (self-service, RequireSession). Request (`aadhaarKYCRequest`, models.go:178) — FE sends `{ aadhaar_number, consent, requested_tier }` (auth.ts:268). `requested_tier` ∈ `FARMER|STANDARD|RIDER|HIGH`. Response (`aadhaarKYCResponse`, models.go:199), **201 on new / 200 on idempotent replay**:
```json
{ "data": { "record": { …domain.KYCRecord, "status":"PENDING", "requested_tier":"FARMER", "aadhaar_last4":"3210" },
            "status":"PENDING", "message":"awaiting verification" } }
```
No auto-verify, no tier change.

**`POST /kyc/bank`** (RequireSession). Request `{ account_number, ifsc }` (auth.ts:303). Response = full `domain.KYCRecord` (models.go, `verifyBank` service.go:574) with `bank_account_masked`, `bank_ifsc`, `bank_verified:true`, `bank_name_match:0.92`, `status:"PENDING"`.

**`GET /kyc/pending/count`** (reviewer roles only: `ORGANISING_MANAGER, DISTRICT_VERIFIER, PCDF_ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN`). Response (`pendingKYCCountResponse`, models.go:252): `{ "data": { "count": 7, "capped": false } }`. FE `events.ts:14` maps to `{ count, capped }`; live badge re-fetched on the `kyc.pending.changed` SSE nudge. Related: `GET /kyc/pending` (list), `GET /kyc/me`, `POST /kyc/{id}/approve`, `POST /kyc/{id}/reject` also exist.

---

## 6. GAPS / MISMATCHES vs the current backend identity module

### A. CRITICAL — role-picker crash on backend-only role codes
`app/select-role.tsx:46-47` does `const meta = ROLES[a.role]; const Icon = meta.icon;` with **no null guard**. The FE `ROLE_CODES` (roles.ts:33) and backend `domain.AllRoles` (roles.go:64) diverge:
- **Backend-only roles** (can be returned in `/parties/me.assignments[].role_code`, absent from FE `ROLES`): **`ORGANISING_MANAGER`**, **`CONSUMER`**. If either is assigned to a multi-role party, the picker throws `Cannot read property 'icon' of undefined` and the tree unmounts. (`roleHomePath` is guarded with `?.`, but the picker is not.)
- **FE-only roles** (in FE `ROLES`, NOT grantable by backend — `createAssignmentRequest.validate` returns `INVALID_ROLE`): **`ONBOARDING_EXECUTIVE`**, **`STORE_MANAGER`**. The FE mock seeds these (`p_onboard`, `p_store`), and whole FE modules (`/onboarding`, `/store`) target them, but the real backend cannot create or issue tokens for them.
  → Backend must either add `ORGANISING_MANAGER`/`CONSUMER` to the FE role catalog (or the FE must guard), and add `ONBOARDING_EXECUTIVE`/`STORE_MANAGER` to `AllRoles` + `RequiredKYCTier` if those modules ship.

### B. `POST /kyc/aadhaar` response shape mismatch
FE `submitAadhaarKyc.mapResponse` reads `(raw).kyc_tier` and returns `{ kycTier }` (auth.ts:273). Backend returns `{ record, status, message }` with **no `kyc_tier` field** and **no tier upgrade** (record is PENDING pending review). Result: FE gets `kycTier: undefined`. The FE mock also optimistically sets `party.kycTier = requested_tier` immediately — the real backend never does. Any FE UI that assumes "Aadhaar submitted ⇒ tier upgraded" is wrong against the real backend (the tier only changes after a reviewer approves).

### C. KYC summary field name: `tier` vs `requested_tier`
FE `WireKycSummary` declares `tier: string` (auth.ts:52); backend `kycSummary` serialises `requested_tier` (models.go:133). Currently harmless (FE mapping only reads `aadhaar_last4`/`bank_verified`, both of which match), but the declared contract is misaligned — if FE later reads `kyc.tier` it will be `undefined`.

### D. OrgUnit `type` enum mismatch
Backend `domain.OrgUnit.Type` values are `FEDERATION, MILK_UNION, PROCESSING_PLANT, BMC, DCS` (orgunit.go:11). FE `OrgUnitType` expects `FEDERATION, UNION, DCS, BMC, PLANT, STORE, DISTRICT` (domain.ts:7). So `org_type` arriving as `MILK_UNION`/`PROCESSING_PLANT` is not a valid FE `OrgUnitType`, and FE has `UNION`/`PLANT`/`STORE`/`DISTRICT` that the backend never emits (no STORE org type exists backend-side at all). Low blast radius today (picker shows `org_name`, not type), but any type-driven FE logic breaks. `orgFromAssignment` also defaults `type` to `'DCS'` when `org_name` is present but `org_type` empty.

### E. Missing routes the FE calls (onboarding flow has no backend)
All in `onboarding.ts`, marked `// TODO(backend)`, mock-only — the identity module implements NONE:
- `POST /onboarding/requests`, `GET /onboarding/requests?submitted_by=…`, `GET /onboarding/requests?status=PENDING`, `POST /onboarding/requests/{id}/approve`, `POST /onboarding/requests/{id}/reject` — the assisted-onboarding verification queue.
- `GET /parties?role=SAMITI_SACHEEV` (`listSachivs`) — backend exposes only `GET /parties/me`, no party-by-role listing.
The backend’s nearest primitive is `POST /roles/assignments` (direct grant, no PENDING queue) + `GET /roles/assignments?org_unit_id=…`. The whole onboarding→admin-approval UX (`ONBOARDING_EXECUTIVE`) is unbacked.

### F. Behavioral divergence — brand-new number is a dead-end on the real backend
FE mock `verifyOtp` throws `404 NOT_REGISTERED` for an unknown phone (auth.ts:154). The real backend `verifyOTP` **find-or-creates** the party (`upsertPartyByPhone`, service.go:215) → new party with **0 assignments** → `getMe` returns `assignments: []` → `login.tsx` (`length !== 1`) routes to `/select-role`, which renders an **empty grid with no logout/exit** (`select-role.tsx` only early-returns for `length === 1`). New users get stuck. FE either needs an empty-state on `/select-role`, or the backend needs a "not registered / no roles" signal.

### G. Picker can show roles that then fail `role/select` silently
`listMyRoles`/`getMe` filter by `UsableAt` only (no KYC gate), but `selectRole` enforces the KYC tier. A tile for a role whose `RequiredKYCTier` the party doesn't hold will render, and tapping it returns `403 KYC_TIER_INSUFFICIENT` — which `select-role.tsx:60` swallows (`catch { setSelecting(null) }`) with **no user-facing error**. (Not hit by the seed since Ramesh is HIGH, but real data can trigger it.) Same silent-failure applies to the single-role auto-enter path in `login.tsx:72`, where a thrown `activateRole` is unhandled.

### H. Error-code expectations differ (login path)
FE mock uses `INVALID_OTP`/`NOT_REGISTERED`; the real backend returns generic `code:"UNAUTHORIZED"` (401) for wrong/expired OTP and `no active OTP` (service.go:193-207), and `429 TOO_MANY_REQUESTS` after `maxOTPAttempts=5`. FE only renders `ApiError.message` on the OTP screen, so text still shows, but any FE logic keyed on specific codes (there is none today on this screen) would miss. `role/select` special codes the FE does not branch on: `KYC_TIER_INSUFFICIENT`, and generic `FORBIDDEN`/`NOT_FOUND`.

### Things that DO line up (no action needed)
`/auth/otp/request`, `/auth/otp/verify`, `/auth/refresh` (rotation handled in `client.ts:156`), `/auth/logout` (`{refresh_token}` → `{logged_out:true}`; `RequireSession` accepts the ROLE token so revoke works), `GET /parties/me` core shape, `PATCH /parties/me` (`{full_name, preferred_language}` → Party), `POST /auth/role/select` core shape, `POST /kyc/bank`, `GET /kyc/pending/count`, and both success/error envelopes.

148		h, okH := kycRank[have]

152		}

154	}

44	// PricePour computes (ratePerLitre, amount) for a pour, rounded to paise.
45	func (rc RateChart) PricePour(fatPct, snfPct, qtyLitres float64) (rate, amount float64) {
46		rate = rc.BaseRatePerLitre + fatPct*rc.FatRatePerPoint + snfPct*rc.SNFRatePerPoint
47		rate = math.Round(rate*100) / 100

94	// CheckPlausibility validates fat/SNF/qty against physical bounds and returns

97		var flags []string

104		}
105		return flags

1	package domain
2	
3	import (
4		"time"
5	
6		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson/primitive"
7	)
8	
9	// Org-unit types — the cooperative backbone RBAC is scoped to (blueprint §5.1,
10	// PCDF constitution: Samiti/DCS → Sangh/Union → PCDF apex).
11	const (
12		OrgTypeFederation      = "FEDERATION"       // PCDF / Parag (state apex)
13		OrgTypeMilkUnion       = "MILK_UNION"       // district Sangh
14		OrgTypeProcessingPlant = "PROCESSING_PLANT" // PCDF plant
15		OrgTypeBMC             = "BMC"              // bulk milk cooler / chilling centre
16		OrgTypeDCS             = "DCS"              // village samiti
17	)
18	
19	// AllOrgTypes is the closed set of org-unit types.
20	var AllOrgTypes = []string{
21		OrgTypeFederation, OrgTypeMilkUnion, OrgTypeProcessingPlant, OrgTypeBMC, OrgTypeDCS,
22	}
23	
24	// ValidOrgParent encodes the allowed hierarchy edges.
25	var ValidOrgParent = map[string][]string{
26		OrgTypeFederation:      {}, // root
27		OrgTypeMilkUnion:       {OrgTypeFederation},
28		OrgTypeProcessingPlant: {OrgTypeMilkUnion, OrgTypeFederation},
29		OrgTypeBMC:             {OrgTypeMilkUnion},
30		OrgTypeDCS:             {OrgTypeMilkUnion, OrgTypeBMC},
31	}
32	
33	// OrgUnit is a node in the cooperative hierarchy.
34	//
35	// ID scheme: `_id` is a generated ObjectID (relations always reference it);
36	// Code is the human-readable unique business key (e.g. "DCS-01842") used for
37	// display, lookups and seed idempotency — never for joins.
38	//
39	// Path holds the ObjectIDs of all ancestors from the root down to (and
40	// excluding) this node — denormalised so "is X inside Y's scope" is a single
41	// indexed array-containment check with no recursive queries on the hot path.
42	type OrgUnit struct {
43		ID        primitive.ObjectID   `bson:"_id,omitempty" json:"id"`
44		Type      string               `bson:"type"          json:"type"`
45		Name      string               `bson:"name"          json:"name"`
46		Code      string               `bson:"code"          json:"code"` // unique business key, e.g. "DCS-01842"
47		ParentID  *primitive.ObjectID  `bson:"parent_id,omitempty" json:"parent_id,omitempty"`
48		Path      []primitive.ObjectID `bson:"path"          json:"path"`
49		District  string               `bson:"district,omitempty" json:"district,omitempty"`
50		State     string               `bson:"state,omitempty"    json:"state,omitempty"`
51		GeoLat    float64              `bson:"geo_lat,omitempty"  json:"geo_lat,omitempty"`
52		GeoLng    float64              `bson:"geo_lng,omitempty"  json:"geo_lng,omitempty"`
53		Active    bool                 `bson:"active"        json:"active"`
54		CreatedAt time.Time            `bson:"created_at"    json:"created_at"`
55		UpdatedAt time.Time            `bson:"updated_at"    json:"updated_at"`
56	}
57	
58	// IsValidOrgType reports whether t is a known org-unit type.
59	func IsValidOrgType(t string) bool {
60		for _, v := range AllOrgTypes {
61			if v == t {
62				return true
63			}
64		}
65		return false
66	}
67

22		ID                  primitive.ObjectID   `bson:"_id,omitempty" json:"id"`

25		Shift               string               `bson:"shift"   json:"shift"`

10	// FSSAI limits for liquid milk (blueprint §8.3). Aflatoxin M1 is heat-stable
11	// and survives pasteurisation, so it MUST be gated upstream (BMC + plant),
12	// never only at the finished product.
13	const (
14		FSSAIAflatoxinM1MaxMicrogramPerKg = 0.5  // AFM1 ≤ 0.5 µg/kg
15		FSSAIColiformMaxCFUPerMl          = 10.0 // coliform ≤ 10 CFU/ml
16		FSSAITetracyclineMaxMgPerKg       = 0.1  // antibiotic MRL example
17	)
18

20	const (
21		TestAflatoxinM1 = "AFLATOXIN_M1"            // µg/kg
22		TestColiform    = "COLIFORM"                // CFU/ml
23		TestTPC         = "TPC"                     // CFU/ml, graded — recorded, not hard-gated here
24		TestAntibiotic  = "ANTIBIOTIC_TETRACYCLINE" // mg/kg
25		TestPhosphatase = "PHOSPHATASE"             // 0 = negative (pass post-pasteurisation), 1 = positive
26		TestFat         = "FAT"                     // %
27		TestSNF         = "SNF"                     // %
28	)
29	
30	// QC stages.
31	const (
32		QCStageBMCRapid = "BMC_RAPID" // strip/rapid tests at the chilling centre
33		QCStagePlantLab = "PLANT_LAB" // full lab: ELISA/HPLC, culture, LC-MS/MS
34	)
35	
36	// QC subject types.
37	const (
38		QCSubjectDCSConsignment  = "DCS_CONSIGNMENT"
39		QCSubjectBMCLot          = "BMC_LOT"
40		QCSubjectProcessingBatch = "PROCESSING_BATCH"
41	)
42	
43	// QCTest is a single measurement inside a QC result.
44	type QCTest struct {
45		Name  string  `bson:"name"  json:"name"`
46		Value float64 `bson:"value" json:"value"`
47		Unit  string  `bson:"unit"  json:"unit"`
48		Pass  bool    `bson:"pass"  json:"pass"`
49	}
50	
51	// QCResult is the recorded outcome of testing one subject at one stage.
52	// OverallPass drives the safety gate; a certificate is attached to provenance
53	// on pass, a block + quarantine on fail.
54	type QCResult struct {
55		ID                primitive.ObjectID `bson:"_id,omitempty" json:"id"`
56		SubjectType       string             `bson:"subject_type"  json:"subject_type"`
57		SubjectID         primitive.ObjectID `bson:"subject_id"    json:"subject_id"`
58		Stage             string             `bson:"stage"         json:"stage"`
59		Tests             []QCTest           `bson:"tests"         json:"tests"`
60		OverallPass       bool               `bson:"overall_pass"  json:"overall_pass"`
61		FailureReasons    []string           `bson:"failure_reasons,omitempty" json:"failure_reasons,omitempty"`
62		AnalystPartyID    primitive.ObjectID `bson:"analyst_party_id" json:"analyst_party_id"`
63		LabRef            string             `bson:"lab_ref,omitempty"            json:"lab_ref,omitempty"`
64		CertificateNumber string             `bson:"certificate_number,omitempty" json:"certificate_number,omitempty"`
65		// Superseded marks a result voided after losing the gate race — the
66		// verdict on the subject came from a different, earlier result.
67		Superseded    bool      `bson:"superseded,omitempty" json:"superseded,omitempty"`
68		RecordedAt    time.Time `bson:"recorded_at"   json:"recorded_at"`
69		ProvenanceSeq int64     `bson:"provenance_seq,omitempty" json:"provenance_seq,omitempty"`
70	}
71	
72	// EvaluateQCTests applies the FSSAI gate to a set of tests: it fills each
73	// test's Pass verdict and returns the overall verdict plus human-readable
74	// failure reasons. Unknown test names are recorded but do not gate.
75	func EvaluateQCTests(tests []QCTest) (overallPass bool, failures []string, evaluated []QCTest) {
76		overallPass = true
77		evaluated = make([]QCTest, 0, len(tests))
78		for _, t := range tests {
79			pass := true
80			switch t.Name {
81			case TestAflatoxinM1:
82				if t.Value > FSSAIAflatoxinM1MaxMicrogramPerKg {
83					pass = false
84					failures = append(failures, fmt.Sprintf(
85						"AFLATOXIN_M1 %.3f µg/kg exceeds FSSAI limit %.1f µg/kg", t.Value, FSSAIAflatoxinM1MaxMicrogramPerKg))
86				}
87			case TestColiform:
88				if t.Value > FSSAIColiformMaxCFUPerMl {
89					pass = false
90					failures = append(failures, fmt.Sprintf(
91						"COLIFORM %.1f CFU/ml exceeds FSSAI limit %.0f CFU/ml", t.Value, FSSAIColiformMaxCFUPerMl))
92				}
93			case TestAntibiotic:
94				if t.Value > FSSAITetracyclineMaxMgPerKg {
95					pass = false
96					failures = append(failures, fmt.Sprintf(
97						"ANTIBIOTIC_TETRACYCLINE %.3f mg/kg exceeds MRL %.1f mg/kg", t.Value, FSSAITetracyclineMaxMgPerKg))
98				}
99			case TestPhosphatase:
100				if t.Value != 0 {
101					pass = false
102					failures = append(failures, "PHOSPHATASE positive — pasteurisation check failed (must be negative)")
103				}
104			}
105			t.Pass = pass
106			if !pass {
107				overallPass = false
108			}
109			evaluated = append(evaluated, t)
110		}
111		return overallPass, failures, evaluated
112	}
113

# Identity Module Audit — `parag-saathi-be`

## Global response envelope (applies to EVERY route)

All handlers respond through `httpx.JSON` / `httpx.JSONMeta` (`internal/platform/httpx/respond.go`), which wrap the DTO in a uniform envelope. The frontend never sees the raw DTO at the top level:

- Success (single object): `{ "data": <DTO> }`
- Success (list): `{ "data": [<DTO>...], "meta": { "limit": <int64>, "offset": <int64>, "total": <int64> } }`
- Error: `{ "error": { ...AppError } }`

Every JSON field name below is the real `json:"..."` tag. Every route is under `/api/v1` (confirmed: `internal/httpapi/modules.go:33` calls `identity.Register(api, d)` where `api` is the `/api/v1` chi subtree; `router.go:65`).

---

## 1. Every registered route (method + full path + middleware + DTOs)

Source: `internal/modules/identity/module.go`.

### `/auth` group

| GET | `/api/v1/auth/roles` | listMyRoles | Authenticate + RequireSession |

### Per-route request/response DTOs (exact JSON)

**POST /auth/otp/request** — `otpRequestRequest` → `otpRequestResponse`
- Req: `phone`
- Resp: `phone`, `expires_at`, `dev_otp` (omitempty; present only when `OTPDevMode` on)

**POST /auth/otp/verify** — `otpVerifyRequest` → `authTokensResponse` (see §2)
- Req: `phone`, `otp`

**POST /auth/refresh** — `refreshRequest` → `authTokensResponse`
- Req: `refresh_token`
- Resp: `access_token`, `refresh_token`, `party`

**POST /auth/logout** — `logoutRequest` → `{ "logged_out": true }` (a `map[string]bool`, still enveloped as `data`)
- Req: `refresh_token`

**GET /auth/roles** — no body → `[]assignmentWithOrg` (see §3)

**POST /auth/role/select** — `roleSelectRequest` → `roleSelectResponse` (see §4)

**GET /parties/me** — no body → `meResponse` (see §5)

**PATCH /parties/me** — `patchMeRequest` → `domain.Party`

- Req: `aadhaar_number` (12 digits), `consent` (bool, must be true), `requested_tier` (`FARMER|STANDARD|RIDER|HIGH`)
- Resp: `record` (full `domain.KYCRecord`), `status`, `message`

**POST /kyc/bank** — `bankKYCRequest` → `domain.KYCRecord`; **200**

- Req: `reason` (1–500 chars, required)

- Resp: full `domain.RoleAssignment`

**DELETE /roles/assignments/{id}** — no body → `domain.RoleAssignment` (the revoked record); **200**

**GET /roles/assignments** — query `org_unit_id` (required), `role_code` (optional), `limit`, `offset` → `[]domain.RoleAssignment` + `meta`

---

## 2. What POST /auth/otp/verify returns exactly

Returns `authTokensResponse` (`models.go:71-75`), enveloped as `data`. **Tokens + party only. No assignments, no KYC.**

```
{ "data": {
    "access_token":  string,        // SESSION-kind JWT
    "refresh_token": string,        // opaque rotating token
    "party":         domain.Party   // full party object
}}
```

`party` is the full `domain.Party`: `id`, `phone`, `full_name` (omitempty), `preferred_language` (omitempty), `kyc_tier`, `status`, `created_at`, `updated_at`.

Note: the access token here is SESSION kind (`IssueSessionToken`, `jwt.go:51`) — it carries only `pid`/`phn`/`kyc`/`knd`; no role/org claims. The client must call `/auth/roles` then `/auth/role/select` to get a ROLE token. `/auth/refresh` returns the identical `authTokensResponse` shape.

---

## 3. What GET /auth/roles returns

Returns a bare JSON array `[]assignmentWithOrg` (`service.go:323`, `models.go:103-108`), enveloped as `data` (no `meta` — not paginated). Only assignments that are `UsableAt(now)` are included (active status + inside validity window).

`assignmentWithOrg` embeds the whole `domain.RoleAssignment` inline (Go struct embedding → fields are flattened, not nested) plus three org enrichment fields:

```
{ "data": [ {
    // --- embedded domain.RoleAssignment (flattened) ---
    "id":          ObjectID,
    "party_id":    ObjectID,
    "role_code":   string,
    "org_unit_id": ObjectID,
    "granted_by":  ObjectID,   // omitempty ptr
    "valid_from":  time,
    "valid_to":    time,       // omitempty ptr (nil = open-ended)
    "status":      string,     // ACTIVE | REVOKED
    "revoked_at":  time,       // omitempty ptr
    "revoked_by":  ObjectID,   // omitempty ptr
    "created_at":  time,
    // --- org enrichment (best-effort; omitempty) ---
    "org_name":    string,     // omitempty
    "org_type":    string,     // omitempty
    "org_code":    string      // omitempty
} ] }
```

Org enrichment is best-effort via `s.deps.Orgs.Get` (`withOrg`, `service.go:345`) — if the org lookup fails, the three `org_*` fields are simply omitted; the assignment still lists. Yes, it includes **org_name, org_type, org_code**.

---

## 4. What POST /auth/role/select returns

Returns `roleSelectResponse` (`models.go:124-129`), enveloped as `data`. It includes **role_code, org_unit_id, org_type, and the token** — but NOT `role_assignment_id` in the body (that lives inside the JWT claim `rid`).

```
{ "data": {
    "access_token": string,     // ROLE-kind JWT (IssueRoleToken)
    "role_code":    string,
    "org_unit_id":  ObjectID,
    "org_type":     string
}}
```

The ROLE JWT itself (`jwt.go:61`) carries claims `pid, phn, kyc, knd="role", rid` (role_assignment_id), `rol` (role_code), `org` (org_unit_id), `ogt` (org_type).

Validation gates before issuing (`selectRole`, `service.go:358-427`):
1. Assignment must exist and `assignment.PartyID == actor.PartyID` — else returns `404 NotFound("role assignment")` (deliberately same shape as unknown ID; never confirms other parties' grants).
2. `assignment.UsableAt(now)` — else `403 Forbidden` "revoked or outside validity window".
3. Party re-read; must be `ACTIVE` — else `403`.
4. `KYCTierSatisfies(party.KYCTier, RequiredKYCTier[role_code])` — else `403` with `Code = "KYC_TIER_INSUFFICIENT"` and details `{ current_tier, required_tier }`.

---

## 5. What GET /parties/me returns

Returns `meResponse` (`models.go:144-148`, `service.go:433`), enveloped as `data`. **Party + assignments + kyc (optional).**

```
{ "data": {
    "party":       domain.Party,          // full party
    "assignments": []assignmentWithOrg,   // same shape as §3 (usable only, org-enriched)
    "kyc":         kycSummary             // omitempty — present only if a KYC record exists
}}
```

`party` (`domain.Party`, `party.go:19`): `id`, `phone`, `full_name` (omitempty), `preferred_language` (omitempty), `kyc_tier`, `status`, `created_at`, `updated_at`.

`assignments` reuses `listMyRoles` — identical `assignmentWithOrg` shape as §3 (only usable assignments, org-enriched).

`kyc` is `kycSummary` (`models.go:132-140`), the masked digest of the **latest** KYC record (omitted if none exists; a non-404 error propagates):
```
{
    "requested_tier":      string,
    "status":              string,   // PENDING | VERIFIED | REJECTED
    "aadhaar_last4":       string,   // omitempty
    "bank_account_masked": string,   // omitempty
    "bank_ifsc":           string,   // omitempty
    "bank_verified":       bool,
    "verified_at":         time      // omitempty ptr
}
```

---

## 6. Role codes in `domain.AllRoles` (exact strings)

From `roles.go:64-75` — 24 roles:

```

SAMITI_SACHEEV

LRP

```

Related maps in the same file the frontend may need for alignment:
- `RequiredKYCTier` maps each role → min KYC tier (e.g. `FARMER→FARMER`, `CONSUMER→MINIMAL`, `UNION_PRESIDENT/PCDF_ADMIN/ORGANISING_MANAGER→HIGH`, `VAN_RIDER/DELIVERY_RIDER→RIDER`, `SUPER_ADMIN→HIGHEST`, `SERVICE_ACCOUNT→SERVICE`).
- KYC tiers: `MINIMAL, FARMER, STANDARD, RIDER, HIGH, HIGHEST, SERVICE`. Self-requestable tiers (via `/kyc/aadhaar`): only `FARMER, STANDARD, RIDER, HIGH`.

---

## 7. KYC endpoints present and their shapes

Self-service (RequireSession):
- **POST /kyc/aadhaar** → `aadhaarKYCResponse` = `{ record: domain.KYCRecord, status: string, message: string }`. `status` = `"PENDING"`, `message` = `"awaiting verification"`. 201 fresh / 200 idempotent replay. No auto-verify, no tier change — record created PENDING.
- **POST /kyc/bank** → full `domain.KYCRecord` (200). Attaches masked bank tail + IFSC to the latest PENDING record, or creates a new PENDING record if latest is terminal/absent.
- **GET /kyc/me** → `[]domain.KYCRecord` + `meta` (paginated).

Reviewer console (RequireRoles OM/DV/PCDF/SUPER):
- **GET /kyc/pending** → `[]pendingKYCItem` + `meta`. Each item embeds the full `domain.KYCRecord` (flattened) plus `party` (omitempty) = `pendingPartySummary` `{ id, phone, full_name(omitempty), kyc_tier }`. Scoped to the reviewer's org area.
- **GET /kyc/pending/count** → `pendingKYCCountResponse` = **`{ "count": int64, "capped": bool }`** (`models.go:252-255`). `capped` is true when the pending scan hit the cap (1000, `pendingKYCScanCap`), meaning display "count+". Scoped to the reviewer's area, reuses the same scope logic as the list.
- **POST /kyc/{id}/approve** → `kycReviewResponse` = `{ record: domain.KYCRecord, kyc_tier: string }` (`kyc_tier` = party tier after upgrade).
- **POST /kyc/{id}/reject** → same `kycReviewResponse`; requires body `{ reason }`.

`domain.KYCRecord` JSON fields (`party.go:82`): `id`, `party_id`, `requested_tier`, `aadhaar_last4` (omitempty), `bank_account_masked` (omitempty), `bank_ifsc` (omitempty), `bank_verified` (bool), `bank_name_match` (omitempty float 0..1), `digilocker_docs` (omitempty), `video_kyc_ref` (omitempty), `consent_id` (omitempty), `status`, `rejection_reason` (omitempty), `reviewed_by` (omitempty), `reviewed_by_role` (omitempty), `reviewed_at` (omitempty), `verified_at` (omitempty), `created_at`, `updated_at`. **Important:** `aadhaar_vault_ref` is `json:"-"` — persisted but NEVER serialized to any client.

Reviewer authorization for approve/reject enforces, in service: record must be PENDING (else `409 KYC_NOT_PENDING`); no self-review (`403 KYC_SELF_REVIEW`); subject must be in reviewer's org scope (`403 KYC_SUBJECT_OUT_OF_SCOPE`); role must be allowed for the tier via `CanApproveKYCTier` (`403 KYC_TIER_NOT_APPROVABLE`).

---

## 8. How multi-role is currently handled

**Model = one `Party`, many `RoleAssignment`s** — confirmed exactly as blueprint §4.1.

- `domain.Party` (`party.go:19`) is the single identity record: `phone` is the unique natural key; one phone = one Party. It carries no role — roles are entirely separate records.
- `domain.RoleAssignment` (`party.go:39`) grants **one role** (`role_code`) to **one party** (`party_id`) inside **one org unit** (`org_unit_id`) for a validity window (`valid_from` / nullable `valid_to`), with `status` ACTIVE/REVOKED plus `revoked_at`/`revoked_by`. A party can hold many of these simultaneously.
- `RoleAssignment.UsableAt(t)` (`party.go:55`) is the single usability predicate: status must be ACTIVE, `t >= valid_from`, and (`valid_to == nil` OR `t <= valid_to`).

Login vs. role selection:
- OTP verify issues only a **SESSION** token (no role). The client fetches `/auth/roles` (usable assignments, org-enriched) and picks one via `/auth/role/select`, which mints a **ROLE** token pinned to that single assignment (`rid`/`rol`/`org`/`ogt` claims). Switching roles = issue a fresh ROLE token; no server session state changes.

How `/auth/role/select` validates the assignment belongs to the caller and is usable (`selectRole`, `service.go:358-427`):
1. **Ownership**: after `findAssignmentByID`, it checks `assignment.PartyID != aid` (the actor's party id parsed from JWT `pid`). Mismatch → `404 NotFound("role assignment")` — indistinguishable from an unknown ID, so a caller can never probe other parties' grants.
2. **Usability**: `assignment.UsableAt(now)` — false (revoked or outside window) → `403`.
3. **Party active**: re-reads the party (tier may have changed since session mint); must be `ACTIVE`.
4. **KYC gate**: `KYCTierSatisfies(party.KYCTier, RequiredKYCTier[role_code])`; insufficient → `403 KYC_TIER_INSUFFICIENT` with `{ current_tier, required_tier }`. This genuinely blocks un-approved parties from assuming a role — there is no auto-verify path.

`listMyRoles` / `getMe.assignments` also filter by `UsableAt(now)`, so the switcher UI only ever shows selectable assignments.

---

### Cross-cutting notes for frontend alignment
- Every payload is wrapped: read `response.data` (and `response.meta` for lists). Errors are `response.error` with `{ code, message, status, details? }`.
- ObjectIDs serialize as 24-char hex strings; `role_assignment_id` in the select request must be that hex string.
- Pagination query params: `limit` (default 50, max 200), `offset` (default 0). `meta` returns `{ limit, offset, total }`.

24	// Register wires repo → service → handler and mounts the identity routes.
25	func Register(r chi.Router, d *deps.Deps) {
26		log := d.Log.With(slog.String("module", "identity"))
27		repo := newRepository(d.DB)
28		svc := newService(d, repo, log)

32			// Public login flow — no token yet.

34			r.Post("/otp/verify", h.verifyOTP)
35			r.Post("/refresh", h.refresh)
36	
37			// Any logged-in party (session or role token).
38			r.Group(func(r chi.Router) {
39				r.Use(middleware.Authenticate(d.JWT), middleware.RequireSession)
40				r.Post("/logout", h.logout)
41				r.Get("/roles", h.listMyRoles)
42				r.Post("/role/select", h.selectRole)
43			})
44		})
45	
46		r.Route("/parties", func(r chi.Router) {
47			r.Use(middleware.Authenticate(d.JWT), middleware.RequireSession)
48			r.Get("/me", h.getMe)
49			r.Patch("/me", h.patchMe)
50		})
51	
52		r.Route("/kyc", func(r chi.Router) {
53			r.Use(middleware.Authenticate(d.JWT))
54	
55			// Self-service KYC: any logged-in party submits evidence.
56			r.Group(func(r chi.Router) {
57				r.Use(middleware.RequireSession)

63			// Review console: ground staff and admins approve/reject PENDING KYC.
64			r.Group(func(r chi.Router) {
65				r.Use(middleware.RequireRoles(
66					domain.RoleOrganisingManager,
67					domain.RoleDistrictVerifier,

22	// actorOr401 extracts the authenticated actor; the middleware guarantees it

24	func actorOr401(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) (auth.Actor, bool) {
25		actor, ok := auth.ActorFrom(r.Context())
26		if !ok {

73	// granterMayGrant reports whether granterRole may grant (or revoke)
74	// roleCode. Admin granters pass unconditionally.
75	func granterMayGrant(granterRole, roleCode string) bool {
76		if granterRole == domain.RoleSuperAdmin || granterRole == domain.RolePCDFAdmin {
77			return true
78		}
79		allowed, ok := grantableRoles[granterRole]
80		return ok && allowed[roleCode]

129	// --- Auth: OTP login ---
130	
131	// requestOTP creates a hashed OTP challenge and queues the SMS through the
132	// notification outbox (the platformops worker delivers it).
133	func (s *service) requestOTP(ctx context.Context, phone string) (*otpRequestResponse, error) {
134		now := time.Now().UTC()
135		code, err := auth.GenerateNumericOTP(otpLength)
136		if err != nil {
137			s.log.ErrorContext(ctx, "otp generation failed", slog.Any("err", err))
138			return nil, httpx.Internal(err)
139		}
140	
141		challenge := otpChallenge{
142			ID:        uuid.NewString(),
143			Phone:     phone,
144			CodeHash:  auth.HMACHash(s.deps.Cfg.OTPHashSecret, phone, code),
145			ExpiresAt: now.Add(s.deps.Cfg.OTPTTL),
146			Attempts:  0,
147		}
148		if err := s.repo.insertOTPChallenge(ctx, challenge); err != nil {
149			s.log.ErrorContext(ctx, "otp challenge insert failed", slog.String("phone", phone), slog.Any("err", err))
150			return nil, err
151		}
152	
153		// Outbox SMS: the plaintext code travels only inside the notification
154		// params so the sender can deliver it; the challenge stores the hash.
155		notification := domain.Notification{
156			Phone:       phone,
157			Channel:     domain.ChannelSMS,
158			TemplateKey: domain.TemplateOTP,
159			Language:    defaultLanguage,
160			Params:      map[string]string{"otp": code},
161			Status:      domain.NotificationQueued,
162			QueuedAt:    now,
163		}
164		if party, err := s.repo.findPartyByPhone(ctx, phone); err == nil {
165			pid := party.ID
166			notification.PartyID = &pid
167			if party.PreferredLanguage != "" {
168				notification.Language = party.PreferredLanguage
169			}
170		}
171		if err := s.repo.insertNotification(ctx, notification); err != nil {
172			s.log.ErrorContext(ctx, "otp notification queue failed", slog.String("phone", phone), slog.Any("err", err))
173			return nil, err
174		}
175	
176		s.log.InfoContext(ctx, "otp requested", slog.String("phone", phone))
177		resp := &otpRequestResponse{Phone: phone, ExpiresAt: challenge.ExpiresAt}
178		if s.deps.Cfg.OTPDevMode {
179			resp.DevOTP = code // dev only — config refuses OTP_DEV_MODE in prod
180		}
181		return resp, nil
182	}
183	
184	// verifyOTP checks the challenge and logs the phone in, creating the Party
185	// on first login (find-or-create, §4.1).
186	func (s *service) verifyOTP(ctx context.Context, phone, otp string) (*authTokensResponse, error) {
187		now := time.Now().UTC()
188	
189		challenge, err := s.repo.latestOTPChallenge(ctx, phone, now)
190		if err != nil {
191			if isNotFound(err) {
192				s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "otp verify rejected: no active challenge", slog.String("phone", phone))
193				return nil, httpx.Unauthorized("no active OTP for this phone — request a new code")
194			}
195			return nil, err
196		}
197		if challenge.Attempts >= maxOTPAttempts {
198			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "otp verify rejected: too many attempts", slog.String("phone", phone))
199			return nil, httpx.TooManyRequests("too many incorrect OTP attempts — request a new code")
200		}
201		expected := auth.HMACHash(s.deps.Cfg.OTPHashSecret, phone, otp)
202		if !auth.ConstantTimeEqual(challenge.CodeHash, expected) {
203			if err := s.repo.incrementOTPAttempts(ctx, challenge.ID); err != nil {
204				return nil, err
205			}
206			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "otp verify rejected: incorrect code", slog.String("phone", phone))
207			return nil, httpx.Unauthorized("incorrect OTP")
208		}
209	
210		// Burn every outstanding challenge for this phone.
211		if err := s.repo.deleteOTPChallenges(ctx, phone); err != nil {
212			return nil, err
213		}
214	
215		party, err := s.repo.upsertPartyByPhone(ctx, phone, now)
216		if err != nil {
217			return nil, err
218		}
219		if party.Status != domain.PartyStatusActive {
220			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "otp verify rejected: party suspended",
221				slog.String("phone", phone), slog.String("party_id", party.ID.Hex()))
222			return nil, httpx.Forbidden("party is suspended")
223		}
224		tokens, err := s.issueLoginTokens(ctx, party, now)
225		if err != nil {
226			return nil, err
227		}
228		s.log.InfoContext(ctx, "party logged in",
229			slog.String("party_id", party.ID.Hex()), slog.String("phone", phone))
230		return tokens, nil
231	}
232	
233	// issueLoginTokens mints a SESSION access token plus a fresh rotating
234	// refresh token (stored only as an HMAC digest).
235	func (s *service) issueLoginTokens(ctx context.Context, party *domain.Party, now time.Time) (*authTokensResponse, error) {
236		refreshToken, err := auth.RandomToken(32)
237		if err != nil {
238			s.log.ErrorContext(ctx, "refresh token generation failed", slog.Any("err", err))
239			return nil, httpx.Internal(err)
240		}
241		doc := refreshTokenDoc{
242			TokenHash: auth.HMACHash(s.deps.Cfg.OTPHashSecret, refreshHashLabel, refreshToken),
243			PartyID:   party.ID,
244			ExpiresAt: now.Add(s.deps.Cfg.RefreshTokenTTL),
245			CreatedAt: now,
246		}
247		if err := s.repo.insertRefreshToken(ctx, doc); err != nil {
248			return nil, err
249		}
250		accessToken, err := s.deps.JWT.IssueSessionToken(*party)
251		if err != nil {
252			s.log.ErrorContext(ctx, "session token issue failed",
253				slog.String("party_id", party.ID.Hex()), slog.Any("err", err))
254			return nil, httpx.Internal(err)
255		}
256		return &authTokensResponse{
257			AccessToken:  accessToken,
258			RefreshToken: refreshToken,
259			Party:        party,
260		}, nil
261	}
262	
263	// refresh rotates a refresh token: the old token is consumed atomically and
264	// a new pair is issued — a replayed token always fails.
265	func (s *service) refresh(ctx context.Context, refreshToken string) (*authTokensResponse, error) {
266		now := time.Now().UTC()
267		tokenHash := auth.HMACHash(s.deps.Cfg.OTPHashSecret, refreshHashLabel, refreshToken)
268	
269		doc, err := s.repo.findRefreshToken(ctx, tokenHash)
270		if err != nil {
271			if isNotFound(err) {
272				s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "refresh rejected: unknown token")
273				return nil, httpx.Unauthorized("invalid refresh token")
274			}
275			return nil, err
276		}
277		if !now.Before(doc.ExpiresAt) {
278			_, _ = s.repo.deleteRefreshToken(ctx, tokenHash)
279			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "refresh rejected: token expired", slog.String("party_id", doc.PartyID.Hex()))
280			return nil, httpx.Unauthorized("refresh token expired — log in again")
281		}
282	
283		// ROTATE: consume the old token first; DeletedCount==0 means a parallel
284		// request won the race, so this presentation is treated as a replay.
285		deleted, err := s.repo.deleteRefreshToken(ctx, tokenHash)
286		if err != nil {
287			return nil, err
288		}
289		if deleted == 0 {
290			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "refresh rejected: token already used", slog.String("party_id", doc.PartyID.Hex()))
291			return nil, httpx.Unauthorized("refresh token already used")
292		}
293	
294		party, err := s.repo.findPartyByID(ctx, doc.PartyID)
295		if err != nil {
296			if isNotFound(err) {
297				s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "refresh rejected: party gone", slog.String("party_id", doc.PartyID.Hex()))
298				return nil, httpx.Unauthorized("party no longer exists")
299			}
300			return nil, err
301		}
302		if party.Status != domain.PartyStatusActive {
303			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "refresh rejected: party suspended", slog.String("party_id", party.ID.Hex()))
304			return nil, httpx.Forbidden("party is suspended")
305		}
306		return s.issueLoginTokens(ctx, party, now)
307	}
308

355	// selectRole exchanges the session for a ROLE-kind token pinned to one

375			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "role select rejected: assignment not usable",
376				slog.String("assignment_id", assignmentID.Hex()), slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID))
377			return nil, httpx.Forbidden("role assignment is revoked or outside its validity window")
378		}
379	
380		// Re-read the party: the KYC tier may have upgraded since the session
381		// token was minted.
382		party, err := s.repo.findPartyByID(ctx, aid)
383		if err != nil {
384			return nil, err
385		}
386		if party.Status != domain.PartyStatusActive {
387			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "role select rejected: party suspended", slog.String("party_id", party.ID.Hex()))
388			return nil, httpx.Forbidden("party is suspended")
389		}
390		requiredTier := domain.RequiredKYCTier[assignment.RoleCode]
391		if !domain.KYCTierSatisfies(party.KYCTier, requiredTier) {
392			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "role select rejected: kyc tier insufficient",
393				slog.String("party_id", party.ID.Hex()),
394				slog.String("role_code", assignment.RoleCode),
395				slog.String("current_tier", party.KYCTier),
396				slog.String("required_tier", requiredTier))
397			appErr := httpx.Forbidden("your KYC tier does not permit this role — complete verification first").
398				WithDetails(map[string]string{
399					"current_tier":  party.KYCTier,
400					"required_tier": requiredTier,
401				})
402			appErr.Code = "KYC_TIER_INSUFFICIENT"
403			return nil, appErr
404		}
405	
406		org, err := s.deps.Orgs.Get(ctx, assignment.OrgUnitID)
407		if err != nil {
408			return nil, err
409		}
410		accessToken, err := s.deps.JWT.IssueRoleToken(*party, *assignment, org.Type)
411		if err != nil {
412			s.log.ErrorContext(ctx, "role token issue failed",
413				slog.String("assignment_id", assignmentID.Hex()), slog.Any("err", err))
414			return nil, httpx.Internal(err)
415		}
416		s.log.InfoContext(ctx, "role selected",
417			slog.String("party_id", party.ID.Hex()),
418			slog.String("assignment_id", assignmentID.Hex()),
419			slog.String("role_code", assignment.RoleCode),
420			slog.String("org_unit_id", assignment.OrgUnitID.Hex()))
421		return &roleSelectResponse{
422			AccessToken: accessToken,
423			RoleCode:    assignment.RoleCode,
424			OrgUnitID:   assignment.OrgUnitID,
425			OrgType:     org.Type,
426		}, nil
427	}

432	// summary in one call.

437		}

439		if err != nil {
440			return nil, err
441		}

443		if err != nil {
444			return nil, err
445		}
446		resp := &meResponse{Party: party, Assignments: assignments}
447		if latest, err := s.repo.latestKYCRecord(ctx, aid); err == nil {
448			resp.KYC = &kycSummary{
449				RequestedTier:     latest.RequestedTier,

451				AadhaarLast4:      latest.AadhaarLast4,

453				BankIFSC:          latest.BankIFSC,
454				BankVerified:      latest.BankVerified,
455				VerifiedAt:        latest.VerifiedAt,
456			}
457		} else if !isNotFound(err) {
458			return nil, err
459		}
460		return resp, nil
461	}

463	// patchMe updates the caller's own profile fields.
464	func (s *service) patchMe(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, req patchMeRequest) (*domain.Party, error) {
465		aid, err := actorID(actor)
466		if err != nil {

470	}
471	
472	// --- KYC (mock DPI adapters — real UIDAI / penny-drop integration later) ---
473	
474	// verifyAadhaar runs the MOCK Aadhaar eKYC capture (§18-A). The full Aadhaar
475	// number exists only in this request's memory: what is persisted is the
476	// last 4 digits plus an opaque reference from the (mock) Aadhaar Data Vault.
477	//
478	// There is NO auto-verify and NO tier change here: the record is created
479	// PENDING and enters the approval workflow. Returns created=false when an
480	// identical PENDING request already exists (idempotent replay → 200).
481	func (s *service) verifyAadhaar(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, req aadhaarKYCRequest) (*aadhaarKYCResponse, bool, error) {
482		now := time.Now().UTC()
483		aid, err := actorID(actor)
484		if err != nil {
485			return nil, false, err
486		}
487		party, err := s.repo.findPartyByID(ctx, aid)
488		if err != nil {
489			return nil, false, err
490		}
491	
492		// Idempotency: an existing PENDING request for the same tier is returned
493		// as-is rather than duplicated.
494		if existing, err := s.repo.findPendingKYCRecord(ctx, party.ID, req.RequestedTier); err == nil {
495			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "kyc submit replayed idempotently",
496				slog.String("kyc_id", existing.ID.Hex()),
497				slog.String("party_id", party.ID.Hex()),
498				slog.String("requested_tier", req.RequestedTier))
499			return &aadhaarKYCResponse{
500				Record:  existing,
501				Status:  domain.KYCStatusPending,
502				Message: msgAwaitingVerification,
503			}, false, nil
504		} else if !isNotFound(err) {
505			return nil, false, err
506		}
507	
508		language := party.PreferredLanguage
509		if language == "" {
510			language = defaultLanguage
511		}
512		// Pre-generate the consent id so the KYC record can reference it in the
513		// same flow.
514		consentID := primitive.NewObjectID()
515		consent := domain.Consent{
516			ID:          consentID,
517			PartyID:     party.ID,
518			Purpose:     consentPurposeAadhaarEKYC,
519			TextVersion: consentTextVersion,
520			Language:    language,
521			GrantedAt:   now,
522		}
523		if err := s.repo.insertConsent(ctx, consent); err != nil {
524			return nil, false, err
525		}
526	
527		// MOCK Aadhaar Data Vault (§18-A): a real deployment sends the number to
528		// the vault service and receives an opaque token. The mock mints a UUID.
529		vaultRef := uuid.NewString()
530		last4 := req.AadhaarNumber[len(req.AadhaarNumber)-4:]
531	
532		record := domain.KYCRecord{
533			ID:              primitive.NewObjectID(),
534			PartyID:         party.ID,
535			RequestedTier:   req.RequestedTier,
536			AadhaarLast4:    last4,
537			AadhaarVaultRef: vaultRef,
538			ConsentID:       &consentID,
539			Status:          domain.KYCStatusPending,
540			CreatedAt:       now,
541			UpdatedAt:       now,
542		}
543		if err := s.repo.insertKYCRecord(ctx, record); err != nil {
544			return nil, false, err
545		}
546	
547		s.log.InfoContext(ctx, "kyc submitted",
548			slog.String("kyc_id", record.ID.Hex()),
549			slog.String("party_id", party.ID.Hex()),
550			slog.String("requested_tier", req.RequestedTier))
551		// Nudge reviewer dashboards: a new record entered the PENDING queue.
552		s.publishKYCQueueChanged("submitted", record.ID, party.ID)
553		return &aadhaarKYCResponse{
554			Record:  &record,
555			Status:  domain.KYCStatusPending,
556			Message: msgAwaitingVerification,
557		}, true, nil
558	}
559	
560	// publishKYCQueueChanged nudges the live "pending KYC" dashboard badge via the
561	// event bus → SSE hub. It is a nudge only; subscribers re-query the scoped
562	// pending count. Never blocks the request path (the bus dispatches async).
563	func (s *service) publishKYCQueueChanged(reason string, kycID, subjectID primitive.ObjectID) {
564		s.deps.Bus.Publish(eventbus.TopicKYCQueueChanged, eventbus.KYCQueueEvent{
565			Reason:    reason,
566			KYCID:     kycID.Hex(),
567			SubjectID: subjectID.Hex(),
568		})
569	}
570	
571	// verifyBank runs the MOCK penny-drop verification and stores ONLY the
572	// masked account tail and IFSC on the caller's latest KYC record (creating a
573	// PENDING record carrying just the bank evidence when none exists yet).
574	func (s *service) verifyBank(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, req bankKYCRequest) (*domain.KYCRecord, error) {
575		now := time.Now().UTC()
576		aid, err := actorID(actor)
577		if err != nil {
578			return nil, err
579		}
580		party, err := s.repo.findPartyByID(ctx, aid)
581		if err != nil {
582			return nil, err
583		}
584		masked := maskAccount(req.AccountNumber)
585	
586		latest, err := s.repo.latestKYCRecord(ctx, aid)
587		switch {
588		case err == nil && latest.Status == domain.KYCStatusPending:
589			// Only a PENDING record may accrue bank evidence in place — a reviewer
590			// has not yet decided it. MOCK penny-drop: fixed name-match score.
591			rec, err := s.repo.updateKYCRecordBank(ctx, latest.ID, masked, req.IFSC, mockPennyDropNameMatch, now)
592			if err != nil {
593				return nil, err
594			}
595			s.log.InfoContext(ctx, "bank evidence attached",
596				slog.String("kyc_id", rec.ID.Hex()), slog.String("party_id", party.ID.Hex()))
597			return rec, nil
598		case err == nil, isNotFound(err):
599			// The latest record is terminal (VERIFIED/REJECTED) or none exists yet:
600			// a changed bank account must NOT silently overwrite reviewer-approved
601			// evidence, so route it back through review as a fresh PENDING record.
602			record := domain.KYCRecord{
603				ID:                primitive.NewObjectID(),
604				PartyID:           party.ID,
605				RequestedTier:     party.KYCTier,
606				BankAccountMasked: masked,
607				BankIFSC:          req.IFSC,
608				BankVerified:      true, // MOCK penny-drop: always succeeds
609				BankNameMatch:     mockPennyDropNameMatch,
610				Status:            domain.KYCStatusPending,
611				CreatedAt:         now,
612				UpdatedAt:         now,
613			}
614			if err := s.repo.insertKYCRecord(ctx, record); err != nil {
615				return nil, err
616			}
617			s.log.InfoContext(ctx, "bank evidence recorded on new pending kyc",
618				slog.String("kyc_id", record.ID.Hex()), slog.String("party_id", party.ID.Hex()))
619			return &record, nil
620		default:
621			return nil, err
622		}
623	}

627	func (s *service) listMyKYC(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, page httpx.Page) ([]domain.KYCRecord, int64, error) {
628		aid, err := actorID(actor)
629		if err != nil {

631		}
