960	// --- Role administration ---
961	
962	// requireGrantAuthority enforces the non-admin granter matrix (§5.2):
963	// UNION_PRESIDENT manages village/logistics/union-tier roles anywhere in
964	// scope; SAMITI_ADHYAKSH manages only FARMER/MILK_TESTER/LRP inside their
965	// own DCS; ORGANISING_MANAGER enrols FARMER/CONSUMER within org scope.
966	// Admin granters pass.
967	func (s *service) requireGrantAuthority(actor auth.Actor, roleCode string, orgUnitID primitive.ObjectID) error {
968		if !granterMayGrant(actor.RoleCode, roleCode) {
969			return httpx.Forbidden("role " + actor.RoleCode + " may not grant or revoke " + roleCode)
970		}
971		if actor.RoleCode == domain.RoleSamitiAdhyaksh && orgUnitID.Hex() != actor.OrgUnitID {
972			return httpx.Forbidden("SAMITI_ADHYAKSH may manage roles only within their own DCS")
973		}
974		return nil
975	}
976	
977	// createAssignment grants a role to a party inside an org unit.
978	func (s *service) createAssignment(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, req createAssignmentRequest) (*domain.RoleAssignment, error) {
979		aid, err := actorID(actor)
980		if err != nil {
981			return nil, err
982		}
983	
984		// Resolve the target party (party_id wins over phone).
985		var party *domain.Party
986		if req.PartyID != nil {
987			party, err = s.repo.findPartyByID(ctx, *req.PartyID)
988		} else {
989			party, err = s.repo.findPartyByPhone(ctx, req.Phone)
990		}
991		if err != nil {
992			return nil, err
993		}
994	
995		if err := s.deps.Orgs.RequireInScope(ctx, actor, req.OrgUnitID); err != nil {
996			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "assignment grant denied: out of scope",
997				slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID),
998				slog.String("org_unit_id", req.OrgUnitID.Hex()),
999				slog.String("role_code", req.RoleCode))
1000			return nil, err
1001		}
1002		if err := s.requireGrantAuthority(actor, req.RoleCode, req.OrgUnitID); err != nil {
1003			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "assignment grant denied: granter not authorised",
1004				slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID),
1005				slog.String("granter_role", actor.RoleCode),
1006				slog.String("role_code", req.RoleCode))
1007			return nil, err
1008		}
1009	
1010		exists, err := s.repo.activeAssignmentExists(ctx, party.ID, req.RoleCode, req.OrgUnitID)
1011		if err != nil {
1012			return nil, err
1013		}
1014		if exists {
1015			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "assignment grant rejected: already exists",
1016				slog.String("party_id", party.ID.Hex()),
1017				slog.String("role_code", req.RoleCode),
1018				slog.String("org_unit_id", req.OrgUnitID.Hex()))
1019			return nil, httpx.Conflict("ASSIGNMENT_EXISTS", "party already holds an active "+req.RoleCode+" assignment in this org unit")
1020		}
1021	
1022		now := time.Now().UTC()
1023		validFrom := now
1024		if req.ValidFrom != nil {
1025			validFrom = req.ValidFrom.UTC()
1026		}
1027		var validTo *time.Time
1028		if req.ValidTo != nil {
1029			t := req.ValidTo.UTC()
1030			validTo = &t
1031		}
1032		assignment := domain.RoleAssignment{
1033			ID:        primitive.NewObjectID(),
1034			PartyID:   party.ID,
1035			RoleCode:  req.RoleCode,
1036			OrgUnitID: req.OrgUnitID,
1037			GrantedBy: &aid,
1038			ValidFrom: validFrom,
1039			ValidTo:   validTo,
1040			Status:    domain.RoleAssignmentActive,
1041			CreatedAt: now,
1042		}
1043		if err := s.repo.insertAssignment(ctx, assignment); err != nil {
1044			return nil, err
1045		}
1046		s.deps.Audit.Record(ctx, audit.Entry{
1047			Action:     "role.grant",
1048			TargetType: "role_assignment",
1049			TargetID:   assignment.ID.Hex(),
1050			Meta: map[string]any{
1051				"party_id":    party.ID.Hex(),
1052				"role_code":   req.RoleCode,
1053				"org_unit_id": req.OrgUnitID.Hex(),
1054			},
1055		})
1056		s.log.InfoContext(ctx, "role assignment created",
1057			slog.String("assignment_id", assignment.ID.Hex()),
1058			slog.String("party_id", party.ID.Hex()),
1059			slog.String("role_code", req.RoleCode),
1060			slog.String("org_unit_id", req.OrgUnitID.Hex()),
1061			slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID))
1062		return &assignment, nil
1063	}

1065	// revokeAssignment flips an assignment to REVOKED — the record is never
1066	// deleted (§4.1). Revocation authority mirrors grant authority.
1067	func (s *service) revokeAssignment(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, assignmentID primitive.ObjectID) (*domain.RoleAssignment, error) {
1068		aid, err := actorID(actor)
1069		if err != nil {
1070			return nil, err
1071		}
1072		assignment, err := s.repo.findAssignmentByID(ctx, assignmentID)
1073		if err != nil {
1074			return nil, err
1075		}
1076		if err := s.deps.Orgs.RequireInScope(ctx, actor, assignment.OrgUnitID); err != nil {
1077			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "assignment revoke denied: out of scope",
1078				slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID),
1079				slog.String("assignment_id", assignmentID.Hex()))
1080			return nil, err
1081		}
1082		if err := s.requireGrantAuthority(actor, assignment.RoleCode, assignment.OrgUnitID); err != nil {
1083			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "assignment revoke denied: granter not authorised",
1084				slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID),
1085				slog.String("granter_role", actor.RoleCode),
1086				slog.String("role_code", assignment.RoleCode))
1087			return nil, err
1088		}
1089		if assignment.Status != domain.RoleAssignmentActive {
1090			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "assignment revoke rejected: already revoked",
1091				slog.String("assignment_id", assignmentID.Hex()))
1092			return nil, httpx.Conflict("ALREADY_REVOKED", "role assignment is already revoked")
1093		}
1094		revoked, err := s.repo.revokeAssignment(ctx, assignmentID, aid, time.Now().UTC())
1095		if err != nil {
1096			return nil, err
1097		}
1098		s.deps.Audit.Record(ctx, audit.Entry{
1099			Action:     "role.revoke",
1100			TargetType: "role_assignment",
1101			TargetID:   assignmentID.Hex(),
1102			Meta: map[string]any{
1103				"party_id":    revoked.PartyID.Hex(),
1104				"role_code":   revoked.RoleCode,
1105				"org_unit_id": revoked.OrgUnitID.Hex(),
1106			},
1107		})
1108		s.log.InfoContext(ctx, "role assignment revoked",
1109			slog.String("assignment_id", assignmentID.Hex()),
1110			slog.String("party_id", revoked.PartyID.Hex()),
1111			slog.String("role_code", revoked.RoleCode),
1112			slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID))
1113		return revoked, nil
1114	}

1	// Package identity owns authentication (OTP login, refresh-token rotation,
2	// role selection), the Party registry, org-scoped role assignments and the
3	// KYC approval workflow — blueprint §4 (identity) and §5 (roles & RBAC).
4	//
5	// The KYC flow is: login → submit KYC (PENDING) → an authorised reviewer
6	// (Organising Manager / District Verifier / PCDF Admin / Super Admin)
7	// approves or rejects → only a VERIFIED tier unlocks the matching role token.
8	//
9	// Route prefixes (mounted under /api/v1): /auth, /parties, /roles, /kyc.
10	// This module emits no provenance events; identity changes are covered by
11	// the audit middleware and explicit audit records on KYC review.
12	package identity
13	
14	import (
15		"log/slog"
16	
17		"github.com/go-chi/chi/v5"
18	
19		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/domain"
20		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/deps"
21		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/middleware"
22	)
23	
24	// Register wires repo → service → handler and mounts the identity routes.
25	func Register(r chi.Router, d *deps.Deps) {
26		log := d.Log.With(slog.String("module", "identity"))

6	/**
7	 * Same-day payment rail (§8.1) wired to the real Go backend:
8	 *   - collection module (mount /collection): per-farmer invoices + rate charts
9	 *       GET  /collection/invoices            → list (dcs_id/farmer_party_id/status/date)
10	 *       GET  /collection/rate-charts/active  → the active pricing chart
11	 *       POST /collection/rate-charts         → create/replace the active chart
12	 *   - settlement module (mount /settlements): READ-only from the client's view
13	 *       GET  /settlements                    → the day's computed batches
14	 *
15	 * Settlement WRITES (approve invoices / settle / assisted release) are
16	 * computed + event-driven on the backend: the settlement models exist
17	 * (InitiateSettlementRequest / RejectSettlementRequest) but no POST route is
18	 * registered, so those endpoints stay mock-only until the backend exposes them.
19	 * Settlement is always an authorised human action - Saathi computes and
20	 * initiates, it never moves funds autonomously (§18-B guardrail).

79	function mapInvoiceStatus(s: string | undefined): Invoice['status'] {
80	  switch (s) {
81	    case 'SETTLED':
82	    case 'PAID':
83	      return 'SETTLED';
84	    case 'APPROVED':
85	      return 'APPROVED';
86	    default:
87	      return 'DRAFT';

118	/** Map a settlement batch status onto the assisted-release stage machine. */
119	function mapReleaseStage(status: string | undefined): ReleaseStage {
120	  switch (status) {
121	    case 'APPROVED':
122	      return 'UNION_FUNDED';
123	    case 'EXECUTING':
124	    case 'DISTRIBUTING':
125	      return 'DISTRIBUTING';
126	    case 'EXECUTED':
127	    case 'PAID':
128	    case 'SETTLED':
129	    case 'COMPLETED':
130	      return 'FARMERS_PAID';
131	    default: // INITIATED / PENDING / unknown
132	      return 'PENDING_APPROVAL';
133	  }
134	}

136	/** Derive the assisted-release stage for a DCS + date from its invoices. */
137	function computeRelease(
138	  invoices: Invoice[],
139	  dcsId: string,
140	  date: string,
141	): ReleaseSummary {
142	  const day = invoices.filter((i) => i.dcsId === dcsId && i.date === date);
143	  const approved = day.filter((i) => i.status === 'APPROVED');
144	  const settled = day.filter((i) => i.status === 'SETTLED');
145	  const drafts = day.filter((i) => i.status === 'DRAFT');
146	  const releasable = [...approved, ...settled];
147	  const farmerCount = new Set(releasable.map((i) => i.farmerPartyId)).size;
148	  const totalAmount = Math.round(releasable.reduce((s, i) => s + i.netAmount, 0) * 100) / 100;
149	
150	  let stage: ReleaseStage;
151	  if (drafts.length > 0 || releasable.length === 0) stage = 'PENDING_APPROVAL';
152	  else if (approved.length > 0) stage = 'UNION_FUNDED';
153	  else stage = 'FARMERS_PAID';
154	
155	  const firstSettled = settled.find((i) => i.settledAt);
156	  return {
157	    dcsId,
158	    date,
159	    unionRef: `UNION-${dcsId.replace('org_dcs_', '').toUpperCase()}-${date.slice(2).replaceAll('-', '')}`,
160	    farmerCount,
161	    totalAmount,
162	    stage,
163	    approvedInvoiceIds: approved.map((i) => i.id),
164	    sachivApprovedAt: firstSettled?.settledAt,
165	    distributedAt: firstSettled?.settledAt,
166	    utrBatch: firstSettled?.utr ? `BATCH-${firstSettled.utr}` : undefined,
167	  };
168	}

225	/** Create a processing batch from silo intakes (provenance edge, §7.1). */
226	export const createBatch = endpoint<
227	  { plantId: string; intakeIds: string[]; createdByPartyId: string },
228	  PlantBatch
229	>({
230	  method: 'POST',
231	  path: () => '/plant/batches',
232	  // product_type has no source in the domain input; default to MILK. The
233	  // backend also pools BMC lots, not raw silo intakes - intakeIds is forwarded
234	  // as bmc_lot_ids, which matches the real intake grain. See issues.
235	  mapRequest: ({ plantId, intakeIds }) => ({

241	  mock: ({ plantId, intakeIds, createdByPartyId }, db) => {
242	    const intakes = db.intakes.filter((i) => intakeIds.includes(i.id));
243	    if (intakes.length === 0) throw new ApiError(422, 'NO_INTAKES', 'Select at least one silo intake');

245	    if (alreadyPooled) {

248	        'INTAKE_ALREADY_POOLED',
249	        `Intake ${alreadyPooled.siloLotCode} is already in a batch and cannot be pooled again`,
250	      );
251	    }
252	    const notArrived = intakes.find((i) => i.status !== 'DISPATCHED_TO_PLANT');
253	    if (notArrived) {
254	      throw new ApiError(
255	        409,
256	        'INTAKE_NOT_AT_PLANT',
257	        `Intake ${notArrived.siloLotCode} has not been dispatched to the plant by the branch yet`,
258	      );

261	      .flatMap((i) => i.lotIds)
262	      .map((id) => db.lots.find((l) => l.id === id))
263	      .filter((l): l is NonNullable<typeof l> => Boolean(l));
264	    const date = todayISO();
265	    const suffix = String.fromCharCode(65 + db.batches.filter((b) => b.date === date).length);
266	    const batch: PlantBatch = {
267	      id: nextId('batch'),
268	      code: batchCode('LKO', date, suffix),
269	      plantId,
270	      date,
271	      intakeIds,
272	      contributingDcsIds: [...new Set(lots.map((l) => l.dcsId))],
273	      volumeLitres: Math.round(lots.reduce((s, l) => s + l.totalLitres, 0)),
274	      stage: 'RECEIVED',
275	      qcStatus: 'PENDING',
276	      productOutputs: [],
277	    };
278	    db.batches.push(batch);
279	    // The branch already dispatched these to the plant; pooling just marks them
280	    // consumed by this batch (the double-pool guard).
281	    for (const i of intakes) i.batchId = batch.id;
282	    for (const l of lots) l.status = 'AT_PLANT';
283	    audit(db, {
284	      actorPartyId: createdByPartyId,
285	      actorRole: 'PLANT_OPERATOR',
286	      action: 'BATCH_CREATED',
287	      subject: batch.code,
288	      detail: `${batch.volumeLitres}L from ${batch.contributingDcsIds.length} samitis - QC pending`,
289	    });
290	    appendChainEvent(db, {
291	      kind: 'BATCH_POOLED',
292	      subjectType: 'BATCH',
293	      subjectId: batch.id,
294	      actorPartyId: createdByPartyId,
295	      detail: `${batch.code}: pooled ${intakeIds.length} intakes, ${batch.volumeLitres}L`,
296	    });
297	    return batch;
298	  },

301	/**
302	 * Advance the batch through processing stages. The QC gate is enforced here:
303	 * a batch cannot be PACKED or RELEASED unless the lab has passed it (§8.3).
304	 */
305	export const advanceBatchStage = endpoint<
306	  { batchId: string; stage: BatchStage; byPartyId: string },
307	  PlantBatch
308	>({
309	  method: 'POST',
310	  // The backend exposes only a single terminal transition (.../complete) - it
311	  // cannot express the RECEIVED→PASTEURIZED→PACKED→RELEASED ladder or a
312	  // REJECTED move. Every advance maps to "complete"; the requested `stage` is
313	  // dropped on the wire. Input type is kept for the mock's full state machine.
314	  // See issues.
315	  path: ({ batchId }) => `/plant/batches/${batchId}/complete`,
316	  mapRequest: () => ({}),
317	  mapResponse: (raw) => mapBatch(raw as WireBatch),
318	  mock: ({ batchId, stage, byPartyId }, db) => {
319	    const batch = db.batches.find((b) => b.id === batchId);
320	    if (!batch) throw new ApiError(404, 'BATCH_NOT_FOUND', `Unknown batch ${batchId}`);
321	    const order: BatchStage[] = ['RECEIVED', 'PASTEURIZED', 'PACKED', 'RELEASED'];
322	    if (stage === 'REJECTED') {
323	      batch.stage = 'REJECTED';
324	    } else {
325	      const from = order.indexOf(batch.stage);
326	      const to = order.indexOf(stage);
327	      if (from === -1 || to !== from + 1) {
328	        throw new ApiError(409, 'INVALID_TRANSITION', `Cannot move ${batch.stage} → ${stage}`);
329	      }
330	      if ((stage === 'PACKED' || stage === 'RELEASED') && batch.qcStatus !== 'PASS') {
331	        throw new ApiError(
332	          409,
333	          'QC_GATE_BLOCKED',
334	          'Safety gate: batch cannot advance until all mandatory FSSAI tests PASS (§8.3)',
335	        );
336	      }
337	      if (stage === 'RELEASED' && batch.productOutputs.length === 0) {
338	        throw new ApiError(409, 'NO_OUTPUTS', 'Assign product outputs before release');
339	      }
340	      batch.stage = stage;
341	    }
342	    audit(db, {
343	      actorPartyId: byPartyId,
344	      actorRole: 'PLANT_OPERATOR',
345	      action: stage === 'REJECTED' ? 'BATCH_REJECTED' : 'BATCH_STAGE_ADVANCED',
346	      subject: batch.code,
347	      detail: `Stage → ${batch.stage}`,
348	    });
349	    if (batch.stage === 'PACKED' || batch.stage === 'RELEASED') {
350	      appendChainEvent(db, {
351	        kind: 'LOT_RELEASED',
352	        subjectType: 'BATCH',
353	        subjectId: batch.id,
354	        actorPartyId: byPartyId,
355	        detail: `${batch.code} → ${batch.stage} (behind the QC gate)`,
356	      });
357	    }
358	    return batch;
359	  },
360	});

362	/** Assign packed product outputs; each output gets a batch-level QR (§8.4). */
363	export const assignOutputs = endpoint<
364	  { batchId: string; outputs: Array<{ productId: string; units: number }>; byPartyId: string },
365	  PlantBatch
366	>({
367	  method: 'POST',
368	  // Shape mismatch: the backend creates ONE product-lot per call (needs full
369	  // SKU metadata) and returns that lot, whereas this endpoint assigns an array
370	  // of outputs and returns the whole batch. Only the first output is sent, and
371	  // sku/product_name/unit_size/expiry cannot be derived from the domain input
372	  // (they live in the products catalogue, unavailable here) - placeholders go
373	  // on the wire and mapResponse rebuilds a stub PlantBatch. See issues.
374	  path: () => '/plant/product-lots',
375	  mapRequest: ({ batchId, outputs }) => {
376	    const first = outputs[0];
377	    return {
378	      batch_id: batchId,
379	      sku: first?.productId ?? '',
380	      product_name: '',
381	      units: first?.units ?? 0,
382	      unit_size: '',
383	      expiry_date: '',
384	    };
385	  },
386	  mapResponse: (raw) => {
387	    const d = raw as WireProductLot;
388	    return {
389	      id: d.batch_id ?? '',
390	      code: '',
391	      plantId: '',
392	      date: d.mfg_date ?? d.created_at?.slice(0, 10) ?? '',
393	      intakeIds: [],
394	      contributingDcsIds: [],
395	      volumeLitres: 0,
396	      stage: 'PACKED',
397	      qcStatus: 'PASS',
398	      productOutputs: [
399	        { productId: d.sku ?? '', units: d.units ?? 0, qrBatchCode: d.qr_batch_code ?? d.id ?? '' },
400	      ],
401	    };
402	  },
403	  mock: ({ batchId, outputs, byPartyId }, db) => {
404	    const batch = db.batches.find((b) => b.id === batchId);
405	    if (!batch) throw new ApiError(404, 'BATCH_NOT_FOUND', `Unknown batch ${batchId}`);
406	    if (batch.qcStatus !== 'PASS') {
407	      throw new ApiError(409, 'QC_GATE_BLOCKED', 'Outputs can only be assigned after QC PASS');
408	    }
409	    for (const out of outputs) {
410	      const product = db.products.find((p) => p.id === out.productId);
411	      if (!product || out.units <= 0) continue;
412	      const skuCompact = product.sku.replace('PRG-', '').replace('-', '');
413	      const code = packQrCode(skuCompact, batch.date, batch.code.slice(-1));
414	      // Sign the pack (§6.6): the QR encodes the token, so an edited/guessed
415	      // code cannot resolve or verify at the public trace.
416	      const token = issueTraceToken(code);
417	      batch.productOutputs.push({ productId: out.productId, units: out.units, qrBatchCode: code });
418	      db.qrs.push({
419	        code,
420	        batchId: batch.id,
421	        productId: out.productId,
422	        packedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
423	        bestBefore: todayISO(product.category === 'MILK' ? 3 : 30),
424	        token,
425	      });
426	      appendChainEvent(db, {
427	        kind: 'QR_ISSUE',
428	        subjectType: 'QR',
429	        subjectId: code,
430	        actorPartyId: byPartyId,
431	        detail: `${code} issued for ${batch.code}`,
432	      });
433	    }
434	    audit(db, {
435	      actorPartyId: byPartyId,
436	      actorRole: 'PLANT_OPERATOR',
437	      action: 'OUTPUTS_ASSIGNED',
438	      subject: batch.code,
439	      detail: `${outputs.length} product outputs with batch QRs`,
440	    });
441	    return batch;
442	  },
443	});

76	/** Resolve a wire test name to the closed FE parameter union (tolerant). */
77	function mapParameter(name: string): TestParameter | null {
78	  const s = (name || '').toUpperCase().replace(/[\s-]/g, '_');
79	  if (Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(QUALITY_PARAMETERS, s)) return s as TestParameter;
80	  if (s.includes('AFLATOX') || s.includes('AFM1')) return 'AFM1';
81	  if (s.includes('COLIFORM')) return 'COLIFORM';

1	// Package auth owns tokens and credentials: JWT issue/verify, OTP generation
2	// and HMAC hashing, opaque refresh tokens. Nothing secret is ever stored in
3	// plaintext — OTPs and refresh tokens live in the DB only as HMAC-SHA256
4	// digests.
5	package auth
6	
7	import (
8		"fmt"
9		"time"
10	
11		"github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v5"
12		"github.com/google/uuid"
13	
14		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/domain"
15	)
16	
17	// Token kinds. A SESSION token proves "this phone logged in"; a ROLE token
18	// additionally pins one active role assignment + org scope (the role switcher
19	// simply issues a fresh ROLE token).
20	const (
21		TokenKindSession = "session"
22		TokenKindRole    = "role"
23	)
24	
25	// Claims is the JWT payload.
26	type Claims struct {
27		PartyID          string `json:"pid"`
28		Phone            string `json:"phn"`
29		KYCTier          string `json:"kyc"`
30		Kind             string `json:"knd"`
31		RoleAssignmentID string `json:"rid,omitempty"`
32		RoleCode         string `json:"rol,omitempty"`
33		OrgUnitID        string `json:"org,omitempty"`
34		OrgType          string `json:"ogt,omitempty"`
35		jwt.RegisteredClaims
36	}
37	
38	// JWTManager issues and parses access tokens.
39	type JWTManager struct {
40		secret []byte
41		ttl    time.Duration
42	}
43	
44	// NewJWTManager builds a manager with the shared HS256 secret and access TTL.
45	func NewJWTManager(secret string, ttl time.Duration) *JWTManager {
46		return &JWTManager{secret: []byte(secret), ttl: ttl}
47	}
48	
49	// IssueSessionToken returns a SESSION-kind access token for a logged-in party.
50	// ObjectIDs travel in claims as hex strings (JWTs are JSON).
51	func (m *JWTManager) IssueSessionToken(p domain.Party) (string, error) {
52		return m.sign(Claims{
53			PartyID: p.ID.Hex(),
54			Phone:   p.Phone,
55			KYCTier: p.KYCTier,
56			Kind:    TokenKindSession,
57		})
58	}
59	
60	// IssueRoleToken returns a ROLE-kind access token pinned to one assignment.
61	func (m *JWTManager) IssueRoleToken(p domain.Party, ra domain.RoleAssignment, orgType string) (string, error) {
62		return m.sign(Claims{
63			PartyID:          p.ID.Hex(),
64			Phone:            p.Phone,
65			KYCTier:          p.KYCTier,
66			Kind:             TokenKindRole,
67			RoleAssignmentID: ra.ID.Hex(),
68			RoleCode:         ra.RoleCode,
69			OrgUnitID:        ra.OrgUnitID.Hex(),
70			OrgType:          orgType,
71		})
72	}
73	
74	func (m *JWTManager) sign(c Claims) (string, error) {
75		now := time.Now()
76		c.RegisteredClaims = jwt.RegisteredClaims{
77			Issuer:    "saathi-backend",
78			Subject:   c.PartyID,
79			IssuedAt:  jwt.NewNumericDate(now),
80			ExpiresAt: jwt.NewNumericDate(now.Add(m.ttl)),
81			ID:        uuid.NewString(),
82		}
83		return jwt.NewWithClaims(jwt.SigningMethodHS256, c).SignedString(m.secret)
84	}
85	
86	// Parse validates signature+expiry and returns the claims.
87	func (m *JWTManager) Parse(token string) (*Claims, error) {
88		parsed, err := jwt.ParseWithClaims(token, &Claims{},
89			func(t *jwt.Token) (any, error) { return m.secret, nil },
90			jwt.WithValidMethods([]string{jwt.SigningMethodHS256.Alg()}),
91			jwt.WithIssuer("saathi-backend"),
92		)
93		if err != nil {
94			return nil, fmt.Errorf("parse token: %w", err)
95		}
96		claims, ok := parsed.Claims.(*Claims)
97		if !ok || !parsed.Valid {
98			return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid token claims")
99		}
100		return claims, nil
101	}

1	package auth

3	import (
4		"context"

7	
8	// Actor is the authenticated caller extracted from a verified token and
9	// stored on the request context by the auth middleware.
10	type Actor struct {
11		PartyID          string
12		Phone            string
13		KYCTier          string
14		Kind             string // session | role
15		RoleAssignmentID string
16		RoleCode         string
17		OrgUnitID        string
18		OrgType          string
19	}
20	
21	// HasRole reports whether the actor operates under one of the given roles.
22	func (a Actor) HasRole(roles ...string) bool {
23		for _, r := range roles {
24			if a.RoleCode == r {
25				return true
26			}
27		}
28		return false
29	}
30	
31	type actorCtxKey struct{}
32	
33	// actorHolder is a mutable cell installed by OUTER middleware (audit) so
34	// identity established by INNER middleware (Authenticate) can flow back out.
35	// Context values only propagate inward; the shared pointer bridges the gap.
36	type actorHolder struct {
37		mu sync.Mutex
38		a  *Actor
39	}
40	
41	type actorHolderCtxKey struct{}
42	
43	// WithActorHolder installs an empty actor holder on the context. Middleware
44	// mounted before authentication uses it to observe the actor after the
45	// handler chain ran.
46	func WithActorHolder(ctx context.Context) context.Context {
47		return context.WithValue(ctx, actorHolderCtxKey{}, &actorHolder{})
48	}
49	
50	// HeldActor returns the actor captured by an inner WithActor call, if a
51	// holder was installed and authentication happened.
52	func HeldActor(ctx context.Context) (Actor, bool) {
53		h, ok := ctx.Value(actorHolderCtxKey{}).(*actorHolder)
54		if !ok {
55			return Actor{}, false
56		}
57		h.mu.Lock()
58		defer h.mu.Unlock()
59		if h.a == nil {
60			return Actor{}, false
61		}
62		return *h.a, true
63	}
64	
65	// WithActor stores the actor on the context, and also fills the outward
66	// actor holder when one was installed upstream (see WithActorHolder).
67	func WithActor(ctx context.Context, a Actor) context.Context {
68		if h, ok := ctx.Value(actorHolderCtxKey{}).(*actorHolder); ok {
69			h.mu.Lock()
70			cp := a
71			h.a = &cp
72			h.mu.Unlock()
73		}
74		return context.WithValue(ctx, actorCtxKey{}, a)
75	}
76	
77	// ActorFrom retrieves the actor, if any.
78	func ActorFrom(ctx context.Context) (Actor, bool) {
79		a, ok := ctx.Value(actorCtxKey{}).(Actor)
80		return a, ok
81	}

1	package auth
2	
3	import (
4		"crypto/hmac"
5		"crypto/rand"
6		"crypto/sha256"
7		"crypto/subtle"
8		"encoding/base64"
9		"encoding/hex"
10		"fmt"
11		"math/big"
12	)
13	
14	// GenerateNumericOTP returns a cryptographically random n-digit code.
15	func GenerateNumericOTP(n int) (string, error) {
16		if n <= 0 || n > 10 {
17			return "", fmt.Errorf("otp length out of range: %d", n)
18		}
19		max := big.NewInt(1)
20		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
21			max.Mul(max, big.NewInt(10))
22		}
23		v, err := rand.Int(rand.Reader, max)
24		if err != nil {
25			return "", fmt.Errorf("otp entropy: %w", err)
26		}
27		return fmt.Sprintf("%0*d", n, v), nil
28	}
29	
30	// HMACHash returns hex(HMAC-SHA256(secret, parts joined by '|')). Used for
31	// OTP codes (keyed to the phone) and refresh tokens, so a DB leak alone
32	// reveals no usable credentials.
33	func HMACHash(secret string, parts ...string) string {
34		mac := hmac.New(sha256.New, []byte(secret))
35		for i, p := range parts {
36			if i > 0 {
37				mac.Write([]byte{'|'})
38			}
39			mac.Write([]byte(p))
40		}
41		return hex.EncodeToString(mac.Sum(nil))
42	}
43	
44	// ConstantTimeEqual compares two hex digests without timing leaks.
45	func ConstantTimeEqual(a, b string) bool {
46		return subtle.ConstantTimeCompare([]byte(a), []byte(b)) == 1
47	}
48	
49	// RandomToken returns a URL-safe random token with nBytes of entropy —
50	// used for opaque refresh tokens.
51	func RandomToken(nBytes int) (string, error) {
52		buf := make([]byte, nBytes)
53		if _, err := rand.Read(buf); err != nil {
54			return "", fmt.Errorf("token entropy: %w", err)
55		}
56		return base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString(buf), nil
57	}

1	package httpx
2	
3	import (
4		"encoding/json"
5		"errors"
6		"log/slog"
7		"net/http"
8	)
9	
10	// envelope is the uniform success shape: {"data": ..., "meta": {...}?}.
11	type envelope struct {
12		Data any `json:"data"`
13		Meta any `json:"meta,omitempty"`
14	}
15	
16	type errEnvelope struct {
17		Error *AppError `json:"error"`
18	}
19	
20	// JSON writes a success response wrapped in the standard envelope.
21	func JSON(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, data any) {
22		writeJSON(w, status, envelope{Data: data})
23	}
24	
25	// JSONMeta writes a success response with list metadata (pagination etc.).
26	func JSONMeta(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, data, meta any) {
27		writeJSON(w, status, envelope{Data: data, Meta: meta})
28	}
29	
30	// Error writes the standard error envelope. Unexpected (non-AppError) errors
31	// become an opaque 500 and the cause is logged with the request context.
32	func Error(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, err error) {
33		var ae *AppError
34		if !errors.As(err, &ae) {
35			ae = Internal(err)
36		}
37		if ae.Status >= 500 {
38			slog.ErrorContext(r.Context(), "request failed",
39				slog.String("method", r.Method),
40				slog.String("path", r.URL.Path),
41				slog.String("code", ae.Code),
42				slog.Any("cause", ae.CauseOrSelf()),
43			)
44		}
45		writeJSON(w, ae.Status, errEnvelope{Error: ae})
46	}
47	
48	// CauseOrSelf returns the wrapped cause if present, else the error itself.
49	func (e *AppError) CauseOrSelf() error {
50		if e.cause != nil {
51			return e.cause
52		}
53		return e
54	}
55	
56	func writeJSON(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, v any) {
57		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json; charset=utf-8")
58		w.WriteHeader(status)
59		_ = json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(v)
60	}

16	// DecodeJSON strictly decodes the request body into dst. It enforces the

19		r.Body = http.MaxBytesReader(nil, r.Body, maxBodyBytes)
20		dec := json.NewDecoder(r.Body)
21		if err := dec.Decode(dst); err != nil {
22			var maxErr *http.MaxBytesError
23			switch {
24			case errors.As(err, &maxErr):
25				return BadRequest("BODY_TOO_LARGE", fmt.Sprintf("request body exceeds %d bytes", maxBodyBytes))
26			case errors.Is(err, io.EOF):
27				return BadRequest("EMPTY_BODY", "request body is required")
28			default:
29				return BadRequest("MALFORMED_JSON", "request body is not valid JSON: "+err.Error())
30			}
31		}
32		if dec.More() {
33			return BadRequest("MALFORMED_JSON", "request body must contain a single JSON value")
34		}
35		return nil
36	}
37	
38	// Page holds validated pagination parameters.
39	type Page struct {
40		Limit  int64 `json:"limit"`
41		Offset int64 `json:"offset"`
42	}
43	
44	// ParsePage reads ?limit= and ?offset= with sane bounds (default 50, max 200).
45	func ParsePage(r *http.Request) Page {
46		p := Page{Limit: 50, Offset: 0}
47		if v := r.URL.Query().Get("limit"); v != "" {
48			if n, err := strconv.ParseInt(v, 10, 64); err == nil && n > 0 {
49				p.Limit = min(n, 200)
50			}
51		}
52		if v := r.URL.Query().Get("offset"); v != "" {
53			if n, err := strconv.ParseInt(v, 10, 64); err == nil && n >= 0 {
54				p.Offset = n
55			}
56		}
57		return p
58	}
59

7	/**

9	 * temperature logging, delivery to the BMC. Aligned with the Go backend
10	 * (parag-saathi-be, internal/modules/logistics, mounted at /logistics):
11	 *
12	 *   POST /logistics/trips                                   → plan a route trip
13	 *   GET  /logistics/trips ?union_id&date&van_rider_party_id → list trips
14	 *   GET  /logistics/trips/{tripID}                          → one trip
15	 *   POST /logistics/trips/{tripID}/stops/{consignmentID}/pickup → record pickup
16	 *   POST /logistics/trips/{tripID}/cold-chain              → log transit temp
17	 *   POST /logistics/trips/{tripID}/deliver                 → hand load to a BMC
18	 *
19	 * NOTE: the backend only ships the *request* structs (logistics_models.go);
20	 * its trip/stop/intake *responses* embed `domain.*` structs that are not in
21	 * the shared contract snapshot. The Wire* shapes below are therefore the
22	 * inferred snake_case serialisation (see `issues` in the sync report) and
23	 * fill safe defaults for any field the wire may omit.
24	 */
25	
26	/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
27	/* Wire shapes (snake_case, inferred from the domain + BE conventions) */
28	/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
29	
30	interface WireTripStop {
31	  dcs_id: string;
32	  /** The pooled DCS consignment collected at this stop (frontend `lotId`). */
33	  consignment_id?: string;
34	  planned_time?: string;
35	  arrived_at?: string;
36	  lat?: number;
37	  lng?: number;
38	  photo_uri?: string;
39	  collected?: boolean;
40	  status?: string;
41	}
42	
43	interface WireTrip {
44	  id: string;
45	  code?: string;
46	  route_name?: string;
47	  van_rider_party_id?: string;
48	  van_no?: string;
49	  union_id?: string;
50	  date: string;
51	  shift: string;
52	  stops?: WireTripStop[];
53	  bmc_id?: string;
54	  status?: string;
55	  departed_at?: string;
56	  completed_at?: string;
57	}
58	
59	interface WireBmcIntake {
60	  id: string;
61	  bmc_id: string;
62	  trip_id: string;
63	  lot_ids?: string[];
64	  consignment_ids?: string[];
65	  silo_lot_code?: string;
66	  received_at?: string;
67	  temp_c?: number;
68	  status?: string;
69	}
70	
71	/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
72	/* Wire → domain mappers                                               */
73	/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
74	
75	function mapTripStatus(s?: string): RouteTrip['status'] {
76	  switch (s) {
77	    case 'ASSIGNED':
78	    case 'IN_PROGRESS':
79	    case 'DELIVERED_TO_BMC':
80	    case 'COMPLETED':
81	      return s;
82	    case 'PLANNED':
83	    case 'CREATED':
84	      return 'ASSIGNED';
85	    case 'STARTED':
86	    case 'IN_TRANSIT':
87	      return 'IN_PROGRESS';
88	    case 'DELIVERED':
89	      return 'DELIVERED_TO_BMC';
90	    default:
91	      return 'ASSIGNED';
92	  }
93	}
94	
95	function mapIntakeStatus(s?: string): BmcIntake['status'] {
96	  switch (s) {
97	    case 'CHILLED':
98	    case 'DISPATCHED_TO_PLANT':
99	    case 'REJECTED':
100	      return s;
101	    default:
102	      return 'RECEIVED';
103	  }
104	}
105	
106	function mapStop(w: WireTripStop): RouteStop {
107	  return {
108	    dcsId: w.dcs_id,
109	    lotId: w.consignment_id || undefined,
110	    plannedTime: w.planned_time ?? '',
111	    arrivedAt: w.arrived_at,
112	    geo: w.lat != null && w.lng != null ? { lat: w.lat, lng: w.lng } : undefined,
113	    photoUri: w.photo_uri || undefined,
114	    collected: w.collected ?? (w.status ? w.status !== 'PENDING' : false),
115	  };
116	}
117	
118	function mapTrip(w: WireTrip): RouteTrip {
119	  return {
120	    id: w.id,
121	    code: w.code || w.route_name || w.id,
122	    riderPartyId: w.van_rider_party_id ?? '',
123	    vanNo: w.van_no ?? '',
124	    date: w.date,
125	    shift: w.shift === 'EVENING' ? 'EVENING' : 'MORNING',
126	    stops: (w.stops ?? []).map(mapStop),
127	    bmcId: w.bmc_id ?? '',
128	    status: mapTripStatus(w.status),
129	    departedAt: w.departed_at,
130	    completedAt: w.completed_at,
131	  };
132	}
133	
134	function mapIntake(w: WireBmcIntake): BmcIntake {
135	  return {
136	    id: w.id,
137	    bmcId: w.bmc_id,
138	    tripId: w.trip_id,
139	    lotIds: w.lot_ids ?? w.consignment_ids ?? [],
140	    siloLotCode: w.silo_lot_code ?? '',
141	    receivedAt: w.received_at ?? new Date().toISOString(),
142	    tempC: w.temp_c ?? 0,
143	    status: mapIntakeStatus(w.status),
144	  };
145	}
146	
147	/** Derive a best-effort intake from a delivered trip when the backend
148	 *  deliver response returns only the trip (no separate intake object). */
149	function intakeFromTrip(trip: RouteTrip): BmcIntake {
150	  return {
151	    id: '',
152	    bmcId: trip.bmcId,
153	    tripId: trip.id,
154	    lotIds: trip.stops.filter((s) => s.collected && s.lotId).map((s) => s.lotId as string),
155	    siloLotCode: '',
156	    receivedAt: trip.completedAt ?? new Date().toISOString(),
157	    tempC: 0,
158	    status: 'RECEIVED',
159	  };
160	}
161	
162	function asTripArray(raw: unknown): WireTrip[] {
163	  if (Array.isArray(raw)) return raw as WireTrip[];
164	  const wrapped = (raw as { trips?: WireTrip[] } | null)?.trips;
165	  return Array.isArray(wrapped) ? wrapped : [];
166	}
167	
168	/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
169	/* Endpoints                                                           */
170	/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
171	
172	export const getMyTrip = endpoint<{ riderPartyId: string; date: string }, RouteTrip | null>({
173	  method: 'GET',
174	  path: ({ riderPartyId, date }) =>
175	    `/logistics/trips?van_rider_party_id=${riderPartyId}&date=${date}`,
176	  // GET /logistics/trips returns a filtered list; a rider has at most one trip
177	  // per date+van, so take the first (or null when none is planned).
178	  mapResponse: (raw) => {
179	    const trips = asTripArray(raw);
180	    return trips.length ? mapTrip(trips[0]) : null;
181	  },
182	  mock: ({ riderPartyId, date }, db) =>
183	    db.trips.find((t) => t.riderPartyId === riderPartyId && t.date === date) ?? null,
184	});
185	
186	export const listTrips = endpoint<{ date?: string } | void, RouteTrip[]>({
187	  method: 'GET',
188	  path: (input) => `/logistics/trips${input?.date ? `?date=${input.date}` : ''}`,
189	  mapResponse: (raw) =>
190	    asTripArray(raw)
191	      .map(mapTrip)
192	      .sort((a, b) => b.date.localeCompare(a.date)),
193	  mock: (input, db) =>
194	    (input?.date ? db.trips.filter((t) => t.date === input.date) : db.trips).sort((a, b) =>
195	      b.date.localeCompare(a.date),
196	    ),
197	});
198	
199	// TODO(backend): no endpoint yet - mock only.
200	// The backend has no "start an already-planned trip" route: POST /logistics/trips
201	// *creates* a trip (createTripRequest: route_name, union_id, date, shift,
202	// van_rider_party_id, stops[]), which the {tripId}-only input here cannot build.
203	// Left on the mock path until the FE input carries a full plan or the BE adds a
204	// /trips/{tripID}/start transition.
205	export const startTrip = endpoint<{ tripId: string }, RouteTrip>({
206	  method: 'POST',
207	  path: ({ tripId }) => `/logistics/trips/${tripId}/start`,
208	  mock: ({ tripId }, db) => {
209	    const trip = db.trips.find((t) => t.id === tripId);
210	    if (!trip) throw new ApiError(404, 'TRIP_NOT_FOUND', `Unknown trip ${tripId}`);
211	    if (trip.status !== 'ASSIGNED') throw new ApiError(409, 'ALREADY_STARTED', 'Trip already started');
212	    trip.status = 'IN_PROGRESS';
213	    trip.departedAt = new Date().toISOString();
214	    audit(db, {
215	      actorPartyId: trip.riderPartyId,
216	      actorRole: 'VAN_RIDER',
217	      action: 'TRIP_STARTED',
218	      subject: trip.code,
219	      detail: `Van ${trip.vanNo} departed on ${trip.stops.length}-stop route`,
220	    });
221	    return trip;
222	  },
223	});
224	
225	/**
226	 * Record pickup at a DCS stop: the consignment scan, a geotag of where it was
227	 * collected, and a milk photo for verification (no temperature - the cold-chain
228	 * temperature is logged by the chilling branch, not the van).
229	 */
230	export const recordPickup = endpoint<
231	  { tripId: string; dcsId: string; geo?: GeoPoint; photoUri?: string; sealCode?: string },
232	  RouteTrip
233	>({
234	  method: 'POST',
235	  // Backend keys the pickup by the pooled consignment, not the DCS. The FE input
236	  // only carries dcsId, so it stands in for {consignmentID} here - see issues:
237	  // the input type should eventually carry the consignment/lot id.
238	  path: ({ tripId, dcsId }) => `/logistics/trips/${tripId}/stops/${dcsId}/pickup`,
239	  mapRequest: ({ geo, photoUri, sealCode }) => ({
240	    lat: geo?.lat,
241	    lng: geo?.lng,
242	    photo_uri: photoUri,
243	    seal_code: sealCode,
244	  }),
245	  mapResponse: (raw) => mapTrip(raw as WireTrip),
246	  mock: ({ tripId, dcsId, geo, photoUri, sealCode }, db) => {
247	    const trip = db.trips.find((t) => t.id === tripId);
248	    if (!trip) throw new ApiError(404, 'TRIP_NOT_FOUND', `Unknown trip ${tripId}`);
249	    const stop = trip.stops.find((s) => s.dcsId === dcsId);
250	    if (!stop) throw new ApiError(404, 'STOP_NOT_FOUND', 'This DCS is not on the route');
251	    if (!stop.lotId) {
252	      throw new ApiError(409, 'LOT_NOT_DISPATCHED', 'The samiti has not dispatched a consignment yet');
253	    }
254	    if (stop.collected) throw new ApiError(409, 'ALREADY_COLLECTED', 'Stop already collected');
255	    if (!photoUri) {
256	      throw new ApiError(422, 'PHOTO_REQUIRED', 'Add a milk photo to verify the collection');
257	    }
258	    const lot = db.lots.find((l) => l.id === stop.lotId);
259	    // Seal verification (§6.4): a sealed consignment must have its seal confirmed
260	    // at pickup, and the confirmed code must match the one frozen at dispatch, so
261	    // milk cannot be swapped between the DCS and the branch.
262	    if (lot?.sealCode) {
263	      if (!sealCode) {
264	        throw new ApiError(422, 'SEAL_REQUIRED', 'Confirm the consignment seal before pickup');
265	      }
266	      if (sealCode !== lot.sealCode) {
267	        throw new ApiError(422, 'SEAL_MISMATCH', 'Seal does not match the dispatched consignment - do not collect');
268	      }
269	    }
270	    stop.arrivedAt = new Date().toISOString();
271	    stop.geo = geo;
272	    stop.photoUri = photoUri;
273	    stop.sealCode = sealCode ?? lot?.sealCode;
274	    stop.collected = true;
275	    if (geo) {
276	      trip.lastKnownGeo = geo;
277	      trip.lastLocationAt = stop.arrivedAt;
278	    }
279	    if (lot) lot.status = 'PICKED_UP';
280	    audit(db, {
281	      actorPartyId: trip.riderPartyId,
282	      actorRole: 'VAN_RIDER',
283	      action: 'PICKUP_RECORDED',
284	      subject: lot?.consignmentCode ?? stop.lotId,
285	      detail: `Collected with geotag + photo + seal ${stop.sealCode ?? 'n/a'}`,
286	    });
287	    if (lot) {
288	      appendChainEvent(db, {
289	        kind: 'PICKUP',
290	        subjectType: 'LOT',
291	        subjectId: lot.id,
292	        actorPartyId: trip.riderPartyId,
293	        detail: `Seal ${stop.sealCode ?? 'n/a'} confirmed; geotag + photo`,
294	      });
295	    }
296	    return trip;
297	  },
298	});
299	
300	/** Live-location breadcrumb from the van during the trip (best-effort). */
301	// TODO(backend): live-location stream not exposed yet - mock only
302	export const pushVanLocation = endpoint<{ tripId: string; geo: GeoPoint }, RouteTrip>({
303	  method: 'POST',
304	  path: ({ tripId }) => `/logistics/trips/${tripId}/location`,
305	  mapRequest: ({ geo }) => ({ lat: geo.lat, lng: geo.lng }),
306	  mock: ({ tripId, geo }, db) => {
307	    const trip = db.trips.find((t) => t.id === tripId);
308	    if (!trip) throw new ApiError(404, 'TRIP_NOT_FOUND', `Unknown trip ${tripId}`);
309	    trip.lastKnownGeo = geo;
310	    trip.lastLocationAt = new Date().toISOString();
311	    return trip;
312	  },
313	});
314	
315	/**
316	 * Deliver collected consignments to the chilling branch (BMC) - pools them into
317	 * a silo lot the branch will chill. The branch logs the tank temperature, so no
318	 * temperature is captured here.
319	 */
320	export const deliverToBmc = endpoint<
321	  { tripId: string; bmcId?: string },
322	  { trip: RouteTrip; intake: BmcIntake }
323	>({
324	  method: 'POST',
325	  path: ({ tripId }) => `/logistics/trips/${tripId}/deliver`,
326	  // deliverRequest wants bmc_id: sourced from trip.bmcId at the call site and
327	  // passed in, so the http deliver targets the right chilling branch.
328	  mapRequest: ({ bmcId }) => ({ bmc_id: bmcId ?? '' }),
329	  mapResponse: (raw) => {
330	    const d = (raw ?? {}) as { trip?: WireTrip; intake?: WireBmcIntake } & Partial<WireTrip>;
331	    const wireTrip = d.trip ?? (d as WireTrip);
332	    const trip = mapTrip(wireTrip);
333	    const intake = d.intake ? mapIntake(d.intake) : intakeFromTrip(trip);
334	    return { trip, intake };
335	  },
336	  mock: ({ tripId }, db) => {
337	    const trip = db.trips.find((t) => t.id === tripId);
338	    if (!trip) throw new ApiError(404, 'TRIP_NOT_FOUND', `Unknown trip ${tripId}`);
339	    const collectedLots = trip.stops.filter((s) => s.collected && s.lotId).map((s) => s.lotId!);
340	    if (collectedLots.length === 0) {
341	      throw new ApiError(409, 'NOTHING_COLLECTED', 'No collected consignments on board');
342	    }
343	    trip.status = 'DELIVERED_TO_BMC';
344	    trip.completedAt = new Date().toISOString();
345	    const intake: BmcIntake = {
346	      id: nextId('intake'),
347	      bmcId: trip.bmcId,
348	      tripId: trip.id,
349	      lotIds: collectedLots,
350	      siloLotCode: intakeCode('BBK', trip.date, trip.shift),
351	      receivedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
352	      tempC: 0, // logged by the branch when it chills the lot
353	      status: 'RECEIVED',
354	    };
355	    db.intakes.push(intake);
356	    for (const lotId of collectedLots) {
357	      const lot = db.lots.find((l) => l.id === lotId);
358	      if (lot) lot.status = 'AT_BMC';
359	    }
360	    audit(db, {
361	      actorPartyId: trip.riderPartyId,
362	      actorRole: 'VAN_RIDER',
363	      action: 'DELIVERED_TO_BMC',
364	      subject: intake.siloLotCode,
365	      detail: `${collectedLots.length} consignments handed to the chilling branch`,
366	    });
367	    appendChainEvent(db, {
368	      kind: 'INTAKE',
369	      subjectType: 'INTAKE',
370	      subjectId: intake.id,
371	      actorPartyId: trip.riderPartyId,
372	      detail: `${intake.siloLotCode}: ${collectedLots.length} consignments received at the branch`,
373	    });
374	    return { trip, intake };
375	  },
376	});

9	// Party statuses.

15	// Party is the single identity record per human (blueprint §4.1):
16	// one phone number = one Party = many org-scoped RoleAssignments.
17	// `_id` is a generated ObjectID; `phone` is the unique natural key used for
18	// login — relations always reference the ObjectID, never the phone.

22		FullName          string             `bson:"full_name,omitempty"          json:"full_name,omitempty"`

25		Status            string             `bson:"status"        json:"status"`

27		UpdatedAt         time.Time          `bson:"updated_at"    json:"updated_at"`

33		RoleAssignmentRevoked = "REVOKED"
34	)
35	
36	// RoleAssignment grants one role to one party inside one org unit for a
37	// validity window. Revoking a Sacheev after an election is a single record
38	// update — never an account deletion (blueprint §4.1).
39	type RoleAssignment struct {
40		ID        primitive.ObjectID  `bson:"_id,omitempty" json:"id"`
41		PartyID   primitive.ObjectID  `bson:"party_id"      json:"party_id"`
42		RoleCode  string              `bson:"role_code"     json:"role_code"`
43		OrgUnitID primitive.ObjectID  `bson:"org_unit_id"   json:"org_unit_id"`
44		GrantedBy *primitive.ObjectID `bson:"granted_by,omitempty" json:"granted_by,omitempty"`
45		ValidFrom time.Time           `bson:"valid_from"    json:"valid_from"`
46		ValidTo   *time.Time          `bson:"valid_to,omitempty"   json:"valid_to,omitempty"` // nil = open-ended
47		Status    string              `bson:"status"        json:"status"`
48		RevokedAt *time.Time          `bson:"revoked_at,omitempty" json:"revoked_at,omitempty"`
49		RevokedBy *primitive.ObjectID `bson:"revoked_by,omitempty" json:"revoked_by,omitempty"`
50		CreatedAt time.Time           `bson:"created_at"    json:"created_at"`
51	}
52	
53	// UsableAt reports whether the assignment is active and inside its validity
54	// window at instant t.
55	func (ra RoleAssignment) UsableAt(t time.Time) bool {
56		if ra.Status != RoleAssignmentActive {
57			return false
58		}
59		if t.Before(ra.ValidFrom) {
60			return false
61		}
62		if ra.ValidTo != nil && t.After(*ra.ValidTo) {
63			return false
64		}
65		return true
66	}

33	// OrgUnit is a node in the cooperative hierarchy.
34	//
35	// ID scheme: `_id` is a generated ObjectID (relations always reference it);
36	// Code is the human-readable unique business key (e.g. "DCS-01842") used for
37	// display, lookups and seed idempotency — never for joins.
38	//
39	// Path holds the ObjectIDs of all ancestors from the root down to (and
40	// excluding) this node — denormalised so "is X inside Y's scope" is a single
41	// indexed array-containment check with no recursive queries on the hot path.

1	import AsyncStorage from '@react-native-async-storage/async-storage';
2	import type { MockDb } from '@/core/mocks/db';
3	
4	/**
5	 * API transport layer, aligned with the real Go backend (parag-saathi-be):
6	 *   - success envelope  { "data": ..., "meta"?: ... }
7	 *   - error envelope    { "error": { "code", "message", "details"? } }
8	 *   - bearer auth with a SESSION/ROLE access token + rotating refresh token
9	 *     (POST /auth/refresh) - a 401 triggers one single-flight refresh + retry
10	 *
11	 * Every endpoint in src/core/api/endpoints/ is declared once with:
12	 *   - its HTTP method + path        → the contract the backend implements
13	 *   - optional mapRequest/mapResponse → snake_case wire ⇄ camelCase domain
14	 *   - a mock implementation         → runs fully in-app against the seeded
15	 *                                     mock DB until the backend is connected
16	 *
17	 * Switch modes with EXPO_PUBLIC_API_MODE (mock | http) - see .env.example and
18	 * docs/api-contract.md. No feature code changes when the backend lands.
19	 */
20	
21	export type ApiMode = 'mock' | 'http';
22	
23	// Authentic by default: the app talks to the real Saathi backend. `mock` is an
24	// explicit offline-development fallback only (never the shipped experience).
25	const MODE: ApiMode = (process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_API_MODE as ApiMode) || 'http';
26	const BASE: string = process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL || 'http://localhost:8080/api/v1';
27	
28	/** The active API mode ('http' = real backend, 'mock' = in-app fixtures). */
29	export const API_MODE: ApiMode = MODE;
30	/** The Saathi backend base URL every endpoint is resolved against. */
31	export const API_BASE_URL: string = BASE;
32	
33	const ACCESS_KEY = 'saathi-access-token';
34	const REFRESH_KEY = 'saathi-refresh-token';
35	
36	/** In-memory token cache, persisted to AsyncStorage (hydrated at app start). */
37	let accessToken: string | null = null;
38	let refreshToken: string | null = null;
39	
40	export function getAuthToken(): string | null {
41	  return accessToken;
42	}
43	export function getRefreshToken(): string | null {
44	  return refreshToken;
45	}
46	
47	/** Store both tokens (login / refresh rotation). */
48	export function setTokens(t: { access: string | null; refresh: string | null }): void {
49	  accessToken = t.access;
50	  refreshToken = t.refresh;
51	  if (t.access) void AsyncStorage.setItem(ACCESS_KEY, t.access);
52	  else void AsyncStorage.removeItem(ACCESS_KEY);
53	  if (t.refresh) void AsyncStorage.setItem(REFRESH_KEY, t.refresh);
54	  else void AsyncStorage.removeItem(REFRESH_KEY);
55	}
56	
57	/** Swap only the access token (role-select issues a ROLE-kind token). */
58	export function setAccessToken(token: string): void {
59	  accessToken = token;
60	  void AsyncStorage.setItem(ACCESS_KEY, token);
61	}
62	
63	export function clearTokens(): void {
64	  setTokens({ access: null, refresh: null });
65	}
66	
67	/** Call once at startup (root layout) before authenticated requests. */
68	export async function hydrateAuthToken(): Promise<void> {
69	  const [a, r] = await Promise.all([
70	    AsyncStorage.getItem(ACCESS_KEY),
71	    AsyncStorage.getItem(REFRESH_KEY),
72	  ]);
73	  accessToken = a;
74	  refreshToken = r;
75	}
76	
77	/** Registered by the root layout: fired when auth is irrecoverably lost. */
78	let onUnauthorized: (() => void) | null = null;
79	export function setOnUnauthorized(cb: (() => void) | null): void {
80	  onUnauthorized = cb;
81	}
82	
83	export class ApiError extends Error {
84	  constructor(
85	    public status: number,
86	    public code: string,
87	    message: string,
88	    public details?: unknown,
89	  ) {
90	    super(message);
91	    this.name = 'ApiError';
92	  }
93	}
94	
95	type HttpMethod = 'GET' | 'POST' | 'PUT' | 'PATCH' | 'DELETE';
96	
97	export interface EndpointSpec<TIn, TOut> {
98	  method: HttpMethod;
99	  /** REST path for http mode; also documents the backend contract */
100	  path: (input: TIn) => string;
101	  /** camelCase input → snake_case wire body (http mode only) */
102	  mapRequest?: (input: TIn) => unknown;
103	  /** snake_case wire data → domain shape (http mode only) */
104	  mapResponse?: (raw: unknown) => TOut;
105	  /** In-app implementation for mock mode */
106	  mock: (input: TIn, db: MockDb) => TOut | Promise<TOut>;
107	}
108	
109	function sleep(ms: number): Promise<void> {
110	  return new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));
111	}
112	
113	/** JSON-safe deep clone (results are plain data; keeps Hermes compatibility). */
114	function deepClone<T>(value: T): T {
115	  return value === undefined ? value : (JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value)) as T);
116	}
117	
118	/** Raw http call: bearer header, envelope unwrap, AppError mapping. */
119	async function httpCall(method: HttpMethod, path: string, body: unknown): Promise<unknown> {
120	  const hasBody = method !== 'GET' && method !== 'DELETE' && body !== undefined;
121	  const res = await fetch(BASE + path, {
122	    method,
123	    headers: {
124	      Accept: 'application/json',
125	      ...(hasBody ? { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } : {}),
126	      ...(accessToken ? { Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}` } : {}),
127	    },
128	    body: hasBody ? JSON.stringify(body) : undefined,
129	  });
130	  const text = await res.text().catch(() => '');
131	  let json: unknown;
132	  try {
133	    json = text ? JSON.parse(text) : undefined;
134	  } catch {
135	    json = undefined;
136	  }
137	  if (!res.ok) {
138	    const err = (json as { error?: { code?: string; message?: string; details?: unknown } })
139	      ?.error;
140	    throw new ApiError(
141	      res.status,
142	      err?.code ?? `HTTP_${res.status}`,
143	      err?.message ?? res.statusText,
144	      err?.details,
145	    );
146	  }
147	  // Success envelope: { data, meta? } - unwrap data; tolerate bare payloads.
148	  if (json && typeof json === 'object' && 'data' in (json as Record<string, unknown>)) {
149	    return (json as { data: unknown }).data;
150	  }
151	  return json;
152	}
153	
154	/** Single-flight refresh: rotate the token pair via POST /auth/refresh. */
155	let refreshInFlight: Promise<boolean> | null = null;
156	async function tryRefresh(): Promise<boolean> {
157	  if (!refreshToken) return false;
158	  refreshInFlight ??= (async () => {
159	    try {
160	      const data = (await httpCall('POST', '/auth/refresh', {
161	        refresh_token: refreshToken,
162	      })) as { access_token: string; refresh_token: string };
163	      setTokens({ access: data.access_token, refresh: data.refresh_token });
164	      return true;
165	    } catch {
166	      return false;
167	    } finally {
168	      refreshInFlight = null;
169	    }
170	  })();
171	  return refreshInFlight;
172	}
173	
174	/** Declare a typed API endpoint. Returns the callable used by feature code. */
175	export function endpoint<TIn = void, TOut = unknown>(
176	  spec: EndpointSpec<TIn, TOut>,
177	): (input: TIn) => Promise<TOut> {
178	  return async (input: TIn): Promise<TOut> => {
179	    if (MODE === 'mock') {
180	      const { db } = await import('@/core/mocks/db');
181	      // Simulated network latency so loading states are honest
182	      await sleep(120 + Math.random() * 230);
183	      const result = await spec.mock(input, db);
184	      // Deep-clone so callers can never mutate the mock store through results
185	      return deepClone(result);
186	    }
187	
188	    const path = spec.path(input);
189	    const body = spec.mapRequest ? spec.mapRequest(input) : (input as unknown);
190	    try {
191	      const raw = await httpCall(spec.method, path, body);
192	      return spec.mapResponse ? spec.mapResponse(raw) : (raw as TOut);
193	    } catch (e) {
194	      // One refresh + retry on expired access tokens (never for /auth/* itself)
195	      if (e instanceof ApiError && e.status === 401 && !path.startsWith('/auth/')) {
196	        if (await tryRefresh()) {
197	          const raw = await httpCall(spec.method, path, body);
198	          return spec.mapResponse ? spec.mapResponse(raw) : (raw as TOut);
199	        }
200	        clearTokens();
201	        onUnauthorized?.();
202	      }
203	      throw e;
204	    }
205	  };
206	}

109	function ledgerPayload(e: {
110	  kind: string;
111	  subjectType: string;
112	  subjectId: string;
113	  at: string;
114	  clientEventId: string;

121	/**

123	 * audit() (a mutable operational log), each link's eventHash is derived from the
124	 * previous link, so the chain is tamper-evident end to end. Every chain writer
125	 * (pour, seal, pickup, intake, batch, QC, release, QR) calls this.
126	 */
127	export function appendChainEvent(
128	  db: MockDb,
129	  e: {
130	    kind: ChainEvent['kind'];
131	    subjectType: ChainEvent['subjectType'];
132	    subjectId: string;
133	    actorPartyId?: string;
134	    detail?: string;
135	    clientEventId?: string;
136	  },
137	): ChainEvent {
138	  const prevHash = db.chainEvents.length ? db.chainEvents[db.chainEvents.length - 1].eventHash : GENESIS_HASH;
139	  const at = new Date().toISOString();
140	  const clientEventId = e.clientEventId ?? nextId('evt');
141	  const payload = ledgerPayload({ ...e, at, clientEventId });
142	  const event: ChainEvent = {
143	    id: nextId('che'),
144	    kind: e.kind,
145	    subjectType: e.subjectType,
146	    subjectId: e.subjectId,
147	    at,
148	    clientEventId,
149	    prevHash,
150	    eventHash: chainHash(prevHash, payload),
151	    actorPartyId: e.actorPartyId,
152	    detail: e.detail,
153	  };
154	  db.chainEvents.push(event);
155	  return event;

158	/**
159	 * Verify the ledger's integrity (§5): recompute every link's hash from its
160	 * predecessor and confirm it matches what is stored. Any in-place edit to a
161	 * recorded event (including its clientEventId) breaks the chain from that point
162	 * on. NOTE: like any bare hash chain, this catches edits and mid-chain deletions
163	 * but not truncation of the tail - detecting that needs a signed chain head /
164	 * Merkle anchor, which is the real backend's job (§5), not the mock's. Returns
165	 * the event count touching the given subject id set + whether the chain is intact.
166	 */
167	export function verifyLedger(db: MockDb, subjectIds: string[]): { events: number; intact: boolean } {
168	  const wanted = new Set(subjectIds);
169	  let prev = GENESIS_HASH;
170	  let intact = true;
171	  let events = 0;
172	  for (const ev of db.chainEvents) {
173	    const payload = ledgerPayload(ev);
174	    if (ev.prevHash !== prev || ev.eventHash !== chainHash(prev, payload)) intact = false;
175	    prev = ev.eventHash;
176	    if (wanted.has(ev.subjectId)) events += 1;
177	  }
178	  return { events, intact };
179	}

184	    .filter((i) => batch.intakeIds.includes(i.id))
185	    .flatMap((i) => i.lotIds)
186	    .map((lotId) => db.lots.find((l) => l.id === lotId))
187	    .filter((l): l is DcsLot => Boolean(l));
188	  const total = lots.reduce((s, l) => s + l.totalLitres, 0) || 1;
189	  const byDcs = new Map<
190	    string,
191	    { litres: number; pourCount: number; dates: string[]; pourIds: string[] }
192	  >();
193	  for (const lot of lots) {
194	    const cur = byDcs.get(lot.dcsId) ?? { litres: 0, pourCount: 0, dates: [], pourIds: [] };
195	    cur.litres += lot.totalLitres;
196	    cur.pourCount += lot.pourIds.length;
197	    cur.dates.push(lot.date);
198	    cur.pourIds.push(...lot.pourIds);
199	    byDcs.set(lot.dcsId, cur);
200	  }
201	  return [...byDcs.entries()]
202	    .map(([dcsId, v]) => ({
203	      dcs: db.orgUnits.find((o) => o.id === dcsId)!,
204	      pourCount: v.pourCount,
205	      volumeShare: Math.round((v.litres / total) * 1000) / 1000,
206	      collectedOn: v.dates.sort()[0],
207	      sachivName: sachivOf(db, dcsId),
208	      // Opt-in roster (§6.7): only farmers who set publicConsent are named; the
209	      // samiti-level share above stays the honest floor when none consent.
210	      consentedFarmers: consentedFarmersFor(db, v.pourIds),
211	    }))
212	    .sort((a, b) => b.volumeShare - a.volumeShare);
213	}
214	
215	/** Distinct opted-in farmers behind a set of pours (§6.7) - never anyone else. */
216	function consentedFarmersFor(
217	  db: MockDb,
218	  pourIds: string[],
219	): Array<{ name: string; village?: string }> {
220	  const partyIds = new Set(
221	    pourIds
222	      .map((id) => db.pours.find((p) => p.id === id)?.farmerPartyId)
223	      .filter((pid): pid is string => Boolean(pid)),
224	  );
225	  const roster: Array<{ name: string; village?: string }> = [];
226	  for (const pid of partyIds) {
227	    const party = db.parties.find((p) => p.id === pid);
228	    if (party?.publicConsent) roster.push({ name: party.name, village: party.village });
229	  }
230	  return roster.sort((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name));
231	}
232	
233	/** Name of the Sachiv (SAMITI_SACHEEV) who currently heads a samiti, if any. */
234	export function sachivOf(db: MockDb, dcsId: string): string | undefined {
235	  const asg = db.assignments.find(
236	    (a) => a.orgUnitId === dcsId && a.role === 'SAMITI_SACHEEV' && a.active,
237	  );
238	  if (!asg) return undefined;
239	  return db.parties.find((p) => p.id === asg.partyId)?.name;
240	}
241	
242	/** Count of Sachivs currently appointed across the whole cooperative. */
243	export function countActiveSachivs(db: MockDb): number {
244	  return db.assignments.filter((a) => a.role === 'SAMITI_SACHEEV' && a.active).length;
245	}
246	
247	/**
248	 * Shared appointment guard - called by EVERY writer that creates a role
249	 * assignment (admin grant + onboarding approval) so the rules cannot be
250	 * bypassed through a side door. Enforces (§5): a Sachiv is scoped to a samiti
251	 * (DCS), and the super-admin-set global Sachiv cap is never exceeded.
252	 */
253	export function assertAssignable(db: MockDb, role: RoleCode, orgUnitId: string): void {
254	  if (role !== 'SAMITI_SACHEEV') return;
255	  const org = db.orgUnits.find((o) => o.id === orgUnitId);
256	  if (!org || org.type !== 'DCS') {
257	    throw new ApiError(
258	      422,
259	      'SACHIV_WRONG_ORG',
260	      'A Sachiv can only be appointed to a samiti (a village dairy cooperative society)',
261	    );
262	  }
263	  // A samiti is headed by exactly one Sachiv, so the consumer QR/trace can name
264	  // a single accountable person. Replacing a Sachiv means revoking first.
265	  const alreadyHeaded = db.assignments.some(
266	    (a) => a.orgUnitId === orgUnitId && a.role === 'SAMITI_SACHEEV' && a.active,
267	  );
268	  if (alreadyHeaded) {
269	    throw new ApiError(
270	      409,
271	      'SACHIV_ALREADY_HEADED',
272	      'This samiti already has a Sachiv. Revoke the current one before appointing another.',
273	    );
274	  }
275	  if (countActiveSachivs(db) >= db.sachivCap) {
276	    throw new ApiError(
277	      409,
278	      'SACHIV_CAP_REACHED',
279	      `The Sachiv appointment limit (${db.sachivCap}) has been reached. Raise the limit or revoke a Sachiv first.`,
280	    );
281	  }
282	}

721	  const addPour = (

729	    const share = shift === 'MORNING' ? 0.55 : 0.45;
730	    const quantityLitres = Math.round(p.dailyLitres * share * (0.85 + rng() * 0.3) * 10) / 10;
731	    const fatPct = Math.round((p.fatBase + (rng() - 0.5) * 0.6) * 10) / 10;
732	    const snfPct = Math.round((8.6 + (rng() - 0.5) * 0.5) * 10) / 10;
733	    const { ratePerLitre, amount } = computePourAmount(quantityLitres, fatPct, snfPct, rateConfig);

740	      shift,

1	// Package domain holds the pure entity model of Saathi — structs, enums and
2	// invariants shared by every module. It has no behaviour beyond validation
3	// and no dependencies outside the standard library and BSON primitives.
4	// This is the contract layer: modules depend on domain, never the other way
5	// around.
6	package domain
7	
8	// Role codes — the role catalog from blueprint §5.2, grounded in the PCDF
9	// cooperative constitution (Farmer → Samiti/DCS → Sangh/Union → PCDF).
10	// A Party may hold many time-bounded, org-scoped RoleAssignments.
11	//
12	// The catalog is deliberately open for extension: adding a future role is a
13	// new constant + AllRoles entry + RequiredKYCTier entry — nothing else.
14	const (
15		// Village tier
16		RoleFarmer         = "FARMER"
17		RoleSamitiSacheev  = "SAMITI_SACHEEV"  // DCS paid Secretary (UPCS Act §31) — runs the collection console

27		RoleOrganisingManager = "ORGANISING_MANAGER"

29		// Logistics tier
30		RoleVanRider      = "VAN_RIDER"

37	
38		// Plant tier

40		RolePlantLabAnalyst = "PLANT_LAB_ANALYST"
41	
42		// State / district tier
43		RolePCDFAdmin        = "PCDF_ADMIN"
44		RoleMissionOfficial  = "MISSION_OFFICIAL"
45		RoleDistrictVerifier = "DISTRICT_VERIFIER"
46	
47		// Health tier
48		RoleVeterinarian = "VETERINARIAN"

51		// Consumer tier

60		RoleServiceAccount = "SERVICE_ACCOUNT"

63	// AllRoles is the closed set of grantable role codes (extend here).
64	var AllRoles = []string{
65		RoleFarmer, RoleSamitiSacheev, RoleSamitiAdhyaksh, RoleMilkTester, RoleLRP, RoleAITech,
66		RoleOrganisingManager,
67		RoleVanRider, RoleDeliveryRider,
68		RoleBMCOperator, RoleUnionFieldSupervisor, RoleUnionPresident,

71		RoleVeterinarian, RoleMVUDriver,
72		RoleConsumer,
73		RoleSupportAgent, RoleStateAuditor, RoleSuperAdmin,
74		RoleServiceAccount,
75	}
76	
77	var roleSet = func() map[string]struct{} {
78		s := make(map[string]struct{}, len(AllRoles))
79		for _, r := range AllRoles {
80			s[r] = struct{}{}
81		}
82		return s
83	}()

85	// IsValidRole reports whether code is one of the catalog roles.
86	func IsValidRole(code string) bool {
87		_, ok := roleSet[code]
88		return ok
89	}

91	// KYC assurance tiers (blueprint §4.2). Higher tiers unlock higher-trust roles.
92	const (
93		KYCTierMinimal  = "MINIMAL"  // mobile OTP only (consumer)
94		KYCTierFarmer   = "FARMER"   // Aadhaar OTP eKYC or offline XML + penny-drop
95		KYCTierStandard = "STANDARD" // Aadhaar eKYC
96		KYCTierRider    = "RIDER"    // Aadhaar eKYC + DL/RC
97		KYCTierHigh     = "HIGH"     // eKYC + org record / V-CIP for officials
98		KYCTierHighest  = "HIGHEST"  // platform admin: MFA + dual-control
99		KYCTierService  = "SERVICE"  // machine accounts: mTLS / scoped keys
100	)
101	
102	// RequiredKYCTier maps each role to the minimum KYC tier a party must hold
103	// before a role token for it can be issued (blueprint §5.2 "KYC tier").
104	// Tier upgrades happen ONLY through the KYC approval workflow: submit →
105	// PENDING → reviewed by an authorised approver → VERIFIED. There is no
106	// self-service tier upgrade.
107	var RequiredKYCTier = map[string]string{
108		RoleFarmer:               KYCTierFarmer,
109		RoleSamitiSacheev:        KYCTierHigh,
110		RoleSamitiAdhyaksh:       KYCTierHigh,
111		RoleMilkTester:           KYCTierStandard,
112		RoleLRP:                  KYCTierStandard,
113		RoleAITech:               KYCTierStandard,
114		RoleOrganisingManager:    KYCTierHigh,
115		RoleVanRider:             KYCTierRider,
116		RoleDeliveryRider:        KYCTierRider,
117		RoleBMCOperator:          KYCTierStandard,
118		RoleUnionFieldSupervisor: KYCTierHigh,
119		RoleUnionPresident:       KYCTierHigh,
120		RolePlantOperator:        KYCTierHigh,
121		RolePlantLabAnalyst:      KYCTierHigh,
122		RolePCDFAdmin:            KYCTierHigh,
123		RoleMissionOfficial:      KYCTierHigh,
124		RoleDistrictVerifier:     KYCTierHigh,
125		RoleVeterinarian:         KYCTierHigh,
126		RoleMVUDriver:            KYCTierStandard,
127		RoleConsumer:             KYCTierMinimal,
128		RoleSupportAgent:         KYCTierHigh,
129		RoleStateAuditor:         KYCTierHigh,
130		RoleSuperAdmin:           KYCTierHighest,
131		RoleServiceAccount:       KYCTierService,
132	}
133	
134	// kycRank orders tiers so "tier X satisfies requirement Y" is a comparison.
135	var kycRank = map[string]int{
136		KYCTierMinimal:  0,
137		KYCTierFarmer:   1,
138		KYCTierStandard: 1, // Farmer and Standard are parallel tier-1 proofs
139		KYCTierRider:    2,
140		KYCTierHigh:     3,
141		KYCTierHighest:  4,
142		KYCTierService:  4,
143	}
144	
145	// KYCTierSatisfies reports whether a party at tier `have` meets `need`.
146	// Parallel tier-1 proofs (FARMER vs STANDARD) satisfy each other.
147	func KYCTierSatisfies(have, need string) bool {
148		h, okH := kycRank[have]
149		n, okN := kycRank[need]
150		if !okH || !okN {
151			return false
152		}
153		return h >= n
154	}
155	
156	// KYCApprovableTiers maps an approver ROLE to the KYC tiers it may approve.
157	// Ground staff clear the field tiers; only federation admins clear HIGH;
158	// only SUPER_ADMIN clears HIGHEST. Extend when new approver roles arrive.
159	var KYCApprovableTiers = map[string][]string{
160		RoleOrganisingManager: {KYCTierMinimal, KYCTierFarmer, KYCTierStandard, KYCTierRider},
161		RoleDistrictVerifier:  {KYCTierMinimal, KYCTierFarmer, KYCTierStandard, KYCTierRider},
162		RolePCDFAdmin:         {KYCTierMinimal, KYCTierFarmer, KYCTierStandard, KYCTierRider, KYCTierHigh},
163		RoleSuperAdmin:        {KYCTierMinimal, KYCTierFarmer, KYCTierStandard, KYCTierRider, KYCTierHigh, KYCTierHighest, KYCTierService},
164	}
165	
166	// CanApproveKYCTier reports whether approverRole may approve a KYC record
167	// requesting the given tier.
168	func CanApproveKYCTier(approverRole, tier string) bool {
169		for _, t := range KYCApprovableTiers[approverRole] {
170			if t == tier {
171				return true
172			}
173		}
174		return false
175	}
176

16	const queryClient = new QueryClient({

21	    },

25	export default function RootLayout() {
26	  const [ready, setReady] = useState(false);
27	  const router = useRouter();
28	
29	  useEffect(() => {
30	    // Guarded: a cold-launch hydration failure (corrupt store, storage full, a
31	    // native module not-yet-ready race) must still boot the app to a clean
32	    // signed-out state — never leave it stuck or crash at init (no LogBox in release).
33	    let alive = true;
34	    (async () => {
35	      try {
36	        await Promise.all([hydrateAuthToken(), hydrateLanguage()]);
37	      } catch {
38	        // degrade gracefully — boot signed-out
39	      } finally {
40	        if (alive) setReady(true);
41	      }
42	    })();
43	    return () => {
44	      alive = false;
45	    };
46	  }, []);
47	
48	  // Auth irrecoverably lost (401 + failed refresh) → clean sign-out.
49	  useEffect(() => {
50	    setOnUnauthorized(() => {
51	      useAuthStore.getState().logout();
52	      queryClient.clear();
53	      router.replace('/login');
54	    });
55	    return () => setOnUnauthorized(null);
56	  }, [router]);
57	
58	  // Refresh the session snapshot on start (role grants/revocations, KYC tier).
59	  useEffect(() => {
60	    if (!ready) return;
61	    const { session, setSession } = useAuthStore.getState();
62	    if (session) {
63	      authApi
64	        .fetchMe()
65	        .then(setSession)
66	        .catch(() => undefined); // offline or stale token - keep cached session (§3.1)
67	    }
68	  }, [ready]);
69	
70	  return (
71	    <GestureHandlerRootView style={{ flex: 1 }}>
72	      <RootErrorBoundary>
73	        <SafeAreaProvider>
74	          <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
75	            <StatusBar style="dark" />
76	            <LiveSync />
77	            {ready ? (
78	              <Stack
79	                screenOptions={{
80	                  headerShown: false,
81	                  contentStyle: { backgroundColor: colors.page },
82	                }}
83	              />
84	            ) : (

86	            )}
87	          </QueryClientProvider>
88	        </SafeAreaProvider>
89	      </RootErrorBoundary>

101	/**
102	 * Catches render-time throws anywhere in the tree so a release build shows a
103	 * recoverable message instead of a native crash-loop (production has no LogBox,
104	 * so an uncaught render error would tear down the tree and kill the process).
105	 */
106	class RootErrorBoundary extends Component<{ children: ReactNode }, { error: Error | null }> {
107	  state: { error: Error | null } = { error: null };
108	
109	  static getDerivedStateFromError(error: Error): { error: Error } {
110	    return { error };
111	  }
112	
113	  render(): ReactNode {
114	    if (this.state.error) {

117	          <Text style={[font.h2, { color: colors.ink, textAlign: 'center' }]}>
118	            Something went wrong
119	          </Text>
120	          <Text

122	          >
123	            Please close and reopen the app. If it keeps happening, update to the latest version.
124	          </Text>
125	        </View>
126	      );
127	    }
128	    return this.props.children;
129	  }
130	}
