# Identity Module Audit — `parag-saathi-be`

## Global response envelope (applies to EVERY route)

All handlers respond through `httpx.JSON` / `httpx.JSONMeta` (`internal/platform/httpx/respond.go`), which wrap the DTO in a uniform envelope. The frontend never sees the raw DTO at the top level:

- Success (single object): `{ "data": <DTO> }`
- Success (list): `{ "data": [<DTO>...], "meta": { "limit": <int64>, "offset": <int64>, "total": <int64> } }`
- Error: `{ "error": { ...AppError } }`

Every JSON field name below is the real `json:"..."` tag. Every route is under `/api/v1` (confirmed: `internal/httpapi/modules.go:33` calls `identity.Register(api, d)` where `api` is the `/api/v1` chi subtree; `router.go:65`).

---

## 1. Every registered route (method + full path + middleware + DTOs)

Source: `internal/modules/identity/module.go`.

### `/auth` group

| Method | Full path | Handler | Auth |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/v1/auth/otp/request` | requestOTP | public |
| POST | `/api/v1/auth/otp/verify` | verifyOTP | public |
| POST | `/api/v1/auth/refresh` | refresh | public |
| POST | `/api/v1/auth/logout` | logout | Authenticate + RequireSession |
| GET | `/api/v1/auth/roles` | listMyRoles | Authenticate + RequireSession |
| POST | `/api/v1/auth/role/select` | selectRole | Authenticate + RequireSession |

### `/parties` group (Authenticate + RequireSession)

| Method | Full path | Handler |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/v1/parties/me` | getMe |
| PATCH | `/api/v1/parties/me` | patchMe |

### `/kyc` group (Authenticate; then sub-groups)

Self-service sub-group (RequireSession):

| Method | Full path | Handler |
|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/v1/kyc/aadhaar` | verifyAadhaar |
| POST | `/api/v1/kyc/bank` | verifyBank |
| GET | `/api/v1/kyc/me` | listMyKYC |

Reviewer sub-group (RequireRoles: `ORGANISING_MANAGER`, `DISTRICT_VERIFIER`, `PCDF_ADMIN`, `SUPER_ADMIN`):

| Method | Full path | Handler |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/v1/kyc/pending` | listPendingKYC |
| GET | `/api/v1/kyc/pending/count` | pendingKYCCount |
| POST | `/api/v1/kyc/{id}/approve` | approveKYC |
| POST | `/api/v1/kyc/{id}/reject` | rejectKYC |

### `/roles` group (Authenticate + RequireRoles: `PCDF_ADMIN`, `UNION_PRESIDENT`, `SAMITI_ADHYAKSH`, `ORGANISING_MANAGER`; SUPER_ADMIN auto-passes RequireRoles)

| Method | Full path | Handler |
|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/v1/roles/assignments` | createAssignment |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/roles/assignments/{id}` | revokeAssignment |
| GET | `/api/v1/roles/assignments?org_unit_id=&role_code=` | listAssignments |

### Per-route request/response DTOs (exact JSON)

**POST /auth/otp/request** — `otpRequestRequest` → `otpRequestResponse`
- Req: `phone`
- Resp: `phone`, `expires_at`, `dev_otp` (omitempty; present only when `OTPDevMode` on)

**POST /auth/otp/verify** — `otpVerifyRequest` → `authTokensResponse` (see §2)
- Req: `phone`, `otp`

**POST /auth/refresh** — `refreshRequest` → `authTokensResponse`
- Req: `refresh_token`
- Resp: `access_token`, `refresh_token`, `party`

**POST /auth/logout** — `logoutRequest` → `{ "logged_out": true }` (a `map[string]bool`, still enveloped as `data`)
- Req: `refresh_token`

**GET /auth/roles** — no body → `[]assignmentWithOrg` (see §3)

**POST /auth/role/select** — `roleSelectRequest` → `roleSelectResponse` (see §4)
- Req: `role_assignment_id` (ObjectID hex string)

**GET /parties/me** — no body → `meResponse` (see §5)

**PATCH /parties/me** — `patchMeRequest` → `domain.Party`
- Req: `full_name` (omitempty ptr), `preferred_language` (omitempty ptr); at least one required
- Resp: full `domain.Party` (see §5 for field list)

**POST /kyc/aadhaar** — `aadhaarKYCRequest` → `aadhaarKYCResponse`; **201** on fresh create, **200** on idempotent PENDING replay
- Req: `aadhaar_number` (12 digits), `consent` (bool, must be true), `requested_tier` (`FARMER|STANDARD|RIDER|HIGH`)
- Resp: `record` (full `domain.KYCRecord`), `status`, `message`

**POST /kyc/bank** — `bankKYCRequest` → `domain.KYCRecord`; **200**
- Req: `account_number` (9–18 digits), `ifsc`
- Resp: full `domain.KYCRecord`

**GET /kyc/me** — no body → `[]domain.KYCRecord` + `meta` (list envelope)

**GET /kyc/pending** — no body → `[]pendingKYCItem` + `meta` (see §7)

**GET /kyc/pending/count** — no body → `pendingKYCCountResponse` = `count` (int64), `capped` (bool)

**POST /kyc/{id}/approve** — no body → `kycReviewResponse` = `record` (full KYCRecord), `kyc_tier`

**POST /kyc/{id}/reject** — `kycRejectRequest` → `kycReviewResponse`
- Req: `reason` (1–500 chars, required)
- Resp: `record`, `kyc_tier`

**POST /roles/assignments** — `createAssignmentRequest` → `domain.RoleAssignment`; **201**
- Req: `party_id` (omitempty ptr ObjectID), `phone` (omitempty), `role_code`, `org_unit_id`, `valid_from` (omitempty), `valid_to` (omitempty). One of `party_id`/`phone` required; `party_id` wins.
- Resp: full `domain.RoleAssignment`

**DELETE /roles/assignments/{id}** — no body → `domain.RoleAssignment` (the revoked record); **200**

**GET /roles/assignments** — query `org_unit_id` (required), `role_code` (optional), `limit`, `offset` → `[]domain.RoleAssignment` + `meta`

---

## 2. What POST /auth/otp/verify returns exactly

Returns `authTokensResponse` (`models.go:71-75`), enveloped as `data`. **Tokens + party only. No assignments, no KYC.**

```
{ "data": {
    "access_token":  string,        // SESSION-kind JWT
    "refresh_token": string,        // opaque rotating token
    "party":         domain.Party   // full party object
}}
```

`party` is the full `domain.Party`: `id`, `phone`, `full_name` (omitempty), `preferred_language` (omitempty), `kyc_tier`, `status`, `created_at`, `updated_at`.

Note: the access token here is SESSION kind (`IssueSessionToken`, `jwt.go:51`) — it carries only `pid`/`phn`/`kyc`/`knd`; no role/org claims. The client must call `/auth/roles` then `/auth/role/select` to get a ROLE token. `/auth/refresh` returns the identical `authTokensResponse` shape.

---

## 3. What GET /auth/roles returns

Returns a bare JSON array `[]assignmentWithOrg` (`service.go:323`, `models.go:103-108`), enveloped as `data` (no `meta` — not paginated). Only assignments that are `UsableAt(now)` are included (active status + inside validity window).

`assignmentWithOrg` embeds the whole `domain.RoleAssignment` inline (Go struct embedding → fields are flattened, not nested) plus three org enrichment fields:

```
{ "data": [ {
    // --- embedded domain.RoleAssignment (flattened) ---
    "id":          ObjectID,
    "party_id":    ObjectID,
    "role_code":   string,
    "org_unit_id": ObjectID,
    "granted_by":  ObjectID,   // omitempty ptr
    "valid_from":  time,
    "valid_to":    time,       // omitempty ptr (nil = open-ended)
    "status":      string,     // ACTIVE | REVOKED
    "revoked_at":  time,       // omitempty ptr
    "revoked_by":  ObjectID,   // omitempty ptr
    "created_at":  time,
    // --- org enrichment (best-effort; omitempty) ---
    "org_name":    string,     // omitempty
    "org_type":    string,     // omitempty
    "org_code":    string      // omitempty
} ] }
```

Org enrichment is best-effort via `s.deps.Orgs.Get` (`withOrg`, `service.go:345`) — if the org lookup fails, the three `org_*` fields are simply omitted; the assignment still lists. Yes, it includes **org_name, org_type, org_code**.

---

## 4. What POST /auth/role/select returns

Returns `roleSelectResponse` (`models.go:124-129`), enveloped as `data`. It includes **role_code, org_unit_id, org_type, and the token** — but NOT `role_assignment_id` in the body (that lives inside the JWT claim `rid`).

```
{ "data": {
    "access_token": string,     // ROLE-kind JWT (IssueRoleToken)
    "role_code":    string,
    "org_unit_id":  ObjectID,
    "org_type":     string
}}
```

The ROLE JWT itself (`jwt.go:61`) carries claims `pid, phn, kyc, knd="role", rid` (role_assignment_id), `rol` (role_code), `org` (org_unit_id), `ogt` (org_type).

Validation gates before issuing (`selectRole`, `service.go:358-427`):
1. Assignment must exist and `assignment.PartyID == actor.PartyID` — else returns `404 NotFound("role assignment")` (deliberately same shape as unknown ID; never confirms other parties' grants).
2. `assignment.UsableAt(now)` — else `403 Forbidden` "revoked or outside validity window".
3. Party re-read; must be `ACTIVE` — else `403`.
4. `KYCTierSatisfies(party.KYCTier, RequiredKYCTier[role_code])` — else `403` with `Code = "KYC_TIER_INSUFFICIENT"` and details `{ current_tier, required_tier }`.

---

## 5. What GET /parties/me returns

Returns `meResponse` (`models.go:144-148`, `service.go:433`), enveloped as `data`. **Party + assignments + kyc (optional).**

```
{ "data": {
    "party":       domain.Party,          // full party
    "assignments": []assignmentWithOrg,   // same shape as §3 (usable only, org-enriched)
    "kyc":         kycSummary             // omitempty — present only if a KYC record exists
}}
```

`party` (`domain.Party`, `party.go:19`): `id`, `phone`, `full_name` (omitempty), `preferred_language` (omitempty), `kyc_tier`, `status`, `created_at`, `updated_at`.

`assignments` reuses `listMyRoles` — identical `assignmentWithOrg` shape as §3 (only usable assignments, org-enriched).

`kyc` is `kycSummary` (`models.go:132-140`), the masked digest of the **latest** KYC record (omitted if none exists; a non-404 error propagates):
```
{
    "requested_tier":      string,
    "status":              string,   // PENDING | VERIFIED | REJECTED
    "aadhaar_last4":       string,   // omitempty
    "bank_account_masked": string,   // omitempty
    "bank_ifsc":           string,   // omitempty
    "bank_verified":       bool,
    "verified_at":         time      // omitempty ptr
}
```

---

## 6. Role codes in `domain.AllRoles` (exact strings)

From `roles.go:64-75` — 24 roles:

```
FARMER
SAMITI_SACHEEV
SAMITI_ADHYAKSH
MILK_TESTER
LRP
AI_TECH
ORGANISING_MANAGER
VAN_RIDER
DELIVERY_RIDER
BMC_OPERATOR
UNION_FIELD_SUPERVISOR

PLANT_OPERATOR
PLANT_LAB_ANALYST

DISTRICT_VERIFIER
VETERINARIAN
MVU_DRIVER

SUPPORT_AGENT

SUPER_ADMIN

```

Related maps in the same file the frontend may need for alignment:
- `RequiredKYCTier` maps each role → min KYC tier (e.g. `FARMER→FARMER`, `CONSUMER→MINIMAL`, `UNION_PRESIDENT/PCDF_ADMIN/ORGANISING_MANAGER→HIGH`, `VAN_RIDER/DELIVERY_RIDER→RIDER`, `SUPER_ADMIN→HIGHEST`, `SERVICE_ACCOUNT→SERVICE`).
- KYC tiers: `MINIMAL, FARMER, STANDARD, RIDER, HIGH, HIGHEST, SERVICE`. Self-requestable tiers (via `/kyc/aadhaar`): only `FARMER, STANDARD, RIDER, HIGH`.

---

## 7. KYC endpoints present and their shapes

Self-service (RequireSession):
- **POST /kyc/aadhaar** → `aadhaarKYCResponse` = `{ record: domain.KYCRecord, status: string, message: string }`. `status` = `"PENDING"`, `message` = `"awaiting verification"`. 201 fresh / 200 idempotent replay. No auto-verify, no tier change — record created PENDING.
- **POST /kyc/bank** → full `domain.KYCRecord` (200). Attaches masked bank tail + IFSC to the latest PENDING record, or creates a new PENDING record if latest is terminal/absent.
- **GET /kyc/me** → `[]domain.KYCRecord` + `meta` (paginated).

Reviewer console (RequireRoles OM/DV/PCDF/SUPER):
- **GET /kyc/pending** → `[]pendingKYCItem` + `meta`. Each item embeds the full `domain.KYCRecord` (flattened) plus `party` (omitempty) = `pendingPartySummary` `{ id, phone, full_name(omitempty), kyc_tier }`. Scoped to the reviewer's org area.
- **GET /kyc/pending/count** → `pendingKYCCountResponse` = **`{ "count": int64, "capped": bool }`** (`models.go:252-255`). `capped` is true when the pending scan hit the cap (1000, `pendingKYCScanCap`), meaning display "count+". Scoped to the reviewer's area, reuses the same scope logic as the list.
- **POST /kyc/{id}/approve** → `kycReviewResponse` = `{ record: domain.KYCRecord, kyc_tier: string }` (`kyc_tier` = party tier after upgrade).
- **POST /kyc/{id}/reject** → same `kycReviewResponse`; requires body `{ reason }`.

`domain.KYCRecord` JSON fields (`party.go:82`): `id`, `party_id`, `requested_tier`, `aadhaar_last4` (omitempty), `bank_account_masked` (omitempty), `bank_ifsc` (omitempty), `bank_verified` (bool), `bank_name_match` (omitempty float 0..1), `digilocker_docs` (omitempty), `video_kyc_ref` (omitempty), `consent_id` (omitempty), `status`, `rejection_reason` (omitempty), `reviewed_by` (omitempty), `reviewed_by_role` (omitempty), `reviewed_at` (omitempty), `verified_at` (omitempty), `created_at`, `updated_at`. **Important:** `aadhaar_vault_ref` is `json:"-"` — persisted but NEVER serialized to any client.

Reviewer authorization for approve/reject enforces, in service: record must be PENDING (else `409 KYC_NOT_PENDING`); no self-review (`403 KYC_SELF_REVIEW`); subject must be in reviewer's org scope (`403 KYC_SUBJECT_OUT_OF_SCOPE`); role must be allowed for the tier via `CanApproveKYCTier` (`403 KYC_TIER_NOT_APPROVABLE`).

---

## 8. How multi-role is currently handled

**Model = one `Party`, many `RoleAssignment`s** — confirmed exactly as blueprint §4.1.

- `domain.Party` (`party.go:19`) is the single identity record: `phone` is the unique natural key; one phone = one Party. It carries no role — roles are entirely separate records.
- `domain.RoleAssignment` (`party.go:39`) grants **one role** (`role_code`) to **one party** (`party_id`) inside **one org unit** (`org_unit_id`) for a validity window (`valid_from` / nullable `valid_to`), with `status` ACTIVE/REVOKED plus `revoked_at`/`revoked_by`. A party can hold many of these simultaneously.
- `RoleAssignment.UsableAt(t)` (`party.go:55`) is the single usability predicate: status must be ACTIVE, `t >= valid_from`, and (`valid_to == nil` OR `t <= valid_to`).

Login vs. role selection:
- OTP verify issues only a **SESSION** token (no role). The client fetches `/auth/roles` (usable assignments, org-enriched) and picks one via `/auth/role/select`, which mints a **ROLE** token pinned to that single assignment (`rid`/`rol`/`org`/`ogt` claims). Switching roles = issue a fresh ROLE token; no server session state changes.

How `/auth/role/select` validates the assignment belongs to the caller and is usable (`selectRole`, `service.go:358-427`):
1. **Ownership**: after `findAssignmentByID`, it checks `assignment.PartyID != aid` (the actor's party id parsed from JWT `pid`). Mismatch → `404 NotFound("role assignment")` — indistinguishable from an unknown ID, so a caller can never probe other parties' grants.
2. **Usability**: `assignment.UsableAt(now)` — false (revoked or outside window) → `403`.
3. **Party active**: re-reads the party (tier may have changed since session mint); must be `ACTIVE`.
4. **KYC gate**: `KYCTierSatisfies(party.KYCTier, RequiredKYCTier[role_code])`; insufficient → `403 KYC_TIER_INSUFFICIENT` with `{ current_tier, required_tier }`. This genuinely blocks un-approved parties from assuming a role — there is no auto-verify path.

`listMyRoles` / `getMe.assignments` also filter by `UsableAt(now)`, so the switcher UI only ever shows selectable assignments.

---

### Cross-cutting notes for frontend alignment
- Every payload is wrapped: read `response.data` (and `response.meta` for lists). Errors are `response.error` with `{ code, message, status, details? }`.
- ObjectIDs serialize as 24-char hex strings; `role_assignment_id` in the select request must be that hex string.
- Pagination query params: `limit` (default 50, max 200), `offset` (default 0). `meta` returns `{ limit, offset, total }`.
- Embedded structs (`assignmentWithOrg`, `pendingKYCItem`) flatten their embedded fields to the top level of each array element — they are NOT nested under a sub-key.

# Saathi Auth + Multi-Role Login Flow — FE ⇄ BE Alignment Report

Scope: `parag-saathi-fe` (React Native/Expo, `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_MODE` defaults to `http` → real backend at `…/api/v1`) vs `parag-saathi-be` `internal/modules/identity`. All wire shapes are the snake_case JSON the Go backend serialises, wrapped in the standard envelope.

## Envelope (both confirmed to match)
- Success: `{ "data": <payload>, "meta"?: {...} }` — `httpx.JSON`/`JSONMeta` (`respond.go:21`). FE unwraps `.data` in `client.ts:148`.
- Error: `{ "error": { "code": "...", "message": "...", "details"?: {...} } }` — `errEnvelope` + `AppError` json tags `code`/`message`/`details` (`errors.go:12`). FE maps to `ApiError(status, code, message, details)` (`client.ts:137`).
- Auth: `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`. A 401 on a non-`/auth/*` path triggers one single-flight `POST /auth/refresh` + retry (`client.ts:195`).

---

## 1. THE LOGIN FLOW

It is a **two-call** flow. `verify` does NOT return assignments; the app then calls `GET /parties/me`.

**Step A — `POST /auth/otp/request`**
Request `{ "phone": "9876543210" }` → Response (`otpRequestResponse`, models.go:47):
```json
{ "data": { "phone": "9876543210", "expires_at": "2026-07-09T12:05:00Z", "dev_otp": "483920" } }
```
`dev_otp` present ONLY when `cfg.OTPDevMode` on. FE maps to `{ otpSent, expiresAt, devHint }` (`auth.ts:115`).

**Step B — `POST /auth/otp/verify`**
Request `{ "phone": "9876543210", "otp": "483920" }` → Response (`authTokensResponse`, models.go:71):
```json
{ "data": {
  "access_token": "<JWT kind=session>",
  "refresh_token": "<opaque>",
  "party": { "id":"...", "phone":"9876543210", "full_name":"Ramesh Yadav",
             "preferred_language":"hi", "kyc_tier":"HIGH", "status":"ACTIVE",
             "created_at":"...", "updated_at":"..." }
} }
```
Returns tokens + party only — **no assignments, no role picker data**. The SESSION JWT claims (`jwt.go:26`) carry `pid/phn/kyc/knd=session` but NOT role/org.

**Step C — `GET /parties/me`** (with the SESSION token; `RequireSession` allows session or role tokens, rbac.go:45). Returns party + usable assignments + KYC (see §3).

**Decision logic** (`app/login.tsx:69-77`): the mutation chains `verifyOtp → setTokens → fetchMe`, and on the resulting `Session`:
- `session.assignments.length === 1` → `activateRole(assignments[0].id)` (calls `/auth/role/select`) then `router.replace(roleHomePath(...))` → straight to dashboard.
- otherwise (`>1` **or `0`**) → `router.replace('/select-role')`.

So the picker is shown whenever there is **not exactly one** assignment. `RoleGate`/`app/index.tsx` enforce the same: no session → `/login`; session but no active role → `/select-role`. The backend `listMyRoles` filters assignments to `UsableAt(now)` (ACTIVE + inside validity window) — but does NOT filter by KYC tier, so the count driving the picker is the count of active assignments.

---

## 2. ROLE SELECT — `POST /auth/role/select`

Requires an authenticated session/role token (mounted under `/auth` group with `RequireSession`).

Request (`roleSelectRequest`, models.go:112) — FE `mapRequest` at `auth.ts:210` sends:
```json
{ "role_assignment_id": "<ObjectID hex>" }
```
Response (`roleSelectResponse`, models.go:124):
```json
{ "data": { "access_token":"<JWT kind=role>", "role_code":"SAMITI_SACHEEV",
            "org_unit_id":"<hex>", "org_type":"DCS" } }
```
FE reads `access_token`, `role_code`, `org_unit_id` (ignores `org_type`) and calls `setAccessToken(...)` — swaps ONLY the access token to the ROLE-kind JWT (`store.ts:45-49`). The ROLE JWT adds claims `rid/rol/org/ogt`.

Service gates before issuing (`service.go:358`): ownership (assignment.PartyID == actor) else `404 NOT_FOUND`; `UsableAt` else `403 FORBIDDEN`; party active; and **KYC tier** — `403` with `code:"KYC_TIER_INSUFFICIENT"` + `details:{current_tier, required_tier}` if `party.KYCTier` doesn't satisfy `RequiredKYCTier[role]`.

**Org fields the app needs per assignment**: the picker needs `org_name` (rendered as the tile subtitle). It also consumes `org_type` and `org_code` to build the `OrgUnit` (`orgFromAssignment`, auth.ts:84) but only `name` is displayed. These come from `/parties/me` assignment enrichment (§3), not from role/select.

---

## 3. `GET /parties/me` WIRE SHAPE

`meResponse` (models.go:144), enriched. Example for Ramesh (multi-role):
```json
{ "data": {
  "party": { "id":"...", "phone":"9876543210", "full_name":"Ramesh Yadav",
             "preferred_language":"hi", "kyc_tier":"HIGH", "status":"ACTIVE",
             "created_at":"...", "updated_at":"..." },
  "assignments": [
    { "id":"<hex A>", "party_id":"...", "role_code":"FARMER",
      "org_unit_id":"<semari hex>", "valid_from":"...", "valid_to":null,
      "status":"ACTIVE", "granted_by":"...", "created_at":"...",
      "org_name":"Semari Dairy Cooperative Society", "org_type":"DCS", "org_code":"DCS-BBK-0142" },
    { "id":"<hex B>", "party_id":"...", "role_code":"SAMITI_SACHEEV",
      "org_unit_id":"<semari hex>", "valid_from":"...", "valid_to":null,
      "status":"ACTIVE", "granted_by":"...", "created_at":"...",
      "org_name":"Semari Dairy Cooperative Society", "org_type":"DCS", "org_code":"DCS-BBK-0142" }
  ],
  "kyc": { "requested_tier":"HIGH", "status":"VERIFIED", "aadhaar_last4":"3210",
           "bank_account_masked":"****3210", "bank_ifsc":"SBIN0001234",
           "bank_verified":true, "verified_at":"..." }
} }
```
- **Party fields**: `id, phone, full_name?, preferred_language?, kyc_tier, status, created_at, updated_at`. FE `mapParty` (auth.ts:60) reads `full_name, phone, kyc_tier, created_at` + derives `aadhaarMasked`/`bankVerified` from `kyc`.
- **assignments[]** — each is `assignmentWithOrg` = full `domain.RoleAssignment` (`id, party_id, role_code, org_unit_id, granted_by?, valid_from, valid_to?, status, revoked_at?, revoked_by?, created_at`) + enrichment `org_name?, org_type?, org_code?` (models.go:101, `withOrg` service.go:345, best-effort — omitted if org lookup fails). FE `mapAssignment` maps `role_code→role`, `status==='ACTIVE'→active` (auth.ts:72). FE dedupes `orgUnits[]` from the enrichment.
- **kyc summary** (`kycSummary`, models.go:131): `requested_tier, status, aadhaar_last4?, bank_account_masked?, bank_ifsc?, bank_verified, verified_at?`. Omitted entirely if no KYC record.

---

## 4. MULTI-ROLE (farmer + sachiv)

**FE representation**: `Session = { party, assignments: RoleAssignment[], orgUnits: OrgUnit[] }` (domain.ts:67). A party with 2 roles = 2 entries in `assignments`, each a distinct `{ id, role, orgUnitId, active }`. Seed proof: Ramesh `9876543210` = `p_ramesh`, HIGH tier, with `mkAsg('p_ramesh','FARMER','org_dcs_semari')` + `mkAsg('p_ramesh','SAMITI_SACHEEV','org_dcs_semari')` (db.ts:517-518) — both ACTIVE, same DCS.

**Picker render** (`app/select-role.tsx:45-87`): maps `session.assignments`, and per assignment:
- `const meta = ROLES[a.role]` → tile icon + `meta.label`/`meta.labelHi`.
- `session.orgUnits.find(o => o.id === a.orgUnitId)` → subtitle `org.name`/`org.nameHi`.
- Two tiles ("Farmer" and "Sachiv"), both subtitled "Semari…", keyed by `a.id`.

**Switching**: tap → `activateRole(a.id)` → `POST /auth/role/select {role_assignment_id: a.id}` → new ROLE token via `setAccessToken`, `activeAssignmentId` persisted to AsyncStorage → `router.replace(roleHomePath(a))`. To re-switch, the user returns to `/select-role` and picks the other assignment; a fresh role/select mints a new ROLE token that overwrites the previous one. `useActiveRole`/`useActiveOrgUnit` (store.ts:74-86) resolve the active assignment/org from `activeAssignmentId`.

**What the backend MUST return for this to work**:
1. `/parties/me` returns **all** usable assignments (it does — `listMyRoles`), each with a **stable distinct `id`** (used as `role_assignment_id`) and **distinct `role_code`**.
2. Each assignment carries **org enrichment** (`org_name` at minimum) so the picker subtitle renders without a second call.
3. `/auth/role/select` accepts any of those `id`s and returns a role-scoped `access_token`.
4. **`role_code` values must be in the FE `ROLES` map** — see §6 (crash risk).

**`POST /kyc/aadhaar`** (self-service, RequireSession). Request (`aadhaarKYCRequest`, models.go:178) — FE sends `{ aadhaar_number, consent, requested_tier }` (auth.ts:268). `requested_tier` ∈ `FARMER|STANDARD|RIDER|HIGH`. Response (`aadhaarKYCResponse`, models.go:199), **201 on new / 200 on idempotent replay**:
```json
{ "data": { "record": { …domain.KYCRecord, "status":"PENDING", "requested_tier":"FARMER", "aadhaar_last4":"3210" },
            "status":"PENDING", "message":"awaiting verification" } }
```
No auto-verify, no tier change.

**`POST /kyc/bank`** (RequireSession). Request `{ account_number, ifsc }` (auth.ts:303). Response = full `domain.KYCRecord` (models.go, `verifyBank` service.go:574) with `bank_account_masked`, `bank_ifsc`, `bank_verified:true`, `bank_name_match:0.92`, `status:"PENDING"`.

**`GET /kyc/pending/count`** (reviewer roles only: `ORGANISING_MANAGER, DISTRICT_VERIFIER, PCDF_ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN`). FE `events.ts:14` maps to `{ count, capped }`; live badge re-fetched on the `kyc.pending.changed` SSE nudge. Related: `GET /kyc/pending` (list), `GET /kyc/me`, `POST /kyc/{id}/approve`, `POST /kyc/{id}/reject` also exist.

## 6. GAPS / MISMATCHES vs the current backend identity module

### A. CRITICAL — role-picker crash on backend-only role codes
`app/select-role.tsx:46-47` does `const meta = ROLES[a.role]; const Icon = meta.icon;` with **no null guard**. The FE `ROLE_CODES` (roles.ts:33) and backend `domain.AllRoles` (roles.go:64) diverge:
- **Backend-only roles** (can be returned in `/parties/me.assignments[].role_code`, absent from FE `ROLES`): **`ORGANISING_MANAGER`**, **`CONSUMER`**. If either is assigned to a multi-role party, the picker throws `Cannot read property 'icon' of undefined` and the tree unmounts. (`roleHomePath` is guarded with `?.`, but the picker is not.)
- **FE-only roles** (in FE `ROLES`, NOT grantable by backend — `createAssignmentRequest.validate` returns `INVALID_ROLE`): **`ONBOARDING_EXECUTIVE`**, **`STORE_MANAGER`**. The FE mock seeds these (`p_onboard`, `p_store`), and whole FE modules (`/onboarding`, `/store`) target them, but the real backend cannot create or issue tokens for them.
  → Backend must either add `ORGANISING_MANAGER`/`CONSUMER` to the FE role catalog (or the FE must guard), and add `ONBOARDING_EXECUTIVE`/`STORE_MANAGER` to `AllRoles` + `RequiredKYCTier` if those modules ship.

### B. `POST /kyc/aadhaar` response shape mismatch
FE `submitAadhaarKyc.mapResponse` reads `(raw).kyc_tier` and returns `{ kycTier }` (auth.ts:273). Backend returns `{ record, status, message }` with **no `kyc_tier` field** and **no tier upgrade** (record is PENDING pending review). Result: FE gets `kycTier: undefined`. The FE mock also optimistically sets `party.kycTier = requested_tier` immediately — the real backend never does. Any FE UI that assumes "Aadhaar submitted ⇒ tier upgraded" is wrong against the real backend (the tier only changes after a reviewer approves).

### C. KYC summary field name: `tier` vs `requested_tier`
FE `WireKycSummary` declares `tier: string` (auth.ts:52); backend `kycSummary` serialises `requested_tier` (models.go:133). Currently harmless (FE mapping only reads `aadhaar_last4`/`bank_verified`, both of which match), but the declared contract is misaligned — if FE later reads `kyc.tier` it will be `undefined`.

### D. OrgUnit `type` enum mismatch
Backend `domain.OrgUnit.Type` values are `FEDERATION, MILK_UNION, PROCESSING_PLANT, BMC, DCS` (orgunit.go:11). FE `OrgUnitType` expects `FEDERATION, UNION, DCS, BMC, PLANT, STORE, DISTRICT` (domain.ts:7). So `org_type` arriving as `MILK_UNION`/`PROCESSING_PLANT` is not a valid FE `OrgUnitType`, and FE has `UNION`/`PLANT`/`STORE`/`DISTRICT` that the backend never emits (no STORE org type exists backend-side at all). Low blast radius today (picker shows `org_name`, not type), but any type-driven FE logic breaks. `orgFromAssignment` also defaults `type` to `'DCS'` when `org_name` is present but `org_type` empty.

### E. Missing routes the FE calls (onboarding flow has no backend)
All in `onboarding.ts`, marked `// TODO(backend)`, mock-only — the identity module implements NONE:
- `POST /onboarding/requests`, `GET /onboarding/requests?submitted_by=…`, `GET /onboarding/requests?status=PENDING`, `POST /onboarding/requests/{id}/approve`, `POST /onboarding/requests/{id}/reject` — the assisted-onboarding verification queue.
- `GET /parties?role=SAMITI_SACHEEV` (`listSachivs`) — backend exposes only `GET /parties/me`, no party-by-role listing.
The backend’s nearest primitive is `POST /roles/assignments` (direct grant, no PENDING queue) + `GET /roles/assignments?org_unit_id=…`. The whole onboarding→admin-approval UX (`ONBOARDING_EXECUTIVE`) is unbacked.

### F. Behavioral divergence — brand-new number is a dead-end on the real backend
FE mock `verifyOtp` throws `404 NOT_REGISTERED` for an unknown phone (auth.ts:154). The real backend `verifyOTP` **find-or-creates** the party (`upsertPartyByPhone`, service.go:215) → new party with **0 assignments** → `getMe` returns `assignments: []` → `login.tsx` (`length !== 1`) routes to `/select-role`, which renders an **empty grid with no logout/exit** (`select-role.tsx` only early-returns for `length === 1`). New users get stuck. FE either needs an empty-state on `/select-role`, or the backend needs a "not registered / no roles" signal.

### G. Picker can show roles that then fail `role/select` silently
`listMyRoles`/`getMe` filter by `UsableAt` only (no KYC gate), but `selectRole` enforces the KYC tier. A tile for a role whose `RequiredKYCTier` the party doesn't hold will render, and tapping it returns `403 KYC_TIER_INSUFFICIENT` — which `select-role.tsx:60` swallows (`catch { setSelecting(null) }`) with **no user-facing error**. (Not hit by the seed since Ramesh is HIGH, but real data can trigger it.) Same silent-failure applies to the single-role auto-enter path in `login.tsx:72`, where a thrown `activateRole` is unhandled.

### H. Error-code expectations differ (login path)
FE mock uses `INVALID_OTP`/`NOT_REGISTERED`; the real backend returns generic `code:"UNAUTHORIZED"` (401) for wrong/expired OTP and `no active OTP` (service.go:193-207), and `429 TOO_MANY_REQUESTS` after `maxOTPAttempts=5`. FE only renders `ApiError.message` on the OTP screen, so text still shows, but any FE logic keyed on specific codes (there is none today on this screen) would miss. `role/select` special codes the FE does not branch on: `KYC_TIER_INSUFFICIENT`, and generic `FORBIDDEN`/`NOT_FOUND`.

### Things that DO line up (no action needed)
`/auth/otp/request`, `/auth/otp/verify`, `/auth/refresh` (rotation handled in `client.ts:156`), `/auth/logout` (`{refresh_token}` → `{logged_out:true}`; `RequireSession` accepts the ROLE token so revoke works), `GET /parties/me` core shape, `PATCH /parties/me` (`{full_name, preferred_language}` → Party), `POST /auth/role/select` core shape, `POST /kyc/bank`, `GET /kyc/pending/count`, and both success/error envelopes.

Analysis is read-only. "Wire name" = the snake_case key the FE's `mapRequest`/`mapResponse` actually reads/writes (from `src/core/api/endpoints/*.ts`); "backend json" = the Go struct `json:` tag in `internal/domain/*.go` and module `models.go`.

## 1. WIRE CONVENTIONS

| Concern | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| **Base URL** | `http://localhost:8080/api/v1` (env `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL`; default in `client.ts:26`). Backend confirms `/api/v1` tree in `internal/httpapi/router.go:65`. | ✅ aligned |
| **Module mount prefixes** | Backend mounts each module *under* `/api/v1`: `/auth`, `/parties`, `/kyc`, `/orgs`, `/collection`, `/logistics`, `/plant`, `/quality`, `/settlements`, `/dbt`, `/cattle`, `/public`. | ✅ FE endpoints use these exact prefixes (`/collection/pours`, `/logistics/consignments`, `/plant/batches`, `/quality/qc-results`, `/settlements`, `/public/qr/…`). |
| **Success envelope** | `{"data": ..., "meta"?: ...}` — `httpx` `envelope{Data, Meta}`. FE unwraps `.data` (`client.ts:148`), tolerates bare payloads. | ✅ aligned |
| **Error envelope** | `{"error": {"code", "message", "details"?}}` — `httpx.AppError{Code, Message, Details}`. FE maps to `ApiError(status, code, message, details)` (`client.ts:137-146`). | ✅ aligned |
| **Error code style** | UPPER_SNAKE string codes. Backend generic codes: `UNAUTHORIZED`, `FORBIDDEN`, `NOT_FOUND`, `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED`, `RATE_LIMITED`, `INTERNAL`, plus per-case codes (`CONSENT_REQUIRED`, etc.). FE falls back to `HTTP_<status>` if `error.code` absent. | ✅ style aligned. ⚠️ FE invents many domain codes the backend may not emit yet (`IMPLAUSIBLE_READING`, `QC_GATE_BLOCKED`, `LOT_NOT_DISPATCHED`) — these live only in mock bodies for mock-only endpoints. |
| **Auth header** | `Authorization: Bearer <access token>` (`client.ts:126`). | ✅ aligned |
| **Token model** | SESSION token from `POST /auth/otp/verify`; ROLE-scoped token from `POST /auth/role/select`; rotating refresh via `POST /auth/refresh` `{refresh_token}` → `{access_token, refresh_token}`. | ✅ aligned (`identity/models.go` `authTokensResponse`, `refreshRequest`, `roleSelectResponse`) |
| **Refresh-on-401** | Single-flight: one refresh + one retry per 401, never for `/auth/*` paths, `clearTokens()` + `onUnauthorized()` on failure (`client.ts:154-205`). | ✅ |
| **snake_case ⇄ camelCase** | **Per-endpoint, in FE code.** Each endpoint declares `mapRequest` (camel→snake) and `mapResponse` (snake→camel). There is **no global auto-transform** — each wire field is hand-mapped, which is exactly where the silent mismatches in §3 hide. | ⚠️ fragile by design |
| **ID format** | Backend `_id` = Mongo `primitive.ObjectID` → serialized as 24-char hex string; all relations are ObjectID refs. FE treats every ID as an opaque string. Round-trips fine on reads. ⚠️ **Request risk:** backend request structs type IDs as `primitive.ObjectID`, so FE sending an empty/placeholder string (e.g. `org_unit_id:''` in `updateRateConfig`, `payments.ts:368`) will **fail ObjectID unmarshalling** (400), not be accepted. | ⚠️ |
| **Date/time** | Timestamps: Go `time.Time` → RFC3339/ISO-8601; FE consumes ISO strings and `.slice(0,10)`. Day-keys: `pour_date`/`invoice_date`/`date` are `"YYYY-MM-DD"` strings (IST settlement-day key, `DateKeyIST`). | ✅ aligned |
| **Idempotency** | `client_event_id` — device-minted unique string, offline-replay key. Backend `MilkPour.ClientEventID` (`bson/json:"client_event_id"`, unique index) + `CreatePourRequest.ClientEventID` + `PourResponse.IdempotentReplay`. FE mints `nextId('evt')` per attempt (`collections.ts:225`). ⚠️ FE mints a **fresh** id every attempt, so a retried pour is a **new** event, defeating the dedupe (only true offline-queue replays would reuse an id — the current UI path does not). | ⚠️ semantics |
| **Pour create response** | `{"pour": MilkPour, "idempotent_replay"?: bool}` — FE reads `raw.pour` (`collections.ts:236`). | ✅ aligned |

## 4. FE-DOMAIN CONCEPTS THE BACKEND DOMAIN LACKS

1. **`Pour.assurance` (A|B|C)** — capture-assurance level (§6.2). No backend field/enum; FE derives it client-side from entry method. Downstream `DcsLot.assurance` (weakest-of-set) also FE-only.
2. **`rate_chart_version` / `RateConfig.version` / `Pour.rateChartVersion`** — backend pins pricing via `rate_chart_id` (ObjectID ref), has no immutable version string.
3. **Tamper seal: `DcsLot.sealCode`/`sealedAt`, `RouteStop.sealCode`** (§6.4) — backend `DCSConsignment` and `RouteStop` have **no seal fields**; the van-rider seal-match check (`SEAL_MISMATCH`) is mock-only.
4. **`Party.publicConsent`** (§6.7 opt-in to public trace) — no backend Party field → consented-farmer names on the trace can't be sourced.
5. **`Animal.ageMonths`, `lactationNo`, `avgDailyYieldLitres`** — backend has only `birth_date` + `lactation_status`. (Neither side has the "tag_status" the brief asked about.)
6. **`OnboardingRequest` entity** (assisted-KYC, `onboarding.ts` + `domain.ts`) — no backend counterpart; backend models this as `KYCRecord` + `Party` + `RoleAssignment` (fundamentally different shape).
7. **`ConsignmentInvoice`** (DCS→Union B2B GST e-invoice, HSN 0401) — FE-only, mock-only; no backend entity.
8. **`ReleaseSummary` + assisted-release stage machine** (`PENDING_APPROVAL\|UNION_FUNDED\|DISTRIBUTING\|FARMERS_PAID`) — FE-only; backend `SettlementBatch` uses a different vocabulary (`INITIATED\|PENDING_APPROVAL\|APPROVED\|EXECUTING\|EXECUTED\|PARTIAL\|FAILED\|REJECTED`) with a `PayoutInstruction` sub-entity.
9. **Invoice gross/deductions/net model** — backend Invoice carries a single `total_amount`; no deductions concept.
10. **Batch-embedded `contributingDcsIds`, `productOutputs`, `certificateId`, `qcStatus`, `volumeLitres`** — none exist on `ProcessingBatch`; they're separate collections (`ProductLot`, `QCResult`) or absent.
11. **Retail/last-mile domain**: `Delivery`, `DeliveryPreferences`, `StoreInventoryItem`, `RiderSummary`, `Order`/`OrderItem`, `Product` catalogue — **no backend domain files** for store/commerce/delivery.
12. **`SchemeApplication`, `EducationContent` (FE shape), `FeatureFlag`, `AuditEvent` (FE shape), `HealthEvent.CHECKUP`** — partial/absent. Backend has `EducationContent` (different fields: `media_type`/`media_url`/`duration_sec`), platform `audit`, and routes subsidies via `DBTRequest` (not FE's `SchemeApplication`).

**Conversely, backend-only entities the FE has no model for:** `AnalyzerReading` (separate reading record with anti-tamper envelope), `KYCRecord`, `Consent`, `DocRef`, `SettlementBatch`, `PayoutInstruction`, `DBTRequest`, `Notification`, `ColdChainEntry`, and `ProvenanceSeq` on every ledgered entity.

func (r *repository) updatePartyProfile(ctx context.Context, id primitive.ObjectID, fullName, preferredLanguage *string, now time.Time) (*domain.Party, error) {
	set := bson.D{{Key: "updated_at", Value: now}}
	if fullName != nil {
		set = append(set, bson.E{Key: "full_name", Value: *fullName})
	}
	if preferredLanguage != nil {
		set = append(set, bson.E{Key: "preferred_language", Value: *preferredLanguage})
	}
	opts := options.FindOneAndUpdate().SetReturnDocument(options.After)
	var p domain.Party
	err := r.parties.FindOneAndUpdate(ctx, bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: id}}, bson.D{{Key: "$set", Value: set}}, opts).Decode(&p)
	if errors.Is(err, mongo.ErrNoDocuments) {
		return nil, httpx.NotFound("party")
	}
	if err != nil {
		return nil, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("update party profile: %w", err))
	}
	return &p, nil
}

# Saathi Backend ⇄ Frontend Alignment Spec

> **Goal:** align the Go backend (`parag-saathi-be`) to the 80%-built React Native app
> (`parag-saathi-fe`), reconciled with the **Developer Technical Note** (the authoritative
> traceability build spec). Integration (wiring the FE mappers) comes later — **first the backend
> is made spec-clean and capable**: we ADD genuinely-missing fields/endpoints/relations; we do NOT
> pollute the backend with FE-name aliases (those are FE-mapper fixes at integration time).
>
> This doc is derived from a 3-agent deep analysis of both repos (identity round) + the full
> Developer Note. It is the running plan; each **Piece** is fixed completely before the next.

---

## 0. What's already aligned (no work needed)

- **Wire conventions**: base `/api/v1`, success `{data, meta?}`, error `{error:{code,message,details?}}`,
  `Authorization: Bearer`, refresh-on-401, snake_case wire, ObjectID hex ids, ISO-8601 / `YYYY-MM-DD`
  dates, `client_event_id` idempotency. ✅
- **Module mounts** match the FE's `backend-integration.md` map exactly (identity, orgs, collection,
  logistics, plant, quality, settlement, cattle, platformops, publictrace). ✅
- **Multi-role model** (one phone = one Party = many org-scoped RoleAssignments) — the farmer+sachiv
  picker works: `/parties/me` returns all usable assignments org-enriched; `/auth/role/select` mints
  a role-scoped token for either. ✅ (verified live)

---

## 1. Cross-cutting mismatch catalog (from the identity-round analysis)

These recur across every entity. Classification drives WHO fixes it:

| Kind | Rule | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| **Field-name mismatch** (backend HAS the data under a different name) | **FE-mapper fix at integration** — backend stays canonical | `total_litres`→`total_quantity_litres`, invoice `date`→`invoice_date`, batch `volume_litres`→`input_litres`, QC `passed`→`pass`/`overall_pass`, `recorded_by_party_id`→`analyst_party_id`, MVU `created_at`→`requested_at`, health `by_role`→`recorded_by_role` |
| **Enum value mismatch** (spec canonical differs) | **fix the WRONG side vs Developer Note** | 🔴 QC `AFM1`→**`AFLATOXIN_M1`** (FE sends wrong → silently bypasses the aflatoxin gate — FE fix, safety-critical); pour `ANALYZER_AUTO`→**`ANALYZER_DIRECT`** (FE fix); org `UNION`↔`MILK_UNION`, `PLANT`↔`PROCESSING_PLANT`; health `AI`↔`ARTIFICIAL_INSEMINATION`, `ILLNESS`↔`DISEASE_REPORT`; QC subject `PLANT_BATCH`→`PROCESSING_BATCH` |
| **Missing backend field** (Developer Note / FE needs it) | **backend ADDS it** | `assurance` A\|B\|C on pour, `rate_chart_version` on pour, `seal_code`+`wavg_fat/snf` on consignment, `Party.public_consent`, cattle yield/lactation fields, batch `contributing_dcs_ids`, LOTSUMMARY materialization |
| **Missing backend endpoint** (FE 404s) | **backend BUILDS it** | onboarding-request queue, `GET /parties?role=`, `/quality/qc-queue`, certificate + trace-back, OCR extract, `/dashboards/*`, `/products`, CMS `/content?since=` |
| **Role/tier catalog gap** | **backend ADDS to catalog** | `ONBOARDING_EXECUTIVE`, `STORE_MANAGER`, `MTLS` tier |

**Danger findings (silent breaks) — must not ship:**
1. 🔴 **QC `AFM1` vs `AFLATOXIN_M1`** — the FE posts `name:"AFM1"`; the backend gate only matches `AFLATOXIN_M1`, so **the aflatoxin safety gate silently does not fire**. (FE fix; backend could also accept the alias defensively.)
2. 🔴 Consignment `total_litres`, invoice `date`/amounts, batch `volume_litres`/`qc_status` — all silently default to 0/'' in the FE (mapper reads wrong keys).
3. 🔴 Role-picker crash: FE `ROLES[code]` is unguarded; a backend-only code (`ORGANISING_MANAGER`, `CONSUMER`) in an assignment throws. (FE fix: guard + add codes.)

---

## 2. Per-Piece build roadmap (one role/functionality at a time)

Priorities: **P0** = FE calls it today and it 404s / breaks integration. **P1** = Developer-Note
correctness. **P2** = dormant / Phase-3.

### ✅ Piece 1 — Identity / Auth core  — **DONE**
- Added roles `ONBOARDING_EXECUTIVE`, `STORE_MANAGER` to `AllRoles` + `RequiredKYCTier` + granter
  matrix; `ONBOARDING_EXECUTIVE` wired as a KYC reviewer + enrolment granter (peer of `ORGANISING_MANAGER`)
  via new `domain.OnboardingReviewerRoles`.
- Added KYC tier `MTLS` (alias of `SERVICE`).
- Added `Party.public_consent` (§6.7) + `PATCH /parties/me {public_consent}`.
- Seed: the Sacheev (9000000001, Ramesh) now ALSO holds a FARMER role → login role-picker exercised.
- **Verified live:** multi-role `/parties/me` (SAMITI_SACHEEV + FARMER, org-enriched), role-select on
  both, `public_consent` toggle, and `ONBOARDING_EXECUTIVE`/`STORE_MANAGER` grants accepted.

### Piece 2 — Collection / Sachiv (the core loop) — P0/P1  ← NEXT
- **DB fields:** `MilkPour.assurance` (A|B|C, enum), `MilkPour.rate_chart_version` (string; store the
  chart's version alongside `rate_chart_id`), `RateChart.version` string. Assurance propagates as
  **weakest-in-set** to consignment/batch/lot.
- **Endpoints:** `POST /collection/pours/ocr-extract` (photo→{fat,snf,confidence}, mock OCR);
  `POST /collection/invoices/approve` (DRAFT→APPROVED per DCS/date — reconcile daily-DRAFT lifecycle
  the FE uses with the backend's ISSUED/SETTLEMENT_PENDING/PAID).
- **Reconcile:** invoice status vocabulary (FE `DRAFT|APPROVED|SETTLED`); assurance on readings.
- Multi-role note: a Sacheev logging a pour is often also a farmer — pours are keyed by
  `farmer_party_id`, never the actor, so self-pour is fine.

### Piece 3 — Farmer — P0/P1
- Farmer dashboard aggregate `GET /dashboards/farmer/:partyId` (today/month/pending + 12-day trend).
- Cattle fields the FE reads (`age_months`/`lactation_no`/`avg_daily_yield_litres` OR FE maps from

I have traced the full flow across both repos. Here is the detailed report.

---

# COLLECTION relations — end-to-end trace (Saathi Go backend vs. Expo FE)

Core answer up front: When a sachiv collects a farmer's milk via `POST /collection/pours`, the backend creates exactly **one** business document — a `MilkPour` with a server-generated `_id` (ObjectID). It does **not** create/update an `AnalyzerReading`, and it does **not** create/update any invoice. The FE's whole "same-day DRAFT invoice, pour.lotId, assurance, rate-chart version" model is only implemented in the FE mock; the real backend does not populate most of it.

---

## 1. `POST /collection/pours` — what gets created

Handler `createPour` → `service.CreatePour` (`internal/modules/collection/service.go:355-505`). Route is gated to `SAMITI_SACHEEV` or `MILK_TESTER` (`module.go:52-53`).

**IDs generated (per successful pour):**
| ID | Where | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `MilkPour._id` (ObjectID) | `service.go:450` `primitive.NewObjectID()` | the pour document, in `milk_pours` |
| provenance `Event` (seq int64 + its own `_id`) | `recordPourProvenance` `service.go:581-593`, stamped back to `pour.provenance_seq` at `service.go:600` | `EventPourRecorded` in `provenance_events` |
| `Notification._id` (ObjectID) | `queueFarmerSMS` `service.go:1190` | farmer receipt SMS outbox, `TemplatePourReceipt` |

Plus a bus publish `TopicPourRecorded` (`service.go:555`). **No AnalyzerReading. No Invoice.**

`ClientEventID` is a device-minted **string** idempotency key (not an ObjectID), unique-indexed (`indexes.go` `milk_pours` → unique `client_event_id`). Replays return the stored pour with `idempotent_replay=true` (`service.go:382-386, 513-550`).

**Foreign-key fields set on the pour** (`MilkPour` struct `internal/domain/collection.go:122-148`; assignment `service.go:449-471`):
- `farmer_party_id` (from request)
- `animal_id` (optional `*ObjectID`, from request)
- `dcs_id` (from request)
- `rate_chart_id` = resolved active chart `chart.ID` (`service.go:463`)
- `analyzer_reading_id` (optional `*ObjectID`, **only if the client sends it** — see bug 6)
- `recorded_by` = actor party id (`service.go:468`)
- `supersedes_pour_id` — only on the `SupersedePour` correction path (`service.go:776`)
- **NOT present at all:** `lot_id` / `consignment_id`, `assurance`, `rate_chart_version`, `temperature_c` (no such fields on the struct)

Provenance refs on the pour.recorded event (`service.go:572-580`): `produced_by`→Party(farmer), `from_animal`→Animal (if `animal_id`), `measured_by`→AnalyzerReading (if `analyzer_reading_id`).

---

## 2. farmer → pour relation

The farmer is linked purely by the `farmer_party_id` ObjectID on the pour, and **is validated as an active DCS member**: `farmerIsActiveMember` (`repo.go:137-157`, called at `service.go:389`) requires a `role_assignments` row with `party_id=farmer`, `org_unit_id=dcs`, `role_code=FARMER`, `status=ACTIVE`, and `UsableAt(now)`. Failure → `422 FARMER_NOT_MEMBER` (`service.go:399`).

**Sacheev self-pour (multi-role):** fully supported and works. The actor (a `SAMITI_SACHEEV`) sets `farmer_party_id` to their own party id; the membership check keys off `farmer_party_id`'s FARMER assignment, so as long as the sachiv also holds a FARMER role at that DCS it passes. `recorded_by` ends up equal to `farmer_party_id`. There is **no anti-self-dealing guard** (no check that `recorded_by != farmer_party_id`) — this is necessary for the legitimate multi-role case, but note there is no second-person control on a sachiv recording their own milk.

---

## 3. pour → invoice relation

**The backend does NOT auto-create/update a same-day invoice on pour.** Invoices are created only by an explicit `POST /collection/invoices/generate` (`GenerateInvoices` `service.go:862-989`), gated to `SAMITI_SACHEEV` only (`module.go:65-66`). That call groups the day's RECORDED, un-invoiced pours by farmer and issues one invoice each:
- `Invoice._id` = `primitive.NewObjectID()` (`service.go:916`)
- `invoice_number` = `INV-<dcsCode>-<date>-<seq>` from an atomic per-DCS-per-day counter (`service.go:911, 917`)
- link to pours: **`pour_ids []ObjectID`** on the invoice (`service.go:925`); there is no back-pointer on the pour.
- unique index `farmer_party_id + dcs_id + invoice_date` is the true duplicate guard; late pours are merged into the existing ISSUED invoice (`mergeIntoExistingInvoice` `service.go:996-1104`).

**Lifecycle mismatch (backend vs FE §8.1):**
- Backend `Invoice` statuses (`collection.go:150-156`): `ISSUED → SETTLEMENT_PENDING → PAID`, plus `HOLD`. There is **no DRAFT and no APPROVED** on the invoice; `APPROVED` lives on the separate settlement-batch rail (`domain/settlement.go:15`).
- FE `Invoice.status` (`domain.ts:399`): `DRAFT → APPROVED → SETTLED`. The FE reconciles by collapsing (`payments.ts:79-89`): `PAID/SETTLED→SETTLED`, `APPROVED→APPROVED`, **everything else incl. `ISSUED`→`DRAFT`**. So a real backend `ISSUED` invoice surfaces in the FE as `DRAFT`, and the FE `APPROVED` state never comes from the invoice object.
- Field shape mismatch: FE `WireInvoice`/`mapInvoice` (`payments.ts:28-40, 91-105`) read `gross_amount`, `deductions`, `net_amount`; backend `Invoice` only has `total_quantity_litres` and `total_amount` (`collection.go:168-169`) — so FE `grossAmount/deductions/netAmount` are always `0` against the real backend.
- The FE mock `recordPour` builds/updates a per-farmer `DRAFT` invoice on every pour (`collections.ts:283-303`); the real backend has no equivalent — the farmer's bill does not exist server-side until a sachiv runs generate.

---

## 4. pour → consignment relation

Consignment creation: `logistics.createConsignment` (`internal/modules/logistics/service.go:74-181`). It reads the shift's RECORDED pours (`repo.findRecordedPours`, filters on `dcs_id + pour_date + shift + status=RECORDED`), aggregates them, and writes:
- `DCSConsignment._id` = `primitive.NewObjectID()` (`service.go:117`)
- **`pour_ids []ObjectID`** (forward reference), `total_quantity_litres`, `can_count`, quantity-weighted `avg_fat_pct`/`avg_snf_pct` (`service.go:118-129`)
- unique index `dcs_id + date + shift`.

**There is NO back-reference written onto the pour.** The `MilkPour` struct has no `lot_id`/`consignment_id`/`bmc_lot_id` field, and neither logistics nor collection ever updates a pour when it is consigned. The pour's `status` stays `RECORDED` (the pour status enum is only `RECORDED|SUPERSEDED|CANCELLED` — no `IN_LOT`). The "sealed shift" freeze is enforced indirectly by counting the consignments collection (`repo.shiftConsigned` `collection/repo.go:476-487`, called at `service.go:433`), not via any field on the pour.

**FE expectation broken:** `mapPour` sets `lotId: w.lot_id ?? w.consignment_id` (`collections.ts:121`). The backend sends **neither**, so `pour.lotId` is always `undefined`. FE code that keys off it — `db.pours.filter(... && !po.lotId)` and `po.lotId = lot.id` in `createLot` (`collections.ts:384, 409`), the invoice route `app/collection/invoice/[lotId].tsx`, and the `IN_LOT` pour status — has no real backend backing.

---

## 5. assurance (A|B|C) and rate_chart_version

**Neither is stored on the pour by the backend.**
- No `assurance` field anywhere in `internal/` (grep: only an unrelated "KYC assurance tiers" comment in `roles.go`). The pour stores only `source` (the reading mode). The FE reconstructs assurance at read time from `source` via `assuranceOf()` (`collections.ts:118`, `utils/assurance.ts`), so it is derivable client-side but never persisted, and — critically — the §6.2 "aggregate inherits the weakest assurance" rule is **unimplemented on the backend**: `logistics.aggregatePours` computes only litres + weighted fat/SNF (`service.go:733-747`); it never computes/stores an assurance on the consignment, and `mapConsignment` never reads one.
- No `rate_chart_version` field anywhere (grep empty). The pour pins `rate_chart_id` (the chart's ObjectID), and `RateChart` has no `version`/immutable-version field (`collection.go:31-42`). FE `mapPour` reads `w.rate_chart_version` (`collections.ts:119`) → always `undefined`. So §6.3's "pin the chart version so a later revision can't rewrite a historical amount" is only half-met: the chart doc is referenced by id, but there is no version string and it isn't surfaced under the field the FE reads.

---

## 6. Photo evidence

- `AnalyzerReading` has `PhotoObjectKey` (bson `photo_object_key`, `collection.go:82`) plus `OCRConfidence`. There is **no `photo_link`** field. `CreateReading` requires `photo_object_key` when `mode=PHOTO_OCR` (`service.go:254-256`) and the `PHOTO_OCR` feature flag must be enabled (`service.go:245-253`). This is the intended §8.2 immutable-evidence anchor.
- **But the payment-driving object is the pour, and the pour carries no photo and is never forced to reference a reading.** The FE only ever hits `POST /collection/pours` — grep confirms the FE **never** calls `POST /collection/readings`, never sends `analyzer_reading_id`, and never uploads a photo / sends `photo_object_key` (`recordPour.mapRequest` `collections.ts:224-235`). The FE `photoOcrExtract` is mock-only (`collections.ts:320` `TODO(backend): no OCR endpoint yet`). Net: a pour can be recorded with `source=PHOTO_OCR` while `analyzer_reading_id` is nil and no photo exists anywhere — the §8.2 evidence retention does not attach to the artefact that actually drives payment.

---

## 7. BUGS / mismatches (concrete)

1. **pour→lot back-reference missing (breaks `pour.lotId`).** `MilkPour` (`internal/domain/collection.go:122-148`) has no `lot_id`/`consignment_id`; logistics never writes one back (`internal/modules/logistics/service.go:114-181` only sets `consignment.pour_ids`). FE `mapPour` reads `w.lot_id ?? w.consignment_id` (`src/core/api/endpoints/collections.ts:121`) → always `undefined`. Downstream FE lot logic (`collections.ts:384, 409`) and the invoice-by-lot screen are unbacked.

2. **Pour status enum divergence.** Backend: `RECORDED|SUPERSEDED|CANCELLED` (`collection.go:110-114`) and status never advances when consigned/invoiced. FE `Pour.status`: `RECORDED|IN_LOT|INVOICED|PAID` (`domain.ts:159`). `IN_LOT`/`INVOICED`/`PAID` are never emitted by the backend.

3. **No same-day auto invoice on pour (FE §8.1 expectation unmet).** `CreatePour` touches no invoice; invoices exist only after an explicit sachiv-only `generate` (`service.go:862-989`). FE mock creates/updates a DRAFT invoice per pour (`collections.ts:283-303`). Farmer's "same-day bill" does not exist server-side between pour and generate.

4. **Invoice status vocabulary mismatch.** Backend `ISSUED/SETTLEMENT_PENDING/PAID/HOLD` (`collection.go:150-156`) vs FE `DRAFT/APPROVED/SETTLED` (`domain.ts:399`). FE maps `ISSUED→DRAFT` (`payments.ts:79-89`); a genuine backend `APPROVED` invoice state does not exist.

5. **Invoice amount fields mismatch.** FE reads `gross_amount/deductions/net_amount` (`payments.ts:28-40, 91-105`); backend only serialises `total_amount`/`total_quantity_litres` (`collection.go:161-174`). FE `grossAmount/netAmount/deductions` are always `0` against the real API.

6. **`assurance` not persisted and not inherited by aggregates (§6.2).** No field on `MilkPour`; `logistics.aggregatePours` (`service.go:733-747`) never derives/stores a consignment-level weakest-assurance. FE `DcsLot.assurance` (`domain.ts:178`) is never populated by `mapConsignment` (`collections.ts:128-143`).

7. **`rate_chart_version` never set (§6.3 partial).** No version field on `MilkPour` or `RateChart`; FE `rateChartVersion` (`domain.ts:158`, read at `collections.ts:119`) is always `undefined`. Only `rate_chart_id` pins pricing.

8. **OCR photo evidence never reaches the backend for pours (§8.2 gap).** FE never creates an `AnalyzerReading`, never sends `photo_object_key` or `analyzer_reading_id`, and `photoOcrExtract` is mock-only (`collections.ts:320`). A `PHOTO_OCR` pour is stored with no linked reading and no evidence photo.

9. **`temperature_c` silently dropped.** FE `recordPour` sends `temperature_c` (`collections.ts:233`) and models `Pour.temperatureC`/`clr` (`domain.ts:148`); backend `CreatePourRequest`/`MilkPour` have `clr` but **no temperature field at all** (grep empty). Milk temperature captured at collection is lost server-side.

10. **Latent `source` value mismatch.** Backend accepts `ANALYZER_DIRECT|PHOTO_OCR|MANUAL` (`service.go:365-368`); FE domain uses `ANALYZER_AUTO` and sends `source: entryMethod` raw (`collections.ts:234`). Not triggered today because `RecordPourSheet` only ever sends `PHOTO_OCR`/`MANUAL` (`RecordPourSheet.tsx:115`), but any analyzer-auto path would be rejected `422 VALIDATION`. (FE handles the reverse direction on read via `mapEntryMethod`, `collections.ts:92-102`.)

# LOGISTICS Relation Trace — Saathi Go Backend vs Frontend

## ID generation summary (where each id is minted)

| id | Where minted | Line | Notes |

| `seal_code` | **NOWHERE** | — | not modeled in backend |

All ObjectIDs serialize as 24-hex `id` in JSON.

## 1. Sachiv seals a consignment — `POST /logistics/consignments` + `.../dispatch`

**Create** (`createConsignment`, service.go:74; role `SAMITI_SACHEEV` only, module.go:30-31):
- Generates `consignment.ID` (service.go:117). No human `consignment_code`.
- **FK consignment → pours:** `PourIDs []ObjectID` → `pour_ids` (domain/logistics.go:27). Built by `aggregatePours` (service.go:733) over `findRecordedPours(dcs_id, pour_date, shift, status=RECORDED)` (repo.go:47). This is a **forward-only** reference.
- **FK consignment → dcs:** `DCSID` → `dcs_id` (domain/logistics.go:24).
- Also computes quantity-weighted `AvgFatPct`/`AvgSNFPct` → `avg_fat_pct`/`avg_snf_pct` (service.go:114, 743-745), plus `can_count`, `total_quantity_litres`. Status `OPEN`.
- Unique index on dcs+date+shift → replay returns `CONSIGNMENT_EXISTS` (service.go:135).

**Dispatch** (`dispatchConsignment`, service.go:188; `SAMITI_SACHEEV` only):
- OPEN→DISPATCHED (repo.go:95 optimistic on `status=OPEN`). **Re-aggregates** pours at the seal boundary and re-stamps `pour_ids`/litres/can_count/avg fat/snf (service.go:207-227).
- Sets `dispatched_at` (service.go:261). Emits `consignment.dispatched` ledger event.

**§6.4 check — seal_code / wavg:**
- **`seal_code`: MISSING.** No field on `DCSConsignment` (domain/logistics.go:22-39), never minted at dispatch. `pickupRequest` has no seal param (models.go:30-33), `RouteStop` has no seal field (domain/logistics.go:50-56).
- **`sealed_at`: MISSING** — only `dispatched_at` exists.
- **wavg_fat/wavg_snf: present as DATA but under different names** (`avg_fat_pct`/`avg_snf_pct`). The quantity-weighted average the Note asks for is computed, just not named `wavg_*`.
- Confirmed by the repo's own `docs/ALIGNMENT_SPEC.md:136`: `dcs_consignments seal_code, sealed_at, wavg_fat, wavg_snf → planned (P4) → §6.4 tamper seal`, and line 79 lists `RouteStop.seal_code verify (409 SEAL_MISMATCH)` as still-planned.

**Pour → consignment back-reference: MISSING.** The logistics `pours` collection is opened read-only (repo.go:25) and no module writes `lot_id`/`consignment_id`/`IN_LOT` onto pours (grep of collection module + domain came back empty; `MilkPour` statuses are only `RECORDED|SUPERSEDED|CANCELLED`, domain/collection.go:111-113). So the pour never learns it was pooled, even though FE `mapPour` reads `lot_id ?? consignment_id` and expects statuses `RECORDED|IN_LOT|INVOICED|PAID` (collections.ts:52-53, 120-121).

---

## 2. Van rider picks up — `POST /logistics/trips/{tripID}/stops/{consignmentID}/pickup`

**Trip creation** (`createTrip`, service.go:320; role `UNION_FIELD_SUPERVISOR` or `VAN_RIDER`, module.go:44):
- Generates `trip_id` (service.go:396). Each stop validated: consignment must be `DISPATCHED` and belong to the stop's `dcs_id` (`validateStopConsignment`, service.go:815). Stops stored as `[]RouteStop{dcs_id, consignment_id}` (domain/logistics.go:50). Status `PLANNED`.

**Pickup** (`pickupStop`, service.go:423; `VAN_RIDER` only):
- Links pickup→trip→consignment via the path `{tripID}` + `{consignmentID}`; `findStop` requires the consignment to be a stop on the trip (service.go:836-839).
- **Consignment back-reference `route_trip_id`: YES, set here.** `markConsignmentPickedUp(consignmentID, trip.ID)` does DISPATCHED→PICKED_UP **and** `$set route_trip_id = tripID` atomically (repo.go:112-118). Serializes as `route_trip_id` (domain/logistics.go:35).
- Stamps the stop `picked_up_at`, `temp_c`, `notes` (repo.go:199); trip → `IN_PROGRESS`.
- **Seal verification: NONE.** No seal is checked or matched — there is no seal to check. `pickupRequest` carries only `temp_c` + `notes` (models.go:30). No `SEAL_MISMATCH` path exists anywhere in the backend.

---

## 3. Van delivers → BMC lot

Two **separate** steps — delivery does NOT create a lot:

**a) Deliver** (`deliverTrip`, service.go:552; `VAN_RIDER` only; `POST /trips/{tripID}/deliver {bmc_id}`):
- Requires every stop picked up (`validateDeliver`, service.go:859). Trip IN_PROGRESS→DELIVERED, sets `delivered_to_bmc_id` + `delivered_at` (repo.go:226). Consignments PICKED_UP→DELIVERED in bulk (`markConsignmentsDelivered`, repo.go:127). **No BMCLot is created here**; only status flips.

**b) Pool into lot** (`plant/service.go` `CreateBMCLot`, service.go:128; role `BMC_OPERATOR`, plant/module.go:39; `POST /plant/bmc-lots`):
- Generates `bmc_lot_id` (service.go:181).
- **FK lot → consignments:** `ConsignmentIDs` → `consignment_ids` (from request, deduped; domain/processing.go:26).
- **FK lot → trips:** `RouteTripIDs` → `route_trip_ids`, derived by de-duping each pooled consignment's `route_trip_id` (service.go:199-207, domain/processing.go:27). So trip linkage flows consignment.`route_trip_id` → lot.`route_trip_ids`.
- **Consignment back-reference `bmc_lot_id`: YES.** `ClaimConsignments` atomically flips DELIVERED→ACCEPTED and `$set bmc_lot_id = lotID` (repo.go:60-75). Lost-race compensation via `ReleaseConsignments` (repo.go:79).
- Net result: a pooled consignment ends holding BOTH `route_trip_id` and `bmc_lot_id` — the full chain survives on the doc.

---

## 4. "Batch mint" (Note §6.4) vs actual chain

The Developer Note's "van mints a BATCH code binding its consignments" is **not modeled**. There is:
- No batch/`batch_code` at the trip level; the `RouteTrip` has no such field.
- The only human-readable batch number (`BATCH-<orgCode>-<date>-<seq>`) is minted at the **PLANT** by the plant operator (`CreateBatch`, plant/service.go:464), pooling **BMC lots**, not the van pooling consignments.

**Actual relation chain (as built):**
```
MilkPour (RECORDED)
  └─pour_ids──▶ DCSConsignment            (pooling boundary #1, Sacheev; dcs+date+shift)
                 status: OPEN→DISPATCHED→PICKED_UP→DELIVERED→ACCEPTED
                 ├─route_trip_id──▶ RouteTrip  (transport binding, van; NOT a "batch")
                 └─bmc_lot_id─────▶ BMCLot     (pooling #2, BMC operator)
                                      consignment_ids[], route_trip_ids[]
                                      status: OPEN→QC_PENDING→PASSED→DISPATCHED→POOLED
                                      └─batch_id──▶ ProcessingBatch  (pooling #3, plant)
                                                      bmc_lot_ids[], batch_number
                                                      └─▶ ProductLot ─▶ BatchQR
```
The van's "binding of its consignments" corresponds only to the `RouteTrip` (via `route_trip_id` + `lot.route_trip_ids`); there is no minted van-level batch code. Note ALIGNMENT_SPEC.md:80 lists "Van batch-mint code (Developer Note `BATCH`), GPS track" as still-planned (P4).

---

**Missing model / relation (backend):**

1. **`seal_code` + `sealed_at` entirely absent** (§6.4). `DCSConsignment` domain/logistics.go:22-39, `dispatchConsignment` service.go:188-270, `RouteStop` domain/logistics.go:50-56, `pickupRequest` models.go:30-33. No seal minting, no `SEAL_MISMATCH` verification at pickup. The whole FE seal chain (collections.ts:74-75, 438; logistics.ts:239-268 `SEAL_REQUIRED`/`SEAL_MISMATCH`; domain.ts DcsLot.sealCode:184, RouteStop.sealCode:272) is a **no-op against the backend**.

2. **Pour → consignment back-reference missing.** Consignment references `pour_ids` forward, but no module writes `lot_id`/`consignment_id`/`IN_LOT` back onto pours (logistics `pours` is read-only, repo.go:25; no writer found in collection). FE `mapPour` (collections.ts:121) and pour status `IN_LOT` (domain.ts:159) can never populate.

3. **`wavg_fat`/`wavg_snf` naming.** Data exists as `avg_fat_pct`/`avg_snf_pct` (domain/logistics.go:30-31); Note §6.4 / ALIGNMENT_SPEC.md:136 expect `wavg_*`. Naming gap only (FE happens to read `avg_*`, so FE is fine; the Note is unmet).

**FE↔BE field/enum mismatches (integration breaks):**

4. **Pickup path keyed wrong + missing required field.** FE `recordPickup` puts `dcsId` in the `{consignmentID}` slot (logistics.ts:236-238, acknowledged in comment) → BE `findStop` matches on `consignment_id`, so a `dcs_id` never matches → 404. Additionally BE **requires** `temp_c` (`validateTemp`, service.go:424/773 → 400 `MISSING_TEMP`) but FE sends only lat/lng/photo_uri/seal_code and explicitly assumes "no temperature" at pickup (logistics.ts:228-244). Real HTTP pickup fails.

5. **`total_quantity_litres` vs `total_litres`.** BE emits `total_quantity_litres` (domain/logistics.go:28); FE `WireConsignment` reads `total_litres` (collections.ts:71→136) → `totalLitres` silently 0. Documented 🔴 in ALIGNMENT_SPEC.md:41.

6. **`consignment_code` missing.** BE has no code field; FE reads `consignment_code`/`code` (collections.ts:65-66→131) → `consignmentCode: ''`. `DcsLot.consignmentCode` (domain.ts:169) is used as audit subject/display.

7. **RouteStop pickup-state shape mismatch.** BE serializes stops with `picked_up_at`/`temp_c`/`notes` (domain/logistics.go:53-55). FE `WireTripStop` reads `arrived_at`/`collected`/`status`/`planned_time`/geo/`photo_uri` (logistics.ts:30-41); `collected` derives from absent `status` → **always false** (mapStop, logistics.ts:114). The FE trip UI can never see a stop as collected.

8. **Trip → `bmc_id` mismatch.** BE serializes `delivered_to_bmc_id` (domain/logistics.go:78); FE `WireTrip` reads `bmc_id` (logistics.ts:51→128) → `trip.bmcId: ''`. Chains into `deliverToBmc` sourcing `bmc_id` from `trip.bmcId` (logistics.ts:328) → BE 400 `MISSING_BMC_ID`.

9. **Trip timestamps absent.** BE has no `departed_at`/`completed_at` (uses status + `delivered_at`); FE reads `departed_at`/`completed_at` (logistics.ts:56, 129-130) → always undefined.

10. **BMCLot trip linkage mismatch.** BE serializes array `route_trip_ids` (domain/processing.go:27); FE `WireBMCLot` reads singular `trip_id` (plant.ts:41→108) → `tripId: ''` (comment even admits "tripId has no wire source"). BE `total_quantity_litres` on the lot isn't read at all by the FE intake mapper.

11. **BMCLot status enum mismatch.** BE emits `OPEN|QC_PENDING|PASSED|BLOCKED|DISPATCHED|POOLED` (domain/processing.go:11-18). FE `mapBmcLotStatus` (plant.ts:87-101) handles `OPEN`, `CLOSED` (never emitted — BE uses `QC_PENDING`), `DISPATCHED`, `REJECTED`/`QUARANTINED` (BE uses `BLOCKED`). So `QC_PENDING`/`PASSED`/`BLOCKED`/`POOLED` all fall through to `RECEIVED` — lot state misrepresented.

12. **No "intake" entity / no auto-lot on delivery.** FE `deliverToBmc` expects `{ trip, intake }` (logistics.ts:320-335) but BE `deliverTrip` returns only the trip (service.go:626) → intake always synthesized client-side (`intakeFromTrip`). BE has no intake concept; the BMCLot is the intake grain and is created by a separate BMC-operator call. The FE `bmc.ts` console (chill/dispatch-to-plant) is entirely mock — no backend module ships it (bmc.ts:11-13).

# ACCESS-CONTROL & ORG-HIERARCHY Verification — Saathi Go backend

## 1. SUPER_ADMIN access — is there a global bypass?

**Yes, two independent global bypasses, and they cover both gates:**

- **RBAC gate bypass** — `internal/platform/middleware/rbac.go:30-33`. Inside `RequireRoles(...)`, before the allow-list is consulted:
  ```go
  if actor.RoleCode == domain.RoleSuperAdmin {
      next.ServeHTTP(w, r); return
  }
  ```
  So SUPER_ADMIN passes **every** `RequireRoles(...)` gate on every route, regardless of the listed roles.

- **Org-scope bypass** — `internal/platform/orgscope/resolver.go:116-119`. `RequireInScope` returns `nil` immediately for SUPER_ADMIN (and STATE_AUDITOR):
  ```go
  if actor.RoleCode == domain.RoleSuperAdmin || actor.RoleCode == domain.RoleStateAuditor {
      return nil
  }
  ```
  I confirmed the **only** raw `Resolver.InScope(...)` call (the path-containment check with no role bypass) is *inside* `RequireInScope` itself, after this early-return (`resolver.go:127`). Every module reaches scope enforcement through `RequireInScope`/wrappers (`requireInScope`, `requireScope`, `requireSubjectScope`) — I enumerated all ~45 call sites across collection, logistics, plant, quality, settlement, cattle, orgs, identity, and none bypass the exemption. So SUPER_ADMIN passes every org-scope check everywhere.

**Does super_admin "see everything"? Effectively yes for reads, with caveats:**

- SUPER_ADMIN is seeded at the **federation root** (`cmd/seed/main.go:111`, org `federation.ID`), and its role token carries `OrgType=FEDERATION` (resolved at role-select in `identity/service.go:415` → `IssueRoleToken(..., org.Type)`). Since the federation is the ancestor of every node, even if the bypass were removed, path-containment would still make everything in-scope.

- **Endpoints where SUPER_ADMIN is NOT effectively allowed** (passes RBAC + scope but is stopped by a secondary *per-actor ownership* check — these are by design, not the org-scope system):
  - `logistics` **pickupStop / logColdChain / deliverTrip** — service calls `requireTripRider(trip, actorID)` which compares `trip.VanRiderPartyID` to the actor's own party ID (`service.go:806-811`, invoked via `validatePickup`/`validateColdChain`/`validateDeliver`). SUPER_ADMIN's party ≠ the assigned rider → `403 "this trip is assigned to another van rider"`. So SUPER_ADMIN can read any trip (`getTrip` takes the non-rider branch → `RequireInScope` passes) but cannot perform rider transitions.
  - `logistics` **createTrip** without an explicit `van_rider_party_id` → `RIDER_REQUIRED` (`service.go:358`), because SUPER_ADMIN isn't a `VAN_RIDER`. Must pass the rider id explicitly.
  - `settlement` **Approve** — dual-control (`validateApproval`, `service.go:49-53`) blocks approving a batch it *initiated*, checked on party identity so "not even SUPER_ADMIN's role bypass can approve its own batch." SUPER_ADMIN can still approve batches initiated by others.

- **Inconsistency (not a hole, but a "sees everything" gap):** some list endpoints special-case SUPER_ADMIN/STATE_AUDITOR for *unfiltered* scans (`logistics.listConsignments:285`, `logistics.listTrips:643`, `settlement.List:572`), but **collection** `ListPours`/`ListInvoices`/`ListReadings` do **not** — they hard-require a `dcs_id` for any non-FARMER role (`collection/service.go:838-839, 1125-1126, 333-334`). SUPER_ADMIN can still read any DCS by naming it, but cannot list pours/invoices federation-wide in one call.

## 2. Parent/child relation model

**Modeled exactly as described** (`internal/domain/orgunit.go:42-56`):
- `ParentID *primitive.ObjectID` (`bson:"parent_id,omitempty"`) — direct parent by ObjectID.
- `Path []primitive.ObjectID` (`bson:"path"`) — denormalized ancestor ObjectIDs, root→parent, **excluding** self.
- `Type` + `ValidOrgParent` map (`orgunit.go:25-31`) encodes allowed edges: FEDERATION=root; MILK_UNION←FEDERATION; PROCESSING_PLANT←{UNION,FEDERATION}; BMC←UNION; DCS←{UNION,BMC}.

**Seed builds the chain correctly** (`cmd/seed/main.go:56-102`):
| Org | Type | ParentID | Path |
|---|---|---|---|
| PCDF | FEDERATION | — | `[]` |
| UNION-LKO | MILK_UNION | federation | `[fed]` |
| PLANT-LKO-01 | PROCESSING_PLANT | union | `[fed, union]` |
| BMC-LKO-007 | BMC | union | `[fed, union]` |
| DCS-01842 | DCS | **bmc** | `[fed, union, bmc]` |
| DCS-01907 | DCS | **bmc** | `[fed, union, bmc]` |

The FEDERATION→UNION→BMC→DCS chain is correct: each DCS's `parent_id = bmc` and `path = [fed, union, bmc]`. Plant and BMC are siblings under the union. Idempotency is sound — `upsertOrg` returns the stored doc (`SetReturnDocument(After)`), so on re-runs `federation.ID`/`union.ID`/`bmc.ID` resolve to the persisted IDs and child paths stay consistent; `$setOnInsert` never rewrites.

**`InScope` uses path-containment** (`resolver.go:96-110`): `scope == target` OR `scope ∈ target.Path`. This is correct downward-only semantics (a DCS actor is *not* in scope of its union). The `path` field is indexed (`mongodb/indexes.go:74`), and subtree reads use `{path: rootID}` array-containment (`orgs/repo.go:128`). Runtime `InScope` reads only the target's `Path` in memory (cached 60s) — no recursive walk.

## 3. Org-scope enforcement on write paths (IDOR audit)

All five named write flows **do** call scope enforcement:

| Write path | File:line | Scope target | OK |
|---|---|---|---|
| pour create | `collection/service.go:370` | `req.DCSID` | ✓ |
| pour batch-sync | via `CreatePour` (`:638`) | per-item DCSID | ✓ |
| pour supersede | `collection/service.go:671` | `old.DCSID` | ✓ |
| invoice generate | `collection/service.go:880` | `req.DCSID` | ✓ |
| consignment create | `logistics/service.go:90` | `req.DCSID` | ✓ |
| consignment dispatch | `logistics/service.go:193` | `consignment.DCSID` | ✓ |
| bmc-lot create | `plant/service.go:133` | `req.BMCID` | ✓ |
| bmc-lot close/dispatch | `plant/service.go:267, 322` | `lot.BMCID` | ✓ |
| batch create/complete | `plant/service.go:416, 549` | `req.PlantID`/`batch.PlantID` | ✓ |
| product-lot create/recall/QR | `plant/service.go:644, 725, 851` | plant | ✓ |
| qc record | `quality/service.go:163` | `subject.orgUnitID` (BMC/plant) + stage×role pairing (`:135`) | ✓ |
| settlement initiate/approve/reject/execute | `settlement/service.go:118, 240, 323, 386` | `DCSID` | ✓ |

A sachiv/BMC operator/plant operator is confined to their own subtree on every one of these. **Rider transitions** (pickup/cold-chain/deliver) are guarded by trip-rider *ownership* instead of org-scope (`validatePickup`/`validateColdChain`/`validateDeliver` → `requireTripRider`), which is appropriate for a mobile rider.

**Missing / weak scope checks found (see BUGS):** logistics `createTrip` stop consignments, and `deliverTrip` destination BMC.

## 4. STATE_AUDITOR — federation-wide read?

**Partially — and this is the notable finding.** STATE_AUDITOR is federation-wide **at the org-scope layer only**: it shares the SUPER_ADMIN early-return in `RequireInScope` (`resolver.go:117`), so any scope check passes. **But it does NOT bypass `RequireRoles`** (only SUPER_ADMIN does). Therefore STATE_AUDITOR can actually reach a read endpoint only where it is explicitly listed in that route's allow-list. It is listed in:
- `orgs` `/{id}/tree` (`orgs/module.go:50`)
- `quality` qc-results list/get (`quality/module.go:49`)
- `settlement` list/detail/payouts and DBT list (`settlement/module.go:38, 68, 85`)

It is **absent** from all `collection`, `logistics`, and `plant` read routes. So STATE_AUDITOR cannot read pours, invoices, readings, rate charts, consignments, trips, BMC lots, batches, product lots, or QRs — despite the org-scope layer treating it as federation-wide. See BUG-3 (the service even has dead unfiltered-scan branches for it in `listConsignments`/`listTrips`).

## 5. BUGS / findings (concrete)

**BUG-1 (Medium — IDOR / cross-scope integrity): `createTrip` does not scope-check stop consignments.**
`internal/modules/logistics/service.go:341` scope-checks only `req.UnionID`. Each stop is then validated by `validateStopConsignment` (`service.go:815-825`), which checks only `status == DISPATCHED` and `consignment.DCSID == stop.DCSID` — **no** check that the stop's DCS/consignment lies under `req.UnionID` or in the actor's scope. A UNION_FIELD_SUPERVISOR (or VAN_RIDER) of union A can enroll another union's DISPATCHED consignment onto union A's trip; the subsequent `pickupStop` then flips that foreign consignment DISPATCHED→PICKED_UP (`service.go:444`). Result: cross-union milk pooling and a state mutation on an out-of-scope consignment. Add `RequireInScope(actor, stop.DCSID)` (or verify `stop.DCSID`'s path contains `req.UnionID`) in the stop loop.

**BUG-2 (Low/Medium — missing scope check on delivery target): `deliverTrip` does not scope-check the destination BMC.**
`internal/modules/logistics/service.go:552-576` validates rider ownership and `bmc.Type == BMC` but never calls `RequireInScope` on `req.BMCID`. A trip can be "delivered" to any BMC in the system regardless of union. Lower severity because riders legitimately cross org lines, but the destination is entirely unconstrained.

**BUG-3 (Medium — dead code / broken STATE_AUDITOR read promise):** `listConsignments` (`logistics/service.go:285`) and `listTrips` (`logistics/service.go:643`) contain explicit `RoleStateAuditor` unfiltered-scan branches, but the corresponding GET routes' `RequireRoles` allow-lists (`logistics/module.go:33-36, 41-43`) omit STATE_AUDITOR. Those branches are unreachable for STATE_AUDITOR (only SUPER_ADMIN reaches them via RBAC bypass). Either add STATE_AUDITOR to the read allow-lists (to fulfill "federation-wide read") or drop the dead branches. Same "federation-wide read" gap applies across all collection/plant read routes.

**BUG-4 (Low — cross-union pooling at the plant): `CreateBatch` doesn't scope-check the pooled BMC lots.**
`internal/modules/plant/service.go:411-456` scope-checks only `req.PlantID`; the BMC lots are pulled by ID and validated only for `canPoolBMCLot` (status DISPATCHED). A plant operator can pool a DISPATCHED lot from *any* union's BMC into their batch. Likely tolerable given the "plant receives tankers from sibling BMCs" design note, but there is no union-boundary enforcement, so a *different* union's lot is not rejected. Consistent with BUG-1's pattern.

**Non-bug observations (by design, but relevant to "super_admin sees everything"):**
- `collection.ListPours/ListInvoices/ListReadings` require a `dcs_id` even for SUPER_ADMIN (no wide-scan branch) — inconsistent with consignments/trips/settlements which do special-case wide roles. Not a security hole (any DCS is reachable by naming it), just an asymmetry.
- `ListBMCLots` (`plant/service.go:393-404`) only scope-checks when the caller is a BMC_OPERATOR with a BMCID filter; plant-side readers list across BMCs unrestricted — documented behavior.
- `orgs.Create` performs no scope check when creating a **root FEDERATION** (no parent → the `if parent != nil` scope block at `orgs/service.go:147` is skipped), relying on the federation-uniqueness conflict (`service.go:133-143`) and the PCDF_ADMIN/SUPER_ADMIN route gate. Minor.

**Verified correct / no bug:** the SUPER_ADMIN RBAC bypass exists and is complete; the SUPER_ADMIN + STATE_AUDITOR org-scope bypass exists; the `parent_id` + `path[]` model and its `path` index are correct; the seed builds FEDERATION→UNION→BMC→DCS accurately and idempotently; `InScope` is correct downward-only path-containment; and all five named write paths (pour, consignment, bmc-lot, batch, qc) enforce `RequireInScope`.

38	// service holds all business logic of the collection module.

45	// newService wires the service onto the platform dependencies. log is the
46	// module-scoped logger derived in Register.
