=== assurance util ===
import type { PourAssurance, PourEntryMethod } from '@/core/types/domain';

/**
 * Capture-assurance level of a fat/SNF reading (developer note §6.2).
 * Derived from how the reading was captured:
 *   A - instrument-linked (analyzer streams over RS-232 / BLE)
 *   B - OCR-with-photo (Sachiv photographs the display, app OCRs + stores it)
 *   C - manual (Sachiv keys the value; last resort, drives higher audit)
 */
export function assuranceOf(entryMethod: PourEntryMethod): PourAssurance {
  switch (entryMethod) {
    case 'ANALYZER_AUTO':
      return 'A';
    case 'PHOTO_OCR':
      return 'B';
    default:
      return 'C';
  }
}

/** A is strongest, C weakest. */
const RANK: Record<PourAssurance, number> = { A: 0, B: 1, C: 2 };

/**
 * The WEAKEST assurance in a set - the value a consignment / batch / lot
 * inherits from its pours (§6.2: "aggregates inherit the weakest assurance in
 * their set, so capture quality is measured, not papered over").
 */
export function weakestAssurance(levels: PourAssurance[]): PourAssurance | undefined {
  if (levels.length === 0) return undefined;
  return levels.reduce((worst, l) => (RANK[l] > RANK[worst] ? l : worst), levels[0]);
}

1	// Package auth owns tokens and credentials: JWT issue/verify, OTP generation
2	// and HMAC hashing, opaque refresh tokens. Nothing secret is ever stored in
3	// plaintext — OTPs and refresh tokens live in the DB only as HMAC-SHA256
4	// digests.
5	package auth
6	
7	import (
8		"fmt"
9		"time"
10	
11		"github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v5"
12		"github.com/google/uuid"
13	
14		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/domain"
15	)
16	
17	// Token kinds. A SESSION token proves "this phone logged in"; a ROLE token
18	// additionally pins one active role assignment + org scope (the role switcher
19	// simply issues a fresh ROLE token).
20	const (
21		TokenKindSession = "session"
22		TokenKindRole    = "role"
23	)
24	
25	// Claims is the JWT payload.
26	type Claims struct {
27		PartyID          string `json:"pid"`
28		Phone            string `json:"phn"`
29		KYCTier          string `json:"kyc"`
30		Kind             string `json:"knd"`
31		RoleAssignmentID string `json:"rid,omitempty"`
32		RoleCode         string `json:"rol,omitempty"`
33		OrgUnitID        string `json:"org,omitempty"`
34		OrgType          string `json:"ogt,omitempty"`
35		jwt.RegisteredClaims
36	}
37	
38	// JWTManager issues and parses access tokens.
39	type JWTManager struct {
40		secret []byte
41		ttl    time.Duration
42	}
43	
44	// NewJWTManager builds a manager with the shared HS256 secret and access TTL.
45	func NewJWTManager(secret string, ttl time.Duration) *JWTManager {
46		return &JWTManager{secret: []byte(secret), ttl: ttl}
47	}
48	
49	// IssueSessionToken returns a SESSION-kind access token for a logged-in party.
50	// ObjectIDs travel in claims as hex strings (JWTs are JSON).
51	func (m *JWTManager) IssueSessionToken(p domain.Party) (string, error) {
52		return m.sign(Claims{
53			PartyID: p.ID.Hex(),
54			Phone:   p.Phone,
55			KYCTier: p.KYCTier,
56			Kind:    TokenKindSession,
57		})
58	}
59	
60	// IssueRoleToken returns a ROLE-kind access token pinned to one assignment.
61	func (m *JWTManager) IssueRoleToken(p domain.Party, ra domain.RoleAssignment, orgType string) (string, error) {
62		return m.sign(Claims{
63			PartyID:          p.ID.Hex(),
64			Phone:            p.Phone,
65			KYCTier:          p.KYCTier,
66			Kind:             TokenKindRole,
67			RoleAssignmentID: ra.ID.Hex(),
68			RoleCode:         ra.RoleCode,
69			OrgUnitID:        ra.OrgUnitID.Hex(),
70			OrgType:          orgType,
71		})
72	}
73	
74	func (m *JWTManager) sign(c Claims) (string, error) {
75		now := time.Now()
76		c.RegisteredClaims = jwt.RegisteredClaims{
77			Issuer:    "saathi-backend",
78			Subject:   c.PartyID,
79			IssuedAt:  jwt.NewNumericDate(now),
80			ExpiresAt: jwt.NewNumericDate(now.Add(m.ttl)),
81			ID:        uuid.NewString(),
82		}
83		return jwt.NewWithClaims(jwt.SigningMethodHS256, c).SignedString(m.secret)
84	}
85	
86	// Parse validates signature+expiry and returns the claims.
87	func (m *JWTManager) Parse(token string) (*Claims, error) {
88		parsed, err := jwt.ParseWithClaims(token, &Claims{},
89			func(t *jwt.Token) (any, error) { return m.secret, nil },
90			jwt.WithValidMethods([]string{jwt.SigningMethodHS256.Alg()}),
91			jwt.WithIssuer("saathi-backend"),
92		)
93		if err != nil {
94			return nil, fmt.Errorf("parse token: %w", err)
95		}
96		claims, ok := parsed.Claims.(*Claims)
97		if !ok || !parsed.Valid {
98			return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid token claims")
99		}
100		return claims, nil
101	}
102

1	// Package httpapi assembles the HTTP surface: global middleware, operational
2	// endpoints (health/readiness/metrics/version), and the /api/v1 tree where
3	// every domain module mounts its routes.
4	package httpapi
5	
6	import (
7		"context"
8		"net/http"
9		"time"
10	
11		"github.com/go-chi/chi/v5"
12		chimw "github.com/go-chi/chi/v5/middleware"
13		"github.com/prometheus/client_golang/prometheus/promhttp"
14	
15		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/deps"
16		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/httpx"
17		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/middleware"
18		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/sse"
19	)
20	
21	// Version is stamped via -ldflags at release build time.
22	var Version = "0.1.0-dev"
23	
24	// New builds the fully wired HTTP handler.
25	func New(d *deps.Deps) http.Handler {
26		r := chi.NewRouter()
27	
28		// Order matters: recover innermost-last so panics in anything above are caught.
29		r.Use(chimw.RequestID)
30		r.Use(chimw.RealIP)
31		r.Use(middleware.Metrics)
32		r.Use(middleware.RequestLogger(d.Log))
33		r.Use(middleware.RateLimit(d.RateLimiter))
34		r.Use(chimw.Recoverer)
35		r.Use(chimw.Timeout(30 * time.Second))
36	
37		// Unmatched routes and wrong methods must carry the same JSON error
38		// envelope every other response uses — never chi's plain-text defaults.
39		// (chimw.Timeout's bare 504 on handler deadline is a known, accepted gap.)
40		r.NotFound(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
41			httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.RouteNotFound())
42		})
43		r.MethodNotAllowed(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
44			httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.MethodNotAllowed())
45		})
46	
47		// Operational endpoints — outside /api/v1, never authenticated.
48		r.Get("/healthz", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
49			httpx.JSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]string{"status": "ok"})
50		})
51		r.Get("/readyz", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
52			ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(r.Context(), 2*time.Second)
53			defer cancel()
54			if err := d.DB.Client().Ping(ctx, nil); err != nil {
55				httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Internal(err))
56				return
57			}
58			httpx.JSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]string{"status": "ready"})
59		})
60		r.Handle("/metrics", promhttp.Handler())
61		r.Get("/version", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
62			httpx.JSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]string{"version": Version, "service": "saathi-backend"})
63		})
64	
65		r.Route("/api/v1", func(api chi.Router) {
66			// Inner Route() calls create fresh chi Muxes — re-register the JSON
67			// 404/405 handlers so the envelope also covers /api/v1 subtrees.
68			api.NotFound(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
69				httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.RouteNotFound())
70			})
71			api.MethodNotAllowed(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
72				httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.MethodNotAllowed())
73			})
74			api.Use(middleware.AuditMutations(d.Audit))
75	
76			// Live event stream (SSE) for already-open dashboards — any
77			// authenticated party; the hub targets events by role. Mounted here
78			// (cross-cutting, not owned by one domain module).
79			api.With(middleware.Authenticate(d.JWT), middleware.RequireSession).
80				Get("/events/stream", sse.StreamHandler(d.SSE))
81	
82			RegisterModules(api, d)
83		})
84	
85		return r
86	}
87

19	// RegisterModules mounts every domain module under /api/v1.

22	//
23	//	func Register(r chi.Router, d *deps.Deps)
24	//
25	// and mounts its own subtree with its own auth/RBAC middleware. Modules are
26	// the future microservice seams — they may import domain and platform
27	// packages, but NEVER each other; cross-module reactions go through the
28	// event bus.
29	func RegisterModules(api chi.Router, d *deps.Deps) {
30		// publictrace first — it mounts /public without auth.

20	
21	// initiateRefsCap bounds how many invoice refs the settlement.initiated
22	// ledger event carries (per module spec: cap 300).
23	const initiateRefsCap = 300
24	
25	// service holds all settlement business logic: the §8.1/§18-B payment
26	// guardrail (compute+initiate → dual-control approve → licensed-PA execute)
27	// and the strictly separate DBT subsidy rail (§13).
28	type service struct {
29		repo   *repo
30		ledger *provenance.Ledger
31		orgs   *orgscope.Resolver
32		bus    *eventbus.Bus
33		log    *slog.Logger
34	}
35	
36	// actorObjectID parses the actor's party identity. JWT claims carry ObjectIDs
37	// as hex strings (tokens are JSON); every service method that compares or
38	// stores the actor's identity goes through this one helper.
39	func actorObjectID(actor auth.Actor) (primitive.ObjectID, error) {
40		return httpx.ParseID(actor.PartyID, "actor")
41	}
42	
43	// ---- pure guardrail checks (unit-tested without a database) ----
44	
45	// validateApproval enforces the dual-control guardrail (§8.1/§18-B): the
46	// approving party MUST differ from the initiator — checked FIRST and on the
47	// party identity itself, so not even SUPER_ADMIN's role bypass can approve a
48	// batch it initiated. Then the batch must still be awaiting approval.
49	func validateApproval(b domain.SettlementBatch, approverPartyID primitive.ObjectID) error {
50		if b.InitiatedBy == approverPartyID {
51			return httpx.Forbidden("dual-control violation: the settlement initiator cannot approve their own batch (§8.1/§18-B)").
52				WithDetails(map[string]string{"reason": "DUAL_CONTROL_VIOLATION"})
53		}
54		if b.Status != domain.SettlementStatusPendingApproval {
55			return httpx.Conflict("INVALID_STATUS", "settlement batch is "+b.Status+", expected "+domain.SettlementStatusPendingApproval)
56		}
57		return nil
58	}
59	
60	// executionLease is how long an APPROVED→EXECUTING claim is considered live.
61	// A batch stuck EXECUTING longer than this (crashed executor) may be resumed —
62	// the per-invoice payout logic is idempotent, so a replay is safe.
63	const executionLease = 2 * time.Minute
64	
65	// validateExecution gates which states may (re-)enter execution:
66	//   - APPROVED:  the normal dual-controlled first run.
67	//   - EXECUTING: resume of an interrupted run (the lease check in
68	//     claimExecution prevents stealing a live executor's batch).
69	//   - FAILED:    re-execution after a recorded mid-run failure.
70	//
71	// Anything pre-approval is a guardrail breach, not a race; EXECUTED/REJECTED
72	// are terminal.
73	func validateExecution(b domain.SettlementBatch) error {
74		switch b.Status {
75		case domain.SettlementStatusApproved, domain.SettlementStatusExecuting, domain.SettlementStatusFailed:
76			return nil
77		default:
78			return httpx.Conflict("INVALID_STATUS", "settlement batch is "+b.Status+", must be "+domain.SettlementStatusApproved+" before execution")
79		}
80	}
81	
82	// mockUTR builds a mock bank transaction reference: "UTRMOCK" + 12 hex chars.

85	}

90	}
91	
92	// mockPFMSRef builds a mock PFMS acknowledgement reference (§13).
93	func mockPFMSRef() string {
94		return "PFMS-MOCK-" + uuid.NewString()[:8]
95	}

97	// ---- settlement lifecycle ----
98	
99	// Initiate collects a DCS day's ISSUED invoices into a new settlement batch
100	// and parks it PENDING_APPROVAL. The INITIATED status is momentary by design
101	// (§8.1): computation and initiation are one Saathi action; nothing proceeds
102	// until a different human approves.
103	func (s *service) Initiate(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, in InitiateSettlementRequest) (*domain.SettlementBatch, error) {
104		actorID, err := actorObjectID(actor)
105		if err != nil {
106			return nil, err
107		}
108		if in.DCSID.IsZero() {
109			return nil, httpx.BadRequest("MISSING_FIELD", "dcs_id is required")
110		}
111		now := time.Now().UTC()
112		date := in.Date
113		if date == "" {
114			date = domain.DateKeyIST(now)
115		} else if _, err := time.Parse("2006-01-02", date); err != nil {
116			return nil, httpx.BadRequest("INVALID_DATE", "date must be YYYY-MM-DD")
117		}
118		if err := s.orgs.RequireInScope(ctx, actor, in.DCSID); err != nil {
119			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "settlement initiation denied: out of scope",
120				slog.String("dcs_id", in.DCSID.Hex()),
121				slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID))
122			return nil, err
123		}
124	
125		candidates, err := s.repo.issuedInvoices(ctx, in.DCSID, date)
126		if err != nil {
127			s.log.ErrorContext(ctx, "settlement initiation: load issued invoices",
128				slog.String("dcs_id", in.DCSID.Hex()), slog.String("date", date), slog.Any("err", err))
129			return nil, err
130		}
131		if len(candidates) == 0 {
132			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "settlement initiation rejected: no ISSUED invoices",
133				slog.String("dcs_id", in.DCSID.Hex()), slog.String("date", date),
134				slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID))
135			return nil, httpx.Unprocessable("NO_INVOICES", "no ISSUED invoices for DCS "+in.DCSID.Hex()+" on "+date)
136		}
137	
138		// Claim optimistically: the status guard on the update means each invoice
139		// lands in exactly one batch even under concurrent initiations. The batch
140		// ID is pre-generated so claim, insert and ledger all share one identity.
141		batchID := primitive.NewObjectID()
142		ids := make([]primitive.ObjectID, 0, len(candidates))
143		for _, inv := range candidates {
144			ids = append(ids, inv.ID)
145		}
146		if _, err := s.repo.claimInvoices(ctx, ids, batchID); err != nil {
147			s.log.ErrorContext(ctx, "settlement initiation: claim invoices",
148				slog.String("batch_id", batchID.Hex()), slog.Any("err", err))
149			return nil, err
150		}
151		claimed, err := s.repo.invoicesByBatch(ctx, batchID)
152		if err != nil {
153			s.log.ErrorContext(ctx, "settlement initiation: read claimed invoices",
154				slog.String("batch_id", batchID.Hex()), slog.Any("err", err))
155			return nil, err
156		}
157		if len(claimed) == 0 {
158			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "settlement initiation rejected: invoices claimed by concurrent batch",
159				slog.String("dcs_id", in.DCSID.Hex()), slog.String("date", date),
160				slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID))
161			return nil, httpx.Unprocessable("NO_INVOICES", "invoices were claimed by a concurrent settlement for DCS "+in.DCSID.Hex()+" on "+date)
162		}
163	
164		batch := &domain.SettlementBatch{
165			ID:          batchID,
166			DCSID:       in.DCSID,
167			Date:        date,
168			Status:      domain.SettlementStatusPendingApproval, // INITIATED → PENDING_APPROVAL immediately
169			InitiatedBy: actorID,
170			CreatedAt:   now,
171		}
172		for _, inv := range claimed {
173			batch.InvoiceIDs = append(batch.InvoiceIDs, inv.ID)
174			batch.TotalAmount += inv.TotalAmount
175		}
176		if err := s.repo.insertBatch(ctx, batch); err != nil {
177			s.log.ErrorContext(ctx, "settlement initiation: insert batch",
178				slog.String("batch_id", batchID.Hex()), slog.Any("err", err))
179			// Best-effort release so the claimed invoices are not stranded.
180			if relErr := s.repo.releaseInvoices(ctx, batchID); relErr != nil {
181				s.log.ErrorContext(ctx, "settlement: release after failed insert",
182					slog.String("batch_id", batchID.Hex()), slog.Any("err", relErr))
183			}
184			return nil, err
185		}
186	
187		refs := make([]provenance.Ref, 0, min(len(claimed), initiateRefsCap))
188		for i, inv := range claimed {
189			if i >= initiateRefsCap {
190				break
191			}
192			refs = append(refs, provenance.Ref{EntityType: domain.EntityInvoice, EntityID: inv.ID.Hex(), Relation: "settles"})
193		}
194		ev, err := s.ledger.Append(ctx, provenance.AppendInput{
195			Type:       domain.EventSettlementInitiated,
196			EntityType: domain.EntitySettlement,
197			EntityID:   batch.ID.Hex(),
198			Refs:       refs,
199			Actor:      provenance.ActorRef{PartyID: actor.PartyID, RoleCode: actor.RoleCode},
200			OrgUnitID:  batch.DCSID.Hex(),
201			Payload: map[string]any{
202				"dcs_id":        batch.DCSID.Hex(),
203				"date":          batch.Date,
204				"invoice_count": len(claimed),
205				"total_amount":  batch.TotalAmount,
206			},
207		})
208		if err != nil {
209			s.log.ErrorContext(ctx, "settlement initiation: ledger append",
210				slog.String("batch_id", batch.ID.Hex()), slog.Any("err", err))
211			return nil, httpx.Internal(err)
212		}
213		if err := s.repo.setBatchProvenanceSeq(ctx, batch.ID, ev.Seq); err != nil {
214			s.log.ErrorContext(ctx, "settlement initiation: stamp provenance seq",
215				slog.String("batch_id", batch.ID.Hex()), slog.Any("err", err))
216			return nil, err
217		}
218		batch.ProvenanceSeq = ev.Seq
219	
220		s.log.InfoContext(ctx, "settlement batch initiated",
221			slog.String("batch_id", batch.ID.Hex()),
222			slog.String("dcs_id", batch.DCSID.Hex()),
223			slog.String("date", batch.Date),
224			slog.Int("invoice_count", len(claimed)),
225			slog.Float64("total_amount", batch.TotalAmount),
226			slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID))
227		return batch, nil
228	}
229	
230	// Approve applies the human dual-control sign-off: PENDING_APPROVAL→APPROVED.
231	func (s *service) Approve(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, batchID primitive.ObjectID) (*domain.SettlementBatch, error) {
232		actorID, err := actorObjectID(actor)
233		if err != nil {
234			return nil, err
235		}
236		batch, err := s.repo.batchByID(ctx, batchID)
237		if err != nil {
238			return nil, err
239		}
240		if err := s.orgs.RequireInScope(ctx, actor, batch.DCSID); err != nil {
241			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "settlement approval denied: out of scope",
242				slog.String("batch_id", batch.ID.Hex()),
243				slog.String("dcs_id", batch.DCSID.Hex()),
244				slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID))
245			return nil, err
246		}
247		if err := validateApproval(*batch, actorID); err != nil {
248			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "settlement approval rejected",
249				slog.String("batch_id", batch.ID.Hex()),
250				slog.String("status", batch.Status),
251				slog.String("initiated_by", batch.InitiatedBy.Hex()),
252				slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID),
253				slog.String("reason", err.Error()))
254			return nil, err
255		}
256	
257		now := time.Now().UTC()
258		ok, err := s.repo.transitionBatch(ctx, batch.ID, domain.SettlementStatusPendingApproval, bson.D{
259			{Key: "status", Value: domain.SettlementStatusApproved},
260			{Key: "approved_by", Value: actorID},
261			{Key: "approved_at", Value: now},
262		})
263		if err != nil {
264			s.log.ErrorContext(ctx, "settlement approval: transition batch",
265				slog.String("batch_id", batch.ID.Hex()), slog.Any("err", err))
266			return nil, err
267		}
268		if !ok {
269			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "settlement approval rejected: batch left PENDING_APPROVAL concurrently",
270				slog.String("batch_id", batch.ID.Hex()),
271				slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID))
272			return nil, httpx.Conflict("INVALID_STATUS", "settlement batch already left "+domain.SettlementStatusPendingApproval)
273		}
274		batch.Status = domain.SettlementStatusApproved
275		batch.ApprovedBy = &actorID
276		batch.ApprovedAt = &now
277	
278		ev, err := s.ledger.Append(ctx, provenance.AppendInput{
279			Type:       domain.EventSettlementApproved,
280			EntityType: domain.EntitySettlement,
281			EntityID:   batch.ID.Hex(),
282			Actor:      provenance.ActorRef{PartyID: actor.PartyID, RoleCode: actor.RoleCode},
283			OrgUnitID:  batch.DCSID.Hex(),
284			Payload: map[string]any{
285				"approved_by":  actor.PartyID,
286				"total_amount": batch.TotalAmount,
287			},
288		})
289		if err != nil {
290			s.log.ErrorContext(ctx, "settlement approval: ledger append",
291				slog.String("batch_id", batch.ID.Hex()), slog.Any("err", err))
292			return nil, httpx.Internal(err)
293		}
294		if err := s.repo.setBatchProvenanceSeq(ctx, batch.ID, ev.Seq); err != nil {
295			s.log.ErrorContext(ctx, "settlement approval: stamp provenance seq",
296				slog.String("batch_id", batch.ID.Hex()), slog.Any("err", err))
297			return nil, err
298		}
299		batch.ProvenanceSeq = ev.Seq
300	
301		s.log.InfoContext(ctx, "settlement batch approved",
302			slog.String("batch_id", batch.ID.Hex()),
303			slog.String("dcs_id", batch.DCSID.Hex()),
304			slog.Float64("total_amount", batch.TotalAmount),
305			slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID))
306		return batch, nil
307	}
308	
309	// Reject declines a pending batch and returns its invoices to ISSUED so they
310	// can be re-settled.
311	func (s *service) Reject(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, batchID primitive.ObjectID, reason string) (*domain.SettlementBatch, error) {
312		actorID, err := actorObjectID(actor)
313		if err != nil {
314			return nil, err
315		}
316		if strings.TrimSpace(reason) == "" {
317			return nil, httpx.BadRequest("MISSING_FIELD", "reason is required")
318		}
319		batch, err := s.repo.batchByID(ctx, batchID)
320		if err != nil {
321			return nil, err
322		}
323		if err := s.orgs.RequireInScope(ctx, actor, batch.DCSID); err != nil {
324			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "settlement rejection denied: out of scope",
325				slog.String("batch_id", batch.ID.Hex()),
326				slog.String("dcs_id", batch.DCSID.Hex()),
327				slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID))
328			return nil, err
329		}
330		if batch.Status != domain.SettlementStatusPendingApproval {
331			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "settlement rejection refused: invalid status",
332				slog.String("batch_id", batch.ID.Hex()),
333				slog.String("status", batch.Status),
334				slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID))
335			return nil, httpx.Conflict("INVALID_STATUS", "settlement batch is "+batch.Status+", expected "+domain.SettlementStatusPendingApproval)
336		}
337	
338		ok, err := s.repo.transitionBatch(ctx, batch.ID, domain.SettlementStatusPendingApproval, bson.D{
339			{Key: "status", Value: domain.SettlementStatusRejected},
340			{Key: "rejected_by", Value: actorID},
341			{Key: "reject_reason", Value: reason},
342		})
343		if err != nil {
344			s.log.ErrorContext(ctx, "settlement rejection: transition batch",
345				slog.String("batch_id", batch.ID.Hex()), slog.Any("err", err))
346			return nil, err
347		}
348		if !ok {
349			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "settlement rejection refused: batch left PENDING_APPROVAL concurrently",
350				slog.String("batch_id", batch.ID.Hex()),
351				slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID))
352			return nil, httpx.Conflict("INVALID_STATUS", "settlement batch already left "+domain.SettlementStatusPendingApproval)
353		}
354		if err := s.repo.releaseInvoices(ctx, batch.ID); err != nil {
355			s.log.ErrorContext(ctx, "settlement rejection: release invoices",
356				slog.String("batch_id", batch.ID.Hex()), slog.Any("err", err))
357			return nil, err
358		}
359		batch.Status = domain.SettlementStatusRejected
360		batch.RejectedBy = &actorID
361		batch.RejectReason = reason
362	
363		s.log.InfoContext(ctx, "settlement batch rejected",
364			slog.String("batch_id", batch.ID.Hex()),
365			slog.String("dcs_id", batch.DCSID.Hex()),
366			slog.String("reason", reason),
367			slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID))
368		return batch, nil
369	}
370	
371	// Execute hands the APPROVED batch to the payment-aggregator adapter and
372	// records the resulting payouts.
373	//
374	// MOCK LICENSED-PA ADAPTER — this is a stand-in for the real integration.
375	// In production (§18-B) execution goes through an RBI-licensed Payment
376	// Aggregator operating a nodal/escrow account: Saathi submits the payout
377	// file, the PA moves the money, and UTRs come back asynchronously via
378	// webhook. Saathi itself never touches funds. The mock credits every payout
379	// instantly with a synthetic UTR so the downstream flow (invoice→PAID,
380	// provenance, farmer SMS) is exercised end to end.
381	func (s *service) Execute(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, batchID primitive.ObjectID) (*SettlementDetail, error) {
382		batch, err := s.repo.batchByID(ctx, batchID)
383		if err != nil {
384			return nil, err
385		}
386		if err := s.orgs.RequireInScope(ctx, actor, batch.DCSID); err != nil {
387			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "settlement execution denied: out of scope",
388				slog.String("batch_id", batch.ID.Hex()),
389				slog.String("dcs_id", batch.DCSID.Hex()),
390				slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID))
391			return nil, err
392		}
393		if err := validateExecution(*batch); err != nil {
394			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "settlement execution refused: invalid status",
395				slog.String("batch_id", batch.ID.Hex()),
396				slog.String("status", batch.Status),
397				slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID))
398			return nil, err
399		}
400	
401		// Guarded claim: first run (APPROVED), re-run after FAILED, or resume of
402		// a stale EXECUTING lease. The per-invoice work below is idempotent
403		// (unique payout-per-invoice index + payout reuse), so replays are safe.
404		now := time.Now().UTC()
405		claimed, err := s.repo.claimExecution(ctx, batch.ID, now, now.Add(-executionLease))
406		if err != nil {
407			s.log.ErrorContext(ctx, "settlement execution: claim",
408				slog.String("batch_id", batch.ID.Hex()), slog.Any("err", err))
409			return nil, err
410		}
411		if !claimed {
412			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "settlement execution refused: live execution lease held elsewhere",
413				slog.String("batch_id", batch.ID.Hex()),
414				slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID))
415			return nil, httpx.Conflict("INVALID_STATUS", "settlement batch is already being executed")
416		}
417	
418		// From here on, any error must not strand the batch in EXECUTING forever:
419		// flip it to FAILED (best-effort) so a retry can claim FAILED→EXECUTING.
420		failExecution := func(cause error) error {
421			s.log.ErrorContext(ctx, "settlement execution failed mid-run",
422				slog.String("batch_id", batch.ID.Hex()), slog.Any("err", cause))
423			if ferr := s.repo.markExecutionFailed(ctx, batch.ID, cause.Error()); ferr != nil {
424				s.log.ErrorContext(ctx, "settlement: mark execution failed",
425					slog.String("batch_id", batch.ID.Hex()), slog.Any("err", ferr))
426			}
427			return cause
428		}
429	
430		invoices, err := s.repo.invoicesByBatch(ctx, batch.ID)
431		if err != nil {
432			return nil, failExecution(err)
433		}
434	
435		payouts := make([]domain.PayoutInstruction, 0, len(invoices))
436		for _, inv := range invoices {
437			masked, err := s.repo.latestBankMasked(ctx, inv.FarmerPartyID)
438			if err != nil {
439				return nil, failExecution(err)
440			}
441			creditedAt := now
442			payout := &domain.PayoutInstruction{
443				ID:                primitive.NewObjectID(),
444				SettlementBatchID: batch.ID,
445				InvoiceID:         inv.ID,
446				FarmerPartyID:     inv.FarmerPartyID,
447				Amount:            inv.TotalAmount,
448				BankAccountMasked: masked,
449				UTR:               mockUTR(),
450				Status:            domain.PayoutStatusSuccess,
451				CreditedAt:        &creditedAt,
452				CreatedAt:         now,
453			}
454			exists, err := s.repo.insertPayout(ctx, payout)
455			if err != nil {
456				return nil, failExecution(err)
457			}
458			if exists {
459				// Retry of an interrupted run — reuse the payout already credited.
460				s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "settlement execution: payout already credited, reusing (idempotent replay)",
461					slog.String("batch_id", batch.ID.Hex()),
462					slog.String("invoice_id", inv.ID.Hex()))
463				existing, err := s.repo.payoutByInvoice(ctx, inv.ID)
464				if err != nil {
465					return nil, failExecution(err)
466				}
467				payout = existing
468			}
469			payouts = append(payouts, *payout)
470		}
471	
472		if err := s.repo.markInvoicesPaid(ctx, batch.ID); err != nil {
473			return nil, failExecution(err)
474		}
475	
476		paRef := mockPARef()
477		ok, err := s.repo.transitionBatch(ctx, batch.ID, domain.SettlementStatusExecuting, bson.D{
478			{Key: "status", Value: domain.SettlementStatusExecuted},
479			{Key: "pa_ref", Value: paRef},
480			{Key: "executed_at", Value: now},
481		})
482		if err != nil {
483			s.log.ErrorContext(ctx, "settlement execution: transition to EXECUTED",
484				slog.String("batch_id", batch.ID.Hex()), slog.Any("err", err))
485			return nil, err
486		}
487		if !ok {
488			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "settlement execution: batch left EXECUTING unexpectedly",
489				slog.String("batch_id", batch.ID.Hex()))
490			return nil, httpx.Conflict("INVALID_STATUS", "settlement batch left EXECUTING unexpectedly")
491		}
492		batch.Status = domain.SettlementStatusExecuted
493		batch.PARef = paRef
494		batch.ExecutedAt = &now
495	
496		ev, err := s.ledger.Append(ctx, provenance.AppendInput{
497			Type:       domain.EventSettlementExecuted,
498			EntityType: domain.EntitySettlement,
499			EntityID:   batch.ID.Hex(),
500			Actor:      provenance.ActorRef{PartyID: actor.PartyID, RoleCode: actor.RoleCode},
501			OrgUnitID:  batch.DCSID.Hex(),
502			Payload: map[string]any{
503				"pa_ref":       paRef,
504				"payout_count": len(payouts),
505				"total_amount": batch.TotalAmount,
506			},
507		})
508		if err != nil {
509			s.log.ErrorContext(ctx, "settlement execution: ledger append",
510				slog.String("batch_id", batch.ID.Hex()), slog.Any("err", err))
511			return nil, httpx.Internal(err)
512		}
513		if err := s.repo.setBatchProvenanceSeq(ctx, batch.ID, ev.Seq); err != nil {
514			s.log.ErrorContext(ctx, "settlement execution: stamp provenance seq",
515				slog.String("batch_id", batch.ID.Hex()), slog.Any("err", err))
516			return nil, err
517		}
518		batch.ProvenanceSeq = ev.Seq
519	
520		s.log.InfoContext(ctx, "settlement batch executed",
521			slog.String("batch_id", batch.ID.Hex()),
522			slog.String("dcs_id", batch.DCSID.Hex()),
523			slog.String("pa_ref", paRef),
524			slog.Int("payout_count", len(payouts)),
525			slog.Float64("total_amount", batch.TotalAmount),
526			slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID))
527	
528		// One payout.credited ledger event per invoice, then the SMS fan-out.
529		// Per-payout ledger/lookup failures are logged, not fatal: the money
530		// outcome is already anchored by settlement.executed above.
531		for _, p := range payouts {
532			if _, err := s.ledger.Append(ctx, provenance.AppendInput{
533				Type:       domain.EventPayoutCredited,
534				EntityType: domain.EntityInvoice,
535				EntityID:   p.InvoiceID.Hex(),
536				Refs: []provenance.Ref{
537					{EntityType: domain.EntitySettlement, EntityID: batch.ID.Hex(), Relation: "paid_by"},
538				},
539				Actor:     provenance.ActorRef{PartyID: actor.PartyID, RoleCode: actor.RoleCode},
540				OrgUnitID: batch.DCSID.Hex(),
541				Payload:   map[string]any{"utr": p.UTR, "amount": p.Amount},
542			}); err != nil {
543				s.log.ErrorContext(ctx, "settlement: payout.credited ledger append",
544					slog.String("invoice_id", p.InvoiceID.Hex()), slog.Any("err", err))
545			}
546	
547			phone, err := s.repo.partyPhone(ctx, p.FarmerPartyID)
548			if err != nil {
549				s.log.ErrorContext(ctx, "settlement: farmer phone lookup for payout SMS",
550					slog.String("farmer_party_id", p.FarmerPartyID.Hex()), slog.Any("err", err))
551				continue
552			}
553			s.bus.Publish(eventbus.TopicPayoutCredited, PayoutCreditedEvent{
554				FarmerPartyID: p.FarmerPartyID.Hex(),
555				Phone:         phone,
556				Amount:        p.Amount,
557				UTR:           p.UTR,
558			})
559		}
560	
561		return &SettlementDetail{Batch: *batch, Payouts: payouts}, nil
562	}
563	
564	// List pages settlement batches. Callers with a DCS-scoped token default to
565	// their own DCS; wider roles must name a dcs_id (SUPER_ADMIN and
566	// STATE_AUDITOR may list unscoped).
567	func (s *service) List(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, dcsID, date, status string, page httpx.Page) ([]domain.SettlementBatch, int64, error) {
568		if dcsID == "" {
569			switch {
570			case actor.OrgType == domain.OrgTypeDCS:
571				dcsID = actor.OrgUnitID
572			case actor.RoleCode == domain.RoleSuperAdmin || actor.RoleCode == domain.RoleStateAuditor:
573				// federation-wide read roles may list across DCSes
574			default:
575				return nil, 0, httpx.BadRequest("MISSING_FIELD", "dcs_id is required for your scope")
576			}
577		}
578		filter := bson.D{}
579		if dcsID != "" {
580			dcsOID, err := httpx.ParseID(dcsID, "dcs_id")
581			if err != nil {
582				return nil, 0, err
583			}
584			if err := s.orgs.RequireInScope(ctx, actor, dcsOID); err != nil {
585				s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "settlement list denied: out of scope",
586					slog.String("dcs_id", dcsOID.Hex()),
587					slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID))
588				return nil, 0, err
589			}
590			filter = append(filter, bson.E{Key: "dcs_id", Value: dcsOID})
591		}
592		if date != "" {
593			filter = append(filter, bson.E{Key: "date", Value: date})
594		}
595		if status != "" {
596			filter = append(filter, bson.E{Key: "status", Value: status})
597		}
598		return s.repo.listBatches(ctx, filter, page)
599	}
600	
601	// Detail returns one batch plus its payout instructions.
602	func (s *service) Detail(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, batchID primitive.ObjectID) (*SettlementDetail, error) {
603		batch, err := s.repo.batchByID(ctx, batchID)
604		if err != nil {
605			return nil, err
606		}
607		if err := s.orgs.RequireInScope(ctx, actor, batch.DCSID); err != nil {
608			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "settlement detail denied: out of scope",
609				slog.String("batch_id", batch.ID.Hex()),
610				slog.String("dcs_id", batch.DCSID.Hex()),
611				slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID))
612			return nil, err
613		}
614		payouts, err := s.repo.payoutsByBatch(ctx, batch.ID)
615		if err != nil {
616			return nil, err
617		}
618		return &SettlementDetail{Batch: *batch, Payouts: payouts}, nil
619	}

621	// PayoutHistory pages payout instructions for one farmer, newest first.
622	// A FARMER token is always forced to its own party — "my payment history".
623	// Staff roles are bound to their org scope: the target farmer must hold an
624	// ACTIVE FARMER assignment at a DCS inside the caller's scope, so a village
625	// Sacheev cannot enumerate the financials of farmers nationwide.
626	func (s *service) PayoutHistory(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, farmerPartyID string, page httpx.Page) ([]domain.PayoutInstruction, int64, error) {
627		if actor.RoleCode == domain.RoleFarmer {
628			farmerPartyID = actor.PartyID
629		}
630		if farmerPartyID == "" {
631			return nil, 0, httpx.BadRequest("MISSING_FIELD", "farmer_party_id is required")
632		}
633		farmerOID, err := httpx.ParseID(farmerPartyID, "farmer_party_id")
634		if err != nil {
635			return nil, 0, err
636		}
637		if actor.RoleCode != domain.RoleFarmer &&
638			actor.RoleCode != domain.RoleSuperAdmin && actor.RoleCode != domain.RoleStateAuditor {
639			dcsIDs, err := s.repo.farmerDCSIDs(ctx, farmerOID)
640			if err != nil {
641				return nil, 0, err
642			}
643			inScope := false
644			for _, dcsID := range dcsIDs {
645				if err := s.orgs.RequireInScope(ctx, actor, dcsID); err == nil {
646					inScope = true
647					break
648				}
649			}
650			if !inScope {
651				s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "payout history denied: farmer out of scope",
652					slog.String("farmer_party_id", farmerOID.Hex()),
653					slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID))
654				return nil, 0, httpx.Forbidden("farmer is outside your organisational scope")
655			}
656		}
657		return s.repo.payoutsByFarmer(ctx, farmerOID, page)
658	}
659	
660	// ---- DBT subsidy rail (§13) — strictly separate from milk payments ----
661	
662	// CreateDBT submits a scheme subsidy request to the (mocked) PFMS rail.
663	// Saathi only tracks the request; the subsidy is disbursed by PFMS/DBT,
664	// never by Saathi and never through the milk-payment rail.
665	func (s *service) CreateDBT(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, in CreateDBTRequestInput) (*domain.DBTRequest, error) {
666		actorID, err := actorObjectID(actor)
667		if err != nil {
668			return nil, err
669		}
670		if in.SchemeCode == "" || in.FarmerPartyID.IsZero() {
671			return nil, httpx.BadRequest("MISSING_FIELD", "scheme_code and farmer_party_id are required")
672		}
673		if in.Amount <= 0 {
674			return nil, httpx.BadRequest("INVALID_AMOUNT", "amount must be positive")
675		}
676		if _, err := s.repo.partyPhone(ctx, in.FarmerPartyID); err != nil {
677			return nil, err // farmer must exist
678		}
679	
680		// MOCK PFMS — real integration files the beneficiary+amount with PFMS
681		// and receives an acknowledgement reference (§13).
682		req := &domain.DBTRequest{
683			ID:            primitive.NewObjectID(),
684			SchemeCode:    in.SchemeCode,
685			FarmerPartyID: in.FarmerPartyID,
686			Amount:        in.Amount,
687			PFMSRef:       mockPFMSRef(),
688			Status:        domain.DBTStatusSubmitted,
689			SubmittedBy:   actorID,
690			CreatedAt:     time.Now().UTC(),
691		}
692		if err := s.repo.insertDBT(ctx, req); err != nil {
693			s.log.ErrorContext(ctx, "dbt request insert",
694				slog.String("farmer_party_id", in.FarmerPartyID.Hex()),
695				slog.String("scheme_code", in.SchemeCode), slog.Any("err", err))
696			return nil, err
697		}
698	
699		s.log.InfoContext(ctx, "dbt request submitted",
700			slog.String("dbt_request_id", req.ID.Hex()),
701			slog.String("scheme_code", req.SchemeCode),
702			slog.String("farmer_party_id", req.FarmerPartyID.Hex()),
703			slog.Float64("amount", req.Amount),
704			slog.String("pfms_ref", req.PFMSRef),
705			slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID))
706		return req, nil
707	}
708	
709	// UpdateDBTStatus records the DBT rail's progress for a request. CREDITED
710	// stamps credited_at; CREDITED/REJECTED are terminal.
711	func (s *service) UpdateDBTStatus(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, id primitive.ObjectID, status string) (*domain.DBTRequest, error) {
712		switch status {
713		case domain.DBTStatusAccepted, domain.DBTStatusCredited, domain.DBTStatusRejected:
714		default:
715			return nil, httpx.BadRequest("INVALID_STATUS", "status must be one of ACCEPTED, CREDITED, REJECTED")
716		}
717		req, err := s.repo.dbtByID(ctx, id)
718		if err != nil {
719			return nil, err
720		}
721		if req.Status == domain.DBTStatusCredited || req.Status == domain.DBTStatusRejected {
722			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "dbt status update refused: terminal status",
723				slog.String("dbt_request_id", req.ID.Hex()),
724				slog.String("status", req.Status),
725				slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID))
726			return nil, httpx.Conflict("TERMINAL_STATUS", "dbt request is already "+req.Status)
727		}
728	
729		var creditedAt *time.Time
730		if status == domain.DBTStatusCredited {
731			now := time.Now().UTC()
732			creditedAt = &now
733		}
734		ok, err := s.repo.transitionDBT(ctx, req.ID, req.Status, status, creditedAt)
735		if err != nil {
736			s.log.ErrorContext(ctx, "dbt status transition",
737				slog.String("dbt_request_id", req.ID.Hex()), slog.Any("err", err))
738			return nil, err
739		}
740		if !ok {
741			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "dbt status update refused: concurrent change",
742				slog.String("dbt_request_id", req.ID.Hex()),
743				slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID))
744			return nil, httpx.Conflict("INVALID_STATUS", "dbt request changed concurrently, retry")
745		}
746		fromStatus := req.Status
747		req.Status = status
748		req.CreditedAt = creditedAt
749	
750		s.log.InfoContext(ctx, "dbt request status updated",
751			slog.String("dbt_request_id", req.ID.Hex()),
752			slog.String("from_status", fromStatus),
753			slog.String("to_status", status),
754			slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID))
755		return req, nil
756	}
757	
758	// ListDBT pages DBT requests. A FARMER token is always forced to its own
759	// party.
760	func (s *service) ListDBT(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, farmerPartyID, status string, page httpx.Page) ([]domain.DBTRequest, int64, error) {
761		if actor.RoleCode == domain.RoleFarmer {
762			farmerPartyID = actor.PartyID
763		}
764		filter := bson.D{}
765		if farmerPartyID != "" {
766			farmerOID, err := httpx.ParseID(farmerPartyID, "farmer_party_id")
767			if err != nil {
768				return nil, 0, err
769			}
770			filter = append(filter, bson.E{Key: "farmer_party_id", Value: farmerOID})
771		}
772		if status != "" {
773			filter = append(filter, bson.E{Key: "status", Value: status})
774		}
775		return s.repo.listDBT(ctx, filter, page)
776	}

## Report: Photo / Evidence storage — Saathi Go (BE vs FE)

### 1. Does the backend already have a photo field? What is it called? Key or URL?

Yes — on **`AnalyzerReading`**, not on `MilkPour`.

- `internal/domain/collection.go:82`
  ```go
  PhotoObjectKey string `bson:"photo_object_key,omitempty" json:"photo_object_key,omitempty"` // immutable evidence in object store
  ```
- It is a **storage/object key, not a URL** — deliberately. Comments make this explicit: the domain field says "immutable evidence in object store", and `internal/platform/httpx/decode.go:13` notes "photo evidence goes to the object store, not the API."
- It's accepted on input via `CreateReadingRequest.PhotoObjectKey` (`internal/modules/collection/models.go:35`, json `photo_object_key`) on `POST /collection/readings`, and is **required when `mode == PHOTO_OCR`** (`service.go:254-255`: "photo_object_key is required for PHOTO_OCR (evidence retention, §8.2)").
- Important: **`MilkPour` has NO photo field at all.** The photo lives only on the reading; a pour links to it via the optional `AnalyzerReadingID` (`analyzer_reading_id`). Pours store fat/snf/qty/amount but no evidence pointer.

### 2. What does the FE send/expect for the analyzer photo? Does it call POST /pours/ocr-extract? Does that endpoint exist?

- The FE's photo model everywhere is a **URL**. `src/core/media/upload.ts` (`uploadImage`) does presigned-S3 upload and returns **both** `{ url, key }` (`UploadedImage`). Other flows store the URL as `photoUri` / `proofPhotoUri` (e.g. logistics `photo_uri`, onboarding `kycPhotoUri`).
- **But the pour/reading capture flow does NOT currently attach any photo.** `RecordPourInput` (`collections.ts`) has no photo field, and `recordPour` maps only fat/snf/qty/clr/source to `POST /collection/pours`. No photo bytes, URI, or key are sent.
- The FE **does call `POST /pours/ocr-extract`** (`collections.ts:321-330`, `photoOcrExtract`), used by `RecordPourSheet.tsx:85` (`ocr.mutate({ dcsId })`). Notably it sends **only `{ dcsId }` — not even a photo** — and returns `{ fatPct, snfPct, confidence }`, which the sheet uses to autofill and set `entryMethod = 'PHOTO_OCR'`.
- **This endpoint does NOT exist on the backend.** It is explicitly a mock: `// TODO(backend): no OCR endpoint yet - mock only`. There is no `/pours/ocr-extract` route (all collection routes are under `/collection/*`; note the FE path even omits the `/collection` prefix), and no OCR/vision computation anywhere in the Go code.

### 3. RECOMMENDATION on the photo field

**Keep `photo_object_key`. Do NOT rename, and do NOT add a stored `photo_link`/`photo_url` column.** Per the user's own rule ("if already done then no need to change the field name") — it's done and it's the correct model:

- Storing a stable **object key** is better than a URL: bucket/CDN/host and presigned expiry can change, but the key is immutable evidence.
- The FE already has the key it needs — `uploadImage` returns `{ url, key }`. The FE just needs to **map its uploaded `key` → `photo_object_key`** when it POSTs the reading. No backend field change required.
- The only place a URL is genuinely useful is **display** (showing the evidence photo back to a supervisor). If that's needed, add a **read-only, computed `photo_url`** on the reading *response* (a presigned GET minted from the key) — never a second persisted field. That is optional and additive, not a rename.

### 4. OCR-extract endpoint gap

Yes, there is a real gap **and a design mismatch**:

- The FE expects a **server-side** OCR endpoint (`POST /pours/ocr-extract`: photo → `{fat, snf, confidence}`). The backend has **no such endpoint** and does no OCR.
- The backend design assumes OCR happens **on-device**: the client extracts fat/snf + confidence + uploads the photo (getting a key), then POSTs a finished reading to `POST /collection/readings` with `mode=PHOTO_OCR`, `photo_object_key`, and `ocr_confidence`. The server only *flags* low confidence (`lowOCRConfidenceThreshold = 0.75`, `service.go:206`), it does not produce the numbers.

Two ways to close it:
- **Option A (matches current BE design, less work):** FE performs OCR on-device, uploads the photo → key, then calls `POST /collection/readings` (PHOTO_OCR, `photo_object_key`, `ocr_confidence`) and links the returned reading to the pour via `analyzer_reading_id`. Then `photoOcrExtract`/`/pours/ocr-extract` should be removed, not implemented.
- **Option B (matches current FE call):** BE adds a `POST /collection/pours/ocr-extract` (or `/readings/ocr-extract`) that accepts an uploaded photo or `photo_object_key` and returns `{fat_pct, snf_pct, confidence}`. This requires a server OCR/vision integration.

Either way, the FE's OCR call needs the `/collection` path prefix, and today the FE captures/sends **no photo at all** in the pour flow — that wiring (capture → `uploadImage` → key → reading) is the missing piece, independent of which OCR option is chosen.

# ONBOARDING → NOTIFICATION → VERIFICATION → APPROVAL: Verification Report

## Verdict
The relation **exists only partially**. The VERIFICATION-pending record and the APPROVAL flow are fully implemented and correct. But the **NOTIFICATION-to-reviewer on submit is missing** (only an ephemeral SSE badge nudge fires, no persisted notification), the **assisted-onboarding request entity the FE expects does not exist on the backend at all**, and **approval does not create the role assignment** the FE relation model assumes.

---

## 1. Current KYC verification relation (what actually happens)

**Submit — `POST /kyc/aadhaar` → `verifyAadhaar`** (`internal/modules/identity/service.go:486-563`)
- Creates a `KYCRecord` with `Status = PENDING` (`domain.KYCStatusPending`), `RequestedTier`, `AadhaarLast4`, opaque `AadhaarVaultRef`, and a linked `Consent`. Idempotent on an existing PENDING record for the same tier.
- **Who is notified? NOBODY.** There is *no* `insertNotification` call in `verifyAadhaar`. No notification row is queued to a reviewer or admin. (The only notification on any submit-type path is the login OTP in `requestOTP`, unrelated.)
- **SSE badge fired? YES.** `publishKYCQueueChanged("submitted", …)` (`service.go:557,568`) → `Bus.Publish(TopicKYCQueueChanged, KYCQueueEvent{…})`. The bridge in `cmd/server/main.go:107-120` subscribes and calls `sseHub.Broadcast(Event{Type:"kyc.pending.changed", Roles:[…]})`. Connected reviewer dashboards re-fetch `GET /kyc/pending/count` (`handler.go:272-286`, service `pendingKYCCount` at `service.go:742`). This is *nudge-then-recount*: ephemeral, in-process, lossy (buffer-full sends are dropped, `hub.go:119`), delivered only to dashboards open at that instant.

**Approve — `POST /kyc/{id}/approve` → `approveKYC`** (`service.go:772-869`)
- Guards, in order: record must be PENDING (else `409 KYC_NOT_PENDING`); self-review forbidden (`KYC_SELF_REVIEW`); org-scope (`requireKYCSubjectInScope`); tier authority (`CanApproveKYCTier`).
- Atomically flips PENDING→VERIFIED via `approveKYCRecord`, stamping `reviewed_by`, `reviewed_by_role`, `reviewed_at`, `verified_at` (race-safe: a lost race returns `KYC_NOT_PENDING`).
- **Party tier upgraded? YES.** `upgradedKYCTier(party.KYCTier, requestedTier)` (upgrade-only, never downgrade) → `updatePartyKYCTier`. The relation `KYCRecord.party_id → Party.kyc_tier` is wired and works.
- **Party gets KYC_APPROVED notification? YES.** Inserts `domain.Notification{TemplateKey: TemplateKYCApproved, Channel: SMS, Params:{tier}}` addressed to the **party** (`service.go:836-847`). Rendered EN/HI in `platformops/service.go:243-245`. Audited (`kyc.approve`) and `publishKYCQueueChanged("approved", …)` re-nudges.
- **Reject** (`rejectKYC`, `service.go:874-963`) is symmetric: `TemplateKYCRejected` with `reason` to the party, audited, nudge `"rejected"`.

So the chain **submit(PENDING) → [reviewer notified] → approve → party notified + tier upgraded** is intact **except** the bracketed "reviewer notified" link, which is SSE-only, not a persisted notification.

---

## 2. NOTIFICATION relation on submit — GAP (user's explicit requirement)

The user wants "**a notification + verification-pending should be created**" after onboarding. Current state:
- **Verification-pending record:** ✅ created (`KYCRecord` PENDING).
- **Notification to reviewer:** ❌ **not created.** There is only the in-memory SSE nudge. No outbox/notification row, no persistent "a verification is pending" alert. If no reviewer dashboard is live at that moment, *nothing* informs a reviewer; discovery relies entirely on a reviewer manually polling `GET /kyc/pending`.

This is the primary gap against the stated requirement. Note also the `KYCRecord` carries **no org and no intended-reviewer field** (`kycSubjectInScope` comment at `service.go:642-648` confirms "the KYC record itself carries no org"), so there is currently no addressee even if one wanted to queue a reviewer notification — the reviewer set is computed dynamically from the subject's assignments' org scope.

---

## 3. Assisted-onboarding flow the FE expects — NOT IMPLEMENTED

`parag-saathi-fe/src/core/api/endpoints/onboarding.ts` expects these endpoints (all marked `// TODO(backend)`, mock-only):
- `POST /onboarding/requests` (submit)
- `GET /onboarding/requests?submitted_by=…` (my submissions)
- `GET /onboarding/requests?status=PENDING` (reviewer queue)
- `POST /onboarding/requests/{id}/approve`
- `POST /onboarding/requests/{id}/reject`
- `GET /parties?role=SAMITI_SACHEEV` (`listSachivs`)

**Backend implements NONE of these.** Confirmed: no `OnboardingRequest` entity anywhere in `internal/` (grep returns zero), no `/onboarding` route in any module, and `/parties` (`identity/module.go:46-50`) exposes only `GET /me` and `PATCH /me` — no `?role=` listing.

**FE relation model (single-entity, proxy/assisted):** an `ONBOARDING_EXECUTIVE` submits one `OnboardingRequest` (domain.ts:625) bundling person details + requested `role` + `orgUnitId` + KYC doc/photos + role-specific fields (`cattleCount`, `cattleBreed`, `vehicleNumber`, `employeeId`, `kycNote`). It enters a PENDING queue; a `SUPER_ADMIN` approves → **atomically creates the Party + pushes a RoleAssignment** (onboarding.ts:162-188), deriving `kycTier` from `ROLES[role].kycTier`.

**Backend model (three disjoint flows, self-service):**
- `Party` is created implicitly at **OTP login** (`upsertPartyByPhone`, `verifyOTP`), not at onboarding approval.
- KYC is a **self-service submit by the subject themselves** — `verifyAadhaar` uses the *actor's own* party id (`actorID(actor)`), so there is no path for an executive to submit KYC *on behalf of* a not-yet-logged-in person.
- `RoleAssignment` is a **separate admin action** (`POST /roles/assignments`, `createAssignment`).

**What's missing to satisfy the FE:** the entire `OnboardingRequest` entity + 5 routes; the `GET /parties?role=` listing; storage for `profilePhotoUri`/`kycPhotoUri`/`documentType`/role-specific fields (only `DigiLockerDocs`/`VideoKYCRef` exist on `KYCRecord` and neither is wired to a submit path); and a proxy/assisted enrolment path (executive-enrols-another-person). The backend has no single object binding person+role+KYC+photos, and no atomic "approve → create Party + KYCRecord + RoleAssignment."

---

## 4. Super_admin's role in approval — CONFIRMED unrestricted (for KYC)

- **`CanApproveKYCTier`** (`domain/roles.go:179-196`): `KYCApprovableTiers[SUPER_ADMIN] = {MINIMAL, FARMER, STANDARD, RIDER, HIGH, HIGHEST, SERVICE}` — **every tier**. Super_admin can approve any KYC tier. (Contrast: `ORGANISING_MANAGER`/`ONBOARDING_EXECUTIVE`/`DISTRICT_VERIFIER` cap at RIDER; `PCDF_ADMIN` adds HIGH; only SUPER_ADMIN gets HIGHEST/SERVICE.)
- **Route access**: `OnboardingReviewerRoles` (`roles.go:89-91`) = `{ONBOARDING_EXECUTIVE, ORGANISING_MANAGER, DISTRICT_VERIFIER, PCDF_ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN}` gates `/kyc/pending`, `/approve`, `/reject` (`module.go:65-71`). SUPER_ADMIN is included.
- **Org scope**: `kycSubjectInScope` (`service.go:649-663`) returns `true` unconditionally for `SUPER_ADMIN` (and `STATE_AUDITOR`) → platform-wide, can approve **any** subject regardless of org.

Net: super_admin can approve **any KYC tier for any subject**. For *onboarding requests*, "who approves" is moot — no backend onboarding approval exists; the FE mock simply hardcodes `SUPER_ADMIN` as approver.

---

## 5. BUGS / GAPS (concrete)

1. **No reviewer notification on KYC submit** — `verifyAadhaar` (`service.go:486-563`) queues no `Notification`. Only an ephemeral, single-process, lossy SSE nudge (`publishKYCQueueChanged`) informs reviewers, and only those with a live dashboard. The user's "notification + verification-pending" is half-met: the PENDING record exists, the notification does not. *This is the headline gap.*

2. **SSE nudge role targeting omits `ONBOARDING_EXECUTIVE`** — `cmd/server/main.go:115-118` broadcasts to `{ORGANISING_MANAGER, DISTRICT_VERIFIER, PCDF_ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN}`, but `domain.OnboardingReviewerRoles` also includes `ONBOARDING_EXECUTIVE`. An ONBOARDING_EXECUTIVE reviewer — a first-class reviewer that *can* hit `/kyc/pending` and approve — never receives the live badge nudge; their badge only updates on manual refresh. Inconsistency between the two role lists.

3. **Assisted-onboarding request entity + endpoints entirely absent** — no `OnboardingRequest` type, no `POST/GET /onboarding/requests`, no `…/approve`, `…/reject`. FE `onboarding.ts` is 100% mock. There is no atomic "approve → create Party + KYCRecord + RoleAssignment."

4. **`GET /parties?role=` missing** — `listSachivs` (FE) has no backend; `/parties` only serves `/me`.

5. **Relation-model mismatch (proxy vs self-service)** — FE assumes one executive-submitted request that an admin approves to spawn Party+role. Backend splits this into login-time Party creation, subject-self-service KYC, and a separate admin role grant, with **no path for an executive to enrol a person who has not logged in themselves** (`verifyAadhaar` binds to the actor's own party id).

6. **APPROVAL → role relation incomplete** — `approveKYC` upgrades `Party.kyc_tier` but does **not** create any `RoleAssignment`. After KYC approval the party has the tier but still no role until a separate `POST /roles/assignments` call. The FE relation model expects approval to also produce the assignment; the backend does not.

7. **`KYCRecord` has no reviewer/org linkage at creation** — no field naming an intended reviewer/org, and no queued notification, so "who should verify this" is resolved only dynamically via the subject's assignment org-scope at list time. Reinforces gaps #1/#5.

### Minor / non-functional
- `STATE_AUDITOR` is short-circuited to "in scope for all" in `kycSubjectInScope` (`service.go:650`) but is absent from both `OnboardingReviewerRoles` and `KYCApprovableTiers`, so `RequireRoles` blocks it from ever reaching approve/reject — dead branch, not a live bug.

- Tier/role logic: `/Users/divyanshmangla/parag-saathi-be/internal/domain/roles.go` (`CanApproveKYCTier`, `OnboardingReviewerRoles`, `RequiredKYCTier`), `party.go`, `notification.go`

# COLLECTION relations — end-to-end trace (Saathi Go backend vs. Expo FE)

Core answer up front: When a sachiv collects a farmer's milk via `POST /collection/pours`, the backend creates exactly **one** business document — a `MilkPour` with a server-generated `_id` (ObjectID). It does **not** create/update an `AnalyzerReading`, and it does **not** create/update any invoice. The FE's whole "same-day DRAFT invoice, pour.lotId, assurance, rate-chart version" model is only implemented in the FE mock; the real backend does not populate most of it.

---

## 1. `POST /collection/pours` — what gets created

Handler `createPour` → `service.CreatePour` (`internal/modules/collection/service.go:355-505`). Route is gated to `SAMITI_SACHEEV` or `MILK_TESTER` (`module.go:52-53`).

**IDs generated (per successful pour):**
| ID | Where | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `MilkPour._id` (ObjectID) | `service.go:450` `primitive.NewObjectID()` | the pour document, in `milk_pours` |
| provenance `Event` (seq int64 + its own `_id`) | `recordPourProvenance` `service.go:581-593`, stamped back to `pour.provenance_seq` at `service.go:600` | `EventPourRecorded` in `provenance_events` |
| `Notification._id` (ObjectID) | `queueFarmerSMS` `service.go:1190` | farmer receipt SMS outbox, `TemplatePourReceipt` |

Plus a bus publish `TopicPourRecorded` (`service.go:555`). **No AnalyzerReading. No Invoice.**

`ClientEventID` is a device-minted **string** idempotency key (not an ObjectID), unique-indexed (`indexes.go` `milk_pours` → unique `client_event_id`). Replays return the stored pour with `idempotent_replay=true` (`service.go:382-386, 513-550`).

**Foreign-key fields set on the pour** (`MilkPour` struct `internal/domain/collection.go:122-148`; assignment `service.go:449-471`):
- `farmer_party_id` (from request)
- `animal_id` (optional `*ObjectID`, from request)
- `dcs_id` (from request)
- `rate_chart_id` = resolved active chart `chart.ID` (`service.go:463`)
- `analyzer_reading_id` (optional `*ObjectID`, **only if the client sends it** — see bug 6)
- `recorded_by` = actor party id (`service.go:468`)
- `supersedes_pour_id` — only on the `SupersedePour` correction path (`service.go:776`)
- **NOT present at all:** `lot_id` / `consignment_id`, `assurance`, `rate_chart_version`, `temperature_c` (no such fields on the struct)

Provenance refs on the pour.recorded event (`service.go:572-580`): `produced_by`→Party(farmer), `from_animal`→Animal (if `animal_id`), `measured_by`→AnalyzerReading (if `analyzer_reading_id`).

---

## 2. farmer → pour relation

The farmer is linked purely by the `farmer_party_id` ObjectID on the pour, and **is validated as an active DCS member**: `farmerIsActiveMember` (`repo.go:137-157`, called at `service.go:389`) requires a `role_assignments` row with `party_id=farmer`, `org_unit_id=dcs`, `role_code=FARMER`, `status=ACTIVE`, and `UsableAt(now)`. Failure → `422 FARMER_NOT_MEMBER` (`service.go:399`).

**Sacheev self-pour (multi-role):** fully supported and works. The actor (a `SAMITI_SACHEEV`) sets `farmer_party_id` to their own party id; the membership check keys off `farmer_party_id`'s FARMER assignment, so as long as the sachiv also holds a FARMER role at that DCS it passes. `recorded_by` ends up equal to `farmer_party_id`. There is **no anti-self-dealing guard** (no check that `recorded_by != farmer_party_id`) — this is necessary for the legitimate multi-role case, but note there is no second-person control on a sachiv recording their own milk.

---

## 3. pour → invoice relation

**The backend does NOT auto-create/update a same-day invoice on pour.** Invoices are created only by an explicit `POST /collection/invoices/generate` (`GenerateInvoices` `service.go:862-989`), gated to `SAMITI_SACHEEV` only (`module.go:65-66`). That call groups the day's RECORDED, un-invoiced pours by farmer and issues one invoice each:
- `Invoice._id` = `primitive.NewObjectID()` (`service.go:916`)
- `invoice_number` = `INV-<dcsCode>-<date>-<seq>` from an atomic per-DCS-per-day counter (`service.go:911, 917`)
- link to pours: **`pour_ids []ObjectID`** on the invoice (`service.go:925`); there is no back-pointer on the pour.
- unique index `farmer_party_id + dcs_id + invoice_date` is the true duplicate guard; late pours are merged into the existing ISSUED invoice (`mergeIntoExistingInvoice` `service.go:996-1104`).

**Lifecycle mismatch (backend vs FE §8.1):**
- Backend `Invoice` statuses (`collection.go:150-156`): `ISSUED → SETTLEMENT_PENDING → PAID`, plus `HOLD`. There is **no DRAFT and no APPROVED** on the invoice; `APPROVED` lives on the separate settlement-batch rail (`domain/settlement.go:15`).
- FE `Invoice.status` (`domain.ts:399`): `DRAFT → APPROVED → SETTLED`. The FE reconciles by collapsing (`payments.ts:79-89`): `PAID/SETTLED→SETTLED`, `APPROVED→APPROVED`, **everything else incl. `ISSUED`→`DRAFT`**. So a real backend `ISSUED` invoice surfaces in the FE as `DRAFT`, and the FE `APPROVED` state never comes from the invoice object.
- Field shape mismatch: FE `WireInvoice`/`mapInvoice` (`payments.ts:28-40, 91-105`) read `gross_amount`, `deductions`, `net_amount`; backend `Invoice` only has `total_quantity_litres` and `total_amount` (`collection.go:168-169`) — so FE `grossAmount/deductions/netAmount` are always `0` against the real backend.
- The FE mock `recordPour` builds/updates a per-farmer `DRAFT` invoice on every pour (`collections.ts:283-303`); the real backend has no equivalent — the farmer's bill does not exist server-side until a sachiv runs generate.

---

## 4. pour → consignment relation

Consignment creation: `logistics.createConsignment` (`internal/modules/logistics/service.go:74-181`). It reads the shift's RECORDED pours (`repo.findRecordedPours`, filters on `dcs_id + pour_date + shift + status=RECORDED`), aggregates them, and writes:
- `DCSConsignment._id` = `primitive.NewObjectID()` (`service.go:117`)
- **`pour_ids []ObjectID`** (forward reference), `total_quantity_litres`, `can_count`, quantity-weighted `avg_fat_pct`/`avg_snf_pct` (`service.go:118-129`)
- unique index `dcs_id + date + shift`.

**There is NO back-reference written onto the pour.** The `MilkPour` struct has no `lot_id`/`consignment_id`/`bmc_lot_id` field, and neither logistics nor collection ever updates a pour when it is consigned. The pour's `status` stays `RECORDED` (the pour status enum is only `RECORDED|SUPERSEDED|CANCELLED` — no `IN_LOT`). The "sealed shift" freeze is enforced indirectly by counting the consignments collection (`repo.shiftConsigned` `collection/repo.go:476-487`, called at `service.go:433`), not via any field on the pour.

**FE expectation broken:** `mapPour` sets `lotId: w.lot_id ?? w.consignment_id` (`collections.ts:121`). The backend sends **neither**, so `pour.lotId` is always `undefined`. FE code that keys off it — `db.pours.filter(... && !po.lotId)` and `po.lotId = lot.id` in `createLot` (`collections.ts:384, 409`), the invoice route `app/collection/invoice/[lotId].tsx`, and the `IN_LOT` pour status — has no real backend backing.

---

## 5. assurance (A|B|C) and rate_chart_version

**Neither is stored on the pour by the backend.**
- No `assurance` field anywhere in `internal/` (grep: only an unrelated "KYC assurance tiers" comment in `roles.go`). The pour stores only `source` (the reading mode). The FE reconstructs assurance at read time from `source` via `assuranceOf()` (`collections.ts:118`, `utils/assurance.ts`), so it is derivable client-side but never persisted, and — critically — the §6.2 "aggregate inherits the weakest assurance" rule is **unimplemented on the backend**: `logistics.aggregatePours` computes only litres + weighted fat/SNF (`service.go:733-747`); it never computes/stores an assurance on the consignment, and `mapConsignment` never reads one.
- No `rate_chart_version` field anywhere (grep empty). The pour pins `rate_chart_id` (the chart's ObjectID), and `RateChart` has no `version`/immutable-version field (`collection.go:31-42`). FE `mapPour` reads `w.rate_chart_version` (`collections.ts:119`) → always `undefined`. So §6.3's "pin the chart version so a later revision can't rewrite a historical amount" is only half-met: the chart doc is referenced by id, but there is no version string and it isn't surfaced under the field the FE reads.

---

## 6. Photo evidence

- `AnalyzerReading` has `PhotoObjectKey` (bson `photo_object_key`, `collection.go:82`) plus `OCRConfidence`. There is **no `photo_link`** field. `CreateReading` requires `photo_object_key` when `mode=PHOTO_OCR` (`service.go:254-256`) and the `PHOTO_OCR` feature flag must be enabled (`service.go:245-253`). This is the intended §8.2 immutable-evidence anchor.
- **But the payment-driving object is the pour, and the pour carries no photo and is never forced to reference a reading.** The FE only ever hits `POST /collection/pours` — grep confirms the FE **never** calls `POST /collection/readings`, never sends `analyzer_reading_id`, and never uploads a photo / sends `photo_object_key` (`recordPour.mapRequest` `collections.ts:224-235`). The FE `photoOcrExtract` is mock-only (`collections.ts:320` `TODO(backend): no OCR endpoint yet`). Net: a pour can be recorded with `source=PHOTO_OCR` while `analyzer_reading_id` is nil and no photo exists anywhere — the §8.2 evidence retention does not attach to the artefact that actually drives payment.

## 7. BUGS / mismatches (concrete)

1. **pour→lot back-reference missing (breaks `pour.lotId`).** `MilkPour` (`internal/domain/collection.go:122-148`) has no `lot_id`/`consignment_id`; logistics never writes one back (`internal/modules/logistics/service.go:114-181` only sets `consignment.pour_ids`). FE `mapPour` reads `w.lot_id ?? w.consignment_id` (`src/core/api/endpoints/collections.ts:121`) → always `undefined`. Downstream FE lot logic (`collections.ts:384, 409`) and the invoice-by-lot screen are unbacked.

2. **Pour status enum divergence.** Backend: `RECORDED|SUPERSEDED|CANCELLED` (`collection.go:110-114`) and status never advances when consigned/invoiced. FE `Pour.status`: `RECORDED|IN_LOT|INVOICED|PAID` (`domain.ts:159`). `IN_LOT`/`INVOICED`/`PAID` are never emitted by the backend.

3. **No same-day auto invoice on pour (FE §8.1 expectation unmet).** `CreatePour` touches no invoice; invoices exist only after an explicit sachiv-only `generate` (`service.go:862-989`). FE mock creates/updates a DRAFT invoice per pour (`collections.ts:283-303`). Farmer's "same-day bill" does not exist server-side between pour and generate.

4. **Invoice status vocabulary mismatch.** Backend `ISSUED/SETTLEMENT_PENDING/PAID/HOLD` (`collection.go:150-156`) vs FE `DRAFT/APPROVED/SETTLED` (`domain.ts:399`). FE maps `ISSUED→DRAFT` (`payments.ts:79-89`); a genuine backend `APPROVED` invoice state does not exist.

5. **Invoice amount fields mismatch.** FE reads `gross_amount/deductions/net_amount` (`payments.ts:28-40, 91-105`); backend only serialises `total_amount`/`total_quantity_litres` (`collection.go:161-174`). FE `grossAmount/netAmount/deductions` are always `0` against the real API.

6. **`assurance` not persisted and not inherited by aggregates (§6.2).** No field on `MilkPour`; `logistics.aggregatePours` (`service.go:733-747`) never derives/stores a consignment-level weakest-assurance. FE `DcsLot.assurance` (`domain.ts:178`) is never populated by `mapConsignment` (`collections.ts:128-143`).

7. **`rate_chart_version` never set (§6.3 partial).** No version field on `MilkPour` or `RateChart`; FE `rateChartVersion` (`domain.ts:158`, read at `collections.ts:119`) is always `undefined`. Only `rate_chart_id` pins pricing.

8. **OCR photo evidence never reaches the backend for pours (§8.2 gap).** FE never creates an `AnalyzerReading`, never sends `photo_object_key` or `analyzer_reading_id`, and `photoOcrExtract` is mock-only (`collections.ts:320`). A `PHOTO_OCR` pour is stored with no linked reading and no evidence photo.

9. **`temperature_c` silently dropped.** FE `recordPour` sends `temperature_c` (`collections.ts:233`) and models `Pour.temperatureC`/`clr` (`domain.ts:148`); backend `CreatePourRequest`/`MilkPour` have `clr` but **no temperature field at all** (grep empty). Milk temperature captured at collection is lost server-side.

10. **Latent `source` value mismatch.** Backend accepts `ANALYZER_DIRECT|PHOTO_OCR|MANUAL` (`service.go:365-368`); FE domain uses `ANALYZER_AUTO` and sends `source: entryMethod` raw (`collections.ts:234`). Not triggered today because `RecordPourSheet` only ever sends `PHOTO_OCR`/`MANUAL` (`RecordPourSheet.tsx:115`), but any analyzer-auto path would be rejected `422 VALIDATION`. (FE handles the reverse direction on read via `mapEntryMethod`, `collections.ts:92-102`.)

# LOGISTICS Relation Trace — Saathi Go Backend vs Frontend

## ID generation summary (where each id is minted)

| id | Where minted | Line | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `consignment_id` (`_id`/`id`) | `logistics/service.go` `createConsignment` | service.go:117 `primitive.NewObjectID()` | pre-generated before insert so ledger refs align |
| `trip_id` (`_id`/`id`) | `logistics/service.go` `createTrip` | service.go:396 | pre-generated |
| `bmc_lot_id` (`_id`/`id`) | `plant/service.go` `CreateBMCLot` | service.go:181 | pre-generated, used as consignment claim stamp |
| `batch_id` (`_id`/`id`) + `batch_number` | `plant/service.go` `CreateBatch` | service.go:471 / 464 | `batch_number = BATCH-<orgCode>-<YYYYMMDD>-<seq>`, minted at the PLANT |
| `seal_code` | **NOWHERE** | — | not modeled in backend |

All ObjectIDs serialize as 24-hex `id` in JSON.

## 1. Sachiv seals a consignment — `POST /logistics/consignments` + `.../dispatch`

**Create** (`createConsignment`, service.go:74; role `SAMITI_SACHEEV` only, module.go:30-31):
- Generates `consignment.ID` (service.go:117). No human `consignment_code`.
- **FK consignment → pours:** `PourIDs []ObjectID` → `pour_ids` (domain/logistics.go:27). Built by `aggregatePours` (service.go:733) over `findRecordedPours(dcs_id, pour_date, shift, status=RECORDED)` (repo.go:47). This is a **forward-only** reference.
- **FK consignment → dcs:** `DCSID` → `dcs_id` (domain/logistics.go:24).
- Also computes quantity-weighted `AvgFatPct`/`AvgSNFPct` → `avg_fat_pct`/`avg_snf_pct` (service.go:114, 743-745), plus `can_count`, `total_quantity_litres`. Status `OPEN`.
- Unique index on dcs+date+shift → replay returns `CONSIGNMENT_EXISTS` (service.go:135).

**Dispatch** (`dispatchConsignment`, service.go:188; `SAMITI_SACHEEV` only):
- OPEN→DISPATCHED (repo.go:95 optimistic on `status=OPEN`). **Re-aggregates** pours at the seal boundary and re-stamps `pour_ids`/litres/can_count/avg fat/snf (service.go:207-227).
- Sets `dispatched_at` (service.go:261). Emits `consignment.dispatched` ledger event.

**§6.4 check — seal_code / wavg:**
- **`seal_code`: MISSING.** No field on `DCSConsignment` (domain/logistics.go:22-39), never minted at dispatch. `pickupRequest` has no seal param (models.go:30-33), `RouteStop` has no seal field (domain/logistics.go:50-56).
- **`sealed_at`: MISSING** — only `dispatched_at` exists.
- **wavg_fat/wavg_snf: present as DATA but under different names** (`avg_fat_pct`/`avg_snf_pct`). The quantity-weighted average the Note asks for is computed, just not named `wavg_*`.
- Confirmed by the repo's own `docs/ALIGNMENT_SPEC.md:136`: `dcs_consignments seal_code, sealed_at, wavg_fat, wavg_snf → planned (P4) → §6.4 tamper seal`, and line 79 lists `RouteStop.seal_code verify (409 SEAL_MISMATCH)` as still-planned.

**Pour → consignment back-reference: MISSING.** The logistics `pours` collection is opened read-only (repo.go:25) and no module writes `lot_id`/`consignment_id`/`IN_LOT` onto pours (grep of collection module + domain came back empty; `MilkPour` statuses are only `RECORDED|SUPERSEDED|CANCELLED`, domain/collection.go:111-113). So the pour never learns it was pooled, even though FE `mapPour` reads `lot_id ?? consignment_id` and expects statuses `RECORDED|IN_LOT|INVOICED|PAID` (collections.ts:52-53, 120-121).

## 2. Van rider picks up — `POST /logistics/trips/{tripID}/stops/{consignmentID}/pickup`

**Trip creation** (`createTrip`, service.go:320; role `UNION_FIELD_SUPERVISOR` or `VAN_RIDER`, module.go:44):
- Generates `trip_id` (service.go:396). Each stop validated: consignment must be `DISPATCHED` and belong to the stop's `dcs_id` (`validateStopConsignment`, service.go:815). Stops stored as `[]RouteStop{dcs_id, consignment_id}` (domain/logistics.go:50). Status `PLANNED`.

**Pickup** (`pickupStop`, service.go:423; `VAN_RIDER` only):
- Links pickup→trip→consignment via the path `{tripID}` + `{consignmentID}`; `findStop` requires the consignment to be a stop on the trip (service.go:836-839).
- **Consignment back-reference `route_trip_id`: YES, set here.** `markConsignmentPickedUp(consignmentID, trip.ID)` does DISPATCHED→PICKED_UP **and** `$set route_trip_id = tripID` atomically (repo.go:112-118). Serializes as `route_trip_id` (domain/logistics.go:35).
- Stamps the stop `picked_up_at`, `temp_c`, `notes` (repo.go:199); trip → `IN_PROGRESS`.
- **Seal verification: NONE.** No seal is checked or matched — there is no seal to check. `pickupRequest` carries only `temp_c` + `notes` (models.go:30). No `SEAL_MISMATCH` path exists anywhere in the backend.

---

## 3. Van delivers → BMC lot

Two **separate** steps — delivery does NOT create a lot:

**a) Deliver** (`deliverTrip`, service.go:552; `VAN_RIDER` only; `POST /trips/{tripID}/deliver {bmc_id}`):
- Requires every stop picked up (`validateDeliver`, service.go:859). Trip IN_PROGRESS→DELIVERED, sets `delivered_to_bmc_id` + `delivered_at` (repo.go:226). Consignments PICKED_UP→DELIVERED in bulk (`markConsignmentsDelivered`, repo.go:127). **No BMCLot is created here**; only status flips.

**b) Pool into lot** (`plant/service.go` `CreateBMCLot`, service.go:128; role `BMC_OPERATOR`, plant/module.go:39; `POST /plant/bmc-lots`):
- Generates `bmc_lot_id` (service.go:181).
- **FK lot → consignments:** `ConsignmentIDs` → `consignment_ids` (from request, deduped; domain/processing.go:26).
- **FK lot → trips:** `RouteTripIDs` → `route_trip_ids`, derived by de-duping each pooled consignment's `route_trip_id` (service.go:199-207, domain/processing.go:27). So trip linkage flows consignment.`route_trip_id` → lot.`route_trip_ids`.
- **Consignment back-reference `bmc_lot_id`: YES.** `ClaimConsignments` atomically flips DELIVERED→ACCEPTED and `$set bmc_lot_id = lotID` (repo.go:60-75). Lost-race compensation via `ReleaseConsignments` (repo.go:79).
- Net result: a pooled consignment ends holding BOTH `route_trip_id` and `bmc_lot_id` — the full chain survives on the doc.

---

## 4. "Batch mint" (Note §6.4) vs actual chain

The Developer Note's "van mints a BATCH code binding its consignments" is **not modeled**. There is:
- No batch/`batch_code` at the trip level; the `RouteTrip` has no such field.
- The only human-readable batch number (`BATCH-<orgCode>-<date>-<seq>`) is minted at the **PLANT** by the plant operator (`CreateBatch`, plant/service.go:464), pooling **BMC lots**, not the van pooling consignments.

**Actual relation chain (as built):**
```
MilkPour (RECORDED)
  └─pour_ids──▶ DCSConsignment            (pooling boundary #1, Sacheev; dcs+date+shift)
                 status: OPEN→DISPATCHED→PICKED_UP→DELIVERED→ACCEPTED
                 ├─route_trip_id──▶ RouteTrip  (transport binding, van; NOT a "batch")
                 └─bmc_lot_id─────▶ BMCLot     (pooling #2, BMC operator)
                                      consignment_ids[], route_trip_ids[]
                                      status: OPEN→QC_PENDING→PASSED→DISPATCHED→POOLED
                                      └─batch_id──▶ ProcessingBatch  (pooling #3, plant)
                                                      bmc_lot_ids[], batch_number
                                                      └─▶ ProductLot ─▶ BatchQR
```
The van's "binding of its consignments" corresponds only to the `RouteTrip` (via `route_trip_id` + `lot.route_trip_ids`); there is no minted van-level batch code. Note ALIGNMENT_SPEC.md:80 lists "Van batch-mint code (Developer Note `BATCH`), GPS track" as still-planned (P4).

# ACCESS-CONTROL & ORG-HIERARCHY Verification — Saathi Go backend

## 1. SUPER_ADMIN access — is there a global bypass?

**Yes, two independent global bypasses, and they cover both gates:**

- **RBAC gate bypass** — `internal/platform/middleware/rbac.go:30-33`. Inside `RequireRoles(...)`, before the allow-list is consulted:
  ```go
  if actor.RoleCode == domain.RoleSuperAdmin {
      next.ServeHTTP(w, r); return
  }
  ```
  So SUPER_ADMIN passes **every** `RequireRoles(...)` gate on every route, regardless of the listed roles.

- **Org-scope bypass** — `internal/platform/orgscope/resolver.go:116-119`. `RequireInScope` returns `nil` immediately for SUPER_ADMIN (and STATE_AUDITOR):
  ```go
  if actor.RoleCode == domain.RoleSuperAdmin || actor.RoleCode == domain.RoleStateAuditor {
      return nil
  }
  ```
  I confirmed the **only** raw `Resolver.InScope(...)` call (the path-containment check with no role bypass) is *inside* `RequireInScope` itself, after this early-return (`resolver.go:127`). Every module reaches scope enforcement through `RequireInScope`/wrappers (`requireInScope`, `requireScope`, `requireSubjectScope`) — I enumerated all ~45 call sites across collection, logistics, plant, quality, settlement, cattle, orgs, identity, and none bypass the exemption. So SUPER_ADMIN passes every org-scope check everywhere.

**Does super_admin "see everything"? Effectively yes for reads, with caveats:**

- SUPER_ADMIN is seeded at the **federation root** (`cmd/seed/main.go:111`, org `federation.ID`), and its role token carries `OrgType=FEDERATION` (resolved at role-select in `identity/service.go:415` → `IssueRoleToken(..., org.Type)`). Since the federation is the ancestor of every node, even if the bypass were removed, path-containment would still make everything in-scope.

- **Endpoints where SUPER_ADMIN is NOT effectively allowed** (passes RBAC + scope but is stopped by a secondary *per-actor ownership* check — these are by design, not the org-scope system):
  - `logistics` **pickupStop / logColdChain / deliverTrip** — service calls `requireTripRider(trip, actorID)` which compares `trip.VanRiderPartyID` to the actor's own party ID (`service.go:806-811`, invoked via `validatePickup`/`validateColdChain`/`validateDeliver`). SUPER_ADMIN's party ≠ the assigned rider → `403 "this trip is assigned to another van rider"`. So SUPER_ADMIN can read any trip (`getTrip` takes the non-rider branch → `RequireInScope` passes) but cannot perform rider transitions.
  - `logistics` **createTrip** without an explicit `van_rider_party_id` → `RIDER_REQUIRED` (`service.go:358`), because SUPER_ADMIN isn't a `VAN_RIDER`. Must pass the rider id explicitly.
