```text
275		if errors.Is(err, mongo.ErrNoDocuments) {
276			return nil, httpx.NotFound("payout for invoice " + invoiceID.Hex())
277		}
278		if err != nil {
279			return nil, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("find payout by invoice: %w", err))
280		}

321	// ---- lookups in adjacent collections (read-only, per module spec) ----
322	
323	// latestBankMasked returns the masked bank account from the farmer's most
324	// recent VERIFIED KYC record carrying one, or "" when none exists. Payouts
325	// must only ever be issued against a reviewer-approved bank account, so
326	// PENDING/REJECTED (self-submitted, unreviewed) evidence is ignored.
327	func (rp *repo) latestBankMasked(ctx context.Context, partyID primitive.ObjectID) (string, error) {
328		var rec domain.KYCRecord
329		err := rp.kyc.FindOne(ctx,
330			bson.D{
331				{Key: "party_id", Value: partyID},
332				{Key: "status", Value: domain.KYCStatusVerified},
333				{Key: "bank_account_masked", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$exists", Value: true}, {Key: "$ne", Value: ""}}},
334			},
335			options.FindOne().SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "created_at", Value: -1}}),
336		).Decode(&rec)
337		if errors.Is(err, mongo.ErrNoDocuments) {
338			return "", nil
339		}
340		if err != nil {
341			return "", httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("find latest bank masked: %w", err))
342		}
343		return rec.BankAccountMasked, nil
344	}
345	
346	// farmerDCSIDs returns the org units where the party holds an ACTIVE FARMER
347	// assignment — the scope anchors for staff reads of the farmer's financials.
348	func (rp *repo) farmerDCSIDs(ctx context.Context, farmerPartyID primitive.ObjectID) ([]primitive.ObjectID, error) {
349		cur, err := rp.assignments.Find(ctx,

354			},

356		)
357		if err != nil {
358			return nil, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("find farmer DCS assignments: %w", err))
359		}
360		var docs []struct {
361			OrgUnitID primitive.ObjectID `bson:"org_unit_id"`
362		}
363		if err := cur.All(ctx, &docs); err != nil {
364			return nil, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("decode farmer DCS assignments: %w", err))
365		}
366		ids := make([]primitive.ObjectID, 0, len(docs))
367		for _, d := range docs {
368			if !d.OrgUnitID.IsZero() {
369				ids = append(ids, d.OrgUnitID)
370			}
371		}
372		return ids, nil
373	}

400		var d domain.DBTRequest
401		err := rp.dbt.FindOne(ctx, bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: id}}).Decode(&d)
402		if errors.Is(err, mongo.ErrNoDocuments) {
403			return nil, httpx.NotFound("dbt request " + id.Hex())

411	// transitionDBT performs a status-guarded DBT update; false = lost the race
412	// or the request already left fromStatus.
413	func (rp *repo) transitionDBT(ctx context.Context, id primitive.ObjectID, fromStatus, toStatus string, creditedAt *time.Time) (bool, error) {
414		set := bson.D{{Key: "status", Value: toStatus}}
415		if creditedAt != nil {
416			set = append(set, bson.E{Key: "credited_at", Value: creditedAt})
417		}
418		res, err := rp.dbt.UpdateOne(ctx,
419			bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: id}, {Key: "status", Value: fromStatus}},
420			bson.D{{Key: "$set", Value: set}},
421		)
422		if err != nil {
423			return false, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("transition dbt request: %w", err))
424		}
425		return res.MatchedCount > 0, nil
426	}
427

435			SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "created_at", Value: -1}}).
436			SetSkip(page.Offset).SetLimit(page.Limit),
437		)

443			return nil, 0, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("decode dbt requests: %w", err))
444		}
```

```text
1	// Package logistics moves sealed milk from village societies to chilling
2	// centres (blueprint §7.1): a Samiti Sacheev pools a shift's RECORDED pours
3	// into a DCS consignment and dispatches it; a van rider runs a route trip
4	// that picks consignments up stop by stop, logs cold-chain temperatures in
5	// transit, and hands the load to a BMC. Every hop is chained into the
6	// provenance ledger so the pour→QR trace survives the pooling boundary.
7	package logistics
8	
9	import (
10		"log/slog"
11	
12		"github.com/go-chi/chi/v5"
13	
14		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/domain"
15		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/deps"
16		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/middleware"
17	)
18	
19	// Register mounts the logistics routes under /logistics (the router hands us
20	// the /api/v1 subtree) and wires handler → service → repo.
21	func Register(r chi.Router, d *deps.Deps) {
22		log := d.Log.With(slog.String("module", "logistics"))
23		svc := newService(newRepo(d.DB), d.Orgs, d.Ledger, log)
24		h := &handler{svc: svc}
25	
26		r.Route("/logistics", func(r chi.Router) {
27			r.Use(middleware.Authenticate(d.JWT))
28	
29			r.Route("/consignments", func(r chi.Router) {
30				sacheevOnly := middleware.RequireRoles(domain.RoleSamitiSacheev)
31				r.With(sacheevOnly).Post("/", h.createConsignment)
32				r.With(sacheevOnly).Post("/{consignmentID}/dispatch", h.dispatchConsignment)
33				r.With(middleware.RequireRoles(
34					domain.RoleSamitiSacheev, domain.RoleSamitiAdhyaksh, domain.RoleVanRider,
35					domain.RoleUnionFieldSupervisor, domain.RoleBMCOperator,
36				)).Get("/", h.listConsignments)
37			})
38	
39			r.Route("/trips", func(r chi.Router) {
40				riderOnly := middleware.RequireRoles(domain.RoleVanRider)
41				tripReaders := middleware.RequireRoles(
42					domain.RoleVanRider, domain.RoleUnionFieldSupervisor, domain.RoleUnionPresident,
43				)
44				r.With(middleware.RequireRoles(domain.RoleUnionFieldSupervisor, domain.RoleVanRider)).
45					Post("/", h.createTrip)
46				r.With(riderOnly).Post("/{tripID}/stops/{consignmentID}/pickup", h.pickupStop)
47				r.With(riderOnly).Post("/{tripID}/cold-chain", h.logColdChain)
48				r.With(riderOnly).Post("/{tripID}/deliver", h.deliverTrip)
49				r.With(tripReaders).Get("/", h.listTrips)
50				r.With(tripReaders).Get("/{tripID}", h.getTrip)
51			})
52		})
53	}
54
```

```text
1	package logistics
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"fmt"
6		"time"
7	
8		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson"
9		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson/primitive"
10		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo"
11		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo/options"
12	
13		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/domain"
14		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/httpx"
15		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/mongodb"
16	)
17	
18	// repo owns every MongoDB access for the logistics module. It returns raw
19	// driver errors wrapped with operation context (mongo.ErrNoDocuments stays
20	// detectable via errors.Is); the service layer maps them to httpx errors.
21	// No business logic lives here.
22	type repo struct {
23		consignments *mongo.Collection
24		trips        *mongo.Collection
25		pours        *mongo.Collection // read-only view into the collection module's pours (sanctioned by spec)
26	}
27	
28	// newRepo binds the repo to its collections via the shared name constants.
29	func newRepo(db *mongo.Database) *repo {
30		return &repo{
31			consignments: db.Collection(mongodb.CollConsignments),
32			trips:        db.Collection(mongodb.CollRouteTrips),
33			pours:        db.Collection(mongodb.CollMilkPours),
34		}
35	}
36	
37	// pourRow is the projected slice of a milk pour needed for aggregation.
38	type pourRow struct {
39		ID             primitive.ObjectID `bson:"_id"`
40		QuantityLitres float64            `bson:"quantity_litres"`
41		FatPct         float64            `bson:"fat_pct"`
42		SNFPct         float64            `bson:"snf_pct"`
43		Assurance      string             `bson:"assurance"`
44	}
45	
46	// findRecordedPours returns the RECORDED pours of one DCS date+shift,
47	// projected down to the fields the consignment aggregate needs.
48	func (r *repo) findRecordedPours(ctx context.Context, dcsID primitive.ObjectID, date, shift string) ([]pourRow, error) {
49		filter := bson.D{
50			{Key: "dcs_id", Value: dcsID},
51			{Key: "pour_date", Value: date},
52			{Key: "shift", Value: shift},
53			{Key: "status", Value: domain.PourStatusRecorded},
54		}
55		projection := bson.D{
56			{Key: "_id", Value: 1},
57			{Key: "quantity_litres", Value: 1},
58			{Key: "fat_pct", Value: 1},
59			{Key: "snf_pct", Value: 1},
60			{Key: "assurance", Value: 1},
61		}
62		cur, err := r.pours.Find(ctx, filter,
63			options.Find().SetProjection(projection).SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "created_at", Value: 1}}))
64		if err != nil {
65			return nil, fmt.Errorf("find recorded pours: %w", err)
66		}
67		var rows []pourRow
68		if err := cur.All(ctx, &rows); err != nil {
69			return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode recorded pours: %w", err)
70		}
71		return rows, nil
72	}
73	
74	// insertConsignment stores a new consignment (the service pre-generates its
75	// ObjectID). The unique index on dcs_id+date+shift turns duplicates into a
76	// duplicate-key error — kept unwrapped-detectable via %w.
77	func (r *repo) insertConsignment(ctx context.Context, c *domain.DCSConsignment) error {
78		if _, err := r.consignments.InsertOne(ctx, c); err != nil {
79			return fmt.Errorf("insert consignment: %w", err)
80		}
81		return nil
82	}
83	
84	// findConsignmentByID loads one consignment.
85	func (r *repo) findConsignmentByID(ctx context.Context, id primitive.ObjectID) (*domain.DCSConsignment, error) {
86		var c domain.DCSConsignment
87		if err := r.consignments.FindOne(ctx, bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: id}}).Decode(&c); err != nil {
88			return nil, fmt.Errorf("find consignment %s: %w", id.Hex(), err)
89		}
90		return &c, nil
91	}
92	
93	// markConsignmentDispatched transitions OPEN→DISPATCHED optimistically:
94	// the status filter makes the guard atomic without transactions. The seal
95	// also re-stamps the pour aggregates (extraSet) so pours recorded between
96	// creation and dispatch are never lost from the consignment's totals.
97	func (r *repo) markConsignmentDispatched(ctx context.Context, id primitive.ObjectID, at time.Time, extraSet bson.D) (bool, error) {
98		set := bson.D{
99			{Key: "status", Value: domain.ConsignmentStatusDispatch},
100			{Key: "dispatched_at", Value: at},
101		}
102		set = append(set, extraSet...)
103		res, err := r.consignments.UpdateOne(ctx,
104			bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: id}, {Key: "status", Value: domain.ConsignmentStatusOpen}},
105			bson.D{{Key: "$set", Value: set}})
106		if err != nil {
107			return false, fmt.Errorf("mark consignment dispatched: %w", err)
108		}
109		return res.MatchedCount > 0, nil
110	}
111	
112	// markConsignmentPickedUp transitions DISPATCHED→PICKED_UP and pins the
113	// carrying trip, guarded atomically by the status filter.
114	func (r *repo) markConsignmentPickedUp(ctx context.Context, id, tripID primitive.ObjectID) (bool, error) {
115		res, err := r.consignments.UpdateOne(ctx,
116			bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: id}, {Key: "status", Value: domain.ConsignmentStatusDispatch}},
117			bson.D{{Key: "$set", Value: bson.D{
118				{Key: "status", Value: domain.ConsignmentStatusPickedUp},
119				{Key: "route_trip_id", Value: tripID},
120			}}})
121		if err != nil {
122			return false, fmt.Errorf("mark consignment picked up: %w", err)
123		}
124		return res.MatchedCount > 0, nil
125	}
126	
127	// markConsignmentsDelivered transitions every listed PICKED_UP consignment
128	// to DELIVERED (bulk companion of the trip delivery).
129	func (r *repo) markConsignmentsDelivered(ctx context.Context, ids []primitive.ObjectID) error {
130		_, err := r.consignments.UpdateMany(ctx,
131			bson.D{
132				{Key: "_id", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$in", Value: ids}}},
133				{Key: "status", Value: domain.ConsignmentStatusPickedUp},
134			},
135			bson.D{{Key: "$set", Value: bson.D{{Key: "status", Value: domain.ConsignmentStatusDelivered}}}})
136		if err != nil {
137			return fmt.Errorf("mark consignments delivered: %w", err)
138		}
139		return nil
140	}
141	
142	// setConsignmentProvenanceSeq pins the latest ledger sequence on the doc.
143	func (r *repo) setConsignmentProvenanceSeq(ctx context.Context, id primitive.ObjectID, seq int64) error {
144		_, err := r.consignments.UpdateByID(ctx, id,
145			bson.D{{Key: "$set", Value: bson.D{{Key: "provenance_seq", Value: seq}}}})
146		if err != nil {
147			return fmt.Errorf("set consignment provenance seq: %w", err)
148		}
149		return nil
150	}
151	
152	// listConsignments returns a filtered, newest-first page plus the total count.
153	// A zero dcsID means "no DCS filter".
154	func (r *repo) listConsignments(ctx context.Context, dcsID primitive.ObjectID, date, status string, page httpx.Page) ([]domain.DCSConsignment, int64, error) {
155		filter := bson.D{}
156		if !dcsID.IsZero() {
157			filter = append(filter, bson.E{Key: "dcs_id", Value: dcsID})
158		}
159		if date != "" {
160			filter = append(filter, bson.E{Key: "date", Value: date})
161		}
162		if status != "" {
163			filter = append(filter, bson.E{Key: "status", Value: status})
164		}
165		total, err := r.consignments.CountDocuments(ctx, filter)
166		if err != nil {
167			return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("count consignments: %w", err)
168		}
169		cur, err := r.consignments.Find(ctx, filter, options.Find().
170			SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "created_at", Value: -1}}).
171			SetSkip(page.Offset).SetLimit(page.Limit))
172		if err != nil {
173			return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("list consignments: %w", err)
174		}
175		items := []domain.DCSConsignment{}
176		if err := cur.All(ctx, &items); err != nil {
177			return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("decode consignments: %w", err)
178		}
179		return items, total, nil
180	}
181	
182	// insertTrip stores a new route trip (the service pre-generates its ObjectID).
183	func (r *repo) insertTrip(ctx context.Context, t *domain.RouteTrip) error {
184		if _, err := r.trips.InsertOne(ctx, t); err != nil {
185			return fmt.Errorf("insert trip: %w", err)
186		}
187		return nil
188	}
189	
190	// findTripByID loads one trip.
191	func (r *repo) findTripByID(ctx context.Context, id primitive.ObjectID) (*domain.RouteTrip, error) {
192		var t domain.RouteTrip
193		if err := r.trips.FindOne(ctx, bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: id}}).Decode(&t); err != nil {
194			return nil, fmt.Errorf("find trip %s: %w", id.Hex(), err)
195		}
196		return &t, nil
197	}
198	
199	// markStopPickedUp stamps the matched stop with pickup time/temperature and
200	// moves the trip to IN_PROGRESS (idempotent once it is already there).
201	func (r *repo) markStopPickedUp(ctx context.Context, tripID, consignmentID primitive.ObjectID, at time.Time, tempC float64, notes string) error {
202		_, err := r.trips.UpdateOne(ctx,
203			bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: tripID}, {Key: "stops.consignment_id", Value: consignmentID}},
204			bson.D{{Key: "$set", Value: bson.D{
205				{Key: "stops.$.picked_up_at", Value: at},
206				{Key: "stops.$.temp_c", Value: tempC},
207				{Key: "stops.$.notes", Value: notes},
208				{Key: "status", Value: domain.TripStatusInProgress},
209			}}})
210		if err != nil {
211			return fmt.Errorf("mark stop picked up: %w", err)
212		}
213		return nil
214	}
215	
216	// pushColdChain appends one temperature sample to the trip's cold-chain log.
217	func (r *repo) pushColdChain(ctx context.Context, tripID primitive.ObjectID, entry domain.ColdChainEntry) error {
218		_, err := r.trips.UpdateByID(ctx, tripID,
219			bson.D{{Key: "$push", Value: bson.D{{Key: "cold_chain", Value: entry}}}})
220		if err != nil {
221			return fmt.Errorf("push cold chain entry: %w", err)
222		}
223		return nil
224	}
225	
226	// markTripDelivered transitions IN_PROGRESS→DELIVERED optimistically and
227	// records the receiving BMC.
228	func (r *repo) markTripDelivered(ctx context.Context, tripID, bmcID primitive.ObjectID, at time.Time) (bool, error) {
229		res, err := r.trips.UpdateOne(ctx,
230			bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: tripID}, {Key: "status", Value: domain.TripStatusInProgress}},
231			bson.D{{Key: "$set", Value: bson.D{
232				{Key: "status", Value: domain.TripStatusDelivered},
233				{Key: "delivered_to_bmc_id", Value: bmcID},
234				{Key: "delivered_at", Value: at},
235			}}})
236		if err != nil {
237			return false, fmt.Errorf("mark trip delivered: %w", err)
238		}
239		return res.MatchedCount > 0, nil
240	}
241	
242	// setTripProvenanceSeq pins the latest ledger sequence on the trip doc.
243	func (r *repo) setTripProvenanceSeq(ctx context.Context, id primitive.ObjectID, seq int64) error {
244		_, err := r.trips.UpdateByID(ctx, id,
245			bson.D{{Key: "$set", Value: bson.D{{Key: "provenance_seq", Value: seq}}}})
246		if err != nil {
247			return fmt.Errorf("set trip provenance seq: %w", err)
248		}
249		return nil
250	}
251	
252	// listTrips returns a filtered, newest-first page plus the total count.
253	// Zero ObjectIDs mean "no filter" on that field.
254	func (r *repo) listTrips(ctx context.Context, unionID primitive.ObjectID, date string, vanRiderPartyID primitive.ObjectID, page httpx.Page) ([]domain.RouteTrip, int64, error) {
255		filter := bson.D{}
256		if !unionID.IsZero() {
257			filter = append(filter, bson.E{Key: "union_id", Value: unionID})
258		}
259		if date != "" {
260			filter = append(filter, bson.E{Key: "date", Value: date})
261		}
262		if !vanRiderPartyID.IsZero() {
263			filter = append(filter, bson.E{Key: "van_rider_party_id", Value: vanRiderPartyID})
264		}
265		total, err := r.trips.CountDocuments(ctx, filter)
266		if err != nil {
267			return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("count trips: %w", err)
268		}
269		cur, err := r.trips.Find(ctx, filter, options.Find().
270			SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "created_at", Value: -1}}).
271			SetSkip(page.Offset).SetLimit(page.Limit))
272		if err != nil {
273			return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("list trips: %w", err)
274		}
275		items := []domain.RouteTrip{}
276		if err := cur.All(ctx, &items); err != nil {
277			return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("decode trips: %w", err)
278		}
279		return items, total, nil
280	}
```

```text
37		// (Developer Note §6.3, Appendix C). Human-readable, e.g. "GON-2026-06".

48	// Assurance levels (Developer Note §6.2) — how fat/SNF was captured. Every
49	// pour carries one; every downstream aggregate (consignment, batch, lot)
50	// inherits the WEAKEST assurance in its set, so capture quality is measurable
51	// and drives societies toward instrument-linked capture.
52	const (
53		AssuranceInstrument = "A" // analyzer streamed the reading (RS-232/BLE) — strongest
54		AssuranceOCRPhoto   = "B" // OCR of an analyzer-screen photo, photo retained as evidence
55		AssuranceManual     = "C" // keyed by hand — weakest, drives supervisor sampling
56	)
57	
58	// AssuranceForSource maps a reading/pour capture mode to its assurance level.
59	func AssuranceForSource(source string) string {
60		switch source {
61		case ReadingModeDirect:
62			return AssuranceInstrument
63		case ReadingModePhotoOCR:
64			return AssuranceOCRPhoto
65		default:
66			return AssuranceManual
67		}
68	}
69	
70	// assuranceRank orders assurance so "weakest in a set" is a max-rank pick
71	// (higher rank = weaker).
72	var assuranceRank = map[string]int{AssuranceInstrument: 0, AssuranceOCRPhoto: 1, AssuranceManual: 2}
73	
74	// WeakestAssurance returns the weakest (lowest-trust) assurance among the
75	// given levels — the value an aggregate inherits (§6.2). Empty input → "".
76	func WeakestAssurance(levels ...string) string {
77		weakest, seen := "", -1
78		for _, l := range levels {
79			if r, ok := assuranceRank[l]; ok && r > seen {
80				weakest, seen = l, r
81			}
82		}
83		return weakest
84	}

87	func (rc RateChart) PricePour(fatPct, snfPct, qtyLitres float64) (rate, amount float64) {
88		rate = rc.BaseRatePerLitre + fatPct*rc.FatRatePerPoint + snfPct*rc.SNFRatePerPoint
89		rate = math.Round(rate*100) / 100
90		amount = math.Round(rate*qtyLitres*100) / 100
91		return rate, amount

136	// CheckPlausibility validates fat/SNF/qty against physical bounds and returns
137	// the violated flags (empty slice = plausible).
138	func CheckPlausibility(fatPct, snfPct, qtyLitres float64) []string {
139		var flags []string
140		if fatPct < PlausibleFatMin || fatPct > PlausibleFatMax ||
141			snfPct < PlausibleSNFMin || snfPct > PlausibleSNFMax {
142			flags = append(flags, IntegrityFlagImplausibleValue)
143		}
144		if qtyLitres != 0 && (qtyLitres < PlausibleQtyMin || qtyLitres > PlausibleQtyMax) {
145			flags = append(flags, IntegrityFlagImplausibleValue)
146		}
147		return flags
148	}
```

 `./docs/ALIGNMENT_SPEC.md`

```text
1	# Saathi Backend ⇄ Frontend Alignment Spec
2	
3	> **Goal:** align the Go backend (`parag-saathi-be`) to the 80%-built React Native app
4	> (`parag-saathi-fe`), reconciled with the **Developer Technical Note** (the authoritative
5	> traceability build spec). Integration (wiring the FE mappers) comes later — **first the backend
6	> is made spec-clean and capable**: we ADD genuinely-missing fields/endpoints/relations; we do NOT
7	> pollute the backend with FE-name aliases (those are FE-mapper fixes at integration time).
8	>
9	> This doc is derived from a 3-agent deep analysis of both repos (identity round) + the full
10	> Developer Note. It is the running plan; each **Piece** is fixed completely before the next.
11	
12	---
13	
14	## 0. What's already aligned (no work needed)
15	
16	- **Wire conventions**: base `/api/v1`, success `{data, meta?}`, error `{error:{code,message,details?}}`,
17	  `Authorization: Bearer`, refresh-on-401, snake_case wire, ObjectID hex ids, ISO-8601 / `YYYY-MM-DD`
18	  dates, `client_event_id` idempotency. ✅
19	- **Module mounts** match the FE's `backend-integration.md` map exactly (identity, orgs, collection,
20	  logistics, plant, quality, settlement, cattle, platformops, publictrace). ✅
21	- **Multi-role model** (one phone = one Party = many org-scoped RoleAssignments) — the farmer+sachiv
```

```text
13		ConsignmentStatusPickedUp  = "PICKED_UP"  // on the van

19	// DCSConsignment aggregates a DCS's pours for one date+shift into the unit
20	// the van picks up. It is the pooling boundary: past this point milk traces
21	// to a *set* of contributors (blueprint §7.4).
22	type DCSConsignment struct {
23		ID                  primitive.ObjectID   `bson:"_id,omitempty" json:"id"`
24		DCSID               primitive.ObjectID   `bson:"dcs_id"    json:"dcs_id"`
25		Date                string               `bson:"date"      json:"date"` // YYYY-MM-DD
26		Shift               string               `bson:"shift"     json:"shift"`
27		PourIDs             []primitive.ObjectID `bson:"pour_ids"  json:"pour_ids"`
28		TotalQuantityLitres float64              `bson:"total_quantity_litres" json:"total_quantity_litres"`
29		CanCount            int                  `bson:"can_count,omitempty"   json:"can_count,omitempty"`
30		// AvgFatPct/AvgSNFPct are the QUANTITY-WEIGHTED averages the Developer Note
31		// §6.4 calls wavg_fat / wavg_snf — computed over the sealed pour set.
32		AvgFatPct float64 `bson:"avg_fat_pct,omitempty" json:"avg_fat_pct,omitempty"`
33		AvgSNFPct float64 `bson:"avg_snf_pct,omitempty" json:"avg_snf_pct,omitempty"`
34		// Assurance is the WEAKEST capture assurance among the pooled pours (§6.2).
35		Assurance string `bson:"assurance,omitempty" json:"assurance,omitempty"`
36		// SealCode freezes the physical cans to this shift's pour set at dispatch
37		// (§6.4, Appendix A: SEAL-<consignment>-<checksum>); the van verifies it.
38		SealCode     string             `bson:"seal_code,omitempty" json:"seal_code,omitempty"`
39		SealedAt     *time.Time         `bson:"sealed_at,omitempty" json:"sealed_at,omitempty"`
40		Status       string             `bson:"status"    json:"status"`
41		CreatedBy    primitive.ObjectID `bson:"created_by"    json:"created_by"`
42		DispatchedAt *time.Time         `bson:"dispatched_at,omitempty" json:"dispatched_at,omitempty"`
43		RouteTripID         *primitive.ObjectID  `bson:"route_trip_id,omitempty" json:"route_trip_id,omitempty"`
44		BMCLotID            *primitive.ObjectID  `bson:"bmc_lot_id,omitempty"    json:"bmc_lot_id,omitempty"`
45		ProvenanceSeq       int64                `bson:"provenance_seq,omitempty" json:"provenance_seq,omitempty"`
46		CreatedAt           time.Time            `bson:"created_at" json:"created_at"`
```

```text
// Package audit writes the immutable who-did-what trail required for
// government accountability and DPDP breach forensics (blueprint §12, §16).
// Entries are insert-only; the STATE_AUDITOR role reads them via the
// platformops module.
package audit

import (
	"context"
	"log/slog"
	"time"

	"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson/primitive"
	"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo"

	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/auth"
)

const collection = "audit_logs"

// Entry is one audit record. `_id` is a generated ObjectID; actor identifiers
// arrive from JWT claims as ObjectID hex strings.
type Entry struct {
	ID           primitive.ObjectID `bson:"_id,omitempty" json:"id"`
	ActorPartyID string             `bson:"actor_party_id" json:"actor_party_id"`
	ActorRole    string             `bson:"actor_role,omitempty" json:"actor_role,omitempty"`
	Action       string             `bson:"action"         json:"action"` // e.g. "http.POST /api/v1/collection/pours" or "support.pii_lookup"
	TargetType   string             `bson:"target_type,omitempty" json:"target_type,omitempty"`
	TargetID     string             `bson:"target_id,omitempty"   json:"target_id,omitempty"`
	Status       int                `bson:"status,omitempty"      json:"status,omitempty"`
	IP           string             `bson:"ip,omitempty"          json:"ip,omitempty"`
	RequestID    string             `bson:"request_id,omitempty"  json:"request_id,omitempty"`
	Meta         map[string]any     `bson:"meta,omitempty"        json:"meta,omitempty"`
	TS           time.Time          `bson:"ts"             json:"ts"`
}

// Recorder persists audit entries asynchronously so auditing never adds
// latency to the request path.
type Recorder struct {
	coll *mongo.Collection
	log  *slog.Logger
}

// NewRecorder binds the recorder to the database.
func NewRecorder(db *mongo.Database, log *slog.Logger) *Recorder {
	return &Recorder{coll: db.Collection(collection), log: log}
}

// Record fills identity fields from the request context and persists the
// entry in the background (fire-and-forget with its own timeout).
func (r *Recorder) Record(ctx context.Context, e Entry) {
	if a, ok := auth.ActorFrom(ctx); ok {
		if e.ActorPartyID == "" {
			e.ActorPartyID = a.PartyID
		}
		if e.ActorRole == "" {
			e.ActorRole = a.RoleCode
		}
	}
	e.ID = primitive.NewObjectID()
	e.TS = time.Now().UTC()

	go func() {
		writeCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
		defer cancel()
		if _, err := r.coll.InsertOne(writeCtx, e); err != nil {
			r.log.Error("audit write failed", slog.String("action", e.Action), slog.Any("err", err))
		}
	}()
}
```

```text
92	func (s *Service) internalErr(ctx context.Context, op string, err error, attrs ...any) error {
93		var appErr *httpx.AppError
94		if errors.As(err, &appErr) {
95			return appErr

103	// (plant module signQRToken) mints: "base64url(qr_code|product_lot_id_hex|
104	// issued_unix)" + "." + hex(HMAC-SHA256(secret, decoded payload)), where
105	// product_lot_id_hex is productLotID.Hex(). The HMAC is computed over the
106	// DECODED payload bytes — exactly what issuance signed. The comparison is
107	// constant-time so a forger learns nothing from response timing.
108	func VerifyQRToken(secret, token string) bool {
109		payloadB64, signature, found := strings.Cut(token, ".")
110		if !found || payloadB64 == "" || signature == "" {
111			return false // malformed: no payload/signature split
112		}
113		payload, err := base64.RawURLEncoding.DecodeString(payloadB64)
114		if err != nil || len(payload) == 0 {
115			return false // malformed: payload is not valid base64url
116		}
117		expected := auth.HMACHash(secret, string(payload))
118		return auth.ConstantTimeEqual(expected, signature)
119	}

176		sourcing, err := s.buildSourcing(ctx, events)
177		if err != nil {
178			return nil, err
179		}
180	
181		ledgerInfo, err := s.verifyTracedRange(ctx, events)
182		if err != nil {
183			return nil, err
184		}
185	
186		resp := &QRScanResponse{
187			Product: ProductInfo{
188				Name:       lot.ProductName,
189				SKU:        lot.SKU,
190				UnitSize:   lot.UnitSize,
191				MfgDate:    lot.MfgDate,
192				ExpiryDate: lot.ExpiryDate,
193			},
194			BatchNumber: batch.BatchNumber,
195			Plant:       PlantInfo{Name: plant.Name, District: plant.District},
196			Sourcing:    *sourcing,
197			Ledger:      *ledgerInfo,
198			ScanCount:   qr.ScanCount + 1, // reflect this scan; the $inc lands async
199		}
200	
201		// PLANT_LAB pass certificate — omitted (not an error) when absent.
202		qc, err := s.repo.latestPlantLabPass(ctx, batch.ID)
203		if err != nil {
204			return nil, s.internalErr(ctx, "qr scan: load plant lab certificate", err,
205				slog.String("batch_id", batch.ID.Hex()))
206		}
207		if qc != nil {
208			resp.Quality = &QualityInfo{
209				CertificateNumber: qc.CertificateNumber,
210				Stage:             qc.Stage,
211				Tests:             qc.Tests,
212				RecordedAt:        qc.RecordedAt,
213			}
214		}
215	
216		// A recalled lot still resolves with 200 — consumers must SEE the recall
217		// notice, not hit a dead link.
218		if lot.Status == domain.ProductLotStatusRecalled {
219			resp.Recalled = true
220			notice := "This product lot has been RECALLED. Do not consume — return it to the point of purchase."
221			if lot.RecallReason != "" {
222				notice += " Reason: " + lot.RecallReason
223			}
224			resp.RecallNotice = notice
225		}
226	
227		s.log.InfoContext(ctx, "qr scan resolved",
228			slog.String("qr_code", qrCode),
229			slog.String("qr_id", qr.ID.Hex()),
230			slog.String("product_lot_id", lot.ID.Hex()),
231			slog.String("batch_id", batch.ID.Hex()),
232			slog.String("batch_number", batch.BatchNumber),
233			slog.Int("samitis", len(sourcing.Samitis)),
234			slog.Bool("ledger_intact", ledgerInfo.Intact),
235			slog.Bool("recalled", resp.Recalled))
236		return resp, nil
237	}
238	
239	// buildSourcing derives the samiti-set view from traced consignment events:
240	// contributing DCS org ids from each event's org_unit_id/payload, collection
241	// dates from payloads, with the consignment documents as fallback when the
242	// events did not carry those fields. Ledger events carry ObjectIDs as hex
243	// strings, so the sets are hex-keyed and parsed at the DB/orgscope boundary.
244	func (s *Service) buildSourcing(ctx context.Context, events []provenance.Event) (*SourcingInfo, error) {
245		dcsIDs := map[string]struct{}{}
246		dates := map[string]struct{}{}
247		consignmentIDs := map[string]struct{}{}
248	
249		for _, ev := range events {
250			if ev.EntityType != domain.EntityConsignment {
251				continue
252			}
253			consignmentIDs[ev.EntityID] = struct{}{}
254			// Only created/dispatched events carry the DCS in org_unit_id —
255			// consignment.picked_up is appended by logistics under the UNION's
256			// org id, which must never be counted as a contributing samiti.
257			switch ev.Type {
258			case domain.EventConsignmentCreated, domain.EventConsignmentDispatched:
259				if ev.OrgUnitID != "" {
260					dcsIDs[ev.OrgUnitID] = struct{}{}
261				} else if v, ok := ev.Payload["dcs_id"].(string); ok && v != "" {
262					dcsIDs[v] = struct{}{}
263				}
264			}
265			if v, ok := ev.Payload["date"].(string); ok && v != "" {
266				dates[v] = struct{}{}
267			}
268		}
269	
270		// Fallback: if the events lacked DCS ids or dates, read the consignment
271		// docs themselves (still samiti-level — pour ids are never surfaced).
272		if len(consignmentIDs) > 0 && (len(dcsIDs) == 0 || len(dates) == 0) {
273			ids := make([]primitive.ObjectID, 0, len(consignmentIDs))
274			for _, hexID := range sortedKeys(consignmentIDs) {
275				cid, err := primitive.ObjectIDFromHex(hexID)
276				if err != nil {
277					// Ledger event ids should always be ObjectID hex — flag and skip.
278					s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "QR scan: traced consignment id is not a valid object id",
279						slog.String("consignment_id", hexID))
280					continue
281				}
282				ids = append(ids, cid)
283			}
284			docs, err := s.repo.consignmentsByIDs(ctx, ids)
285			if err != nil {
286				return nil, s.internalErr(ctx, "qr scan: load consignments for sourcing", err)
287			}
288			for _, c := range docs {
289				if !c.DCSID.IsZero() {
290					dcsIDs[c.DCSID.Hex()] = struct{}{}
291				}
292				if c.Date != "" {
293					dates[c.Date] = struct{}{}
294				}
295			}
296		}
297	
298		samitis := make([]SamitiInfo, 0, len(dcsIDs))
299		districts := map[string]struct{}{}
300		for _, hexID := range sortedKeys(dcsIDs) {
301			orgID, err := primitive.ObjectIDFromHex(hexID)
302			if err != nil {
303				// A malformed id must not break a consumer scan — log and skip.
304				s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "QR scan: contributing DCS id is not a valid object id",
305					slog.String("dcs_org_id", hexID))
306				continue
307			}
308			org, err := s.orgs.Get(ctx, orgID)
309			if err != nil {
310				// A missing org unit must not break a consumer scan — log and skip.
311				s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "QR scan: contributing DCS org not resolvable",
312					slog.String("dcs_org_id", hexID), slog.Any("err", err))
313				continue
314			}
315			// Defence in depth: the §7.4 samiti set may only contain DCS units.
316			if org.Type != domain.OrgTypeDCS {
317				s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "QR scan: non-DCS org unit skipped from samiti set",
318					slog.String("org_id", hexID), slog.String("org_type", org.Type))
319				continue
320			}
321			samitis = append(samitis, SamitiInfo{Name: org.Name, Code: org.Code, District: org.District})
322			if org.District != "" {
323				districts[org.District] = struct{}{}
324			}
325		}
326		sort.Slice(samitis, func(i, j int) bool { return samitis[i].Name < samitis[j].Name })
327	
328		collectionDates := sortedKeys(dates)
329		return &SourcingInfo{
330			Message:         sourcingMessage(collectionDates, len(samitis), sortedKeys(districts)),
331			Samitis:         samitis,
332			CollectionDates: collectionDates,
333		}, nil
334	}
335	
336	// sourcingMessage renders the consumer-facing pooled-provenance sentence,
337	// e.g. "Made from milk collected on 2026-07-05 from 3 samitis in Lucknow".
338	func sourcingMessage(dates []string, samitiCount int, districts []string) string {
339		var b strings.Builder
340		b.WriteString("Made from milk collected")
341		if len(dates) > 0 {
342			b.WriteString(" on " + strings.Join(dates, ", "))
343		}
344		noun := "samitis"
345		if samitiCount == 1 {
346			noun = "samiti"
347		}
348		fmt.Fprintf(&b, " from %d %s", samitiCount, noun)
349		if len(districts) > 0 {
350			b.WriteString(" in " + strings.Join(districts, ", "))
351		}
352		return b.String()
353	}
354	
355	// verifyTracedRange answers the per-scan tamper-evidence check from a
356	// cumulative verification watermark: the chain is verified incrementally up
357	// to the traced range's max seq, and once a prefix is verified, later scans
358	// inside it are O(1) — no per-request re-hash of thousands of interleaved
359	// events. Spans over scanVerifySpanCap are verified partially (most recent
360	// tail) and flagged, matching the previous per-scan behaviour.
361	func (s *Service) verifyTracedRange(ctx context.Context, events []provenance.Event) (*LedgerInfo, error) {
362		if len(events) == 0 {
363			return &LedgerInfo{Events: 0, Intact: true, VerifiedRange: [2]int64{0, 0}}, nil
364		}
365		maxSeq := events[0].Seq
366		for _, ev := range events[1:] {
367			if ev.Seq > maxSeq {
368				maxSeq = ev.Seq
369			}
370		}
371	
372		s.verifyMu.Lock()
373		defer s.verifyMu.Unlock()
374	
375		if s.chainBroken {
376			return &LedgerInfo{
377				Events:        len(events),
378				Intact:        false,
379				VerifiedRange: [2]int64{s.brokenAtSeq, s.brokenAtSeq},
380			}, nil
381		}
382		if maxSeq <= s.verifiedUpTo {
383			return &LedgerInfo{
384				Events:        len(events),
385				Intact:        true,
386				VerifiedRange: [2]int64{1, s.verifiedUpTo},
387			}, nil
388		}
389	
390		// Extend the watermark: start at the last verified event (re-hashing it
391		// covers the boundary linkage), capped to the per-request span budget.
392		from, partial := max(int64(1), s.verifiedUpTo), false
393		if maxSeq-from+1 > scanVerifySpanCap {
394			from, partial = maxSeq-scanVerifySpanCap+1, true
395		}
396		intact, brokenAt, err := s.ledger.VerifyChain(ctx, from, maxSeq)
397		if err != nil {
398			return nil, s.internalErr(ctx, "qr scan: verify ledger chain", err,
399				slog.Int64("from", from), slog.Int64("to", maxSeq))
400		}
401		if intact {
402			s.verifiedUpTo = maxSeq
403		} else {
404			s.chainBroken, s.brokenAtSeq = true, brokenAt
405			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "provenance chain break detected during scan verification",
406				slog.Int64("broken_at_seq", brokenAt),
407				slog.Int64("from", from), slog.Int64("to", maxSeq))
408		}
409		return &LedgerInfo{
410			Events:        len(events),
411			Intact:        intact,
412			VerifiedRange: [2]int64{from, maxSeq},
413			Partial:       partial,
414		}, nil
415	}
416	
417	// VerifyLedger runs the public tamper-evidence check over [from,to]. Both
418	// bounds are optional: `to` defaults to the chain head, `from` to the start
419	// of the last publicVerifySpanCap events. Spans over the cap are rejected.
420	func (s *Service) VerifyLedger(ctx context.Context, fromRaw, toRaw string) (*LedgerVerifyResponse, error) {
421		latest, err := s.ledger.LatestSeq(ctx)
422		if err != nil {
423			return nil, s.internalErr(ctx, "ledger verify: read chain head", err)
424		}
425		if latest == 0 {
426			return &LedgerVerifyResponse{Intact: true, From: 0, To: 0}, nil // empty chain is trivially intact
427		}
428	
429		to := latest
430		if toRaw != "" {
431			n, err := strconv.ParseInt(toRaw, 10, 64)
432			if err != nil || n < 1 {
433				return nil, httpx.BadRequest("INVALID_RANGE", "'to' must be a positive sequence number")
434			}
435			to = min(n, latest)
436		}
437		from := max(int64(1), to-publicVerifySpanCap+1)
438		if fromRaw != "" {
439			n, err := strconv.ParseInt(fromRaw, 10, 64)
440			if err != nil || n < 1 {
441				return nil, httpx.BadRequest("INVALID_RANGE", "'from' must be a positive sequence number")
442			}
443			from = n
444		}
445		if from > to {
446			return nil, httpx.BadRequest("INVALID_RANGE", "'from' must not exceed 'to'")
447		}
448		if to-from+1 > publicVerifySpanCap {
449			return nil, httpx.BadRequest("SPAN_TOO_WIDE",
450				fmt.Sprintf("verification span is capped at %d events per request", publicVerifySpanCap))
451		}
452	
453		intact, brokenAt, err := s.ledger.VerifyChain(ctx, from, to)
454		if err != nil {
455			return nil, s.internalErr(ctx, "ledger verify: verify chain", err,
456				slog.Int64("from", from), slog.Int64("to", to))
457		}
458		resp := &LedgerVerifyResponse{Intact: intact, From: from, To: to}
459		if !intact {
460			resp.BrokenAtSeq = &brokenAt
461			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "public ledger verification found a broken chain",
462				slog.Int64("broken_at_seq", brokenAt),
463				slog.Int64("from", from), slog.Int64("to", to))
464		}
465		return resp, nil
466	}
467	
468	// TraceGraph returns the full event graph around one entity: upstream via
469	// the recursive ref walk, downstream via reverse-ref lookup — the recall /
470	// root-cause tool (§8.3). entityID is the entity's ObjectID as a hex string
471	// (already validated by the handler; the ledger stores ids as hex).
472	func (s *Service) TraceGraph(ctx context.Context, entityType, entityID string) (*TraceGraphResponse, error) {
473		if err := validateEntityType(entityType); err != nil {
474			return nil, err
475		}
476		upstream, err := s.ledger.Trace(ctx, entityType, entityID, traceDepth)
477		if err != nil {
478			return nil, s.internalErr(ctx, "trace graph: upstream walk", err,
479				slog.String("entity_type", entityType), slog.String("entity_id", entityID))
480		}
481		// The cap is pushed into the query: only the LAST downstreamEventCap
482		// referencing events are fetched, instead of decoding an unbounded set
483		// into memory and truncating afterwards.
484		downstream, err := s.ledger.DownstreamRefs(ctx, entityID, downstreamEventCap)
485		if err != nil {
486			return nil, s.internalErr(ctx, "trace graph: downstream refs", err,
487				slog.String("entity_type", entityType), slog.String("entity_id", entityID))
488		}
489		if len(upstream) == 0 && len(downstream) == 0 {
490			return nil, httpx.NotFound("provenance for entity")
491		}
492		if upstream == nil {
493			upstream = []provenance.Event{}
494		}
495		if downstream == nil {
496			downstream = []provenance.Event{}
497		}
498		return &TraceGraphResponse{Upstream: upstream, Downstream: downstream}, nil
499	}
500	
501	// Timeline returns one entity's own events in chain order, paginated. The
502	// skip/limit is pushed into the Mongo query so a page read never loads the
503	// entity's full history. The second return value is the total event count.
504	// entityID is the entity's ObjectID as a hex string (handler-validated).
505	func (s *Service) Timeline(ctx context.Context, entityType, entityID string, page httpx.Page) ([]provenance.Event, int, error) {
506		if err := validateEntityType(entityType); err != nil {
507			return nil, 0, err
508		}
509		total, err := s.ledger.CountEventsForEntity(ctx, entityType, entityID)
510		if err != nil {
511			return nil, 0, s.internalErr(ctx, "timeline: count entity events", err,
512				slog.String("entity_type", entityType), slog.String("entity_id", entityID))
513		}
514		if total == 0 {
515			return nil, 0, httpx.NotFound("provenance for entity")
516		}
517		events, err := s.ledger.EventsForEntityPage(ctx, entityType, entityID, page.Offset, page.Limit)
518		if err != nil {
519			return nil, 0, s.internalErr(ctx, "timeline: load entity events page", err,
520				slog.String("entity_type", entityType), slog.String("entity_id", entityID))
521		}
522		return events, int(total), nil
523	}
524	
525	// validateEntityType rejects entity types outside the domain.Entity* catalog.
526	func validateEntityType(entityType string) error {
527		if _, ok := validEntityTypes[entityType]; !ok {
528			return httpx.BadRequest("INVALID_ENTITY_TYPE",
529				"unknown entity type "+entityType+" — use one of the provenance entity type constants")
530		}
531		return nil
532	}
533	
534	// sortedKeys returns a set's keys in deterministic (lexicographic) order.
535	func sortedKeys(set map[string]struct{}) []string {
536		out := make([]string, 0, len(set))
537		for k := range set {
538			out = append(out, k)
539		}
540		sort.Strings(out)
541		return out
542	}
```

```text
271	6.1 Farmer profile and services
272	The farmer module is the trust surface for the producer. It is deliberately light — it must run on an entry-level
273	Android phone, in Hindi, often on a weak connection — and it does four jobs: show who you are on the
274	system, show what you delivered and are owed, connect you to help, and connect you to schemes and
275	learning.
276	
277	Profile and cattle. The profile shows the member code, society, village, KYC status, "member since", and the
278	cattle count. Cattle is a simple counter for the pilot, backed by an optional per-animal registry so it can later
279	bind to the national animal identity (12-digit Pashu Aadhaar under Bharat Pashudhan / NDLM). Binding
280	animals to the national ear-tag ID is what makes a future herd-health / collar / per-animal yield capability
281	possible; the pilot keeps that path present but dormant behind a feature flag, storing pashu_aadhaar on
282	CATTLE when available and never inventing it.
283	
284	CATTLE { cattle_id, farmer_id, species, breed?, pashu_aadhaar? (nullable),
285	              tag_status: [untagged|tagged|verified], added_at }
286	
287	Editing cattle count is a low-risk, self-service write; changes are logged (not append-only ledgered — cattle is
288	master data, not a custody event).
289	
290	Helpline. A single "Get help" screen with click-to-call and click-to-ticket, populated from region config so
291	numbers can change without an app release:
292	
293	    Society Sachiv (the farmer's own society contact)
294	    Milk Union / district help desk
295	    1962 Mobile Veterinary Unit (animal emergency)
296	    Pyaas / Saathi support line
297	    In-app ticket (category, free text, optional photo) → routed to Union desk with SLA tracking
298	
299	Numbers and labels come from the CMS (below), scoped by society/district, cached offline, and dialled via the
300	OS dialer ( tel: intent) so no calling infrastructure is needed for the pilot.
301	
302	
303	
304	
305	CONFIDENTIAL · PYAAS · Saathi — Developer Technical Note                                                  Page 7 of 20
306	Schemes and educational videos. These are CMS-driven content, never hardcoded links, so the
307	Union/administrator can curate per region and per language and update instantly. Two collections render as
308	simple, cached lists with thumbnails:
309	
310	    Schemes — deep links to the Nand Baba Dugdh Mission portal, the state Animal Husbandry & Dairying
311	    department, NDDB producer resources, DBT/subsidy and insurance schemes, etc.
312	    Learning — a curated video playlist (clean-milk production, mastitis prevention, cattle nutrition and
313	    fodder, artificial insemination and breeding, calf care), deep-linked to the hosting platform; thumbnails and
314	    titles are cached for offline browsing, playback opens the external app/browser.
315	
316	CONTENT { content_id, type: [scheme|video|article|helpline],
317	               title_i18n, description_i18n, url, thumbnail_url,
318	               languages[], region_scope: [state|district|society|all],
319	               category, order, published, valid_from, valid_to }
320	
321	Content sync is a versioned delta pull ( GET /content?since=<version> ), so the app fetches only what changed;
322	the last-good set is always available offline.

325	This is where trustworthy data enters the system, so it gets the most care.

327	For each pour the Sachiv (a) identifies the farmer (search by code/name, or scan the member card; recent
328	farmers cached for the shift), (b) captures quantity (from the weigh scale/DPU, or manual with a reason), (c)
329	captures fat and SNF, and (d) lets the app compute the rate and amount from the active chart. The pour is
330	written to the local ledger immediately and syncs when possible.

339	 linked

342	 evidence                value and stores the photo as evidence                       automated       stored
343	                                                                                      societies
344	
345	 C — Manual              Sachiv keys the value                                        Manual          assurance=C , flagged
346	                                                                                      societies /     for higher audit
347	                                                                                      fallback
```

```text
// listDBT handles GET /dbt/requests.
func (h *handler) listDBT(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	actor, _ := auth.ActorFrom(r.Context())
	q := r.URL.Query()
	page := httpx.ParsePage(r)
	items, total, err := h.svc.ListDBT(r.Context(), actor, q.Get("farmer_party_id"), q.Get("status"), page)
	if err != nil {
		httpx.Error(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	httpx.JSONMeta(w, http.StatusOK, items, map[string]int64{
		"limit": page.Limit, "offset": page.Offset, "total": total,
	})
}
```

```text
81	export function evaluateReading(parameter: TestParameter, value: number): 'PASS' | 'FAIL' {
```

```text
import AsyncStorage from '@react-native-async-storage/async-storage';
import type { MockDb } from '@/core/mocks/db';

/**
 * API transport layer, aligned with the real Go backend (parag-saathi-be):
 *   - success envelope  { "data": ..., "meta"?: ... }
 *   - error envelope    { "error": { "code", "message", "details"? } }
 *   - bearer auth with a SESSION/ROLE access token + rotating refresh token
 *     (POST /auth/refresh) - a 401 triggers one single-flight refresh + retry
 *
 * Every endpoint in src/core/api/endpoints/ is declared once with:
 *   - its HTTP method + path        → the contract the backend implements
 *   - optional mapRequest/mapResponse → snake_case wire ⇄ camelCase domain
 *   - a mock implementation         → runs fully in-app against the seeded
 *                                     mock DB until the backend is connected
 *
 * Switch modes with EXPO_PUBLIC_API_MODE (mock | http) - see .env.example and
 * docs/api-contract.md. No feature code changes when the backend lands.
 */

export type ApiMode = 'mock' | 'http';

// Authentic by default: the app talks to the real Saathi backend. `mock` is an
// explicit offline-development fallback only (never the shipped experience).
const MODE: ApiMode = (process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_API_MODE as ApiMode) || 'http';
const BASE: string = process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL || 'http://localhost:8080/api/v1';

/** The active API mode ('http' = real backend, 'mock' = in-app fixtures). */
export const API_MODE: ApiMode = MODE;
/** The Saathi backend base URL every endpoint is resolved against. */
export const API_BASE_URL: string = BASE;

const ACCESS_KEY = 'saathi-access-token';
const REFRESH_KEY = 'saathi-refresh-token';

/** In-memory token cache, persisted to AsyncStorage (hydrated at app start). */
let accessToken: string | null = null;
let refreshToken: string | null = null;

export function getAuthToken(): string | null {
  return accessToken;
}
export function getRefreshToken(): string | null {
  return refreshToken;
}

/** Store both tokens (login / refresh rotation). */
export function setTokens(t: { access: string | null; refresh: string | null }): void {
  accessToken = t.access;
  refreshToken = t.refresh;
  if (t.access) void AsyncStorage.setItem(ACCESS_KEY, t.access);
  else void AsyncStorage.removeItem(ACCESS_KEY);
  if (t.refresh) void AsyncStorage.setItem(REFRESH_KEY, t.refresh);
  else void AsyncStorage.removeItem(REFRESH_KEY);
}

/** Swap only the access token (role-select issues a ROLE-kind token). */
export function setAccessToken(token: string): void {
  accessToken = token;
  void AsyncStorage.setItem(ACCESS_KEY, token);
}

export function clearTokens(): void {
  setTokens({ access: null, refresh: null });
}

/** Call once at startup (root layout) before authenticated requests. */
export async function hydrateAuthToken(): Promise<void> {
  const [a, r] = await Promise.all([
    AsyncStorage.getItem(ACCESS_KEY),
    AsyncStorage.getItem(REFRESH_KEY),
  ]);
  accessToken = a;
  refreshToken = r;
}

/** Registered by the root layout: fired when auth is irrecoverably lost. */
let onUnauthorized: (() => void) | null = null;
export function setOnUnauthorized(cb: (() => void) | null): void {
  onUnauthorized = cb;
}

export class ApiError extends Error {
  constructor(
    public status: number,
    public code: string,
    message: string,
    public details?: unknown,
  ) {
    super(message);
    this.name = 'ApiError';
  }
}

type HttpMethod = 'GET' | 'POST' | 'PUT' | 'PATCH' | 'DELETE';

export interface EndpointSpec<TIn, TOut> {
  method: HttpMethod;
  /** REST path for http mode; also documents the backend contract */
  path: (input: TIn) => string;
  /** camelCase input → snake_case wire body (http mode only) */
  mapRequest?: (input: TIn) => unknown;
  /** snake_case wire data → domain shape (http mode only) */
  mapResponse?: (raw: unknown) => TOut;
  /** In-app implementation for mock mode */
  mock: (input: TIn, db: MockDb) => TOut | Promise<TOut>;
}

function sleep(ms: number): Promise<void> {
  return new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));
}

/** JSON-safe deep clone (results are plain data; keeps Hermes compatibility). */
function deepClone<T>(value: T): T {
  return value === undefined ? value : (JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value)) as T);
}

/** Raw http call: bearer header, envelope unwrap, AppError mapping. */
async function httpCall(method: HttpMethod, path: string, body: unknown): Promise<unknown> {
  const hasBody = method !== 'GET' && method !== 'DELETE' && body !== undefined;
  const res = await fetch(BASE + path, {
    method,
    headers: {
      Accept: 'application/json',
      ...(hasBody ? { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } : {}),
      ...(accessToken ? { Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}` } : {}),
    },
    body: hasBody ? JSON.stringify(body) : undefined,
  });
  const text = await res.text().catch(() => '');
  let json: unknown;
  try {
    json = text ? JSON.parse(text) : undefined;
  } catch {
    json = undefined;
  }
  if (!res.ok) {
    const err = (json as { error?: { code?: string; message?: string; details?: unknown } })
      ?.error;
    throw new ApiError(
      res.status,
      err?.code ?? `HTTP_${res.status}`,
      err?.message ?? res.statusText,
      err?.details,
    );
  }
  // Success envelope: { data, meta? } - unwrap data; tolerate bare payloads.
  if (json && typeof json === 'object' && 'data' in (json as Record<string, unknown>)) {
    return (json as { data: unknown }).data;
  }
  return json;
}

/** Single-flight refresh: rotate the token pair via POST /auth/refresh. */
let refreshInFlight: Promise<boolean> | null = null;
async function tryRefresh(): Promise<boolean> {
  if (!refreshToken) return false;
  refreshInFlight ??= (async () => {
    try {
      const data = (await httpCall('POST', '/auth/refresh', {
        refresh_token: refreshToken,
      })) as { access_token: string; refresh_token: string };
      setTokens({ access: data.access_token, refresh: data.refresh_token });
      return true;
    } catch {
      return false;
    } finally {
      refreshInFlight = null;
    }
  })();
  return refreshInFlight;
}

/** Declare a typed API endpoint. Returns the callable used by feature code. */
export function endpoint<TIn = void, TOut = unknown>(
  spec: EndpointSpec<TIn, TOut>,
): (input: TIn) => Promise<TOut> {
  return async (input: TIn): Promise<TOut> => {
    if (MODE === 'mock') {
      const { db } = await import('@/core/mocks/db');
      // Simulated network latency so loading states are honest
      await sleep(120 + Math.random() * 230);
      const result = await spec.mock(input, db);
      // Deep-clone so callers can never mutate the mock store through results
      return deepClone(result);
    }

    const path = spec.path(input);
    const body = spec.mapRequest ? spec.mapRequest(input) : (input as unknown);
    try {
      const raw = await httpCall(spec.method, path, body);
      return spec.mapResponse ? spec.mapResponse(raw) : (raw as TOut);
    } catch (e) {
      // One refresh + retry on expired access tokens (never for /auth/* itself)
      if (e instanceof ApiError && e.status === 401 && !path.startsWith('/auth/')) {
        if (await tryRefresh()) {
          const raw = await httpCall(spec.method, path, body);
          return spec.mapResponse ? spec.mapResponse(raw) : (raw as TOut);
        }
        clearTokens();
        onUnauthorized?.();
      }
      throw e;
    }
  };
}
```

```text
=== KYCQueueEvent payload ===
	// the SSE hub. Payload: KYCQueueEvent.
	TopicKYCQueueChanged = "kyc.queue_changed"
)

// KYCQueueEvent is the payload for TopicKYCQueueChanged. It is a nudge, not a
// count — subscribers re-query the authoritative, org-scoped pending count.
type KYCQueueEvent struct {
	Reason    string `json:"reason"` // "submitted" | "approved" | "rejected"
	KYCID     string `json:"kyc_id"`
	SubjectID string `json:"subject_id"` // party whose KYC it is (hex)
}

// Handler consumes a published event. Payload types are documented per topic
// by the publishing module.
type Handler func(ctx context.Context, topic string, payload any)

// Bus is a minimal async pub/sub.
type Bus struct {
	log *slog.Logger

	mu   sync.RWMutex
	subs map[string][]Handler
}

// New builds an empty bus.
func New(log *slog.Logger) *Bus {
	return &Bus{log: log, subs: make(map[string][]Handler)}
}

// Subscribe registers a handler for a topic. Call during module wiring only
// (not concurrently with Publish traffic).
func (b *Bus) Subscribe(topic string, h Handler) {
	b.mu.Lock()
	defer b.mu.Unlock()
	b.subs[topic] = append(b.subs[topic], h)
}
```

```text
2	// SUPER_ADMIN feature-flag console, the STATE_AUDITOR read-only audit surface

9	package platformops

23	// Register wires the platformops module and mounts /admin, /audit,
24	// /notifications and /support (the router hands us the /api/v1 subtree).
25	func Register(r chi.Router, d *deps.Deps) {
26		log := d.Log.With(slog.String("module", "platformops"))
27		repo := newRepository(d.DB)
28		svc := newService(d, repo, log)
29		h := newHandler(svc)
30	
31		r.Route("/admin", func(r chi.Router) {
32			r.Use(middleware.Authenticate(d.JWT))
33	
34			// PCDF_ADMIN may LIST flags; flipping one is SUPER_ADMIN only —
35			// capability gating is a deliberate act (blueprint principle #6).
36			r.With(middleware.RequireRoles(domain.RoleSuperAdmin, domain.RolePCDFAdmin)).
37				Get("/flags", h.listFlags)
38			r.With(middleware.RequireRoles(domain.RoleSuperAdmin)).
39				Put("/flags/{key}", h.setFlag)
40		})
41	
42		r.Route("/audit", func(r chi.Router) {
43			r.Use(middleware.Authenticate(d.JWT))
44			r.Use(middleware.RequireRoles(domain.RoleStateAuditor, domain.RoleSuperAdmin))
45	
46			// Read-only by design: there is deliberately NO write/delete API
47			// surface for audit logs (§12) — entries land via deps.Audit only.
48			r.Get("/logs", h.listAuditLogs)
49			r.Get("/logs/export", h.exportAuditLogs)
50		})
51	
52		r.Route("/notifications", func(r chi.Router) {
53			r.Use(middleware.Authenticate(d.JWT))
54	
55			// SUPER_ADMIN only: a help-desk role has no need to read outbox
56			// message bodies, and the outbox carries credential-adjacent traffic
57			// (OTP notifications — additionally redacted in the service).
58			r.With(middleware.RequireRoles(domain.RoleSuperAdmin)).
59				Get("/", h.listNotifications)
60			r.With(middleware.RequireRoles(domain.RoleSuperAdmin)).
61				Post("/worker/run", h.runWorker)
62		})
63	
64		r.Route("/support", func(r chi.Router) {
65			r.Use(middleware.Authenticate(d.JWT))
66			r.Use(middleware.RequireRoles(domain.RoleSupportAgent, domain.RoleSuperAdmin))
67	
68			r.Get("/parties/lookup", h.lookupParty)
69		})
70	
71		// Cross-module reactions arrive over the bus (modules never import each
72		// other). The bus already runs each handler on its own goroutine with a
73		// bounded context and panic recovery; the wrapper below adds an explicit
74		// second belt at this module's boundary.
75		d.Bus.Subscribe(eventbus.TopicPayoutCredited, safeHandler(log, svc.onPayoutCredited))
76		d.Bus.Subscribe(eventbus.TopicGateBlocked, safeHandler(log, svc.onGateBlocked))
77		d.Bus.Subscribe(eventbus.TopicMVUDispatched, safeHandler(log, svc.onMVUDispatched))
78	}
79	
80	// safeHandler wraps a bus reaction so a programming error in notification
81	// fan-out can never disturb the publishing flow.
82	func safeHandler(log *slog.Logger, reaction func(ctx context.Context, payload any)) eventbus.Handler {
83		return func(ctx context.Context, topic string, payload any) {
84			defer func() {
85				if rec := recover(); rec != nil {
86					log.Error("platformops bus handler panic",
87						slog.String("topic", topic), slog.Any("panic", rec))
88				}
89			}()
90			reaction(ctx, payload)
91		}
92	}
```

```text
11	// RequireRoles allows only ROLE-kind tokens whose role is in the allow-list.
12	// SUPER_ADMIN passes every gate (break-glass admin — all its calls are
13	// audited by the audit middleware).
14	func RequireRoles(roles ...string) func(http.Handler) http.Handler {
15		allowed := make(map[string]struct{}, len(roles))
16		for _, r := range roles {
17			allowed[r] = struct{}{}
18		}
19		return func(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
20			return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
21				actor, ok := auth.ActorFrom(r.Context())
22				if !ok {
23					httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Unauthorized("authentication required"))
24					return
25				}
26				if actor.Kind != auth.TokenKindRole {
27					httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Forbidden("a role token is required — select a role first (POST /api/v1/auth/role/select)"))
28					return
29				}
30				if actor.RoleCode == domain.RoleSuperAdmin {
31					next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
32					return
33				}
34				if _, ok := allowed[actor.RoleCode]; !ok {
35					httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Forbidden("role "+actor.RoleCode+" is not permitted for this action"))
36					return
37				}
38				next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
39			})
40		}
41	}
42	
43	// RequireSession allows any authenticated party (session or role token) —
44	// used for identity endpoints like "list my roles".
45	func RequireSession(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
46		return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
47			if _, ok := auth.ActorFrom(r.Context()); !ok {
48				httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Unauthorized("authentication required"))
49				return
50			}
51			next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
52		})
53	}
```

```text
1	// Package middleware carries the cross-cutting HTTP concerns: token
2	// authentication, role enforcement, audit capture, per-IP rate limiting,
3	// Prometheus metrics.
4	package middleware
5	
6	import (
7		"net/http"
8		"strings"
9	
10		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/auth"
11		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/httpx"
12	)
13	
14	// Authenticate verifies the Bearer token and installs the Actor on the
15	// request context. Requests without a valid token are rejected — public
16	// routes simply don't mount this middleware.
17	func Authenticate(jwtm *auth.JWTManager) func(http.Handler) http.Handler {
18		return func(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
19			return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
20				header := r.Header.Get("Authorization")
21				token, ok := strings.CutPrefix(header, "Bearer ")
22				if !ok || token == "" {
23					httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Unauthorized("missing bearer token"))
24					return
25				}
26				claims, err := jwtm.Parse(token)
27				if err != nil {
28					httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Unauthorized("invalid or expired token"))
29					return
30				}
31				actor := auth.Actor{
32					PartyID:          claims.PartyID,
33					Phone:            claims.Phone,
34					KYCTier:          claims.KYCTier,
35					Kind:             claims.Kind,
36					RoleAssignmentID: claims.RoleAssignmentID,
37					RoleCode:         claims.RoleCode,
38					OrgUnitID:        claims.OrgUnitID,
39					OrgType:          claims.OrgType,
40				}
41				next.ServeHTTP(w, r.WithContext(auth.WithActor(r.Context(), actor)))
42			})
43		}
44	}
45
```

```text
// write on the lot after the QR insert, so recalled or blocked product can
// never be freshly labelled even when the recall races this request.
func (s *Service) IssueQR(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, productLotID primitive.ObjectID) (*domain.BatchQR, error) {
	actID, err := actorID(actor)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	lot, err := s.getProductLot(ctx, productLotID)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if err := s.requireScope(ctx, actor, lot.PlantID, "issue qr"); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	batch, err := s.getBatch(ctx, lot.BatchID)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if !canIssueQR(lot.Status, batch.Status) {
		s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "qr issuance refused: safety gate",
			slog.String("product_lot_id", productLotID.Hex()),
			slog.String("product_lot_status", lot.Status),
			slog.String("batch_id", batch.ID.Hex()),
			slog.String("batch_status", batch.Status),
			slog.String("recall_reason", lot.RecallReason),
			slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID))
		return nil, httpx.Unprocessable(codeSafetyGateBlocked,
			"QR issuance refused: product lot must be ACTIVE and its batch COMPLETED").
			WithDetails(map[string]any{
				"product_lot_status": lot.Status,
				"batch_status":       batch.Status,
				"recall_reason":      lot.RecallReason,
			})
	}

	now := time.Now().UTC()
	var qr *domain.BatchQR
	const maxMintAttempts = 5
	for attempt := 0; attempt < maxMintAttempts; attempt++ {
		code, err := newQRCode()
		if err != nil {
			return nil, s.fail(ctx, "generate qr code", err)
		}
		candidate := &domain.BatchQR{
			ID:           primitive.NewObjectID(),
			QRCode:       code,
			ProductLotID: lot.ID,
			SignedToken:  signQRToken(s.qrSecret, code, lot.ID.Hex(), now),
			IssuedBy:     actID,
			ScanCount:    0,
			IssuedAt:     now,
		}
		insertErr := s.repo.InsertQR(ctx, candidate)
		if insertErr == nil {
			qr = candidate
			break
		}
		if mongo.IsDuplicateKeyError(insertErr) {
			continue // short-code collision — regenerate
		}
		return nil, s.fail(ctx, "insert qr", insertErr)
	}
	if qr == nil {
		return nil, s.fail(ctx, "mint qr code",
			fmt.Errorf("%d consecutive short-code collisions", maxMintAttempts))
	}

	// Recall re-check at WRITE time: the initial read cannot see a recall that
	// lands mid-request, so the mint is confirmed with a conditional no-op
	// write on the lot (filter status=ACTIVE). If the lot left ACTIVE, the
	// just-inserted QR is deleted and issuance refused — a freshly minted QR
	// can never label recalled product.
	active, err := s.repo.TouchActiveLot(ctx, lot.ID)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, s.fail(ctx, "confirm product lot active", err)
	}
	if !active {
		if delErr := s.repo.DeleteQR(ctx, qr.ID); delErr != nil {
			return nil, s.fail(ctx, "delete qr after lot left ACTIVE", delErr)
		}
		s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "qr issuance refused: product lot left ACTIVE during issuance",
			slog.String("product_lot_id", lot.ID.Hex()),
			slog.String("qr_id", qr.ID.Hex()),
			slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID))
		return nil, httpx.Unprocessable(codeSafetyGateBlocked,
			"QR issuance refused: product lot left ACTIVE (e.g. recalled) during issuance")
	}

	ev, err := s.ledger.Append(ctx, provenance.AppendInput{
		Type:       domain.EventQRIssued,
		EntityType: domain.EntityBatchQR,
		EntityID:   qr.ID.Hex(),
		Refs: []provenance.Ref{
			{EntityType: domain.EntityProductLot, EntityID: lot.ID.Hex(), Relation: "labels"},
		},
		Actor:     provenance.ActorRef{PartyID: actor.PartyID, RoleCode: actor.RoleCode},
		OrgUnitID: lot.PlantID.Hex(),
		Payload:   map[string]any{"qr_code": qr.QRCode},
	})
	if err != nil {
		return nil, s.fail(ctx, "append qr.issued event", err)
	}
	if err := s.repo.SetQRProvenanceSeq(ctx, qr.ID, ev.Seq); err != nil {
		return nil, s.fail(ctx, "stamp qr provenance seq", err)
	}
	qr.ProvenanceSeq = ev.Seq
	s.log.InfoContext(ctx, "qr issued",
		slog.String("qr_id", qr.ID.Hex()),
		slog.String("qr_code", qr.QRCode),
		slog.String("product_lot_id", lot.ID.Hex()),
		slog.String("plant_id", lot.PlantID.Hex()),
		slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID))
	return qr, nil
}
```
