161	// transitionBatch performs a status-guarded update (optimistic concurrency —
162	// no transactions on a standalone server). Returns false when the batch was
163	// not in fromStatus, i.e. another actor won the transition.
164	func (rp *repo) transitionBatch(ctx context.Context, id primitive.ObjectID, fromStatus string, set bson.D) (bool, error) {
165		res, err := rp.batches.UpdateOne(ctx,
166			bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: id}, {Key: "status", Value: fromStatus}},
167			bson.D{{Key: "$set", Value: set}},
168		)
169		if err != nil {
170			return false, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("transition settlement batch: %w", err))
171		}
172		return res.MatchedCount > 0, nil
173	}
174	
175	// claimExecution atomically claims a batch for execution. Three legal claims:
176	//   - APPROVED  → EXECUTING (first run)
177	//   - FAILED    → EXECUTING (re-execution after a recorded failure)
178	//   - EXECUTING → EXECUTING with a STALE lease (resume of a run whose process
179	//     died before it could mark FAILED; staleBefore guards against stealing a
180	//     live executor's batch)
181	//
182	// Every claim stamps executing_at as the new lease. Returns false when no
183	// claim matched — someone else holds a fresh lease or the batch is terminal.
184	func (rp *repo) claimExecution(ctx context.Context, id primitive.ObjectID, now, staleBefore time.Time) (bool, error) {
185		for _, from := range []string{domain.SettlementStatusApproved, domain.SettlementStatusFailed} {
186			ok, err := rp.transitionBatch(ctx, id, from, bson.D{
187				{Key: "status", Value: domain.SettlementStatusExecuting},
188				{Key: "executing_at", Value: now},
189			})
190			if err != nil || ok {
191				return ok, err
192			}
193		}
194		res, err := rp.batches.UpdateOne(ctx,
195			bson.D{
196				{Key: "_id", Value: id},
197				{Key: "status", Value: domain.SettlementStatusExecuting},
198				{Key: "executing_at", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$lt", Value: staleBefore}}},
199			},
200			bson.D{{Key: "$set", Value: bson.D{{Key: "executing_at", Value: now}}}},
201		)
202		if err != nil {
203			return false, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("claim settlement execution: %w", err))
204		}
205		return res.MatchedCount > 0, nil
206	}
207	
208	// markExecutionFailed best-effort flips EXECUTING→FAILED with the reason so a
209	// mid-execution error leaves a re-executable batch, never a stuck one.
210	func (rp *repo) markExecutionFailed(ctx context.Context, id primitive.ObjectID, reason string) error {
211		_, err := rp.batches.UpdateOne(ctx,
212			bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: id}, {Key: "status", Value: domain.SettlementStatusExecuting}},
213			bson.D{{Key: "$set", Value: bson.D{
214				{Key: "status", Value: domain.SettlementStatusFailed},
215				{Key: "fail_reason", Value: reason},
216			}}},
217		)
218		if err != nil {
219			return httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("mark settlement execution failed: %w", err))
220		}
221		return nil
222	}

411	// transitionDBT performs a status-guarded DBT update; false = lost the race
412	// or the request already left fromStatus.
413	func (rp *repo) transitionDBT(ctx context.Context, id primitive.ObjectID, fromStatus, toStatus string, creditedAt *time.Time) (bool, error) {
414		set := bson.D{{Key: "status", Value: toStatus}}
415		if creditedAt != nil {
416			set = append(set, bson.E{Key: "credited_at", Value: creditedAt})
417		}
418		res, err := rp.dbt.UpdateOne(ctx,
419			bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: id}, {Key: "status", Value: fromStatus}},
420			bson.D{{Key: "$set", Value: set}},
421		)
422		if err != nil {
423			return false, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("transition dbt request: %w", err))
424		}
425		return res.MatchedCount > 0, nil
426	}

11	// Payment Aggregator *executes*. Money never moves autonomously.

25	// authorised signatory).
26	type SettlementBatch struct {

1	package cattle

3	import (
4		"context"

9		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson"

17	)
18	
19	// repository is the module's only MongoDB touchpoint. It maps driver errors
20	// to httpx errors (mongo.ErrNoDocuments → NotFound, duplicate key → Conflict)
21	// so the service layer stays driver-free. Unexpected driver errors are wrapped
22	// with the failing operation so ERROR logs upstream name the op.
23	type repository struct {
24		animals   *mongo.Collection
25		health    *mongo.Collection
26		mvuCases  *mongo.Collection
27		education *mongo.Collection
28	}
29	
30	// newRepository binds the repository to the module's collections.
31	func newRepository(db *mongo.Database) *repository {
32		return &repository{
33			animals:   db.Collection(mongodb.CollAnimals),
34			health:    db.Collection(mongodb.CollHealthEvents),
35			mvuCases:  db.Collection(mongodb.CollMVUCases),
36			education: db.Collection(mongodb.CollEducation),
37		}
38	}
39	
40	// InsertAnimal persists a new animal. The unique index on pashu_aadhaar
41	// (mongodb.EnsureIndexes) turns a duplicate registration into ANIMAL_EXISTS.
42	func (r *repository) InsertAnimal(ctx context.Context, a *domain.Animal) error {
43		if _, err := r.animals.InsertOne(ctx, a); err != nil {
44			if mongo.IsDuplicateKeyError(err) {
45				return httpx.Conflict("ANIMAL_EXISTS", "an animal with this pashu_aadhaar is already registered")
46			}
47			return httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("insert animal: %w", err))
48		}
49		return nil
50	}
51	
52	// FindAnimalByID loads one animal or returns NotFound.
53	func (r *repository) FindAnimalByID(ctx context.Context, id primitive.ObjectID) (*domain.Animal, error) {
54		var a domain.Animal
55		err := r.animals.FindOne(ctx, bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: id}}).Decode(&a)
56		if errors.Is(err, mongo.ErrNoDocuments) {
57			return nil, httpx.NotFound("animal")
58		}
59		if err != nil {
60			return nil, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("find animal %s: %w", id.Hex(), err))
61		}
62		return &a, nil
63	}
64	
65	// ListAnimals returns a page of animals filtered by owner and/or DCS (zero
66	// ObjectID = no filter), newest first, plus the total match count.
67	func (r *repository) ListAnimals(ctx context.Context, ownerPartyID, dcsID primitive.ObjectID, page httpx.Page) ([]domain.Animal, int64, error) {
68		filter := bson.D{}
69		if !ownerPartyID.IsZero() {
70			filter = append(filter, bson.E{Key: "owner_party_id", Value: ownerPartyID})
71		}
72		if !dcsID.IsZero() {
73			filter = append(filter, bson.E{Key: "dcs_id", Value: dcsID})
74		}
75		total, err := r.animals.CountDocuments(ctx, filter)
76		if err != nil {
77			return nil, 0, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("count animals: %w", err))
78		}
79		cur, err := r.animals.Find(ctx, filter, options.Find().
80			SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "created_at", Value: -1}}).
81			SetSkip(page.Offset).SetLimit(page.Limit))
82		if err != nil {
83			return nil, 0, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("list animals: %w", err))
84		}
85		out := []domain.Animal{}
86		if err := cur.All(ctx, &out); err != nil {
87			return nil, 0, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("decode animals: %w", err))
88		}
89		return out, total, nil
90	}
91	
92	// InsertHealthEvent appends one entry to an animal's health history.
93	func (r *repository) InsertHealthEvent(ctx context.Context, e *domain.HealthEvent) error {
94		if _, err := r.health.InsertOne(ctx, e); err != nil {
95			return httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("insert health event: %w", err))
96		}
97		return nil
98	}
99	
100	// ListHealthEventsByAnimal returns a page of an animal's health history,
101	// most recent occurrence first, plus the total count.
102	func (r *repository) ListHealthEventsByAnimal(ctx context.Context, animalID primitive.ObjectID, page httpx.Page) ([]domain.HealthEvent, int64, error) {
103		filter := bson.D{{Key: "animal_id", Value: animalID}}
104		total, err := r.health.CountDocuments(ctx, filter)
105		if err != nil {
106			return nil, 0, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("count health events: %w", err))
107		}
108		cur, err := r.health.Find(ctx, filter, options.Find().
109			SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "occurred_at", Value: -1}}).
110			SetSkip(page.Offset).SetLimit(page.Limit))
111		if err != nil {
112			return nil, 0, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("list health events: %w", err))
113		}
114		out := []domain.HealthEvent{}
115		if err := cur.All(ctx, &out); err != nil {
116			return nil, 0, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("decode health events: %w", err))
117		}
118		return out, total, nil
119	}
120	
121	// MarkPendingHealthEventsSynced flips every PENDING event of one animal to
122	// SYNCED with the given Bharat Pashudhan reference, returning how many synced.
123	func (r *repository) MarkPendingHealthEventsSynced(ctx context.Context, animalID primitive.ObjectID, bpSyncRef string) (int64, error) {
124		res, err := r.health.UpdateMany(ctx,
125			bson.D{
126				{Key: "animal_id", Value: animalID},
127				{Key: "bp_sync_status", Value: domain.BPSyncPending},
128			},
129			bson.D{{Key: "$set", Value: bson.D{
130				{Key: "bp_sync_status", Value: domain.BPSyncSynced},
131				{Key: "bp_sync_ref", Value: bpSyncRef},
132			}}})
133		if err != nil {
134			return 0, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("mark health events synced: %w", err))
135		}
136		return res.ModifiedCount, nil
137	}
138	
139	// InsertMVUCase persists a new MVU case.
140	func (r *repository) InsertMVUCase(ctx context.Context, c *domain.MVUCase) error {
141		if _, err := r.mvuCases.InsertOne(ctx, c); err != nil {
142			return httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("insert mvu case: %w", err))
143		}
144		return nil
145	}
146	
147	// FindMVUCaseByID loads one MVU case or returns NotFound.
148	func (r *repository) FindMVUCaseByID(ctx context.Context, id primitive.ObjectID) (*domain.MVUCase, error) {
149		var c domain.MVUCase
150		err := r.mvuCases.FindOne(ctx, bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: id}}).Decode(&c)
151		if errors.Is(err, mongo.ErrNoDocuments) {
152			return nil, httpx.NotFound("MVU case")
153		}
154		if err != nil {
155			return nil, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("find mvu case %s: %w", id.Hex(), err))
156		}
157		return &c, nil
158	}
159	
160	// DispatchMVUCase moves a case REQUESTED → DISPATCHED, recording the vet
161	// and/or driver. The status guard in the filter is the optimistic lock (no
162	// transactions on a standalone server): a false return means the case was
163	// not in REQUESTED state — e.g. a concurrent dispatch won the race.
164	func (r *repository) DispatchMVUCase(ctx context.Context, id primitive.ObjectID, vetPartyID, driverPartyID *primitive.ObjectID) (bool, error) {
165		set := bson.D{{Key: "status", Value: domain.MVUCaseDispatched}}
166		if vetPartyID != nil {
167			set = append(set, bson.E{Key: "vet_party_id", Value: *vetPartyID})
168		}
169		if driverPartyID != nil {
170			set = append(set, bson.E{Key: "driver_party_id", Value: *driverPartyID})
171		}
172		res, err := r.mvuCases.UpdateOne(ctx,
173			bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: id}, {Key: "status", Value: domain.MVUCaseRequested}},
174			bson.D{{Key: "$set", Value: set}})
175		if err != nil {
176			return false, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("dispatch mvu case %s: %w", id.Hex(), err))
177		}
178		return res.MatchedCount == 1, nil
179	}
180	
181	// CloseMVUCase moves a DISPATCHED (or ARRIVED) case to CLOSED with the visit
182	// log. Same optimistic status-guard pattern as DispatchMVUCase.
183	func (r *repository) CloseMVUCase(ctx context.Context, id primitive.ObjectID, visitNotes string, healthEventIDs []primitive.ObjectID, closedAt time.Time) (bool, error) {
184		set := bson.D{
185			{Key: "status", Value: domain.MVUCaseClosed},
186			{Key: "visit_notes", Value: visitNotes},
187			{Key: "closed_at", Value: closedAt},
188		}
189		if len(healthEventIDs) > 0 {
190			set = append(set, bson.E{Key: "health_event_ids", Value: healthEventIDs})
191		}
192		res, err := r.mvuCases.UpdateOne(ctx,
193			bson.D{
194				{Key: "_id", Value: id},
195				{Key: "status", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$in", Value: []string{
196					domain.MVUCaseDispatched, domain.MVUCaseArrived,
197				}}}},
198			},
199			bson.D{{Key: "$set", Value: set}})
200		if err != nil {
201			return false, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("close mvu case %s: %w", id.Hex(), err))
202		}
203		return res.MatchedCount == 1, nil
204	}
205

11	const (

13		BMCLotStatusQCPending  = "QC_PENDING" // closed, awaiting rapid tests
14		BMCLotStatusPassed     = "PASSED"     // rapid tests within limits
15		BMCLotStatusBlocked    = "BLOCKED"    // failed — quarantined, cannot advance
16		BMCLotStatusDispatched = "DISPATCHED" // tankered to plant

20	// BMCLot pools consignments delivered to one bulk-milk-cooler for a date+shift.
21	type BMCLot struct {
22		ID                  primitive.ObjectID   `bson:"_id,omitempty" json:"id"`
23		BMCID               primitive.ObjectID   `bson:"bmc_id"  json:"bmc_id"`

29		ChillingTempC       float64              `bson:"chilling_temp_c,omitempty" json:"chilling_temp_c,omitempty"`
30		Status              string               `bson:"status"  json:"status"`
31		// BatchID stamps the processing batch that pooled (consumed) this lot —
32		// set atomically by the DISPATCHED→POOLED claim so one lot can never feed
33		// two batches.
34		BatchID       *primitive.ObjectID  `bson:"batch_id,omitempty" json:"batch_id,omitempty"`
35		QCResultIDs   []primitive.ObjectID `bson:"qc_result_ids,omitempty" json:"qc_result_ids,omitempty"`
36		BlockReason   string               `bson:"block_reason,omitempty"  json:"block_reason,omitempty"`

// ListDBT pages DBT requests. A FARMER token is always forced to its own
// party.
func (s *service) ListDBT(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, farmerPartyID, status string, page httpx.Page) ([]domain.DBTRequest, int64, error) {
	if actor.RoleCode == domain.RoleFarmer {
		farmerPartyID = actor.PartyID
	}
	filter := bson.D{}
	if farmerPartyID != "" {
		farmerOID, err := httpx.ParseID(farmerPartyID, "farmer_party_id")
		if err != nil {
			return nil, 0, err
		}
		filter = append(filter, bson.E{Key: "farmer_party_id", Value: farmerOID})
	}
	if status != "" {
		filter = append(filter, bson.E{Key: "status", Value: status})
	}
	return s.repo.listDBT(ctx, filter, page)
}

<tool-use data-tool-type="read" data-tool-name="Read"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Read**</summary>
 `./docs/strict_brief.md`

```text
1	# Saathi Backend — Strict Brief (How Every API Works)
2	
3	> **Purpose.** This is the single source of truth for *how the backend is built and how each API
4	> behaves* — the contract a frontend engineer, a new backend dev, or an LLM needs to integrate
5	> without reading every file. It is generated from the actual routes in `internal/modules/*/module.go`
6	> and kept in lockstep with the code.
7	>
8	> **Scope reminder:** backend only. The frontend is a separate repo. Consumer commerce is
9	> descoped (only the public QR scan is consumer-facing). Every route below is live and covered by
10	> `scripts/smoke.sh` (21-step E2E).
11	
12	---
13	
14	## 1. Ground rules that apply to EVERY endpoint
15	
16	### 1.1 Identifiers — ObjectID everywhere, business keys are separate
17	- Every document's `_id` is a **MongoDB ObjectID** (24-hex string in JSON, e.g. `6a4b607236c46b14a294ec4d`).
18	- **Every cross-collection reference stores the ObjectID**, never a name or code:
19	  `farmer_party_id`, `dcs_id`, `org_unit_id`, `batch_id`, `settlement_batch_id`, … This is what
20	  makes `$lookup` / populate trivial and mapping unambiguous.
21	- **Human-readable business keys are separate, unique-indexed fields** — used for display and
22	  lookup, never for joins: org `code` (`DCS-01842`), party `phone`, `invoice_number`,
23	  `batch_number`, `qr_code`, `pashu_aadhaar`.
24	- **One deliberate exception:** `milk_pours.client_event_id` is a **string** minted on the device
25	  (offline-first idempotency key, blueprint §3.1) — the server still assigns a proper ObjectID `_id`.
26	- In JWTs and query params, ObjectIDs travel as hex strings and are parsed server-side via
27	  `httpx.ParseID` / `httpx.PathID`. A malformed id → `400 INVALID_ID`.
28	
29	### 1.2 Response envelope (uniform)
30	Success:
31	```json
32	{ "data": { ... }, "meta": { "limit": 50, "offset": 0, "total": 137 } }   // meta only on list endpoints
33	```
34	Error:
35	```json
36	{ "error": { "code": "SAFETY_GATE_BLOCKED", "message": "human readable", "details": {...}? } }
37	```
38	`code` is a stable machine string the frontend switches on. `500`s are opaque (`INTERNAL`) — the
39	real cause is logged server-side, never leaked.
40	
41	### 1.3 Auth — two token kinds
42	1. `SESSION` token — proves "this phone logged in". Enough for identity/profile endpoints.
43	2. `ROLE` token — a session that has **selected one role**; carries `role_code` + `org_unit_id` +
44	   `org_type`. **Required for every business action.** Obtain via `POST /auth/role/select`.
45	
46	Middleware chain per route group:
47	`Authenticate` (verifies JWT → puts `Actor` on context) → `RequireRoles(...)` or `RequireSession`
48	→ handler → (mutations) `AuditMutations` writes the audit trail. **`SUPER_ADMIN` passes every
49	`RequireRoles` gate** (and every such call is audited).
50	
51	### 1.4 Org scoping (multi-tenant safety)
52	Before touching a resource that belongs to an org unit, the service calls
53	`d.Orgs.RequireInScope(actor, targetOrgID)`. Passes when the actor's org == target, or the
54	actor's org is an **ancestor** in the target's denormalized `path[]` (O(1), no tree walk).
55	`SUPER_ADMIN` and `STATE_AUDITOR` are federation-wide. Failure → `403 FORBIDDEN`.
56	
57	### 1.5 Provenance (append-only, hash-chained)
58	State-changing steps in the milk→QR chain append an immutable event to `provenance_events`
59	(SHA-256 chained on the previous hash). Corrections never mutate — they append a new event with a
60	`supersedes` ref. This is what the public QR scan re-verifies (`ledger.intact`).
61	
62	### 1.6 Logging & error handling (debugging backbone)
63	- **One structured log line per request** (global middleware): `method, path, status, duration_ms,
64	  request_id, ip, actor_party_id, actor_role`. `4xx → WARN`, `5xx → ERROR`.
65	- **Inside each module** (tagged `module=<name>`, correlatable by `request_id`):
66	  `INFO` on every creation/state transition, `WARN` on every business rejection (gate block,
67	  dual-control violation, scope denial, idempotent replay, 409s), `ERROR` with the wrapped cause
68	  before any `500`. Repo errors are wrapped with the operation name (`fmt.Errorf("insert pour: %w")`).
69	
70	### 1.7 Pagination
71	List endpoints accept `?limit=` (default 50, max 200) & `?offset=`, and return `meta.total`.
72	
73	### 1.8 Concurrency & duplicate prevention (how "only one wins")
74	Every "two actors at once → only one completes" case is enforced by a **MongoDB atomic
75	status-guarded update** — the state check lives *inside* the update filter
76	(`update where _id=X AND status=EXPECTED`), so exactly one writer matches and the rest get a
77	`409`. This is used for KYC approve/reject, settlement `execute` (with a resume lease), and the
78	BMC-lot→batch claim (`DISPATCHED → POOLED`, so one lot can never feed two batches). **No Redis
79	lock is used for this** — a single-document atomic update is strictly safer than an external lock
80	(one source of truth, no lock-vs-DB drift, no TTL failure modes). Offline pour ingest dedupes the
81	same way via the unique `client_event_id`.
82	
83	### 1.9 Real-time (live dashboards)
84	`GET /api/v1/events/stream` is a **Server-Sent Events** stream (any authenticated party). The
85	server pushes typed events down the open connection so an already-open dashboard updates without a
86	refresh — e.g. `kyc.pending.changed` nudges reviewer dashboards to re-fetch their scoped
87	`/kyc/pending/count` badge. The nudge is never trusted as the value; the client re-queries the
88	authoritative scoped count (so it can never drift). Single-instance today; at multi-replica scale
89	the cross-node fan-out swaps to Redis pub/sub with no route changes.
90	
91	### 1.10 Rate limiting (single-instance vs replicas)
92	Per-IP token bucket. **In-process by default** (each replica limits what it sees). Set `REDIS_URL`
93	and it switches to a **shared Redis token bucket** (atomic Lua) for global fairness across
94	replicas — fails *open* on a Redis outage so the limiter can never take down the API. Over-limit →
95	`429 RATE_LIMITED`.
96	
97	---
98	
99	## 2. Layered architecture (how a request flows through the code)
100	
101	```
102	HTTP request
103	  → router (internal/httpapi)         global middleware: request-id, metrics, request-log, rate-limit, recover
104	  → module.go                         mounts routes + auth/RBAC; wires handler→service→repo; subscribes to bus
105	  → handler.go                        HTTP ONLY: decode (httpx.DecodeJSON), parse ids, call service, write envelope
106	  → service.go                        ALL business logic: validation, RBAC/scope, gates, provenance, bus, logging
107	  → repo.go                           ALL MongoDB access: collection consts, ObjectID filters, no business logic
108	  → models.go                         request/response DTOs for the module
109	```
110	Modules never import each other. Cross-module effects go through the **in-process event bus**
111	(`eventbus`), which is the seam that becomes Kafka/NATS when this splits into microservices.
112	Shared services arrive via one `deps.Deps` container: `Cfg, Log, DB, JWT, Ledger, Audit, Flags, Orgs, Bus`.
113	
114	---
115	
116	## 3. The 10 modules & every endpoint
117	
118	> Legend — **Auth**: `public` (none) · `session` · `role:X,Y` (needs a role token with one of those
119	> roles; `SUPER_ADMIN` always allowed). Paths are under `/api/v1` unless marked public.

121	### 3.1 `identity` — auth, parties, KYC approval, role grants
122	The heart of "one phone = one Party = many roles" + the KYC approval workflow.
123	
124	| Method | Path | Auth | What it does |
125	|---|---|---|---|
126	| POST | `/auth/otp/request` | public | Sends 6-digit OTP (stored HMAC-hashed, 5-min TTL, max 5 attempts). Dev mode returns `dev_otp`. |
127	| POST | `/auth/otp/verify` | public | Verifies OTP → find-or-create Party (tier `MINIMAL`) → returns `session` token + rotating refresh token. |
128	| POST | `/auth/refresh` | public | Rotates refresh token → new session token. |
129	| POST | `/auth/logout` | session | Deletes the refresh token. |
130	| GET | `/auth/roles` | session | Lists my usable role assignments, each enriched with org `{id, code, name, type}`. **This is what the frontend reads to know which dashboard(s) to offer.** |
131	| POST | `/auth/role/select` | session | Body `{role_assignment_id}`. Checks it's mine + usable + my KYC tier satisfies the role's `RequiredKYCTier` (else `403 KYC_TIER_INSUFFICIENT`). Returns a `role` token. **This is the role switcher.** |
132	| GET | `/parties/me` | session | My party + active assignments + KYC summary (masked). |
133	| PATCH | `/parties/me` | session | Update `full_name` / `preferred_language`. |
134	| POST | `/kyc/aadhaar` | session | Body `{aadhaar_number, consent:true, requested_tier}`. Stores **only last-4 + a vault ref** (never the number). Creates a **PENDING** KYC record. **No auto-approval.** |
135	| POST | `/kyc/bank` | session | Mock penny-drop; attaches masked bank details to a PENDING record. |
136	| GET | `/kyc/me` | session | My KYC records (masked; vault ref never serialized). |
137	| GET | `/kyc/pending` | role:`ORGANISING_MANAGER, DISTRICT_VERIFIER, PCDF_ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN` | Pending records **within the reviewer's org scope**, enriched with party `{phone, name, tier}`. Audited. |
138	| GET | `/kyc/pending/count` | role:(same) | Live badge value — scoped count of pending KYC. The dashboard renders this and re-fetches it on each SSE `kyc.pending.changed` nudge. Returns `{count, capped}`. |
139	| POST | `/kyc/{id}/approve` | role:(same) | Verifies scope + **not self-review** + `CanApproveKYCTier(role, tier)`; sets `VERIFIED` via an **atomic status-guarded update** (two simultaneous approvals → exactly one wins, the other gets `409 KYC_NOT_PENDING`), **upgrades party tier upward only**, notifies the party. Audited. |
140	| POST | `/kyc/{id}/reject` | role:(same) | `{reason}` → `REJECTED` + reason, notifies party. Audited. |
141	| POST | `/roles/assignments` | role:`SUPER_ADMIN, PCDF_ADMIN, UNION_PRESIDENT, SAMITI_ADHYAKSH, ORGANISING_MANAGER` | Grants a role at an org unit (this is **"deciding a user's position"**). Scope-checked; grant matrix limits who can grant what. Audited (`role.grant`). |
142	| DELETE | `/roles/assignments/{id}` | role:(same) | Revokes (status → `REVOKED`, never deleted). Audited (`role.revoke`). |
143	| GET | `/roles/assignments` | role:(same) | Lists assignments at an org (scope-checked, paged). |
144	
145	**The position/onboarding flow (exact):** login → `POST /kyc/aadhaar` (PENDING) → reviewer
146	`POST /kyc/{id}/approve` (tier upgraded) → an admin `POST /roles/assignments` to set the position
147	(e.g. `SAMITI_SACHEEV @ DCS-01842`) → user logs in, `GET /auth/roles` shows it, `POST /auth/role/select`
148	issues the role token whose `role_code` tells the frontend which UI to render.

271	make seed                 # org tree + one party per role (prints their ObjectIDs)
272	make run                  # API on :8080

274	```

276	sacheev `9000000001`, adhyaksh `9000000002`, farmer `9000000011`, van-rider `9000000021`,
277	bmc-op `9000000031`, plant-op `9000000041`, lab `9000000042`, **org-manager `9000000071`**.

281	## 5. Error codes the frontend should handle
282	
283	| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
284	|---|---|---|
285	| `UNAUTHORIZED` / `FORBIDDEN` | 401 / 403 | No/invalid token · role or scope denied |
286	| `KYC_TIER_INSUFFICIENT` | 403 | Role selected before KYC approved to the required tier |
287	| `KYC_NOT_PENDING` / `KYC_SELF_REVIEW` / `KYC_TIER_NOT_APPROVABLE` | 409 / 403 | KYC approval guardrails |
288	| `SAFETY_GATE_BLOCKED` | 422 | A blocked (failed-QC) lot/batch cannot advance |
289	| `DUAL_CONTROL_VIOLATION` | 403 | Settlement approver == initiator |
290	| `IMPLAUSIBLE_VALUES` | 422 | Pour fat/SNF/qty outside physical bounds |
291	| `FARMER_NOT_MEMBER` | 422 | Pour for a farmer not assigned to that DCS |
292	| `INVALID_ID` | 400 | Malformed ObjectID |
293	| `FEATURE_DISABLED` | 403 | Capability-gated (dormant) endpoint |
294	| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | Per-IP throttle |
295	| `NOT_FOUND` / `CONFLICT` / `MALFORMED_JSON` | 404 / 409 / 400 | Standard |

300	
301	**Real:** auth, RBAC, org scoping, KYC approval workflow, pricing, idempotent ingest, the safety

305	**Mocked (single named seams — swap without touching the flow):** Aadhaar eKYC, bank penny-drop,

308	**Dormant (flag-gated OFF):** collar telemetry, ONDC, consumer commerce.

// Invoice statuses through the same-day payment loop (blueprint §8.1).
const (
	InvoiceStatusIssued            = "ISSUED"
	InvoiceStatusSettlementPending = "SETTLEMENT_PENDING"
	InvoiceStatusPaid              = "PAID"
	InvoiceStatusHold              = "HOLD" // e.g. safety-gate payment hold
)

// Invoice aggregates one farmer's pours at one DCS for one day — the artefact
// behind "same-day farmer payment". InvoiceNumber is the human-readable
// unique business key; relations use ObjectIDs.
type Invoice struct {
	ID                  primitive.ObjectID   `bson:"_id,omitempty" json:"id"`
	InvoiceNumber       string               `bson:"invoice_number" json:"invoice_number"` // unique, e.g. INV-DCS01842-20260706-0001
	FarmerPartyID       primitive.ObjectID   `bson:"farmer_party_id" json:"farmer_party_id"`
	DCSID               primitive.ObjectID   `bson:"dcs_id"        json:"dcs_id"`
	InvoiceDate         string               `bson:"invoice_date"  json:"invoice_date"` // YYYY-MM-DD
	PourIDs             []primitive.ObjectID `bson:"pour_ids"      json:"pour_ids"`
	TotalQuantityLitres float64              `bson:"total_quantity_litres" json:"total_quantity_litres"`
	TotalAmount         float64              `bson:"total_amount"  json:"total_amount"`
	Status              string               `bson:"status"        json:"status"`
	SettlementBatchID   *primitive.ObjectID  `bson:"settlement_batch_id,omitempty" json:"settlement_batch_id,omitempty"`
	IssuedAt            time.Time            `bson:"issued_at"     json:"issued_at"`
	ProvenanceSeq       int64                `bson:"provenance_seq,omitempty" json:"provenance_seq,omitempty"`
}

// DateKeyIST formats t as the YYYY-MM-DD settlement-day key in IST.

873	func (s *service) GenerateInvoices(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, req GenerateInvoicesRequest) (*GenerateInvoicesResponse, error) {
874		if req.DCSID.IsZero() {
875			return nil, httpx.BadRequest("VALIDATION", "dcs_id is required")
876		}
877		now := time.Now().UTC()
878		dateKey := req.Date
879		if dateKey == "" {
880			dateKey = domain.DateKeyIST(now)
881		} else if err := validateDateKey(dateKey); err != nil {
882			return nil, err
883		}
884		dcs, err := s.d.Orgs.Get(ctx, req.DCSID)
885		if err != nil {
886			return nil, err
887		}
888		if dcs.Type != domain.OrgTypeDCS {
889			return nil, httpx.BadRequest("NOT_A_DCS", "org unit "+req.DCSID.Hex()+" is not a DCS")
890		}
891		if err := s.requireInScope(ctx, actor, req.DCSID, "generate invoices"); err != nil {
892			return nil, err
893		}
894	
895		pours, err := s.repo.recordedPoursForDay(ctx, req.DCSID, dateKey)
896		if err != nil {
897			return nil, err
898		}
899		alreadyInvoiced, err := s.repo.invoicedPourIDs(ctx, req.DCSID, dateKey)
900		if err != nil {
901			return nil, err
902		}
903	
904		byFarmer := make(map[primitive.ObjectID][]domain.MilkPour)
905		for _, p := range pours {
906			if alreadyInvoiced[p.ID] {
907				continue
908			}
909			byFarmer[p.FarmerPartyID] = append(byFarmer[p.FarmerPartyID], p)
910		}
911		farmerIDs := make([]primitive.ObjectID, 0, len(byFarmer))
912		for id := range byFarmer {
913			farmerIDs = append(farmerIDs, id)
914		}
915		sort.Slice(farmerIDs, func(i, j int) bool { return farmerIDs[i].Hex() < farmerIDs[j].Hex() })
916	
917		resp := &GenerateInvoicesResponse{Invoices: []domain.Invoice{}}
918		// Counter keys stay strings and keep using the org CODE — internal only.
919		counterKey := "invoice:" + dcs.Code + ":" + dateKey
920		for _, farmerID := range farmerIDs {
921			group := byFarmer[farmerID]
922			seq, err := s.repo.nextInvoiceSeq(ctx, counterKey)
923			if err != nil {
924				return nil, err
925			}
926			inv := &domain.Invoice{
927				ID:            primitive.NewObjectID(),
928				InvoiceNumber: domain.InvoiceNumberFor(dcs.Code, dateKey, seq),
929				FarmerPartyID: farmerID,
930				DCSID:         req.DCSID,
931				InvoiceDate:   dateKey,
932				Status:        domain.InvoiceStatusIssued,
933				IssuedAt:      now,
934			}
935			for _, p := range group {
936				inv.PourIDs = append(inv.PourIDs, p.ID)
937				inv.TotalQuantityLitres += p.QuantityLitres
938				inv.TotalAmount += p.Amount
939			}
940			inv.TotalQuantityLitres = math.Round(inv.TotalQuantityLitres*100) / 100
941			inv.TotalAmount = math.Round(inv.TotalAmount*100) / 100
942	
943			duplicate, err := s.repo.insertInvoice(ctx, inv)
944			if err != nil {
945				return nil, err
946			}
947			if duplicate {
948				// The farmer already has today's invoice (e.g. the MORNING run) —
949				// merge the not-yet-invoiced pours into it instead of silently
950				// dropping them, or surface them when the invoice is frozen.
951				if err := s.mergeIntoExistingInvoice(ctx, actor, req.DCSID, dateKey, farmerID, group, resp); err != nil {
952					return nil, err
953				}
954				continue
955			}
956	
957			refs := make([]provenance.Ref, 0, len(inv.PourIDs))
958			for _, pid := range inv.PourIDs {
959				refs = append(refs, provenance.Ref{EntityType: domain.EntityMilkPour, EntityID: pid.Hex(), Relation: "aggregates"})
960			}

962				Type:       domain.EventInvoiceIssued,
963				EntityType: domain.EntityInvoice,
964				EntityID:   inv.ID.Hex(),
965				Refs:       refs,
966				Actor:      provenance.ActorRef{PartyID: actor.PartyID, RoleCode: actor.RoleCode},
967				OrgUnitID:  inv.DCSID.Hex(),

      inv.status = 'SETTLED';
      inv.settledAt = new Date().toISOString();
      inv.utr = `UTR${todayISO().slice(2).replaceAll('-', '')}${inv.id.slice(-4).toUpperCase()}`;

        if (pour) pour.status = 'PAID';

import AsyncStorage from '@react-native-async-storage/async-storage';
import type { MockDb } from '@/core/mocks/db';

/**
 * API transport layer, aligned with the real Go backend (parag-saathi-be):
 *   - success envelope  { "data": ..., "meta"?: ... }
 *   - error envelope    { "error": { "code", "message", "details"? } }
 *   - bearer auth with a SESSION/ROLE access token + rotating refresh token
 *     (POST /auth/refresh) - a 401 triggers one single-flight refresh + retry
 *
 * Every endpoint in src/core/api/endpoints/ is declared once with:
 *   - its HTTP method + path        → the contract the backend implements
 *   - optional mapRequest/mapResponse → snake_case wire ⇄ camelCase domain
 *   - a mock implementation         → runs fully in-app against the seeded
 *                                     mock DB until the backend is connected
 *
 * Switch modes with EXPO_PUBLIC_API_MODE (mock | http) - see .env.example and
 * docs/api-contract.md. No feature code changes when the backend lands.
 */

export type ApiMode = 'mock' | 'http';

// Authentic by default: the app talks to the real Saathi backend. `mock` is an
// explicit offline-development fallback only (never the shipped experience).
const MODE: ApiMode = (process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_API_MODE as ApiMode) || 'http';
const BASE: string = process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL || 'http://localhost:8080/api/v1';

/** The active API mode ('http' = real backend, 'mock' = in-app fixtures). */
export const API_MODE: ApiMode = MODE;
/** The Saathi backend base URL every endpoint is resolved against. */
export const API_BASE_URL: string = BASE;

const ACCESS_KEY = 'saathi-access-token';
const REFRESH_KEY = 'saathi-refresh-token';

/** In-memory token cache, persisted to AsyncStorage (hydrated at app start). */
let accessToken: string | null = null;
let refreshToken: string | null = null;

export function getAuthToken(): string | null {
  return accessToken;
}
export function getRefreshToken(): string | null {
  return refreshToken;
}

/** Store both tokens (login / refresh rotation). */
export function setTokens(t: { access: string | null; refresh: string | null }): void {
  accessToken = t.access;
  refreshToken = t.refresh;
  if (t.access) void AsyncStorage.setItem(ACCESS_KEY, t.access);
  else void AsyncStorage.removeItem(ACCESS_KEY);
  if (t.refresh) void AsyncStorage.setItem(REFRESH_KEY, t.refresh);
  else void AsyncStorage.removeItem(REFRESH_KEY);
}

/** Swap only the access token (role-select issues a ROLE-kind token). */
export function setAccessToken(token: string): void {
  accessToken = token;
  void AsyncStorage.setItem(ACCESS_KEY, token);
}

export function clearTokens(): void {
  setTokens({ access: null, refresh: null });
}

/** Call once at startup (root layout) before authenticated requests. */
export async function hydrateAuthToken(): Promise<void> {
  const [a, r] = await Promise.all([
    AsyncStorage.getItem(ACCESS_KEY),
    AsyncStorage.getItem(REFRESH_KEY),
  ]);
  accessToken = a;
  refreshToken = r;
}

/** Registered by the root layout: fired when auth is irrecoverably lost. */
let onUnauthorized: (() => void) | null = null;
export function setOnUnauthorized(cb: (() => void) | null): void {
  onUnauthorized = cb;
}

export class ApiError extends Error {
  constructor(
    public status: number,
    public code: string,
    message: string,
    public details?: unknown,
  ) {
    super(message);
    this.name = 'ApiError';
  }
}

type HttpMethod = 'GET' | 'POST' | 'PUT' | 'PATCH' | 'DELETE';

export interface EndpointSpec<TIn, TOut> {
  method: HttpMethod;
  /** REST path for http mode; also documents the backend contract */
  path: (input: TIn) => string;
  /** camelCase input → snake_case wire body (http mode only) */
  mapRequest?: (input: TIn) => unknown;
  /** snake_case wire data → domain shape (http mode only) */
  mapResponse?: (raw: unknown) => TOut;
  /** In-app implementation for mock mode */
  mock: (input: TIn, db: MockDb) => TOut | Promise<TOut>;
}

function sleep(ms: number): Promise<void> {
  return new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));
}

/** JSON-safe deep clone (results are plain data; keeps Hermes compatibility). */
function deepClone<T>(value: T): T {
  return value === undefined ? value : (JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value)) as T);
}

/** Raw http call: bearer header, envelope unwrap, AppError mapping. */
async function httpCall(method: HttpMethod, path: string, body: unknown): Promise<unknown> {
  const hasBody = method !== 'GET' && method !== 'DELETE' && body !== undefined;
```

398	// CreateMVUCase opens a 1962 MVU request (§10). The DCS comes from the
399	// farmer's own animal when animal_id is given, else from the actor's org.
400	func (s *service) CreateMVUCase(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, req CreateMVUCaseRequest) (*domain.MVUCase, error) {
401		farmerID, err := actorID(actor)
402		if err != nil {
403			return nil, err
404		}
405		if strings.TrimSpace(req.Symptoms) == "" {
406			return nil, httpx.BadRequest("SYMPTOMS_REQUIRED", "symptoms description is required")
407		}
408	
409		var dcsID primitive.ObjectID
410		if actor.OrgUnitID != "" {
411			dcsID, err = httpx.ParseID(actor.OrgUnitID, "org_unit")
412			if err != nil {
413				return nil, err
414			}
415		}
416		var caseAnimalID *primitive.ObjectID
417		if req.AnimalID != nil && !req.AnimalID.IsZero() {
418			animal, err := s.repo.FindAnimalByID(ctx, *req.AnimalID)
419			if err != nil {
420				return nil, err
421			}
422			if animal.OwnerPartyID != farmerID {

424					slog.String("animal_id", animal.ID.Hex()),
425					slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID))
426				return nil, httpx.Forbidden("you may only raise an MVU case for your own animal")
427			}
428			id := animal.ID
429			caseAnimalID = &id
430			dcsID = animal.DCSID
431		}
432		if dcsID.IsZero() {
433			return nil, httpx.BadRequest("DCS_UNRESOLVED", "cannot resolve a DCS for this case — provide animal_id or use a DCS-scoped role token")
434		}
435	
436		mvuCase := &domain.MVUCase{
437			// Pre-generated so downstream logging/refs share one ID.

441			DCSID:         dcsID,
442			Symptoms:      strings.TrimSpace(req.Symptoms),
443			Status:        domain.MVUCaseRequested,
444			RequestedAt:   time.Now().UTC(),
445		}
446		if err := s.repo.InsertMVUCase(ctx, mvuCase); err != nil {
447			return nil, s.logFailure(ctx, "insert mvu case", err,
448				slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID))
449		}
450		animalHex := ""
451		if mvuCase.AnimalID != nil {
452			animalHex = mvuCase.AnimalID.Hex()
453		}
454		s.log.InfoContext(ctx, "mvu case created",
455			slog.String("case_id", mvuCase.ID.Hex()),
456			slog.String("farmer_party_id", mvuCase.FarmerPartyID.Hex()),
457			slog.String("dcs_id", mvuCase.DCSID.Hex()),
458			slog.String("animal_id", animalHex),
459			slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID))
460		return mvuCase, nil
461	}

463	// DispatchMVUCase moves a case REQUESTED → DISPATCHED, records the assignee
464	// from the caller's role, and publishes eventbus.TopicMVUDispatched with an
465	// explicit payload contract — keys: case_id, farmer_party_id, animal_id,
466	// dcs_id, values ObjectID hex strings (the notifications module reacts, §10).
467	func (s *service) DispatchMVUCase(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, caseID primitive.ObjectID) (*domain.MVUCase, error) {
468		callerID, err := actorID(actor)
469		if err != nil {
470			return nil, err
471		}
472		mvuCase, err := s.repo.FindMVUCaseByID(ctx, caseID)
473		if err != nil {
474			return nil, err
475		}
476		if err := s.d.Orgs.RequireInScope(ctx, actor, mvuCase.DCSID); err != nil {
477			return nil, s.logFailure(ctx, "dispatch mvu case scope check", err,
478				slog.String("case_id", mvuCase.ID.Hex()),
479				slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID))
480		}
481	
482		var vetPartyID, driverPartyID *primitive.ObjectID
483		switch actor.RoleCode {
484		case domain.RoleVeterinarian:
485			vetPartyID = &callerID
486		case domain.RoleMVUDriver:
487			driverPartyID = &callerID
488			// Any other role reaching here is break-glass SUPER_ADMIN: the case
489			// is dispatched without pinning an assignee.
490		}
491	
492		transitioned, err := s.repo.DispatchMVUCase(ctx, mvuCase.ID, vetPartyID, driverPartyID)
493		if err != nil {
494			return nil, s.logFailure(ctx, "dispatch mvu case", err,
495				slog.String("case_id", mvuCase.ID.Hex()))
496		}
497		if !transitioned {
498			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "mvu dispatch rejected: case not in REQUESTED state",
499				slog.String("case_id", mvuCase.ID.Hex()),
500				slog.String("status", mvuCase.Status),
501				slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID))
502			return nil, httpx.Conflict("MVU_NOT_REQUESTED", "MVU case is not in REQUESTED state")
503		}
504	
505		updated, err := s.repo.FindMVUCaseByID(ctx, mvuCase.ID)
506		if err != nil {
507			return nil, s.logFailure(ctx, "reload mvu case", err,
508				slog.String("case_id", mvuCase.ID.Hex()))
509		}
510		// Explicit event shape: the subscriber decodes structurally by JSON key,
511		// so the case ID must travel under "case_id" — publishing the raw domain
512		// document (whose ID marshals as "id") left the farmer SMS caseless.
513		// Values are ObjectID hex strings; a caseless animal travels as "".
514		animalHex := ""
515		if updated.AnimalID != nil {
516			animalHex = updated.AnimalID.Hex()
517		}
518		s.d.Bus.Publish(eventbus.TopicMVUDispatched, map[string]any{
519			"case_id":         updated.ID.Hex(),
520			"farmer_party_id": updated.FarmerPartyID.Hex(),
521			"animal_id":       animalHex,
522			"dcs_id":          updated.DCSID.Hex(),
523		})
524		s.log.InfoContext(ctx, "mvu case dispatched",
525			slog.String("case_id", updated.ID.Hex()),
526			slog.String("farmer_party_id", updated.FarmerPartyID.Hex()),
527			slog.String("dcs_id", updated.DCSID.Hex()),
528			slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID),
529			slog.String("actor_role", actor.RoleCode))
530		return updated, nil
531	}

537		}

540			return nil, err
541		}
542		if err := s.d.Orgs.RequireInScope(ctx, actor, mvuCase.DCSID); err != nil {

553		if !transitioned {
554			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "mvu close rejected: case not DISPATCHED or ARRIVED",
555				slog.String("case_id", mvuCase.ID.Hex()),
556				slog.String("status", mvuCase.Status),
557				slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID))
558			return nil, httpx.Conflict("MVU_NOT_OPEN", "MVU case must be DISPATCHED or ARRIVED to close")
559		}
560		closed, err := s.repo.FindMVUCaseByID(ctx, mvuCase.ID)
561		if err != nil {
562			return nil, s.logFailure(ctx, "reload mvu case", err,
563				slog.String("case_id", mvuCase.ID.Hex()))
564		}
565		s.log.InfoContext(ctx, "mvu case closed",
566			slog.String("case_id", closed.ID.Hex()),
567			slog.String("farmer_party_id", closed.FarmerPartyID.Hex()),
568			slog.Int("health_event_count", len(req.HealthEventIDs)),
569			slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID))
570		return closed, nil

_**Agent - sidechain (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-08 20:21:37Z)**_

Both defects are confirmed by the actual code. This is REAL.

**Defect 1 — Farmer 403 on GET /cattle/mvu-cases (module.go:64-68):**
The POST route is `RequireRoles(domain.RoleFarmer)` (line 64), but the GET route (lines 65-68) is gated to exactly `RoleVeterinarian, RoleMVUDriver, RoleSamitiSacheev, RoleMissionOfficial`. `RoleFarmer` is absent, so a farmer token hits `RequireRoles` and is rejected before reaching the handler. A farmer can create a case but cannot list it back.

**Defect 2 — farmer_party_id is silently dropped:**
- Handler `listMVUCases` (handler.go:195-209) only reads `dcs_id` (line 198) and `status` (line 203). It never reads `farmer_party_id` from the query string.
- `service.ListMVUCases` (service.go:575) has signature `(ctx, actor, dcsID, status, page)` — no farmer param, and it does not pin a farmer to their own party.
- `repo.ListMVUCases` (repo.go:208-215) builds a filter from only `dcs_id` and `status`. No `farmer_party_id` field is ever queried.

So even if the route admitted farmers, there is no code path that scopes results to a single farmer's cases.

**Contrast with the sibling settlement module (confirms the intended contract):**
- Route: settlement/module.go:82-86 — `GET /dbt/requests` includes `domain.RoleFarmer` with the inline comment "forced to own requests in the service."
- Service: `ListDBT` (settlement/service.go:758) takes `farmerPartyID`, forces `farmerPartyID = actor.PartyID` when the actor is a farmer, and appends a `farmer_party_id` filter to the query.

The cattle MVU list is missing exactly this treatment despite the domain document carrying `FarmerPartyID` (populated at creation, service.go:441). There is also no `GET /mvu-cases/{caseID}` fallback route — the only reads are dispatch/close (staff-only), so a farmer has no way at all to read their own 1962 requests.

Net: a farmer gets a hard 403, and no role can filter the list by farmer. The claim's two backend defects both hold.

- `domain.Invoice` (collection.go lines 205-218): confirmed — no `utr`, no `settled_at`/`settledAt` field. The struct carries `TotalAmount`, `InvoiceDate`, `Status`, `SettlementBatchID`, etc., but nothing bank-reference-related. A repo-wide grep for `settled_at`/`SettledAt` returns nothing anywhere in `internal/`.
- `domain.PayoutInstruction` (settlement.go lines 63, 66): confirmed — `UTR string` and `CreditedAt *time.Time` live here, the correct domain location for a per-farmer bank credit.
- Backend exposes this data: `GET /settlements/payouts` is wired (module.go line 69, `h.payouts` → `service.PayoutHistory`, service.go line 626), returns `[]domain.PayoutInstruction` (UTR + CreditedAt included), and is explicitly authorized for `RoleFarmer` (forced to own party inside the service). The execute path stamps `UTR: mockUTR()` and `CreditedAt` on each payout (service.go lines 449-451).

Assessment: this is fundamentally a frontend-consumption claim (the claimant tags it `[fe-gap]` themselves), and there is NO frontend in this repo — it is a Go backend only (no `.ts`/`.tsx` files exist; `payments.ts`, `MemberDetailSheet.tsx`, etc. are not present). On the backend side, nothing is broken: the UTR/credited-timestamp data is modeled on the correct entity (`PayoutInstruction`, not `Invoice`) and is fully exposed through a dedicated, farmer-accessible endpoint. There is no missing endpoint, no broken relation, and no unmet Note requirement on the backend. The claim's own text concedes "The backend does expose that data via GET /settlements/payouts." Per the verification rule (if the backend already handles it, mark not real), this is not a real backend issue.

    const err = (json as { error?: { code?: string; message?: string; details?: unknown } })
      ?.error;
    throw new ApiError(
      res.status,
      err?.code ?? `HTTP_${res.status}`,
      err?.message ?? res.statusText,
      err?.details,
    );
  }
  // Success envelope: { data, meta? } - unwrap data; tolerate bare payloads.
  if (json && typeof json === 'object' && 'data' in (json as Record<string, unknown>)) {
    return (json as { data: unknown }).data;
  }
  return json;
}

/** Single-flight refresh: rotate the token pair via POST /auth/refresh. */
let refreshInFlight: Promise<boolean> | null = null;
async function tryRefresh(): Promise<boolean> {
  if (!refreshToken) return false;
  refreshInFlight ??= (async () => {
    try {
      const data = (await httpCall('POST', '/auth/refresh', {
        refresh_token: refreshToken,
      })) as { access_token: string; refresh_token: string };
      setTokens({ access: data.access_token, refresh: data.refresh_token });
      return true;
    } catch {
      return false;
    } finally {
      refreshInFlight = null;
    }
  })();
  return refreshInFlight;
}

/** Declare a typed API endpoint. Returns the callable used by feature code. */
export function endpoint<TIn = void, TOut = unknown>(
  spec: EndpointSpec<TIn, TOut>,
): (input: TIn) => Promise<TOut> {
  return async (input: TIn): Promise<TOut> => {
    if (MODE === 'mock') {
      const { db } = await import('@/core/mocks/db');
      // Simulated network latency so loading states are honest
      await sleep(120 + Math.random() * 230);
      const result = await spec.mock(input, db);
      // Deep-clone so callers can never mutate the mock store through results
      return deepClone(result);
    }

    const path = spec.path(input);
    const body = spec.mapRequest ? spec.mapRequest(input) : (input as unknown);
    try {
      const raw = await httpCall(spec.method, path, body);
      return spec.mapResponse ? spec.mapResponse(raw) : (raw as TOut);
    } catch (e) {
      // One refresh + retry on expired access tokens (never for /auth/* itself)
      if (e instanceof ApiError && e.status === 401 && !path.startsWith('/auth/')) {
        if (await tryRefresh()) {
          const raw = await httpCall(spec.method, path, body);
          return spec.mapResponse ? spec.mapResponse(raw) : (raw as TOut);
        }
        clearTokens();
        onUnauthorized?.();
      }
      throw e;
    }
  };
}

105	// product_lot_id_hex is productLotID.Hex(). The HMAC is computed over the
106	// DECODED payload bytes — exactly what issuance signed. The comparison is
107	// constant-time so a forger learns nothing from response timing.
108	func VerifyQRToken(secret, token string) bool {
109		payloadB64, signature, found := strings.Cut(token, ".")
110		if !found || payloadB64 == "" || signature == "" {
111			return false // malformed: no payload/signature split
112		}
113		payload, err := base64.RawURLEncoding.DecodeString(payloadB64)
114		if err != nil || len(payload) == 0 {
115			return false // malformed: payload is not valid base64url
116		}
117		expected := auth.HMACHash(secret, string(payload))
118		return auth.ConstantTimeEqual(expected, signature)
119	}

239	// buildSourcing derives the samiti-set view from traced consignment events:
240	// contributing DCS org ids from each event's org_unit_id/payload, collection
241	// dates from payloads, with the consignment documents as fallback when the
242	// events did not carry those fields. Ledger events carry ObjectIDs as hex
243	// strings, so the sets are hex-keyed and parsed at the DB/orgscope boundary.
244	func (s *Service) buildSourcing(ctx context.Context, events []provenance.Event) (*SourcingInfo, error) {
245		dcsIDs := map[string]struct{}{}
246		dates := map[string]struct{}{}
247		consignmentIDs := map[string]struct{}{}
248	
249		for _, ev := range events {
250			if ev.EntityType != domain.EntityConsignment {
251				continue
252			}
253			consignmentIDs[ev.EntityID] = struct{}{}
254			// Only created/dispatched events carry the DCS in org_unit_id —
255			// consignment.picked_up is appended by logistics under the UNION's
256			// org id, which must never be counted as a contributing samiti.
257			switch ev.Type {
258			case domain.EventConsignmentCreated, domain.EventConsignmentDispatched:
259				if ev.OrgUnitID != "" {
260					dcsIDs[ev.OrgUnitID] = struct{}{}
261				} else if v, ok := ev.Payload["dcs_id"].(string); ok && v != "" {
262					dcsIDs[v] = struct{}{}
263				}
264			}
265			if v, ok := ev.Payload["date"].(string); ok && v != "" {
266				dates[v] = struct{}{}
267			}
268		}
269	
270		// Fallback: if the events lacked DCS ids or dates, read the consignment
271		// docs themselves (still samiti-level — pour ids are never surfaced).
272		if len(consignmentIDs) > 0 && (len(dcsIDs) == 0 || len(dates) == 0) {
273			ids := make([]primitive.ObjectID, 0, len(consignmentIDs))
274			for _, hexID := range sortedKeys(consignmentIDs) {
275				cid, err := primitive.ObjectIDFromHex(hexID)
276				if err != nil {
277					// Ledger event ids should always be ObjectID hex — flag and skip.
278					s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "QR scan: traced consignment id is not a valid object id",
279						slog.String("consignment_id", hexID))
280					continue
281				}
282				ids = append(ids, cid)
283			}
284			docs, err := s.repo.consignmentsByIDs(ctx, ids)
285			if err != nil {
286				return nil, s.internalErr(ctx, "qr scan: load consignments for sourcing", err)
287			}
288			for _, c := range docs {
289				if !c.DCSID.IsZero() {
290					dcsIDs[c.DCSID.Hex()] = struct{}{}
291				}
292				if c.Date != "" {
293					dates[c.Date] = struct{}{}
294				}
295			}
296		}
297	
298		samitis := make([]SamitiInfo, 0, len(dcsIDs))
299		districts := map[string]struct{}{}
300		for _, hexID := range sortedKeys(dcsIDs) {
301			orgID, err := primitive.ObjectIDFromHex(hexID)
302			if err != nil {
303				// A malformed id must not break a consumer scan — log and skip.
304				s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "QR scan: contributing DCS id is not a valid object id",
305					slog.String("dcs_org_id", hexID))
306				continue
307			}
308			org, err := s.orgs.Get(ctx, orgID)
309			if err != nil {
310				// A missing org unit must not break a consumer scan — log and skip.
311				s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "QR scan: contributing DCS org not resolvable",
312					slog.String("dcs_org_id", hexID), slog.Any("err", err))
313				continue
314			}
315			// Defence in depth: the §7.4 samiti set may only contain DCS units.
316			if org.Type != domain.OrgTypeDCS {
317				s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "QR scan: non-DCS org unit skipped from samiti set",
318					slog.String("org_id", hexID), slog.String("org_type", org.Type))
319				continue
320			}
321			samitis = append(samitis, SamitiInfo{Name: org.Name, Code: org.Code, District: org.District})
322			if org.District != "" {
323				districts[org.District] = struct{}{}
324			}
325		}
326		sort.Slice(samitis, func(i, j int) bool { return samitis[i].Name < samitis[j].Name })
327	
328		collectionDates := sortedKeys(dates)
329		return &SourcingInfo{
330			Message:         sourcingMessage(collectionDates, len(samitis), sortedKeys(districts)),
331			Samitis:         samitis,
332			CollectionDates: collectionDates,
333		}, nil
334	}

336	// sourcingMessage renders the consumer-facing pooled-provenance sentence,
337	// e.g. "Made from milk collected on 2026-07-05 from 3 samitis in Lucknow".
338	func sourcingMessage(dates []string, samitiCount int, districts []string) string {
339		var b strings.Builder
340		b.WriteString("Made from milk collected")
341		if len(dates) > 0 {
342			b.WriteString(" on " + strings.Join(dates, ", "))
343		}
344		noun := "samitis"
345		if samitiCount == 1 {
346			noun = "samiti"
347		}
348		fmt.Fprintf(&b, " from %d %s", samitiCount, noun)
349		if len(districts) > 0 {
350			b.WriteString(" in " + strings.Join(districts, ", "))
351		}
352		return b.String()
353	}
354	
355	// verifyTracedRange answers the per-scan tamper-evidence check from a
356	// cumulative verification watermark: the chain is verified incrementally up
357	// to the traced range's max seq, and once a prefix is verified, later scans
358	// inside it are O(1) — no per-request re-hash of thousands of interleaved
359	// events. Spans over scanVerifySpanCap are verified partially (most recent
360	// tail) and flagged, matching the previous per-scan behaviour.
361	func (s *Service) verifyTracedRange(ctx context.Context, events []provenance.Event) (*LedgerInfo, error) {
362		if len(events) == 0 {
363			return &LedgerInfo{Events: 0, Intact: true, VerifiedRange: [2]int64{0, 0}}, nil
364		}
365		maxSeq := events[0].Seq
366		for _, ev := range events[1:] {
367			if ev.Seq > maxSeq {
368				maxSeq = ev.Seq
369			}
370		}
371	
372		s.verifyMu.Lock()
373		defer s.verifyMu.Unlock()
374	
375		if s.chainBroken {
376			return &LedgerInfo{
377				Events:        len(events),
378				Intact:        false,
379				VerifiedRange: [2]int64{s.brokenAtSeq, s.brokenAtSeq},
380			}, nil
381		}
382		if maxSeq <= s.verifiedUpTo {
383			return &LedgerInfo{
384				Events:        len(events),
385				Intact:        true,
386				VerifiedRange: [2]int64{1, s.verifiedUpTo},
387			}, nil
388		}
389	
390		// Extend the watermark: start at the last verified event (re-hashing it
391		// covers the boundary linkage), capped to the per-request span budget.
392		from, partial := max(int64(1), s.verifiedUpTo), false
393		if maxSeq-from+1 > scanVerifySpanCap {
394			from, partial = maxSeq-scanVerifySpanCap+1, true
395		}
396		intact, brokenAt, err := s.ledger.VerifyChain(ctx, from, maxSeq)
397		if err != nil {
398			return nil, s.internalErr(ctx, "qr scan: verify ledger chain", err,
399				slog.Int64("from", from), slog.Int64("to", maxSeq))
400		}
401		if intact {
402			s.verifiedUpTo = maxSeq
403		} else {
404			s.chainBroken, s.brokenAtSeq = true, brokenAt
405			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "provenance chain break detected during scan verification",
406				slog.Int64("broken_at_seq", brokenAt),
407				slog.Int64("from", from), slog.Int64("to", maxSeq))
408		}
409		return &LedgerInfo{
410			Events:        len(events),
411			Intact:        intact,
412			VerifiedRange: [2]int64{from, maxSeq},
413			Partial:       partial,
414		}, nil
415	}
416	
417	// VerifyLedger runs the public tamper-evidence check over [from,to]. Both
418	// bounds are optional: `to` defaults to the chain head, `from` to the start
419	// of the last publicVerifySpanCap events. Spans over the cap are rejected.
420	func (s *Service) VerifyLedger(ctx context.Context, fromRaw, toRaw string) (*LedgerVerifyResponse, error) {
421		latest, err := s.ledger.LatestSeq(ctx)
422		if err != nil {
423			return nil, s.internalErr(ctx, "ledger verify: read chain head", err)
424		}
425		if latest == 0 {
426			return &LedgerVerifyResponse{Intact: true, From: 0, To: 0}, nil // empty chain is trivially intact
427		}
428	
429		to := latest
430		if toRaw != "" {
431			n, err := strconv.ParseInt(toRaw, 10, 64)
432			if err != nil || n < 1 {
433				return nil, httpx.BadRequest("INVALID_RANGE", "'to' must be a positive sequence number")
434			}
435			to = min(n, latest)
436		}
437		from := max(int64(1), to-publicVerifySpanCap+1)
438		if fromRaw != "" {
439			n, err := strconv.ParseInt(fromRaw, 10, 64)
440			if err != nil || n < 1 {
441				return nil, httpx.BadRequest("INVALID_RANGE", "'from' must be a positive sequence number")
442			}
443			from = n
444		}
445		if from > to {
446			return nil, httpx.BadRequest("INVALID_RANGE", "'from' must not exceed 'to'")
447		}
448		if to-from+1 > publicVerifySpanCap {
449			return nil, httpx.BadRequest("SPAN_TOO_WIDE",
450				fmt.Sprintf("verification span is capped at %d events per request", publicVerifySpanCap))
451		}
452	
453		intact, brokenAt, err := s.ledger.VerifyChain(ctx, from, to)
454		if err != nil {
455			return nil, s.internalErr(ctx, "ledger verify: verify chain", err,
456				slog.Int64("from", from), slog.Int64("to", to))
457		}
458		resp := &LedgerVerifyResponse{Intact: intact, From: from, To: to}
459		if !intact {
460			resp.BrokenAtSeq = &brokenAt
461			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "public ledger verification found a broken chain",
462				slog.Int64("broken_at_seq", brokenAt),
463				slog.Int64("from", from), slog.Int64("to", to))
464		}
465		return resp, nil
466	}
467	
468	// TraceGraph returns the full event graph around one entity: upstream via
469	// the recursive ref walk, downstream via reverse-ref lookup — the recall /
470	// root-cause tool (§8.3). entityID is the entity's ObjectID as a hex string
471	// (already validated by the handler; the ledger stores ids as hex).
472	func (s *Service) TraceGraph(ctx context.Context, entityType, entityID string) (*TraceGraphResponse, error) {
473		if err := validateEntityType(entityType); err != nil {
474			return nil, err
475		}
476		upstream, err := s.ledger.Trace(ctx, entityType, entityID, traceDepth)
477		if err != nil {
478			return nil, s.internalErr(ctx, "trace graph: upstream walk", err,
479				slog.String("entity_type", entityType), slog.String("entity_id", entityID))
480		}
481		// The cap is pushed into the query: only the LAST downstreamEventCap
482		// referencing events are fetched, instead of decoding an unbounded set
483		// into memory and truncating afterwards.
484		downstream, err := s.ledger.DownstreamRefs(ctx, entityID, downstreamEventCap)
485		if err != nil {
486			return nil, s.internalErr(ctx, "trace graph: downstream refs", err,
487				slog.String("entity_type", entityType), slog.String("entity_id", entityID))
488		}
489		if len(upstream) == 0 && len(downstream) == 0 {
490			return nil, httpx.NotFound("provenance for entity")
491		}
492		if upstream == nil {
493			upstream = []provenance.Event{}
494		}
495		if downstream == nil {
496			downstream = []provenance.Event{}
497		}
498		return &TraceGraphResponse{Upstream: upstream, Downstream: downstream}, nil
499	}
500	
501	// Timeline returns one entity's own events in chain order, paginated. The
502	// skip/limit is pushed into the Mongo query so a page read never loads the
503	// entity's full history. The second return value is the total event count.
504	// entityID is the entity's ObjectID as a hex string (handler-validated).
505	func (s *Service) Timeline(ctx context.Context, entityType, entityID string, page httpx.Page) ([]provenance.Event, int, error) {
506		if err := validateEntityType(entityType); err != nil {
507			return nil, 0, err
508		}
509		total, err := s.ledger.CountEventsForEntity(ctx, entityType, entityID)
510		if err != nil {
511			return nil, 0, s.internalErr(ctx, "timeline: count entity events", err,
512				slog.String("entity_type", entityType), slog.String("entity_id", entityID))
513		}
514		if total == 0 {
515			return nil, 0, httpx.NotFound("provenance for entity")
516		}
517		events, err := s.ledger.EventsForEntityPage(ctx, entityType, entityID, page.Offset, page.Limit)
518		if err != nil {
519			return nil, 0, s.internalErr(ctx, "timeline: load entity events page", err,
520				slog.String("entity_type", entityType), slog.String("entity_id", entityID))
521		}
522		return events, int(total), nil
523	}
524	
525	// validateEntityType rejects entity types outside the domain.Entity* catalog.
526	func validateEntityType(entityType string) error {
527		if _, ok := validEntityTypes[entityType]; !ok {
528			return httpx.BadRequest("INVALID_ENTITY_TYPE",
529				"unknown entity type "+entityType+" — use one of the provenance entity type constants")
530		}
531		return nil
532	}
533	
534	// sortedKeys returns a set's keys in deterministic (lexicographic) order.
535	func sortedKeys(set map[string]struct{}) []string {
536		out := make([]string, 0, len(set))
537		for k := range set {
538			out = append(out, k)
539		}
540		sort.Strings(out)
541		return out
542	}

**Confirmed defect** in `/Users/divyanshmangla/parag-saathi-be/internal/modules/settlement/service.go`, `Execute` loop (lines 436-470):

- `latestBankMasked` (repo.go:327-344) returns `("", nil)` via the `mongo.ErrNoDocuments` branch when the farmer has no VERIFIED KYC record carrying a non-empty `bank_account_masked`.
- The loop never inspects `masked` for emptiness. It unconditionally builds a `PayoutInstruction{BankAccountMasked: masked /* "" */, UTR: mockUTR(), Status: domain.PayoutStatusSuccess, CreditedAt: &creditedAt}` and inserts it.
- `markInvoicesPaid` (service.go:472 → repo.go:127-136) then flips **every** invoice in the batch to `PAID` with no per-invoice guard, and the `payout.credited` ledger event + `TopicPayoutCredited` SMS (service.go:531-559) fire for that farmer.

Net effect: an un-KYC'd / bank-less farmer's invoice is recorded as a SUCCESS payout to a blank destination account (`BankAccountMasked: ""`), invoice marked PAID, "money credited" SMS sent — exactly the outcome repo.go's own comment forbids ("Payouts must only ever be issued against a reviewer-approved bank account").

- `InvoiceStatusHold = "HOLD"` ("safety-gate payment hold", domain/collection.go:199) exists but is never assigned anywhere in the settlement module (grep shows it only in a collection list-filter allowlist and one exclusion filter). `PayoutStatusFailed` also exists and is unused here.

19		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/eventbus"
20		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/middleware"
21	)
22	
23	// Register wires the platformops module and mounts /admin, /audit,
24	// /notifications and /support (the router hands us the /api/v1 subtree).
25	func Register(r chi.Router, d *deps.Deps) {
26		log := d.Log.With(slog.String("module", "platformops"))
27		repo := newRepository(d.DB)
28		svc := newService(d, repo, log)
29		h := newHandler(svc)
30	
31		r.Route("/admin", func(r chi.Router) {
32			r.Use(middleware.Authenticate(d.JWT))
33	
34			// PCDF_ADMIN may LIST flags; flipping one is SUPER_ADMIN only —
35			// capability gating is a deliberate act (blueprint principle #6).
36			r.With(middleware.RequireRoles(domain.RoleSuperAdmin, domain.RolePCDFAdmin)).
37				Get("/flags", h.listFlags)
38			r.With(middleware.RequireRoles(domain.RoleSuperAdmin)).
39				Put("/flags/{key}", h.setFlag)
40		})
41	
42		r.Route("/audit", func(r chi.Router) {
43			r.Use(middleware.Authenticate(d.JWT))
44			r.Use(middleware.RequireRoles(domain.RoleStateAuditor, domain.RoleSuperAdmin))
45	
46			// Read-only by design: there is deliberately NO write/delete API
47			// surface for audit logs (§12) — entries land via deps.Audit only.
48			r.Get("/logs", h.listAuditLogs)
49			r.Get("/logs/export", h.exportAuditLogs)
50		})
51	
52		r.Route("/notifications", func(r chi.Router) {
53			r.Use(middleware.Authenticate(d.JWT))
54	
55			// SUPER_ADMIN only: a help-desk role has no need to read outbox
56			// message bodies, and the outbox carries credential-adjacent traffic
57			// (OTP notifications — additionally redacted in the service).
58			r.With(middleware.RequireRoles(domain.RoleSuperAdmin)).
59				Get("/", h.listNotifications)
60			r.With(middleware.RequireRoles(domain.RoleSuperAdmin)).
61				Post("/worker/run", h.runWorker)
62		})
63	
64		r.Route("/support", func(r chi.Router) {
65			r.Use(middleware.Authenticate(d.JWT))
66			r.Use(middleware.RequireRoles(domain.RoleSupportAgent, domain.RoleSuperAdmin))
67	
68			r.Get("/parties/lookup", h.lookupParty)
69		})
70	
71		// Cross-module reactions arrive over the bus (modules never import each
72		// other). The bus already runs each handler on its own goroutine with a
73		// bounded context and panic recovery; the wrapper below adds an explicit
74		// second belt at this module's boundary.
75		d.Bus.Subscribe(eventbus.TopicPayoutCredited, safeHandler(log, svc.onPayoutCredited))
76		d.Bus.Subscribe(eventbus.TopicGateBlocked, safeHandler(log, svc.onGateBlocked))
77		d.Bus.Subscribe(eventbus.TopicMVUDispatched, safeHandler(log, svc.onMVUDispatched))
78	}
79	
80	// safeHandler wraps a bus reaction so a programming error in notification
81	// fan-out can never disturb the publishing flow.
82	func safeHandler(log *slog.Logger, reaction func(ctx context.Context, payload any)) eventbus.Handler {
83		return func(ctx context.Context, topic string, payload any) {
84			defer func() {
85				if rec := recover(); rec != nil {
86					log.Error("platformops bus handler panic",
87						slog.String("topic", topic), slog.Any("panic", rec))
88				}
89			}()
90			reaction(ctx, payload)
91		}
92	}
93

167	// values mean UTC midnight; with endOfDay they cover the whole day, so
168	// ?to=2026-07-06 is inclusive of the 6th.
169	func parseTimeParam(value string, endOfDay bool) (*time.Time, error) {
170		if value == "" {
171			return nil, nil
172		}
173		if t, err := time.Parse(time.RFC3339, value); err == nil {
174			t = t.UTC()
175			return &t, nil
176		}
177		t, err := time.Parse("2006-01-02", value)
178		if err != nil {
179			return nil, err
180		}
181		if endOfDay {
182			t = t.Add(24*time.Hour - time.Nanosecond)
183		}
184		t = t.UTC()
185		return &t, nil
186	}

21	// notifications outbox, reads audit_logs strictly read-only (writes go
22	// through deps.Audit only — the collection is insert-only by design, §12),
23	// and reads parties / role_assignments for the support lookup and for
24	// addressing safety alerts. bmc_lots / processing_batches are read solely to
25	// resolve a gate-blocked subject back to its org unit.

28		notifications *mongo.Collection
29		parties       *mongo.Collection
30		assignments   *mongo.Collection
31		bmcLots       *mongo.Collection
32		batches       *mongo.Collection

36	func newRepository(db *mongo.Database) *repository {
37		return &repository{
38			auditLogs:     db.Collection(mongodb.CollAuditLogs),
39			notifications: db.Collection(mongodb.CollNotifications),
40			parties:       db.Collection(mongodb.CollParties),
41			assignments:   db.Collection(mongodb.CollRoleAssignments),
42			bmcLots:       db.Collection(mongodb.CollBMCLots),
43			batches:       db.Collection(mongodb.CollBatches),

47	// auditFilter builds the bson filter shared by the list and export reads.
48	func auditFilter(f auditLogFilter) bson.D {
49		filter := bson.D{}
50		if f.ActorPartyID != "" {
51			filter = append(filter, bson.E{Key: "actor_party_id", Value: f.ActorPartyID})
52		}
53		if f.TargetType != "" {
54			filter = append(filter, bson.E{Key: "target_type", Value: f.TargetType})
55		}
56		if f.Action != "" {
57			filter = append(filter, bson.E{Key: "action", Value: f.Action})
58		}
59		if f.From != nil || f.To != nil {
60			tsRange := bson.D{}
61			if f.From != nil {
62				tsRange = append(tsRange, bson.E{Key: "$gte", Value: *f.From})
63			}
64			if f.To != nil {
65				tsRange = append(tsRange, bson.E{Key: "$lte", Value: *f.To})
66			}
67			filter = append(filter, bson.E{Key: "ts", Value: tsRange})
68		}
69		return filter
70	}

122	// listNotifications returns a page of outbox documents, newest first,
123	// optionally filtered by phone and status.
124	func (r *repository) listNotifications(ctx context.Context, phone, status string, page httpx.Page) ([]StoredNotification, int64, error) {
125		filter := bson.D{}
126		if phone != "" {
127			filter = append(filter, bson.E{Key: "phone", Value: phone})
128		}
129		if status != "" {
130			filter = append(filter, bson.E{Key: "status", Value: status})
131		}
132	
133		total, err := r.notifications.CountDocuments(ctx, filter)
134		if err != nil {
135			return nil, 0, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("count notifications: %w", err))
136		}
137	
138		cur, err := r.notifications.Find(ctx, filter, options.Find().
139			SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "queued_at", Value: -1}}).
140			SetSkip(page.Offset).
141			SetLimit(page.Limit),
142		)
143		if err != nil {
144			return nil, 0, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("list notifications: %w", err))
145		}
146		notifications := []StoredNotification{}
147		if err := cur.All(ctx, &notifications); err != nil {
148			return nil, 0, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("decode notifications: %w", err))
149		}
150		return notifications, total, nil
151	}
152	
153	// claimQueuedNotification atomically claims the oldest QUEUED document
154	// (QUEUED→SENT, sent_at, provider_ref) and returns it, or nil when the queue
155	// is drained. FindOneAndUpdate makes the claim race-safe across concurrent
156	// worker runs — never find-then-update.
157	func (r *repository) claimQueuedNotification(ctx context.Context, providerRef string, now time.Time) (*StoredNotification, error) {
158		var n StoredNotification
159		err := r.notifications.FindOneAndUpdate(ctx,
160			bson.D{{Key: "status", Value: domain.NotificationQueued}},
161			bson.D{{Key: "$set", Value: bson.D{
162				{Key: "status", Value: domain.NotificationSent},
163				{Key: "sent_at", Value: now},
164				{Key: "provider_ref", Value: providerRef},
165			}}},
166			options.FindOneAndUpdate().
167				SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "queued_at", Value: 1}}).
168				SetReturnDocument(options.After),
169		).Decode(&n)
170		if errors.Is(err, mongo.ErrNoDocuments) {
171			return nil, nil
172		}
173		if err != nil {
174			return nil, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("claim queued notification: %w", err))
175		}
176		return &n, nil
177	}
178	
179	// setNotificationMeta stamps the rendered-message meta block onto a claimed
180	// notification (visibility only — the claim has already succeeded).
181	func (r *repository) setNotificationMeta(ctx context.Context, notificationID primitive.ObjectID, meta map[string]any) error {
182		_, err := r.notifications.UpdateOne(ctx,
183			bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: notificationID}},
184			bson.D{{Key: "$set", Value: bson.D{{Key: "meta", Value: meta}}}},
185		)
186		if err != nil {
187			return httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("set notification meta: %w", err))
188		}
189		return nil
190	}
191	
192	// findPartyByPhone returns the party owning a phone number, or NotFound.
193	func (r *repository) findPartyByPhone(ctx context.Context, phone string) (*domain.Party, error) {
194		var party domain.Party
195		err := r.parties.FindOne(ctx, bson.D{{Key: "phone", Value: phone}}).Decode(&party)
196		if errors.Is(err, mongo.ErrNoDocuments) {
197			return nil, httpx.NotFound("party")
198		}
199		if err != nil {
200			return nil, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("find party by phone: %w", err))
201		}
202		return &party, nil
203	}
204

207		var party domain.Party
208		err := r.parties.FindOne(ctx, bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: partyID}}).Decode(&party)
209		if errors.Is(err, mongo.ErrNoDocuments) {
210			return nil, httpx.NotFound("party")
211		}
212		if err != nil {
213			return nil, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("find party: %w", err))
214		}
215		return &party, nil
216	}
217

219	// (bounded — a party holds at most a handful of roles).
220	func (r *repository) listActiveAssignmentsForParty(ctx context.Context, partyID primitive.ObjectID) ([]domain.RoleAssignment, error) {
221		cur, err := r.assignments.Find(ctx,

224				{Key: "status", Value: domain.RoleAssignmentActive},
225			},

234		}

239	// org unit (bounded — used to address supervisor safety alerts).
240	func (r *repository) listActiveRoleHolders(ctx context.Context, orgUnitID primitive.ObjectID, roleCode string) ([]domain.RoleAssignment, error) {
241		cur, err := r.assignments.Find(ctx,
242			bson.D{
243				{Key: "org_unit_id", Value: orgUnitID},
244				{Key: "role_code", Value: roleCode},
245				{Key: "status", Value: domain.RoleAssignmentActive},
246			},
247			options.Find().SetLimit(50),
248		)
249		if err != nil {
250			return nil, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("list role holders: %w", err))
251		}
252		assignments := []domain.RoleAssignment{}
253		if err := cur.All(ctx, &assignments); err != nil {
254			return nil, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("decode role holders: %w", err))
255		}

259	// subjectOrgUnit resolves a gate-blocked QC subject to the org unit that
260	// holds it (BMC lot → bmc_id, processing batch → plant_id). Both the subject
261	// _id and the reference field are ObjectIDs.
262	func (r *repository) subjectOrgUnit(ctx context.Context, subjectType string, subjectID primitive.ObjectID) (primitive.ObjectID, error) {
263		var coll *mongo.Collection
264		var field string
265		switch subjectType {
266		case domain.QCSubjectBMCLot:
267			coll, field = r.bmcLots, "bmc_id"
268		case domain.QCSubjectProcessingBatch:
269			coll, field = r.batches, "plant_id"
270		default:
271			return primitive.NilObjectID, fmt.Errorf("gate-blocked subject type %q has no org resolution", subjectType)
272		}
273	
274		var doc bson.M
275		err := coll.FindOne(ctx, bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: subjectID}},
276			options.FindOne().SetProjection(bson.D{{Key: field, Value: 1}}),
277		).Decode(&doc)
278		if err != nil {
279			return primitive.NilObjectID, fmt.Errorf("resolve org of %s %s: %w", subjectType, subjectID.Hex(), err)
280		}
281		orgUnitID, _ := doc[field].(primitive.ObjectID)
282		if orgUnitID.IsZero() {
283			return primitive.NilObjectID, fmt.Errorf("%s %s carries no %s", subjectType, subjectID.Hex(), field)
284		}
285		return orgUnitID, nil
286	}

_**Agent - sidechain (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-08 20:22:12Z)**_

I have all the evidence needed. Let me record my findings.

The code facts in the claim are all accurate — I verified each one:
- `repo` binds only 5 collections (batchQRs, productLots, batches, qcResults, consignments); there is no `lot_summaries` collection (repo.go:25-42).
- `ScanQR` walks live: `TraceStopAt(EntityProductLot,...)` (service.go:169), then `buildSourcing` re-loads consignment docs via `consignmentsByIDs` and issues one `s.orgs.Get` per contributing DCS (service.go:284-321), plus `latestPlantLabPass` and a `VerifyChain` (service.go:396).
- `ProductLot` has no summary fields; `ProcessingBatch` has no `contributing_dcs_ids` (processing.go:55-96).

But the claim's characterization as a shipped high-severity nonconformance does not survive scrutiny, which is what I was asked to test.

1	package platformops
