14	)
15	
16	// handler is the HTTP layer: decode, validate shape, call service, respond.
17	type handler struct {
18		svc *service
19	}
20	
21	// newHandler wires the handler.
22	func newHandler(svc *service) *handler {
23		return &handler{svc: svc}
24	}
25	
26	// listFlags handles GET /admin/flags.
27	func (h *handler) listFlags(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
28		all, err := h.svc.listFlags(r.Context())
29		if err != nil {
30			httpx.Error(w, r, err)
31			return
32		}
33		httpx.JSON(w, http.StatusOK, all)
34	}
35	
36	// setFlag handles PUT /admin/flags/{key}.
37	func (h *handler) setFlag(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
38		actor, ok := auth.ActorFrom(r.Context())
39		if !ok {
40			httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Unauthorized("authentication required"))
41			return
42		}
43	
44		var req SetFlagRequest
45		if err := httpx.DecodeJSON(r, &req); err != nil {
46			httpx.Error(w, r, err)
47			return
48		}
49		if req.Enabled == nil {
50			httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.BadRequest("MISSING_ENABLED", "enabled is required"))
51			return
52		}
53	
54		flag, err := h.svc.setFlag(r.Context(), actor, chi.URLParam(r, "key"), *req.Enabled)
55		if err != nil {
56			httpx.Error(w, r, err)
57			return
58		}
59		httpx.JSON(w, http.StatusOK, flag)
60	}
61	
62	// listAuditLogs handles GET /audit/logs?actor_party_id=&target_type=&action=&from=&to=.
63	func (h *handler) listAuditLogs(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
64		query := r.URL.Query()
65		filter := auditLogFilter{
66			ActorPartyID: query.Get("actor_party_id"),
67			TargetType:   query.Get("target_type"),
68			Action:       query.Get("action"),
69		}
70	
71		from, err := parseTimeParam(query.Get("from"), false)
72		if err != nil {
73			httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.BadRequest("INVALID_FROM", "from must be RFC3339 or YYYY-MM-DD"))
74			return
75		}
76		to, err := parseTimeParam(query.Get("to"), true)
77		if err != nil {
78			httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.BadRequest("INVALID_TO", "to must be RFC3339 or YYYY-MM-DD"))
79			return
80		}
81		filter.From, filter.To = from, to
82	
83		page := httpx.ParsePage(r)
84		entries, total, err := h.svc.listAuditLogs(r.Context(), filter, page)
85		if err != nil {
86			httpx.Error(w, r, err)
87			return
88		}
89		httpx.JSONMeta(w, http.StatusOK, entries, listMeta{Limit: page.Limit, Offset: page.Offset, Total: total})
90	}
91	
92	// exportAuditLogs handles GET /audit/logs/export?from=&to= — the capped JSON
93	// attachment for the GIGW/DPDP immutable audit export (§12).
94	func (h *handler) exportAuditLogs(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
95		query := r.URL.Query()
96		from, err := parseTimeParam(query.Get("from"), false)
97		if err != nil {
98			httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.BadRequest("INVALID_FROM", "from must be RFC3339 or YYYY-MM-DD"))
99			return
100		}
101		to, err := parseTimeParam(query.Get("to"), true)
102		if err != nil {
103			httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.BadRequest("INVALID_TO", "to must be RFC3339 or YYYY-MM-DD"))
104			return
105		}
106	
107		export, err := h.svc.exportAuditLogs(r.Context(), from, to)
108		if err != nil {
109			httpx.Error(w, r, err)
110			return
111		}
112	
113		filename := "audit-export-" + export.ExportedAt.Format("20060102-150405") + ".json"
114		w.Header().Set("Content-Disposition", fmt.Sprintf("attachment; filename=%q", filename))
115		httpx.JSON(w, http.StatusOK, export)
116	}
117	
118	// listNotifications handles GET /notifications?phone=&status=.
119	func (h *handler) listNotifications(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
120		query := r.URL.Query()
121		phone := strings.TrimSpace(query.Get("phone"))
122		status := query.Get("status")
123		switch status {
124		case "", domain.NotificationQueued, domain.NotificationSent, domain.NotificationFailed:
125		default:
126			httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.BadRequest("INVALID_STATUS", "status must be QUEUED, SENT or FAILED"))
127			return
128		}
129	
130		page := httpx.ParsePage(r)
131		notifications, total, err := h.svc.listNotifications(r.Context(), phone, status, page)
132		if err != nil {
133			httpx.Error(w, r, err)
134			return
135		}
136		httpx.JSONMeta(w, http.StatusOK, notifications, listMeta{Limit: page.Limit, Offset: page.Offset, Total: total})
137	}
138	
139	// runWorker handles POST /notifications/worker/run — the manual mock-SMS
140	// dispatch trigger (deterministic demo; production = cron/queue consumer).
141	func (h *handler) runWorker(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
142		result, err := h.svc.runWorker(r.Context())
143		if err != nil {
144			httpx.Error(w, r, err)
145			return
146		}
147		httpx.JSON(w, http.StatusOK, result)
148	}
149	
150	// lookupParty handles GET /support/parties/lookup?phone=.
151	func (h *handler) lookupParty(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
152		phone := strings.TrimSpace(r.URL.Query().Get("phone"))
153		if phone == "" {
154			httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.BadRequest("MISSING_PHONE", "phone is required"))
155			return
156		}
157	
158		view, err := h.svc.lookupParty(r.Context(), phone)
159		if err != nil {
160			httpx.Error(w, r, err)
161			return
162		}
163		httpx.JSON(w, http.StatusOK, view)
164	}
165	
166	// parseTimeParam accepts RFC3339 or plain YYYY-MM-DD (empty → nil). Date-only
167	// values mean UTC midnight; with endOfDay they cover the whole day, so
168	// ?to=2026-07-06 is inclusive of the 6th.
169	func parseTimeParam(value string, endOfDay bool) (*time.Time, error) {
170		if value == "" {
171			return nil, nil
172		}
173		if t, err := time.Parse(time.RFC3339, value); err == nil {
174			t = t.UTC()
175			return &t, nil
176		}
177		t, err := time.Parse("2006-01-02", value)
178		if err != nil {
179			return nil, err
180		}
181		if endOfDay {
182			t = t.Add(24*time.Hour - time.Nanosecond)
183		}
184		t = t.UTC()
185		return &t, nil
186	}

1	// Package platformops is the platform-operations module (blueprint §12): the
2	// SUPER_ADMIN feature-flag console, the STATE_AUDITOR read-only audit surface
3	// with its GIGW/DPDP immutable export, the notifications outbox with the mock
4	// SMS dispatch worker (real deployment: MSG91 / telecom DLT gateway, §13),
5	// and the SUPPORT_AGENT audited limited-PII lookup (§5.2 role 20).
6	//
7	// It also subscribes to cross-module bus topics — payout credited, safety
8	// gate blocked, MVU dispatched — and turns them into queued vernacular SMS.
9	package platformops
10	
11	import (
12		"context"
13		"log/slog"
14	
15		"github.com/go-chi/chi/v5"

17		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/domain"

21	)

23	// Register wires the platformops module and mounts /admin, /audit,
24	// /notifications and /support (the router hands us the /api/v1 subtree).
25	func Register(r chi.Router, d *deps.Deps) {
26		log := d.Log.With(slog.String("module", "platformops"))
27		repo := newRepository(d.DB)
28		svc := newService(d, repo, log)
29		h := newHandler(svc)
30	
31		r.Route("/admin", func(r chi.Router) {
32			r.Use(middleware.Authenticate(d.JWT))
33	
34			// PCDF_ADMIN may LIST flags; flipping one is SUPER_ADMIN only —
35			// capability gating is a deliberate act (blueprint principle #6).
36			r.With(middleware.RequireRoles(domain.RoleSuperAdmin, domain.RolePCDFAdmin)).
37				Get("/flags", h.listFlags)
38			r.With(middleware.RequireRoles(domain.RoleSuperAdmin)).
39				Put("/flags/{key}", h.setFlag)
40		})
41	
42		r.Route("/audit", func(r chi.Router) {
43			r.Use(middleware.Authenticate(d.JWT))
44			r.Use(middleware.RequireRoles(domain.RoleStateAuditor, domain.RoleSuperAdmin))
45	
46			// Read-only by design: there is deliberately NO write/delete API
47			// surface for audit logs (§12) — entries land via deps.Audit only.
48			r.Get("/logs", h.listAuditLogs)
49			r.Get("/logs/export", h.exportAuditLogs)
50		})
51	
52		r.Route("/notifications", func(r chi.Router) {
53			r.Use(middleware.Authenticate(d.JWT))
54	
55			// SUPER_ADMIN only: a help-desk role has no need to read outbox
56			// message bodies, and the outbox carries credential-adjacent traffic
57			// (OTP notifications — additionally redacted in the service).
58			r.With(middleware.RequireRoles(domain.RoleSuperAdmin)).
59				Get("/", h.listNotifications)
60			r.With(middleware.RequireRoles(domain.RoleSuperAdmin)).
61				Post("/worker/run", h.runWorker)
62		})
63	
64		r.Route("/support", func(r chi.Router) {
65			r.Use(middleware.Authenticate(d.JWT))
66			r.Use(middleware.RequireRoles(domain.RoleSupportAgent, domain.RoleSuperAdmin))
67	
68			r.Get("/parties/lookup", h.lookupParty)
69		})
70	
71		// Cross-module reactions arrive over the bus (modules never import each
72		// other). The bus already runs each handler on its own goroutine with a
73		// bounded context and panic recovery; the wrapper below adds an explicit
74		// second belt at this module's boundary.
75		d.Bus.Subscribe(eventbus.TopicPayoutCredited, safeHandler(log, svc.onPayoutCredited))
76		d.Bus.Subscribe(eventbus.TopicGateBlocked, safeHandler(log, svc.onGateBlocked))
77		d.Bus.Subscribe(eventbus.TopicMVUDispatched, safeHandler(log, svc.onMVUDispatched))
78	}
79	
80	// safeHandler wraps a bus reaction so a programming error in notification
81	// fan-out can never disturb the publishing flow.
82	func safeHandler(log *slog.Logger, reaction func(ctx context.Context, payload any)) eventbus.Handler {
83		return func(ctx context.Context, topic string, payload any) {
84			defer func() {
85				if rec := recover(); rec != nil {
86					log.Error("platformops bus handler panic",
87						slog.String("topic", topic), slog.Any("panic", rec))
88				}
89			}()
90			reaction(ctx, payload)
91		}
92	}
93

**FE side (confirmed):**

Resolved against `BASE` these become `/api/v1/dcs/.../invoices/approve`, `/api/v1/invoices/settle`, `/api/v1/dcs/.../release/approve` — none registered → chi 404.

No DRAFT/APPROVED on backend; the authorized action lives at batch level (initiate → dual-control approve → execute), not per invoice.

43			r.Use(middleware.Authenticate(d.JWT))
44			r.Use(middleware.RequireRoles(domain.RoleStateAuditor, domain.RoleSuperAdmin))
45	
46			// Read-only by design: there is deliberately NO write/delete API
47			// surface for audit logs (§12) — entries land via deps.Audit only.
48			r.Get("/logs", h.listAuditLogs)
49			r.Get("/logs/export", h.exportAuditLogs)

52		r.Route("/notifications", func(r chi.Router) {
53			r.Use(middleware.Authenticate(d.JWT))

55			// SUPER_ADMIN only: a help-desk role has no need to read outbox

58			r.With(middleware.RequireRoles(domain.RoleSuperAdmin)).

71		// Cross-module reactions arrive over the bus (modules never import each

73		// bounded context and panic recovery; the wrapper below adds an explicit

75		d.Bus.Subscribe(eventbus.TopicPayoutCredited, safeHandler(log, svc.onPayoutCredited))
76		d.Bus.Subscribe(eventbus.TopicGateBlocked, safeHandler(log, svc.onGateBlocked))

80	// safeHandler wraps a bus reaction so a programming error in notification
81	// fan-out can never disturb the publishing flow.
82	func safeHandler(log *slog.Logger, reaction func(ctx context.Context, payload any)) eventbus.Handler {
83		return func(ctx context.Context, topic string, payload any) {
84			defer func() {
85				if rec := recover(); rec != nil {
86					log.Error("platformops bus handler panic",
87						slog.String("topic", topic), slog.Any("panic", rec))
88				}
89			}()
90			reaction(ctx, payload)
91		}
92	}

**But the "note-nonconformance" framing fails:**
- The authoritative endpoint contract in `docs/strict_brief.md:243` for `GET /public/qr/{qr_code}` requires exactly: "honest samiti-SET provenance (never per-farmer) + QC certificate + ledger.intact" + recall notice. All four ARE served. `farmers_total` is not in this contract.
- `WORKFLOW_GUIDE.md:301-305` confirms the intended response shape ("product + batch + plant + QC + '...from N samitis' + ledger.intact") and states the scan is deliberately built so it "*cannot*" say more than the samiti set.

Piece 7 is P1-planned; only Piece 1 is marked DONE.
- The §6.7 primary text is not in the repo. The ALIGNMENT_SPEC's own reading of §6.7 (lines 56, 132) attributes it to `Party.public_consent` and the "consumer-trace roster" (the opt-in *named* `farmers_public` list) — not to a "non-consenting farmers must be COUNTED / farmers_total is mandatory" clause. The claim's premise that §6.7 mandates an aggregate count is an unsubstantiated interpretation.

1	// Package orgscope answers the RBAC question "is this resource inside the
2	// caller's organisational scope?" in O(1) DB reads. Org units denormalise
3	// their ancestor chain into Path ([]ObjectID), so scope checking is a
4	// set-membership test — no recursive tree walks on the hot path.
5	package orgscope
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"errors"
10		"sync"
11		"time"
12	
13		"go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/bson"

23	
24	type cachedOrg struct {
25		org domain.OrgUnit
26		at  time.Time
27	}
28	
29	// Resolver caches org units briefly (the tree changes rarely, reads are hot).
30	type Resolver struct {
31		coll *mongo.Collection
32		ttl  time.Duration
33	
34		mu    sync.RWMutex
35		cache map[string]cachedOrg // keyed by ObjectID hex
36	}
37	
38	// NewResolver binds the resolver to the database.
39	func NewResolver(db *mongo.Database) *Resolver {
40		return &Resolver{
41			coll:  db.Collection(collection),
42			ttl:   60 * time.Second,
43			cache: make(map[string]cachedOrg),
44		}
45	}
46	
47	// Get returns an org unit by ObjectID (cached).
48	func (r *Resolver) Get(ctx context.Context, id primitive.ObjectID) (*domain.OrgUnit, error) {
49		key := id.Hex()
50		r.mu.RLock()
51		c, ok := r.cache[key]
52		r.mu.RUnlock()
53		if ok && time.Since(c.at) < r.ttl {
54			org := c.org
55			return &org, nil
56		}
57	
58		var org domain.OrgUnit
59		err := r.coll.FindOne(ctx, bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: id}}).Decode(&org)
60		if errors.Is(err, mongo.ErrNoDocuments) {
61			return nil, httpx.NotFound("org unit " + key)
62		}
63		if err != nil {
64			return nil, httpx.Internal(err)
65		}
66	
67		r.mu.Lock()
68		r.cache[key] = cachedOrg{org: org, at: time.Now()}
69		r.mu.Unlock()
70		return &org, nil
71	}
72	
73	// GetByCode returns an org unit by its unique human-readable business code
74	// (e.g. "DCS-01842") — display/lookup use only, never for joins.
75	func (r *Resolver) GetByCode(ctx context.Context, code string) (*domain.OrgUnit, error) {
76		var org domain.OrgUnit
77		err := r.coll.FindOne(ctx, bson.D{{Key: "code", Value: code}}).Decode(&org)
78		if errors.Is(err, mongo.ErrNoDocuments) {
79			return nil, httpx.NotFound("org unit with code " + code)
80		}
81		if err != nil {
82			return nil, httpx.Internal(err)
83		}
84		return &org, nil
85	}
86	
87	// Invalidate drops a cached entry (call after updates).
88	func (r *Resolver) Invalidate(id primitive.ObjectID) {
89		r.mu.Lock()
90		delete(r.cache, id.Hex())
91		r.mu.Unlock()
92	}
93	
94	// InScope reports whether target sits at-or-below scope in the hierarchy:
95	// true when scope == target, or scope appears in target's ancestor Path.
96	func (r *Resolver) InScope(ctx context.Context, scopeOrgID, targetOrgID primitive.ObjectID) (bool, error) {
97		if scopeOrgID == targetOrgID {
98			return true, nil
99		}
100		target, err := r.Get(ctx, targetOrgID)
101		if err != nil {
102			return false, err
103		}
104		for _, ancestor := range target.Path {
105			if ancestor == scopeOrgID {
106				return true, nil
107			}
108		}
109		return false, nil
110	}
111	
112	// RequireInScope enforces the actor's org scope over a target org unit.
113	// SUPER_ADMIN and STATE_AUDITOR (read-wide roles rooted at the federation)
114	// pass automatically; everyone else needs ancestry. The actor carries its
115	// org unit as an ObjectID hex string (JWT claims are JSON); it is parsed here.
116	func (r *Resolver) RequireInScope(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, targetOrgID primitive.ObjectID) error {
117		if actor.RoleCode == domain.RoleSuperAdmin || actor.RoleCode == domain.RoleStateAuditor {
118			return nil
119		}
120		if actor.OrgUnitID == "" {
121			return httpx.Forbidden("role token with org scope required")
122		}
123		scopeID, err := primitive.ObjectIDFromHex(actor.OrgUnitID)
124		if err != nil {
125			return httpx.Forbidden("role token carries an invalid org scope")
126		}
127		ok, err := r.InScope(ctx, scopeID, targetOrgID)
128		if err != nil {
129			return err
130		}
131		if !ok {
132			return httpx.Forbidden("resource is outside your organisational scope")
133		}
134		return nil
135	}
136

Claim [high/relation] Onboarding approve does not create the Party + KYCRecord + RoleAssignment relation (§4.2/§6.1) @ internal/modules/identity/service.go — The Developer Note's assisted-onboarding flow requires that approving a request materialise a three-part relation for a brand-new person: (1) a Party (find-or-create by phone), (2) a KYCRecord capturing the executive-collected evidence (documentType/documentNumber/kycPhotoUri, requested tier, reviewed_by = approver, status VERIFIED) linked to that Party via party_id, and (3) a RoleAssignment (role_code + org_unit_id + granted_by) linked to the same Party. No backend path builds this. The existing identity approveKYC (service.go ~L815) only handles a self-submitted KYCRecord that already references an existing Party, and merely upgrades party.kyc_tier — it never creates a Party and never creates a RoleAssignment. createAssignment (service.go ~L1026) creates only a RoleAssignment and requires the Party to already exist. So there is no code that, on approving an executive submission, lands all three linked records. Note the intended relation is stronger than even the FE mock: approveOnboarding in src/core/api/endpoints/onboarding.ts creates Party + RoleAssignment but omits the KYCRecord entirely, so the produced party carries no KYC provenance — the backend must persist the KYCRecord so an onboarded party has a verifiable identity trail, not a role granted with no verification record.

1	// Package plant implements the processing tier of the pour→QR chain:
2	// BMC lots (pooled consignments at the chilling centre), processing batches,
3	// product lots and QR issuance. It is the ENFORCEMENT layer of the safety
4	// gate (blueprint §8.3): a lot or batch that has not PASSED quality control
5	// can never advance — not into a tanker, not into a batch, not onto a shelf.
6	// Aflatoxin M1 survives pasteurisation, so the gate is checked at every hop,
7	// belt-and-braces.
8	package plant
9	
10	import (
11		"log/slog"
12	
13		"github.com/go-chi/chi/v5"
14	
15		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/domain"
16		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/deps"
17		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/middleware"
18	)
19	
20	// Register wires the plant module under /api/v1/plant.
21	func Register(r chi.Router, d *deps.Deps) {
22		log := d.Log.With(slog.String("module", "plant"))
23		repo := NewRepo(d.DB)
24		svc := NewService(repo, d, log)
25		h := NewHandler(svc)
26	
27		r.Route("/plant", func(pr chi.Router) {
28			pr.Use(middleware.Authenticate(d.JWT))
29	
30			// BMC lots — created/closed/dispatched by the chilling-centre operator;
31			// readable by everyone downstream who receives or supervises the milk.
32			pr.Route("/bmc-lots", func(lr chi.Router) {
33				lr.With(middleware.RequireRoles(
34					domain.RoleBMCOperator, domain.RolePlantOperator,
35					domain.RoleUnionFieldSupervisor, domain.RolePlantLabAnalyst,
36				)).Get("/", h.ListBMCLots)
37	
38				lr.Group(func(wr chi.Router) {
39					wr.Use(middleware.RequireRoles(domain.RoleBMCOperator))
40					wr.Post("/", h.CreateBMCLot)
41					wr.Post("/{id}/close", h.CloseBMCLot)
42					wr.Post("/{id}/dispatch", h.DispatchBMCLot)
43				})
44			})
45	
46			// Processing batches — plant operator pools dispatched (gate-passed)
47			// BMC lots into a production run; plant lab + supervisor read along.
48			pr.Route("/batches", func(br chi.Router) {
49				read := middleware.RequireRoles(
50					domain.RolePlantOperator, domain.RolePlantLabAnalyst,
51					domain.RoleUnionFieldSupervisor,
52				)
53				br.With(read).Get("/", h.ListBatches)
54				br.With(read).Get("/{id}", h.GetBatch)
55	
56				br.Group(func(wr chi.Router) {
57					wr.Use(middleware.RequireRoles(domain.RolePlantOperator))
58					wr.Post("/", h.CreateBatch)
59					wr.Post("/{id}/complete", h.CompleteBatch)
60				})
61			})
62	
63			// Product lots — packaged SKUs out of a COMPLETED batch. Recall is the
64			// FSSAI path (§18-C): admin or plant lab pulls the lot from market.
65			pr.Route("/product-lots", func(plr chi.Router) {
66				plr.With(middleware.RequireRoles(
67					domain.RolePlantOperator, domain.RolePlantLabAnalyst,
68				)).Post("/", h.CreateProductLot)
69				plr.With(middleware.RequireRoles(
70					domain.RolePCDFAdmin, domain.RolePlantLabAnalyst,
71				)).Post("/{id}/recall", h.RecallProductLot)
72			})
73	
74			// QR issuance — the consumer-facing end of the trace chain (§7).
75			pr.Route("/qrs", func(qr chi.Router) {
76				qr.Use(middleware.RequireRoles(
77					domain.RolePlantOperator, domain.RolePlantLabAnalyst,
78				))
79				qr.Post("/", h.IssueQR)
80				qr.Get("/", h.ListQRs)
81			})
82		})
83	
84		// No bus subscriptions: the quality module flips lot/batch statuses in
85		// their own collections, and every gate here re-reads status at use time.
86	}

Claim [high/note-nonconformance] §6.1 CONTENT entity missing — EducationContent cannot carry scheme/article/helpline, region scope, or i18n @ internal/domain/cattle.go — §6.1 defines a single CMS CONTENT entity: { content_id, type:[scheme|video|article|helpline], title_i18n, description_i18n, url, thumbnail_url, languages[], region_scope:[state|district|society|all], category, order, published, valid_from, valid_to } — one curated, region-scoped, multi-language, multi-type collection so the Union/administrator can curate per region and language and update instantly without an app release. The backend only has domain.EducationContent { topic, title, language, media_type(AUDIO|VIDEO|INFOGRAPHIC), media_url, duration_sec, published, created_at } served at /cattle/education. It structurally cannot represent the note's CMS: no `type` discriminator (so it can't hold scheme/article/helpline items — only cattle media), no `region_scope` (state/district/society/all) so content cannot be curated per society/district as the note requires, single `language` per row instead of title_i18n/description_i18n maps, and no valid_from/valid_to/category/order/thumbnail_url. This is a capability gap, not a field-rename (the mapper differences media_type→kind, duration_sec→durationMin are separately handled in the FE and are not reported). spec-conformance.md already flags §6.1 CMS as 'mock, not region-scoped'.

6		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/domain"
7		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/auth"
8		"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/httpx"
9	)
10	
11	// RequireRoles allows only ROLE-kind tokens whose role is in the allow-list.
12	// SUPER_ADMIN passes every gate (break-glass admin — all its calls are
13	// audited by the audit middleware).
14	func RequireRoles(roles ...string) func(http.Handler) http.Handler {
15		allowed := make(map[string]struct{}, len(roles))
16		for _, r := range roles {
17			allowed[r] = struct{}{}
18		}
19		return func(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
20			return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
21				actor, ok := auth.ActorFrom(r.Context())
22				if !ok {
23					httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Unauthorized("authentication required"))
24					return
25				}
26				if actor.Kind != auth.TokenKindRole {
27					httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Forbidden("a role token is required — select a role first (POST /api/v1/auth/role/select)"))
28					return
29				}
30				if actor.RoleCode == domain.RoleSuperAdmin {
31					next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
32					return
33				}
34				if _, ok := allowed[actor.RoleCode]; !ok {
35					httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Forbidden("role "+actor.RoleCode+" is not permitted for this action"))
36					return
37				}
38				next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
39			})
40		}
41	}
42	
43	// RequireSession allows any authenticated party (session or role token) —
44	// used for identity endpoints like "list my roles".
45	func RequireSession(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
46		return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
47			if _, ok := auth.ActorFrom(r.Context()); !ok {
48				httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Unauthorized("authentication required"))
49				return
50			}
51			next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
52		})
53	}
54
```

```text
### 1.4 Org scoping (multi-tenant safety)
Before touching a resource that belongs to an org unit, the service calls
`d.Orgs.RequireInScope(actor, targetOrgID)`. Passes when the actor's org == target, or the
actor's org is an **ancestor** in the target's denormalized `path[]` (O(1), no tree walk).
`SUPER_ADMIN` and `STATE_AUDITOR` are federation-wide. Failure → `403 FORBIDDEN`.

### 1.5 Provenance (append-only, hash-chained)
State-changing steps in the milk→QR chain append an immutable event to `provenance_events`
(SHA-256 chained on the previous hash). Corrections never mutate — they append a new event with a
`supersedes` ref. This is what the public QR scan re-verifies (`ledger.intact`).
=== WORKFLOW ===

A role is always granted **at** one of these org units, and its powers stop at that unit's
subtree (enforced by `RequireInScope` on every API). A Union President sees their district;
a Sacheev sees only their samiti; Super Admin and State Auditor see everything (all audited).

---
| Role | What they do | Key APIs |
|---|---|---|
| **SUPER_ADMIN** | Break-glass admin: feature flags, any role grant, full access — **every action audited** | `PUT /admin/flags/{key}` `POST /roles/assignments` |
| **STATE_AUDITOR** | Read-only everywhere + immutable audit-log export | `GET /audit/logs` `…/export` `GET /trace/*` |
| **SUPPORT_AGENT** | Helpdesk: limited PII lookup (each lookup itself audit-logged) | `GET /support/parties/lookup` |
| **SERVICE_ACCOUNT** | Machines (AMCU devices, connectors) — e.g. the dormant collar telemetry endpoint | `POST /cattle/telemetry` (403 until flag flips) |
```

## Evidence

**No `/admin/products` route exists.** `internal/modules/platformops/module.go` (lines 31-40) mounts `/admin` with only two routes: `Get("/flags", …)` and `Put("/flags/{key}", …)`. A repo-wide grep for `admin/products`, `listAllProducts`, `upsertProduct`, and any `products` route registration across all `*.go` files returns nothing. So both `GET /admin/products` and `PUT /admin/products` hit no handler and 404.

**No product/SKU master collection.** `internal/platform/mongodb/indexes.go` (lines 14-43) defines every collection. There is `CollProductLots = "product_lots"` (line 34) but no `products` / `product_master` / SKU-catalogue collection. `product_lots` is indexed by `batch_id` and `(sku, mfg_date)` — clearly per-manufacture-run data, not a catalogue.

**`product_lots` is not a SKU master.** `internal/domain/processing.go` (lines 79-96): `ProductLot` is documented as "a packaged SKU output of a passed batch" and carries `BatchID`, `PlantID`, `Units`, `UnitSize`, `MfgDate`, `ExpiryDate`, `RecallReason`, `ProvenanceSeq`. It is a lot instance tied to a specific batch, not a reusable SKU/product master with a simple `name/sku/mrp/active` shape. Its `Status` field is lot lifecycle (`ACTIVE`/`RECALLED`/`EXPIRED`), not a catalogue active/inactive toggle.

**FE self-confirms mock-only.** `parag-saathi-fe/src/core/api/endpoints/admin.ts` lines 347-352 and 354-361 both carry the literal comment `// TODO(backend): not exposed - mock only` above `listAllProducts` and `upsertProduct`, each returning/mutating `db.products` (the mock store) only.

Refutation attempt failed: there is no aliased route, no alternate module mounting `/admin/products`, and `product_lots` cannot stand in for a SKU master. The FE product-master screen is mock-only and both live calls 404.

// DCSConsignment aggregates a DCS's pours for one date+shift into the unit
// the van picks up. It is the pooling boundary: past this point milk traces
// to a *set* of contributors (blueprint §7.4).
type DCSConsignment struct {
	ID                  primitive.ObjectID   `bson:"_id,omitempty" json:"id"`
	DCSID               primitive.ObjectID   `bson:"dcs_id"    json:"dcs_id"`
	Date                string               `bson:"date"      json:"date"` // YYYY-MM-DD
	Shift               string               `bson:"shift"     json:"shift"`
	PourIDs             []primitive.ObjectID `bson:"pour_ids"  json:"pour_ids"`
	TotalQuantityLitres float64              `bson:"total_quantity_litres" json:"total_quantity_litres"`
	CanCount            int                  `bson:"can_count,omitempty"   json:"can_count,omitempty"`
	// AvgFatPct/AvgSNFPct are the QUANTITY-WEIGHTED averages the Developer Note
	// §6.4 calls wavg_fat / wavg_snf — computed over the sealed pour set.
	AvgFatPct float64 `bson:"avg_fat_pct,omitempty" json:"avg_fat_pct,omitempty"`
	AvgSNFPct float64 `bson:"avg_snf_pct,omitempty" json:"avg_snf_pct,omitempty"`
	// Assurance is the WEAKEST capture assurance among the pooled pours (§6.2).
	Assurance string `bson:"assurance,omitempty" json:"assurance,omitempty"`
	// SealCode freezes the physical cans to this shift's pour set at dispatch
	// (§6.4, Appendix A: SEAL-<consignment>-<checksum>); the van verifies it.
	SealCode     string             `bson:"seal_code,omitempty" json:"seal_code,omitempty"`
	SealedAt     *time.Time         `bson:"sealed_at,omitempty" json:"sealed_at,omitempty"`
	Status       string             `bson:"status"    json:"status"`
	CreatedBy    primitive.ObjectID `bson:"created_by"    json:"created_by"`
	DispatchedAt *time.Time         `bson:"dispatched_at,omitempty" json:"dispatched_at,omitempty"`
	RouteTripID         *primitive.ObjectID  `bson:"route_trip_id,omitempty" json:"route_trip_id,omitempty"`
	BMCLotID            *primitive.ObjectID  `bson:"bmc_lot_id,omitempty"    json:"bmc_lot_id,omitempty"`
	ProvenanceSeq       int64                `bson:"provenance_seq,omitempty" json:"provenance_seq,omitempty"`
	CreatedAt           time.Time            `bson:"created_at" json:"created_at"`
}

// Route trip statuses.
const (
	TripStatusPlanned    = "PLANNED"

)

// RouteStop is one DCS pickup on a trip, with the cold-chain temperature
// captured at pickup time.
type RouteStop struct {
	DCSID         primitive.ObjectID `bson:"dcs_id"         json:"dcs_id"`
	ConsignmentID primitive.ObjectID `bson:"consignment_id" json:"consignment_id"`
	PickedUpAt    *time.Time         `bson:"picked_up_at,omitempty" json:"picked_up_at,omitempty"`
	TempC         float64            `bson:"temp_c,omitempty"       json:"temp_c,omitempty"`
	Notes         string             `bson:"notes,omitempty"        json:"notes,omitempty"`
}

// ColdChainEntry is a timestamped temperature+location sample during transit.
type ColdChainEntry struct {
	TS     time.Time `bson:"ts"      json:"ts"`
	TempC  float64   `bson:"temp_c"  json:"temp_c"`
	GeoLat float64   `bson:"geo_lat,omitempty" json:"geo_lat,omitempty"`
	GeoLng float64   `bson:"geo_lng,omitempty" json:"geo_lng,omitempty"`
}

// RouteTrip is one van run: pick up consignments across DCS stops, log
// cold-chain, deliver to a BMC.
type RouteTrip struct {
	ID               primitive.ObjectID  `bson:"_id,omitempty" json:"id"`

	Shift            string              `bson:"shift"         json:"shift"`
	Stops            []RouteStop         `bson:"stops"         json:"stops"`
	ColdChain        []ColdChainEntry    `bson:"cold_chain,omitempty" json:"cold_chain,omitempty"`
	Status           string              `bson:"status"        json:"status"`
	DeliveredToBMCID *primitive.ObjectID `bson:"delivered_to_bmc_id,omitempty" json:"delivered_to_bmc_id,omitempty"`
	DeliveredAt      *time.Time          `bson:"delivered_at,omitempty"        json:"delivered_at,omitempty"`
	ProvenanceSeq    int64               `bson:"provenance_seq,omitempty"      json:"provenance_seq,omitempty"`
	CreatedAt        time.Time           `bson:"created_at"    json:"created_at"`
}

// lookupParty handles GET /support/parties/lookup?phone=.
func (h *handler) lookupParty(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	phone := strings.TrimSpace(r.URL.Query().Get("phone"))
	if phone == "" {
		httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.BadRequest("MISSING_PHONE", "phone is required"))
		return
	}

	view, err := h.svc.lookupParty(r.Context(), phone)
	if err != nil {
		httpx.Error(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	httpx.JSON(w, http.StatusOK, view)
}

// parseTimeParam accepts RFC3339 or plain YYYY-MM-DD (empty → nil). Date-only
// values mean UTC midnight; with endOfDay they cover the whole day, so
// ?to=2026-07-06 is inclusive of the 6th.
func parseTimeParam(value string, endOfDay bool) (*time.Time, error) {
	if value == "" {
		return nil, nil
	}
	if t, err := time.Parse(time.RFC3339, value); err == nil {
		t = t.UTC()
		return &t, nil
	}
	t, err := time.Parse("2006-01-02", value)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if endOfDay {
		t = t.Add(24*time.Hour - time.Nanosecond)
	}
	t = t.UTC()
	return &t, nil
}

			r.Post("/", h.create)
			r.Patch("/{id}", h.update)

			r.Use(middleware.RequireSession)
			r.Get("/", h.list)
			r.Get("/{id}", h.get)
			r.Get("/{id}/children", h.children)
		})

		// Subtree read — oversight roles, scope-checked in the service.

No backend route serves /content, and neither content entity carries a monotonically increasing version/cursor to diff against. On weak rural connections this forces a full refetch every open instead of a delta, which is exactly what §6.1 designs against.

## 6. What is mocked vs real (so you know what to wire next)

**Real:** auth, RBAC, org scoping, KYC approval workflow, pricing, idempotent ingest, the safety
gate, hash-chained ledger + trace, settlement state machine + dual control, audit, flags, metrics,
structured logging.

**Mocked (single named seams — swap without touching the flow):** Aadhaar eKYC, bank penny-drop,
Bharat Pashudhan sync, PFMS/DBT, licensed-PA payout execution, SMS provider.

**Dormant (flag-gated OFF):** collar telemetry, ONDC, consumer commerce.

See [`TECHNICAL_NOTES.md`](TECHNICAL_NOTES.md) for architecture/scaling and the ordered next-steps
list; [`WORKFLOW_GUIDE.md`](WORKFLOW_GUIDE.md) for role-by-role flows with diagrams; and
[`PCDF_Cooperative_Constitution.md`](PCDF_Cooperative_Constitution.md) for *why* the org/role model
is shaped this way (the UP cooperative structure it is grounded in).

func (r *Repo) ConsignmentsByIDs(ctx context.Context, ids []primitive.ObjectID) ([]domain.DCSConsignment, error) {
	cur, err := r.consignments.Find(ctx, bson.D{{Key: "_id", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$in", Value: ids}}}})
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	out := []domain.DCSConsignment{}
	if err := cur.All(ctx, &out); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return out, nil
}

// ClaimConsignments atomically flips DELIVERED consignments to ACCEPTED and
// stamps the pooling lot ID. Returns how many were actually claimed — fewer
// than requested means another lot raced us on at least one consignment.
func (r *Repo) ClaimConsignments(ctx context.Context, ids []primitive.ObjectID, bmcLotID primitive.ObjectID) (int64, error) {
	res, err := r.consignments.UpdateMany(ctx,
		bson.D{
			{Key: "_id", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$in", Value: ids}}},
			{Key: "status", Value: domain.ConsignmentStatusDelivered},
		},
		bson.D{{Key: "$set", Value: bson.D{
			{Key: "status", Value: domain.ConsignmentStatusAccepted},
			{Key: "bmc_lot_id", Value: bmcLotID},
		}}},
	)
	if err != nil {

=== requireScope ===
func (s *Service) requireScope(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, targetOrgID primitive.ObjectID, op string) error {
	err := s.orgs.RequireInScope(ctx, actor, targetOrgID)
	if err == nil {
		return nil
	}
	var app *httpx.AppError
	if errors.As(err, &app) && app.Status == http.StatusForbidden {
		s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "org scope denied",
			slog.String("op", op),
			slog.String("target_org_id", targetOrgID.Hex()),
			slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID),
			slog.String("actor_role", actor.RoleCode))
	}
	return err
}

// --- safety-gate predicates (§8.3) ---
//
// Pure functions so the refusal matrix is unit-testable without a database.
// Every mutation below ALSO re-checks the status inside the MongoDB update
// filter, so a concurrent QC block can never slip a bad lot through.

// canDispatchBMCLot: only a lot with a passing BMC rapid test may leave on a
// tanker. BLOCKED, QC_PENDING and OPEN lots stay put.
func canDispatchBMCLot(status string) bool {
	return status == domain.BMCLotStatusPassed
}

	// a trip cannot be delivered into an unrelated union's chilling centre.
	if err := s.orgs.RequireInScope(ctx, actor, req.BMCID); err != nil {
		s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "trip delivery rejected: BMC out of scope",
			slog.String("bmc_id", req.BMCID.Hex()), slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID))
		return nil, err
	}

	now := time.Now().UTC()
	matched, err := s.repo.markTripDelivered(ctx, trip.ID, req.BMCID, now)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, s.internal(ctx, "deliver trip: mark delivered", err)
	}
	if !matched { // lost a state race since the read above
		s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "trip delivery rejected: lost state race",
			slog.String("trip_id", tripID.Hex()), slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID))
		return nil, httpx.Conflict("INVALID_TRIP_STATE", "trip was modified concurrently; reload and retry")
	}

	consignmentIDs := make([]primitive.ObjectID, 0, len(trip.Stops))
	refs := make([]provenance.Ref, 0, len(trip.Stops))
	for _, stop := range trip.Stops {
		consignmentIDs = append(consignmentIDs, stop.ConsignmentID)
		refs = append(refs, provenance.Ref{
			EntityType: domain.EntityConsignment, EntityID: stop.ConsignmentID.Hex(), Relation: "delivered",
		})
	}
	if err := s.repo.markConsignmentsDelivered(ctx, consignmentIDs); err != nil {
		return nil, s.internal(ctx, "deliver trip: mark consignments delivered", err)
	}

	event, err := s.ledger.Append(ctx, provenance.AppendInput{
		Type:       domain.EventTripDelivered,
		EntityType: domain.EntityRouteTrip,
		EntityID:   trip.ID.Hex(),
		Refs:       refs,
		Actor:      provenance.ActorRef{PartyID: actor.PartyID, RoleCode: actor.RoleCode},
		OrgUnitID:  trip.UnionID.Hex(),
		Payload:    map[string]any{"bmc_id": req.BMCID.Hex()},
	})
	if err != nil {
		return nil, s.internal(ctx, "deliver trip: append provenance", err)
	}
	if err := s.repo.setTripProvenanceSeq(ctx, trip.ID, event.Seq); err != nil {
		return nil, s.internal(ctx, "deliver trip: set provenance seq", err)
	}

	trip.Status = domain.TripStatusDelivered
	trip.DeliveredToBMCID = &req.BMCID
	trip.DeliveredAt = &now
	trip.ProvenanceSeq = event.Seq
	s.log.InfoContext(ctx, "trip delivered",
		slog.String("trip_id", trip.ID.Hex()),
		slog.String("bmc_id", req.BMCID.Hex()),
		slog.Int("consignment_count", len(consignmentIDs)),
		slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID))
	return trip, nil
}

// handler adapts HTTP to the service: decode, call, respond — no business
// logic and no MongoDB in this file. Path and query ObjectIDs are parsed
// here (httpx.PathID / httpx.ParseID) so the service sees typed IDs only.
type handler struct {
	svc *service
}

// newHandler binds the handler to the service.
func newHandler(svc *service) *handler {
	return &handler{svc: svc}
}

// queryID parses an optional ObjectID query parameter: absent → NilObjectID.
func queryID(r *http.Request, param string) (primitive.ObjectID, error) {
	v := r.URL.Query().Get(param)
	if v == "" {
		return primitive.NilObjectID, nil
	}
	return httpx.ParseID(v, param)
}

func (h *handler) ingestTelemetry(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	var req TelemetryRequest
	if err := httpx.DecodeJSON(r, &req); err != nil {
		httpx.Error(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	ack, err := h.svc.IngestTelemetry(r.Context(), req)
	if err != nil {
		httpx.Error(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	httpx.JSON(w, http.StatusAccepted, ack)
}
// Package cattle owns the livestock side of Saathi: the animal registry keyed
// on the 12-digit Pashu Aadhaar ear-tag ID, the animal health history with its
// mock Bharat Pashudhan sync, the 1962 Mobile Veterinary Unit dispatch flow,
// the vernacular education hub, and the dormant collar-telemetry path that is
// provisioned but capability-gated until a government collar scheme lands
// (blueprint §9, §10).
package cattle

import (
	"log/slog"

	"github.com/go-chi/chi/v5"

	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/domain"
	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/deps"
	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/middleware"
)

// Register wires the cattle module under /cattle. The router mounts this
// subtree at /api/v1, so routes land at /api/v1/cattle/...
func Register(r chi.Router, d *deps.Deps) {
	log := d.Log.With(slog.String("module", "cattle"))
	repo := newRepository(d.DB)
	svc := newService(d, repo, log)
	h := newHandler(svc)

	r.Route("/cattle", func(r chi.Router) {
		r.Use(middleware.Authenticate(d.JWT))

		r.Route("/animals", func(r chi.Router) {
			// Registration: farmers self-serve; village-tier staff and the
			// health tier register on a farmer's behalf.
			r.With(middleware.RequireRoles(
				domain.RoleFarmer, domain.RoleSamitiSacheev, domain.RoleLRP,
				domain.RoleAITech, domain.RoleVeterinarian,
			)).Post("/", h.registerAnimal)

			// Any authenticated party may list; the service pins farmers and
			// plain session tokens to their own herd.
			r.With(middleware.RequireSession).Get("/", h.listAnimals)

			// Reads: the owner farmer, or care-circle roles. Consent gating
			// is a v2 TODO — see canViewAnimal in service.go.
			r.Group(func(r chi.Router) {
				r.Use(middleware.RequireRoles(
					domain.RoleFarmer, domain.RoleVeterinarian,
					domain.RoleAITech, domain.RoleMissionOfficial,
				))
				r.Get("/{animalID}", h.getAnimal)
				r.Get("/{animalID}/health-events", h.listHealthEvents)
			})

			r.With(middleware.RequireRoles(domain.RoleVeterinarian, domain.RoleAITech)).
				Post("/{animalID}/health-events", h.logHealthEvent)

			// Mock Bharat Pashudhan push (§9) — real integration is a swap of
			// the service internals, not an API change.
			r.With(middleware.RequireRoles(domain.RoleVeterinarian, domain.RolePCDFAdmin)).
				Post("/{animalID}/bp-sync", h.syncBharatPashudhan)
		})

		// 1962 Mobile Veterinary Unit dispatch loop (§10).
		r.Route("/mvu-cases", func(r chi.Router) {
			r.With(middleware.RequireRoles(domain.RoleFarmer)).Post("/", h.createMVUCase)
			r.With(middleware.RequireRoles(
				domain.RoleVeterinarian, domain.RoleMVUDriver,
				domain.RoleSamitiSacheev, domain.RoleMissionOfficial,
			)).Get("/", h.listMVUCases)
			r.With(middleware.RequireRoles(domain.RoleVeterinarian, domain.RoleMVUDriver)).
				Post("/{caseID}/dispatch", h.dispatchMVUCase)
			r.With(middleware.RequireRoles(domain.RoleVeterinarian)).
				Post("/{caseID}/close", h.closeMVUCase)
		})

		// Education hub (§10): published content is readable by everyone.
		r.Route("/education", func(r chi.Router) {
			r.With(middleware.RequireSession).Get("/", h.listEducation)
			r.With(middleware.RequireRoles(domain.RolePCDFAdmin, domain.RoleMissionOfficial)).
				Post("/", h.createEducation)
		})

		// Dormant collar backdoor (§9): the endpoint ships now but stays
		// behind flags.FlagCollarTelemetry — activation is a flag flip.
		r.With(middleware.RequireRoles(domain.RoleServiceAccount)).
			Post("/telemetry", h.ingestTelemetry)
	})
}

// findPartiesByRoles returns the distinct parties holding an ACTIVE assignment
// for any of the given role codes — used to notify KYC reviewers that a
// verification is pending. Capped so a broad role never floods the outbox.
func (r *repository) findPartiesByRoles(ctx context.Context, roleCodes []string, limit int64) ([]domain.Party, error) {
	assignFilter := bson.D{
		{Key: "role_code", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$in", Value: roleCodes}}},
		{Key: "status", Value: domain.RoleAssignmentActive},
	}
	cur, err := r.assignments.Find(ctx, assignFilter,
		options.Find().SetProjection(bson.D{{Key: "party_id", Value: 1}}).SetLimit(limit))
	if err != nil {
		return nil, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("find reviewer assignments: %w", err))
	}
	var rows []struct {
		PartyID primitive.ObjectID `bson:"party_id"`
	}
	if err := cur.All(ctx, &rows); err != nil {
		return nil, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("decode reviewer assignments: %w", err))
	}
	seen := make(map[primitive.ObjectID]struct{}, len(rows))
	ids := make([]primitive.ObjectID, 0, len(rows))
	for _, row := range rows {
		if _, ok := seen[row.PartyID]; ok {
			continue
		}
		seen[row.PartyID] = struct{}{}
		ids = append(ids, row.PartyID)

- **Endpoints:** `POST /collection/pours/ocr-extract` (photo→{fat,snf,confidence}, mock OCR);
  `POST /collection/invoices/approve` (DRAFT→APPROVED per DCS/date — reconcile daily-DRAFT lifecycle
  the FE uses with the backend's ISSUED/SETTLEMENT_PENDING/PAID).
- **Reconcile:** invoice status vocabulary (FE `DRAFT|APPROVED|SETTLED`); assurance on readings.
- Multi-role note: a Sacheev logging a pour is often also a farmer — pours are keyed by
  `farmer_party_id`, never the actor, so self-pour is fine.

### Piece 3 — Farmer — P0/P1
- Farmer dashboard aggregate `GET /dashboards/farmer/:partyId` (today/month/pending + 12-day trend).
- Cattle fields the FE reads (`age_months`/`lactation_no`/`avg_daily_yield_litres` OR FE maps from
  `birth_date`/`lactation_status` — decide). Health-event enums.
- Schemes (`/schemes` → reconcile with `/dbt/requests`), education/CMS content.

### Piece 4 — Logistics / Van + Delivery — P1
- `Consignment.seal_code` + `sealed_at` + `wavg_fat/wavg_snf` (§6.4 seal); `RouteStop.seal_code`
  verify (409 SEAL_MISMATCH). Van batch-mint code (Developer Note `BATCH`), GPS track.

### Piece 5 — BMC + Plant — P1
- Batch `contributing_dcs_ids` denormalized (§7.4); product outputs → QR wiring; LOTSUMMARY
  materialization at lot seal (consumer O(1) read).

### Piece 6 — Quality / Lab — P0
- `GET /quality/qc-queue`; `POST /quality/batches/{id}/certificate`; `GET .../trace-back`.
- Accept `AFM1` alias defensively so the gate can't be bypassed by name.

### Piece 7 — Traceability (public) — P1
- Serve the materialized LOTSUMMARY shape (societies + volume shares, farmers_total,
  consented `farmers_public` roster driven by `Party.public_consent`, quality).

### Piece 8 — Admin / governance — P0/P2
- `GET /admin/stats`, `GET /admin/parties?q`, `/admin/feature-flags` (reconcile `/admin/flags`),
  `/admin/products` master, `/admin/audit-events` (reconcile `/audit/logs`).

### Piece 9 — Onboarding-executive assisted flow — P1
- Onboarding-request entity + `POST /onboarding/requests`, list, approve/reject; `GET /parties?role=`.
- Relation: approve → creates Party + KYCRecord + RoleAssignment.

### Piece 10 — Cattle / 1962 — P1
- `POST /cattle/animals/{id}/health-events` (POST exists? confirm); vet-request↔mvu-case enum reconcile.

### Piece 11 — Commerce / Store / Delivery — P2 (dormant)
- `GET /products` catalogue, orders, delivery — behind `consumer_commerce_enabled` flag.

### Piece 12 — Dashboards + Live sync — P1
- `GET /dashboards/society/:dcsId`; SSE already emits `kyc.queue_changed` — add
  `settlement.changed`, `quality.changed`, `pour.recorded` topics the FE `useLiveSync` listens for.

}

// markConsignmentsDelivered transitions every listed PICKED_UP consignment
// to DELIVERED (bulk companion of the trip delivery).
func (r *repo) markConsignmentsDelivered(ctx context.Context, ids []primitive.ObjectID) error {
	_, err := r.consignments.UpdateMany(ctx,
		bson.D{
			{Key: "_id", Value: bson.D{{Key: "$in", Value: ids}}},
			{Key: "status", Value: domain.ConsignmentStatusPickedUp},
		},
		bson.D{{Key: "$set", Value: bson.D{{Key: "status", Value: domain.ConsignmentStatusDelivered}}}})
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("mark consignments delivered: %w", err)
	}
	return nil
}
```

### 3.5 `plant` — BMC lots → batches → product lots → QR (safety-gate enforcement)

| Method | Path | Auth | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET/POST | `/plant/bmc-lots` | role:`BMC_OPERATOR` (+ readers on GET) | Pool delivered consignments into a lot. |
| POST | `/plant/bmc-lots/{id}/close` | role:`BMC_OPERATOR` | `OPEN → QC_PENDING` (+ chilling temp). |
| POST | `/plant/bmc-lots/{id}/dispatch` | role:`BMC_OPERATOR` | **Only a `PASSED` lot may dispatch** (else `422 SAFETY_GATE_BLOCKED`). |
| GET/POST | `/plant/batches` | role:`PLANT_OPERATOR` (+ readers) | Batch from **PASSED+DISPATCHED** lots; each lot atomically claimed `→ POOLED` (one batch only). |
| GET | `/plant/batches/{id}` | role (readers) | Batch detail + its QC results. |
| POST | `/plant/batches/{id}/complete` | role:`PLANT_OPERATOR` | Requires plant-lab `PASSED` → `COMPLETED`. |
| POST | `/plant/product-lots` | role:`PLANT_OPERATOR, PLANT_LAB_ANALYST` | Only from a `COMPLETED` batch. |
| POST | `/plant/product-lots/{id}/recall` | role:`PCDF_ADMIN, PLANT_LAB_ANALYST` | FSSAI recall path. |
| POST | `/plant/qrs` | role:`PLANT_OPERATOR, PLANT_LAB_ANALYST` | Issues an HMAC-signed QR (`qr_code` + signed token over `productLotID.Hex()`). |
| GET | `/plant/qrs` | role:(same) | List QRs. |
```

```text
/opt/homebrew/bin/pdftotext
# Saathi Backend ⇄ Frontend Alignment Spec

> **Goal:** align the Go backend (`parag-saathi-be`) to the 80%-built React Native app
> (`parag-saathi-fe`), reconciled with the **Developer Technical Note** (the authoritative
> traceability build spec). Integration (wiring the FE mappers) comes later — **first the backend
> is made spec-clean and capable**: we ADD genuinely-missing fields/endpoints/relations; we do NOT
> pollute the backend with FE-name aliases (those are FE-mapper fixes at integration time).
>
> This doc is derived from a 3-agent deep analysis of both repos (identity round) + the full
> Developer Note. It is the running plan; each **Piece** is fixed completely before the next.

---

## 0. What's already aligned (no work needed)

- **Wire conventions**: base `/api/v1`, success `{data, meta?}`, error `{error:{code,message,details?}}`,
  `Authorization: Bearer`, refresh-on-401, snake_case wire, ObjectID hex ids, ISO-8601 / `YYYY-MM-DD`
  dates, `client_event_id` idempotency. ✅
- **Module mounts** match the FE's `backend-integration.md` map exactly (identity, orgs, collection,
  logistics, plant, quality, settlement, cattle, platformops, publictrace). ✅
- **Multi-role model** (one phone = one Party = many org-scoped RoleAssignments) — the farmer+sachiv
  picker works: `/parties/me` returns all usable assignments org-enriched; `/auth/role/select` mints
  a role-scoped token for either. ✅ (verified live)

---

## 1. Cross-cutting mismatch catalog (from the identity-round analysis)

These recur across every entity. Classification drives WHO fixes it:

| Kind | Rule | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| **Field-name mismatch** (backend HAS the data under a different name) | **FE-mapper fix at integration** — backend stays canonical | `total_litres`→`total_quantity_litres`, invoice `date`→`invoice_date`, batch `volume_litres`→`input_litres`, QC `passed`→`pass`/`overall_pass`, `recorded_by_party_id`→`analyst_party_id`, MVU `created_at`→`requested_at`, health `by_role`→`recorded_by_role` |
| **Enum value mismatch** (spec canonical differs) | **fix the WRONG side vs Developer Note** | 🔴 QC `AFM1`→**`AFLATOXIN_M1`** (FE sends wrong → silently bypasses the aflatoxin gate — FE fix, safety-critical); pour `ANALYZER_AUTO`→**`ANALYZER_DIRECT`** (FE fix); org `UNION`↔`MILK_UNION`, `PLANT`↔`PROCESSING_PLANT`; health `AI`↔`ARTIFICIAL_INSEMINATION`, `ILLNESS`↔`DISEASE_REPORT`; QC subject `PLANT_BATCH`→`PROCESSING_BATCH` |
| **Missing backend field** (Developer Note / FE needs it) | **backend ADDS it** | `assurance` A\|B\|C on pour, `rate_chart_version` on pour, `seal_code`+`wavg_fat/snf` on consignment, `Party.public_consent`, cattle yield/lactation fields, batch `contributing_dcs_ids`, LOTSUMMARY materialization |
| **Missing backend endpoint** (FE 404s) | **backend BUILDS it** | onboarding-request queue, `GET /parties?role=`, `/quality/qc-queue`, certificate + trace-back, OCR extract, `/dashboards/*`, `/products`, CMS `/content?since=` |
| **Role/tier catalog gap** | **backend ADDS to catalog** | `ONBOARDING_EXECUTIVE`, `STORE_MANAGER`, `MTLS` tier |

**Danger findings (silent breaks) — must not ship:**
1. 🔴 **QC `AFM1` vs `AFLATOXIN_M1`** — the FE posts `name:"AFM1"`; the backend gate only matches `AFLATOXIN_M1`, so **the aflatoxin safety gate silently does not fire**. (FE fix; backend could also accept the alias defensively.)
2. 🔴 Consignment `total_litres`, invoice `date`/amounts, batch `volume_litres`/`qc_status` — all silently default to 0/'' in the FE (mapper reads wrong keys).
3. 🔴 Role-picker crash: FE `ROLES[code]` is unguarded; a backend-only code (`ORGANISING_MANAGER`, `CONSUMER`) in an assignment throws. (FE fix: guard + add codes.)

---

## 2. Per-Piece build roadmap (one role/functionality at a time)

Priorities: **P0** = FE calls it today and it 404s / breaks integration. **P1** = Developer-Note
correctness. **P2** = dormant / Phase-3.

### ✅ Piece 1 — Identity / Auth core  — **DONE**
- Added roles `ONBOARDING_EXECUTIVE`, `STORE_MANAGER` to `AllRoles` + `RequiredKYCTier` + granter
  matrix; `ONBOARDING_EXECUTIVE` wired as a KYC reviewer + enrolment granter (peer of `ORGANISING_MANAGER`)
  via new `domain.OnboardingReviewerRoles`.
- Added KYC tier `MTLS` (alias of `SERVICE`).
- Added `Party.public_consent` (§6.7) + `PATCH /parties/me {public_consent}`.
- Seed: the Sacheev (9000000001, Ramesh) now ALSO holds a FARMER role → login role-picker exercised.
- **Verified live:** multi-role `/parties/me` (SAMITI_SACHEEV + FARMER, org-enriched), role-select on
  both, `public_consent` toggle, and `ONBOARDING_EXECUTIVE`/`STORE_MANAGER` grants accepted.

```text
   6. High-level system architecture




Architectural stance: event-driven microservices behind a gateway, BFFs tailoring payloads per
client (the farmer app payload is radically simpler than the official console), an append-only



CONFIDENTIAL · PYAAS · Saathi — Developer Architecture Framework                                                                   Page 8 of 20
provenance store as the source of truth for traceability, and a thin, well-guarded integration
edge to the DPI systems.



   7. Milk traceability — the provenance graph
7.1 The ID chain




CONFIDENTIAL · PYAAS · Saathi — Developer Architecture Framework                           Page 9 of 20
7.2 Entity model (simplified ER)




CONFIDENTIAL · PYAAS · Saathi — Developer Architecture Framework   Page 10 of 20
7.3 Why append-only / ledger-style
Traceability is only trustworthy if it cannot be quietly rewritten. Store provenance edges as
immutable events; corrections are new events that supersede (never overwrite) prior ones. This
gives you audit-grade recall capability (FSSAI food-recall requirement) and tamper-evidence. A graph
database (or a hash-chained event log projected into a graph) fits the many-to-many pooling
naturally.

7.4 The honest limit of pack-level traceability
Because milk is pooled at the can, BMC, and plant silo, a finished pack does not trace to one farmer.
It traces to the set of contributing samitis in that batch (with approximate volume proportions).
Design the consumer view accordingly: "This pack's batch was made from milk collected on 3–4 Jul
from N samitis in Barabanki district" + quality certificate. Samiti-level granularity is achievable
and truthful; per-farmer-per-pack is not. Don't promise the impossible in the UI or to the
government.
```
</details></tool-use>

_**Agent - sidechain (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-08 20:27:21Z)**_

Confirmed the claim by reading the actual code. The defect is real.

**Evidence:**

1. `CreateBatch` (service.go:411-456) calls `requireScope(actor, req.PlantID)` only (line 416) — it authorizes the actor against the *plant* being written to, and nothing else.
2. The BMC lots are loaded via `repo.BMCLotsByIDs` (repo.go:108) — a bare `{_id: {$in: ids}}` query with **no** `bmc_id`/scope/org filter.
3. The only per-lot validation is `canPoolBMCLot(lot.Status)` == `DISPATCHED` (service.go:442). There is **zero** check that `lot.BMCID` sits within the plant's union/federation subtree or the actor's scope.
4. `ClaimBMCLots` (repo.go:158-173) then unconditionally flips each referenced lot `DISPATCHED → POOLED` and stamps `batch_id`, filtered only by `_id ∈ ids` and `status == DISPATCHED`.

The org model (domain/orgunit.go) confirms plant and BMC are *siblings* under a `MILK_UNION` (or `FEDERATION`), and `orgscope.InScope` is pure ancestry — so no ancestor relation exists to accidentally constrain the BMC. The `ListBMCLots` sibling-BMC comment justifies skipping an ancestry check for *listing within a union*, but nothing bounds pooling to the plant's own union.

**Exploitability is concrete, not theoretical:** `ListBMCLots` (service.go:393-404) only scope-checks when `BMCID` is set AND the caller is a `BMC_OPERATOR`. A `PLANT_OPERATOR` is an authorized reader of `GET /plant/bmc-lots` (module.go:33-36) and, calling it with no `BMCID` filter, receives **every** BMC lot system-wide — including union B's `DISPATCHED` lots and their IDs. They then POST those IDs to `/plant/batches` and get a 201.

**How it misbehaves:**
- Cross-scope write: an actor with no scope over union B mutates union B's lot (`DISPATCHED → POOLED`, stamped with union A's `batch_id`) — an IDOR-class authorization gap. Contrast `CreateBMCLot`, which does scope-check `req.BMCID`.
- Denial: union B's legitimate plant can no longer pool that lot (the `status == DISPATCHED` claim filter no longer matches).
- Provenance corruption: the `batch.created` ledger event and downstream product-lot/QR/LOTSUMMARY now attribute union B's societies/farmers into union A's batch, breaking the "honest samiti-set provenance" the public QR trace (§7) promises.

Nothing in the handler (handler.go:129-148, only non-empty check), tests (service_test.go has no union/scope coverage), or repo compensates.

**Suggested fix:** In `CreateBatch`, after loading the lots, resolve the plant's scope root (its parent union/federation via `org.ParentID`, or the plant itself) and require each `lot.BMCID` to be within that subtree — e.g. `s.orgs.InScope(ctx, plantScopeRoot, lot.BMCID)` — rejecting foreign lots with a 403/422 before `ClaimBMCLots`. The same enumeration hole should be closed in `ListBMCLots` for non-`BMC_OPERATOR` readers by scoping results to the caller's org subtree.

// EducationContent is a vernacular audio/video/infographic item for the
// education hub (blueprint §10) — icon-navigable, pre-cacheable offline.
type EducationContent struct {
	ID          primitive.ObjectID `bson:"_id,omitempty" json:"id"`
	Topic       string             `bson:"topic"      json:"topic"` // CLEAN_MILKING, FEED_RATION, BREED_CARE...
	Title       string             `bson:"title"      json:"title"`
	Language    string             `bson:"language"   json:"language"`
	MediaType   string             `bson:"media_type" json:"media_type"` // AUDIO, VIDEO, INFOGRAPHIC
	MediaURL    string             `bson:"media_url"  json:"media_url"`
	DurationSec int                `bson:"duration_sec,omitempty" json:"duration_sec,omitempty"`
	Published   bool               `bson:"published"  json:"published"`
	CreatedAt   time.Time          `bson:"created_at" json:"created_at"`
}
===repo list impl===
// ListPublishedEducation returns a page of published content filtered by
// topic and/or language, newest first, plus the total match count.
func (r *repository) ListPublishedEducation(ctx context.Context, topic, language string, page httpx.Page) ([]domain.EducationContent, int64, error) {
	filter := bson.D{{Key: "published", Value: true}}
	if topic != "" {
		filter = append(filter, bson.E{Key: "topic", Value: topic})
	}
	if language != "" {
		filter = append(filter, bson.E{Key: "language", Value: language})
	}
	total, err := r.education.CountDocuments(ctx, filter)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, 0, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("count education content: %w", err))
	}
	cur, err := r.education.Find(ctx, filter, options.Find().
		SetSort(bson.D{{Key: "created_at", Value: -1}}).
		SetSkip(page.Offset).SetLimit(page.Limit))
	if err != nil {
		return nil, 0, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("list education content: %w", err))
	}
	out := []domain.EducationContent{}
	if err := cur.All(ctx, &out); err != nil {
		return nil, 0, httpx.Internal(fmt.Errorf("decode education content: %w", err))
	}
	return out, total, nil
}

func (s *service) ListMVUCases(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, dcsID primitive.ObjectID, status string, page httpx.Page) ([]domain.MVUCase, int64, error) {
	if status != "" {
		if _, ok := validMVUStatuses[status]; !ok {
			return nil, 0, httpx.BadRequest("INVALID_MVU_STATUS", "status must be one of REQUESTED, DISPATCHED, ARRIVED, CLOSED, CANCELLED")
		}
	}
	if !dcsID.IsZero() {
		if err := s.d.Orgs.RequireInScope(ctx, actor, dcsID); err != nil {
			return nil, 0, s.logFailure(ctx, "list mvu cases scope check", err,
				slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID),
				slog.String("dcs_id", dcsID.Hex()))
		}
	}
	cases, total, err := s.repo.ListMVUCases(ctx, dcsID, status, page)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, 0, s.logFailure(ctx, "list mvu cases", err)
	}
	return cases, total, nil
}

## The audit found 23 confirmed issues (adversarially verified). This round I fixed all the risky ones:

**🔴 Safety-critical**
- **AFM1 gate bypass** — the audit caught that my earlier fix was *incomplete*: `NormalizeTestName` only ran inside the evaluator, but two guards ran first on the raw name, so `AFM1` still 400'd before normalization. Now names are canonicalized at the very top of `recordQCResult`, so the aflatoxin gate can't be dodged by any alias.

**🟠 Money / PII / integrity**
- **Settlement paid without a bank** — `Execute` was crediting SUCCESS + marking invoices PAID even for farmers with no verified bank. Now: no verified bank → payout `FAILED`, invoice stays unpaid, batch ends `PARTIAL` (re-executable), and no false "credited" SMS. Seeded farmers get realistic verified banks so real settlement works.
- **MVU case PII leak** — any field role could list every farmer's vet cases (symptoms) federation-wide; and farmers couldn't see their own. Now farmers are forced to self, scoped roles must name an in-scope DCS.
- **Cross-union pooling (×2)** — `CreateBatch` now rejects BMC lots outside the plant's union; `CreateBMCLot` now verifies each consignment's trip was actually delivered to *this* BMC (`WRONG_DELIVERY_BMC`). Plus the earlier trip-IDOR and deliver-scope fixes.

package httpapi

import (
	"github.com/go-chi/chi/v5"

	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/modules/cattle"
	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/modules/collection"
	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/modules/dashboards"
	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/modules/identity"
	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/modules/logistics"
	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/modules/orgs"
	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/modules/plant"
	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/modules/platformops"
	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/modules/publictrace"
	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/modules/quality"
	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/modules/settlement"
	"github.com/pyaas/saathi-backend/internal/platform/deps"
)

// RegisterModules mounts every domain module under /api/v1.
//
// Module contract: each package under internal/modules/<name> exposes
//
//	func Register(r chi.Router, d *deps.Deps)
//
// and mounts its own subtree with its own auth/RBAC middleware. Modules are
// the future microservice seams — they may import domain and platform
// packages, but NEVER each other; cross-module reactions go through the
// event bus.
func RegisterModules(api chi.Router, d *deps.Deps) {
	// publictrace first — it mounts /public without auth.
	publictrace.Register(api, d)

	identity.Register(api, d)
	orgs.Register(api, d)
	cattle.Register(api, d)
	collection.Register(api, d)
	logistics.Register(api, d)
	plant.Register(api, d)
	quality.Register(api, d)
	settlement.Register(api, d)
	platformops.Register(api, d)
	dashboards.Register(api, d)
}
```
</details></tool-use>

 `/Users/divyanshmangla/parag-saathi-fe/docs/api-contract.md`

```text
1	# Saathi API contract (frontend ↔ backend)
2	
3	The mobile app ships with an in-app mock backend; flipping
4	`EXPO_PUBLIC_API_MODE=http` + `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` points the same typed
5	calls at the real API. **This file is the request-for-implementation for the
6	backend team.** The authoritative, always-current definitions (exact TS
7	request/response types + reference semantics in the `mock` bodies) live in
8	[`src/core/api/endpoints/`](../src/core/api/endpoints/) with the shared domain
9	model in [`src/core/types/domain.ts`](../src/core/types/domain.ts).
10	
11	Conventions (matching the implemented backend): success envelope
12	`{"data": ..., "meta"?}`; error envelope `{"error": {"code", "message", "details"?}}`;
13	snake_case wire fields (the app maps them to its camelCase domain in
14	`mapRequest`/`mapResponse` per endpoint); `Authorization: Bearer <access token>`;
15	rotating refresh tokens via `POST /auth/refresh` (the client auto-refreshes
16	once on 401 and retries); IDs opaque strings; timestamps ISO-8601.
17	
18	## Auth / identity (`auth.ts`) - ✅ aligned with `parag-saathi-be` `internal/modules/identity`
19	| Method & path | Purpose |
20	| --- | --- |
21	| `POST /auth/otp/request` | `{phone}` → `{phone, expires_at, dev_otp?}` (dev_otp only in dev mode) |
22	| `POST /auth/otp/verify` | `{phone, otp}` → `{access_token (SESSION), refresh_token, party}`; find-or-creates the Party on first login (§4.1) |
23	| `GET /parties/me` | → `{party, assignments (+org_name/org_type/org_code), kyc?}` - feeds the role switcher |
24	| `POST /auth/role/select` | `{role_assignment_id}` → `{access_token (ROLE-scoped), role_code, org_unit_id}` |
25	| `POST /auth/refresh` | `{refresh_token}` → rotated token pair (single-flight in the client) |
26	| `POST /auth/logout` | `{refresh_token}` - revoke (called fire-and-forget on sign-out) |
27	| `PATCH /parties/me` | `{full_name?, preferred_language?}` |
28	| `POST /kyc/aadhaar` | `{aadhaar_number, consent, requested_tier}` - number transient, never stored (§18-A) |
29	| `POST /kyc/bank` | `{account_number, ifsc}` - penny-drop; only masked tail persisted |
30	
31	## Real-time & live badges (`events.ts` + `sse.ts`) - ✅ PR #2
32	| Method & path | Purpose |
33	| --- | --- |

365	// QC. Only BMC lots and processing batches carry the software safety gate.
366	func (s *service) loadGateSubject(ctx context.Context, subjectType string, subjectID primitive.ObjectID) (gateSubject, error) {
367		switch subjectType {

369			lot, err := s.repo.findBMCLot(ctx, subjectID)
370			if err != nil {
371				return gateSubject{}, err
372			}
373			if lot.Status != domain.BMCLotStatusQCPending {
374				return gateSubject{}, httpx.Conflict("SUBJECT_NOT_QC_PENDING", "bmc lot is in status "+lot.Status+" — only QC_PENDING subjects can be gated")
375			}
376			return gateSubject{entityType: domain.EntityBMCLot, orgUnitID: lot.BMCID, status: lot.Status}, nil
377	
378		case domain.QCSubjectProcessingBatch:
379			batch, err := s.repo.findBatch(ctx, subjectID)
380			if err != nil {
381				return gateSubject{}, err
382			}
383			if batch.Status != domain.BatchStatusQCPending {
384				return gateSubject{}, httpx.Conflict("SUBJECT_NOT_QC_PENDING", "processing batch is in status "+batch.Status+" — only QC_PENDING subjects can be gated")
385			}
386			return gateSubject{entityType: domain.EntityBatch, orgUnitID: batch.PlantID, status: batch.Status}, nil
387	
388		case domain.QCSubjectDCSConsignment:
389			return gateSubject{}, httpx.Unprocessable("SUBJECT_NOT_GATE_ELIGIBLE", "DCS consignments are not gate subjects — gate at the BMC lot or processing batch")
390	
391		default:
392			return gateSubject{}, httpx.BadRequest("INVALID_SUBJECT_TYPE", "subject_type must be one of "+domain.QCSubjectBMCLot+", "+domain.QCSubjectProcessingBatch)
393		}

396	// applyGate routes the conditional verdict write to the subject's collection,
397	// mapping the verdict onto that subject kind's status constants.
398	func (s *service) applyGate(ctx context.Context, subjectType string, subjectID, resultID primitive.ObjectID, pass bool, blockReason string) (bool, error) {
399		switch subjectType {
400		case domain.QCSubjectBMCLot:
401			status := domain.BMCLotStatusBlocked
402			if pass {
403				status = domain.BMCLotStatusPassed
404			}
405			return s.repo.gateBMCLot(ctx, subjectID, resultID, status, blockReason)
406		case domain.QCSubjectProcessingBatch:
407			status := domain.BatchStatusBlocked
408			if pass {
409				status = domain.BatchStatusPassed
410			}
411			return s.repo.gateBatch(ctx, subjectID, resultID, status, blockReason)
412		default:
413			return false, httpx.BadRequest("INVALID_SUBJECT_TYPE", "subject_type is not gate-eligible")
414		}
415	}
416	
417	// listQCResults returns a page of results, newest first. When the filter
418	// identifies an org-owned subject, the caller must be in that org's scope.
419	// A zero subjectID means "no subject filter".
420	func (s *service) listQCResults(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, subjectType string, subjectID primitive.ObjectID, page httpx.Page) ([]domain.QCResult, int64, error) {
421		if subjectType != "" && !isValidSubjectType(subjectType) {
422			return nil, 0, httpx.BadRequest("INVALID_SUBJECT_TYPE", "unknown subject_type "+subjectType)
423		}
424		if !subjectID.IsZero() && subjectType == "" {
425			return nil, 0, httpx.BadRequest("MISSING_SUBJECT_TYPE", "subject_id requires subject_type")
426		}
427		if !subjectID.IsZero() {
428			if err := s.requireSubjectScope(ctx, actor, subjectType, subjectID); err != nil {
429				return nil, 0, err
430			}
431		}
432		return s.repo.listResults(ctx, subjectType, subjectID, page)
433	}
434	
435	// getQCResult returns one result (its tests carry the stored pass verdicts),
436	// enforcing the subject org scope.
437	func (s *service) getQCResult(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, resultID primitive.ObjectID) (*domain.QCResult, error) {
438		result, err := s.repo.findResultByID(ctx, resultID)
439		if err != nil {
440			return nil, err
441		}
442		if err := s.requireSubjectScope(ctx, actor, result.SubjectType, result.SubjectID); err != nil {
443			return nil, err
444		}
445		return result, nil
446	}
447	
448	// requireSubjectScope enforces the caller's org scope over the org unit that
449	// owns a QC subject. Subjects that no longer resolve (or subject types that
450	// carry no org) skip the check — the role gate still applies.
451	func (s *service) requireSubjectScope(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, subjectType string, subjectID primitive.ObjectID) error {
452		orgID, err := s.subjectOrgUnit(ctx, subjectType, subjectID)
453		if err != nil {
454			return err
455		}
456		if orgID.IsZero() {
457			return nil
458		}
459		if err := s.deps.Orgs.RequireInScope(ctx, actor, orgID); err != nil {
460			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "qc read scope denied",
461				slog.String("subject_type", subjectType),
462				slog.String("subject_id", subjectID.Hex()),
463				slog.String("subject_org_unit_id", orgID.Hex()),
464				slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID),
465				slog.Any("err", err))
466			return err
467		}
468		return nil
469	}

471	// subjectOrgUnit resolves the owning org unit of a subject, or the zero
472	// ObjectID when the subject is missing or not an org-owned gate subject.
473	func (s *service) subjectOrgUnit(ctx context.Context, subjectType string, subjectID primitive.ObjectID) (primitive.ObjectID, error) {
474		switch subjectType {
475		case domain.QCSubjectBMCLot:
476			lot, err := s.repo.findBMCLot(ctx, subjectID)
477			if err != nil {
478				return primitive.NilObjectID, ignoreNotFound(err)
479			}
480			return lot.BMCID, nil
481		case domain.QCSubjectProcessingBatch:
482			batch, err := s.repo.findBatch(ctx, subjectID)
483			if err != nil {
484				return primitive.NilObjectID, ignoreNotFound(err)
485			}
486			return batch.PlantID, nil
487		default:
488			return primitive.NilObjectID, nil
489		}
490	}

492	// ignoreNotFound swallows 404 AppErrors and passes everything else through.
493	func ignoreNotFound(err error) error {
494		var appErr *httpx.AppError
495		if errors.As(err, &appErr) && appErr.Status == http.StatusNotFound {
496			return nil
497		}
498		return err
499	}

502	func isValidSubjectType(t string) bool {
503		switch t {
504		case domain.QCSubjectDCSConsignment, domain.QCSubjectBMCLot, domain.QCSubjectProcessingBatch:
505			return true
506		default:
507			return false
508		}
509	}

513		out := make([]domain.QCTest, 0, len(in))
514		for _, t := range in {
515			out = append(out, domain.QCTest{Name: t.Name, Value: t.Value, Unit: t.Unit})

90	// resolver errors) pass through untouched so client-facing semantics never

92	func (s *Service) internalErr(ctx context.Context, op string, err error, attrs ...any) error {
93		var appErr *httpx.AppError
94		if errors.As(err, &appErr) {
95			return appErr
96		}

102	// VerifyQRToken checks a stored signed token in the format QR issuance
103	// (plant module signQRToken) mints: "base64url(qr_code|product_lot_id_hex|
104	// issued_unix)" + "." + hex(HMAC-SHA256(secret, decoded payload)), where
105	// product_lot_id_hex is productLotID.Hex(). The HMAC is computed over the
106	// DECODED payload bytes — exactly what issuance signed. The comparison is
107	// constant-time so a forger learns nothing from response timing.
108	func VerifyQRToken(secret, token string) bool {
109		payloadB64, signature, found := strings.Cut(token, ".")
110		if !found || payloadB64 == "" || signature == "" {
111			return false // malformed: no payload/signature split
112		}
113		payload, err := base64.RawURLEncoding.DecodeString(payloadB64)
114		if err != nil || len(payload) == 0 {
115			return false // malformed: payload is not valid base64url
116		}
117		expected := auth.HMACHash(secret, string(payload))
118		return auth.ConstantTimeEqual(expected, signature)
119	}

121	// ScanQR resolves one consumer QR scan into the honest provenance view
122	// (§7.4): product + plant + lab certificate + the SET of contributing

124	func (s *Service) ScanQR(ctx context.Context, qrCode string) (*QRScanResponse, error) {
