---

## 5. Onboarding → verification → position (the full relation)

```
new user logs in (OTP)                → Party, tier MINIMAL, no roles → "pending" screen
  ↓ POST /kyc/aadhaar                  → KYCRecord PENDING  +  KYC_PENDING notification queued to reviewers/super-admin  +  live SSE badge
  ↓ reviewer POST /kyc/{id}/approve    → tier upgraded, record VERIFIED, party notified
  ↓ admin POST /roles/assignments      → the POSITION (role_code @ org) — a RoleAssignment
  ↓ user re-login → GET /auth/roles    → sees the role → /auth/role/select → dashboard
```
The **assisted** variant (`/onboarding/requests` approve) does all of party+KYC+role atomically for
an executive-submitted request.

---

## 6. Error codes to handle

`UNAUTHORIZED` (401) · `FORBIDDEN` (403) · `KYC_TIER_INSUFFICIENT` (403, has `details`) ·
`SAFETY_GATE_BLOCKED` (422) · `DUAL_CONTROL_VIOLATION` (403) · `IMPLAUSIBLE_VALUES` (422) ·
`FARMER_NOT_MEMBER` (422) · `WRONG_DELIVERY_BMC` / `CONSIGNMENT_NOT_DELIVERED` (422) ·
`SHIFT_CONSIGNED` / `POUR_CONSIGNED` (409) · `KYC_NOT_PENDING` / `KYC_SELF_REVIEW` (409/403) ·
`FEATURE_DISABLED` (403) · `INVALID_ID` (400) · `RATE_LIMITED` (429) ·
`NOT_FOUND` / `CONFLICT` / `MALFORMED_JSON`.

---

## 7. Real-time & offline
- **SSE** for live badges (see §4). Multi-replica prod fans out via Redis (transparent to the app).
- **Offline**: pours are idempotent on `client_event_id` — queue locally, replay via
  `/collection/pours/batch-sync`; a replay returns the stored pour with `idempotent_replay: true`.

---

## 8. What's mocked server-side (so you can plan real flows)
Aadhaar eKYC, bank penny-drop, PFMS/DBT, Bharat Pashudhan sync, licensed-PA payout, SMS provider
are single named mock seams — the wire shapes are final; only the provider swaps later.
On-device OCR is the design (§8.2): the app OCRs the analyzer photo, uploads it (gets a key), and
posts a reading with `mode=PHOTO_OCR` + `photo_object_key` + `ocr_confidence`. There is **no**
server `/pours/ocr-extract` — remove that mock and wire on-device OCR → `POST /collection/readings`.

---

## 9. FE-side reconciliation checklist (do these in the mappers before `MODE=http`)

The backend is canonical; adjust the FE `mapRequest`/`mapResponse` to these names/enums.

**Safety-critical**
- QC test name: send **`AFLATOXIN_M1`** (not `AFM1`). Subject type: **`PROCESSING_BATCH`** (not `PLANT_BATCH`), **`BMC_LOT`** (not `BMC_INTAKE`). *(The backend now also normalizes `AFM1`, but send canonical.)*

**Pour**
- Read weighted rate from **`rate_per_litre`**; source enum is **`ANALYZER_DIRECT`** (not `ANALYZER_AUTO`), `PHOTO_OCR`, `MANUAL`. New readable fields: `assurance` (A|B|C), `rate_chart_version`. Backend pour status is only `RECORDED|SUPERSEDED|CANCELLED` (no IN_LOT/INVOICED/PAID — derive lifecycle client-side).

**Consignment / lot**
- `total_quantity_litres` (not `total_litres`); `avg_fat_pct`/`avg_snf_pct` are the weighted averages; new: `seal_code`, `sealed_at`, `assurance`. Status enum: `OPEN|DISPATCHED|PICKED_UP|DELIVERED|ACCEPTED|REJECTED`.

**Invoice**
- `invoice_date` (not `date`); amount is `total_amount` + `total_quantity_litres` (no gross/deductions/net on the invoice — settlement lives on the settlement batch). Status: `ISSUED|SETTLEMENT_PENDING|PAID|HOLD`.

**Batch / QC**
- Batch: `input_litres` (not `volume_litres`); QC verdict from batch `status` (`PASSED`/`BLOCKED`) + `QCResult.overall_pass`; new `contributing_dcs_ids`. QC test: `pass` (not `passed`), result `overall_pass`, `analyst_party_id` (not `recorded_by_party_id`).

**BMC lot**
- Status enum `OPEN|QC_PENDING|PASSED|BLOCKED|DISPATCHED|POOLED`; trips are `route_trip_ids` (array). Trip delivered field: `delivered_to_bmc_id`.

**Org / roles**
- Org types: `FEDERATION|MILK_UNION|PROCESSING_PLANT|BMC|DCS` (map `UNION`→`MILK_UNION`, `PLANT`→`PROCESSING_PLANT`). Add `ORGANISING_MANAGER` and `CONSUMER` to the FE role map and **guard `ROLES[code]`** against unknown codes so the picker never crashes. `ONBOARDING_EXECUTIVE` and `STORE_MANAGER` are valid backend roles. KYC tier: `SERVICE` (backend) ↔ `MTLS` (both accepted).

**Cattle / MVU**
- MVU list: read `requested_at` (not `created_at`); pass `farmer_party_id` for a farmer's own list. Health event: `recorded_by_role`, sync via `bp_sync_status` (`SYNCED`); enums `ARTIFICIAL_INSEMINATION`/`DISEASE_REPORT`.

**Logistics pickup**
- Path is keyed by the **consignment id**: `POST /logistics/trips/{tripID}/stops/{consignmentID}/pickup` — send the consignment id in the `{consignmentID}` slot (not the DCS id), and include `temp_c`.

**Never send empty-string IDs** (e.g. `org_unit_id: ""`) — omit the field.

51	## 2. The global request pipeline (every request passes through this)
52	
53	Order is exactly as wired in `internal/httpapi/router.go`.

55	```mermaid

57	    IN(["HTTP request"]) --> RID["RequestID\n(correlation id)"]
58	    RID --> RIP["RealIP"]
59	    RIP --> MET["Metrics\n(Prometheus)"]
60	    MET --> LOG["RequestLogger\n(1 structured line/request)"]

64	    TO --> BR{"route?"}

69	    BR -->|"unmatched"| NF["JSON 404 / 405\n(never chi plaintext)"]

72	Key facts to note for analysis:
73	- **Rate limiting runs before auth** (cheap abuse protection). It's per-IP; `REDIS_URL` makes it shared across replicas.

75	- **Public routes and the operational endpoints deliberately skip authentication.**
76	- A single `request_id` threads through the request log and every module log line — that's how you trace one request end-to-end.

232	## 8. Concurrency: "two at once → only one wins" (no Redis lock)
233	
234	```mermaid
235	flowchart TD
236	    A["Reviewer A: approve KYC X"] --> DB{{"MongoDB atomic update\nupdate WHERE _id=X AND status=PENDING"}}
237	    B["Reviewer B: approve KYC X\n(same instant)"] --> DB

239	    DB -->|matched 0 docs| LOSE["other → 409 KYC_NOT_PENDING"]
240	```
241	
242	The state check lives **inside** the update filter, so the check-and-write is one indivisible operation.

14	## 1. Ground rules that apply to EVERY endpoint
15	
16	### 1.1 Identifiers — ObjectID everywhere, business keys are separate
17	- Every document's `_id` is a **MongoDB ObjectID** (24-hex string in JSON, e.g. `6a4b607236c46b14a294ec4d`).
18	- **Every cross-collection reference stores the ObjectID**, never a name or code:
19	  `farmer_party_id`, `dcs_id`, `org_unit_id`, `batch_id`, `settlement_batch_id`, … This is what
20	  makes `$lookup` / populate trivial and mapping unambiguous.
21	- **Human-readable business keys are separate, unique-indexed fields** — used for display and
22	  lookup, never for joins: org `code` (`DCS-01842`), party `phone`, `invoice_number`,
23	  `batch_number`, `qr_code`, `pashu_aadhaar`.
24	- **One deliberate exception:** `milk_pours.client_event_id` is a **string** minted on the device
25	  (offline-first idempotency key, blueprint §3.1) — the server still assigns a proper ObjectID `_id`.
26	- In JWTs and query params, ObjectIDs travel as hex strings and are parsed server-side via
27	  `httpx.ParseID` / `httpx.PathID`. A malformed id → `400 INVALID_ID`.
28	
29	### 1.2 Response envelope (uniform)
30	Success:
31	```json
32	{ "data": { ... }, "meta": { "limit": 50, "offset": 0, "total": 137 } }   // meta only on list endpoints
33	```
34	Error:
35	```json
36	{ "error": { "code": "SAFETY_GATE_BLOCKED", "message": "human readable", "details": {...}? } }
37	```
38	`code` is a stable machine string the frontend switches on. `500`s are opaque (`INTERNAL`) — the
39	real cause is logged server-side, never leaked.
40	
41	### 1.3 Auth — two token kinds
42	1. `SESSION` token — proves "this phone logged in". Enough for identity/profile endpoints.
43	2. `ROLE` token — a session that has **selected one role**; carries `role_code` + `org_unit_id` +
44	   `org_type`. **Required for every business action.** Obtain via `POST /auth/role/select`.
45	
46	Middleware chain per route group:
47	`Authenticate` (verifies JWT → puts `Actor` on context) → `RequireRoles(...)` or `RequireSession`
48	→ handler → (mutations) `AuditMutations` writes the audit trail. **`SUPER_ADMIN` passes every
49	`RequireRoles` gate** (and every such call is audited).
50	
51	### 1.4 Org scoping (multi-tenant safety)
52	Before touching a resource that belongs to an org unit, the service calls
53	`d.Orgs.RequireInScope(actor, targetOrgID)`. Passes when the actor's org == target, or the
54	actor's org is an **ancestor** in the target's denormalized `path[]` (O(1), no tree walk).
55	`SUPER_ADMIN` and `STATE_AUDITOR` are federation-wide. Failure → `403 FORBIDDEN`.
56	
57	### 1.5 Provenance (append-only, hash-chained)
58	State-changing steps in the milk→QR chain append an immutable event to `provenance_events`
59	(SHA-256 chained on the previous hash). Corrections never mutate — they append a new event with a
60	`supersedes` ref. This is what the public QR scan re-verifies (`ledger.intact`).
61	
62	### 1.6 Logging & error handling (debugging backbone)
63	- **One structured log line per request** (global middleware): `method, path, status, duration_ms,
64	  request_id, ip, actor_party_id, actor_role`. `4xx → WARN`, `5xx → ERROR`.
65	- **Inside each module** (tagged `module=<name>`, correlatable by `request_id`):
66	  `INFO` on every creation/state transition, `WARN` on every business rejection (gate block,
67	  dual-control violation, scope denial, idempotent replay, 409s), `ERROR` with the wrapped cause
68	  before any `500`. Repo errors are wrapped with the operation name (`fmt.Errorf("insert pour: %w")`).
69	
70	### 1.7 Pagination
71	List endpoints accept `?limit=` (default 50, max 200) & `?offset=`, and return `meta.total`.
72	
73	### 1.8 Concurrency & duplicate prevention (how "only one wins")
74	Every "two actors at once → only one completes" case is enforced by a **MongoDB atomic
75	status-guarded update** — the state check lives *inside* the update filter
76	(`update where _id=X AND status=EXPECTED`), so exactly one writer matches and the rest get a
77	`409`. This is used for KYC approve/reject, settlement `execute` (with a resume lease), and the
78	BMC-lot→batch claim (`DISPATCHED → POOLED`, so one lot can never feed two batches). **No Redis
79	lock is used for this** — a single-document atomic update is strictly safer than an external lock
80	(one source of truth, no lock-vs-DB drift, no TTL failure modes). Offline pour ingest dedupes the
81	same way via the unique `client_event_id`.
82	
83	### 1.9 Real-time (live dashboards)
84	`GET /api/v1/events/stream` is a **Server-Sent Events** stream (any authenticated party). The
85	server pushes typed events down the open connection so an already-open dashboard updates without a
86	refresh — e.g. `kyc.pending.changed` nudges reviewer dashboards to re-fetch their scoped
87	`/kyc/pending/count` badge. The nudge is never trusted as the value; the client re-queries the
88	authoritative scoped count (so it can never drift). Single-instance today; at multi-replica scale
89	the cross-node fan-out swaps to Redis pub/sub with no route changes.
90	
91	### 1.10 Rate limiting (single-instance vs replicas)
92	Per-IP token bucket. **In-process by default** (each replica limits what it sees). Set `REDIS_URL`
93	and it switches to a **shared Redis token bucket** (atomic Lua) for global fairness across
94	replicas — fails *open* on a Redis outage so the limiter can never take down the API. Over-limit →
95	`429 RATE_LIMITED`.
96	
97	---
98	
99	## 2. Layered architecture (how a request flows through the code)
100	
101	```
102	HTTP request
103	  → router (internal/httpapi)         global middleware: request-id, metrics, request-log, rate-limit, recover
104	  → module.go                         mounts routes + auth/RBAC; wires handler→service→repo; subscribes to bus
105	  → handler.go                        HTTP ONLY: decode (httpx.DecodeJSON), parse ids, call service, write envelope
106	  → service.go                        ALL business logic: validation, RBAC/scope, gates, provenance, bus, logging
107	  → repo.go                           ALL MongoDB access: collection consts, ObjectID filters, no business logic
108	  → models.go                         request/response DTOs for the module
109	```
110	Modules never import each other. Cross-module effects go through the **in-process event bus**
111	(`eventbus`), which is the seam that becomes Kafka/NATS when this splits into microservices.
112	Shared services arrive via one `deps.Deps` container: `Cfg, Log, DB, JWT, Ledger, Audit, Flags, Orgs, Bus`.
113

116	## 3. The 10 modules & every endpoint
117	
118	> Legend — **Auth**: `public` (none) · `session` · `role:X,Y` (needs a role token with one of those
119	> roles; `SUPER_ADMIN` always allowed). Paths are under `/api/v1` unless marked public.
120	
121	### 3.1 `identity` — auth, parties, KYC approval, role grants
122	The heart of "one phone = one Party = many roles" + the KYC approval workflow.
123	
124	| Method | Path | Auth | What it does |
125	|---|---|---|---|
126	| POST | `/auth/otp/request` | public | Sends 6-digit OTP (stored HMAC-hashed, 5-min TTL, max 5 attempts). Dev mode returns `dev_otp`. |
127	| POST | `/auth/otp/verify` | public | Verifies OTP → find-or-create Party (tier `MINIMAL`) → returns `session` token + rotating refresh token. |
128	| POST | `/auth/refresh` | public | Rotates refresh token → new session token. |
129	| POST | `/auth/logout` | session | Deletes the refresh token. |
130	| GET | `/auth/roles` | session | Lists my usable role assignments, each enriched with org `{id, code, name, type}`. **This is what the frontend reads to know which dashboard(s) to offer.** |
131	| POST | `/auth/role/select` | session | Body `{role_assignment_id}`. Checks it's mine + usable + my KYC tier satisfies the role's `RequiredKYCTier` (else `403 KYC_TIER_INSUFFICIENT`). Returns a `role` token. **This is the role switcher.** |
132	| GET | `/parties/me` | session | My party + active assignments + KYC summary (masked). |
133	| PATCH | `/parties/me` | session | Update `full_name` / `preferred_language`. |
134	| POST | `/kyc/aadhaar` | session | Body `{aadhaar_number, consent:true, requested_tier}`. Stores **only last-4 + a vault ref** (never the number). Creates a **PENDING** KYC record. **No auto-approval.** |
135	| POST | `/kyc/bank` | session | Mock penny-drop; attaches masked bank details to a PENDING record. |
136	| GET | `/kyc/me` | session | My KYC records (masked; vault ref never serialized). |
137	| GET | `/kyc/pending` | role:`ORGANISING_MANAGER, DISTRICT_VERIFIER, PCDF_ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN` | Pending records **within the reviewer's org scope**, enriched with party `{phone, name, tier}`. Audited. |
138	| GET | `/kyc/pending/count` | role:(same) | Live badge value — scoped count of pending KYC. The dashboard renders this and re-fetches it on each SSE `kyc.pending.changed` nudge. Returns `{count, capped}`. |
139	| POST | `/kyc/{id}/approve` | role:(same) | Verifies scope + **not self-review** + `CanApproveKYCTier(role, tier)`; sets `VERIFIED` via an **atomic status-guarded update** (two simultaneous approvals → exactly one wins, the other gets `409 KYC_NOT_PENDING`), **upgrades party tier upward only**, notifies the party. Audited. |
140	| POST | `/kyc/{id}/reject` | role:(same) | `{reason}` → `REJECTED` + reason, notifies party. Audited. |
141	| POST | `/roles/assignments` | role:`SUPER_ADMIN, PCDF_ADMIN, UNION_PRESIDENT, SAMITI_ADHYAKSH, ORGANISING_MANAGER` | Grants a role at an org unit (this is **"deciding a user's position"**). Scope-checked; grant matrix limits who can grant what. Audited (`role.grant`). |
142	| DELETE | `/roles/assignments/{id}` | role:(same) | Revokes (status → `REVOKED`, never deleted). Audited (`role.revoke`). |
143	| GET | `/roles/assignments` | role:(same) | Lists assignments at an org (scope-checked, paged). |
144	
145	**The position/onboarding flow (exact):** login → `POST /kyc/aadhaar` (PENDING) → reviewer
146	`POST /kyc/{id}/approve` (tier upgraded) → an admin `POST /roles/assignments` to set the position
147	(e.g. `SAMITI_SACHEEV @ DCS-01842`) → user logs in, `GET /auth/roles` shows it, `POST /auth/role/select`
148	issues the role token whose `role_code` tells the frontend which UI to render.

267	## 4. How to exercise it
268	
269	```bash
270	cp .env.example .env      # set MONGO_URI (env-only; server refuses to boot without it)
271	make seed                 # org tree + one party per role (prints their ObjectIDs)
272	make run                  # API on :8080
273	make smoke                # the full 21-step E2E (login → pour → gate → QR → settlement → KYC approval)
274	```
275	Seeded demo phones (OTP returned in the response in dev mode): super-admin `9999999999`,
276	sacheev `9000000001`, adhyaksh `9000000002`, farmer `9000000011`, van-rider `9000000021`,
277	bmc-op `9000000031`, plant-op `9000000041`, lab `9000000042`, **org-manager `9000000071`**.

281	## 5. Error codes the frontend should handle
282	
283	| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
284	|---|---|---|
285	| `UNAUTHORIZED` / `FORBIDDEN` | 401 / 403 | No/invalid token · role or scope denied |
286	| `KYC_TIER_INSUFFICIENT` | 403 | Role selected before KYC approved to the required tier |
287	| `KYC_NOT_PENDING` / `KYC_SELF_REVIEW` / `KYC_TIER_NOT_APPROVABLE` | 409 / 403 | KYC approval guardrails |
288	| `SAFETY_GATE_BLOCKED` | 422 | A blocked (failed-QC) lot/batch cannot advance |
289	| `DUAL_CONTROL_VIOLATION` | 403 | Settlement approver == initiator |
290	| `IMPLAUSIBLE_VALUES` | 422 | Pour fat/SNF/qty outside physical bounds |
291	| `FARMER_NOT_MEMBER` | 422 | Pour for a farmer not assigned to that DCS |
292	| `INVALID_ID` | 400 | Malformed ObjectID |
293	| `FEATURE_DISABLED` | 403 | Capability-gated (dormant) endpoint |
294	| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | Per-IP throttle |
295	| `NOT_FOUND` / `CONFLICT` / `MALFORMED_JSON` | 404 / 409 / 400 | Standard |

299	## 6. What is mocked vs real (so you know what to wire next)
300	
301	**Real:** auth, RBAC, org scoping, KYC approval workflow, pricing, idempotent ingest, the safety
302	gate, hash-chained ledger + trace, settlement state machine + dual control, audit, flags, metrics,

116	
117	```mermaid
118	sequenceDiagram
119	    autonumber
120	    participant U as Any user (phone)
121	    participant OM as 🧑‍🏫 Organising Manager / admin
122	    participant API as Saathi API
123	    participant DB as MongoDB
124	
125	    U->>API: POST /auth/otp/request {phone}
126	    API->>DB: store HMAC-hashed OTP (5-min TTL)
127	    API-->>U: SMS with OTP (dev mode: in response)
128	    U->>API: POST /auth/otp/verify {phone, otp}
129	    API->>DB: find-or-create Party (tier MINIMAL, no roles yet)
130	    API-->>U: session token + refresh token
131	    Note over U,API: at this point the user has NO role →<br/>frontend shows a "pending / submit KYC" screen
132	
133	    U->>API: POST /kyc/aadhaar {aadhaar, consent, requested_tier}
134	    API->>DB: KYCRecord status PENDING (stores last-4 + vault ref only)
135	    OM->>API: GET /kyc/pending  (within my org scope)
136	    OM->>API: POST /kyc/{id}/approve
137	    Note over API: not self-review · CanApproveKYCTier(role, tier)<br/>→ VERIFIED, party tier upgraded (upward only)
138	    OM->>API: POST /roles/assignments {party_id, role_code, org_unit_id}
139	    Note over API: THIS is "deciding the position" —<br/>Farmer / Sacheev / Sangh staff / etc.
140	
141	    U->>API: GET /auth/roles
142	    API-->>U: my assignments, each with org {id, code, name, type}
143	    U->>API: POST /auth/role/select {role_assignment_id}
144	    Note over API: validity window + KYC tier satisfies role<br/>(before approval this returns 403 KYC_TIER_INSUFFICIENT)
145	    API-->>U: ROLE token carrying role_code + org scope
146	    Note over U: frontend renders THAT dashboard from role_code.<br/>Switching hats = role/select again.<br/>Losing an election = one revoked assignment, never a deleted account.
147	```

149	**The position is stored as the `RoleAssignment`** (`role_code` + `org_unit_id`), not a field on the
150	user — because one human can hold several (a Sacheev *is also* a Farmer). The role token's
151	`role_code` is the single value the frontend switches on to pick the dashboard; the assignment's
152	ObjectID is the lookup/revocation handle.

184	**Saathi computes and initiates. A different human approves. A licensed PA executes. Money never moves autonomously.**

191	    participant API as Saathi API

197	    A->>API: POST /settlements/{id}/approve

199	    S->>API: POST /settlements/{id}/execute

201	    PA-->>API: SUCCESS + UTR per farmer
202	    Note over API: crash-safe: EXECUTING holds a 2-min lease,<br/>an interrupted run resumes without double-paying
203	    API-->>F: 📱 SMS: "₹553.88 credited, UTR ..."

247	
248	## 8. Flow 5 — The FSSAI safety gate: the heart of "disease-free milk" (§8.3)
249	
250	**Why it's shaped this way:** Aflatoxin M1 survives pasteurisation. If it isn't caught at the
251	BMC/plant, it ends up in the packet. So the gate fires **twice**, and a failed subject is
252	physically unable to advance through the API.
253	
254	```mermaid
255	flowchart TD
256	    IN["Lot / batch closed → QC_PENDING"] --> T["QC recorded:\nBMC_RAPID by BMC Operator\nPLANT_LAB by Lab Analyst"]
257	    T --> E{"All mandatory tests present\nand within FSSAI limits?\nAFM1 ≤ 0.5 µg/kg · coliform ≤ 10 CFU/ml\nphosphatase negative (plant)"}
258	    E -->|"YES"| P["✅ PASSED\ncertificate number issued\nqc.gate_passed chained"]
259	    E -->|"NO"| B["⛔ BLOCKED + reason\nqc.gate_blocked chained\nSMS alert → Union Field Supervisor"]
260	    P --> N["may dispatch / enter batch / yield product lot / get QR"]
261	    B --> Q["quarantined forever:\ndispatch → 422\nbatch create → 422\nproduct lot → 422\nQR → impossible"]
262	    B --> TR["trace upstream via ledger:\nwhich samitis contributed →\ninvestigate feed / animals (§8.3)"]
263	```
264	
265	```mermaid
266	stateDiagram-v2
267	    [*] --> OPEN: BMC lot created (pools consignments)
268	    OPEN --> QC_PENDING: close (chilling temp logged)
269	    QC_PENDING --> PASSED: rapid tests within limits
270	    QC_PENDING --> BLOCKED: any limit exceeded — terminal quarantine
271	    PASSED --> DISPATCHED: tanker to plant
272	    DISPATCHED --> POOLED: claimed by exactly ONE batch (atomic)
273	    BLOCKED --> [*]
274	```
275	
276	Gate hardening (post-review): unknown test names are rejected, a PASS requires the complete
277	mandatory test set per stage, evidence + ledger events are persisted **before** the status flips,
278	and one lot can never feed two batches.
279	
280	---
281

283	
284	```mermaid
285	sequenceDiagram
286	    autonumber
287	    participant PO as 🏭 Plant Operator
288	    participant LA as 🔬 Lab Analyst
289	    participant API as Saathi API
290	    participant PUB as 📱 Anyone (no login)
291	
292	    PO->>API: POST /plant/batches {bmc_lot_ids, product_type}
293	    Note over API: every lot must be PASSED+DISPATCHED —<br/>atomically claimed → POOLED (one batch only)
294	    LA->>API: POST /quality/qc-results (PLANT_LAB: AFM1, coliform, phosphatase)
295	    Note over API: gate #2 → batch PASSED
296	    PO->>API: POST /plant/batches/{id}/complete
297	    PO->>API: POST /plant/product-lots {sku, units, mfg, expiry}
298	    PO->>API: POST /plant/qrs {product_lot_id}
299	    Note over API: qr_code PRG-XXXXXXXX +<br/>HMAC-SHA256 signed token → unforgeable
300	    PUB->>API: GET /public/qr/PRG-E74X27WV
301	    API-->>PUB: product + batch + plant + QC certificate<br/>+ "made from milk collected on 6 Jul from<br/>2 samitis in Lucknow district" (the HONEST view §7.4)<br/>+ ledger.intact: true (chain re-verified)
302	```

304	The scan never claims per-farmer origin — pooled milk traces to the **set of contributing
305	samitis**, and the API is built so it *cannot* say otherwise.

344	## 12. Quick RBAC cheat-sheet (who can hit what)
345	
346	| Action | Allowed roles |
347	|---|---|
348	| Record reading / pour | Sacheev, Milk Tester |
349	| Generate invoices | Sacheev |
350	| Create/dispatch consignment | Sacheev |
351	| Run trip / pickup / deliver | Van Rider (only their own trip) |
352	| Create/close/dispatch BMC lot | BMC Operator |
353	| QC at BMC (`BMC_RAPID`) | BMC Operator |
354	| QC at plant (`PLANT_LAB`) | Plant Lab Analyst |
355	| Create batch / product lot / QR | Plant Operator (QR also Lab Analyst) |
356	| Recall product lot | PCDF Admin, Lab Analyst |
357	| Initiate settlement | Sacheev |
358	| Approve settlement | Adhyaksh, Union President (never the initiator) |
359	| Rate charts | PCDF Admin, Union President |
360	| Org tree | Super Admin, PCDF Admin |
361	| Review / approve KYC | Organising Manager, District Verifier, PCDF Admin, Super Admin (each within their scope + tier) |
362	| Role grants ("assign position") | Super Admin, PCDF Admin, Union President (their tiers), Adhyaksh (farmers in own DCS), Organising Manager (Farmer/Consumer in scope) |
363	| DBT subsidy | Mission Official, PCDF Admin |
364	| Feature flags | Super Admin |
365	| Audit logs / export | State Auditor, Super Admin |
366	| Public QR scan / ledger verify | **anyone — no login** |
367	
368	Plus, always: **Super Admin bypasses role gates (fully audited)** and **every write is
369	org-scope-checked** — your role only works inside your own subtree of the cooperative.

```text
1	# Saathi — Frontend Integration Brief
2	
3	> **Audience:** the `parag-saathi-fe` (Expo/React Native) team wiring the app to the Go backend
4	> (`parag-saathi-be`). This is the **complete, authoritative** contract: connect, auth, every
5	> endpoint, the wire conventions, the real-time stream, the error codes, and the exact FE-side
6	> reconciliations to make before flipping `MODE=http`.
7	>
8	> The backend is the **canonical source of truth** for field names, enums and status codes. Where
9	> the app's mock used different names, the fix is in the FE mapper (`mapRequest`/`mapResponse`),
10	> never the backend. Section 9 lists every one of those.
11	
12	---
13	
14	## 1. Connect
15	
16	```bash
17	# parag-saathi-fe/.env
18	EXPO_PUBLIC_API_MODE=http
19	EXPO_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL=http://10.0.2.2:8080/api/v1   # Android emulator → host
20	# real device on same LAN: http://<mac-lan-ip>:8080/api/v1
21	```
22	
23	Bring the backend up and seed it:
24	
25	```bash
26	cd ~/parag-saathi-be
27	make run          # API on :8080   (or: make dev  → hot-reload)
28	make seed         # demo org tree + one party per role + verified banks + rate chart
29	```
30	
31	Health: `GET /healthz` · readiness (Mongo ping): `GET /readyz` · `GET /version`.
32	
33	**Seeded test phones** (OTP is returned in the response in dev mode — `dev_otp`):
34	super-admin `9999999999`, **Ramesh `9000000001` = SAMITI_SACHEEV + FARMER** (multi-role → role
35	picker), adhyaksh `9000000002`, farmer `9000000011`/`9000000012`, van-rider `9000000021`,
36	bmc-op `9000000031`, plant-op `9000000041`, lab `9000000042`, org-manager `9000000071`.
37	
38	---
39	
40	## 2. Wire conventions (every request)
41	
42	| Concern | Contract |
43	|---|---|
44	| Base | `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` already includes `/api/v1` |
45	| Success | `{ "data": <payload>, "meta"?: { "limit", "offset", "total" } }` — unwrap `.data` |
46	| Error | `{ "error": { "code": "UPPER_SNAKE", "message": "...", "details"?: {...} } }` |
47	| Auth | `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` |
48	| 401 handling | one silent `POST /auth/refresh` + retry, then sign out (never refresh on `/auth/*`) |
49	| Field case | **snake_case on the wire** — map to camelCase per endpoint |
50	| IDs | Mongo **ObjectID** = 24-hex string; opaque to the client. **Never send `""` for an ID field** — omit it or the server 400s (`INVALID_ID`) |
51	| Dates | `YYYY-MM-DD` (IST) for day keys (`pour_date`, `invoice_date`, `date`); ISO-8601 for timestamps |
52	| Idempotency | pours carry `client_event_id` (device-minted, unique) — reuse the SAME id on a retry so offline replays dedupe |
53	| Pagination | `?limit=` (default 50, max 200) `&offset=`; response `meta.total` |
54	
55	---
56	
57	## 3. Auth & the multi-role flow (one phone = many roles)
58	
59	It is a **two-call login**, then a **role selection** that pins a scope:
60	
61	```
62	1. POST /auth/otp/request  {phone}                 → {phone, expires_at, dev_otp?}
63	2. POST /auth/otp/verify   {phone, otp}            → {access_token (SESSION), refresh_token, party}
64	3. GET  /parties/me        (Bearer SESSION)         → {party, assignments[], kyc?}
65	      • assignments.length === 1 → auto-select it
66	      • else                     → show the role picker
67	4. POST /auth/role/select  {role_assignment_id}    → {access_token (ROLE), role_code, org_unit_id, org_type}
68	      • swap ONLY the access token to this ROLE token; keep the refresh token
69	5. render the dashboard for role_code; every business call now uses the ROLE token
70	```
71	
72	Each item of `assignments[]` is a flattened `RoleAssignment` **plus** `org_name`, `org_type`,
73	`org_code` (org enrichment) — enough to render the picker with no extra call. Switching roles =
74	call `/auth/role/select` again with the other `id`. Losing a role = one revoked assignment, never
75	an account deletion.
76	
77	**Multi-role is real and works:** Ramesh (`9000000001`) returns both `FARMER` and `SAMITI_SACHEEV`
78	assignments; select either.
79	
80	**KYC gate:** `role/select` returns `403 KYC_TIER_INSUFFICIENT` (with `details.current_tier` /
81	`required_tier`) if the party's KYC tier is below the role's requirement. Surface this — the user
82	must complete KYC (or be approved) before entering that role.
83

86	## 4. Endpoint reference (by module, all under `/api/v1`)
87	
88	Legend — **public** = no token · **session** = any logged-in party · **role:X** = a ROLE token
89	with one of those roles (SUPER_ADMIN always allowed).
90	
91	### identity — `/auth`, `/parties`, `/kyc`, `/roles`
92	| Method | Path | Auth | Purpose |
93	|---|---|---|---|
94	| POST | `/auth/otp/request` | public | send OTP |
95	| POST | `/auth/otp/verify` | public | verify → SESSION token + party |
96	| POST | `/auth/refresh` | public | rotate token pair |
97	| POST | `/auth/logout` | session | revoke refresh token |
98	| GET | `/auth/roles` | session | my usable assignments (org-enriched) |
99	| POST | `/auth/role/select` | session | pick a role → ROLE token |
100	| GET/PATCH | `/parties/me` | session | my profile (PATCH: `full_name`, `preferred_language`, `public_consent`) |
101	| GET | `/parties?role=CODE&org_unit_id=?` | role: reviewers | list parties holding a role (org_unit_id optional — defaults to caller's scope) |
102	| POST | `/kyc/aadhaar` | session | submit Aadhaar KYC → **PENDING** (no auto-verify) |
103	| POST | `/kyc/bank` | session | penny-drop; masked tail persisted |
104	| GET | `/kyc/me` | session | my KYC records (masked) |

122	| POST | `/collection/pours/batch-sync` | role:SACHEEV,MILK_TESTER | offline replay (≤500) |

124	| GET | `/collection/pours?dcs_id=&date=&shift=&farmer_party_id=` | role:… (FARMER forced own) | list |

193	re-query; never trust the event as the value). Heartbeat comment every ~25s.

197	## 5. Onboarding → verification → position (the full relation)
198	
199	```
200	new user logs in (OTP)                → Party, tier MINIMAL, no roles → "pending" screen
201	  ↓ POST /kyc/aadhaar                  → KYCRecord PENDING  +  KYC_PENDING notification queued to reviewers/super-admin  +  live SSE badge
202	  ↓ reviewer POST /kyc/{id}/approve    → tier upgraded, record VERIFIED, party notified
203	  ↓ admin POST /roles/assignments      → the POSITION (role_code @ org) — a RoleAssignment
204	  ↓ user re-login → GET /auth/roles    → sees the role → /auth/role/select → dashboard
205	```
206	The **assisted** variant (`/onboarding/requests` approve) does all of party+KYC+role atomically for
207	an executive-submitted request.
208	
209	---

211	## 6. Error codes to handle
212	
213	`UNAUTHORIZED` (401) · `FORBIDDEN` (403) · `KYC_TIER_INSUFFICIENT` (403, has `details`) ·
214	`SAFETY_GATE_BLOCKED` (422) · `DUAL_CONTROL_VIOLATION` (403) · `IMPLAUSIBLE_VALUES` (422) ·
215	`FARMER_NOT_MEMBER` (422) · `WRONG_DELIVERY_BMC` / `CONSIGNMENT_NOT_DELIVERED` (422) ·
216	`SHIFT_CONSIGNED` / `POUR_CONSIGNED` (409) · `KYC_NOT_PENDING` / `KYC_SELF_REVIEW` (409/403) ·
217	`FEATURE_DISABLED` (403) · `INVALID_ID` (400) · `RATE_LIMITED` (429) ·
218	`NOT_FOUND` / `CONFLICT` / `MALFORMED_JSON`.
219	
220	---
221	
222	## 7. Real-time & offline
223	- **SSE** for live badges (see §4). Multi-replica prod fans out via Redis (transparent to the app).
224	- **Offline**: pours are idempotent on `client_event_id` — queue locally, replay via
225	  `/collection/pours/batch-sync`; a replay returns the stored pour with `idempotent_replay: true`.
226	
227	---
228	
229	## 8. What's mocked server-side (so you can plan real flows)
230	Aadhaar eKYC, bank penny-drop, PFMS/DBT, Bharat Pashudhan sync, licensed-PA payout, SMS provider
231	are single named mock seams — the wire shapes are final; only the provider swaps later.
232	On-device OCR is the design (§8.2): the app OCRs the analyzer photo, uploads it (gets a key), and
233	posts a reading with `mode=PHOTO_OCR` + `photo_object_key` + `ocr_confidence`. There is **no**
234	server `/pours/ocr-extract` — remove that mock and wire on-device OCR → `POST /collection/readings`.
235	
236	---
237	
238	## 9. FE-side reconciliation checklist (do these in the mappers before `MODE=http`)
239	
240	The backend is canonical; adjust the FE `mapRequest`/`mapResponse` to these names/enums.
241	
242	**Safety-critical**
243	- QC test name: send **`AFLATOXIN_M1`** (not `AFM1`). Subject type: **`PROCESSING_BATCH`** (not `PLANT_BATCH`), **`BMC_LOT`** (not `BMC_INTAKE`). *(The backend now also normalizes `AFM1`, but send canonical.)*
244	
245	**Pour**
246	- Read weighted rate from **`rate_per_litre`**; source enum is **`ANALYZER_DIRECT`** (not `ANALYZER_AUTO`), `PHOTO_OCR`, `MANUAL`. New readable fields: `assurance` (A|B|C), `rate_chart_version`. Backend pour status is only `RECORDED|SUPERSEDED|CANCELLED` (no IN_LOT/INVOICED/PAID — derive lifecycle client-side).
247	
248	**Consignment / lot**
249	- `total_quantity_litres` (not `total_litres`); `avg_fat_pct`/`avg_snf_pct` are the weighted averages; new: `seal_code`, `sealed_at`, `assurance`. Status enum: `OPEN|DISPATCHED|PICKED_UP|DELIVERED|ACCEPTED|REJECTED`.
250	
251	**Invoice**
252	- `invoice_date` (not `date`); amount is `total_amount` + `total_quantity_litres` (no gross/deductions/net on the invoice — settlement lives on the settlement batch). Status: `ISSUED|SETTLEMENT_PENDING|PAID|HOLD`.
253	
254	**Batch / QC**
255	- Batch: `input_litres` (not `volume_litres`); QC verdict from batch `status` (`PASSED`/`BLOCKED`) + `QCResult.overall_pass`; new `contributing_dcs_ids`. QC test: `pass` (not `passed`), result `overall_pass`, `analyst_party_id` (not `recorded_by_party_id`).
256	
257	**BMC lot**
258	- Status enum `OPEN|QC_PENDING|PASSED|BLOCKED|DISPATCHED|POOLED`; trips are `route_trip_ids` (array). Trip delivered field: `delivered_to_bmc_id`.
259	
260	**Org / roles**
261	- Org types: `FEDERATION|MILK_UNION|PROCESSING_PLANT|BMC|DCS` (map `UNION`→`MILK_UNION`, `PLANT`→`PROCESSING_PLANT`). Add `ORGANISING_MANAGER` and `CONSUMER` to the FE role map and **guard `ROLES[code]`** against unknown codes so the picker never crashes. `ONBOARDING_EXECUTIVE` and `STORE_MANAGER` are valid backend roles. KYC tier: `SERVICE` (backend) ↔ `MTLS` (both accepted).
262	
263	**Cattle / MVU**
264	- MVU list: read `requested_at` (not `created_at`); pass `farmer_party_id` for a farmer's own list. Health event: `recorded_by_role`, sync via `bp_sync_status` (`SYNCED`); enums `ARTIFICIAL_INSEMINATION`/`DISEASE_REPORT`.
265	
266	**Logistics pickup**
267	- Path is keyed by the **consignment id**: `POST /logistics/trips/{tripID}/stops/{consignmentID}/pickup` — send the consignment id in the `{consignmentID}` slot (not the DCS id), and include `temp_c`.
268	
269	**Never send empty-string IDs** (e.g. `org_unit_id: ""`) — omit the field.
270

278	bash scripts/dryrun.sh   # multi-role login, KYC→notification→approve→assignment, dashboards, assurance/seal

2

51	## 1. Cross-cutting mismatch catalog (from the identity-round analysis)
52	
53	These recur across every entity. Classification drives WHO fixes it:

1	# Saathi Backend — Technical Notes & Handoff
2	
3	> **Audience:** the next engineer or LLM working on this repo. Read this file plus
4	> `SAATHI_Architecture_Framework_Parag.pdf` (the blueprint, source of truth) and you have the
5	> complete picture. Blueprint section references look like (§8.3).
6	>
7	> **Status:** P0 + P1 implemented end-to-end (identity → **KYC approval** → pour → invoice →
8	> logistics → safety gate → batch → QR → public trace → settlement), with P2 foundations
9	> (cattle/health, MVU, education, dormant collar path). Consumer commerce is **deliberately
10	> descoped** (dormant flag).
11	>
12	> **For the full API surface + per-endpoint behaviour, see [`strict_brief.md`](strict_brief.md).**
13	> **For role-by-role flows with diagrams, see [`WORKFLOW_GUIDE.md`](WORKFLOW_GUIDE.md).**
14	> **For why the org/role model is shaped this way, see [`PCDF_Cooperative_Constitution.md`](PCDF_Cooperative_Constitution.md)** (the real UP cooperative structure — Farmer → Samiti → Sangh → PCDF — that the org tree and 23-role catalog are grounded in).
15	
16	---
17	
18	## 1. Stack & system design decision
19	
20	| Decision | Choice | Why |
21	|---|---|---|
22	| Language | **Go 1.23+** | memory-safe/typed per §15; single static binary; trivial horizontal scaling for 1cr+ users |
23	| Database | **MongoDB** (env-configured URI only) | team decision; normalized ("scattered") collections with ID references, not embedded blobs |
24	| Architecture | **Modular monolith** with hard module seams | §6 prescribes event-driven microservices as end-state; at greenfield stage one deployable with 10 isolated modules + an in-process event bus gives the same boundaries with none of the ops tax. Each module = one future microservice. |
25	| HTTP | chi router, REST JSON under `/api/v1` | frontend lives in a separate repo; this is a pure API |
26	| Events | in-process pub/sub (`internal/platform/eventbus`) | mirrors a broker API; swap to Kafka/NATS (§15) without touching module code |
27	| Provenance | **hash-chained append-only event ledger in MongoDB** (§7.3 "ledger-style" option) | tamper-evident without running a graph DB; graph traversal implemented over `refs` edges; can be projected to Neo4j later |
28	| IDs | **MongoDB ObjectID `_id`**; every cross-collection reference is an ObjectID (`farmer_party_id`, `dcs_id`, …) so `$lookup`/populate is native. Human-readable strings (`code`, `phone`, `invoice_number`, `qr_code`, `pashu_aadhaar`) are **separate unique business keys**, never used for joins. | ObjectID refs are the natural Mongo mapping/populate primitive. The one string kept for identity is `milk_pours.client_event_id` — an offline device-minted idempotency key (§3.1); the server still assigns a real ObjectID `_id`. |
29	| Onboarding | **KYC approval workflow**: submit → `PENDING` → reviewer (`ORGANISING_MANAGER` / `DISTRICT_VERIFIER` / `PCDF_ADMIN` / `SUPER_ADMIN`) approves → tier upgraded. A role token is only issuable once the party's tier satisfies the role — so "login as rider" is impossible before approval. | Matches the field reality: a ground-level Organising Manager decides a user's position after verifying them; the position itself is a `RoleAssignment` (role_code + org scope), which the frontend reads to pick the dashboard. |
30	| Logging | Structured `slog`: one line per request (id, actor, status, duration) + per-module INFO/WARN/ERROR tagged `module=` and correlatable by `request_id`. | Debugging & CERT-In ≥180-day retention (§17); every rejection and failure is traceable end-to-end. |
31	
32	### Scaling posture (1cr+ users)
33	- Stateless server → run N replicas behind a gateway/LB; per-IP rate limiting is per-replica by
34	  design (global fairness belongs to the WAF/gateway tier, §6).
35	- Every hot query path has a compound index (see `internal/platform/mongodb/indexes.go` — the
36	  single index catalog). No collection scans on request paths.
37	- In-memory caches with short TTLs for org-tree (60s) and feature flags (30s) — the two
38	  read-on-every-request lookups.
39	- Write bursts (twice-daily pour shifts, §16) are absorbed by: connection pool 200, idempotent
40	  ingest (unique `client_event_id`), and batch sync endpoint.
41	- Mongo can be sharded later (shard keys would be `dcs_id`/date for pours); the provenance
42	  ledger's global sequence is the one serialization point — at true national scale, switch
43	  `Append` to per-entity chains or a partitioned ledger (documented trade-off, §20-2).
44	
45	## 2. Repository layout
46	
47	```
48	cmd/server/          boot: config → logger → mongo → indexes → deps → router (graceful shutdown)
49	cmd/seed/            idempotent demo/dev data (org tree, parties per role, rate chart, animals)
50	internal/config/     env-only config (.env supported; MONGO_URI required, no in-code default)
51	internal/domain/     THE CONTRACT: pure entities/enums/invariants; no deps; modules depend on it
52	internal/platform/   shared services: httpx, auth (JWT/OTP/HMAC), middleware (authn/rbac/audit/
53	                     ratelimit/metrics), mongodb (client+index catalog), provenance (hash-chain
54	                     ledger), orgscope (path-based scope checks), flags, audit, eventbus, deps
55	internal/httpapi/    router assembly + module registration
56	internal/modules/    10 domain modules (identity, orgs, cattle, collection, logistics, plant,
57	                     quality, settlement, publictrace, platformops)
58	scripts/smoke.sh     end-to-end test of the entire loop over live HTTP + MongoDB
59	```
60	
61	**Module contract** (enforced): `Register(r chi.Router, d *deps.Deps)`; layering
62	`handler.go` (HTTP only) → `service.go` (business logic) → `repo.go` (Mongo only) + `models.go`
63	(DTOs). Modules never import each other; cross-module reactions go through the event bus;
64	collection names only via `mongodb.Coll*` consts.
65	
66	## 3. Identity model (§4) — how auth works
67	
68	1. `POST /api/v1/auth/otp/request {phone}` → 6-digit OTP (stored **HMAC-hashed**, TTL, max 5
69	   attempts). Dev mode (`OTP_DEV_MODE=true`) returns `dev_otp` in the response.
70	2. `POST /api/v1/auth/otp/verify` → finds-or-creates the **Party** (one phone = one human) →
71	   returns a **session JWT** + rotating **refresh token** (stored hashed).
72	3. `GET /api/v1/auth/roles` → the party's org-scoped **RoleAssignments** (23-role catalog §5.2).
73	4. `POST /api/v1/auth/role/select {role_assignment_id}` → **role JWT** pinned to
74	   role+org (this IS the role switcher; KYC tier gates apply, §4.2).
75	5. Protected routes: `middleware.Authenticate` (JWT) → `middleware.RequireRoles(...)`
76	   (SUPER_ADMIN passes all gates; every mutation is audit-logged) → `orgscope.RequireInScope`
77	   (path-array ancestry check, O(1)).
78	
79	## 4. The core loop (what the smoke test drives)
80	
81	```
82	analyzer reading (anti-tamper: geotag/device-time/OCR-confidence/plausibility §8.2)
83	→ pour (idempotent client_event_id; priced off org-scoped rate chart; SMS receipt) 
84	→ same-day invoice (unique farmer+dcs+date)
85	→ consignment (DCS day+shift aggregate = the pooling boundary §7.4)
86	→ route trip (pickup temp, cold-chain log, deliver to BMC)
87	→ BMC lot (pool consignments, chill temp) → QC BMC_RAPID   ── FSSAI gate §8.3
88	→ processing batch (only PASSED lots can enter)  → QC PLANT_LAB ── gate again
89	→ product lot (only COMPLETED batches) → QR (HMAC-signed, forgery-proof)
90	→ PUBLIC scan /api/v1/public/qr/{code} → honest samiti-SET provenance + QC certificate
91	→ settlement: initiate (Sacheev) → approve (DIFFERENT person — dual control §8.1) 
92	  → execute (mock licensed-PA) → farmer paid, UTR, SMS
93	```
94	
95	Every hop appends a **provenance event** to the hash chain with `refs` edges; the public scan
96	returns `ledger.intact` from re-verifying the chain segment. Corrections (pour supersede) are
97	new events referencing the old — nothing is ever edited in place (§3.4).
98	
99	**FSSAI limits enforced in software** (`internal/domain/quality.go`): AFM1 ≤ 0.5 µg/kg,
100	coliform ≤ 10 CFU/ml, tetracycline MRL 0.1 mg/kg, phosphatase must be negative. A failed subject
101	is BLOCKED and *every* forward path re-checks status (dispatch, batch creation, product lot, QR).
102	
103	## 5. Hashing / crypto inventory
104	
105	| What | Mechanism | Where |
106	|---|---|---|
107	| OTP codes | HMAC-SHA256(secret, phone, code) — DB never sees plaintext | `platform/auth/otp.go` |
108	| Refresh tokens | opaque 32-byte random, stored as HMAC digest, rotated on every refresh | identity module |
109	| Provenance chain | SHA-256 over (prev_hash, seq, type, entity, refs, actor, payload, ts) | `platform/provenance/ledger.go` |
110	| QR tokens | HMAC-SHA256 signature over (qr_code, product_lot_id, issued_at) | plant module + public verify |
111	| JWT | HS256, 15-min access, kind=session/role | `platform/auth/jwt.go` |
112	| Aadhaar | **never stored** — last-4 + mock Data-Vault ref only (§18-A) | identity/KYC |
113

116	**Real:** everything in the loop above — auth, RBAC, org scoping, pricing, idempotent ingest,

1	# Constitution of the UP Dairy Cooperative Structure
2	## Farmer → Samiti (DCS) → Sangh / Milk Union → PCDF
3	
4	*Compiled from the official PCDF website (updairydevelopment.gov.in), the NDDB Dairy Knowledge Portal, and the Uttar Pradesh Co-operative Societies Act, 1965. Date: 05 July 2026.*
5	
6	---
7	
8	## 1. The Big Picture
9	
10	PCDF (Pradeshik Cooperative Dairy Federation Ltd., Lucknow) was established in **1962** to develop organised dairying in Uttar Pradesh on cooperative lines and to eliminate middlemen between milk producers and consumers. It follows the **Anand Pattern three-tier structure**:
11	
12	```
13	                    ┌─────────────────────────────┐
14	   STATE LEVEL      │  PCDF (Apex Federation)     │  Markets milk & products
15	                    │  "Parag" brand              │  (Apex Society, Sec 2(a-4))
16	                    └──────────────▲──────────────┘
17	                                   │ Unions are shareholder-members;
18	                                   │ Union chairmen sit on Federation Board
19	                    ┌──────────────┴──────────────┐
20	   DISTRICT LEVEL   │  Dugdh Utpadak Sahkari      │  Collects, processes,
21	                    │  Sangh = MILK UNION         │  markets milk
22	                    │  (one per district/region)  │  (Central Society, Sec 2(d-1))
23	                    └──────────────▲──────────────┘
24	                                   │ Samitis are shareholder-members;
25	                                   │ Samiti delegates elect Union Board
26	                    ┌──────────────┴──────────────┐
27	   VILLAGE LEVEL    │  Dugdh Utpadak Sahkari      │  Collects surplus milk
28	                    │  Samiti = Dairy Cooperative │  twice daily, tests, pays
29	                    │  Society (DCS)              │  (Primary Society)
30	                    └──────────────▲──────────────┘
31	                                   │ Farmers are shareholder-members;
32	                                   │ one member = one vote
33	                    ┌──────────────┴──────────────┐
34	   GRASSROOTS       │  FARMER (Milk Producer)     │  Owner + supplier + voter
35	                    └─────────────────────────────┘
36	```
37	
38	**Important terminology note:** "Sangh" and "Milk Union" are the **same body** — the district-level *Dugdh Utpadak Sahkari Sangh Ltd.* is simply the Hindi name of the District Milk Union. So the chain is: Farmer → Samiti (village) → Sangh/Milk Union (district) → PCDF (state).
39	
40	Per the official PCDF Three-Tier Structure page: "The DCS in villages collect the surplus milk from farmer members"; "The Milk Unions collect milk from all the village DCS of its district, process and market it"; and "The Apex Federation provides Marketing services and other support to the District Milk Unions of the State."
41	
42	**Legal framework:** All three tiers are registered cooperative societies governed by the **Uttar Pradesh Co-operative Societies Act, 1965** (UP Act No. 11 of 1966) and the **UP Co-operative Societies Rules, 1968**, each operating under its own registered bye-laws.
43	
44	---
45	
46	## 2. Level 1 — The Farmer (Milk Producer Member)
47	
48	The farmer is the foundation and the ultimate **owner** of the entire structure.
49	
50	### How a farmer is constituted as a member
51	- Any milk producer of the village who has attained majority (18+) is eligible for membership (Sec. 17, UPCS Act permits individuals of majority age as members).
52	- The farmer becomes a member by **purchasing at least the minimum share(s)** of the Samiti and **paying the entrance fee** prescribed in the Samiti's bye-laws.
53	- Typical bye-law conditions: the member should reside in the society's area of operation, own a milch animal, and regularly pour milk to the society.
54	
55	### Rights of the member
56	- **One member, one vote** in the General Body of the Samiti, regardless of shares held or milk poured — the core cooperative principle.
57	- Right to elect (and be elected to) the Managing Committee of the Samiti.
58	- Right to receive payment for milk on quality (fat/SNF) and quantity basis, daily or weekly.
59	- Right to a share of profits — **dividend on shares and bonus in proportion to milk supplied** during the year.
60	- Access to input services at cost: artificial insemination (AI), veterinary first aid, cattle feed, fodder seed, cattle insurance.
61	
62	### Duties of the member
63	- Pour surplus milk regularly to the Samiti (not to private vendors).
64	- Abide by the registered bye-laws and General Body resolutions.
65	
66	---
67	
68	## 3. Level 2 — The Samiti (Village Dairy Cooperative Society / DCS)
69	
70	*Hindi: Prarambhik Dugdh Utpadak Sahkari Samiti — the primary society at village level.*
71	
72	### Constitution / formation
73	- Formed when milk producers of a village organise and apply for registration to the **Registrar/Assistant Registrar of Co-operative Societies** (through the Dairy Development Department, which promotes and organises new samitis).
74	- Under **Section 6** of the UPCS Act, a primary society needs **not less than 10 individual members** to be registered (bye-laws for dairy samitis commonly require more in practice).
75	- Under **Section 7**, the Registrar registers the society after verifying compliance with the Act, sound business principles, and reasonable prospects of success.
76	- Each Samiti operates under **registered model bye-laws** which define its area of operation, objects, share capital, membership conditions, and management.
77	
78	### Governance
79	- **General Body (all farmer members) is the supreme/final authority** — Sec. 28: "The final authority of a co-operative society shall vest in the general body of its members in general meeting." An **Annual General Meeting** (Sec. 32) approves the accounts, activities, and disposal of net profits.
80	- **Managing Committee (Prabandh Samiti)**: elected by and from the members. Under Sec. 29 a primary society's committee may have up to **13 members**, including **reserved seats for Scheduled Castes/Tribes, Other Backward Classes, and women**; the elected term is **5 years**, with elections conducted under the UP Co-operative Election Commission.
81	- A **Chairman (Sabhapati)** is elected from among committee members (Sec. 30) — he exercises "control, supervision and guidance" of the society's affairs and presides over meetings. **All Managing Committee positions are honorary** (unpaid).
82	- A paid **Secretary** (Sec. 31) acts as chief executive of the society, and the Samiti employs paid staff (milk tester, helper) in proportion to its business.
83	
84	### Functions
85	- Twice-daily (morning/evening) **milk collection** from members; weighing and **quality testing** (fat testing by Gerber centrifuge or electronic milkotester) in front of the member; recording of each member's quantity and fat.
86	- **Dispatch of milk** to the Milk Union via scheduled routes or bulk milk coolers.
87	- **Payment to members** on quality-cum-quantity basis, daily or weekly.
88	- **Routing of input services** from the Union to farmers: AI service, liquid nitrogen and semen doses, veterinary first aid and medicines, cattle feed, fodder seed, cattle insurance — on a cost-recovery basis.
89	- Maintaining daily registers of transactions; accounts subject to **audit**.
90	- Awareness, training, women's participation, clean milk production, and village development activities.
91	
92	---
93	
94	## 4. Level 3 — The Sangh / District Milk Union
95	
96	*Hindi: (Jila) Dugdh Utpadak Sahkari Sangh Ltd. — e.g., Varanasi Milk Union, Lucknow Milk Union. This is a "Central Society" under Sec. 2(d-1) of the UPCS Act: a cooperative whose ordinary members are other cooperatives (the samitis), not individuals.*
97	
98	### Constitution
99	- All registered **Samitis of the district become members of the Union by subscribing to its share capital** as provided in the Union's bye-laws.
100	- Registered under the UPCS Act 1965 with its own bye-laws; its area of operation is the district (or a group of districts).
101	
102	### Governance
103	- **General Body of the Union** = representatives/delegates (normally the chairmen) of the member Samitis. Sec. 28 allows the final authority to be exercised through elected delegates for federal societies.
104	- **Board of Directors / Committee of Management**: elected by the Samiti representatives. Under Sec. 29 a central society's committee may have up to **15 members**, with the same SC/ST/OBC/women reservations and a **5-year term**.
105	- An elected **Union Chairman** presides; day-to-day operations run under **professional paid management** (General Manager/Managing Director and technical staff), keeping the elected board responsible for policy — the Anand Pattern principle of farmer control + professional management.
106	- Subject to "continuous and concurrent audit to maintain financial propriety."
107	
108	### Functions
109	- **Procures milk from all village DCS of the district**, chills, **processes** it in its dairy plant, and **markets** liquid milk and products (largely under the Parag brand through the Federation).
110	- **Macro-level input supply** through the samitis: compounded cattle feed, fodder seeds, veterinary services for sick animals; owns infrastructure such as dairy plants, cattle-feed plants, fodder farms and semen stations. (PCDF's dairy plants at Noida, Meerut, Lucknow, Kanpur, Allahabad and cattle-feed plants at Meerut and Varanasi are ISO-9002/HACCP certified.)
111	- **Training** of samiti managing committees, secretaries, AI workers and union staff; extension and rural development work.
112	- **Financial returns downward**: pays member samitis **dividend on shares and bonus proportional to milk supplied** annually.
113	- Markets its processed products **through the state federation** (PCDF).
114	
115	---
116	
117	## 5. Level 4 — PCDF (Pradeshik Cooperative Dairy Federation Ltd.)
118	
119	*The state-level apex body, Lucknow. An "Apex Society" under Sec. 2(a-4) of the UPCS Act — a state-level federation covering the whole of Uttar Pradesh whose members are the central societies (Milk Unions).*
120	
121	### Constitution
122	- Established **1962**; registered under the UP Co-operative Societies Act.
123	- **Member Milk Unions subscribe to PCDF's share capital** as per Federation bye-laws (the State Government also holds share capital as it is a government-supported apex federation).
124	
125	### Governance
126	- **General Body** = the member Milk Unions (through their delegates).
127	- **Board of Directors**: comprises the **elected Chairmen of all member Unions** plus the Federation's **Managing Director**, along with ex-officio (government) members and technical experts. Under Sec. 29, an apex society's committee may have up to **17 members**.
128	- The **Managing Director** is, per Sec. 31A of the Act, a senior **Government officer (IAS) nominated by the State Government**, serving ex-officio on the board — currently Shri Vaibhav Srivastava, IAS; the department is headed politically by the Minister of Dairy Development (Shri Dharmpal Singh).
129	- A **Programming Committee** — the chief executives of every member Union plus the Federation's Quality Control Officer and co-opted technical experts — meets regularly to implement Board policies and coordinate day-to-day operations.
130	
131	### Functions
132	- **Marketing** of milk and milk products of the member Unions across the state under the **"Parag"** brand; deciding the **product-price mix** for member unions.
133	- Operating the **state milk grid** — production planning and moving milk between surplus and deficit regions, plus inter-state milk commerce.
134	- **Liaison with the State/Central Government, NDDB** and other agencies; mobilising resources and coordinating development programmes.
135	- **Policy-making** for cooperative marketing of all member Unions' milk and products; joint services (AI/breeding programmes, cattle-feed marketing, technical inputs).
136	- Strengthening the cooperative structure itself (organising new samitis, training, quality assurance through its central labs).
137	- **Profit distribution** to member Unions equitably, based on the volume of business each Union transacted.
138	
139	---
140	
141	## 6. How Democracy Flows Up and Services Flow Down
142	
143	**Election chain (bottom-up):**
144	Farmers elect the Samiti Managing Committee and its Chairman → Samiti chairmen/delegates elect the Union Board of Directors and Union Chairman → Union Chairmen constitute the PCDF Board (with the government-nominated MD). Every officeholder is thus ultimately accountable to the farmer.
145	
146	**Milk chain (bottom-up):**
147	Farmer pours milk at the Samiti → Samiti dispatches to the Union's chilling centre/dairy plant → Union processes and packs → PCDF/Parag markets in cities and coordinates the state grid.
148	
149	**Money & services chain (top-down):**
150	Consumer payments flow from PCDF → Unions → Samitis → farmer's milk payment (quality-cum-quantity basis), plus year-end dividend/bonus at each tier; while inputs (cattle feed, semen, vet care, training) flow from the Federation and Unions through the Samiti to the farmer's doorstep.
151	
152	---
153	
154	## 7. Quick Reference Table
155	
156	| Feature | Samiti (Village DCS) | Sangh / Milk Union (District) | PCDF (State) |
157	|---|---|---|---|
158	| Legal status | Primary society | Central society, Sec 2(d-1) | Apex society, Sec 2(a-4) |
159	| Members | Individual milk producers (min. 10 to register, Sec 6) | Village Samitis (via share capital) | District Milk Unions (via share capital) |
160	| Supreme authority | General Body of farmers (Sec 28) | General Body of samiti delegates | General Body of member unions |
161	| Board | Managing Committee ≤ 13, honorary | Board of Directors ≤ 15 | Board ≤ 17: union chairmen + MD (IAS, Sec 31A) + experts |
162	| Term / elections | 5 years, UP Coop. Election Commission, SC/ST/OBC/women reserved seats | Same | Same |
163	| Chief executive | Paid Secretary (Sec 31) | Professional GM/MD | Managing Director — State-nominated IAS |
164	| Core job | Collect, test, pay; route inputs | Process & market; supply inputs; train | Market (Parag), state milk grid, policy, govt/NDDB liaison |
165	| Returns to members | Milk price + dividend + bonus on milk poured | Dividend + bonus on milk supplied | Profit shared by unions' business volume |

I've now read every file in [docs/](docs/) — the authoritative **Developer Technical Note** (all 20 pages) plus the six companion docs. Here is the strict brief: what the spec mandates, how the backend actually realizes it, and — critically for integration — **where the live backend diverges from the Note's vocabulary/shape**. Nothing was changed; this is read-only.

---

## 0. The one principle everything hangs on

> **Milk is pooled, so traceability is set-valued, not point-valued.** A pack can honestly claim "the milk in this batch came from *these* societies, in *this* window, and passed *these* checks" — never "from one farmer's cow." Pooling happens **twice**: farmers → society consignment, then many trucks → one plant silo/lot. Every UI/claim must respect this. (Note §0, §12.1)

The backend is engineered so it *cannot* say more than this — the public scan returns a **set of societies + a consented farmer roster**, never per-farmer attribution.

---

## 1. The golden path — spec vs. what the backend actually exposes

The Note's §8 endpoint table is explicitly labelled **"Representative."** The **live contract the FE must code against is the nested REST surface** in [strict_brief.md](docs/strict_brief.md) / [FRONTEND_INTEGRATION.md](docs/FRONTEND_INTEGRATION.md) — not the Note's flat paths. This mapping is the single most important thing to internalize:

| Note (spec) step | Note entity / endpoint | **Live backend endpoint** | Live entity |
|---|---|---|---|
| Log a pour | `POST /pours` | `POST /api/v1/collection/pours` | `MilkPour` |
| Correct a pour | `POST /pours/{id}/corrections` | `POST /collection/pours/{id}/supersede` | append-only |
| Seal the shift | `POST /consignments/{id}/seal` | `POST /logistics/consignments/{id}/dispatch` | `DCSConsignment` |
| Van pickup | `POST /pickups` | `POST /logistics/trips/{tripID}/stops/{consignmentID}/pickup` | `RouteTrip` stop |
| Mint batch code | `POST /batches/mint` | *(folded into)* `POST /logistics/trips` + deliver | `RouteTrip` |
| GPS track | `POST /trips/{id}/track` | `POST /logistics/trips/{tripID}/cold-chain` | temp/geo samples |
| Plant intake | `POST /intakes` | `POST /plant/bmc-lots` (+ `/close`, `/dispatch`) | `BMCLot` |
| Quality gate | `POST /qc` | `POST /quality/qc-results` | `QCResult` |
| Build/seal lot | `POST /lots/build` `/lots/{id}/seal` | `POST /plant/batches` → `/complete` → `/plant/product-lots` | `ProcessingBatch`→`ProductLot` |
| Issue QR | `POST /qr/issue` | `POST /plant/qrs` | `BatchQR` |
| **Consumer scan** | `GET /t/{token}` | `GET /api/v1/public/qr/{qr_code}` | LOTSUMMARY-equivalent |
| Farmer invoices | `GET /farmers/{id}/invoices` | `GET /collection/invoices?farmer_party_id=` | `Invoice` |
| Cycle invoice run | `POST /invoices/run` | `POST /collection/invoices/generate` | *(same-day, see §6)* |
| Offline bulk push | `POST /sync/batch` | `POST /collection/pours/batch-sync` | *(pours only)* |
| CMS delta | `GET /content?since=` | `GET /content?since=` | `CMSContent` ✅ same |

**Takeaway for FE:** follow FRONTEND_INTEGRATION.md §4 as the endpoint truth. Treat the Note's §8 paths as design intent only.

---

## 2. The state machines (Note §7 — these are contracts the FE renders against)

- **Consignment (society shift):** `OPEN → SEALED → PICKED`; post-seal fix → `CORRECTION_PENDING → SEALED` (Union approval). Backend enum: `OPEN|DISPATCHED|PICKED_UP|DELIVERED|ACCEPTED|REJECTED` — note **`DISPATCHED`=Note's SEALED**.
- **Batch/transport:** `DRAFT → MINTED → IN_TRANSIT → AT_PLANT → RECEIVED`.
- **Quality gate (per intake):** `SAMPLED → PASS|HOLD|REJECT`; `PASS → TIPPED`, `REJECT → DIVERTED`. Backend BMC-lot enum: `OPEN|QC_PENDING|PASSED|BLOCKED|DISPATCHED|POOLED` (**BLOCKED = terminal quarantine**).
- **QR token:** `ISSUED → ACTIVE → REVOKED` (recall). Backend returns a **recall notice at 200, not 404**, on a revoked lot.

---

## 3. Actors & roles

The Note names 7 role surfaces (Farmer, Sachiv, Van, Plant/QA, Supervisor/Union, Consumer, Administrator). The backend expands these into a **23-role catalog** grounded in the real UP cooperative law ([PCDF_Cooperative_Constitution.md](docs/PCDF_Cooperative_Constitution.md)): **Farmer → Samiti/DCS → Sangh/Milk Union → PCDF**. Org tree: `FEDERATION → MILK_UNION → {PROCESSING_PLANT, BMC} → DCS`.

The governing rule for the FE: **one phone = one Party = many org-scoped RoleAssignments.** Login is **two calls** (`/auth/otp/verify` → `/parties/me`), then **`/auth/role/select`** pins the scope and returns the ROLE token whose `role_code` selects the dashboard. Ramesh (`9000000001`) is seeded as **SACHEEV + FARMER** to exercise the picker.

Onboarding→position relation is a hard sequence: `OTP → /kyc/aadhaar (PENDING) → reviewer /kyc/{id}/approve (tier upgraded) → admin /roles/assignments (the position) → role/select`. A role token is **un-issuable** until KYC tier ≥ the role's requirement (`403 KYC_TIER_INSUFFICIENT`).

---

## 4. Provenance ledger (Note §5) — the tamper-evidence spine

Append-only, SHA-256 hash-chained, device-signed events; corrections **append** a superseding event (never edit); the public scan re-verifies the chain and returns `ledger.intact`. Backend implements this in `provenance_events` + `GET /public/ledger/verify`. ✅ Conformant in substance (internal event-type names differ from the Note's `POUR|CONSIGNMENT_SEAL|PICKUP|BATCH_MINT|INTAKE|QC|LOT_SEAL|QR_ISSUE|CORRECTION` — not FE-visible).

---

## 5. The safety gate (Note §6.5 — "test before tip") — the food-safety heart

**Aflatoxin M1 ≤ 0.5 µg/kg** is heat-stable (survives pasteurisation) → **must** be caught before milk enters a common silo. Note has one gate at plant intake; the **backend runs the gate twice** (`BMC_RAPID` at the chilling centre, `PLANT_LAB` at the plant) — a superset, spec-conformant in spirit. A `BLOCKED` subject is quarantined forever: dispatch/batch/product/QR all re-check and return `422 SAFETY_GATE_BLOCKED`.

⚠️ **Safety-critical FE reconciliation:** the app's mock posts test name `"AFM1"`; the canonical name is **`AFLATOXIN_M1`**. The backend now normalizes the alias defensively, but the FE **must send `AFLATOXIN_M1`** — a wrong name is how the aflatoxin gate silently doesn't fire. Subject type is `PROCESSING_BATCH`/`BMC_LOT` (not `PLANT_BATCH`/`BMC_INTAKE`).

---

## 6. Two genuine modeling divergences the FE must design around (not just field renames)

1. **Invoice = same-day, not 10-day cycle.** The Note (§6.3) describes a **cycle** invoice with `gross / deductions[] / net_payable / pdf_ref`. The backend issues **same-day** invoices (`unique farmer+dcs+date`) carrying only `total_amount` + `total_quantity_litres` — **no deductions/net on the invoice**; deductions & payout live on the **settlement batch**, not the bill. The FE "today's bill" screen must read `invoice_date`/`total_amount` and get deductions/payment from settlement, not from the invoice object.

2. **QR/consumer-scan shape differs.** Note: `https://trace.parag.in/t/<token>`, `token = base62(lot_ref)·HMAC6`. Backend: `GET /api/v1/public/qr/{qr_code}` where `qr_code = PRG-XXXXXXXX` + a separate HMAC-signed token over the product-lot id. Functionally equivalent (unforgeable, revocable, resolves to the set-valued LOTSUMMARY with `societies[] + volume_share`, `farmers_total`, consented `farmers_public`, quality cert, `ledger.intact`) — but the FE consumer view must call the **backend `/public/qr/{code}`** path.

Plus the term **"batch" is overloaded**: the Note's `BATCH` = the *van pickup* unit; the backend's `/plant/batches` = the *plant processing* batch. The van-layer in the backend is `route trip` + `BMC lot`.

---

## 7. Assurance, consent, offline, compliance — conformance snapshot

- **Assurance A|B|C** (§6.2): ✅ on `MilkPour`, **weakest-inherited** to consignment/lot. FE source enum: **`ANALYZER_DIRECT`** (not `ANALYZER_AUTO`), `PHOTO_OCR`, `MANUAL`.
- **Consent roster** (§6.7): ✅ `Party.public_consent` gates whether a farmer is *named* on the public scan; non-consenting are counted, not named.
- **Rate reproducibility** (§6.3): ✅ each pour pins `rate_chart_version`.
- **Offline-first** (§9): backend covers the pour path (`client_event_id` idempotency + `/pours/batch-sync`). The Note's fuller device-side local hash-chained ledger + generic `/sync/batch` for *all* event types + `/reference?since=` delta is **broader than what the backend currently exposes** — offline today is pour-focused. Worth knowing if the FE expected generic offline for consignments/pickups.
- **On-device OCR** (§6.2/§8.2): the design is app-OCR → upload → `POST /collection/readings` with `mode=PHOTO_OCR`+`photo_object_key`+`ocr_confidence`. There is **no** server `/pours/ocr-extract` — the FE must drop that mock.
- **Privacy/DPDP** (§10): Aadhaar never stored clear (last-4 + vault ref); phone/bank masked; no PII on public surface. ✅
- **Cattle / Pashu Aadhaar** (§6.1): present but **dormant behind a flag** — matches the Note exactly.

---

## 8. What to trust, and how to verify

- **Authoritative for FE wiring:** [FRONTEND_INTEGRATION.md](docs/FRONTEND_INTEGRATION.md) (§4 endpoints, §9 the exact FE-mapper reconciliation list) and [strict_brief.md](docs/strict_brief.md) (per-endpoint behaviour).

**Bottom line:** the backend faithfully implements the Note's principles (set-valued pooled traceability, hash-chained ledger, test-before-tip, assurance grading, consent-gated roster, offline idempotent capture).   enrich `/parties?role=` with the holder's org, or point the picker at
  `GET /roles/assignments?role_code=SAMITI_SACHEEV` (`assignmentWithOrg` carries both).

### A2. Settlement write flow — different lifecycle  ·  `src/core/api/endpoints/payments.ts`
- **Backend today:** `POST /settlements {dcs_id, date}` → creates a `SettlementBatch`
  (PENDING_APPROVAL) returned with an **id**; then `POST /settlements/{id}/approve`
  (dual-control: approver ≠ initiator), `/{id}/reject`, `/{id}/execute` (→ PAID + payout
  SMS). Invoice status rail is `ISSUED | SETTLEMENT_PENDING | PAID | HOLD`.
- **FE today:** keys `approveInvoices` / `settleInvoices` / `approveRelease` on
  **DCS + date** and an invoice `DRAFT → APPROVED → SETTLED` lifecycle (a FE-invented
  "approve invoices" pre-step that has no backend equivalent). Posting a DCS id into the
  `/settlements/{id}/…` slot → `INVALID_ID`.
- **FE fix (when reconciling):** rewire the Sachiv settlement UI to
  `POST /collection/invoices/generate` → `POST /settlements` (capture the returned batch
  **id**) → `/{id}/approve` (as Adhyaksh/President) → `/{id}/execute`, and thread that
  batch id through the screen state. Then drop `mockOnly` on the three writes.
- **Reads are already wired to http:** `listInvoices` (`GET /collection/invoices`) and
  `getReleaseSummary` (`GET /settlements`) map real data. Note the domain `SettlementBatch`
  uses `pa_ref` (payment-aggregator ref), not `union_ref`.

- **FE fix:** resolve `sku`/`product_name`/`unit_size` from the products catalogue by
  `productId`, and capture `expiry_date` in the pack sheet; then drop `mockOnly`.
- **Downstream:** `POST /plant/qrs` (QR mint) depends on a real product lot — same gate.
- **Backend option:** accept a `product_id` and derive `sku/name/unit_size` from the product
  master server-side, leaving only `expiry_date` for the client.

### A4. Quality queue / certificate / trace-back — lean projections  ·  `src/core/api/endpoints/quality.ts`
- **Backend today (routes exist):** `GET /quality/qc-queue` → `QCQueueResponse{items:[{subject_id,
  reference, mandatory_tests[], recorded_tests[], pending_tests[]}]}` (no full batch);

- **FE today:** its `QcQueueItem` and `traceBack` render a full `PlantBatch` + weighted

  correct (`AFLATOXIN_M1` is sent — gate is **not** bypassed).

58		if len(r.DocumentRefs) > 20 {

64	// rejectRequest carries the mandatory human-readable rejection reason.
65	type rejectRequest struct {

67	}

69	func (r rejectRequest) validate() error {
70		reason := strings.TrimSpace(r.Reason)
71		if reason == "" || len(reason) > 500 {
72			return httpx.BadRequest("INVALID_REASON", "reason must be 1-500 characters")
73		}
74		return nil
75	}

135	// approve runs the onboarding saga: it claims the PENDING request atomically,
136	// then create-or-finds the Party by phone, writes a VERIFIED KYCRecord at the
137	// requested tier, raises the party's KYC tier upward, grants the requested
138	// role@org and stamps CreatedParty on the request. The request must be PENDING
139	// and the reviewer must be in scope for the target org unit and authorised for
140	// the requested tier.
141	func (s *service) approve(ctx context.Context, actor auth.Actor, id primitive.ObjectID) (*domain.OnboardingRequest, error) {
142		now := time.Now().UTC()
143		rid, err := actorID(actor)
144		if err != nil {
145			return nil, err
146		}
147		request, err := s.repo.findRequestByID(ctx, id)
148		if err != nil {
149			return nil, err
150		}
151		if request.Status != domain.OnboardingStatusPending {
152			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "onboarding approve rejected: not pending",
153				slog.String("request_id", id.Hex()), slog.String("status", request.Status),
154				slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID))
155			return nil, httpx.Conflict("ONBOARDING_NOT_PENDING", "onboarding request is not pending review")
156		}
157		// Org scope: a reviewer may only decide requests within their area.
158		if err := s.deps.Orgs.RequireInScope(ctx, actor, request.OrgUnitID); err != nil {
159			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "onboarding approve denied: out of scope",
160				slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID),
161				slog.String("request_id", id.Hex()),
162				slog.String("org_unit_id", request.OrgUnitID.Hex()))
163			return nil, err
164		}
165		// Tier authority mirrors the KYC review console (§5.2): the reviewer's role
166		// must be permitted to clear the requested tier.
167		if !domain.CanApproveKYCTier(actor.RoleCode, request.RequestedTier) {
168			s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "onboarding approve rejected: tier not approvable",
169				slog.String("request_id", id.Hex()), slog.String("reviewer_role", actor.RoleCode),
170				slog.String("requested_tier", request.RequestedTier))
171			appErr := httpx.Forbidden("your role may not approve onboarding at the " + request.RequestedTier + " tier")
172			appErr.Code = "KYC_TIER_NOT_APPROVABLE"
173			return nil, appErr
174		}
175	
176		// Claim the request FIRST (atomic PENDING→APPROVED) so a concurrent approve
177		// loses the race before any party/kyc/assignment side effect runs.
178		claimed, err := s.repo.markRequestApproved(ctx, id, rid, now)
179		if err != nil {
180			if httpxNotFound(err) {
181				s.log.WarnContext(ctx, "onboarding approve lost race: no longer pending",
182					slog.String("request_id", id.Hex()), slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID))
183				return nil, httpx.Conflict("ONBOARDING_NOT_PENDING", "onboarding request is not pending review")
184			}
185			return nil, err
186		}
187	
188		// 1. Find-or-create the Party by phone.
189		party, err := s.repo.upsertPartyByPhone(ctx, claimed.Phone, claimed.FullName, now)
190		if err != nil {
191			return nil, err
192		}
193	
194		// 2. Write a VERIFIED KYC record at the requested tier, reviewer-stamped.
195		kyc := domain.KYCRecord{
196			ID:             primitive.NewObjectID(),
197			PartyID:        party.ID,
198			RequestedTier:  claimed.RequestedTier,
199			Status:         domain.KYCStatusVerified,
200			ReviewedBy:     &rid,
201			ReviewedByRole: actor.RoleCode,
202			ReviewedAt:     &now,
203			VerifiedAt:     &now,
204			CreatedAt:      now,
205			UpdatedAt:      now,
206		}
207		if err := s.repo.insertKYCRecord(ctx, kyc); err != nil {
208			return nil, err
209		}
210	
211		// 3. Raise the party's KYC tier upward only.
212		newTier := upgradedKYCTier(party.KYCTier, claimed.RequestedTier)
213		if newTier != party.KYCTier {
214			if err := s.repo.updatePartyKYCTier(ctx, party.ID, newTier, now); err != nil {
215				return nil, err
216			}
217		}
218	
219		// 4. Grant the requested role@org (idempotent — skip if already held).
220		exists, err := s.repo.activeAssignmentExists(ctx, party.ID, claimed.RequestedRole, claimed.OrgUnitID)
221		if err != nil {
222			return nil, err
223		}
224		if !exists {
225			assignment := domain.RoleAssignment{
226				ID:        primitive.NewObjectID(),
227				PartyID:   party.ID,
228				RoleCode:  claimed.RequestedRole,
229				OrgUnitID: claimed.OrgUnitID,
230				GrantedBy: &rid,
231				ValidFrom: now,
232				Status:    domain.RoleAssignmentActive,
233				CreatedAt: now,
234			}
235			if err := s.repo.insertAssignment(ctx, assignment); err != nil {
236				return nil, err
237			}
238		}
239	
240		// 5. Stamp the created party onto the request.
241		updated, err := s.repo.setRequestCreatedParty(ctx, id, party.ID, now)
242		if err != nil {

244		}
245	
246		// 6. Notify the new party (best-effort — a notify failure never fails the

248		language := party.PreferredLanguage

251		}
252		pid := party.ID

254			PartyID:     &pid,
255			Phone:       party.Phone,
256			Channel:     domain.ChannelSMS,
257			TemplateKey: domain.TemplateKYCApproved,
258			Language:    language,
259			Params:      map[string]string{"tier": claimed.RequestedTier},
260			Status:      domain.NotificationQueued,

264				slog.String("request_id", id.Hex()), slog.String("party_id", party.ID.Hex()), slog.Any("err", err))
265		}
266	
267		s.deps.Audit.Record(ctx, audit.Entry{
268			Action:     "onboarding.approve",
269			TargetType: "onboarding_request",
270			TargetID:   id.Hex(),
271			Meta: map[string]any{
272				"party_id":       party.ID.Hex(),
273				"requested_role": claimed.RequestedRole,

275				"new_tier":       newTier,

277			},
278		})
279		s.log.InfoContext(ctx, "onboarding request approved",

282			slog.String("requested_role", claimed.RequestedRole),
283			slog.String("requested_tier", claimed.RequestedTier),
284			slog.String("new_tier", newTier),
285			slog.String("actor_party_id", actor.PartyID))

287	}

26	func actorOr401(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) (auth.Actor, bool) {
27		actor, ok := auth.ActorFrom(r.Context())
28		if !ok {
29			httpx.Error(w, r, httpx.Unauthorized("authentication required"))
30		}
31		return actor, ok
32	}

166			}
